title: BCL activist held over torture, extortion of JU student
body: Police on Saturday night arrested an activist of the banned Bangladesh Chhatra League for allegedly torturing and extorting money from a Jahangirnagar University student in Netrokona’s Purbadhala upazila. The arrestee is Shishir Ahmed Talukder Ratul, 22, a resident of Shaldigha village of Purbadhala upazila and member of Purbadhala upazila unit of BCL, said Abdullah Al Mamun, officer-in-charge (OC) of Purbadhala Police Station. The victim, Sharif Hossain, 21 -- a student of the 54th batch in the Department of Drama and Dramatics at Jahangirnagar University -- is from Shunai village in Atpara upazila of Netrokona. OC Mamun also said a police team arrested Shishir from Charpara in Mymensingh on Saturday night after the victim filed a case with the police station against unidentified accused, said the OC. The accused was produced before the court this afternoon with a seven-day remand petition, said the OC, adding that police operations are continuing to identify and arrest the other accomplices involved in the incident. According to the case statement, Sharif boarded a CNG-run auto-rickshaw from Netrokona town on the evening of June 10 for the new bypass area. After mistakenly getting off in Shaldigha, he was walking towards Trimohini when two men intercepted him near the Shaldigha Eidgah Maidan. The assailants allegedly beat him and took him to a secluded location, where another person joined them. The three then physically tortured him and snatched Tk 4,560 in cash, according to the complaint. The perpetrators also allegedly transferred Tk 10,000 from the victim's bKash account using his mobile phone and took a Tk 1,500 loan from the same account. They also snatched his smartphone, valued at around Tk 22,000. Investigation sources said that during the torture, the victim was forced to chant abusive and coerced political slogans and statements. A video of the incident later spread on social media, triggering a widespread reaction. Following the case, police launched an investigation and identified Shishir as the prime accused.

title: Man arrested over shooting of listed criminal ‘Kailla Palash’
body: Police have arrested a man over his alleged involvement in the attempted murder of listed top criminal Yasin Khan , widely known as "Kailla Palash", in Dhaka’s Rampura area. Imam, 27, was arrested from the capital’s Badda area today, said Ibne Mizan, deputy commissioner of Dhaka Metropolitan Police’s Tejgaon Division. He said Imam confessed during primary interrogation that members of a rival group opened fire on Palash over a conflict linked to establishing supremacy in the area. Imam was allegedly riding one of two motorcycles used by the attackers, which has since been seized. According to police, the attack took place near Ekramunnesa Girls’ High School beside Rampura Bridge on Friday afternoon when Palash was returning home after offering Juma prayers. Quoting witnesses, police said a gunman shot Palash and fled on a motorcycle while firing blank rounds to create panic. Palash sustained two bullet wounds to the head and was admitted to Dhaka Medical College Hospital in critical condition. Palash, 50, was released from prison a little over a month ago after serving around 24 years in jail. He was earlier sentenced to death in 2002 for the murder of a Jubo Dal leader in Rampura, a verdict later commuted to life imprisonment by the High Court. DC Mizan said drives are ongoing to arrest the remaining suspects involved in the attack. Investigators are looking into whether the shooting was linked to past enmity or a turf war over local business interests. Law enforcement officials noted that attacks on top criminals by underworld rivals have seen a rise since the political changeover on August 5, 2024. These incidents indicate a resurgence of gang leaders released from prison, leading to recent violent conflicts that have claimed the lives of several other listed criminals, including Tariq Saif Mamun and Khandokar Noyeem Ahmed Titon.

title: Ex-BRUR VC Kalimullah secures permanent bail in graft case
body: The High Court today granted permanent bail to detained Professor Nazmul Ahsan Kalimullah, former vice-chancellor of Begum Rokeya University, Rangpur (BRUR), in a corruption case filed by the Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC). The High Court bench of Justice Md Atowar Rahman and Justice Biswajit Debnath delivered the verdict following a bail petition filed by Kalimulla. The bench asked Kalimullah to submit his passport along with the bail bond to the lower court concerned in connection with the case. There is no legal bar to Prof Kalimullah being released from jail following the High Court judgment, his lawyer Syed Mamun Mahbub told The Daily Star. Senior lawyers Md Fazlur Rahman, AM Mahbub Uddin Khokon, Syed Mamun Mahbub and Advocate Kazi Ahsan Habib appeared for the bail petitioner, while Advocate Khan Md Moinul Hasan Lipon represented the ACC. Attorney General Md Ruhul Quddus Kazal appeared for the state. Earlier, on August 6, 2025, Kalimullah was arrested by the Detective Branch (DB) of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police from a residence in Mohammadpur. He was subsequently placed on a five-day remand in connection with the case. After a metropolitan special judge's court rejected his bail petition on September 4 last year, he sought bail from the High Court. The case was filed on June 6 last year by Minhaz Bin Islam, then assistant director of the ACC's Integrated District Office Dhaka-1, against Kalimullah and four others over alleged irregularities in a special development project at the university. According to the allegations, nearly Tk 4 crore was misappropriated through irregularities in the construction of Sheikh Hasina Hall and the Dr Wazed Miah Research and Training Institute building under the project.

title: Ramisa rape-murder: Sohel, Swapna challenge death penalty
body: The High Court today admitted for hearing the appeals filed by death-row convicts Sohel Rana and his wife, Swapna Khatun, challenging the trial court verdict in the Ramisa Akter rape and murder case . The High Court bench of Justice Mohammad Ali and Justice Md Saiful Islam passed the order after the appeals, filed through the jail authorities, were included in its cause list. The court will hear the appeals along with the death reference in the case after the completion of relevant procedures, Deputy Attorney General Mehedi Hasan told The Daily Star. Attorney General Md Ruhul Quddus Kazal represented the state during the proceedings. No lawyer appeared on behalf of the convicted accused. On June 7, the Women and Children Repression Prevention Tribunal in Dhaka sentenced prime accused Sohel Rana to death for the rape and murder of Ramisa and sentenced his wife, Swapna Khatun, to death for assisting him in the crime. The tribunal also fined Sohel Tk 5 lakh and Swapna Tk 2 lakh. The court ordered that the fines be paid to the victim's legal heirs. If the convicts fail to pay the fines, the district collectors will recover the amount by auctioning their movable and/or immovable properties and hand over the proceeds to the victim's family, according to the verdict. Ramisa, a second-grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded at her neighbour Sohel's house on May 19. The following day, her father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, filed the case with Pallabi Police Station against the couple and an unidentified person.

title: Ex-IGP Benazir Ahmed arrested in Dubai
body: Former Inspector General of Police, Benazir Ahmed, has been arrested in Dubai by the UAE city police in connection with a case filed by the Bangladesh Anti-Corruption Commission. Talking to The Daily Star, Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed said, “Former IGP Benazir Ahmed has been arrested in Dubai." Dubai police arrested him with the help of Interpol in an ACC case on June 12, he said. Later at the Parliament, the minister said, "We will take necessary actions to bring him back.” The former top cop is currently being investigated by the ACC for allegedly amassing huge wealth while in office. Benazir, who faces US sanctions over alleged involvement in extrajudicial killings during his tenure as chief of Rapid Action Battalion, is accused of using two methods to acquire land: direct intimidation and indirect pressure. The ACC has so far found that he and his family bought at least 613.41 bighas of land in different districts, including 605.77 bighas in Gopalganj and Madaripur that once belonged to members of the Hindu community. He built most of his assets, including the Savanna Eco Resort and Natural Park in his hometown of Gopalganj, during his tenure as Rab chief (January 2015–April 2020) and as police chief (April 2020–September 2022).

title: Two injured, one with bullet wounds, in Khulna mosque attack
body: Two people were injured, one of them with bullet wounds, after unidentified assailants opened fire inside a mosque in Khulna city during Fajr prayers today. Lokman Hekim, 55, works as an oil agent at Jamuna Oil Depot suffered bullet injuries and was taken Khulna Medical College Hospital (KMCH) initially. Later, he was shifted to a hospital in Dhaka for better treatment. Another injured, Alam Sheikh, is currently undergoing treatment at KMCH. The incident took place around 5:30am inside the Jame Mosque of the West Zone Power Distribution Company on BL College Road in Daulatpur, Khulna Metropolitan Police Deputy Commissioner (North) Sudarshan Kumar Roy said. According to police, Lokman had gone to the mosque to offer Fajr prayers when the assailants opened fire on him, leaving him seriously injured. Local worshippers rescued him and took him to KMCH. As his condition deteriorated, he was later transferred to Dhaka for advanced treatment. The police official said CCTV footage showed two helmet-wearing individuals on a motorcycle near the scene. "We are examining more footage. The motive behind the shooting is still unknown," Deputy Commissioner Sudarshan Kumar Roy said.

title: Idols of Hindu deities vandalised at three temples in Bogura
body: Miscreants vandalised at least four to five idols of Hindu deities at three temples in Kanachgari area under the newly formed Mokamtala upazila of Bogura. The attacks took place at the Kanachgari Shiva Temple, Shitala Temple and Mahashmashan Temple sometime on Friday night, according to temple committee sources. Devotees discovered the damaged idols around 12:00pm yesterday when they arrived to perform regular religious rituals and immediately informed the local administration. Md Shahinuzzaman, officer-in-charge of Shibganj Police Station, confirmed the incidents. Upon receiving the information, Shibganj Upazila Nirbahi Officer (UNO) Md Ziaur Rahman visited the sites yesterday. “No one could pinpoint the exact time of the vandalism. The administration is investigating the matter. The culprits managed to carry out the act easily because the temples are located outside the main locality,” he told The Daily Star. He said necessary action would be taken following the investigation. The OC said the three temples are situated away from the village, near a crematorium and in open fields. “Looking at the idols, it appears they were vandalised a few days ago, and the villagers noticed it later,” he said. Police have begun investigating the incidents but have not yet received any written complaint. “Legal action will be taken once a written complaint is filed,” the OC added.

title: Mother, teenage daughter stabbed to death in Chattogram house
body: A woman and her teenage daughter were stabbed to death at their residence in Anwara upazila of Chattogram late last night. The victims were identified as Ani Barua, 40, and her daughter Priyonti Barua, 16, police said. Anwara Police Station Officer-in-Charge Junayet Chowdhury said unidentified assailants attacked the mother and daughter with sharp weapons inside their house in the Chenamati area around 11:30pm. They succumbed to their injuries on the way to hospital, the OC. Police rushed to the scene after receiving information about the incident. "A dispute over financial transactions involving the victim's husband and a relative has emerged as a possible motive behind the killing. However, we are investigating all information," the OC said. Police said the bodies were sent to Chattogram Medical College Hospital (CMCH) morgue for autopsy.

title: Shibir leader held in rape, forced abortion case
body: Police have arrested four people, including a leader of Islami Chhatra Shibir, in a case filed over the rape of a woman and allegedly forcing her to undergo an abortion in Cumilla. The arrested Shibir leader is Jisan Mia Pradhan, 28, now expelled central assistant secretary for international affairs, said Cumilla Superintendent of Police Md Anisuzzaman yesterday. Another arrestee is Jisan’s cousin Sajib, while the identities of the two others could not be known immediately. On June 12, Jisan’s family filed a general diary with Daudkandi Model Police Station, claiming that he had been missing since 8:30pm on Thursday. A police investigation found that Jisan went into hiding after a woman he knew brought allegations of rape and forced abortion against him, added the SP. Meanwhile, the woman filed a case against Jisan as the prime accused, bringing allegations of rape, abetment of rape, forced abortion and criminal intimidation. Islami Chhatra Shibir Central Committee relieved Jisan of his post as central assistant secretary for international affairs following his arrest in the case.

title: Mob beats man to death in Barguna
body: A man was beaten to death by a mob after he allegedly hacked a union parishad panel chairman for opposing drug trafficking in Barguna’s Sadar upazila on Friday. The deceased was identified as Ibrahim Hossain Kalu, 35, alleged leader of a group known locally as “Kalu Bahini” and a resident of Dema village in Badarkhali union, police said. The incident took place around 5:30pm on Friday in Chamily Bazar area under Badarkhali union, said Barguna Sadar Police Station Officer-in-Charge Mohammad Abdul Alim today. OC Abdul Alim said Golam Mostafa, a member and panel chairman of Badarkhali Union Parishad, had an altercation with Ibrahim Kalu, a suspected drug trader, for allegedly opposing his involvement in drug trafficking and other criminal activities in Badarkhali union and surrounding areas. On Friday afternoon, Kalu and his associates attacked Mostafa with sharp weapons centring the earlier issue, leaving him critically injured. Mostafa was first taken to Barguna General Hospital and later shifted to Sher-e-Bangla Medical College Hospital in Barishal as his condition deteriorated, he said. The attack sparked outrage among local residents. Shortly afterwards, angry locals allegedly caught Kalu and one of his associates, Tawhid, and beat them. After being informed, police rushed to the scene, rescued the two, and took them to Barguna General Hospital, where doctors declared Kalu dead, said the OC. Tawhid, who sustained serious injuries, was referred to Barishal for advanced treatment. Legal proceedings are underway, and police have launched an investigation into the incident, the OC added. Police said Kalu was accused in 13 to 14 cases, including several narcotics-related charges. He was arrested with homemade weapons in February this year and was released on bail a few days ago.

title: Khulshi OC withdrawn over police assault on Nayeem Hasan
body: The Chattogram Metropolitan Police (CMP) has withdrawn the Officer-in-Charge (OC) of Khulshi Police Station following allegations surrounding the assault of Bangladesh national cricketer Nayeem Hasan by members of Khulshi Police Station. The decision was made last night following huge criticism due to his alleged involvement in the assault. Meanwhile, Mohammad Solaiman, the OC of Bakalia Police Station, has been assigned to take charge of Khulshi Police Station. The development comes a day after Nayeem Hasan alleged that he had been detained and physically assaulted by individuals identifying themselves as members of the Detective Branch (DB) of police in the Lalkhan Bazar area of Chattogram while returning home from a Dhaka Premier League match. The player also alleged that OC Arif asked him to keep mum when BCB President Tamim Iqbal phoned OC regarding the incident. Confirming the transfer, Additional Police Commissioner (Crime and Operations) Faisal Ahmed said OC Arif has been transferred from the police station and attached to the Police Lines. Earlier, two policemen were suspended over the assault and harassment of Bangladesh spinner Nayeem Hasan in Chattogram, while CMP expressed regret and apologised over the incident. CMP Commissioner Shawkat Ali said this while visiting Nayeem at his residence in the Chandgaon area of Chattogram yesterday morning. Shawkat said responsibility for any unprofessional conduct rests with the individuals involved and the police force would not take responsibility for such actions.

title: Jubo Dal leader shot dead in Ctg
body: A local leader of Jatiyatabadi Jubo Dal, the ruling BNP’s youth front, was shot dead by unidentified assailants in Chattogram’s Raozan upazila yesterday. The victim was identified as Maksudul Haque Chowdhury Masud, 45, a senior joint convener of Rangunia upazila Jubo Dal. According to police and locals, Masud came under attack at Pahartali Chowmuhani in Raozan around 1:30pm. The attackers allegedly opened fire on him, leaving him dead on the spot. Locals suspect the killing may have been linked to a long-standing dispute over the sand trade. They also said Masud had been discussed as a potential chairman candidate in the upcoming local government elections. Raozan Police Station Officer-in-Charge Saiful Islam said, “Efforts are underway to identify and arrest those involved in the killing.” Meanwhile, protesting the murder, Jubo Dal activists blocked the Kaptai road in the Ishakhali area by burning tyres. The protesters demanded the immediate arrest of those responsible and punishment for the perpetrators.

title: Outcry as cops assault nat’l cricketer
body: Bangladesh’s cricket community was left stunned after national team off-spinner Nayeem Hasan allegedly became the victim of police assault and harassment in Chattogram on Friday night, triggering widespread condemnation and swift action from the authorities. The incident occurred when Nayeem was returning home after his team Prime Bank Cricket Club’s final Dhaka Premier Division Cricket League (DPL) fixture in Savar. According to the cricketer, he arrived in Chattogram on a delayed flight and was travelling home in a CNG-run auto-rickshaw when a few policemen stopped the vehicle near the Lalkhan Bazar flyover at around 11:25 pm. Nayeem alleged that officers acted aggressively from the outset and physically assaulted him despite his cooperation and identification. “I told them, ‘You can check my bag if needed.’ One of the officers grabbed me by the throat and forced me into their vehicle.” The 26-year-old said he managed to get out and questioned the officers, but the situation escalated further. “I asked them why they were grabbing me by the throat. After that, they continued assaulting and harassing me. Later, many people recognised me, and I showed them my ID card, but they still kept beating me,” he further alleged. Videos of the incident spread rapidly on social media, drawing criticism from fans and the sporting community. Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB), Cricketers’ Welfare Association of Bangladesh (CWAB), and several national cricketers demanded a fair investigation and action against those responsible. BCB strongly condemned what it called “unacceptable and inappropriate conduct” towards a national team player. CWAB also termed the incident “unacceptable for any citizen” and pledged full support for Nayeem, who has played 14 Tests for Bangladesh, taking 48 wickets since his national debut in 2018. Bangladesh T20I captain Litton Das expressed support via Facebook, writing: “Keep your head high, Nayeem. You are a wonderful person,” adding that no citizen, let alone a national cricketer, deserved such treatment. Meanwhile, the Chattogram Metropolitan Police (CMP) responded swiftly, suspending two officers -- sub-inspector Md Shafiqul Islam Bhuiyan and constable Md Rasel Chowdhury -- and expressing regret over the incident. The CMP apologised for the incident. Late last night, it also withdrew Khulshi OC Arif. CMP commissioner Shawkat Ali visited Nayeem’s residence, announced a three-member investigation committee, and said departmental proceedings would be initiated against the accused officers, stressing responsibility for any unprofessional conduct rested with the individuals involved. Later, speaking in Chattogram yesterday, Nayeem thanked supporters and locals who gathered at the scene and accompanied him to the police station. “When they put me into the CNG, I was very frightened. If the 100 to 120 supporters and local people had not been present, the incident could have turned out differently. “I would especially like to thank them. When the police took me to Khulshi Police Station, I appealed to them. The supporters also came from Lalkhan Bazar to the police station with me that night.” Nayeem, who has 300 first-class wickets to his credit, added that he had already taken steps to avoid such incidents in future and was willing to cooperate with any lawful search. He is part of the squad for the upcoming Test against Zimbabwe in Harare starting June 28.

title: Rape victim arrested in trafficking case
body: A rape victim was arrested in a human trafficking case on Wednesday and is undergoing treatment under police custody in Bogura. According to the human trafficking case statement, the 21-year-old woman, Anjum* (not her real name), who is both the rape victim and an accused in the trafficking case, had been acquainted with a woman, Rima* (not her real name), for around eight months. (*Names have been changed to protect identities and avoid confusion in the narrative.) On Tuesday night, Anjum, along with an associate, allegedly took Rima from her home with the intent of trafficking her. On the way, Rima’s husband allegedly intercepted them, rescued his wife and took Anjum and her associate to their home, where they were confined, the statement alleged. On information, police arrived at the house on Wednesday morning and detained Anjum and her associate. Later that night, Rima’s sister filed a human trafficking case against Anjum and her associate, who were subsequently shown arrested in the case. A court later sent Anjum’s associate to jail after police produced him before it. Within a few hours, Anjum’s father filed a rape case against Rima’s husband, Atikur Rahman Gittu, 28, Md Abu Raihan, 24, Abdul Karim, 24, and around three unidentified individuals. Among them, Gittu has given a confessional statement in court and was sent to jail on June 11, said AFM Ashaduzzaman, officer-in-charge of Sariakandi Police Station, According to the rape case statement, Anjum had a cordial relationship with Rima and her sister, who filed the human trafficking case. The statement said that around 9:00pm on Tuesday, Rima called Anjum and sought help, alleging that her husband was torturing her. When Anjum and her associate were on their way to help, Rima, her husband and others intercepted them and took them to the couple’s home. The rape case statement said Rima’s husband and his associates, along with several unidentified men, raped Anjum in the house. Later that night, Rima’s sister filed a human trafficking case against Anjum and her associate. Contacted, the OC said, “Two people were arrested in a trafficking case, while two others were arrested in a rape case. “The accused in the trafficking case, who was reportedly raped, has been sent to a hospital for tests. Meanwhile, one of the men arrested in the rape case has made a confessional statement before a court.” Hospital sources said the rape victim bore several injury marks on her body, and there were signs of multiple sexual exposures. Contacted, Bogura Superintendent of Police Mirza Sayem Mahmud said both cases had been registered. “Necessary legal action will be taken following the investigation.”

title: Jubo Dal leader, associate arrested over rape of woman in Narayanganj
body: Police have arrested two people, including a local Jubo Dal leader, in connection with the alleged gang rape of a housewife in Sonargaon upazila of Narayanganj. The arrestees are Shahidul Islam Shahid, 40, general secretary of ward 2 Jubo Dal unit in Jampur union, and his associate Shahin Mia, 38, from the same area, said police. Sonargaon Police Station Inspector (Investigation) Mohammad Jamal Uddin said the two were arrested on Friday evening shortly after the victim filed a case against three people, including the duo, with the police station under the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act. Efforts are ongoing to apprehend the remaining suspect, the police official added. Her medical examination was conducted at Narayanganj General Hospital today. According to police and family members, the victim lives with her two children and husband in a tin-shed house under Jampur union. The incident took place on Wednesday afternoon when her husband, a construction worker, was away at work. Shahidul and his two associates entered the house and raped her. Family members also alleged that some influential locals initially tried to settle the matter through arbitration. Speaking to reporters, the victim said she was too afraid to return home following the arrests and the filing of the case. The family is currently staying at Narayanganj General (Victoria) Hospital with her husband and children out of fear. Inspector Jamal Uddin further said the victim and her family members can stay in her village without fear, and police will ensure their security.

title: Man beaten by mob, arrested over raping daughter, attempting to rape her classmate
body: A 42-year-old rickshaw puller was arrested after a mob beat him on allegations of raping his daughter and the attempted rape of her classmate in Jhenaidah's Kaliganj today. The accused from Chandipur village in Jhenaidah Sadar upazila was rescued by police around 6:30am after neighbours caught him at his rented house and beat him in Kaliganj municipality. The accused's elder daughter filed a rape case against him and the other victim's father filed the attempted rape case with Kaliganj Police Station today, according to its Officer-in-Charge Jellal Hossain. Citing the case statements, the OC said the accused's daughter and her classmate study in the same class in a madrasa. As the two families live next door to one another, the girls often slept at the same house. Last night, the two girls were sleeping in the accused's house. Around 6:30am today, the accused entered his daughter's room and tried to rape his daughter's classmate, according to one case statement. When the children screamed, the classmate’s parents and locals rushed to his house, subdued him, and beat him up. Later, police arrive at the spot and detained him. He allegedly threatened them to not reveal the matter to anyone, said the policeman. Citing case statement, OC Jellal Hossain told The Daily Star that the accused had repeatedly raped his daughter after sedating his wife with sleeping pills mixed in soft drinks. He added on April 7, the accused reportedly raped his daughter. The accused is currently undergoing treatment at Upazila Health Complex and will be produced before a court, the OC added.

title: Man shot dead in Chattogram's Raozan
body: A man was shot dead in Raozan upazila of Chattogram this noon. The deceased was identified as Masudul Haque Masud, 40, of Betagi union in the upazila. The shooting took place in the Pahartali area of Raozan at around 1:30pm. According to Assistant Superintendent of Police (ASP) Balayat Hossain of Raozan, armed assailants shot Masud in the head, killing him on the spot. "The reason behind the killing is yet to be established," the ASP said. Local sources said Masud was involved in Jubo Dal politics, though this could not be independently verified at the time of publication.

title: 2 cops suspended over assault on cricketer Nayeem Hasan; CMP chief apologises
body: Two police personnel have been suspended over the assault and harassment of Bangladesh spinner Nayeem Hasan in Chattogram, while Chattogram Metropolitan Police (CMP) has expressed regret and apologised over the incident. CMP Commissioner Shawkat Ali made the remarks this morning while visiting Nayeem at his residence in the Chandgaon area of Chattogram. Shawkat said responsibility for any unprofessional conduct rests with the individuals involved and the police force would not take responsibility for such actions. The CMP commissioner said the two police personnel involved in the alleged misconduct had been suspended and a three-member investigation committee had been formed. He added that departmental proceedings would also be initiated against them. "We have formed a three-member committee to investigate what exactly happened. Disciplinary action will be taken against them. A departmental case will also be filed in connection with the incident," he said. During the visit, the CMP commissioner spoke with Nayeem's father. Additional Commissioner (Administration and Finance) Wahidul Haque Chowdhury was also present. Earlier, in a press release, the CMP said preliminary findings suggest unprofessional conduct by the officers while performing their duties. The suspended officers are Sub-Inspector (Unarmed) Md Shafiqul Islam Bhuiyan of Khulshi Police Station and Constable Md Rasel Chowdhury. Departmental proceedings have also been initiated against them, according to the CMP. The press release said Nayeem encountered an "unfortunate incident" with members of Khulshi Police Station's night patrol team in the Lalkhan Bazar area under Khulshi Police Station while returning to his home in Chattogram from Dhaka. Earlier in the day, the Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB), the Cricketers' Welfare Association of Bangladesh (CWAB) and several national cricketers condemned the alleged assault and called for a thorough investigation and action against those responsible. According to a CWAB statement, Nayeem was stopped by police near Lalkhan Bazar while returning home after playing a Dhaka Premier League match in Savar. The association alleged that police displayed hostile behaviour from the outset and that officers grabbed Nayeem by the throat when he attempted to speak. Despite bystanders informing the police that he was national cricketer Nayeem Hasan, he was allegedly beaten with a pipe. CWAB further alleged that Nayeem was taken to Khulshi Police Station, where he was subjected to further mistreatment, and that the officers backed off only after he managed to call for assistance. In a separate statement, the BCB expressed deep concern over the reported incident and strongly condemned what it described as "unacceptable and inappropriate conduct" towards the national cricketer. The board called for a thorough and impartial investigation and urged the relevant authorities to take appropriate action against those found responsible.

title: ‘Top criminal’ Palash shot in city
body: Yeasin Khan alias Palash, also known as “Kailla Palash” and described by police as a “top criminal”, was shot in the head and critically injured in Dhaka’s West Rampura yesterday, just over a month after his release from prison. He was admitted to Dhaka Medical College Hospital, said Md Asaduzzaman, officer-in-charge of Hatirjheel Police Station. “He was a top criminal with many cases filed again him, including on murder charges.” The shooting took place around 1:45pm near Rampura bridge, the OC said. Inspector Md Faruk, in-charge of the DMCH police outpost, said Palash sustained two bullet wounds to the head. “His condition is critical.” Palash, 50, had been in prison for about 24 years in connection with the murder of a Jubo Dal leader and was freed one month and eight days ago, relatives said. He operated in Rampura and Badda areas, police sources said. Although the motive behind the attack could not be confirmed, law enforcement officials said possible angles, including past enmity, turf conflict and rivalries within the criminal underworld, were all being investigated. Ibrahim Mia, a domestic help at Palash’s house, said a milad event was arranged at their West Rampura home yesterday. “He [Palash] was returning home after offering Juma prayers at Makki Mosque. When he reached in front of Royal Mishti Shop, a man, wearing a cap, shot him. Several people chased the attacker, but he fled on a motorcycle,” said Ibrahim, adding that the assailant fired blank shots while fleeing. Palash’s brother Alamin said that after coming out of jail, Palash was involved in the internet and cable TV network trade. “We don’t know yet why he was attacked.” DMP’s DB Chief Shafiqul Islam said police could not immediately determine who carried out the shooting or the motive behind the attack, adding that an investigation was underway. Tejgaon Division Deputy Commissioner Ibn Mizan said Palash had previously faced multiple allegations. “We have launched an investigation to determine whether he had any prior enmity with anyone or was involved in any dispute over territorial dominance.” Asked whether there had been any conflict related to Palash’s current cable TV and internet service trade, the police official said investigators were also looking into that possibility. On May 29, 2002, a trial court sentenced Palash to death in the murder case of Jubo Dal leader Mizan, who was shot dead in Rampura. The High Court later commuted the sentence to life imprisonment. Palash later made headlines in 2016 after it came to light that he had been admitted to hospitals from prison, reportedly posing as a patient and receiving family visits during those stays. Such attacks on “top criminals”, allegedly carried out by their rivals in the underworld, saw a rise after the political changeover on August 5, 2024. According to law enforcement officials, these incidents indicate a resurgence of top gang leaders released from prison, with many of their associates also becoming active again. On November 10 last year, listed “top criminal” Tariq Saif Mamun was shot dead near Dhaka’s busiest court area. Days later, Jubo Dal leader Golam Kibria was killed in a shooting in Pallabi on November 17. Another “top criminal”, Khandokar Noyeem Ahmed Titon, was shot dead near New Market on April 28 this year.

title: Calls grow for fresh probe into Kalpana Chakma’s abduction
body: A human chain was formed in Rangamati yesterday, demanding justice for the abduction of Kalpana Chakma and immediate steps to implement the Chittagong Hill Tracts (CHT) Peace Accord. The programme was organised by the Rangamati district committee of the Hill Women’s Federation around 10:00am on the Rangamati Deputy Commissioner’s Office premises. Addressing the gathering, Mranu Ching Marma, general secretary of the federation’s central committee, alleged that women in the CHT were not safe and that sexual violence continued to affect women of all ages. “Kalpana Chakma fought for the rights of the Jumma people. Thirty years have passed since her abduction, but the government has been unable to do anything about it. We are being subjected to oppression because the Jumma people of the CHT are not being given the right to self-determination,” she said. Lawyer Dipan Chakma said the case had been investigated at different stages before being dismissed by the Senior Judicial Magistrate Court in Rangamati on April 23, 2024. Kalpana’s brothers, Kalindi Chakma and Lal Bihari Chakma, were also abducted on the same day and had clearly seen those responsible, he added. “We, the victims’ lawyers, have filed a revision petition. We will demand that the revision be accepted and that the case be investigated again,” he added. Writer and educationist Shishir Kanti Chakma demanded the case to be reopened and properly investigated. Kalpana Chakma, organising secretary of the Hill Women’s Federation, an affiliate of the Parbatya Chattagram Jana Samghati Samiti (PCJSS), was abducted from her home in Lalyaghona village under Baghaichhari upazila in Rangamati early on June 12, 1996.

title: Two held over attack on motorcyclist in Dhaka
body: Police have arrested two individuals for allegedly attacking a motorcyclist with a brick and leaving him critically injured in Dhaka’s East Shewrapara. The arrests were made during separate drives in Dhaka and Mymensingh on Thursday after CCTV footage of the incident went viral on social media. The arrestees were identified as Parvez, 30, and Anwar Hossain Babu, 32. They are accused in multiple drug-related cases filed with different police stations in Dhaka. Police said the attack was pre-planned and stemmed from a prior enmity. Briefing reporters at the DMP Media Centre yesterday, Deputy Commissioner Mostak Sarker said Parvez was arrested from the Dhobaura border area in Mymensingh, while Babu was apprehended in Dhaka’s Ibrahimpur area. Following the incident, victim’s uncle Nur Hossain filed an attempted murder case with Kafrul Police Station. DC Mostak said Parvez had previously been a tenant at the victim Rafi’s house. A dispute ensued between them as Parvez and his associates were allegedly involved in local drug trade. During a heated argument on Tuesday evening, Parvez and his associate Faisal, alias Kalu, threatened Rafi. According to police, Parvez, Kalu, Babu and another associate, Amin, took positions near East Shewrapara bus stand around 1:15am on Wednesday and waylaid Rafi before hitting him on his head with a brick. Rafi sustained severe head injuries and collapsed on the road. CCTV footage showed the attackers later placing injured Rafi into an auto-rickshaw, while one of them fled with his motorcycle. Police also said the attackers misled locals by claiming that a brick had accidentally fallen on Rafi from a nearby building. They later dumped him in the Ibrahimpur area and fled. The motorcycle was found abandoned near the crime scene. Drives are on to arrest the remaining suspects.

title: Two sent to jail in rape, attempted rape cases
body: Two men were sent to jail yesterday in separate rape and attempted rape cases, while a woman was stabbed after resisting an alleged rape attempt on Thursday night, report our correspondents. In Netrokona’s Kendua upazila, police arrested Abdur Rahim, 65, on Thursday in a case filed by the father of a nine-year-old girl, who alleged that Rahim raped her on June 6 when she went to bring back cattle from a nearby wetland. A court sent him to jail yesterday, said Kendua Police Station OC Md Mehedi Maksud. In Gazipur’s Kapasia upazila, a court sent Amjad Darji, 57, to jail yesterday in a case over the alleged attempted rape of a 14-year-old girl with a physical disability. Kapasia Police Station OC Mohammad Naser Ahmed said he was arrested on Thursday, after the victim’s mother filed the case. In Jashore, a 40-year-old woman was stabbed on the neck and face after resisting an alleged rape attempt at her home on Thursday night, said Kotwali Police Station OC Masud Khan. The accused, Abdul Quader, 27, was arrested. The woman was undergoing treatment at a local hospital.

title: Moulvibazar woman gang-raped at home; 2 accused confess: Police
body: Two men accused of gang-raping a woman in Moulvibazar town have been arrested, with both subsequently giving confessional statements before a magistrate, police said this afternoon. The arrestees -- Ferdous Hossain, 31, and Kannal Mia alias Joynal, 39 -- were arrested during separate operations conducted by Moulvibazar Sadar Model Police Station. Two mobile phones allegedly stolen during the incident were also recovered. Md Saiful Islam, officer-in-charge of Moulvibazar Sadar Model Police Station, said three masked men broke into the victim's home in the early hours of June 3. The woman was sleeping alongside her infant daughter. The assailants allegedly raped her under threat. Following the incident, the victim filed a case against unidentified suspects at Moulvibazar Sadar Model Police Station. Investigators subsequently launched an inquiry, drawing on digital intelligence to trace the accused. Ferdous was apprehended from Rajabari area of Dhaka’s Savar, while Joynal was arrested from Uttar Kalimabad area of Moulvibazar town. Produced before a court, both accused confessed to their involvement under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure yesterday, said the OC. A third suspect remains at large and operations are ongoing to arrest him, added the OC.

title: 2 arrested over brick attack on motorcyclist in Dhaka's Shewrapara
body: Police have arrested two individuals for allegedly attacking a motorcyclist with a brick and leaving him critically injured in Dhaka's East Shewrapara, following the circulation of CCTV footage of the incident on social media. The arrests were made during separate drives in Dhaka and Mymensingh yesterday. The arrestees were identified as Parvez, 30, and Anwar Hossain Babu, 32. Police said the attack was pre-planned and stemmed from a previous enmity. Briefing reporters at the DMP Media Centre today, Deputy Commissioner Mostak Sarker said Parvez was arrested from the Dhobaura border area in Mymensingh, while Babu was apprehended in Dhaka's Ibrahimpur area. Following the incident, the victim's uncle, Nur Hossain, filed an attempted murder case with Kafrul Police Station. Explaining the background to the incident, the Deputy Commissioner Mostak said Parvez had previously been a tenant at the victim Rafi's house. A dispute developed between them as Parvez and his associates were allegedly involved in local drug trading activities. The feud escalated into a heated argument between Rafi, Parvez and Parvez's associate Faisal, alias Kalu, on Tuesday evening, during which the suspects allegedly threatened to teach Rafi a lesson. According to police, Parvez, Kalu, Babu and another associate, Amin, took positions near the East Shewrapara bus stand at around 1:15am on Wednesday as part of their plan. When Rafi was passing through the area on his motorcycle, Amin allegedly attempted to block his path and Parvez struck him on the head with a brick. He sustained severe head injuries and collapsed on the road. CCTV footage showed the attackers later placing the injured Rafi into an auto-rickshaw, while one of them fled with his motorcycle. Police said the attackers misled locals by claiming that a brick had accidentally fallen on Rafi from a nearby building. They later dumped him in the Ibrahimpur area before fleeing. The abandoned motorcycle was subsequently recovered near the crime scene. Parvez and the absconding Kalu are accused in multiple drug-related cases filed with different police stations in Dhaka, the DMP official said, adding that drives are continuing to arrest the remaining suspects.

title: Attempted break-in reported at attorney general’s office in Supreme Court area
body: An attempted break-in was reported at the office of Attorney General Ruhul Quddus Kazal in the Supreme Court area of Dhaka early today. Kazal described the incident as a "possible act of sabotage". He said a group of miscreants, around 1:15am, removed sections of windows on the ground and first floors. “They tried to reach my room on the second floor after removing glass panels. Our security guards went to the spot to investigate suspicious sounds and chased the suspects. The miscreants fled, sensing the presence of the guards and police,” he said. “I believe the incident may have been an act of sabotage rather than an ordinary theft. My office was targeted,” he added. The attorney general alleged that some former employees dismissed from the office, as well as individuals fearing job loss due to corruption allegations, had recently been spreading “false propaganda” about the office on social media. “I think they may have had some role in instigating the incident,” he said. Kazal said he has asked the police officials and the office administration of the Supreme Court to investigate, keeping the issue in mind. He said no important documents or valuables had been reported missing so far, as the suspects fled before gaining full access to the office. Assistant Sub-Inspector Jewel Majumdar of Shahbagh Police Station said senior police officials visited the spot after the incident. No case or general diary had been filed as of this afternoon, he added.

title: Listed top criminal 'Kailla Palash' shot in Dhaka's Hatirjheel: Police
body: Unidentified assailants shot a listed top criminal in Dhaka’s Hatirjheel area this afternoon, police say. Yeasin Khan alias Palash, widely known as "Kailla Palash", 50, was rushed to Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH) with bullet wounds, said Md Asaduzzaman, officer-in-charge of Hatirjheel Police Station. “He is a top-listed criminal with multiple cases against him, including murder,” the OC said, adding that Palash had been released from jail a few days ago after serving long time in prison. The shooting took place around 1:45pm near Ekramunnesa Girls' High School near the Rampura Bridge, he said. The OC also said the identities of the attackers and the motive behind the shooting could not be immediately determined. Police have launched an investigation. Speaking to reporters, Ibra Mia, Palash's employee, said a milad mahfil had been arranged at Palash's home in Poshchim Rampura earlier in the day. After offering Juma prayers at the local Makki Mosque, Palash was returning home. When he reached Rampura Royal Sweet Shop, someone opened fire targeting him, Ibra said. When a few people chased the attacker, he fled the scene on a motorcycle, he said, adding, “After hearing about the incident, we quickly took him to DMCH.” Ibra also said Palash had served 25 years in jail in connection with a murder case and was released from jail 38 days ago. Inspector Md Faruk, in-charge of the DMCH Police Outpost, said Palash sustained two bullet wounds to the head and was taken to the operating theatre. “His condition is critical,” the inspector said. On November 10 last year, another "listed top criminal", Tarik Saif Mamun, was shot dead in broad daylight in Dhaka’s Sutrapur area. On April 28 this year, Khandokar Noyeem Ahmed Titon, also described by police as a "top criminal", was shot dead in the New Market area.

title: Man arrested over attempted rape of disabled girl in Gazipur
body: Police have arrested a man in connection with a case filed over the attempted rape of a physically disabled 14-year-old girl in Kapasia upazila of Gazipur. The accused, Amjad Darji, 57, is a resident of Kandanwa village in Kapasia upazila, Kapasia Police Station Officer-in-Charge Mohammad Naser Ahmed told The Daily Star. A case had been filed and the accused would be produced before a court today, he added. According to the First Information Report filed by the victim's mother, the accused, a distant relative, lured the victim on the pretext of taking her to his house on May 27. However, he took the child to a jungle near her house and tried to rape her. While searching for her daughter, the plaintiff found her daughter screaming near the bushes with the accused laying on top of her. Seeing her, Amjad fled the scene. She later filed a case against him with Kapasia Police Station yesterday. Meanwhile, residents of the area staged a human chain last afternoon in front of the Kapasia Sadar Union Parishad office, demanding death penalty for the accused.

title: 2 policemen stabbed in Dhaka
body: Two policemen were injured after being stabbed by suspected muggers during a chase in Dhaka’s Sher-e-Bangla Nagar area early today. The injured are Sub-Inspector Shamsuzzoha, 34, and Constable Mohammad Hridoy Hossain, 20, both posted at Sher-e-Bangla Nagar Police Station. The incident took place around 1:00am in front of the Glass Bridge at Zia Udyan, police said. According to police and hospital sources, three unidentified muggers attempted to flee on a battery-run rickshaw after committing a mugging. A police patrol team chased them on motorcycles and managed to intercept them. At one stage, one of the suspects stabbed the two policemen with a sharp weapon. Police detained two of the alleged muggers in connection with the incident. Other officers later rescued the injured policemen and took them to Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital. After receiving primary treatment there, they were transferred to Dhaka Medical College Hospital around 2:30am for advanced care. Mahmudul Hasan, sub-inspector of the police camp at DMCH, said the two policemen are currently undergoing treatment at Ward No. 4 of the hospital’s emergency department.

title: Man held over alleged rape of a woman and her niece in Jashore
body: A young man has been detained by police on allegations of raping a woman and her niece after entering a house in the Chanchra Magurpatti area of Jashore early today. The accused, identified as Rocky, 30, from the Chanchra Dal Mill area, was arrested during a late-night police operation. According to police and the victims' family members, the incident occurred around 1:30am when the woman and her teenage niece were asleep in a room. The woman's husband was away from home at the time. The suspect allegedly entered the house, raped the woman, and threatened her. He also allegedly raped her teenage niece, according to the family's account. After the suspect left, the woman informed her husband, and the family went to Jashore Kotwali Police Station to lodge a complaint. Following the complaint, police conducted a raid and detained the suspect. Confirming the arrest, Masud Khan, officer-in-charge of Jashore Kotwali Police Station, said, "The two victims are being sent for medical examinations. The victim's husband has filed a case this afternoon.”

title: Madrasa teacher on the run after alleged rape, knife attack on student in Munshiganj
body: A madrasa teacher allegedly attempted to rape a 14-year-old student before slashing his throat with a knife when the boy resisted, leaving the victim in critical condition, police said. The incident occurred around noon today at an isolated spot in the Pashchim Sonarang area under Sonarang union of Tongibari upazila in Munshiganj. The accused has been on the run since the attack. The accused, Hafez Md Lokman Hossain, 26, is from Char Shashibhushan area under Charfesson upazila in Bhola, and serves as imam of Sonarang Old Jame Mosque and a teacher at Khilpara Sunnatul Madina Madrasa in the same locality. The victim is a student at that madrasa. Quoting locals, Shamim Ahmed, officer-in-charge of Tongibari Police Station, said Lokman allegedly took the student to an isolated location and attempted to rape him. When the boy resisted, Lokman slashed his throat with a knife, the OC added. Hearing the victim's screams, locals rushed to the scene, prompting the attacker to flee. Locals found the blood-soaked boy and initially brought him to Tongibari Upazila Health Complex. As his condition deteriorated, the attending physician referred him urgently to Dhaka Medical College Hospital, where he is currently undergoing treatment in critical condition. OC Shamim said a special drive was underway to detain Lokman.

title: Youth arrested over rape of mentally and visually impaired girl in Patuakhali
body: Police have arrested a teenager accused of raping a 14-year-old girl with mental and visual challenged in Bauphal upazila of Patuakhali last night. The accused, Sabbir Khan, 19, of Uttar Rajnagar village, was produced before court today and sent to jail, said Bauphal Police Station Officer-in-Charge Md Sirajul Islam. According to the case filed by the victim’s mother, the incident occurred sometime between March 5 and March 30 when the girl went to a neighbour’s garden in search of her younger brother. Taking advantage of the secluded spot, Sabbir allegedly raped her. A medical examination later confirmed that the girl is three months pregnant. When questioned by her family, she disclosed that Sabbir had sexually assaulted her. Police arrested Sabbir last night following the case filing. He, however, has denied involvement in the incident. OC Sirajul Islam said the matter is being investigated with utmost seriousness. The victim has been admitted to Patuakhali Medical College Hospital for further examination and care.

title: Class 10 student hacked to death over drug dispute in Noakhali
body: A class 10 student was hacked to death and three others were injured in an attack allegedly by illegal drug traders in Noakhali’s Senbag upazila last night. The deceased, Arafat Hossain Fahim, 16, was the son of Md Shahjahan of Choumuhani Municipality in Begumganj upazila. He was visiting his maternal grandfather’s house at Debisinghpur village in Senbag when the incident occurred. Police have detained a man named Md Harun, 35, in connection with the incident. Abu Tayeb Md Arif Hossain, additional superintendent of police (Finance & Administration) of Noakhali, confirmed the matter in a press release. Eyewitness Delwar Hossain Nobel said a group led by Harun, Jahangir, Abul Khayer and Momin had long been involved in an illegal drug business in the area. They allegedly used to consume drugs on a bridge behind Hazera Dighi. Five or six days ago, local youths, including Fahim, detained a drug user named Manna, who reportedly disclosed Harun’s involvement during initial questioning. Following this, locals protested against the drug trade, forcing the group to stop the illegal activities for a few days. However, around 9:30pm yesterday, Harun, Momin and Jahangir were allegedly consuming marijuana near Sombaria Bazar in Nabipur union of the upazila. At that time, Fahim and his companions tried to stop them, leading to a clash between the two groups. Fahim was stabbed in the chest, while three others were injured. Among them, Rifat suffered severed tendons in his hand, and Sakib sustained injuries to his right hand. Local residents rescued the injured and took them to the 250-bed Noakhali General Hospital in Maijdee that night. Fahim died while undergoing treatment. The hospital’s emergency department doctor said he died due to excessive bleeding. Officer-in-Charge (OC) of Senbag Police Station Abdur Rahim Sarker said the initial investigation suggested that the incident stemmed from a dispute over drug-related activities. After receiving the news, police inspected the scene. The prime suspect, Harun, has been detained, and a blood-stained sharp weapon has been recovered from the spot. The process of taking legal action and filing a case is underway. Formal action will be taken after receiving a written complaint from the victim’s family, the OC said.

title: Case filed over rape of mother, daughter in Cox’s Bazar
body: A case has been filed in connection with the alleged gang rape of a mother and her teenage daughter at their home in Cox’s Bazar. One of the victims, the mother, filed the case early yesterday, accusing seven named and five to six unnamed people, said Md Monir Hossain, officer-in-charge (OC) of Chakaria Police Station. According to police, a group of eight to 10 men cut through a window grille of a house in the Dolnighona area, looted gold jewellery and cash, raped the woman and her teenage daughter, and fled. At the time of the incident, the housewife was at home with her two daughters -- one a teenager and one 7-year-old. Her husband was in Chattogram for business purposes. Police have arrested five of the named accused -- Tofazzal Hossain alias Babu, 23; Kefayat Hossain alias Puittya, 27; Mohammad Tanzid, 24; Mehedi Hasan, 24; and Mohammad Tareq, 26. Another person, Rezaul Karim, 36, was also arrested on suspicion. However, another named accused, Jisan, remains at large, said the OC. The victims’ family has identified him as the key figure behind the incident. Family members also alleged that the same criminal group had targeted their household on two to three previous occasions. Speaking to The Daily Star, Cox’s Bazar Assistant Superintendent of Police Abhijit Das said Jisan was released from jail just five days before the attack. He had been serving time on weapons and robbery charges. The OC said operations are ongoing to arrest the remaining accused. Meanwhile, rights organisation Ain o Salish Kendra (ASK) yesterday expressed deep concern and strongly condemned the incident. In a statement, ASK said the “barbaric and inhumane” incident was not merely a personal tragedy but one that raises serious questions about the country’s law and order situation and its ability to ensure the safety of women and children. The organisation said violence against women and children continues unabated, while shortcomings persist in crime prevention, prompt investigation, and effective accountability in many cases. ASK demanded the swift identification, arrest, and prosecution of all those involved under the existing laws. It also called for emergency medical treatment, mental health support, legal assistance, and maximum security for the victims. “Violence against women and children has no place in a just and democratic state,” the organisation said, urging the government to strictly enforce a zero-tolerance policy to curb such crimes.

title: Dedicated HC bench formed to hear death references in women, children repression cases
body: Chief Justice Zubayer Rahman Chowdhury has formed a High Court bench to exclusively hear and dispose of cases involving death sentences awarded under the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act. According to a directive issued today, Justice Bhishmadev Chakrabortty and Justice KM Rasheduzzaman Raja will sit as a division bench from June 14 to conduct the proceedings. The bench has been tasked with hearing, on a priority basis, death reference cases involving convictions. It will also deal with all criminal appeals and jail appeals arising from the same judgements, as well as related applications and revision petitions. Earlier, on June 7, the chief justice told lawyers at the Appellate Division that he would form a dedicated High Court bench to hear death references and appeals in cases involving crimes against women and children, including the rape and murder of eight-year-old Ramisa Akter. That day, a special court sentenced prime accused Sohel Rana and his wife Swapna Khatun to death for the rape and murder of Ramisa. A death reference is a mandatory judicial process through which a trial court’s death sentence is sent to the High Court for confirmation before it can be carried out. Convicts sentenced to death also retain the right to appeal against their convictions and sentences.

title: HC declares Bar Council’s cancellation of review results illegal
body: The High Court today declared illegal the Bangladesh Bar Council’s decision to cancel the review results of candidates who sat for the written examination for enrolment as advocates. The results had been published on November 18 last year. The court also directed the Bar Council to allow those candidates who had passed the first review but were later excluded in the second review process to participate in the viva voce examination. The verdict was delivered by the bench of Justice Khizir Ahmed Choudhury and Justice Md Ziaul Haque following a writ petition filed by 632 candidates challenging the Bar Council’s cancellation of the review results. Barrister M Ashraful Islam, lawyer for the petitioners, told The Daily Star that the ruling paves the way for candidates initially successful in the first review to continue the enrolment process. Deputy Attorney General Reza Md Sadekin confirmed that the Bar Council has been informed of the verdict and will decide whether to appeal to the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court. He explained that the Bar Council had cancelled the review results because grace marks were awarded to some candidates in the first review, but the High Court has now declared that cancellation illegal. On November 24 last year, the Bar Council scrapped the review results and ordered a re-evaluation of all answer scripts submitted for review. A second review result was then published, and viva examinations were held for those who passed under that process. The details of the High Court’s verdict will be known once its full text is released.

title: Masked men attack Dot Internet office in Dhaka’s Lalmatia
body: A group of masked men attacked the office of internet service provider Dot Internet in Dhaka’s Lalmatia area yesterday -- injuring two employees and looting valuables reportedly worth over Tk 2 lakh. The incident occurred around 8:45pm at Dot Internet’s office on the third floor of a building in Block E, Lalmatia. “We are reviewing CCTV footage and are working to identify those involved,” Mesbah Uddin, officer-in-charge of Mohammadpur Police Station, told The Daily Star. A case was later filed at Mohammadpur Police Station by the company’s Corporate Coordinator Officer Sagir Hossain Asif. The case statement said around 20 to 25 masked individuals forcibly entered the office and began searching for the company’s proprietor, Pradip Dhali, and Chief Technology Officer Mithun Hawlader. At the time, Account Manager Ibrahim Hawlader and electrician Jalal were present in the office. When they asked the intruders about the purpose of their visit, the attackers allegedly became aggressive and assaulted them. The two employees sustained injuries and were later given primary treatment at Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital. The assailants reportedly stole a CPU, a Wi-Fi router and a mobile phone from the office. The stolen items were estimated to be worth Tk 223,500. Before leaving the premises, the attackers also threatened staff members, according to the case statement. Speaking to this correspondent, Sagir Hossain Asif said the attackers initially complained about not receiving phone service, although staff members were unaware of what they were referring to. He added that they then began assaulting one of the employees and recorded the incident on a mobile phone, apparently to show it to someone on the other end of a call. He further said he does not know why the attack was carried out.

title: Over 18,000 arrested in nationwide special drive since May 1: Police
body: A total of 18,328 people have been arrested since May 1 under an ongoing special nationwide drive, according to Police Headquarters. In a release issued today, police said 1,958 of those arrested were identified as individuals involved in creating instability, along with planners and accomplices. The operation has also led to the arrest of a large number of suspects involved in various criminal activities. Among those detained were 331 illegal arms holders, 10,020 smugglers and drug traders, 2,211 muggers and robbers, and 808 extortionists and other criminals.

title: Case filed against 57 over attack on police in Savar; five arrested
body: A case has been filed against 57 people, including 17 named accused, over an attack on two police officers during an operation to arrest a drug case accused in Savar yesterday evening. The case was filed early today by Sub-Inspector (SI) SM Shamim of Savar Model Police Station, naming Rafiqul Islam, a warrant-listed accused in a drug case, as the prime accused. Confirming the matter to The Daily Star, Inspector (Investigation) Noor Mohammad of Savar Model Police Station said police arrested five accused during overnight drives in the Baktarpur area. The arrestees are Arif Islam, 20; Sagar Mia, 23; Maruf, 20; Rakes Mal, 30; and Humayun, 19. "They are all named accused in the case and have been sent to court with a prayer for a five-day remand," he said. According to the case statement, SI Shamim and Assistant Sub-Inspector (ASI) Mashiur Rahman went to the Balur Math area of Baktarpur around 7:40pm yesterday to arrest Rafiqul Islam. Police alleged that Rafiqul shouted for help and gathered others at the scene, who then obstructed the arrest operation and attacked the officers. The complaint states that Rafiqul struck SI Shamim with a brick, while ASI Mashiur Rahman was allegedly assaulted with sticks and iron rods by other accused. Both officers sustained injuries and were later taken to Savar Upazila Health Complex for treatment. Police said additional forces rushed to the area after receiving information, but the attackers fled before they arrived. The investigation is ongoing, and efforts are underway to arrest the remaining accused.

title: Six killed in Kushtia: ICT verdict in case against Hanif, 3 others any day
body: The International Crimes Tribunal-2 may deliver its verdict at any day in a case against Awami League joint general secretary Mahbubul Alam Hanif in a case over the killing of six people in Kushtia during the July uprising as both the prosecution and defence concluded their arguments today. The three other accused are Kushtia district Awami League President and former Zila Parishad Chairman Sadruddin Khan, district Awami League General Secretary Azgar Ali, and Kushtia city Awami League General Secretary Ataur Rahman Ata. All the four accused are absconding. However, the tribunal did not set a date for the pronouncement of the verdict yet. Earlier, the tribunal was told that acting on deposed prime minister Sheikh Hasina's directive to suppress the student- and public-led movement, Hanif executed the order through local Awami League leaders, party activists, and law enforcement agencies in Kushtia, leading to the fatal shooting of six protesters. It was also alleged by the prosecution that at a meeting held on July 27 last year at the Kushtia district Awami League office, Hanif, along with Azgar and Ataur, termed the movement as a "terrorist act" and ordered the use of maximum force to resist it.

title: Man stabbed to death, another critically injured in Chattogram
body: A man was stabbed to death and another critically injured by unidentified assailants in Patiya upazila of Chattogram last night. The deceased was identified as Pankaj Shil, 35, of Joulur Dighi area under Kachuai union. The injured, Tilak Chakraborty, 35, is undergoing treatment at Chattogram Medical College Hospital (CMCH) in critical condition, police said. Quoting locals, Patiya Police Station Officer-in-Charge Ziaul Haque said Pankaj and Tilak were returning home from a local market when they reached the western side of Joulur Dighi around 9:00pm. At that time, they noticed three suspicious individuals, one of whom was wearing a burqa. When the two flashed torchlights towards them, the assailants allegedly attacked them with sharp weapons, leaving both critically injured. Locals rescued the victims and took them to Patiya Upazila Health Complex. They were later shifted to CMCH where Pankaj died around 11:30pm. Law enforcers visited the scene and detained one person for questioning, although the detainee's identity was not immediately disclosed. The OC said drives were underway to identify and arrest those involved, adding that, "Police are investigating the incident to determine the motive behind the killing."

title: Extortion row behind Billal killing: police
body: Former Swechchhasebak Dal leader Billal Talukdar was killed over the collection of waste and electricity bills from shops adjacent to Anarkali Market in Dhaka’s Mouchak, police and party insiders confirmed. According to police, followers of Ramna Thana Jubo Dal leader Riazul Islam Babu had been regularly collecting electricity bills from several shops near the market’s main building -- a practice opposed by Thana BNP President Ashraf and his supporters, including Billal. Police reported that the conflict began when Billal’s nephew, a shop owner, objected to outsiders collecting electricity bills. A meeting was convened on Monday to resolve the dispute, but during the arbitration, Babu’s followers stabbed Billal following an altercation, said Ramna Police Station OC Mohammad Rahat Khan. Immediately after the incident, the Jubo Dal committee was dissolved, and Babu’s follower Riazul was expelled. Two people, including ward-19 Jubo Dal Convener Al Amin and Riazul, were arrested in connection with the killing. Billal’s widow, Ambia Khatun, has since filed a murder case naming 21 individuals and accusing 27 unidentified others. During a visit to Anarkali Market yesterday, posters of Riazul were still visible on the market walls, though shopkeepers were reluctant to discuss the murder. Local sources and eyewitnesses said disputes between Jubo Dal and Swechchhasebak Dal leaders over control of footpaths and alleged extortion in Anarkali Market and Mouchak area had been ongoing. A week earlier, an arbitration meeting was held to settle the matter, where it was decided that no extortion money would be collected. On the day of the incident, Siraj and Riazul were reportedly collecting money from footpath shops when Billal’s nephew protested and was beaten. A senior official of the DMP’s Ramna Division confirmed Riazul’s arrest from Munshiganj, saying initial findings suggest he stabbed Billal. Ramna Thana BNP President Ashraf claimed the killing was “planned murder”. He said, “We took a stand against extortion. A few days ago, the matter was resolved at the MP’s residence. It was decided there that no extortion money would be collected in this area.” BNP sources said Babu is a follower of a central Jubo Dal leader, under whose influence extortion money was collected. Jubo Dal Central Committee Joint Secretary Rabiul Islam Noyon stated, “Babu has been involved in Jubo Dal politics for a long time. However, we were not aware of the extortion. After learning about the incident, we dissolved the committee and expelled Babu.”

title: Violence against women & children: 3 die after fire at house of rape-murder suspect
body: Three people died over the past two days from burn injuries after an alleged arson attack on the house of a man suspected of raping and murdering a teenager in Pabna. The deceased were identified as Sumon Sheikh, 37, of Purbo Raghabpur village, and Saiful Islam Sabbir, 22, and Md Shapu, 19, both of Notunpara village in Sadar upazila. All three were workshop labourers. Pabna Sadar Police Station Officer-in-Charge Tarikul Islam said the three victims died at different times on Monday and early yesterday while undergoing treatment at the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery in Dhaka. Among them, Sumon succumbed to his injuries at around 2:30pm on Monday. His body was taken back to Pabna after an autopsy, and he was buried in his village yesterday afternoon. The bodies of the other two victims had not reached the village from Dhaka by the time this report was filed at around 7:00pm, as legal formalities were still underway. According to police and locals, the body of the teenage girl, stuffed inside a sack, was recovered from the Padma on June 3. A case was filed by the victim’s brother on June 4, naming Naim Pramanik as the prime accused, along with two others. All three accused were arrested, and the victim’s funeral was held the same day. Citing locals, OC Tarikul said that following the funeral, a group of angry locals allegedly set fire to Naim’s house in Purbo Raghabpur village of Sadar upazila. As the fire spread, a container filled with petrol exploded, leaving at least six people with burn injuries -- most of them neighbours and onlookers who had gathered at the scene, police said, adding that no one from the accused family was present when the fire broke out as they had gone into hiding. Badsha Alamgir, a resident of the village and a member of the Bharara Union Parishad, said the six burn victims were initially taken to Pabna General Hospital in critical condition. They were then shifted to the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery in Dhaka for advanced treatment. “Following the rape and murder of the girl, the villagers have now had to witness a series of tragic deaths over the last few days. The village is completely overwhelmed by grief and anxiety. We are working alongside law enforcement agencies to keep the situation under control.” Recalling the series of events, he said, “A young girl was allegedly raped and killed by her cousin near her house. As we were returning home after burying her body, we heard a loud explosion from Naim’s house. We rushed to the spot and found several young men lying on the road with severe burn injuries.” Deceased Sumon’s brother Md Ukil Sheikh yesterday filed a case with Pabna Sadar Police Station against unidentified individuals. In the case statement, he claimed that after some locals set Naim’s house on fire, his brother, along with five to six others, had gone to the spot to help bring the situation under control. Md Shakil, a cousin of deceased Sabbir, and Md Imran, the brother of deceased Shapu, claimed the two had only gone to the scene to watch what happened after the fire broke out. OC Tarikul said an additional police force has been deployed in the village to maintain law and order and prevent further violence, and an investigation into the incident is underway.

title: Violence against women & children: Mother, teenage daughter raped during robbery
body: A woman and her teenage daughter were allegedly raped by armed criminals who broke into their house early yesterday in Cox’s Bazar. The attack reportedly occurred at around 2:30am in an area of the newly formed Matamuhuri upazila. The woman’s husband was in Chattogram for business purposes at the time. The woman’s 5-year-old child was in the house during the attack. Quoting members of the victims’ family, Abhijit Das, assistant superintendent of police for the Chakaria Circle, said a gang of eight to 10 men cut through a window grille, looted gold jewellery and cash, raped the woman and her teenage daughter, and then fled. The teenager’s uncle told journalists that the victims were initially taken to a health complex before being transferred to another hospital as their conditions deteriorated. Contacted, an official of the hospital said the two were admitted to the hospital’s One-Stop Crisis Centre. “After diagnosis and treatment, they were discharged in the afternoon. The girl’s condition was stable.” Six men have been detained so far for interrogation: Rezaul Karim, 36; brothers Tofazzal Hossain alias Babu, 23, and Kefayat Hossain alias Puittya, 27; Mohammad Tanzid, 24; Mehedi Hasan, 24; and Mohammad Tareq, 26. One suspect, identified as Jisan, had been jailed in a case filed over weapon possession and robbery charges and was released just five days before the attack. Abhijit confirmed that an organised local criminal network was responsible and added that police are continuing to search for the remaining suspects. Family members further alleged that the same group had targeted the household on two or three previous occasions. A case had yet to be filed over the incident [by the time this report was filed] at 8:45pm.

title: HC summons judge over delay in rape, murder trial
body: The High Court yesterday summoned a Habiganj court judge to appear on June 23 over her failure to complete the trial of a rape and murder case in the past five years. Judge Syeda Minhaj Um Munira of Habiganj’s Women and Children Repression Prevention Tribunal has been directed to appear before a High Court bench of Justice KM Emrul Kayesh and Justice Md Sagir Hossain to explain the delay in completing the trial of the case. The bench, in a suo motu move, issued the order while hearing a bail petition filed by Golam Hossain, a jailed accused in the rape and murder case, Deputy Attorney General Md Mohsin Kabir Rocky told The Daily Star. He said the HC bench, while examining the case documents, noted that the trial of the case, filed in December 2021, remains unconcluded despite five years having passed. “The case was filed with Nabiganj Police Station on December 28, 2021, after a 17-year-old girl was raped and murdered between December 26 and 27 that year,” the DAG said, adding that the victim’s father filed the case against Khalil Uddin and Md Golam Hossain, who are now in jail. Contacted, accused Hossain’s lawyer Md Abdur Razzak said, “The HC issued the summons order as the Habiganj tribunal is yet to finish trial of the case though the charges were framed around four years ago.” Mohsin further said the trial proceedings of a rape and murder case are supposed to be completed within 180 days after charges are framed by the trial court concerned. The bench observed that the failure to conclude rape-and-murder trials within the prescribed timeframe contributes to the continued occurrence of incidents similar to the rape and murder of eight-year-old Ramisa, he said. Advocate Md Abdur Razzak appeared for accused petitioner Golam Hossain during the hearing of his bail petition yesterday. The court also fixed June 23 for the next hearing on Hossain’s bail petition.

title: Bullet-hit body recovered from floating speedboat in Padma river
body: Police recovered the bullet-hit body of a man from a speedboat floating at Charjajira point of the Padma river in Lalpur upazila of Natore this afternoon. The victim, Azizul Haque Jhoru, 35, was of Pabnapara village in Bagatipara upazila of the district, said police. Jhoru worked at a sand quarry operated by the "Kakon gang" in the Charghat area of Rajshahi, police added. Md Shafiqul Islam, officer-in-charge of Laxmikunda River Police Camp, said a river police team spotted the body inside the speedboat around 3:30pm. The body was recovered and sent to Natore General Hospital morgue for autopsy. According to police, there had been a longstanding rivalry between the "Belal gang" and the "Kakon gang" over control of a sand quarry in the Padma river. A gunfight reportedly broke out between the two gangs at Habir Char, a riverine border area between Daulatpur in Kushtia and Bagha in Rajshahi, centring the dispute. Police suspect that Jhoru may have been killed during the gunfight and his body was later transported by speedboat to the Lalpur area. Law enforcers are investigating the incident, the OC added.

title: Extortion row behind killing of former Swechchhasebak Dal leader: Police
body: Former Swechchhasebak Dal leader Billal Talukdar was killed over the collection of waste and electricity bills from shops adjacent to Anarkali Market in Dhaka's Mouchak, police and party insiders confirmed. According to police, followers of Ramna Thana Jubo Dal leader Riazul Islam Babu had been regularly collecting electricity bills from several shops near the market’s main building -- a practice opposed by Thana BNP President Ashraf and his supporters, including Billal. A meeting was convened on Monday to resolve the dispute, but during the arbitration, Babu’s followers stabbed Billal following an altercation, said Officer-in-Charge of Rampura Police Station, Mohammad Rahat Khan. Police reported that the conflict began when Billal’s nephew, a shop owner, objected to outsiders collecting electricity bills. A meeting was called in the evening, during which Billal was reportedly stabbed. Immediately after the incident, the Jubo Dal committee was dissolved and Babu’s follower Riazul was expelled. Two people, including ward-19 Jubo Dal Convener Al Amin and Riazul, were arrested in connection with the killing. Billal’s widow, Ambia Khatun, has since filed a murder case naming 21 individuals and accusing 27 unidentified others.
