During a visit to Anarkali Market today, posters of Riazul were still visible on the market walls, though shopkeepers were reluctant to discuss the murder. Local sources and eyewitnesses said disputes between Jubo Dal and Swechchhasebak Dal leaders over control of footpaths and alleged extortion in Anarkali Market and Mouchak area had been ongoing. A week earlier, an arbitration meeting was held to settle the matter, where it was decided that no extortion money would be collected. On the day of the incident, Siraj and Riazul were reportedly collecting money from footpath shops when Billal’s nephew protested and was beaten. A senior official of the DMP’s Ramna Division confirmed Riazul’s arrest from Munshiganj, saying initial findings suggest he stabbed Billal. Ramna Thana BNP President Ashraf claimed the killing was “planned murder.” He said, “We took a stand against extortion. A few days ago, the matter was resolved at the MP’s residence. It was decided there that no extortion money would be collected in this area.” BNP sources said Babu is a follower of a central Jubo Dal leader, under whose influence extortion money was collected. Jubo Dal Central Committee Joint Secretary Rabiul Islam Noyon stated, “Babu has been involved in Jubo Dal politics for a long time. However, we were not aware of the extortion. After learning about the incident, we dissolved the committee and expelled Babu.”

title: Bagerhat youth sent to jail over social media post using Zaima Rahman’s photo
body: A Bagerhat court today sent a 24-year-old man to jail for allegedly making an offensive social media post using a photo of Zaima Rahman, daughter of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman. The youth, Sheikh Rasul alias Rafiqul, is from Gopalpur village in Kachua upazila. Police arrested him from the upazila's Badhal area on Monday night in a case filed by local resident Abdus Salam, under the Special Powers Act, said Kachua Police Station Officer-in-Charge Shafiqul Islam. Rafiqul was produced before Bagerhat Cognisance Court-9 this noon, which sent him to jail, said Court Inspector Md Mujibur Rahman The OC said Rafiqul had recently uploaded an offensive post with Zaima Rahman's photo from his personal social media account.

title: Chattogram court orders crackdown on ambulance syndicates
body: A Chattogram court today ordered police to identify the ringleaders of "ambulance syndicates" at Chattogram Medical College Hospital (CMCH) and take legal action against those involved in fare irregularities and holding patients hostage during emergencies. Chief Metropolitan Magistrate AGM Monirul Islam issued the order after taking reports from online news portals into cognisance. The magistrate also directed the Additional Deputy Commissioner (North Zone) of Chattogram Metropolitan Police to investigate the matter and submit a report within seven working days. The written order stated that the directive was passed in the public interest to restore law and order and ensure a proper healthcare environment around CMCH. The order came a day after ambulance fares in Chattogram were raised by 30 percent at a consultation meeting held at CMCH. The meeting was attended by Chattogram city Mayor Shahadat Hossain, leaders of the Chattogram Ambulance Owners Cooperative Society, representatives of CMP, and presided over by CMCH Director Md Taslim Uddin. Earlier, reports had highlighted the suffering of patients due to alleged syndicate control over ambulance services. A scuffle also broke out on Sunday between members of the Bangladesh Ambulance Owners Welfare Association and activists of the National Citizen Party (NCP) over allegations of overcharging. In the order, the magistrate asked police to identify illegal syndicate leaders, extortionists, attackers, and fake ambulance owners. If allegations are proven, the officer-in-charge of Panchlaish Police Station has been directed to file a case under relevant laws. The order further instructed police and hospital authorities to ensure that patients and relatives of the deceased can freely choose ambulances or freezing vans without syndicate interference. The court also directed that fare charts be displayed prominently at CMCH’s emergency department, mortuary, outpatient department, and ambulance parking -- either physically or digitally. It recommended setting up a complaint booth or 24-hour helpline for fare-related grievances and suggested establishing a permanent police guard post to prevent extortion around the hospital.

title: 3 sent to jail over banned Chhatra League procession in Jhenaidah
body: A Jhenaidah court today sent three individuals to jail in a case filed under the Anti-Terrorism Act, following a procession allegedly brought out by activists of the banned Bangladesh Chhatra League in Jhenaidah town early Monday. The accused who were sent to jail are Jhenaidah district Jubo League member Mehedi Hasan Sohel, 35, Chhatra League activist Niloy Farhan Dighal, 20, and Ashik, 22, said Md Asaduzzaman, officer-in-charge of the police station. They were arrested from different parts of the district on Monday night after Rajib Ali, a sub-inspector of Jhenaidah Sadar Police Station, filed the case against 24 local leaders and activists of Chhatra League and Jubo League in connection with the procession, said the OC. Jhenaidah district Chhatra League President Sajib Hossain and General Secretary Al Emran are among the accused. The case also names 10 to 15 unidentified individuals, the OC said. The three arrestees were produced before a court today, which sent them to jail, he added. Police drives are continuing to arrest the remaining accused, said the OC.

title: 48 sued over killing of Swechchhasebak Dal leader in Mouchak
body: A murder case has been filed against 48 people over the killing of former Swechchhasebak Dal leader Billal Hossain Talukder, who was stabbed to death during an arbitration meeting in the capital's Mouchak area last night. The victim's wife, Ambia Khatun, filed the case with Ramna Police Station, accusing 21 named and 27 unidentified individuals, Mohammad Rahat Khan, officer-in-charge (OC) of the police station, told The Daily Star. Police have already arrested two of the accused, said the OC, adding that efforts are underway to arrest the remaining suspects. A woman who identified herself as a relative of the victim said over phone that the family is on its way home with Billal's body. "They are not in a position to talk about the matter right now," she said. Billal, 57, a former convener of Ramna thana Swechchhasebak Dal, was attacked around 8:00pm on Monday in front of Anarkali Market in Mouchak and later died from his injuries.

title: HC summons Habiganj judge for failing to complete rape-murder trial in 5 years
body: The High Court today summoned a Habiganj court judge for failing to complete the trial proceedings in a rape and murder case over the past five years. Judge Syeda Minhaj Um Munira of Habiganj’s Women and Children Repression Prevention Tribunal has been directed to appear before the High Court bench of Justice KM Emrul Kayesh and Justice Md Sagir Hossain on June 23 to explain the delay in the trial. The bench also observed that the failure to conclude the trial within the prescribed timeframe contributes to the continued occurrence of incidents similar to Ramisa rape and murder, he said. The victim’s father filed the case against Khalil Uddin and Md Golam Hossain, who are now in jail. Trial proceedings of the case are supposed to be completed in 180 days after its charges are framed by the trial court concerned, DAG Mohsin added. Advocate Md Abdur Razzak appeared for accused petitioner Golam Hossain during the hearing of his bail petition today.

title: HC questions lack of elderly care system after woman's body found in Mirpur flat
body: The High Court today issued a rule asking why the social welfare secretary should not be directed to appoint, train and deploy caregivers or nurses for elderly and infirm citizens aged 65 and above as part of a social security initiative under the Department of Social Services. The court also asked the authorities concerned to explain why the National Human Rights Commission had not conducted an inquiry into whether the human rights of 75-year-old Nurjahan Begum, whose decomposed body was recovered from her Mirpur residence in Dhaka on May 31, had been violated. The High Court further asked the law secretary to explain why he should not be directed to constitute a three-member committee, to be led by a judicial officer, to conduct an inquiry into the cause of her death. The bench of Justice Fatema Najib and Justice AFM Saiful Karim passed the order after hearing a writ petition seeking necessary directives to this effect. Barrister Shanjid Siddique argued for the petitioner while Deputy Attorney General Abdul Wahhab represented the state. Advocate Mohammad Sharif Sarker, a lawyer of the Dhaka court, submitted the writ petition as a public interest litigation on June 3. He stated in the petition that the death of the 75-year-old woman in her flat, where her decomposed body was discovered in highly unsanitary conditions days later, amounted to a serious violation of her fundamental right to life before her death, as guaranteed under Article 32 of the Constitution.

title: Chandpur man sent to jail over alleged assault, neglect of elderly mother
body: A Chandpur court today sent a man to jail on charges of failing to support his mother and physically assaulting her in Shahrasti upazila. The accused, Abu Yusuf Patwari, 35, is son of late Hafiz Ahmad Patwari and Shefali Begum of Cheriara village in the upazila, said Mir Mahbubur Rahman, officer-in-charge of Shahrasti Model Police Station. A police team arrested Yusuf after his sister Rokeya Begum filed a case with Shahrasti Model Police Station on Monday under Section 5 of the Parents' Maintenance Act, 2013, said Mohammad Abdul Quddus Sarkar, a sub-inspector of the police station. He was produced before a court today, which sent him to jail, the police official added. According to the case statement, Yusuf had misbehaved with his elderly mother on several occasions. On June 2, he allegedly assaulted her, leaving her seriously injured. OC Mahbubur said the case serves as an example of the enforcement of the Parents' Maintenance Act. "It is the responsibility of the offspring to take care of their parents. Legal action has been taken based on the complaint," he said. Recently, the government has withdrawn AKM Anisur Rahman, member (joint secretary) of the Mongla Port Authority, and attached him to the Ministry of Public Administration following the death of his elderly mother at a flat in Dhaka’s Mirpur, an incident that has sparked widespread discussion and allegations of neglect.

title: Mother, teenage daughter allegedly gang-raped during robbery at home in Cox’s Bazar
body: A 40-year-old mother and her 15-year-old daughter were allegedly gang-raped by armed criminals who broke into their home early today in Cox's Bazar. title: Ramisa rape, murder: Death reference sent to Supreme Court
body: The death reference of the case filed over the rape and murder of eight-year-old Ramisa was sent to the Supreme Court today. “We have sent a three-page death reference, a 69-page judgement and other relevant documents of the case to the office of the registrar general of the Supreme Court this afternoon,” Pankoj Peter Gomes, bench assistant of the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal in Dhaka Metropolitan, told The Daily Star. According to legal experts, a death reference is a mandatory judicial process through which a trial court's death sentence is sent to the higher court for confirmation before it can be carried out. On June 7, tribunal judge Masrur Salekin sentenced prime accused Sohel Rana to death for raping and murdering Ramisa, and his wife, Swapna Khatun, to death for assisting him in committing the crime. The judgement came 19 days after the horrific incident in Dhaka’s Pallabi area that set off a fierce wave of public outrage, prompting the government to pledge swift justice. Law Minister Md Asaduzzaman said this was the fastest trial in Bangladesh. In addition to the death penalty, Sohel was fined Tk 5 lakh, while Swapna was fined Tk 2 lakh. The tribunal ordered the fines be paid to the victim’s “legal heirs”. If the convicts fail to pay the fines, the district collectors will recover the amount by auctioning off the convicts’ movable and/or immovable properties and pay it to the victim’s family, said the court. Ramisa, a class 2 student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 in the house of her neighbour, Sohel. The following day, Ramisa's father Abdul Hannan Mollah filed a case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing the couple and an unidentified person. According to the case statement, Sohel called Ramisa into his room and raped her. Investigators said he later slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body to conceal the crime. On May 24, investigator Ohiduzzaman, Sub-Inspector of Pallabi Police Station, submitted the charge sheet before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate's (CMM) Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel and Swapna. Several hours later, the CMM Court transferred the case to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal for trial. On June 1, the tribunal framed charges against the accused. The following day, the tribunal completed testimony. A total of 16 prosecution witnesses, including the victim’s parents and elder sister, three neighbours, a doctor, a Dhaka metropolitan magistrate and the investigator, gave their statements before the tribunal.

title: Three die after arson attack on homes of rape-murder accused in Pabna
body: Three people have died from burn injuries sustained when houses belonging to people accused in the rape and murder of a teenage girl were attacked in Pabna on June 4. The deceased were identified as Sumon Sheikh of Purbo Raghabpur village, and Saiful Islam Sabbir and Md Sapu of Natunpara village. The three deceased's role in the rape and murder could not be independently verified by this correspondent. Pabna Sadar Police Station Officer-in-Charge Tarikul Islam said the three died at different times yesterday and early today while undergoing treatment at the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery in Dhaka. Police and local sources said the body of a teenage girl was recovered from the Padma river on June 3. The body was found stuffed inside a sack. Following her funeral the next day, angry locals allegedly set fire to the houses of those accused in the rape and murder. During the arson attack, a petrol container reportedly exploded, leaving several people injured. Police said no members of the accused families were present in the houses when the fire broke out.

title: Former banker held over misuse of customer's returned credit card
body: The Criminal Investigation Department (CID) of police has arrested a former bank official for allegedly using a customer's returned credit card for nine years and making transactions worth more than Tk 17 lakh. The arrestee, Sarwar Hossain, 40, was detained from the Dhaka’s Gulshan area yesterday afternoon, according to a CID press release issued today. CID said the fraud began in 2017 when a customer applied for a credit card but later decided to return it. Sarwar, who was then working as a senior relationship officer in retail banking card sales, allegedly kept the card instead of submitting it to the bank. He reportedly changed the customer's contact information by adding a fake mobile number and address, enabling him to receive one-time passwords (OTPs) and use the card for transactions. According to CID, Sarwar continued using the card even after leaving the bank in 2019. However, it did not disclose the name of the bank where he had worked. The fraud came to light when the customer checked his Credit Information Bureau (CIB) report, found an outstanding loan in his name, and filed a complaint with Bangladesh Bank. Following an internal investigation, the bank uncovered the irregularities and filed a case with Tejgaon Industrial Area Police Station on April 15. CID said Sarwar made transactions exceeding Tk 17 lakh through the card. Although he repaid Tk 14,13,500 over the years, an outstanding amount of Tk 5,56,995, including interest, remained unpaid. He has been accused of embezzling the outstanding amount. CID said the process of producing him before a court is underway.

title: Appellate Division stays HC verdict on SC secretariat
body: The Appellate Division of the Supreme Court today stayed a High Court verdict that directed the government to establish an independent secretariat for the Supreme Court. The apex court also fixed June 16 for hearing an appeal filed by the state challenging the HC judgment. A full bench of the Appellate Division, headed by Chief Justice Zubayer Rahman Chowdhury, passed the order following a petition filed by the state seeking a stay on the HC verdict. Attorney General Md Ruhul Quddus Kazal, Additional Attorneys General Md Abdul Jabbar Bhuiyan, Md Arshadur Rouf and Aneek R Haque appeared for the state, while senior lawyer Mohammad Shishir Manir represented the writ petitioner. On May 21, the Attorney General’s Office filed the appeal on behalf of the state, challenging the HC judgment. In the appeal, the state argued that the HC erred in declaring Article 116 of the Constitution unconstitutional while leaving Article 115 intact. Article 116 vests the powers of control and discipline of lower court judges in the president, while Article 115 authorises the president to appoint members of the subordinate judiciary. The state further argued that Article 116 contains an important system of checks and balances by requiring the president to act in consultation with the Supreme Court, thereby ensuring meaningful judicial participation in administrative matters concerning the subordinate judiciary. Following a writ petition, the High Court delivered its verdict on September 2 last year, scrapping Article 116 of the Constitution. The HC also directed the government to establish a Supreme Court secretariat within three months and ruled that the authority over the transfer, posting and discipline of lower court judges would rest with the Supreme Court rather than the president. The full text of the verdict was released on April 7. A day later, Attorney General Ruhul Quddus Kazal told reporters that the HC judgment would not take effect until the Appellate Division finally disposed of the planned appeal. After the interim government issued the Supreme Court Secretariat Ordinance, 2025 on November 30 last year, then Chief Justice Syed Refaat Ahmed inaugurated the Supreme Court Secretariat in early December, aiming to bring the judiciary fully under the Supreme Court and strengthen its independence. On May 19, the Law Ministry issued a gazette notification stating that 15 judges serving as officials of the abolished SC Secretariat had been attached to the ministry, in consultation with the Supreme Court, pending reassignment to other offices. The notification gave retrospective effect to their transfer, making the orders effective from April 10.

title: 2 arrested over killing of Swechchhasebak Dal leader in Mouchak
body: Police have arrested two individuals, including a local Jubo Dal leader, in connection with the killing of Swechchhasebak Dal leader Billal Hossain Talukdar, who was stabbed to death during an arbitration meeting in Dhaka’s Mouchak area last night. The arrestees were identified as Al Amin, convener of Ward No 19 Jubo Dal, and Riaz. Confirming the development, Sheikh Jahidul Islam, deputy commissioner (Ramna Division) of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police, told The Daily Star that Al Amin was arrested in Dhaka, while the other was detained in Munshiganj. Billal, 57, a former convener of Ramna thana Swechchhasebak Dal, was attacked around 8:00pm in front of Anarkali Market in Mouchak and later died from his injuries. According to the deceased's nephew, Md Mobarak Hossain Akash, an arbitration meeting was arranged after he was assaulted by several individuals near Anarkali Market earlier in the evening. During the meeting, Billal became involved in an argument with Didarul Islam Babu, convener of Ramna thana Jubo Dal, and Lutfor, the unit's secretary, Akash alleged. At one stage, Billal was stabbed in the chest by Babu's followers, allegedly acting under his directions. Following the incident, Jubo Dal expelled Babu and dissolved its Ramna thana committee, according to a press release issued by the BNP's youth wing.

title: Man hacked to death for 'protesting harassment of granddaughter'
body: An elderly man was hacked to death in Jashore's Monirampur upazila following a dispute linked to the alleged harassment of his granddaughter, according to a murder case filed in connection with the incident. The incident took place around 10:00pm yesterday in Sharmapur village under Rohita union. The deceased was identified as Imamul Hossain, 65, of Farasatpur village in Jhikargachha upazila. According to the case statement, Imamul's granddaughter had been subjected to repeated harassment by a local youth for some time. The issue reportedly led to a dispute a day earlier between Imamul and several local residents. The case alleges that the accused attacked Imamul with sharp weapons and sticks last night over the dispute, leaving him critically injured. He was rushed to Jashore General Hospital, where the on-duty physician declared him dead. Monirampur Police Station Officer-in-Charge Raziullah Khan confirmed the incident and said the body would undergo an autopsy. He said a murder case was filed by the victim’s family this morning against six individuals in connection with the killing. "An accused named Hossain has been detained in connection with the murder case. During primary interrogation, he confessed involvement in the murder," the OC said. "Legal proceedings are underway, and police have intensified efforts to arrest the remaining accused," he added.

title: Two killed in separate incidents in Pabna
body: A man was shot dead and a college student was stabbed to death in separate incidents in Pabna town yesterday. The deceased were identified as Hossain Ali, 55, of Jafrabad village in Pabna Sadar upazila, and Monirul Islam, 22, a college student from Shibrampur Paschimpara village in Santhia upazila, said Tariqul Islam, officer-in-charge (OC) of Pabna Sadar Police Station. Quoting locals, the OC said Hossain had come to Pabna Jamia Ashrafia Madrasa in the district town to admit his son. When he reached the madrasa area around 7:30pm, several assailants opened fire on him in front of his son, leaving him dead on the spot, the OC said, adding that a case has been filed against one named accused and three to four unidentified individuals. Police have yet to determine the motive behind the killing. However, they have learned that the deceased allegedly had links to outlawed groups, the OC added. In a separate incident, Monirul was stabbed behind the Pabna Central Bus Terminal at around 4:30pm following an altercation. The OC said an argument broke out between Monirul and another youth, identified as Rakib. At one stage of the altercation, Rakib allegedly stabbed Monirul with a sharp weapon. Rakib jumped into a nearby pond in an attempt to escape but was detained by police at the scene, he added. Locals rescued Monirul and took him to Pabna General Hospital. As his condition worsened, he was referred to Rajshahi Medical College Hospital, but died on the way. Police recovered both bodies and sent them to the morgue at Pabna General Hospital for autopsies today, the OC said.

title: 11 injured in clash over 'shortage of beef servings' at Faridpur wedding
body: At least 11 people were injured in a clash between the bride's family and some of their invited guests over allegations that too little beef had been served at a wedding feast in Faridpur's Bhanga upazila. The incident took place yesterday afternoon in Deora Nayakandi village under Kalamridha union. Four of the injured were admitted to Bhanga Upazila Health Complex. Confirming the incident, Bhanga Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Md Mizanur Rahman said a clash broke out between members of the bride's family and local residents after some invited guests complained that they had been served less meat than expected. "Four injured persons received treatment at Bhanga Upazila Health Complex. Police rushed to the scene after receiving information and brought the situation under control," he said. According to local residents, the wedding ceremony of Lovlu Sheikh's daughter was underway when several invited villagers complained that they had been served an insufficient amount of beef during the meal. An argument soon broke out and later escalated into a violent clash. Witnesses said both sides hurled bricks and used sticks during the altercation, leaving several people injured. Among those admitted to the health complex were Arif Mia, Shahid Matubbar, Sohrab Matubbar and Momtaz Begum. The remaining injured received primary treatment locally. Kalamridha Union Parishad Chairman Rezaul Matubbar said the clash stemmed from complaints over the amount of meat served, although underlying local rivalries also contributed to the violence. "There was no dispute between the bride's and groom's families," he said. "Those involved in the clash were local villagers who had been invited by the bride's family. Despite the incident, the groom and his relatives later arrived at the bride's house, and the wedding was completed without any further disruption." The bride's father, Lovlu Sheikh, said what was meant to be a joyous occasion for his family turned into a distressing experience because of local factional disputes. "We invited people from the village to the ceremony. They did not create trouble merely over the meat issue; rather, they deliberately tried to disrupt my daughter's wedding programme," he alleged. The OC said the situation in the area was now normal and that no written complaint had been filed with the police as of today.

title: Swechchhasebak Dal man stabbed to death in city
body: A Swechchhasebak Dal leader was stabbed to death during an arbitration in the capital’s Mouchak area last night. The deceased was identified as Billal Hossain Talukdar, 57, former convener of Ramna thana Swechchhasebak Dal. He lived in the Malibagh Baganbari area and ran a sand and cement business in the area, police said. “The victim had a stab wound on his chest. Ramna Police Station has been informed of the incident,” said Inspector Md Faruk, in-charge of the Dhaka Medical College Hospital police outpost. He said the body had been kept at the hospital morgue for an autopsy. The incident took place around 8:00pm in front of Anarkali Market in Mouchak. According to the deceased’s nephew, Md Mobarak Hossain Akash, he was assaulted by several individuals near Anarkali Market earlier in the evening. Following the attack, he called his uncle, Billal, to help resolve the dispute. An arbitration was subsequently held at the spot. During the meeting, Billal got into an argument with Didarul Islam Babu, convener of Ramna thana Jubo Dal, and Lutfor, the unit’s secretary, Akash alleged. At one stage, Billal was stabbed in the chest by Babu’s followers, allegedly acting under his directions, Akash said. Critically injured, Billal was taken to DMCH, where doctors declared him dead around 9:15pm. Assistant Commissioner of Police (Ramna Zone) Majharul Islam told The Daily Star that police have already visited the scene and launched an investigation. “We are collecting CCTV footage from the surrounding areas and examining the evidence to identify those involved,” he said. Meanwhile, Jubo Dal expelled Babu and dissolved its Ramna thana committee, according to a press release issued by the ruling BNP’s youth wing following the incident.

title: Biker tries to save child ‘he hit’; both die
body: Akhi Khatun and her eight-year-old son Alif Hossain were on their way home from Pabna’s Pakshi upazila on Sunday. What was supposed to be just a journey back home ended in tragedy when a motorcycle hit their three-wheeler on the Pabna-Kushtia highway in Ishwardi upazila. On impact, the child slipped from his mother’s lap and fell onto the road. His mother, Akhi, and Baki Billah, 35, the motorcyclist whose bike struck the three-wheeler, rushed to rescue him. Just then, a speeding truck ran over all three. Alif and Baki died on the spot. Akhi survived with injuries. Contacted by The Daily Star yesterday, Pakshi Highway Police Station’s Officer-in-Charge Md Nannu Khan narrated the incident, citing eyewitnesses. “The accident occurred in Koloikandi Bottola area around 9:00pm.... Upon receiving the information, police and firefighters rushed to the spot, recovered the bodies, rescued the injured mother, and sent her to Ishwardi Upazila Health Complex.” He added that the truck driver fled the scene with the vehicle and that police are conducting drives to seize the truck and arrest the driver. “The child’s father, Jahid Hossain, is preparing to file a case in this regard.” Meanwhile, Akhi is expected to return home today, according to the OC.

title: 32 killed in major quake off Philippines
body: The death toll in a powerful 7.8 magnitude earthquake off the southern Philippine island of Mindanao yesterday has risen to at least 32 with dozens of people injured, disaster officials said, as Manila stepped up search and rescue operations. The quake, which triggered tsunami warnings across several countries, hit early in the morning about 20 km (12.4 miles) off Sarangani province, with the tremors felt strongly across Mindanao and 420 km (261 miles) away in the city of Manado on the Indonesian island of Sulawesi. The Philippines mobilised military and disaster response teams and authorities were verifying preliminary reports of 32 people killed and 134 injured across Mindanao, mostly from falling debris and landslides, according to civil defence officials. Tsunami warnings were cancelled after more than six hours in the southern Philippines, northern Indonesia and the Malaysian state of Sabah on Borneo island, where residents in coastal areas had been told to evacuate immediately to higher ground. The Philippine seismology agency said there were more than 200 aftershocks, at least nine of those strong and felt across Mindanao, the highest at a magnitude 6.7. President Ferdinand Marcos Jr ordered an immediate disaster response in Mindanao, an island the size of South Korea, with agencies directed to prepare relief supplies and evacuation centres and be ready for possible rescue operations. “The national government is moving and we will not leave Mindanao behind,” Marcos said in a statement. The Philippines and Indonesia experience hundreds of quakes each year and sit on tectonically complex parts of the “Pacific Ring of Fire”, a seismically active belt stretching from South America to the Russian Far East. Damage to buildings, utilities and infrastructure was still being assessed, but the worst affected area was General Santos, a city of about 700,000 people, where shops and buildings were damaged, some with broken signs and glass, others reduced to piles of concrete and rubble. Video shared by the local government showed the collapse of a building housing a fastfood restaurant, with panicked onlookers fleeing as a cloud of dust spread quickly through the air. One General Santos hospital was evacuated due to concerns about cracks on higher floors. One of the buildings at the city’s Notre Dame of Dadiangas University collapsed, but no one was inside. “I had to duck and shelter myself under the table. And it was very long and strong,” the university’s president Manuel de Leon told broadcaster DZMM. The quake struck just as schools were returning from a long break. A video shared by one school the moment the quake struck showed a large group of children sitting on the floor swaying rapidly from side to side, some hugging teachers, before fleeing en masse as a makeshift shelter collapsed behind them. Benjie Ancheta, police chief of Sarangani’s Alabel town, said the quake occurred during a police flag-raising ceremony, causing some people to faint. “This is the strongest earthquake we’ve experienced,” Ancheta said by phone.

title: Tonu murder case: Seek Interpol’s help to arrest two suspects
body: A Cumilla court yesterday ordered authorities to take necessary legal steps, including seeking Interpol assistance, to trace and arrest two absconding suspects in the murder case of Sohagi Jahan Tonu. The court also issued arrest warrants against the two suspects and directed investigators to collect the investigation and inquiry report prepared by the Bangladesh Army, along with records and documents relevant to the case. Senior Judicial Magistrate Mominul Haque of the Cumilla Sadar Court passed the order. The development was confirmed by PBI Dhaka Inspector Tarikul Islam, the investigating officer in the case. According to court sources, the IO had earlier filed a petition seeking Interpol cooperation, including the issuance of Red Notices, against former sergeant Md Zahiduzzaman, 48, and former soldier Md Shahin Alam, 37, both of whom were stationed at Cumilla Cantonment at the time of the killing. Zahid, from the Garghata area of Morelganj in Bagerhat, was serving with the 12 Engineer Battalion at Cumilla Cantonment at the time. From the outset, Tonu’s family alleged that he led the brutal assault and murder. He has since been retired from service. The other accused, Shahin Alam, from Gobindapur village under Pirjatrapur union in Cumilla’s Burichang upazila, was serving with the 2 Signal Battalion at Cumilla Cantonment at the time. A source said Shahin is currently abroad. He has since retired from the army or been retired from service, according to a Prothom Alo report. In a separate petition submitted yesterday, investigator Tarikul said, “Since the case was initially treated as a murder with no identified leads, the army’s findings may provide important evidentiary support.” He further informed the court that the two suspects had left the country during the course of the investigation and were allegedly evading legal proceedings. “Evidence collected so far has established reasonable grounds to suspect their involvement in the killing, and their presence is required to verify information that has emerged during the investigation.” Yesterday was the scheduled date for submission of the investigation report in the case. Meanwhile, the investigating officer said evidence collected from samples found on Tonu’s clothing indicates the involvement of another individual. DNA testing has now identified samples from four people on her clothing -- semen from three, and blood from one. While information regarding the semen samples of three individuals had previously surfaced, the newly identified person’s blood sample has now been matched to Tonu’s clothing. Former senior warrant officer Hafizur Rahman, who was arrested in connection with the case, was produced before the Senior Judicial Magistrate’s Court in Cumilla around 11:00am yesterday. No bail petition was filed on his behalf, and the court subsequently ordered that he be sent to jail. Hafizur, 52, retired from the army or was retired from service in 2023. He was arrested from his house in Dhaka’s Keraniganj on April 21. At the time of Tonu’s murder, he was also serving at Cumilla Cantonment. On the evening of March 20, 2016, Tonu, a student of Comilla Victoria Government College, went to suspect Zahid’s house inside Cumilla Cantonment to give private tuition to his children and never returned home. After a search, her body was found in bushes near the cantonment’s power house. (Our Cumilla correspondent contributed to this report.)

title: Mob beats man accused of molesting girl in Rajshahi
body: A man was beaten by a mob over allegations of molesting a nine-year-old girl in Rajshahi’s Paba upazila on Monday. Police went to the spot, rescued and detained the accused, Matin Ali, 45, a van driver of Duari area in Nowhata, and admitted him to Rajshahi Medical College Hospital. The incident took place on the highway in the Nowhata area on Monday afternoon, said police. Paba Police Station Officer-in-Charge Abdul Hamid said the 9-year-old girl, from Modonhati village, boarded a van driven by Matin Ali while returning home. During the journey, the van driver touched the child inappropriately. The child protested, but he allegedly repeated the behaviour several times on the way to Modonhati, police said. After returning home, the child informed her family members about the incident. As the news of the incident spread, enraged locals caught the van driver and beat him up. On information, police went to the scene, took the accused into custody. Police also spoke with the victim and her family members. The OC said the child’s father filed a case under the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act, 2000. Necessary legal steps are being taken in connection with the incident, he added.
