title: Paper-book prepared for Magura’s Asiya rape and murder case
body: The government has prepared the paper-book for the much-discussed Asiya rape and murder case, paving the way for its final adjudication. A paper-book, which contains lower court judgments, orders, statements, and evidence, is required for the High Court to hear and dispose of a death reference and relevant appeals. An official at the Supreme Court Registrar General’s office told The Daily Star that the paper-book has been printed at the Bangladesh Government Press and reached the High Court today. It will now be placed before the designated bench for hearing. On May 17 last year, a Magura tribunal sentenced the perpetrator, Hitu Sheikh, to death for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old. The verdict came within 70 days of the case being filed, with the trial completed in 11 working days. The death reference reached the High Court on May 20 last year, and Hitu Sheikh later filed an appeal challenging the judgment. Attorney General Barrister Ruhul Quddus Kazal said on June 7 that Chief Justice Zubayer Rahman Chowdhury will constitute a specific High Court bench to hear cases involving violence against women and children, which will begin functioning next Sunday.

title: Police yet to identify shooters in Motijheel $17,000 robbery
body: Police are yet to identify the assailants 24 hours after a foreign currency trader was shot and robbed of around $17,000 in broad daylight in Motijheel. The victim, Mohammad Lokman, 45, was attacked in front of Janata Bank on Sunday afternoon. He is currently receiving treatment at Mugda Medical College and Hospital. Harun ur Rashid, deputy commissioner of the DMP’s Motijheel division, said officers visited the spot immediately after the incident and collected CCTV footage. “We are launching a combined investigation with DB and CTTC,” he said, adding that progress has been made but was not yet ready to be shared. No case has been filed so far. DC Harun said police contacted the family, but they prefer to wait until Lokman recovers. Rakib, the victim’s son-in-law and assistant, told The Daily Star that Lokman is out of danger but doctors have instructed him not to speak. “When the doctors allow him to talk, we will file the case based on his account of the incident,” he said. Recalling the events, Rakib said Lokman had gone to the Adamjee Court Building before heading towards Bangladesh Bank, where his younger brother was waiting. Rakib mentioned that Lokman had long been involved in forex trading, with his brother also engaged in the same business.

title: Man arrested over alleged sexual abuse of child in Munshiganj
body: Police have arrested a man on allegations of sexually abusing a five-year-old girl in Munshiganj’s Gajaria upazila. The arrestee was identified as Manju Mia, 32, of Karimkha village under Imampur union in the upazila. He currently resides with his family in Siddhirganj area of Narayanganj, said Gajaria Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Hasan Ali. The incident took place today at around 10:00am. Following the incident, an agitated mob beat the accused and handed him over to the police. According to police and local sources, the child was standing in front of a tube-well in the courtyard of their house around 10:00am. At that time, Manju approached the child on the pretext of drinking water while passing by. At one point, he grabbed the child and sexually abused her. Seeing the incident from a distance, the child's mother started screaming, prompting locals to rush to the spot and catch Manju red-handed. The agitated mob then beat him up, detained him, and informed the police. Upon receiving the information, a team from Gajaria Police Station reached the spot, rescued the accused, and took him to the police station. The victim's father filed a case under the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act at Gazaria Police Station as the plaintiff. The OC said the accused was shown arrested after a case was filed based on the written complaint of the child's father. “As the accused was injured in the mob beating, he was initially treated at the upazila health complex under police custody. Later, he was sent to the court," he added.

title: Husband attempts suicide after killing wife in Jashore, police suspect
body: A man "attempted" to take his own life after allegedly killing his wife at their rented house in Jashore town early today. The deceased was identified as Shamina Akter Sammy, 20, from Torof Nawapara in Jashore Sadar upazila. The incident occurred around 6:30am in the Tamaltala area of Shekhhati. Police and family members said Sammy’s husband, Sujon, 22, allegedly attacked her with a sharp weapon following an argument. Neighbours rushed to the scene after hearing her screams and took her to Jashore General Hospital, where doctors declared her dead. Dr Sakirul Islam, duty doctor at the hospital’s emergency department, said the victim had died from excessive bleeding before reaching the hospital. After the attack, Sujon allegedly stabbed himself in an apparent suicide attempt. He is currently undergoing treatment at Jashore General Hospital under police custody. Family members alleged that Sujon was addicted to drugs and frequently abused Sammy while demanding money. Inspector (Investigation) Kazi Babul of Jashore Kotwali Police Station said police were investigating the incident. “The body has been sent to the morgue for autopsy, and preparations are underway to file a murder case. Strict legal action will be taken against the accused,” he said. Police also picked up Sujon’s parents for preliminary questioning.

title: Suspected thief beaten to death in Manikganj
body: A man was killed in a mass beating after being caught on suspicion of theft in Bandail Zianagar area of Singair upazila in Manikganj early today. The deceased was identified as Md Razib, 40, of Dhaka's Nawabganj upazila. Quoting locals, Singair Police Station Officer-in-Charge Md Mazharul Islam said a group of seven to eight people carrying locally made weapons entered Hakim Ali’s house after cutting through a window grill around 2:30am. At one point, Razib remained inside while the others stood outside. Razib allegedly took about Tk 4 lakh in cash and around four bhori of gold ornaments from the house and handed them to his associates waiting outside, the OC said. When Hakim tried to catch Razib, a scuffle broke out between them. Hearing his cries for help, local residents rushed to the scene. Locals later caught Razib and beat him, leaving him dead on the spot, the OC said. Hakim suffered a head injury during the scuffle. He was initially taken to Singair Upazila Health Complex before being transferred to Enam Medical College Hospital for advanced treatment. Police recovered the body and sent it to Manikganj Sadar Hospital morgue for an autopsy. “Initially, it appears the incident may have been a case of theft rather than robbery. However, the matter is under investigation,” the OC said, adding that preparations are underway to file a case on behalf of the deceased's family.

title: Khulna police continue anti-crime drive, arrest 33 more
body: Khulna Metropolitan Police (KMP) arrested 33 more people in its ongoing special anti-crime drive between yesterday evening and this morning, bringing the total number of arrests to 336 since the operation began on June 2. According to a KMP press release, the latest drive also led to the recovery of 204 yaba tablets and nine packets of cannabis. Among those arrested, nine were detained by Khulna Police Station, 10 by Sonadanga Model Police Station, four by Labanchara Police Station, three by Khalishpur Police Station, two by Daulatpur Police Station, three by Khanjahan Ali Police Station, and two by the Detective Branch (DB). KMP said such special drives would continue to ensure the safety of city residents, suppress terrorism, extortion, drug-related crimes, mugging and other criminal activities, and maintain a peaceful law-and-order situation in the metropolitan area. According to KMP sources, the operation's target list includes 181 criminals, 584 drug dealers and 69 extortionists across the city's eight police stations. Additional Commissioner Mohammad Rashidul Islam said the drive would continue to target individuals involved in terrorism, extortion and other crimes.

title: Where rape happens: Inside homes, among familiar faces
body: Key points: Most rape incidents in Bangladesh do not happen in dark alleys or isolated streets. They occur in places people trust the most -- inside homes. An analysis by The Daily Star of 8,067 rape cases recorded by the Bangladesh Peace Observatory (BPO) between 2012 and 2025 shows that one of the most common crime scenes is the victim’s own home. A closer look at 680 reported cases from the last five years found 186 incidents took place inside victims’ homes, followed closely by 179 cases inside the perpetrator’s residence. The recent rape and murder of eight-year-old Ramisa Akter in Dhaka reflects this pattern. She was killed inside the perpetrator’s home, just steps away from her own. Similar cases are repeatedly found in the dataset: children being lured into neighbours’ homes or assaulted in familiar surroundings. ``` ``` For example, in 2025 , a 13-year-old girl in Manikganj was assaulted by a 62-year-old neighbour after being called into his house. A year earlier, a 10-year-old in Munshiganj’s Tongibari was raped after being lured inside with chocolates. Beyond homes, offenders exploit a range of other locations, both secluded and familiar, show the data compiled by the BPO, a Dhaka University-based data platform that tracks and analyses violence and conflict trends across Bangladesh. According to The Daily Star’s deeper analysis of the 680 out of the 8,067 rape cases, orchards, forests, and crop fields accounted for 96 incidents. Another 95 incidents happened in abandoned places. Religious and educational institutions saw a combined 53 cases -- 28 in madrasas, 15 in schools, and 10 in mosques. Commercial and transit spaces also appear in the dataset, though less frequently. There were 25 cases in local shops, 17 in transport, and 12 in hotels. Asked about the high number of rape incidents in Bangladesh, Dr Zobaida Nasreen, who teaches anthropology at Dhaka University, said, “There are multiple layers to it. Generally, a deeply misogynistic mindset is at play, where women are viewed merely as objects of consumption. “Perpetrators commit these crimes deliberately because they are aware of legal loopholes and institutional limitations. They know they can get away without facing severe consequences.” Geographically, the highest number of incidents were recorded in urban and industrial hubs. Of the 8,067 cases analysed, Dhaka division topped the list with 2,531 cases, followed by Chattogram and Rajshahi. At the district level, Dhaka recorded 913 cases, followed by Chattogram and Narayanganj. The pattern becomes more striking at the sub-district level. The five areas with the highest number of reported incidents -- Savar, Narayanganj Sadar, Gazipur Sadar, Dhamrai, and Kaliakair -- are all major industrial hubs. In these areas, minors accounted for nearly 58 percent of victims. The same areas also saw nearly one-third of all garment worker victims recorded nationwide over the 13-year period. “Across the industrial hubs, a large number of women move outside for work and they are constantly harassed and raped on the streets and workplaces. Often, they do not report it for fear of losing jobs or the inability to bear the legal expenses,” said Prof Nasreen. More than half (4,520) the victims involved in the 8,067 cases are young girls. Adult women followed with 1,783 cases. The severity of the crisis is reflected in cases involving very young children. For example, in 2025, a two-year-old girl in Sylhet was sexually assaulted after being lured away with biscuits. Across the dataset, 731 incidents involved children. Other vulnerable groups include students, who were victims in 282 cases, and garment workers, who appeared in 135 cases. Findings also show that sexual violence is not limited to female victims. At least 108 cases involved young boys, including 31 who were reportedly raped either inside religious and educational institutions or by madrasa teachers, principals, mosque imams, or muezzins. In one example, an imam was arrested for allegedly raping a 10-year-old boy in Sunamganj's Dowarabazar upazila last year. In a large number of the cases reviewed, the suspects are people known to the victims -- relatives, neighbours, teachers, or family members. The dataset recorded 169 cases involving relatives, including uncles and in-laws, 53 cases involving fathers, and 51 involving husbands or former husbands. Friends were identified as perpetrators in 73 cases, while other family members were accused in 44 incidents. Neighbours also emerged as frequent suspects, accounting for at least 502 cases. In many instances, they lured victims, often children, into their homes with promises of food or gifts. School, madrasa and university teachers as well as private tutors were reportedly involved in 366 cases. Law enforcement and security personnel, including police and members of other agencies, were accused in at least 64 cases. In 2020 , for example, a police constable was arrested over the rape of a a schoolgirl in Khagrachhari. Beyond these groups, 1,369 cases involved local miscreants, often operating in groups. There were also 196 cases involving stalkers and 112 involving transport workers. Politically affiliated individuals were suspects in 162 incidents. According to Prof Sazzad Siddiqui, acting chairman at Dhaka University’s Peace and Conflict Studies, strong laws alone don’t reduce sexual crime. “Countries with effective rule of law and consistent enforcement keep such crimes under control, while even severe punishments like death sentences have little impact in places like Bangladesh where justice is weak and inconsistent,” he said.

title: Ramisa rape, murder: Sohel, Swapna sentenced to death
body: A special court yesterday sentenced prime accused Sohel Rana and his wife Swapna Khatun to death for the rape and murder of eight-year-old schoolgirl Ramisa Akter, a crime that shook the nation. Delivering the verdict in a packed courtroom, Judge Masrur Salekin of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal observed, “When a child becomes the victim of sexual abuse, violence, or a heinous crime such as murder, it not only devastates a family but also deeply wounds society as a whole and raises questions about the effectiveness of the state’s justice system.” The judgment came 19 days after the horrific incident in the capital’s Pallabi area that set off a fierce wave of public outrage, prompting the government to pledge swift justice. The charges were framed on June 1. The law minister said this was the fastest trial in Bangladesh. According to the verdict, Sohel, 31, got the penalty for murdering Ramisa after rape, while Swapna, 26, was sentenced for aiding and abetting. People from various walks of life, including students, gathered on the court premises to hear the verdict amid tight security. As the judge began reading out the verdict at 11:00am, with the accused couple standing in the dock, the courtroom fell into a hushed silence. Seated on a bench at the back was the victim’s father Abdul Hannan Mollah, quietly awaiting the court’s decision. “Ramisa’s case is not merely a criminal trial; it is a profound and difficult test of the society’s conscience, humanity, law enforcement system, and commitment to the rule of law,” said the judge. “Every page of this case, filed over the allegation of brutally extinguishing the life of an innocent child, is filled with pain, anger, concern, and the expectation of justice,” he said. The judge noted this tribunal, established under the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act, is currently responsible for more than 1,800 pending cases, each involving violence against children, sexual abuse, physical abuse, or other serious crimes. “Behind every case lies the unbearable suffering of a child, the anguish of a family, and the expectations of countless people awaiting justice,” he said. As in the case of Ramisa, the tribunal said it expected that prompt, efficient, impartial, and high-quality investigations and judicial proceedings would serve as an exemplary instance for future cases involving child abuse and violence. It hoped that justice-seeking citizens, particularly child victims and their families, would not be subjected to unnecessary delays and uncertainty and that all relevant authorities would continue to demonstrate the same commitment, competence, and sense of responsibility. Soon after the verdict, Ramisa’s father Hannan said, “I am satisfied with the verdict. I will be 100 percent satisfied when the judgment is executed. “I hope every Ramisa in Bangladesh receives justice without delay and that such incidents never happen again in our country,” Hannan said, thanking Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, members of the judiciary, concerned ministers, journalists and law enforcers for their support during the trial process. Special Public Prosecutor Azizur Rahman Dulu said the verdict would stand as a milestone in efforts to curb the crimes. “The prosecution is happy with the verdict.” State defence counsel Musa Kalimullah, who sought a “light sentence” for the accused during arguments on June 4, said he too was satisfied with the death sentences handed down to both of his clients. He said Sohel had confessed under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and later admitted to the crimes again when examined under section 342. He sought mercy. In addition to the death penalty, Sohel was fined Tk 5 lakh, while Swapna was fined Tk 2 lakh. The tribunal ordered the fines be paid to the victim’s “legal heirs”. If the convicts fail to pay the fines, the District Collectors will recover the amount by auctioning off the convicts’ movable and/or immovable properties and pay it to the victim’s family, said the court. Ramisa, a second-grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 in the house of her neighbour, Sohel. The following day, Hannan filed a case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing the couple and an unidentified person. According to the case statement, Sohel lured Ramisa into his room and raped her. Investigators said he later slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body to conceal the crime. The prime minister, who had pledged swift justice during a visit to Ramisa’s home three days after the incident, yesterday said that the swift investigation, identification, and arrest of the perpetrators in a brutal and heartbreaking murder case reflected the government’s firm commitment to maintaining law and order, according to a press release from the Parliament Secretariat. Tarique, at the Business Advisory Committee meeting held at the Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban yesterday afternoon, expressed hope that the judicial proceedings of the case would be completed promptly and fairly, and that those found guilty would receive appropriate punishment in accordance with the law. The premier called upon law enforcement agencies, investigating officers, and all concerned to continue demonstrating the same level of professionalism and dedication in ensuring public safety. Law Minister Md Asaduzzaman in a statement in parliament said, “From the prosecution side, we presented all the witnesses and evidence. The verdict we had expected, the verdict we had proposed, the verdict we had prayed for before the court ... after reviewing all the testimony and evidence ... the court delivered.” The minister also hoped that the verdict would be upheld by the higher court. “We have been able to conclude all trial proceedings of the brutal murder within six working days. This is the first in Bangladesh’s history,” he told reporters at the Secretariat. On May 24, investigator Ohiduzzaman, sub-inspector of Pallabi Police Station, submitted the charge sheet before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate’s (CMM) Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel and Swapna. Several hours later, the CMM Court transferred the case to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal for trial. On June 1, the tribunal framed charges against the accused. The next day, the tribunal completed recording testimonies. A total of 16 prosecution witnesses, including the victim’s parents and elder sister, three neighbours, a doctor, a Dhaka metropolitan magistrate, and the investigator, testified before the tribunal.

title: Woman held in Brahmanbaria drug raid; husband flees after spotting police on CCTV
body: Police arrested an alleged female drug dealer after raiding a house in the Shantibagh area of Brahmanbaria town on Saturday night. The arrestee, Shipa Begum, 39, is the wife of Md Ziamin, 42, of Shantibagh area, police said. Md Shahidul Islam, officer-in-charge of Brahmanbaria Sadar Model Police Station, said Ziamin fled after noticing police presence through CCTV cameras installed outside their home. During the raid, police recovered 20 yaba pills, Tk 21,520 in cash, a CCTV video recorder and two mobile phones. The OC said the couple had installed three CCTV cameras outside the house, which were allegedly used to monitor law enforcement activity while they continued drug-related activities inside. He added that the house was being used as a discreet hub for drug dealing and consumption by the couple. Police said the operation was conducted on Saturday night following a tip-off. As officers approached the house around 9:00pm, Ziamin managed to flee after sensing the police presence through the surveillance system, while Shipa Begum was arrested inside the house. The OC further said Ziamin has multiple cases under the Narcotics Control Act. Drives are ongoing to arrest him, while Shipa was sent to jail by a court this afternoon, he added.

title: Man beaten by locals in Kushtia over alleged rape of 10-year-old
body: A 32-year-old man was beaten up by locals in Kushtia town today over accusations of raping a 10-year-old child. The incident occurred around 11:00 am today at Char Milpara in Ward-10 of Kushtia municipality. The accused, Ashadul, allegedly lured the child to a local school, which was closed at that time, with food. Hearing the child’s screams, locals rushed to the spot, caught Ashadul, and beat him up. Police later rescued him and admitted him to the 250-bed Kushtia General Hospital. Dr Md Iqbal Hossain, resident medical officer of the hospital, said the child is being treated at the emergency department of the hospital. “Her physical condition is being monitored, and necessary medical tests are underway,” he said. Kabir Hossain Matubbor, officer-in-charge of Kushtia Model Police Station, said a case is being filed in connection with the incident.

title: OC withdrawn after BNP-AL clashes in Noakhali
body: Noakhali's Sudharam Model Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Mohammad Towhidul Islam has been withdrawn and attached to the Noakhali Police Lines. The order was issued through a notification signed by Noakhali Superintendent of Police TM Mosharraf Hossain. The SP also confirmed the development to The Daily Star this afternoon. The move came after at least nine people were injured in a series of clashes between activists of the BNP and the Awami League, whose activities are currently banned, in Noakhali Sadar upazila on Saturday night. Meanwhile, Kamrul Islam, officer-in-charge of Sonagazi Police Station in Feni, has been appointed as the new OC of Sudharam Model Police Station. He joined his new posting today. According to local sources, Towhidul joined Sudharam Model Police Station on December 6 last year. Since then, several incidents, including murders, have occurred in different parts of the upazila. They also alleged that despite several rallies and processions by activists of the Awami League and its affiliated organisations in support of Sheikh Hasina in the district town and various unions during May and this month, the OC failed to take effective action. The latest incident involved a series of clashes between BNP and AL activists between 5:00pm and 7:00pm on Saturday in Poshchim Shullakia village under Kaladrap union of Sadar upazila. SP Mosharraf also said Towhidul's transfer to the Police Lines was a routine administrative move.

title: $17,000 snatched after man shot in Dhaka's Motijheel
body: A man was shot and robbed of USD 17,000 by a group of unidentified assailants in broad daylight in Dhaka's Motijheel area on Sunday afternoon. The incident occurred around 3:00pm in front of a Janata Bank branch, said Kamaruzzaman Talukder, officer-in-charge of Motijheel Police Station. The victim, Lokman from Dhaka's Shahjahanpur, sustained bullet injuries to his hand and leg. He was taken to Mugda Medical College Hospital for treatment, he said. OC Kamaruzzaman also said the attackers had possibly been following the victim. "When the victim arrived in front of the bank, they demanded the money he was carrying. As he refused, they shot him and fled with the cash," the OC told The Daily Star. Police have visited the scene and launched an investigation to identify and arrest those involved, he added.

title: Convicts’ lawyer says he is 'satisfied' with Ramisa rape and murder case verdict
body: State-appointed defence counsel Musa Kalimullah today said he is satisfied with the death sentences handed down to both of his clients in the Ramisa rape and murder case. "Since he [Sohel] has confessed to the crime himself, he is guilty. The offenders have received punishment for their crime, and I am satisfied with the verdict," he told reporters outside the courtroom. This reaction came after a special tribunal in Dhaka today sentenced prime accused Sohel Rana and his wife Swapna Khatun to death for the rape and murder of eight-year-old Ramisa -- 19 days after the brutal crime in Dhaka's Pallabi area on May 19. Musa, appointed by the government after lawyers refused to represent the accused, said his responsibilities from June 1 until the verdict included presenting defence arguments, cross-examining prosecution witnesses, and producing defence witnesses if any came forward. He said Sohel had confessed under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and later admitted guilt again when examined under Section 342, seeking mercy while producing no defence witnesses. "Since he had already made a confessional statement under Section 164 and again admitted his guilt before the trial court while seeking leniency, he effectively acknowledged his involvement in this widely discussed incident,” Musa said. “He did not produce any defence witnesses. In my view, this confirms his guilt,” he added. He said that the actual offender has been brought to justice, adding that he believes the government aims to send a clear message to the state, society, and the public that criminals will not go unpunished. Musa also said the verdict would set a precedent, helping deter similar crimes in the future and strengthening public confidence that offenders cannot escape accountability.

title: CJ to form specific HC bench for death references in cases linked to women children
body: Chief Justice Zubayer Rahman Chowdhury will constitute a dedicated High Court bench to hear death references and appeals in cases involving crimes against women and children, including cases similar to that of child Ramisa Akter. The specific bench will begin functioning next Sunday, said Attorney General Md Ruhul Quddus Kazal. Speaking to reporters at his office on the Supreme Court premises, the attorney general said he had requested the chief justice to take such a step during proceedings at the Appellate Division. "Senior lawyers Prabir Neogi and Md Salahuddin Dolon also supported my proposal, and around 200 lawyers present in the courtroom apparently agreed with me," he said. The move came amid growing concerns over delays in the disposal of death reference cases and appeals involving crimes against women and children. A death reference is a mandatory judicial process through which a trial court's death sentence is sent to the High Court for confirmation before it can be carried out. Convicts sentenced to death also have the right to file appeals against their convictions and sentences. The announcement came after a special tribunal in Dhaka sentenced Sohel Rana and his wife, Swapna Khatun, to death in the rape and murder case of eight-year-old Ramisa Akter.

title: Court says Ramisa case a test of humanity and rule of law
body: A Dhaka court today said the rape and murder of eight-year-old Ramisa is a test of society’s conscience, humanity, and rule of law. Judge Masrur Salekin of the Dhaka Metropolitan Child Violence Suppression Tribunal made the observation while delivering the verdict, sentencing Sohel Rana and his wife Swapna Khatun to death. In its remarks, the court said the killing of a child is not only a crime against a family but a serious blow to society, raising questions about the effectiveness of the justice system. It noted that the tribunal -- constituted under the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act, 2000 -- is currently handling over 1,800 pending cases involving violence, sexual abuse and other crimes against children, with each case reflecting deep suffering and delayed justice. The court stressed that ensuring the safety, dignity, and protection of children is a core responsibility of the state, and that such crimes leave lasting social trauma. It also highlighted that the investigation and trial in the Ramisa case were completed in a relatively short time. The tribunal praised the investigation officer and prosecution for their efficiency in submitting the charge sheet and presenting witnesses without delay. The court expressed hope that the case would serve as a model for handling future child abuse and violence cases, urging all stakeholders to ensure faster justice for victims. It added that a fair trial depends on the collective responsibility of investigators, prosecutors, defence lawyers, witnesses and others involved. The judge said the court’s role is guided by law and evidence, not emotion, but by the pursuit of truth.

title: Pleased, full satisfaction to come after execution of verdict: Ramisa’s father
body: Abdul Hannan Molla, father of slain eight-year-old Ramisa Akter, has expressed satisfaction with the verdict in the rape and murder case, saying it has delivered the justice he had long hoped for. “Alhamdulillah, I am satisfied with the verdict. I will be 100 percent satisfied when the judgment is executed,” the father told reporters after the court pronounced the verdict this morning. “This verdict has fulfilled my expectations and aspirations. In Sha Allah, I am fully hopeful that it will be executed swiftly,” he added. He also voiced hope that justice would be ensured swiftly in all cases involving violence against children. “I hope every Ramisa in Bangladesh receives justice without delay and that such incidents never happen again in our country,” he said. Expressing gratitude, he thanked Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, members of the judiciary, concerned ministers, journalists and law enforcers for their support during the trial process. A special tribunal in Dhaka today sentenced prime accused Sohel Rana and his wife Swapna Khatun to death in the case. The verdict came just 19 days after the horrific incident took place on May 19 in Dhaka’s Pallabi area, which sparked nationwide outrage and prompted the government to pledge swift justice.

title: 39 more arrested in Khulna anti-crime drive; total 268 held so far
body: The Khulna Metropolitan Police's special joint operation against extortion, drug trafficking, and other crimes continued today, with 39 more suspects arrested between 6:00pm yesterday and 10:00am today. With this, the operation's total detainee count has reached 268 since the drive began on the night of June 2. According to a KMP press release this morning, members of KMP's north and south divisions and the Detective Branch conducted the latest round of arrests across areas under eight police station, including Khulna Sadar, Sonadanga, Harintana, Arongghata, and Khan Jahan Ali. KMP's target list for the operation includes 181 identified criminals, 584 drug dealers, and 69 alleged extortionists across the city. KMP Additional Commissioner Mohammad Rashidul Islam said the operation would continue until those involved in extortion, terrorism, and other criminal activities are apprehended. Legal proceedings against all arrested individuals are underway, he added.

title: Law minister hopes Ramisa murder verdict will be upheld by higher court
body: Law Minister Md Asaduzzaman today expressed satisfaction with the verdict that sentenced a couple to death in the case filed over the rape and murder of eight-year-old schoolgirl Ramisa Akter, saying he hopes it will be upheld by the higher court. “We have been able to conclude the trial of the brutal murder within six working days while maintaining all legal procedures, which is a first in Bangladesh’s history,” he told reporters at his office after the verdict was delivered. A journalist pointed out that the trials of the Rakib and Rajon murder cases were completed in 10 and 17 working days, respectively, in 2015, but their appeals have remained pending before the High Court for nine years. The journalist then asked whether the Ramisa killing case would face a similar fate and remain pending before the High Court for years, as in the earlier cases. In reply, the minister explained the appellate process and said he would take steps to urge the court to dispose of such cases as quickly as possible. A special tribunal in Dhaka today sentenced prime accused Sohel Rana and his wife, Swapna Khatun, to death in the Ramisa murder case. The verdict came just 19 days after the incident in Dhaka’s Pallabi area on May 19, which sparked nationwide outrage and prompted the government to pledge swift justice.

title: Death of newborns at Ad-din: Writ petition seeks HC directive for probe, compensation
body: A Supreme Court lawyer today filed a writ petition with the High Court seeking its directive for the authorities concerned to investigate the deaths of six newborns at Ad-din Medical College Hospital and provide Tk 1 crore in compensation to each affected family. Advocate Md Eunus Ali Akond submitted the petition as a public interest litigation, alleging that the six newborns died due to negligence by the authorities concerned of Ad-din hospital and the government. In the petition, he said the authorities had failed to fulfil their constitutional duty to protect the right to life of the newborns. Eunus Ali Akond told The Daily Star that the High Court may hold a hearing on the petition tomorrow.

title: Ramisa Murder: Sohel, wife Swapna sentenced to death
body: A special tribunal in Dhaka today sentenced prime accused Sohel Rana and his wife, Swapna Khatun, to death in a case filed over the rape and murder of eight-year-old schoolgirl Ramisa Akter . According to the judgment, Sohel was fined Tk 5 lakh, while Swapna was fined Tk 2 lakh. The tribunal also ordered that the fines imposed on the convicts be paid to the victim's legal heirs. "If the convicts fails pay to the legal heirs of the victim, then, pursuant to Section 16 of the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act, the concerned District Collectors are directed to recover the compensation amount by auctioning their movable and/or immovable properties and to pay the proceeds of such sale to the victim’s legal heirs as compensation," said the verdict. The verdict came just 19 days after the horrific incident took place in Dhaka’s Pallabi area on May 19 that sparked nationwide outrage and prompted the government to pledge swift justice. Judge Masrur Salekin of the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal in Dhaka Metropolitan delivered the judgement at a packed courtroom, said bench assistant Pankoj Peter Gomes. Around 10:45am, Sohel, 31, and Swapna, 26,were taken to the tribunal amid tight security and kept in the lockup of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court in Dhaka. Later, they were produced before the tribunal. The tribunal wrapped up the trial proceedings in five hearings, according to the prosecution. When a call was made to Ramisa's father's phone, it was answered by his nephew, Ferdous Sultan. He told The Daily Star that the family was satisfied with the verdict being delivered in such a short time following the assurance from Prime Minister Tarique Rahman. They want this verdict to be executed quickly On June 1, the tribunal framed charges against the accused. The next day, the tribunal completed testimony. A total of 16 prosecution witnesses, the victim’s parents and elder sister, three neighbours, a doctor, a Dhaka metropolitan magistrate and the investigator, gave their statements before the tribunal. On May 24, investigator Ohiduzzaman, a sub-inspector of Pallabi Police Station, submitted the charge sheet before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate's (CMM) Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel of rape, murder and destruction of evidence, and Swapna of destruction of evidence, providing false information and assisting her husband to commit the offence. Several hours later, the CMM Court transferred the case to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal for trial. Ramisa, a second-grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 in the house of her neighbour, Sohel. The following day, Ramisa's father Abdul Hannan Mollah filed the case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing the couple and an unidentified person. According to the case statement, Sohel lured Ramisa into his room and raped her. Investigators said he later slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body to conceal the crime.

title: Ramisa Murder: Verdict today, just 19 days after incident
body: A Dhaka court is set to deliver its verdict today in the rape and murder case of eight-year-old schoolgirl Ramisa Akter , just 19 days after the crime that sparked nationwide outrage and prompted the government to pledge swift justice. Judge Masrur Salekin of the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal in Dhaka Metropolitan, is scheduled to announce the verdict around 11:00am, Special Public Prosecutor Azizur Rahman Dulu said. The tribunal concluded the trial in five hearings, with charges framed on June 1 and witness testimony completed the following day. In the closing arguments on June 4, the prosecution sought death penalty for prime accused Sohel Rana, 31, and his wife, co-accused Swapna Khatun, 26, arguing that the charges had been proved beyond reasonable doubt through witness testimonies and cross-examinations. The defence, however, sought a lighter sentence, claiming the charge sheet was based on the prime accused’s confessional statement and that the alleged murder weapon had not undergone forensic testing. Lawyers involved in the case said they could not recall a verdict being delivered so quickly in a rape and murder trial. Ramisa, a second-grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 at the home of her neighbour, Sohel, in the capital’s Pallabi area. The following day, her father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, filed a case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing Sohel, Swapna and an unidentified person. According to the case statement, Sohel lured Ramisa into his room and raped her. Investigators said he later slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body to conceal the crime. On May 24, the investigating officer, Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station, submitted a charge sheet to the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate’s Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel of rape, murder and destruction of evidence. Swapna was charged with destruction of evidence, providing false information and assisting her husband in committing the offence. Several hours later, the court transferred the case to the tribunal for trial.

title: 50 rescued from human traffickers in Teknaf
body: The Coast Guard has rescued 50 people from a fishing trawler bound for Malaysia. Among the rescued victims were 39 Bangladeshis and 11 Rohingyas. Nine suspected traffickers were arrested during the operation off the Teknaf coast in Cox’s Bazar. At a press briefing held at the station headquarters yesterday, Lt Commander Md Muttaqin Siddiqui, commander of the Coast Guard’s Teknaf Station, said the Coast Guard received information on Friday evening that a group was being trafficked by trawler through the Teknaf coast for illegal migration to Malaysia. Following the tip-off, Coast Guard members spotted a suspicious trawler in the sea off Baharchhara. After a chase, Coast Guard personnel intercepted and seized the vessel. A search of the trawler led to the rescue and the subsequent arrest of nine suspected traffickers, he said.

title: Easy bike driver arrested over rape of speech-impaired girl in Narail
body: Police today arrested an easy bike driver on charges of abducting and raping a 13-year-old girl with speech impairment in Lohagara upazila of Narail. Selim Sheikh, 27, of Boyra village under Laxmipasha union, was arrested in his house shortly after the victim’s mother filed an abduction and rape case with Lohagara Police Station around 11:30am today, said its Inspector Ajit Kumar Roy. According to the case statement and police sources, the girl had been living at her maternal grandfather’s house in a village under Lohagara upazila. Around 4:00pm on Friday, Selim lured her into his easy bike from a road near the house and took her to an undisclosed location and raped her. Later in the evening, the accused dropped the victim near Lutiya Bazar under Dighalia union and fled. After being rescued by her family, the girl described the ordeal to her relatives, who then brought her to the local police station. The victim has been sent to Narail District Hospital for medical examination, said the inspector, adding that legal proceedings are underway.

title: Case filed against 5 over 'attack' on journalist in Jhenaidah
body: A case has been filed two days after an alleged attack on a journalist in Jhenaidah’s Harinakundu upazila. The case was filed at Harinakundu Police Station last night, based on a complaint filed by Selim Reza -- the elder brother of the victim Sabuj Shahriar, 32, said its Officer-in-Charge (OC) Asit Kumar Roy. The accused named in the case are Rocky Mondol, 22; Sujon Mondol, 32; Rifat Mondol, 21; Sohel Mondol, 25; and Md Pijir Mondol, 65 -- all residents of Beltala village in the upazila. The OC said no suspects have been arrested so far. According to the case statement, Sabuj Shahriar, Harinakunda upazila correspondent of the daily Kalbela, was attacked at around 9:00pm on June 3 while returning home from a shop in the village. The assailants beat him severely with hammers, iron rods, and bamboo sticks, leaving him critically injured. Local residents and family members rescued him and first took him to Harinakundu Upazila Health Complex. Later that night, as his condition deteriorated, the attending physician referred him to Kushtia Medical College Hospital. While receiving treatment at the upazila health complex, Sabuj alleged that 10 to 12 individuals, including Sujon, Rocky, and Sohel, who are supporters of Joradaha Union Parishad Chairman Zahidul Islam Babu, carried out the attack. Responding to the allegation, Chairman Zahidul said, “Sabuj is a resident of my village. Although the attackers may be my supporters, I had no knowledge of the incident. Even if someone supports me, I cannot be held responsible if they commit wrongdoing.” Sabuj’s elder brother Selim alleged that the attack stemmed from a social feud in the area. “Sabuj is currently undergoing treatment at Kushtia Medical College Hospital. He sustained severe head injuries, one of his legs has been broken, and he suffered injuries to various parts of his body,” added Selim.

title: Journalist attacked inside traffic police box in Gazipur
body: A journalist was attacked inside a traffic police box at Chandana Chowrasta on the Dhaka-Mymensingh Highway in Gazipur this afternoon. The victim, Hossain Ali Babu, Gazipur district correspondent of Star News, suffered injuries in the attack and was taken to Shaheed Tajuddin Ahmad Medical College Hospital, according to Gazipur traffic police. Following the incident, traffic police detained a man named Md Jewel, 25, a resident of Narsingdi district, and handed him over to the relevant police station. Gazipur Traffic Police Inspector Tariqul Islam told The Daily Star that Babu had been conducting a live broadcast on the highway before entering the traffic police box to take rest. Shortly afterwards, an individual entered the facility, questioned him about the live broadcast, and allegedly assaulted him. Tariqul said the attacker snatch tripod and struck the journalist on the head and other parts of his body. On-duty Assistant Traffic Sub-Inspector Taj Uddin immediately intervened, rescued the journalist, and arranged for his treatment, the traffic police official said. "The person involved was detained immediately, and legal proceedings against him are underway," Tariqul added. Basan Police Station Officer-in-Charge Harun ur Rashid said the accused remains in police custody. The OC said preliminary observations suggest that the suspect may have some mental health issues. Police are trying to contact his family, and legal action will be taken in accordance with the law, he added.

title: Special drive: 59, including two aides of ‘Grenade Babu’, arrested in Khulna
body: A special joint operation has arrested 59 individuals in Khulna city as part of an intensified crackdown on violence, drug trafficking, and extortion. Mohammad Rashidul Islam, additional commissioner (Crime and Operations) of KMP, said two close associates of the top-listed gangster “Grenade Babu” were among the arrestees. They are “Kosai Liton” and Rifat. According to KMP sources, the ongoing operation is targeting 834 listed suspects across the city, including 181 alleged criminals, 584 drug dealers, and 69 extortionists operating in areas under the jurisdiction of eight police stations. The joint drive, involving multiple units including the Detective Branch, was conducted from Thursday night until 8:00pm on Friday. During this period, 13 people were arrested by Khulna Sadar police, 13 by Sonadanga Model police, 6 from Lobonchora, 1 from Harintana, 16 from Khalishpur, 8 from Daulatpur, and 2 by the Detective Branch. Rashidul Islam also said the operation was launched in response to growing concern over a series of recent criminal activities in the city. He also said police have decided to carry out coordinated drives involving all operational units, including specialised forces, following a high-level meeting chaired by the police commissioner at KMP headquarters on Wednesday. Earlier, separate operations conducted by the southern division of KMP from Wednesday night to Thursday afternoon resulted in the arrest of 63 suspects. During those drives, police also recovered a locally made weapon and seized 11 motorcycles and a pickup van.

title: BNP man accused of assaulting a pregnant woman
body: A BNP leader in Netrokona’s Mohanganj upazila has been accused of assaulting a three-month-pregnant woman, who later suffered a miscarriage. The incident took place around 12:30pm on Wednesday in Palgaon village under Suair union. The accused, Ferdous Mia, 45, is general secretary of Ward-1 unit of Suair union BNP. Asha Akter, 21, was undergoing treatment at Mohanganj Upazila Health Complex, said Mohanganj police OC Md Hafizur Rahman Harun. According to a complaint filed by Asha’s father, Dilkhush Mia, a dispute began when a dog belonging to Asha’s brother, Jewel Mia, was roaming near Ferdous’s goats. An altercation followed when Ferdous allegedly scolded the family. Ferdous and his associates assaulted Jewel. When Dilkhush and his wife, Salema Akter, intervened, they were also beaten. Asha was kicked in the abdomen while trying to stop the assault. Shahidullah, a sub-assistant community medical officer, said the woman had suffered a miscarriage. Attempts to contact Ferdous for comment were unsuccessful. Mohanganj upazila BNP President Selim Karnayen said the party is trying to resolve the dispute.

title: Violence against women, children rises in May
body: Incidents of violence against women and children, including rape and child abuse, increased in May compared to the previous month, according to rights organisation Human Rights Support Society (HRSS). The findings were published yesterday in HRSS’s monthly human rights monitoring report, based on reports published in 16 national media outlets as well as the organisation’s own fact-finding and monitoring. The report also recorded increases in border killings and mob violence, while warning that killings, extortion, attacks on shrines and other violent crimes continued to challenge public safety and law and order. In particular, HRSS described the human rights situation of women and children as deeply concerning. “Violence against women and children, both online and offline, has emerged as a serious challenge to social security and humanitarian protection,” the report said. According to HRSS, at least 305 women and girls faced violence in May, up from 294 in April. Rape cases rose to 83 from 68 in April. Of the victims, 57, or nearly 70 percent, were under 18, compared with 30 child victims in the previous month. Gang rape cases increased to 17 from 13. Six rape victims, including four children, died after being assaulted. Among the cases highlighted in the report was the rape and killing of eight-year-old schoolgirl Ramisa Akter in Dhaka’s Pallabi on May 19, which sparked nationwide outrage. Reported sexual harassment cases fell slightly to 76 from 79 in April, although the number of child victims increased from 40 to 42. Domestic violence remained severe. In May, family-related violence left 63 women dead and 31 injured, while 45 women died by suicide. In April, 64 women were killed, 36 injured, and 36 died by suicide. Child abuse also increased. HRSS recorded 215 children subjected to abuse in May, compared with 191 in April. Among them, 56 children died and 211 suffered physical or psychological abuse. The organisation also raised concerns over child health services, saying that more than 600 children nationwide died over the past three months after developing measles-like symptoms. It cited inadequate vaccination management, shortages and limited access to advanced treatment. The report further cited the deaths of six newborns at Ad-Din Medical College Hospital in Dhaka’s Moghbazar on May 27, alleging hospital mismanagement. Border areas remained unsafe for civilians, according to HRSS. Along the Bangladesh-India border, the report documented six incidents involving India’s Border Security Force (BSF) in May, leaving four Bangladeshis dead and 20 injured. In April, two people were killed and two injured in similar incidents. At least 14 people were reportedly detained by the BSF in May, up from eight in April. HRSS also said at least 166 people were pushed into Bangladesh through various border points during the month. Along the Bangladesh-Myanmar border, three people were killed and one injured in landmine explosions allegedly caused by mines planted in the area. The report also recorded four incidents in which 18 people were detained by the Arakan Army. Mob violence increased sharply. HRSS documented 66 incidents of mob attacks and public beatings, leaving at least 31 people dead and 68 injured. In April, 44 such incidents resulted in 22 deaths and 39 injuries. In contrast, political violence declined. HRSS recorded 64 incidents of political violence in May, resulting in five deaths and 289 injuries, down from 98 incidents, six deaths and 533 injuries in April. According to the report, most of these incidents stemmed from political rivalries, internal factional disputes, territorial dominance and extortion-related conflicts. Freedom of expression also faced restrictions, with 11 incidents recorded in May. These led to the detention of six individuals and the filing of seven cases involving 12 accused. According to HRSS, one person was detained over a Facebook post critical of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, while six others were detained for allegedly criticising leaders and activists of the ruling BNP. Two people were arrested on allegations of hurting religious sentiments and making derogatory remarks, and another person was detained in a separate incident. The report also noted that 12 individuals were accused in five separate cases filed under various provisions of the Cyber Security Ordinance 2025. Journalists faced continued hostility. HRSS recorded 39 incidents involving harassment or abuse of 78 media professionals during May. Among them, 42 were injured, 18 assaulted, nine threatened and one detained. Eight journalists were named in two separate cases. The organisation also documented three attacks on members of minority communities, injuring five people, vandalising six homes and involving one case of land grabbing. Two separate attacks on shrines in Kushtia and Dhaka were also recorded. At least seven inmates died in prisons across the country in May, while law enforcement agencies recovered 28 unidentified bodies from different areas during the month.

title: Case filed against man over rape of 14-year-old girl in Jamalpur
body: A case was filed today against a man for allegedly raping a 14-year-old girl in Jamalpur’s Sarishabari upazila. The girl’s father filed the case against their neighbour Ibrahim Hossain, 38, with Sarishabari Police Station, said Mohammad Iqbal Hossain, officer-in-charge of the station. The drive to arrest the accused is underway as he has been absconding since the incident, added the OC. According to the case statement, accused Ibrahim, who is married and has two children, had been allegedly making unwanted advances on the girl. On Thursday, while the girl was passing by the accused’s house, Ibrahim allegedly forcibly dragged her inside and raped her. As the girl went missing for a long time, her relatives and neighbours began searching for her. Eventually, they searched the accused’s house and rescued the girl. Sensing their presence, Ibrahim fled the scene. Later, the girl disclosed the incident to her family members, added the case statement.

title: College Chhatra Dal unit president held for attacking police in Netrokona
body: Police have arrested a local Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal (JCD) leader on allegations of assaulting two police officers during an altercation in Madan municipality of Netrokona yesterday evening. The incident took place at the intersection near Madan Government Haji Abdul Aziz Khan Degree College. The detainee, Mithu Mia, 22, is president of the JCD unit at the degree college, said police. "We went to the spot after receiving information about a dispute involving passengers at the bus counter. There, a young man named Mithu assaulted and injured two police officers. He has been detained," Madan Police Station Officer-in-Charge Mohammad Tarikul Islam said speaking to The Daily Star this afternoon. A case had already been filed against the accused on charges of obstructing official duties and attacking police personnel, the OC said, adding that the process of producing him before a Netrokona court was underway. The injured officers, constables Md Faridul Islam and Ataur Rahman of Madan Police Station, received treatment at the Upazila Health Complex. According to police and local sources, frustration among passengers mounted near the college intersection after buses failed to arrive on schedule. Following complaints from passengers, Upazila Nirbahi Officer Nadir Hossain Shamim and OC Mohammad Tarikul Islam, accompanied by law enforcers, went to the scene to bring the situation under control. Passengers informed the administration about prolonged waiting, a shortage of transport services and other inconveniences. Police alleged that while authorities were attempting to calm the situation, Mithu arrived at the scene and sought to escalate tensions. An argument reportedly broke out after police officers, acting on the OC's instructions, asked him to leave the area. At one stage, Mithu allegedly became aggressive and assaulted two police officers, leaving constables Faridul and Ataur injured. Police subsequently detained him and took him to the police station. SH Pipul, president of Madan Upazila Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal, said, "I have heard about Mithu's detention. After verifying the facts of the incident and finding evidence that he violated party discipline, I have learned that he has already been expelled from the organisation."

title: Woman sustains burns in acid attack by ex-husband in Habiganj
body: A woman sustained severe facial burns after her former husband threw acid on her in Habiganj’s Sadar upazila on Thursday night. The victim, Rubina Begum, 30, a factory worker and mother of two, was first taken to Habiganj Sadar Hospital before being transferred to the burn unit of Sylhet MAG Osmani Medical College Hospital (SOMCH) as her condition deteriorated. The assault took place around 9:00pm in the Bahula area, police said. According to Md Jahidul Islam, officer-in-charge of Habiganj Police Station, Rubina married 28-year-old Ujjal Mia two years ago. The couple divorced six months ago, but Ujjal allegedly continued to harass her at her workplace and on her way home. On Thursday night, while Rubina was returning home from work, Ujjal reportedly approached her and threw acid on her face before fleeing. Locals rushed to help her after hearing her screams and took her to the hospital. Police arrested Ujjal around 11:00pm the same night. The OC said the accused admitted to the act during preliminary interrogation. Shahidul Haque Munshi, additional superintendent of police (Sadar Circle), confirmed visiting the scene.

title: Missing former Jubo Dal leader found dead
body: A former Jubo Dal leader was found dead in Tangail’s Ghatail upazila on Wednesday night, three days after he reportedly went missing. The deceased, Mohammad Mintu Khan, 47, was the former organising secretary of Sangrampur union Jubo Dal. According to Ghatail Police Station Officer-in-Charge Moksedur Rahman, Mintu went missing from Chamri Bazar around 9:30pm on May 31. A general diary was filed with the police the following day. Police initially arrested Sohel Rana on suspicion of involvement in the incident. Based on information obtained during interrogation, four more suspects were detained. Following leads provided by the arrestees, police conducted a drive in Maicha Beel near Manpura Bridge on Wednesday night and recovered Mintu’s body. Police are continuing their investigation into the killing.

title: Ramisa murder verdict Sunday, after 19 days
body: A special tribunal in Dhaka yesterday set June 7 for delivering the verdict in a case filed over the rape and murder of eight-year-old schoolgirl Ramisa Akter. The development came just 16 days after the horrific incident in Dhaka’s Pallabi area on May 19, which sparked nationwide outrage and prompted the government to pledge swift justice. Judge Masrur Salekin of the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal in Dhaka Metropolitan wrapped up the trial proceedings in five hearings, bench assistant Pankoj Peter Gomes told The Daily Star. Yesterday, the tribunal heard arguments from both the prosecution and the defence. During the arguments, Special Public Prosecutor Azizur Rahman Dulu told the court that the charges against prime accused Sohel Rana, 31, and his wife and co-accused Swapna Khatun, 26, had been proved beyond reasonable doubt through the testimonies and cross-examination of 16 witnesses. Therefore, both accused deserve the death penalty, he argued. However, state defence counsel Musa Kalimullah sought a light sentence for the accused. He said, “The charge sheet was submitted based on the confessional statement. The knife allegedly used in the killing was not subjected to a forensic test. A conviction cannot be handed down solely on that basis. “The accused, Sohel, gave a confession implicating himself. He was under the influence of drugs at the time of the incident. Taking that into consideration, we seek a sentence of life imprisonment for him.” The lawyer further said, “As for Swapna, the testimonies of the 16 witnesses contain nothing against her except the allegation of concealing the body. She should be punished under Section 201 of the Penal Code.” Section 201 of the Penal Code criminalises concealing or destroying evidence, or providing false information to shield an offender, with penalties of up to seven years’ imprisonment and fines, depending on the severity of the underlying crime. Earlier in the day, the proceedings began at around 11:45am, when the judge took the bench, slightly later than the scheduled 11:30am start after police informed the court that Swapna had fallen ill. Ramisa, a second-grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 in the house of her neighbour, Sohel. The following day, Ramisa’s father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, filed a case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing the couple and an unidentified person. According to the case statement, Sohel lured Ramisa into his room and raped her. Investigators said he later slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body to conceal the crime. The next day, the tribunal completed the recording of testimony. A total of 16 prosecution witnesses -- including the victim’s parents and elder sister, three neighbours, a doctor, a Dhaka metropolitan magistrate, and the investigator -- gave statements before the tribunal. On May 24, investigator Ohiduzzaman, a sub-inspector of Pallabi Police Station, submitted the charge sheet to the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate’s (CMM) Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel of rape, murder, and destruction of evidence, and Swapna of destruction of evidence and providing false information. Several hours later, the CMM Court transferred the case to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal for trial. On Monday, the tribunal framed charges against the accused couple.

title: Section 144 in Nandail after clash over land
body: The local administration yesterday imposed Section 144 in Nandail upazila of Mymensingh after a clash between two groups over a disputed piece of land. The dispute involves ownership of two decimals of land and stems from a long-running conflict between Abdul Rouf Mahajan of Kharua village and Shawkat Ali of Narendra Pur village, said Nandail Model Police Station Officer-in-Charge Azharul Islam. The matter is currently pending before a court, he added. According to police, tensions escalated after a house being built on the disputed land was demolished on Wednesday. Additional law enforcers were deployed in the area following a complaint filed over the incident. Around 11:00am yesterday, supporters of the two sides clashed at Kharua Bazar. Witnesses and police said the groups attacked each other with bamboo sticks, bricks and locally made weapons. Several shops were vandalised during the violence. Mahfuzur Rahman, son of Abdul Rouf, alleged that attempts were made to forcibly build a house on their land and that shops belonging to their side were vandalised. Shawkat, however, claimed he had legally purchased the land and was constructing a house, which was demolished. He alleged that a shop belonging to his brother was later attacked. Police fired eight rounds of blank rubber bullets to disperse the crowd, the OC said. “The situation is now under control. Police and Rapid Action Battalion personnel have been deployed,” he added. Nandail UNO Fatema Jannat said Section 144 came into effect at 12:00pm yesterday and would remain in force until further notice.

title: Woman found dead in Pallabi apartment
body: Police recovered the partially decomposed body of a woman from her apartment in Dhaka’s Pallabi area early Wednesday, with preliminary findings suggesting she had died several days earlier. The deceased was identified as Selina Afroz, 55. Pallabi Police Station Officer-in-Charge Hasan Basir said Selina had been living alone in a flat in Block C of Section 6, while her husband and three children reside in Canada. The body was found on the floor of the apartment, with the door locked from the inside. It was sent to the Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital morgue for an autopsy, he said. According to police and family members, Selina returned to Bangladesh around 12 years ago and had since been living in the family-owned flat. She had been separated from her husband due to family disputes. Ramizul Haidar, Selina’s nephew-in-law, said she inherited the four-storey building and lived alone on the second floor. Her elder sister, who is ill, lives on the top floor, while the lower floors remain vacant. He said Selina met her expenses through rental income from two apartments in a nearby building. Family members last spoke to her two days before Eid-ul-Azha and had not seen her since. After learning about the recent recovery of another woman’s body in the neighbourhood, relatives checked on Selina and noticed a foul smell coming from her flat before informing police. Police said the exact cause of death will be known after the autopsy report is received. The incident comes days after police recovered the body of elderly resident Nurjahan Begum from a nearby apartment in Pallabi, prompting discussion on social media about elderly people living alone. Selina was buried at a graveyard in Mirpur on Wednesday evening.

title: 2,844 arrested in DMP drives last month
body: Dhaka Metropolitan Police has arrested 658 extortionists, 971 muggers, criminals and robbers, and 1,215 drug dealers during special drives in the capital over the past month, said DMP Commissioner Mosleh Uddin Ahmed at a press briefing yesterday. He said a total of 2,844 people were arrested in various drives carried out over the last month. The commissioner also said nine people, including six Chinese nationals, were arrested for their alleged involvement in online gambling, cyber fraud, and illegal digital financial transactions. Special drives will continue to ensure a safe and secure Dhaka, he said. Speaking about Eid-ul-Azha security measures, Mosleh said no major acts of sabotage or serious crimes occurred in the capital during the holiday period. He described the overall law-and-order situation as stable. On traffic management, Mosleh said DMP’s traffic division filed 38,284 cases in May for violations of the Road Transport Act, including 672 cases through an AI-based enforcement system. A total of Tk 8.71 crore in fines was realised through these cases, he added. Mosleh also provided updates on several high-profile cases. In the Ramisa rape and murder case in Pallabi, police arrested the accused within seven hours of the incident and submitted the charge sheet on the sixth day after the case was filed. The verdict is scheduled to be delivered on Sunday. Responding to concerns over rising mugging incidents in Mohammadpur, Uttara and Jatrabari, the commissioner said police were actively working in those areas. Asked whether a list of extortionists would be made public, Mosleh said it would be released and further details would be provided by DMP’s media wing. He also said two people were arrested over the theft of cables connected to the Prime Minister’s “red telephone” at the Secretariat. One of the arrestees is Ranjan Chandra, an outsourced employee at the Secretariat. Based on his information, police recovered around eight kilogrammes of stolen cable from a scrap shop, he said. Regarding allegations that people are harassed or asked for money while filing general diaries or complaints at police stations, Mosleh said strict action would be taken against anyone found responsible after investigation. On measures against battery-run rickshaws, Mosleh said drives against such vehicles are continuing regularly.

title: One dead, 15 injured as villagers clash in Tangail
body: A 65-year-old man was killed and at least 15 others were injured in a clash between residents of two villages in Tangail over a previous dispute this afternoon. Several houses were vandalised and set on fire during the clash in Golpencha village. The deceased was identified as Kalam Talukder, a resident of Jagatkura village, said Kazi Shahnewaz, additional superintendent of police in Tangail. Police and locals said clashes and vandalism had earlier taken place in Golpencha village of Gopalpur upazila and Jagatkura village of Bhuiyanpur upazila on April 22 over a dispute linked to leftover food from a shop. The violence reportedly flared up again this afternoon. Kalam and several others were injured in the clash. They were taken to Bhuiyanpur Upazila Health Complex, where doctors declared Kalam dead. The other injured were sent to Tangail General Hospital for treatment. Gopalpur Police Station Officer-in-Charge Md Anwar Hossain said the situation is now under control. He added that around 500 police personnel have been deployed in the area.

title: Man dies after mob beating over alleged assault of child in Jhenaidah
body: A 45-year-old man died in Jhenaidah on Thursday after being beaten by locals over allegation of attempting to rape a seven-year-old girl. The incident took place around 2:30pm in the Jhinukmala Housing Area under Paglakanai union of Sadar upazila, the deceased was identified as Billal Hossain, Jhenaidah Sadar Police Station Officer-in-Charge Md Asaduzzaman said. He had rented a room in the area about a week ago and worked as a rickshaw-puller, the OC added. The OC also said preparations were underway to conduct an inquest and send the body for an autopsy. Eyewitnesses said residents of the housing area beat up Billal after accusing him of attempting to rape the seven-year-old daughter of a local resident by luring her with food. Billal was seriously injured. Earlier in the afternoon, the child's mother filed a case with the police station accusing Billal of sexually assaulting her daughter. Based on the case, police formally arrested him. Police took him into custody from the scene and admitted him to Jhenaidah 250-Bed General Hospital, where he died while undergoing treatment. Dr Uma Islam, a physician at the emergency department of the hospital, said Billal died at around 6:15pm while undergoing treatment. "He was brought to the hospital in an almost unconscious state," she said. The doctor said he may have died from internal bleeding, although the exact cause of death would only be known after the autopsy report is received.

title: Police press charges in Ctg child rape case within 7 working days
body: Police in Chattogram today pressed charges against the lone accused in a rape case filed with Bakalia Police Station. Inspector Tanvir Ahmed, also the investigation officer of the case, submitted the charge sheet to the prosecution section of the Chattogram Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Court around 3:00pm, accusing Monir Hossen, 30, a staffer of a local decoration shop in Bakalia area of the port city. Tariqul Islam, assistant commissioner (Chawkbazar circle) of Chattogram Metropolitan Police (CMP), confirmed the development to The Daily Star. After analysing DNA tests and other evidence, police pressed the charge sheet against Monir, he said. Mohammad Solaiman, officer-in-charge (OC) of Bakalia Police Station, told The Daily Star that the investigation officer prepared the charge sheet within seven working days. If there had been no Eid vacation, the police could have filed the charge sheet earlier. “We conducted the investigation properly so that the victim can get justice,” said the OC. On May 21, the Nur Hossen Chairmanghata area of Bakalia turned into a battlefield after locals tried to snatch the rape accused, Monir, from police custody for mob justice. Monir allegedly sexually abused a four-year-old girl and tried to rape her after taking her inside a decoration shop near her house that afternoon. Later, the child narrated the incident to her parents. Following the incident, the child’s family held Monir and took him to their house. After the news spread in the locality, hundreds gathered in front of the house to beat the accused. Upon receiving information, police rushed to the spot. When the police removed the accused from the area after seven hours by firing blank shots and using sound grenades and tear gas canisters, a clash erupted in the Bakalia area. The aggravated locals later torched a police truck and vandalised several traffic police boxes, injuring at least 20 police. On May 22, the father of the child filed a rape case.

title: Over 2,800 arrested in month-long special drives across Dhaka: DMP
body: Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) arrested 2,844 people in special drives across the capital over the past month, including 658 extortionists, 971 muggers, terrorists and robbers, and 1,215 drug dealers, DMP Commissioner Mosleh Uddin Ahmed said today. Speaking at a press briefing at DMP headquarters, he said police seized 744kg of cannabis, 179,000 yaba pills, 405 grams of heroin, 1,281 bottles of phensedyl, 29 grams of crystal methamphetamine (ice), six pistols, 21 rounds of ammunition, four magazines, 11 crude bombs and 12 locally made weapons during the drives. Nine people, including six Chinese nationals, were also arrested for their alleged involvement in online gambling, cyber fraud and illegal digital financial transactions, he said. On Eid-ul-Azha security, the commissioner said there had been no major acts of sabotage or serious criminal incidents in Dhaka during the holiday period. The DMP's traffic division filed 38,284 cases in May for violations of the Road Transport Act, including 672 through an AI-based enforcement system, realising Tk 8.71 crore in fines. Mosleh Uddin said 70 AI cameras are currently operating at 57 locations across Dhaka and that the network will be expanded. Providing updates on major cases, he said police arrested the accused in the Ramisa rape and murder case in Pallabi within seven hours and submitted the charge sheet six days after the case was filed. The verdict is scheduled for Sunday. He said investigators found no evidence implicating anyone beyond those named in the charge sheet. The commissioner also said four people, including the main accused, Taslima Akter alias Hasna, were arrested over the murder and dismemberment of Saudi expatriate Mokarram Hossain in Pallabi. Police also arrested three suspects in the gang rape and murder of a mentally challenged woman in Jatrabari, four suspects in a gang robbery case in Demra, three members of a counterfeit currency syndicate, and nine members of a kidnapping gang in Adabor. Responding to concerns over rising mugging incidents, Mosleh Uddin said police had intensified operations in Mohammadpur, Uttara and Jatrabari, recently arresting juvenile gang leader Akash and his associates in Mohammadpur. He also said a list of extortionists would be made public and warned that strict action would be taken against police personnel found harassing service seekers.

title: 2 arrested over theft of PM office ‘red telephone’ cables
body: The Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime (CTTC) unit of Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) has arrested two people for allegedly stealing copper cables connected to the “red telephone” line at the prime minister’s Secretariat office. A CTTC team arrested the suspects during separate drives in and around Dhaka. The arrestees were identified as Ranjan Chandra, 26, and Rejakul Islam, 32. A CTTC official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said Ranjan, an outsourcing worker at the Secretariat, allegedly stole around eight kg of copper cable and sold it to Rejakul Islam. The official added that a syndicate may be involved in the theft of cables from the Secretariat area. During the Eid holidays, copper cables installed between the Old Secretariat Building-2 and New Building-1 were reportedly cut and stolen. These lines were used for key government communications, including connections involving the prime minister’s office, cabinet division, and public administration ministry. On June 1, Bangladesh Telecommunications Company Limited (BTCL) filed a written complaint with the ministry of home affairs over the incident.
