title: Man beaten to death in Patuakhali over land dispute
body: A man was beaten to death and three of his family injured in an attack allegedly stemming from a dispute among neighbours in Patuakhali's Bauphal upazila on Wednesday morning. The deceased, Robin Hawlader, 50, was a resident of Uttar Kalaiya village under Kalaiya union, said police. His wife Thakur Rani Hawlader, 45, and their two sons, Rony Hawlader, 22, and Hridoy Hawlader, 24, were injured in the incident. Bauphal Police Station Officer-in-Charge Md Sirajul Islam confirmed the incident, saying that four suspects had been arrested. The OC said the incident took place around 7:30am in the launch terminal area of Uttar Kalaiya village. According to family and locals, rainwater had long been accumulating in the courtyard of a shared homestead during the monsoon season. Members of seven families living on the property had agreed to install a plastic pipe to drain the water, with the cost to be shared among them. However, the family of one Ananda Bepari objected to the plan, leading to a dispute. Witnesses said an argument broke out between Robin Hawlader and Ananda Bepari on Wednesday morning. At one point, the altercation escalated and a group of eight to ten people, allegedly led by Ananda’s son Ratan Bepari, attacked Robin with sticks and locally-made sharp weapons. When Robin's wife and two sons tried to stop them, they were also hacked, leaving all four seriously injured. Locals rushed them to Bauphal Upazila Health Complex, where doctors declared Robin dead. The three injured family members were admitted to the hospital for treatment. The incident triggered tension in the area. Police later visited the scene and launched a drive, arresting four people in connection with the attack. The arrestees are Ratan Bepari, 32, his brother Pradip Bepari, 27, Ananda Bepari, 60, and Ananda’s nephew Sushila Bepari, 50. "An autopsy will be performed at Patuakhali Medical College Hospital morgue. Further legal action will be taken based on complaints filed and investigation findings," the OC said.

title: Teen raped in Panchagarh Case filed against 6
body: An 18-year-old girl was allegedly raped by three people while returning home from an event in Debiganj upazila of Panchagarh on Sunday night. Her 22-year-old aunt reportedly survived an attempted rape during the same incident. The victim’s father filed a case with Debiganj Police Station on Tuesday night against three local youths, Russel, Parvez and Biswajit, and three unidentified people, said Inspector (Investigation) Probir Kumar Sarkar of the police station yesterday. According to the case statement, the girl and her aunt had attended a cultural programme on Sunday afternoon. While returning home that night, they found the main gate of their house locked, as their family members had gone to a nearby place. They then asked a man nearby to arrange a van to take them there. The man later returned with five others in a battery-run rickshaw-van. The complaint said three of them forced the teenager into a house and allegedly raped her. At the same time, the other three allegedly took the aunt to the bank of the Karatoya river and attempted to rape her. The aunt reportedly escaped by throwing sand into the attackers’ eyes and returned to the victim’s house. The two women informed their family members about the incident the following morning. Police said medical examinations have been completed and steps are being taken to record the victims’ statements before a court. Efforts are underway to arrest the accused, they added.

title: Ivy released on bail
body: Selina Hayat Ivy, former mayor of Narayanganj City Corporation, was released from Kashimpur Central Women’s Jail last night. Jail Superintendent Shirin Akter said Ivy walked out of prison at 10:10pm after all necessary documents were verified. She reached her Deobhog residence in Narayanganj around 12:30am. She spoke to journalists inside her home. Thanking the government, Ivy said, “I want a humane government ... with everyone’s participation. In jail, there are many mothers like me who are innocent. I hope the government will be kind to them as well.” She expressed gratitude towards the judiciary. On May 17, the Supreme Court upheld the High Court’s orders granting ad-interim bail to Ivy on April 30 in two murder cases filed in connection with the July uprising. Chamber Judge of the SC’s Appellate Division, Justice Md Rezaul Haque, passed “no order” on two petitions filed by the state seeking a stay on the HC orders granting bail. Following the apex court chamber judge’s order, there was no legal bar to Ivy’s release, as the Appellate Division recently upheld her HC bail in 10 other cases. Ivy, also a senior leader of Narayanganj Awami League, was arrested on May 9 last year following a night-long raid at her residence. At the time, Additional Superintendent of Narayanganj Police Tarek Al Mehdi said Ivy was accused in at least five cases filed with different police stations in connection with killings and attacks during the July uprising. She was initially arrested in connection with the murder of RMG worker Minarul and was later shown arrested in nine other criminal cases. The High Court granted bail to Ivy in all 10 cases on November 9 last year and February 26 this year through separate orders following bail petitions filed on her behalf.

title: Pallabi rape, murder: Prime accused seeks pardon

title: Eight years on, Akramul’s widow refuses to give up fight for justice
body: Ayesha Begum, widow of former Teknaf councillor Akramul Haque, says she will not step back from her demand for justice, eight years after her husband was killed. The incident drew nationwide outrage in 2018 after audio recordings released by Ayesha appeared to capture events surrounding Akramul’s death. The clips, which quickly went viral, offered what many viewed as a rare glimpse into the reality behind extrajudicial killings. At a press conference at Cox’s Bazar Press Club on May 31, 2018, four days after the incident, Ayesha alleged that her husband had been murdered in cold blood and handed journalists four audio clips. In one recording, a woman can be heard screaming over the sound of gunfire. Ayesha said the voice was hers and that she was speaking to her husband on the phone when he was shot. Another clip captured a conversation between Akramul and his daughter. “I am going to Hnila,” Akramul says. When asked why, he replies, “For emergency work.” Moments later, his daughter asks: “Father, why are you crying?” ("Abbu tumi kanna kortecho je?") The recording ends there. The question struck a chord across the country and remains one of the most haunting elements of the case. Speaking recently, Ayesha described the past eight years as the most difficult period of her life. “There is the grief of losing my husband, and on top of that, two young daughters to raise,” she said. “Only one hope has kept me going -- that one day my husband’s killing will be brought to justice.” Due to security concerns, she said, she left Teknaf. Financial hardship has forced her to rely on loans to support her family. “The hardest part has been raising my two daughters,” she said. “They still ask for their father. They cry talking about him.” Regarding the arrest of former lawmaker Abdur Rahman Bodi in connection with the case, Ayesha said it could be considered the beginning of the justice process but not its conclusion. “My struggle will continue until those truly responsible are punished,” she said, adding that some suspects were reportedly abroad and should be brought back to face trial. Ayesha also expressed hope that Prime Minister Tarique Rahman would ensure a fair and impartial trial. Akramul, a three-time councillor and former president of the Teknaf unit of Jubo League, was killed in an alleged gunfight with Rapid Action Battalion members on Teknaf Marine Drive Road on May 26, 2018, during an anti-narcotics operation. Following the political changes of August 5, 2024, Ayesha said authorities asked her to file a complaint with the International Crimes Tribunal. After assuming office in February this year, ICT Chief Prosecutor Aminul Islam ordered a fresh review and directed investigators to submit a new report over the case. On April 23 he said that the Akramul case was among several major cases nearing formal charges. Investigators have identified 10 suspects, including ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina, former home minister Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal, former Rab chief Benazir Ahmed and former lawmaker Bodi, according to an official familiar with the investigation. On July 20, 2025, the International Crimes Tribunal-1 sent Bodi to jail after formally arresting him in connection with the killing. A senior official involved in the investigation alleged that Akramul was killed in a staged crossfire to suppress dissent, claiming he had become a target after speaking out against Bodi and drug trafficking in the area.

title: Narayanganj gang behind Mohammadpur mugging of 2 sisters: Police
body: The gang involved in the recent mugging of two sisters in Dhaka's Mohammadpur used to travel from Narayanganj in a pickup van, carry out robberies in the area, and return the same way to evade detection, Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) aid today. Police identified the gang during an investigation into the May 31 mugging incident in Mohammadpur, said Fazlul Karim, additional deputy commissioner (ADC) of DMP’s Tejgaon Division, during a briefing at the DMP Media Centre today. Following analysis of CCTV footage, police launched an investigation and arrested two suspects, Anwar Hossain and Jewel, also known as Arif, in connection with the robbery, he added. According to police records, accused Jewel has five cases filed against him at different police stations, including two narcotics cases, one robbery case, and two cases related to violence against women and children. The police official also said the members of the gang were former residents of Mohammadpur and were familiar with its roads and neighbourhoods. The two arrested suspects have provided information about the gang’s activities during interrogation. Based on their statements, police have recovered the pickup van and machetes used in the May 31 robbery. Police said several other suspects involved in the incident have been identified and are expected to be arrested soon. Replying to a question from journalists, ADC Fazlul Karim said both the owner and driver of the pickup van used in the crime were linked to the gang and are currently under police surveillance. According to police, the two sisters had returned to Dhaka from Thakurgaon in the early hours of May 31 after spending the Eid holidays there. They were mugged in front of their home on Nurjahan Road in Mohammadpur. The muggers threatened them with machetes before snatching a trolley bag, a handbag and other belongings and fled the scene.

title: Man sent to jail in Habiganj rape case
body: Police this afternoon sent a man to jail after he was accused of raping a woman at her home in Nabiganj upazila of Habiganj. The accused, Hossain Ahmed, 26, of Dakshin Gaznaipur village under Gaznaipur union, is a member of the union Chhatra Dal and a candidate for the post of union president, said Nabiganj upazila Chhatra Dal acting convener Sheikh Redwan Ahmed. According to the case documents, Hossain had become acquainted with a woman from the village and had allegedly been harassing her for some time. In the early hours of Monday, he allegedly broke into the victim's home, threatened her, and raped her. The woman's screams alerted her parents, who rushed in and detained the accused before handing him over to neighbours. The victim's mother filed a rape case against Hossain at Nabiganj Police Station last night, said the police station’s Officer-in-Charge (OC) Md Monayem Mia. The OC said the accused was produced before a court this afternoon and sent to jail. “We have been informed about the incident. The matter is under investigation. Further decisions will be taken based on the results of the investigation,” added Nabiganj upazila Chhatra Dal acting convener Redwan.

title: Ramisa murder trial: Sohel seeks pardon, Swapna denies charges during examination
body: Prime accused Sohel Rana today sought pardon from a special tribunal while being examined in a case filed over the rape and murder of eight-year-old schoolgirl Ramisa Akter in Dhaka’s Pallabi area. Judge Masrur Salekin of the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal in Dhaka Metropolitan also examined his wife and co-accused Swapna Khatun. Later, the judge set tomorrow for hearing closing arguments, bench assistant Pankoj Peter Gomes told The Daily Star. During today's hearing, Sohel, 31, and Swapna, 26, claimed to be innocent before the judge. Sohel told the court, "Sir, I am innocent. I seek acquittal. Please pardon me." He again blamed one Dollar from Mirpur-11 for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl. "Dollar was with me, but nobody saw him. Catch him, sir. He is guilty too," he said. Public Prosecutor Azizur Rahman Dulu said Sohel mentioned Dollar to confuse people about justice. "He [Sohel] is doing this now at someone's instigation. He did not mention the name 'Dollar' in his confessional statements," he added. Meanwhile, Swapna denied the charges, claiming she had done nothing wrong. Earlier in the day, Sohel and Swapna were produced before the tribunal from the lockup of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court in Dhaka for hearing. Yesterday, the tribunal completed testimony in a single day, a day after framing charges against the couple accused in the rape and murder case. A total of 16 prosecution witnesses, including the victim’s parents and elder sister, three neighbours, a doctor, a Dhaka metropolitan magistrate and the investigator, gave their statements before the tribunal. On May 24, investigator Ohiduzzaman, Sub-Inspector of Pallabi Police Station, submitted the charge sheet before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate's (CMM) Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel of rape, murder and destruction of evidence, and Swapna of destruction of evidence and providing false information. Several hours later, the CMM Court transferred the case to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal for trial. Ramisa, a class-2 student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 in the house of her neighbour, Sohel. The following day, Ramisa's father Abdul Hannan Mollah filed a case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing the couple and an unidentified person. According to the case statement, Sohel lured Ramisa into his room and raped her. Investigators said he later slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body to conceal the crime.

title: Man sued for raping daughter’s classmate in Bogura
body: A case has been filed against the father of a classmate of a class-5 student over allegations of rape and resulting pregnancy in Bogura’s Nandigram upazila. The victim’s mother filed the case as the complainant with Nandigram Police Station yesterday, said Md Tarikul Islam, officer-in-charge (OC) of the police station. According to the case statement, the incident took place on January 13 when the victim went to her friend’s house in search of her. As no one else was present in the house, the friend’s father, 40, allegedly raped her after threatening her and later warned her not to disclose the matter. The victim did not initially inform her family. Recently, as her physical condition changed, her family questioned her, following which she disclosed the incident. On May 24, she was taken to a local clinic for an ultrasound, which confirmed that she was four and a half months pregnant, the case statement added. The family later approached police on June 2 and filed a rape case against the accused, the OC said. “Raids have been conducted over the past two days in several places across Bogura and Natore to arrest the accused. Since the incident took place a long time ago, the accused appears to have fled sensing legal action,” said OC Tarikul.

title: Bangladesh Bank official found dead in Dhaka flat
body: Police on Tuesday recovered the body of a Bangladesh Bank official from his house in Dhaka's Ahmedbagh area of Mugda. The victim, Tanvir Hossain Shuvo, was an additional director of Bangladesh Bank. According to police, his partially decomposed body was found hanging inside his apartment after neighbours reported a foul smell coming from the house. Md Zahid Hossain, additional deputy commissioner (ADC) of Motijheel Division, said locals alerted police after noticing the odour coming from the flat. A police team subsequently arrived at the scene, broke open the door, and recovered the body. Police said an investigation is underway, and further details will be available after the completion of the inquest and post-mortem examination.

title: Journalist hacked in Munshiganj
body: Photojournalist Kabir Hossain, chief photographer of Prothom Alo’s feature department, was hacked and his younger brother beaten in an attack in Sirajdikhan upazila of Munshiganj yesterday. The incident took place around 12:30pm in Dosorpara village under Lotabdi Union. Kabir alleged that the attack was led by Jahangir Madbor, president of BNP’s Ward 7 unit in Lotabdi Union. The family has filed a complaint with police, who have already detained Jahangir. Kabir, 45, is the son of late Malek Madbor of Dosorpara. His injured younger brother, Takbir Hossain, is 44. According to family members and eyewitnesses, Kabir’s family runs a Lalon shrine (akhra) in Dosorpara. Since the fall of the Awami League government, BNP leader Jahangir Madbor and Alauddin Madbor, president of the local Jubo League unit, had allegedly been trying to seize the shrine and its land to establish a brick kiln. They had repeatedly threatened Kabir over the issue. Yesterday afternoon, while Kabir was working on the shrine’s boundary fence, Jahangir Madbor, his son Touhid Madbor, Jahed Madbor, Alauddin Madbor, Shahriar Madbor, Ahmed Madbor, and several others allegedly attacked him. During the assault, Kabir was struck on the head with a sharp weapon. When Takbir tried to intervene, he was also attacked. The injured brothers were taken to Sirajdikhan Upazila Health Complex. Kabir was later referred to Dhaka Medical College Hospital. Asked about the attack, Sirajdikhan upazila BNP General Secretary M Haidar Ali told Prothom Alo, “The perpetrator will not be spared under any circumstances. Organisational action will be taken against him.” Sirajdikhan Police Station Officer-in-Charge Abdul Hannan said, “We have already detained the main accused, Jahangir. Efforts are underway to arrest those involved.”

title: Boy killed by mortar shell in Bandarban
body: A 12-year-old boy was killed in a mortar shell explosion near the Bangladesh-Myanmar border in Bandarban’s Naikhongchhari upazila yesterday afternoon. The victim, Satnaing Tanchangya, was the son of Kinghla Tanchangya of Baishphari Tanchangya Para in Ghumdhum union, said police. His native home is in Medai village under Dekibunia in Myanmar’s Rakhine state, said Mohammad Mozzamel Haque, officer-in-charge of Naikhongchhari Police Station. Police and local representatives said Satnaing and his family came to Bandarban from Myanmar’s Rakhine two years ago following the war between the Arakan Army and Myanmar’s military junta. According to police, the explosion took place in the Moringajhiri area, around 100 yards northeast of Border Pillar 39 in Ward No 3 of Ghumdhum union. Citing locals, the OC said the boy had gone to a jhum field with his parents in the morning. While his parents were constructing a temporary shelter, he wandered around the area and played by himself. At one point, he found a mortar shell and started playing with it. The device exploded, killing him on the spot. His parents were present in the field at the time. The OC said locals later recovered the body and brought it to the Baishphari area. The exact circumstances of the incident will be determined after an investigation. Lt Col SM Khairul Alam, commanding officer of BGB-34 Naikhongchhari Battalion, said a child died in an explosion at a jhum field near the zero line adjacent to Border Pillar 41 in the Baishphari border area of Ghumdhum. He said the matter is being treated with utmost importance and necessary measures have been taken. Babul Chakma, a member of Ghumdhum Union Parishad, expressed concern that unexploded device from past clashes between the Arakan Army and Myanmar’s military junta may still be scattered across several border areas. He urged the authorities to take effective measures to identify and remove such hazardous explosives to prevent further casualties.

title: Ramisa killing trial: Testifying ends in a day, arguments today
body: A special tribunal in Dhaka yesterday completed recording witness testimony in a single day in the case filed over the rape and murder of eight-year-old schoolgirl Ramisa Akter. The proceeding came just a day after charges were framed against prime accused Sohel Rana, 31, and his wife, Swapna Khatun, 26, over the May 19 crime that sparked nationwide outrage and prompted the government to pledge swift justice. Judge Masrur Salekin of the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal in Dhaka Metropolitan recorded statements from 16 prosecution witnesses, bench assistant Pankoj Peter Gomes told The Daily Star. The witnesses included the victim’s parents and elder sister, three neighbours, a doctor, a Dhaka metropolitan magistrate and the investigating officer, said Special Public Prosecutor Azizur Rahman Dulu. The court is scheduled to examine the accused and hear arguments today. Supreme Court lawyer Musa Kalimullah represented the accused as state defence counsel and cross-examined the witnesses. Ramisa’s father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, was the first witness. At one stage, he became emotional and, after feeling unwell, obtained the court’s permission to continue his testimony while seated. He said he left home for work around 9:30am on May 19 and was later informed by his wife that Ramisa was missing. After returning home, he found a crowd gathered outside the building. His wife told him Ramisa was trapped inside a neighbouring flat, whose occupants were not responding despite repeated requests to open the door. “A man was already trying to break the lock… I then ran downstairs, brought a hammer, and tried to break the lock. Other people also joined in.” “Eventually, the lock broke… After entering, … I saw blood inside one of the toilets. At that time, I saw Swapna standing silently. The room where the accused lived was locked. One of the people present lifted a steel bed and found Ramisa’s head inside a bucket. Then, I lost consciousness,” he said. He added, “Later, the police arrived and completed the necessary procedures. Afterwards, I went to the police station and filed the case based on these events.” Then Ramisa’s mother, Parveen Akhter, testified. She said while she was cooking that morning, she asked her elder daughter, Raisa, to visit her uncle’s house. Ramisa also wanted to go, but Raisa left without her, and Parveen did not realise the child had gone out alone. “While I was in the kitchen, I heard screams. I thought it was the child from the neighbouring flat making noise. A little later, I noticed that our door was open.” Parveen continued: “A short while later, Raisa returned home alone. I asked her, ‘Why are you alone? Where is Ramisa?’ I went downstairs but could not find Ramisa there. I asked people whether they had seen her.” She said she had noticed one of her daughter’s shoes in front of the door of the accused’s flat on the second floor. “I knocked on the door, but no one responded. Then I screamed. People from different flats came over. They also knocked on the door, but no one opened it. Later, 10 or 12 people came upstairs. By that time, my husband had returned from work.” She further said, “After the door was opened and we went inside, I saw the bathroom was flooded with blood. I saw my daughter’s head in one place and her body in another. At that time, I saw Swapna inside the flat.” Pointing to Swapna in the dock, Parveen said she repeatedly pleaded with Swapna, a neighbour on the same floor, to open the door, but she did not. She also pointed to Sohel and stated: “Later I heard that he [Sohel] raped my daughter, murdered her, and escaped by cutting through the window grill.” Raisa testified via camera because she is a minor, according to the prosecution. The day’s proceedings concluded with testimony from investigating officer Ohiduzzaman, a sub-inspector of Pallabi Police Station. Amid growing public anger, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on May 23 said the maximum punishment for Ramisa’s killer would be ensured within a month, while Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed promised an exemplary trial at the earliest. The swift proceedings have been welcomed by rights activists. Supreme Court lawyer Ishrat Hasan praised the expeditious trial and expressed hope that all child rape and murder cases would receive the same urgency. “Justice should not be fast-tracked only in a few high-profile cases; every victim deserves timely justice,” she said. Fahmida Akhter, a lawyer with the Bangladesh National Women Lawyers’ Association who works with rape survivors at the One Stop Crisis Centre of Dhaka Medical College Hospital, said, “When the charge sheet is filed quickly, and the judicial process is completed within a short period, it reinforces the rule of law and increases public confidence in justice. Such confidence can also help deter future crimes.” Ramisa, a second-grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded in the flat of her neighbour Sohel on May 19. The next day, her father filed a case with Pallabi Police Station against the couple and an unidentified person. According to the case statement, Sohel took Ramisa to his room and raped her. Investigators said he later slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body to conceal the crime. On May 24, SI Ohiduzzaman submitted the charge sheet to the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate’s Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel of rape, murder and destruction of evidence, and Swapna of destruction of evidence and providing false information. The charge sheet named 18 prosecution witnesses. Several hours later, the CMM Court transferred the case to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal for trial.

title: Body of 75-yr-old recovered from Mirpur
body: Police recovered the body of a 75-year-old woman from an apartment in the capital’s Mirpur on Sunday night. The deceased, Nurjahan Begum, lived with her daughter, Fatima Nasrin Sultana, on the fourth floor of a five-storey building in Block C of Mirpur 6. Pallabi Police Station Officer-in-Charge Md Hasan Basir said they recovered the body after receiving a call on the national emergency hotline -- 999. According to the OC, the victim has three sons -- one a joint secretary, one a teacher at Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology, and the other living in Canada. Since the recovery of the body, allegations of severe neglect by her children have surfaced across the media. Sub-Inspector Shamsur Rahman of the police station said that Fatima’s husband, who was also a university teacher, passed away seven to eight years ago. She has no children of her own. When police and locals visited, the apartment, particularly the victim’s room, was found in an extremely squalid and unhygienic condition. The incident has sparked outrage among neighbours. Around 10 to 12 locals were seen protesting in front of the building yesterday, demanding a thorough investigation and punishment for the deceased’s children. Speaking to The Daily Star, Syed Mohammad Hasan Palash, a neighbour and local mosque committee leader, said some youths went to the local mosque to fetch a funeral bier after Maghrib prayers on Sunday. When asked who had passed away, they evaded the question, prompting Palash and a few others to follow them to the apartment. “We had to force our way in.” Describing the scene, Palash said the woman’s room was reeking of a foul odour, completely dark, and littered with garbage. A video recorded by him showed the floor blackened with accumulated dirt and waste scattered all around. He alleged that the body appeared to have been decomposing for over a week and that the elderly woman had apparently been starved and deprived of basic medical treatment. The OC, however, said the daughter claimed her mother died on Sunday and that she had given her a packet of food just the day before. Following an autopsy at Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital on Monday, morgue sources corroborated the daughter’s timeline. They told this newspaper that the body was relatively fresh and had not undergone significant decomposition. Morgue sources suspect a localised decay occurred because the bedridden woman had been lying on the same side for a prolonged period. Following the autopsy, police handed the body over to the family. When this correspondent visited the Mirpur house yesterday, no one answered the door despite repeated ringing of the doorbell. The victim’s daughter and sons also could not be reached for comment by phone despite repeated attempts.

title: Mob beats 70-year-old over alleged rape attempt of child in Ctg's Halishahar
body: A 72-year-old man was beaten by a mob after he allegedly attempted to rape a 9-year-old girl in the Halishahar area of the port city on this evening. The arrestee has been identified as Mohammed Hossen, confirmed CMP Deputy Commissioner (West Zone) Alamgir Hossen. The incident took place near the B-block public school area in Halishahar. On information, police rushed to the scene, rescued the man from the mob and arrested him in connection with the alleged attempted rape, he added. The child -- a class 3 student, had gone alone to a nearby shop to buy chips around 5:00pm, when the accused allegedly molested and tried to rape her. The girl returned home and revealed the matter to her mother. The mother immediately took the child back to the spot, where the girl identified the accused. Enraged locals present at the scene caught the accused and gave him a beating, but police reached the spot, apprehended the man, and removed him from the scene. The victim's mother has since filed a written complaint with Halishahar Police Station. A video circulated on social media showed hundreds of locals chasing a police van and hurling brickbats at it.

title: Elderly man arrested for attempted rape of 4-yr-old in Shariatpur
body: Police arrested a 65-year-old man yesterday for allegedly attempting to rape a four-year-old girl in Shariatpur Sadar upazila. The incident allegedly occurred around 1:00pm yesterday when the child was playing on the bank of a pond near her house. Palong Model Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Shah Alam confirmed the matter to The Daily Star, saying, Hasan Molla allegedly took the girl into the pond and attempted to rape her. The child’s screams alerted two nearby teenage girls, who informed the girl's mother. Local residents then detained Hasan after the mother raised an alarm. As enraged locals tried to beat up the suspect, police intervened and rescued him before taking him into custody. The OC said initial attempts by police from the Burirhat outpost to take him into custody faced resistance from locals, prompting additional forces to rescue and arrest him. The child’s father filed a case against Hasan under the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act, 2000.

title: Don't click that link: How fake AI traffic fine scam is targeting vehicle owners
body: Imagine receiving a text message claiming that an artificial intelligence-powered traffic camera has caught your vehicle speeding. The message includes a precise fine amount, an offence date and a strict deadline, warning of legal action if you do not pay immediately. Fear and urgency kick in. Conveniently, the message also contains a website link for payment. If this happens to you, stop. It is a trap. Following the recent introduction of automated traffic monitoring systems to detect violations in Dhaka, a highly organised group of cybercriminals has launched a widespread phishing campaign across Bangladesh. The scammers are sending mass text messages containing fake traffic prosecution notices. These messages redirect unsuspecting vehicle owners to fraudulent websites designed to resemble the official Bangladesh Road Transport Authority (BRTA) Service Portal. Once victims enter sensitive information, scammers can gain access to their bank accounts or mobile wallets. "I barely use my car nowadays since the Metro Rail started operations," said Ataur Rahman, a private job holder. "So when I received a text message out of the blue claiming I had a traffic violation, I was utterly surprised. Thankfully, I had already seen warnings about these fraudulent texts shared on various social media groups dedicated to traffic and car enthusiasts. Recognising the pattern, I refrained from clicking the link or interacting with the message at all." Another car owner, Amzad Hossain Tohin, posted on Facebook, saying, "I just got a text from a phone number with dialing code of Philippines for over speeding. Later, I heard many of friends also got such scam messages. We all should be careful before clicking the links embedded with the fake case SMSs." Both the BRTA and the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) have issued urgent warnings, clarifying that they never send SMS alerts containing payment links from personal or generic mobile numbers. Official traffic fines under the Road Transport Act, 2018 are delivered through formal mail, signed by a technical unit officer and sent directly to the vehicle owner's registered address. In rare cases where the DMP sends official SMS notices, they originate only from two designated numbers: 01320-042207 and 01320-042227. Authorities have reminded the public that government agencies never request bank passwords, mobile financial service (MFS) PINs or one-time passwords (OTPs). They advised anyone receiving suspicious messages not to click on embedded links or make payments without verification. Instead, recipients should contact official helplines or call the national emergency service at 999 to confirm whether a notice is genuine. Officials have urged citizens to remain vigilant as cybercriminals increasingly exploit public awareness of new technologies and government services. ASM Shamim Reza, managing director of The Team Phoenix Group, a cybersecurity ecosystem-building initiative, said, "Scammers are increasingly using fear and urgency to trick people into acting before they think. Any traffic fine notification received via SMS, email, or messaging apps should be treated with caution unless it comes through official government channels." "Citizens should never click on links in unsolicited messages or enter banking, card, OTP, or mobile financial service credentials on websites reached through those links," he added. Verify fines directly through official BRTA channels instead of using links sent in messages. Check website addresses carefully. Scammers often use lookalike domains that closely resemble legitimate government portals. Never share OTPs, card details, PINs or MFS credentials in response to a fine notification. Be suspicious of messages that create urgency, threaten penalties or demand immediate payment. If you suspect a scam attempt, report it to the relevant authorities. If you have already shared information, immediately contact your bank or MFS provider.

title: Woman hacked to death in Netrokona home; husband, son injured
body: A woman was hacked to death allegedly by a local rickshaw-puller inside her home in Katli area of Netrokona municipality last night. The deceased was identified as Monowara Begum, 55. Her husband, Abu Chan, 60, and son, Munna Mia, 25, were critically wounded in the attack at their second-floor flat sometime before 9:00pm. Al Mamun Sarkar, officer-in-charge of Netrokona Sadar Police Station, confirmed the information. Police and local residents said there was a power outage at the time. Taking advantage of the darkness, the attacker allegedly entered the apartment and hacked Monowara with a sharp weapon. When Munna rushed to help his mother, he was also attacked. Abu Chan suffered injuries while trying to protect his wife and son. The OC said locals detained the suspect, Abdur Rashid, a rickshaw puller, immediately after the incident and handed him over to police. Quoting Monowara's daughter, Liza Moni, the OC said Rashid and Monowara's family had known each other for years. As neighbours, Rashid frequently borrowed money from the family and regularly visited their home. "We initially suspect the attack may have stemmed from a financial dispute. However, the matter is still under investigation. Rashid has claimed he was intoxicated at the time, but we are trying to determine the actual motive," the OC said. According to police, Abu Chan and Munna were initially taken to Netrokona Sadar Hospital. As Munna's condition deteriorated, he was later transferred to Mymensingh Medical College Hospital for advanced treatment.

title: Man jailed, fined for covering motorcycle number plate to evade AI camera
body: A court has sentenced a man to one month’s imprisonment and fined him Tk 2,000 after a video went viral on social media showing him covering a motorcycle’s number plate with white scotch tape to evade detection by AI-powered traffic surveillance cameras. The person was identified as Lablu Haque, 38, a resident of the Lalbagh area in Dhaka. In default of payment, he will have to serve an additional seven days in jail. The verdict came after the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) produced him before the court today. The punishment was handed down under the Sections 16(3) and 72 of the Road Transport Act, 2018. Additional Commissioner (Traffic) of DMP, Anisur Rahman, disclosed the information at a press briefing at the DMP Media Center today. Earlier, a video circulated widely on social media showed a motorcyclist wearing a helmet while the vehicle’s number plate was partially concealed with white scotch tape. Anisur Rahman said the incident came to the attention of DMP on May 21, prompting concern that such deceptive tactics could encourage others to evade surveillance systems. He said the matter was taken seriously and an investigation was launched immediately. However, identifying the rider was initially difficult as his face was not clearly visible in the footage. Later, with assistance from the Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime (CTTC) unit, CCTV footage from different parts of the capital was analysed. By matching the motorcycle type and registration details, investigators identified the suspect. Deputy Commissioner of CTTC Mohammad Rakib Khan said the accused was later arrested from the Karwan Bazar area. Anisur Rahman added that the aim of DMP is not only punishment but also to raise awareness for voluntary compliance with traffic laws, warning that strict legal action will continue against violations.

title: ‘May no other parent lose a child this way’, says Ramisa’s father
body: The father of eight-year-old Ramisa Akter, who was raped and murdered in the capital’s Pallabi area, today demanded the highest punishment for the accused, saying no other parent should have to endure such a tragedy. “I expect justice for the brutal rape and murder of my innocent child. I want a fair trial and speedy execution of the verdict. May no other parent lose a child this way. May no family suffer such heartbreak,” Abdul Hannan Molla told reporters before testifying at the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Prevention Tribunal, where the recording of testimonies in the sensational case began today. Judge Masrur Salekin of the tribunal is scheduled to record testimonies of key witnesses in the case today. Besides Ramisa’s father, witnesses summoned to testify include the magistrate who recorded the confessional statement of the prime accused, doctors, officials involved in collecting evidence and local residents. Earlier in the morning, prime accused Sohel Rana was brought to the court from Keraniganj Central Jail while his wife, Swapna Khatun, was produced from Kashimpur Jail. They were kept at the Dhaka Metropolitan Sessions Judge Court lockup and were expected to be presented before the tribunal during the hearing. Yesterday, the same tribunal framed charges against Sohel Rana and Swapna Khatun and ordered the commencement of the trial. The court also summoned 17 witnesses to testify in the case. Ramisa Akter, daughter of Abdul Hannan Molla, was raped and murdered by Sohel Rana, tenant of a neighbouring flat, on May 19. On May 24, the investigating officer of the case – Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station – submitted the charge sheet against Sohel Rana and his wife Swapna Akter to the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate’s Court in Dhaka. According to the case details, accused Sohel lured her into his room and later killed her after rape. Ramisa’s decapitated body was found beneath the bed while her severed head was found inside a bucket in the bathroom. While Swapna was detained from the scene, Sohel Rana managed to escape by cutting through a window grille. He was tracked down and arrested by police later in Fatullah of Narayanganj.

title: Ramisa murder: Tribunal frames charges against Sohel, Swapna
body: A special tribunal in Dhaka yesterday framed charges against prime accused Sohel Rana and his wife Swapna Khatun in the case filed over the rape and murder of eight‑year‑old schoolgirl Ramisa Akhter in Pallabi. The couple pleaded not guilty after Judge Masrur Salekin of the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal in Dhaka Metropolitan read out charges, said bench assistant Pankoj Peter Gomes. Meanwhile, Sohel attempted to introduce a new name in the case, telling reporters on the court premises that a man called “Dollar” was also involved. His earlier confessional statement before a metropolitan magistrate on May 20, however, made no mention of Dollar, according to police. Investigating officer Ohiduzzaman, sub‑inspector of Pallabi Police Station, said evidence confirmed no third person was present at the scene of the crime before or after the incident. Eyewitnesses saw Sohel fleeing alone. “The prime accused is deliberately trying to jeopardise trial proceedings,” he observed. Sohel, while being escorted to the tribunal, told reporters: “I’m at fault, but so is Dollar. I’m not the only culprit.” Standing in the dock, he shouted at lawyers: “I did not commit the rape; I only dismembered the body. Dollar committed the rape. I have sinned, so punish me for that sin.” He further claimed Dollar had promised Tk 2 lakh if he brought the girl to him, but police stopped him from speaking further. He also insisted his wife was innocent. Ramisa’s father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, told The Daily Star: “The accused has come up with the name Dollar to delay the trial. We want his highest punishment through the quickest trial.” The judge fixed today for the start of trial, with Ramisa’s father scheduled to testify first. On May 24, SI Ohiduzzaman submitted the charge sheet to the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate’s Court, accusing Sohel of rape, murder and destruction of evidence, and Swapna of destroying evidence and giving false information. The case was later transferred to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal. Ramisa, a second‑grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 in the home of neighbours Sohel and Swapna. Her father filed a case the next day against the couple and an unidentified person. Investigators said Sohel lured Ramisa into his room, raped her, then slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body.

title: Idol at Pirojpur temple vandalised, set on fire; valuables looted
body: Micreants broke into a temple, vandalised an idol before setting it on fire, and looted valuables at the Pirojpur Municipal Cremation Ground, opposite the Pirojpur PWD Office in the town, early today. According to temple authorities, the miscreants entered the temple premises during the early hours and stole around Tk 5,000 in cash from the donation box, along with several brass items. They also vandalised an idol inside the temple and subsequently set it on fire. Police visited the spot after being informed and conducted an initial inspection. Superintendent of Police of Pirojpur Mohammad Manzur Ahamed Siddique said law enforcement agencies are reviewing CCTV footage from nearby areas to identify those involved in the incident. Temple priest Pankaj Tiwari said the intruders broke into the temple in the middle of the night, looted valuables, and desecrated the idol before fleeing the scene. Meanwhile, Md Saiful Islam, officer-in-charge of Pirojpur Sadar Police Station, said no general diary (GD) or case were filed as of Monday afternoon. “However, we have asked the temple authorities to submit a written complaint with the police station,” he said.

title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel named ‘Dollar’ to delay trial, mislead public, IO says
body: Sohel Rana, the prime accused in the Ramisa rape and murder case, spread false information about a third person’s involvement in an attempt to mislead the public and delay the trial, police said today. While being escorted to the courtroom, Sohel denied full responsibility and claimed that a man named “Dollar” was responsible for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl. Sub-Inspector Md Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station, who is also the investigating officer (IO) of the case, told The Daily Star the evidence and eyewitness testimonies have proven that Sohel raped and killed Ramisa and no third party was involved. “The accused is intentionally mentioning various names to cover up his crimes, mislead the investigation, obstruct the judicial process, and spread rumours among the public,” he said. “While he was attempting to dismember the child’s body to conceal the crime, neighbours arrived, forcing him to flee by breaking a window. His wife took no action to stop the crimes and helped him escape, making her equally culpable,” he added. Ramisa's father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, also said Sohel staged the drama on the court premises to save himself. "He wanted to prolong the trial process by spreading false information. After arrest, his wife also said that only she and Sohel were inside the room during the brutal murder," he said. "We want justice as soon as possible," Hannan said, from his bed at the National Institute of Cardiovascular Diseases. Earlier in the day, Sohel shouted on the court premises: “I did not commit the rape; I only dismembered the body. A man named Dollar committed the rape. I have sinned, so punish me for that sin." Sohel made the claim while being escorted to the courtroom of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal. At that time, Sohel further claimed that Dollar had promised to pay him Tk 2 lakh if he brought the girl to him. Sohel also claimed that his wife, Swapna Khatun, was innocent. In the morning, Sohel and Swapna were brought to the lock-up of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court in Dhaka. Later, Judge Masrur Salekin of Children Violence Suppression Tribunal framed charges against the couple in the case over the rape and murder of Ramisa in Dhaka's Pallabi area. Both accused pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out, said Bench Assistant Pankoj Peter Gomes. Ramisa, a second-grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 in the house of her neighbour, Sohel.

title: SSC examinee dies in Habiganj; family alleges rape, torture
body: A 16-year-old girl who sat for this year's SSC examinations died at a hospital in Habiganj today after being found unconscious by the road last night. Her family alleged that she was raped and tortured. The deceased was from Ajmiriganj upazila. Following the death of her mother, she had been living and studying at her maternal grandfather's home in a village of Baniachang upazila. She had completed her SSC written examinations and was awaiting practical tests. Her maternal grandfather told The Daily Star that the girl had been in a relationship with a lawyer's assistant, Jibon Das, from Sunaru village in Baniachang. Days before the incident, Jibon had taken the girl to a temple in Habiganj town, claiming that he intended to marry her. However, temple authorities refused to solemnise the marriage after learning that she was a minor and sent her back to her family. Yesterday morning, he said, Jibon again took the victim away from the family home without their knowledge or consent. At around 8:00pm last night, she was found unconscious beside a road on the outskirts of Habiganj town. “Her nose and mouth were bloodied when she was discovered,” he added. She was rushed to Habiganj 250-Bed District Sadar Modern Hospital, where she died early today. Dr Aminul Islam Sarkar, superintendent of the hospital, confirmed that initial information suggested sexual assault. However, a full account will only be possible after the autopsy report, he said. Sheikh Nazmul Haque, officer-in-charge of Baniachang Police Station, said the matter was being investigated on all fronts. “We are treating this seriously and examining all possibilities -- whether rape or other causes. Appropriate legal action will follow once the autopsy and investigation are complete,” he said.

title: 2 women robbed at machete-point outside Mohammadpur home
body: A video has gone viral on social media where two women were seen being robbed at machete-point outside their home in Dhaka's Mohammadpur. According to police, the incident occurred around 3:00am on Saturday on Noorjahan Road as the victims returned to Dhaka after the Eid-ul-Azha holidays. The footage shows the two women standing in front of their house after getting off a rickshaw, with the puller standing nearby. Suddenly, two men approach them, one wielding a machete. The suspect, clad in a lungi, a black T-shirt, and a cap, threatens the women with the weapon before snatching their luggage, bags, and other belongings. The victims had arrived in Dhaka's Shyamoli by bus from Thakurgaon, said Mohammadpur Police Station Inspector (Investigation) Rakibuzzaman Rakib. "They then took a rickshaw to their home, only to be targeted by muggers right outside their gate," he said. Police have identified one of the suspects involved in the robbery. "We have identified one person involved in the incident and are trying to arrest him," Inspector Rakibuzzaman said.

title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel Rana mentions new name as charges framed

title: 17-year-old killed by younger sibling at Kalabagan
body: A 17-year-old SSC examinee was allegedly killed by his younger brother following an altercation at their residence in Dhaka's Kalabagan area last night. The deceased was identified as Sadman Wasif Supanto, a student of Government Laboratory High School and College who had recently sat for the Secondary School Certificate (SSC) examinations. Police detained his younger brother, aged around 15, in connection with the incident. The incident took place around 9:30pm at their apartment on Free School Street in Kalabagan, where the two brothers lived by themselves, said Sub-Inspector (SI) Shamsul Haque Sumon of Kalabagan Police Station. The brothers locked into an argument that escalated into a physical fight. At one stage, the younger brother allegedly struck Supanto on the head with an iron dumbbell. Supanto suffered severe head injuries and was rushed to a private hospital, where doctors declared him dead around 1:00am, the SI said. Police later recovered the body from the hospital and sent it to the Dhaka Medical College morgue for an autopsy. The SI said the brothers' parents divorced in 2021. Their father, Sirajul Salekin, lives in Canada, while their mother, a doctor by profession, remarried and lives in Middle Badda area. Police said the two brothers had been living alone in the Kalabagan apartment and were often involved in quarrel over various family-related issues. "We suspect longstanding tensions stemming from their family situation may have contributed to the incident," the SI said. A case is being prepared in connection with the killing.

title: Villagers set fire to alleged robber's house in Habiganj
body: Angry villagers allegedly set fire to the house of a man accused in multiple robbery cases in Nabiganj upazila of Habiganj early today following a village meeting over his alleged criminal activities. The accused, Wahid Miah, is facing multiple robbery charges, said Officer-in-Charge of Nabiganj Police Station Md Monayem Mia. The OC said a meeting of the village panchayat committee was held last night, where residents alleged that Wahid's criminal activities were tarnishing the village's reputation. It is alleged that after the meeting, a group of villagers went to the house of Wahid and set it on fire. The blaze quickly engulfed the structure, causing extensive damage. After receiving information, members of the Nabiganj Fire Service and police rushed to the scene and brought the fire under control, the OC said. Police later visited the spot. The matter is currently under investigation, the OC added.

title: Man, woman found dead in Ctg hotel room
body: A man and a woman were found dead in a hotel room in Chattogram's Foy's Lake area this morning. The deceased were identified as Md Ripon, 47, and Sonia, 30. Their bodies were recovered from a room at Royal Park Hotel near Chattogram Zoo, police said. According to Azad Hossain, sub-inspector of Akbar Ali Shah Police Station, the two checked into a fourth-floor room of the hotel on Thursday night, introducing themselves as husband and wife. Hotel staff discovered the bodies this morning, he said. "One was lying on the floor, while the other was found hanging," the police officer said, quoting hotel staff. He added that employees told investigators the hanging body fell to the floor after staff slightly pulled it. Officials from the CID's Crime Scene Unit and the Police Bureau of Investigation were collecting evidence at the scene as of filing this report. Police said they are investigating the circumstances surrounding the deaths.

title: Man in custody over alleged rape of 7-year-old in Noakhali, police say
body: Locals beat up and handed over a man to police over accusations of raping a seven-year-old girl in Senbagh upazila of Noakhali last night. Md Sohel, 34, an auto-rickshaw driver, is currently in police custody, said Md Abdur Rahim Sarkar, officer-in-charge (OC) of Senbagh Police Station. According to the victim’s family and local residents, the accused was caught around 8:00pm after a mass beating and handed over to police. Police said preparations are underway to file a case in connection with the incident. “Necessary legal action will be taken based on the complaint filed by the victim’s family,” the OC added. Family members alleged that the child’s mother witnessed the incident and confronted the driver, who fled the scene. As news spread, locals began searching for him. Around 7:30pm, Sohel was allegedly caught in Notun Bazar area, after which residents called the national emergency service number 999 before handing him over to police.

title: Man arrested over attempted rape of girl
body: A 55-year-old man named Quddus Mia has been detained by locals in Shailkupa upazila of Jhenaidah on allegations of attempting to rape a seven-year-old girl. He was later handed over to the police. The incident took place in Nagirhat village on Saturday, said Shailkupa Police Station Officer-in-Charge Humayun Kabir Molla yesterday. The victim’s father filed a case under the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act, 2000. “The accused was taken into custody after locals detained him. He was shown arrested and produced before a court today,” the OC said.

title: Feud within family, gambling clash leave trail of deaths
body: At least nine people were killed due to previous enmity and the bodies of two others were recovered in five districts over the last two days. One of the incidents was the murder of 28-year-old Amena and her one-and-a-half-year-old son Aswad allegedly by one of their relatives following a family dispute in Manikganj’s Daulatput upazila. Quoting locals, police said there was a longstanding family dispute between Yusuf Molla, 35, and his elder brother Salam Molla, 40, who is Amena’s husband. On Saturday night, Salam was at his shop. Taking the chance, Yusuf allegedly attacked Amena and her child with a sharp weapon in their residence at around 10:00pm, said Swapan Kumar Sarkar, the officer-in-charge of Daulatpur Police Station. He later attacked Salam while he was returning home after closing his shop. Salam was admitted to the local health complex. In a separate incident in Manikganj Sadar upazila, a youth was hacked to death by unidentified miscreants early yesterday. The deceased was identified as Md Sajib, 28, of Uttar Putail village. The incident took place around 1:15am over previous enmity, said Ikram Hossain, the OC of Manikganj Sadar Police Station. Over at Khulna, police recovered the bodies of a woman and two children from a house in the city on Saturday evening. The deceased were identified as Fatema Begum, 60, Shamim Bepari, 13, and Mostakim Bepari, 4. The bodies were recovered around 6:00pm from a house in the Darul Aman area, said Md Rafiqul Islam, the OC of Sonadanga Police Station. According to preliminary findings, Fatema’s second husband might have killed them, he said. In Noakhali, miscreants allegedly beat a young man to death with iron rods on Saturday night. The victim, Jobayer Hossain alias Rakib, 24, was a resident of Sharifpur union under Begumganj upazila. Quoting family members, police said a dispute had reportedly arisen three or four days earlier between the son of Rakib’s cousin and a local shopkeeper. On Saturday night at around 9:30pm, Rakib and his younger brother, Rimon, were heading home from the market when a group of assailants allegedly attacked them. Rakib suffered severe injuries after being struck on the head and other parts of his body with iron rods, police said. He was taken to the hospital, where doctors declared him dead, said Md Shamsuzzaman, the OC of Begumganj Model Police Station. In another incident in Noakhali Sadar upazila, businessman Md Kamal Uddin, 48, died while trying to intervene in a clash between two groups over a dispute related to a gambling den. Shriram Chandra Bhattacharya, inspector (operations) of Sudharam Model Police Station, said Kamal’s nephew Farhad was first assaulted over a gambling-related dispute at Dadpur area at around 10:00pm on Saturday night. Kamal later went to stop the fight but was attacked by members of the opposing group and subsequently lost consciousness. He was taken to the hospital, where doctors declared him dead, said his family members. However, police said they are investigating the death and did not initially find visible injury marks on the body. In Patuakhali, a teenage boy was stabbed to death allegedly by miscreants on Saturday night. The deceased was identified as Tajul Islam, 16, of Machuakhali village under Kalapara upazila. Quoting family members, police said Tajul joined a wedding ceremony on Saturday night in the village. At around 11:30pm, some people called and took him to a nearby secluded area and stabbed him. Hearing his screams, locals rushed there, rescued him, and took him to the nearby health complex, where on-duty doctors declared him dead. Following the incident, local residents detained the three youths on suspicion and handed them over to police, said Nazrul Islam, the OC of Kalapara Police Station. In Pirojpur, police recovered the bodies of two men from separate places in Mathbaria upazila yesterday morning. The deceased were identified as Abdur Rashid, 50, a farmer, and Mohammad Sagar, 28, a motorcycle driver. Both were residents of Dakkhin Amragachia village. The bodies were found less than a kilometre apart. According to family members, Rashid left his home at around 10:00pm on Saturday night after receiving a phone call and did not return. His body was found yesterday morning on the veranda of a local maktab near his house. In a separate incident, Sagar’s body was discovered beside his home. Family members alleged that he had been killed and his body left there by unidentified assailants at around 1:30am. Investigators are yet to determine how the men died, said Partha Chakraborty, additional superintendent of police in Pirojpur. [Our correspondents from Manikganj, Noakhali, Pirojpur, Khulna and Patuakhali contributed to the report]

title: Mob killings hit six-month high in May
body: At least 32 people were killed in mob violence in May -- the highest monthly death toll in the past six months. Another 71 people were critically injured in at least 69 incidents of mob violence, according to the Manabadhikar Shongskriti Foundation (MSF). In its monthly report released yesterday, the rights body said, “The number of people killed in mob violence rose from 21 [in April] to 32 in May, while the number of injured increased from 49 to 71, reflecting a clear rise in the tendency of people taking the law into their own hands.” Law enforcers are also being attacked during incidents of mob violence, it said. In April, 21 people were killed and 49 were critically injured in mob beatings across the country, while 19 people were killed and 31 were injured the month before. According to MSF’s tally, 18 people were killed in February and 21 in January, up from 10 deaths recorded in December 2025. Mob violence has continued unabated despite repeated assurances from Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed that such acts would not be tolerated. The issue has also been discussed in parliament on several occasions. Speaking at a Police Week programme on May 10, Salahuddin said the government would amend existing laws or enact new ones if necessary to curb mob violence. In its May report, undersigned by its founding president Advocate Sultana Kamal, MSF said public safety has become a serious concern amid the alarming rise in mob violence. The group’s statistics show that, of those killed in mob violence in May, 14 were attacked over allegations of theft, four following altercations, two over allegations of robbery, two over allegations of attempted rape and sexual assault, one over allegations of murder, one over “insulting remarks”, one over an allegation of mugging, one over drug peddling, and six over various other allegations. At least 35 of the injured victims were later handed over to police, it added. In another April-May comparative analysis, the MSF said violence against women and children, including rape, had also risen at an alarming rate. Incidents of rape, attempted rape, gang rape, and murder following rape have all increased significantly, indicating a severe deterioration in the situation of women and children in the country, it said. The rights body’s findings show that at least 326 incidents of violence against women and children were recorded in May, 12 more than the previous month. At least 78 rapes were reported in May -- nearly 40 percent higher than the number of rapes recorded in April. Besides, 16 gang rapes and six cases of murder following rape were reported. Fourteen gang rapes were and two murders following rape were reported in April. The MSF report highlighted the rape, murder, and beheading of eight-year-old Ramisa, and praised the state’s prompt action in arresting the accused and initiating the trial process. However, it stressed that the state must ensure impartial and speedy trials in all cases of violence against women and children. The rights body said there were signs of improvement in some areas of the human rights situation in May compared with April, including a decline in incidents of political violence. At least three people were killed and 193 others were injured in May, while three people were killed and 303 were injured the previous month. According to MSF, seven people died in jail custody in May, compared with six in April and 11 in March. It said four Bangladeshi nationals were killed by the Indian Border Security Force in May, including three who were shot dead and one who died after being tortured. Besides, the bodies of a fisherman and an unidentified woman were recovered from areas along the Bangladesh-India border. In addition, a young man was publicly stabbed to death by miscreants in a border-adjacent area, bringing the total number of border-related deaths to 10 in May, up from eight in April. Meanwhile, along the Myanmar border, three Bangladeshis were killed on the spot in two separate landmine explosions in May.

title: Four confess to rape and murder of woman in Munshiganj, says PBI
body: A 19-year-old woman whose decomposed body was recovered from the Phuldi River in Munshiganj's Gazaria upazila on May 29 was raped before being murdered, the Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) said today. The four arrestees have confessed to their involvement in the crime before a court under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, said Asma Ara Jahan, additional superintendent of police of Munshiganj PBI, during a press briefing at her office this evening. The arrestees are Abu Kalam, 48, Jamal Hossain, 44, Al-Amin Pradhan, 50, and Russel Mia, 44. The victim was a resident of the Jamaldi area under Hosendi union in Gazaria upazila. According to PBI sources, a team of Gazaria River Police recovered an unidentified decomposed body from the Phuldi River on May 29. Later, the PBI crime scene team identified the victim. Following the identification, the victim's sister filed a murder case with Gazaria Police Station, and PBI took over the shadow investigation. During initial interrogation, investigators found that Abu Kalam and Russel had financial disputes with the victim, as they owed her Tk 25,000 and Tk 10,000 respectively. Another accused, Jamal, was acquainted with the victim. The three, along with their associate Al-Amin, allegedly planned the murder around 15 days before the incident, Asma Ara Jahan said. According to the investigation, the suspects called the victim to the riverbank in the Borobhaterchar area on the evening of May 26. They then took her by boat to a cornfield across the river, where they raped her. The suspects later strangled her and dumped the body into the river in an attempt to conceal the crime, the PBI official said. The arrestees were produced before a court, where they gave confessional statements. Further investigation is underway to determine whether anyone else was involved in the incident, she added.

title: Man detained over rape of intellectually disabled girl in Ctg
body: Police this afternoon detained a man for allegedly raping a 16-year-old intellectually disabled girl in Chattogram’s Chaktai. The detainee is Jamal alias Jaker, 32, from Bhola, said Chattogram Metropolitan Police (South) Additional Deputy Commissioner Mahmudul Hasan Mamun. Before police took the accused into custody, locals attempted to beat him, but officers intervened and prevented the attack. The rape incident allegedly took place last night at Misti Goli of Bhera Market in Chaktai. The ADC said, “Jamal is a neighbour of the victim. He lured the victim with a cold drink and later raped her. Later, the victim disclosed the matter to her mother.” “Following the incident, the mother and relatives detained Jamal today and tried to beat him. Upon receiving information, police rushed to the spot and detained the accused from the mob,” he added. The victim was sent to Chittagong Medical College Hospital’s One-Stop Crisis Centre for a medical examination, said the ADC.

title: Mob violence kills 32 in May, highest in 6 months: MSF

The monthly report also says, 71 people were critically injured across at least 69 separate incidents -- a sharp rise from April, when 21 people were killed and 49 injured.
