The figures show a steady upward trend, with deaths recorded at 19 in March, 18 in February, 21 in January, and 10 in December 2025. Of the 32 killed in May, 14 died over theft allegations, four following altercations, two over robbery allegations, and two over alleged rape and sexual assault. At least 35 of the injured were handed over to police. MSF said members of law enforcement were also attacked by mobs. The killings continued despite repeated assurances from Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed that mob justice would not be tolerated. The issue was also raised in parliament. During a Police Week programme on May 10, the home minister said the government would amend laws or introduce new legislation if necessary to curb mob violence. MSF Founding President Advocate Sultana Kamal said the surge in violence has made public security "a matter of serious concern." The report also recorded a significant rise in violence against women and children. At least 326 such incidents were logged in May -- 12 more than the previous month. Rape cases rose by 40% to 70 incidents, while gang-rape cases climbed to 16. Cases of rape followed by murder reached six, up from two in April. MSF highlighted the rape, murder, and beheading of eight-year-old Ramisa, praising swift arrests and the initiation of trial proceedings, but called for impartial and speedy justice across all such cases. Meanwhile, seven people died in jail custody during May, the report said. On the India-Bangladesh border, four Bangladeshis were killed by India’s Border Security Force -- three shot and one tortured to death. In addition, the bodies of a fisherman and an unidentified woman were recovered from border areas, and a young man was stabbed to death near the frontier, bringing Bangladesh-India border-related deaths to seven. Along the Myanmar border, three Bangladeshis were killed in two separate landmine explosions. The report also noted a slight improvement in political violence: three people were killed in both April and May, while injuries fell from 303 in April to 193 in May.

title: Four killed in separate attacks in Manikganj, Noakhali
body: Five people, including a woman and her child, were killed in separate violent incidents in Manikganj and Noakhali since last night, police said. Of the three victims from Manikganj, a mother and her son were murdered in Daulatpur upazila, while another person was killed in Sadar upazila. There was a longstanding family dispute between Yusuf Molla, 35, and his elder brother Salam Molla, 40, in Fakirpara area of Daulatpur upazila. According to police, Salam Mollah left the house after a quarrel with his brother last night. Around 10:00pm, Yusuf Molla allegedly attacked Amena, 28, and her one-and-a-half-year-old son Aswad with a sharp weapon, said Officer-in-Charge (OC) of Daulatpur Police Station Swapan Kumar Sarkar. He later attacked Salam while he was returning home after closing his shop, leaving him seriously injured. Salam was admitted to Daulatpur Upazila Health Complex. In a separate incident in Manikganj Sadar upazila, an organised group attacked the house of local resident Lutfar Rahman at Uttar Putail village around 1:15am today over previous enmity. Md Sajib, 28, of the same village was allegedly hacked to death during the attack at the house, said Ikram Hossain, OC of Manikganj Sadar Police Station. Details of the incident and Sajib's relationship with the homeowners could not be immediately confirmed. In Noakhali's Begumganj upazila, miscreants allegedly beat a young man to death with iron rods after intercepting him on his way home from a local market. The victim, Jobayer Hossain alias Rakib, 24, was attacked around 9:30pm at Khanpur village, said Md Shamsuzzaman, OC of Begumganj Model Police Station. Quoting family members and local residents, the OC said, a dispute had reportedly arisen three or four days earlier between the son of Rakib's cousin and a local shopkeeper. Members of both sides gathered at Pakmunshirhat Bazar under Sharifpur union to settle the matter. Locals advised Rakib to leave the area, and he headed home with his younger brother, Rimon. When the two reached a dark stretch near the market, a group of assailants allegedly intercepted them and launched an attack. Rimon was also injured while trying to save his brother. Rakib suffered severe injuries after being struck on the head and other parts of his body with iron rods, police said. He was taken to the 250-bed Noakhali General Hospital, where doctors declared him dead. The victim's family was preparing to file a case, and legal action would be taken based on the investigation, he added today. In another incident in Noakhali Sadar upazila, businessman Md Kamal Uddin, 48, died while trying to intervene in a clash between two groups over a dispute related to a gambling den. Shriram Chandra Bhattacharya, inspector (operations) of Sudharam Model Police Station, said Kamal's nephew Farhad was first assaulted over the gambling-related dispute. Kamal later went to stop the fight and subsequently lost consciousness. Family members took him to the 250-bed Noakhali General Hospital, where doctors declared him dead. The victim's family alleged that Kamal was attacked and killed by members of the opposing group. However, police said they did not initially find visible injury marks on his body. No arrests had been made as of filing this report. [Report by our Manikganj and Noakhali correspondents.]

title: BGB-BSF talks: Border killings, irregular migrants to top the agenda
body: Border killings, push-ins, and repatriation of irregular migrants are expected to top the agenda at the director general-level meeting between the border forces of Bangladesh and India on June 8-11, according to diplomatic sources in Dhaka and New Delhi. Border Guard Bangladesh Director General Maj Gen Mohammad Ashrafuzzaman Siddiqui will lead the Bangladesh delegation, while Border Security Force Director General Praveen Kumar will lead the Indian side at the meeting scheduled in New Delhi. The DG-level meeting is held twice a year, alternately in Delhi and Dhaka. The last such meeting was held in Dhaka on August 25-28 last year. “This meeting discusses all aspects of border management, but border killings and irregular migrants will top the agenda,” a BGB official said. This will be the first border talks after Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman’s visit to India on April 7-9 following the formation of the new BNP-led government. As the relationship between the two countries has begun warming up after the February 2026 election, Dhaka and Delhi are also scheduling meetings on commerce, shipping, consular affairs, the Joint River Commission, etc. The so-called irregular Bangladeshi migrants became an issue in the run-up to elections in West Bengal and Assam. Quoting Indian police, AFP on May 29 reported that hundreds of alleged Bangladeshis had gathered over the previous two days at Hakimpur in India’s West Bengal, hoping to cross the border as authorities tightened enforcement under a new state government. It was part of the Bharatiya Janata Party’s (BJP) election campaign to “detect, delete and deport” illegal migrants in Assam and West Bengal. BJP won in both states. The Hindustan Times on May 29 reported that at least 386 undocumented immigrants held across West Bengal over the last week had been sent to 13 holding centres in eight bordering districts of the state. In a diplomatic note to Bangladesh on April 8, India’s Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said it had not received an “actionable response” from Bangladesh regarding the repatriation of 2,868 suspected illegal Bangladeshi migrants since September 2020. To discuss the issue, Bangladesh High Commissioner Riaz Hamidullah came to Dhaka on May 11. On May 12, Dhaka also sent a diplomatic note to New Delhi, clarifying a number of issues raised by the MEA on the repatriation of alleged irregular Bangladeshis. A foreign ministry official said that over the years many Bangladeshis had been repatriated after nationality verification. “Besides, there are issues with the Indian side as well, including dilly-dallying in providing consular access to the jails, legal procedures, and mismatches in the list of alleged irregular migrants. So, blaming Bangladesh alone is not helpful,” he added. Last year, there were numerous cases of push-ins of so-called irregular Bangladeshis. However, some of them were later identified as Indian and Myanmar nationals. “We would definitely want India to maintain due procedures in repatriation, if there are irregular Bangladeshis in India,” a BGB official told this correspondent yesterday. Border killings also remain a matter of serious concern for Bangladesh. “We will strongly raise the issue of border killings,” the BGB official said. According to rights organisation Ain O Salish Kendra, at least six Bangladeshis have been killed or injured in BSF firing or torture along the border between January and May 9, 2026. It says 594 Bangladeshis were killed by BSF between 2009 and 2023. According to foreign ministry and BGB officials, the meeting will also discuss preventing the smuggling of drugs, arms, and ammunition; preventing unauthorised infrastructure construction along the border; preserving border rivers; and ensuring Bangladesh receives its fair share of water, among others.

title: Death of Infants: Probe report on June 3
body: The investigation committee formed over the deaths of six newborns at Ad-din Medical College Hospital will submit its full report on June 3, as the statements of the mothers have not yet been collected, Health Minister Sardar Md Sakhawat Husain said yesterday. “We couldn’t receive the report today. The committee needed more time because the mothers’ statements were still pending. Their accounts will be included in the final report,” he said while speaking to reporters at the Directorate General of Health Services. He said the mothers were traumatised and had returned to their homes. The committee would now reach out to them to understand what happened on the day of the incident. “Their statements are very important here. We are waiting for them,” the minister said, adding that all other aspects of the probe had already been completed. He said the incident at the hospital was extremely tragic and assured that strict action would follow the findings of the committee. “There will be no leniency. Measures will follow the report’s recommendations. We will not spare anyone,” he told reporters. Earlier, a case was filed over the deaths of the six newborns, bringing charges of the hospital’s negligence that led to the fatalities. Six infants, aged between one and three days, died within a span of a few hours from 6:00am Wednesday at a post-operative room of the hospital. The exact cause of the deaths could not be confirmed immediately. However, health officials suspect a technical failure may have caused the tragedy.

title: Case filed over alleged sexual assault of 7-year-old girl in Netrokona
body: A case was filed yesterday over the alleged sexual assault of a seven-year-old girl in Barhatta upazila of Netrokona. The accused, Abdur Rashid, 36, has been absconding since the incident. Barhatta Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Champak Dam confirmed the matter. The victim’s mother filed the case yesterday at around 11:00pm at Barhatta Police Station, the OC said. According to the case statement and police sources, the incident occurred on the afternoon of May 19. The girl’s mother was busy drying paddy in the field next to their house, leaving the child alone at home. Taking advantage of the situation, Rashid took the girl to the cowshed. There, he covered her mouth and sexually assaulted her, according to the case statement. Hearing the girl’s cries, her mother and people nearby rushed to the house. The accused fled from the scene. As the news spread, local influential individuals allegedly tried to suppress the matter through a traditional salish (arbitration). Later, the girl’s mother submitted a written complaint to the police, leading to the formal registration of the case. “The accused, Abdur Rashid, is currently absconding. Police are making every effort to arrest him,” said the OC.

title: Teen arrested over rape of 8-year-old in Gopalganj
body: A 15-year-old boy was arrested on charges of raping an eight-year-old boy in an area adjacent to BSCIC Bridge intersection in Gopalganj Sadar upazila yesterday. The child's mother has filed a case under the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act with Gopalganj Sadar Police Station, said Nayan Chandra Devnath, officer-in-charge (investigation) of Gopalganj Sadar Police Station. Upon receiving the news, police went to the scene and sent the victim to Gopalganj Medical College Hospital for treatment and medical examination, the OC said, adding that the main accused was arrested. The arrested boy was employed at the Madhumati Bakery in the Gopalganj BSCIC industrial area. According to police and family sources, yesterday, around 5:30pm, he lured the child to the second floor of a bakery by promising Tk 20 and then assaulted him. On information, police reached the spot and rescued the child in critical condition and sent him to Gopalganj Medical College Hospital. Locals caught the accused and handed him over to police. OC Nayan Chandra said, "The accused has confessed to the incident. Legal proceedings are ongoing."

title: Teen killed, 15 injured as rival groups clash in Brahmanbaria
body: A teenage boy was killed and at least 15 others were injured in a violent clash allegedly triggered by a dispute over drugs in Brahmanbaria last night. The incident took place around 11:00pm in Syedtula Uttarpara village under Sarail Sadar union. The deceased was identified as Raihan, 16, a local resident, Sarail Police Station Officer-in-Charge Monjur Kader Bhuiyan said. “The clash took place over a drug-related dispute. Those involved will be identified and brought under the law,” he said. According to locals and police, an argument broke out between two rival groups in the village over a drug-related issue. The altercation soon escalated into violence as members of both sides attacked each other with sharp weapons and sticks. Raihan sustained critical injuries from sharp weapons and died on the way to hospital. The injured were taken to different hospitals for treatment. Police rushed to the scene after being informed and brought the situation under control. Additional police have been deployed in the area to prevent further violence.

title: Man beaten to death over theft allegations
body: A 45-year-old man was beaten to death and two others injured in a mob attack in Satkania upazila of Chattogram on Thursday night. The deceased was identified as Md Selim, of the Katakhali area, said police. Police arrested one accused, Md Ismail Imon, 28, early yesterday in connection with the murder. The incident took place in the Khatirhat area under ward 6 of Charti union, according to police. Police and locals said a chase and counter-chase took place between two groups following an altercation involving the assault of two individuals earlier on the day of Eid-ul-Azha. Later in the evening, several hundred people surrounded a house in the Khatirhat area of Charti union and allegedly beat Selim and his associates over theft allegations. On information, police rescued the injured and took them to Satkania Upazila Health Complex, where Selim died around 9:30pm while undergoing treatment. Md Jahangir Alam, officer-in-charge of Satkania Police Station, told The Daily Star that the victim was beaten by a mob over allegations of theft. “We are investigating whether the incident was related to theft allegations or if there were any previous disputes,” the OC added. The body was sent to Chattogram Medical College Hospital morgue for an autopsy. Selim’s father, Abul Khair, filed a murder case with Satkania Police Station yesterday, naming 29 people and accusing more than 100 unidentified individuals, police said.

title: Man found dead three days after abduction in Rangamati
body: Police recovered the body of a man on Thursday afternoon, three days after he was allegedly abducted from his house by five to six masked men in Naniarchar upazila of Rangamati. The victim, Chongu Bikash Chakma, 48, was a resident of Betchhari Dosarpara village under Naniarchar union, said police. Quoting family, Naniarchar Union Parishad member Rupak Chakma told The Daily Star that around 12:00am on Monday, five to six masked men went to Chongu’s house and took him away. He had remained missing since then. On Thursday afternoon, his body was found in the Burighat area with his hands tied and bullet marks on the body. The UP member also said Chongu was not associated with any political party and did agricultural work. Naniarchar Police Station Officer-in-Charge Taufiqul Islam said the body bore injury marks and the hands were tied. The body has been sent to the hospital morgue for autopsy. A case has been filed with the police station in this regard, he added.

title: Woman's body recovered in Netrokona, husband arrested
body: Police recovered the hanging body of a housewife from her house in Netrokona's Mohanganj upazila yesterday and arrested her husband in a case filed over alleged abetment of suicide. The deceased was identified as Surma Akter, 28, of Manshri village in the upazila. She was the daughter of Sabuj Mia of Mendipur village in neighbouring Khaliajuri upazila, said police. Her husband, Wasim Mia, 35, has been arrested in connection with a case filed over abetting suicide, said Sub-Inspector Md Jasim Uddin, investigating officer of the case. According to police and locals, family members found Surma hanging from a ceiling beam with an orna (scarf) around her neck at her husband's house around 5:00pm on the day of Eid-ul-Azha. Police later recovered the body and sent it for autopsy. The couple had been married for around 12 years and had two children -- a seven-year-old son and a two-and-a-half-year-old daughter. Family members alleged that Surma had been subjected to physical and mental abuse by her husband over the years. They claimed that she took her own life after enduring repeated humiliation and mistreatment. Yesterday night, Surma's brother Anis Mia filed a case with Mohanganj Police Station, accusing Wasim Mia and his two brothers of abetting suicide. Police arrested Wasim shortly after the case was filed and produced him before a court this afternoon. SI Jasim Uddin said the body was sent to Netrokona Modern Sadar Hospital morgue for autopsy. Efforts are underway to arrest the other accused named in the case, he added.

title: A murder case without a murder: How a family’s life was turned upside down
body: For years, Asadul Haque Kajol and three of his family members in Chapainawabganj endured the torment of being falsely accused in a case involving a crime they had no part in – one that, in fact, never happened. Accused of abducting and murdering a teenage girl who was later found alive after seven years, the family said they suffered months of fear, humiliation and sleepless nights, while spending several lakh taka in legal procedures to prove their innocence. Their ordeal began after 17-year-old Ayesha Khatun disappeared from Khale Alampur village in Bholahat upazila in 2019. Although Ayesha went missing in 2019, her family filed a general diary with Bholahat Police Station in 2021. In July 2023, Ayesha’s mother, Aduri Begum, filed a case accusing Kajol, his wife Nazma Begum, and Kajol’s two brothers, Mainul Hasan and Babu, of abducting Ayesha, murdering her and disposing of her body. “We lost everything due to the false cases -- our money, our reputation, our peace. Our family has been devastated,” Kajol recently told The Daily Star. “We lived in constant fear of arrest and uncertainty over the case outcome over the last three years,” he said. The accusations disrupted the lives of the family members as neighbours and acquaintances began distancing themselves from them. Employment opportunities for the three male accused also shrank as many viewed them with suspicion. Kajol, a mason by profession, and his family repeatedly maintained that they had no involvement in Ayesha’s disappearance and knew nothing about where she had gone. However, only some neighbours believed them. “In the eyes of some neighbours, we were already guilty. We were murderers. That was most painful,” Kajol said. The Criminal Investigation Department investigated the abduction and murder case for nearly a year before submitting a report to the court clearing the accused after finding no evidence against them. But the ordeal did not end there. Around 10 months later, Aduri filed another case with similar allegations against the same four family members. The district court later sent the matter to Bholahat Police Station for investigation. While the family continued to battle the cases, Ayesha had reportedly been moving through different areas, including Dhaka, Savar, Kushtia and Rajshahi. The mystery finally unravelled earlier this month. On May 4, Md Alamgir, a neighbour of Kajol, working as a bus helper, noticed a young woman near the Rail Gate area in Rajshahi and suspected she might be the missing Ayesha. After speaking with her and confirming details, he contacted Kajol. Alamgir later brought her to Bholahat on his bus, from where police took her into custody, bringing Kajol’s family’s ordeal to an end. The following day, Sub-Inspector Kamal Hossain of Bholahat Police Station, the investigating officer of the second case, produced Ayesha before a Chapainawabganj court magistrate, who recorded her statement and handed her over to her family. “When I learned she had been found, tears came to my eyes – not out of joy, but relief,” Kajol said. He had spent around Tk 6 lakh fighting the cases over the past three years. “Finally, the truth has come out and our innocence has been proven. The woman’s family filed the cases either out of vengeance or as part of a conspiracy. I will definitely take legal action against those who put our lives through such uncertainty and agony,” Kajol said. Talking to The Daily Star, SI Kamal Hossain said police would submit a report to the court seeking clearance for the four accused now that the woman had been found. During primary interrogation and her deposition before a magistrate, Ayesha said Kajol and his family members did not abduct her, adding that her mother insisted that she implicate them. “During my investigation, Ayesha’s brother even said they talked to her three months after she went missing in 2019, when Ayesha told them that she was in Amin Bazar in Dhaka and would not return to Chapainawabganj,” the SI said. “It seems to me that they might have sued the family either out of vengeance or for financial gain. The accused can take legal action, if they want, for being harassed with a false case,” the investigating officer told The Daily Star. Attempts to contact Aduri were unsuccessful as her phone was found switched off.

title: 25 injured as meat distribution dispute sparks clash in Faridpur
body: At least 25 people were injured in a clash over the distribution of sacrificial meat in Faridpur's Bhanga upazila this morning. The incident took place around 8:00am at an Eidgah field in Purba Aruakandi village under Algi union, Bhanga Police Station Officer-in-Charge Md Mizanur Rahman said. Upon information, police rushed to the spot and brought the situation under control, the OC said, adding that additional police personnel have been deployed in the area. According to local residents and police, villagers in Purba Aruakandi are divided into two rival groups. Traditionally, the portion of Qurbani meat meant for poor people is collected and distributed collectively in the village. This year, however, a dispute arose over whether the meat would be distributed from the mosque or separately from individual households. Locals said the argument began shortly after Eid prayers and quickly escalated into tensions between the two groups. Al Amin Islam, a member of ward 1 of Algi union in Bhanga upazila, said, at one stage, both factions, before animal sacrifice, became involved in a clash using lethal weapons, bricks and sticks. Panic spread across the village during the chase and counter-chase, while four to five houses were vandalised, according to residents. At least 25 people were injured in the violence. Several were admitted to Bhanga Upazila Health Complex, while others received primary treatment there. Tansiv Zubayer, Bhanga upazila health and family planning officer, told The Daily Star that eight injured people had been admitted to the hospital as of 1:25pm. Mujibor Molla, a member of Algi Union Parishad, described the incident as "unfortunate". "Such violence over a minor issue like meat distribution on the day of Eid is undesirable. We could not even complete the animal sacrifice before the two groups clashed," he said.

title: Man held for attempted rape of 9-year-old girl
body: Police have arrested a man on charges of attempting to rape a nine-year-old girl in Kaliganj upazila of Gazipur. The accused, Md Shahin Mia, 30, was taken into custody after the victim’s family filed a case with Kaliganj Police Station on Tuesday night, said Md Ashraful Islam, inspector (investigation) of the police station. Shahin was sent to jail by a court yesterday afternoon. According to the case statement, the incident occurred on Monday afternoon when the victim was playing with Shahin’s daughter near his house. With his wife absent, Shahin confined his own daughter to a room and forcibly took the victim to the toilet, where he attempted to rape her. The child managed to escape when Shahin’s mobile phone fell, distracting him. She ran home and informed her family. Her grandfather later filed a case with the police station, leading to Shahin’s arrest during a raid.

title: Those responsible for death of 6 newborns will be punished: health minister
body: Health Minister Sardar Md Sakhawat Hossain today said those responsible will be punished over the deaths of six newborns at Ad-Din Medical College Hospital in Dhaka allegedly caused by negligence of the hospital authorities. An investigation committee has been formed to investigate the incident, he also said while speaking to journalists in Kishoreganj, reports our local correspondent. According to health officials, the six newborns may have died due to a technical failure in the post-operative room. The health minister also said the hospital authorities switched off the air-conditioning system and did not restart it until 4:00pm. As a result, there was a shortage of oxygen support, leading to the deaths of six children. He said the police had already been deployed, while the director general and additional director general of the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) visited the spot. Meanwhile, an inquiry committee has been formed, the minister said, adding that if evidence is found during the investigation, strict action will be taken against those involved. Meanwhile, families of the six newborns took the bodies without autopsy after receiving police permission, reports UNB. Ashiq Iqbal, inspector (investigation) of Ramna Police Station, said the families collected the bodies following police approval. Earlier in the day, a five-member team from the DMP Bomb Disposal Unit visited the ward and conducted inspections for around an hour, but found nothing harmful there, UNB added. One member of the team, requesting anonymity, said, “We did not find anything hazardous. However, there was a slight smell which can occur if the AC remains switched off.” Earlier, the crime scene unit of the Criminal Investigation Department also visited the hospital.

title: Elderly woman beaten to death over land dispute in Faridpur
body: A 71-year-old woman was allegedly beaten to death during a dispute over the construction of a bathroom on contested land in Faridpur’s Boalmari upazila today. The deceased was identified as Firoza Begum, wife of late Muktar Molla of Bonchaki village under Chatul union. The incident took place around 11:30am in Bonchaki village, police and family members said. According to police and family, Firoza had long been involved in a dispute with Tulu Mia and his family of neighbouring Ramchandrapur village over her father’s property. Family members alleged that Firoza came under attack when she went to supervise work for a sewerage line connected to a bathroom being built on the disputed land this morning. Firoza was taken to Boalmari Upazila Health Complex after becoming critically injured, where doctors declared her dead. Sabur Nesa, sister of the deceased, alleged that Firoza was killed over the land dispute. “Our land had been occupied forcibly. When we went to build a bathroom there, my mother was beaten to death. I want justice for her killing,” said Azizur Molla, son of the victim. Md Jalal Sikder, a member of Chatul Union Parishad, said a court case over the land is still pending between the two parties. Confirming the incident, Md Anowar Hossain, officer-in-charge of Boalmari Police Station, told The Daily Star that the body was brought to the police station from the hospital. “The body will be sent to Faridpur Medical College Hospital tomorrow for autopsy. Legal procedures are underway,” he said.

title: Trader beaten to death at cattle market in Savar
body: A cattle trader was killed in an attack during a clash between two groups of traders at a cattle market in Savar, on the outskirts of Dhaka, early today. The deceased was identified as Shahidullah Kaiser, 50, son of the late Matiar Rahman of Mangalbari area under Baishakanda Union in Dhamrai upazila of Dhaka. He was also a local medicine trader. The incident took place at Paragram Cattle Market in Shimulia Union around 1:00am today, police said. Firoz Kabir, who was present during the incident, said he and his maternal uncle, Shahidullah, went to the cattle market on May 21 to sell 18 cows and two goats. By early today, four cows remained unsold. “Around 1:00am, while we were waiting to sell the remaining cattle, another trader tried to tie his cattle in the same spot, which led to an argument. Later, some market authority staff members and several traders attacked us. When my uncle Shahidullah tried to save me, they brutally assaulted him,” he alleged. Firoz also claimed that during the attack, the assailants took Tk 40,000 from his younger uncle, Masud Rana. Critically injured, Shahidullah was taken to Dhamrai Upazila Health Complex, where doctors declared him dead, Firoz added. Confirming the incident, Dhamrai Police Station Sub-Inspector Kazi Rezaul said police recovered the body from the hospital after being informed of the incident, and legal procedures were underway. He added that since the incident took place within the jurisdiction of Ashulia Police Station, the matter had been referred there for further action.

title: Angry mob catches rape accused, hands him to police after beating in Habiganj
body: Police arrested the main suspect for the alleged gang rape of a nine-year-old girl in Nabiganj upazila of Habiganj on Monday night, after an angry mob captured him and handed him over to law enforcement after beating. The accused is Afroz Mia, 35, a neighbour of the victim, said police. According to police and local sources, the accused and an accomplice abducted a third grader on Sunday afternoon, blindfolding her with a towel before taking her to a nearby bamboo grove, where they raped and physically tortured her. Hearing her screams, when locals rushed to the spot, the accused fled the area. The victim was first taken to Nabiganj Upazila Health Complex and later shifted to Habiganj Modern Sadar Hospital for better treatment. The victim also said to her family that Afroz was the main assailant. On Monday night, the relatives of the victim spotted the suspect in Digombar Bazar in Bahubal upazila of the same district. They apprehended him and brought him to Barachar Bazar, where a mob started beating him. On information, a team from Nabiganj Police Station rushed to the scene, brought the situation under control, and took the accused into custody. Md Monayem Mia, officer-in-charge (OC) of Nabiganj Police Station, said police arrested the main accused. Efforts are underway to apprehend the other accused, who remains at large. The victim’s father filed a case with Nabiganj Police Station on Tuesday.

title: Jungle Salimpur: 242 sued over attack on joint forces camp
body: Chattogram police have filed a case against 242 individuals, including 150 to 200 unidentified persons, over early Monday’s attack on a joint forces camp in Jungle Salimpur. Inspector Sohel Rana of the Faujdarhat police outpost under Sitakunda Police Station filed the case on Monday night, confirmed station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Mohammad Mohinul Islam. The OC said names of a total of 42 people, including five people arrested from the scene and local crime boss Md Yasin, have been mentioned in the case. “Apart from this, 150 to 200 unidentified people have been named as accused.” He said the case has been filed under various sections of the Explosives Act on charges of launching an armed attack on police, obstructing government work and damaging government property. In the early hours of Monday, armed criminals attacked and destroyed a newly built camp for the joint forces in the Alinagar area of Jungle Salimpur. Before the attack, roads leading into the hilly terrain were dug up in at least three places so that law enforcers could not respond to the scene quickly.

title: Rape, abuse of children: One held over attempted rape of 7-year-old in Rangpur
body: Police arrested a man on charge of attempted to rape a seven-year-old child in a jute field in Rangpur city yesterday. The arrestee is Badiuzzaman, 45, a labourer, said Rangpur Metropolitan Police Commissioner Mohammad Abdul Mabud at a press conference. According to the police, the incident occurred on Monday night in Kolabari area of Mahiganj upazila, when Badiuzzaman lured the child with a packet of chips to a nearby jute field and attempted to rape her, but fled when locals noticed him. The child’s family filed a cased with Mahiganj Police Station the same day, and police through a drive arrested the accused early yesterday. Police said Badiuzzaman lives in Dhaka and occasionally visits Rangpur. In Gazipur’s Kaliganj upazila, police arrested a 60-year-old man and sent him to jail on charges of raping and impregnating a 13-year-old girl. The arrested accused is Abdur Rahim, 60, a rickshaw puller of Baligaon area. When the incident came to light yesterday, during the fifth month of the child’s pregnancy, locals detained the and beat him up and later handed him over to the police. The accused was sent to court after his arrest yesterday afternoon. Quoting the family, the victim has two other younger sisters and they all live with their mother, a garment factory worker. On the night of November 4 last year, when the victim’s mother went on night duty at the factory, the accused entered their house and threatened the girl before raping her, they said. Kaliganj Police Station Officer-in-Charge Md Zakir Hossain told The Daily Star, “The girl still doesn’t understand anything [about what happened]. In the meantime, she is now five-months pregnant. The accused has been arrested and sent to jail.” He added that the victim has been sent to the hospital for a health check-up.

title: Man held over rape attempt of seven-year-old girl in Rangpur

title: Mango orchard caretaker arrested for alleged rape of schoolboy in Kushtia
body: Police have arrested a caretaker of a mango orchard in Kushtia, for allegedly raping a fourth grade schoolboy when the child entered the orchard to pick mangoes. The accused Wahed Ali, 50, was arrested today, and later in the day a court sent him to jail. The alleged incident occurred on Sunday morning. Locals said the boy had gone to the field with goats and later entered the orchard to collect mangoes, where the accused reportedly raped him. The boy later narrated the incident to his mother. Local influential figures attempted to settle the matter through a village arbitration. However, the police rushed to the village after receiving information and foiled the arbitration. Following this, the victim’s father filed a case under the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act at Kumarkhali Police Station on Monday night.

title: Those behind Jungle Salimpur attack will face strict action, says home minister
body: Home Minister Salahauddin Ahmed has said strict action will be taken over recent attacks on a Rapid Action Battalion (Rab) camp in Jungle Salimpur . “We are looking into the attacks in Jungle Salimpur. Action is being taken, and it will be visible very soon,” he said while speaking to reporters at the Police Headquaters this afternoon. Referring to Jangal Salimpur, he said the area had effectively functioned as a “state within a state” before being brought under control through joint operations by law enforcement agencies, adding that those operations led to the recovery of arms and the arrest of listed criminals. Plans are also underway to establish facilities such as police and Rab academies, sports complexes and other infrastructure in the area, alongside earlier proposals to shift the Chattogram district jail there, the home minister said. However, he warned that attempts were being made by “criminal elements” to re-establish their presence. “Their provocative activities and audacity will be dealt with strictly. We do not want to reveal the full plan at this moment. But the rule of law will be established. No sanctuary for criminals will be allowed,” he added. Eid security strengthened Highlighting Eid-ul-Azha security arrangements, the home minister said the central monitoring system under the Police Headquarters had been further strengthened ahead of the festival. “The monitoring cell is always active. For Eid, it has been intensified from seven days before Eid to seven days after Eid. Manpower has been increased and highways are under round-the-clock surveillance,” he said. He added that special monitoring had been put in place at cattle markets, expressways and major bridges, including the Jamuna and Padma bridges. CCTV surveillance is being used nationwide, while body-worn cameras have been deployed in areas where fixed systems are unavailable. On road safety, he said the overall number of accidents had decreased compared to previous years, but attributed recent incidents to negligence. Regarding traffic congestion at toll plazas, he said the issue required improved technology. “Now toll is being collected manually. Tickets create long queues. In many countries this is automated. Vehicles will have cards and money will be deducted digitally. Then there will be no waiting. The government is considering this,” he said. Citing a recent accident involving a truck carrying iron rods, where passengers allegedly travelling on top of the vehicle were killed, he said "If passengers remain aware, such tragedies can be avoided.” On cattle markets, he said measures had been taken to prevent the use of counterfeit currency, including the deployment of detection machines by banks and Bangladesh Bank. He also said illegal cattle markets were being shut down, referring to a recent attempt to set up a market under the metro rail line in Mirpur. Eid-ul-Azha waste management Regarding Eid-related waste management, he said arrangements had been made to ensure clearance within 24 hours, with instructions issued to city corporations, district administrations and municipalities. He added that special arrangements were in place as Qurbani continues on the second and third days as well. Border and other issues On border firing incidents, the minister said such matters were usually resolved through flag meetings between border forces and did not indicate any major national-level tension. Responding to a question on the Tirodhan festival of Loknath Brahmachari, he said Bangladesh was a country of communal harmony and ensured freedom for all religious practices. He added that district administrations and police would take necessary steps in this regard. Replying to allegations of open drug trading in Savar, he urged journalists to provide information, assuring action within 24 hours, and reiterated the government’s “zero tolerance” stance on drugs.

title: Hijra person killed in Narsingdi
body: A hijra person was killed by having their throat slit in Raipura upazila of Narsingdi and another was critically injured early yesterday. The incident took place at a poultry farm in the Pirijkandi Railgate area, said Mujibur Rahman, officer-in-charge of Raipura Police Station, adding that police recovered the body from the spot. The deceased was identified as Yasmin, also known as Suman, 26, from Pirijkandi village of the upazila. The injured, Chandni, also known as Babu, 26, from the same area, was sent to Dhaka Medical College Hospital in critical condition. Multiple injury marks were found on the victim’s body, police said. “Primarily, it is suspected that the murder may have happened over previous enmity,” the OC said, adding that police launched an investigation to identify those involved and determine the motive behind the killing. He said police were in contact with the victim’s family, although no written complaint has been filed yet.

title: Jungle Salimpur: Joint forces camp comes under attack
body: Gunshots pierced the stillness of the night in Jungle Salimpur in the early hours of yesterday when armed criminals sprung a surprise attack on a joint forces camp in the Alinagar area. The assault took place between 1:00am and 2:00am at a temporary security camp under construction for joint forces stationed in the remote hilly area of Sitakunda upazila in Chattogram, according to Rab-7 Commanding Officer Lt Col Hafizur Rahman. The attackers, believed to be members of the notorious “Yasin Bahini”, used an excavator to smash the camp’s rear wall, reducing the structure to rubble. At the time of the attack, members of the police, Rapid Action Battalion (Rab), Armed Police Battalion (APBn), and Range Reserve Force (RRF) were stationed at the camp on the Alinagar School compound. Law enforcement officials described the attack as meticulously planned. Roads leading into the hilly terrain were dug up at three points to trap security forces inside and block reinforcements. Gunfire erupted from tin-shed houses on an adjacent hilltop, with barrels thrust through holes in the walls. The Rab commander said the attackers fired weapons resembling AK rifles, forcing law enforcers to retaliate. No casualties were reported among the joint forces. “The criminals pinned our personnel down with gunfire and seized the chance to vandalise the camp,” said Lt Col Hafizur. Chattogram Superintendent of Police Masud Alam said joint forces used shotguns, Chinese rifles, and tear gas. “Police fired a total of 104 rounds. Due to strong resistance, the attackers failed to enter the camp.” The brazen overnight attack comes just days ahead of the home minister’s scheduled visit on May 31 to inaugurate the now-destroyed camp. Lt Col Hafizur said a temporary security camp was being built at the far end of the Alinagar school compound, and about 90 percent of the work had already been completed. “The structure was almost entirely demolished.” Earlier on March 9, joint forces seized control of much of Jungle Salimpur in a large-scale operation that had driven out the Yasin Bahini without resistance. Following yesterday’s attack, several suspects have been detained while joint forces -- including BGB and army personnel -- have launched sweeping operations to regain control of Jungle Salimpur. Chattogram SP Masud and Rab-7 chief Lt Col Hafizur are leading the operation. Witnesses reported hearing the exchange of gunfire echoing through the hills for hours. Yasmin Akhter of Alinagar said, “I was preparing for Tahajjud Namaz around 1:00am when I first heard the gunshots. We immediately locked our doors and windows. The gunfire went on for hours before falling silent around 3:00am.” She added that Rab men stormed her house in the morning, detained her son and husband on suspicion of being attackers and took them away to the camp for interrogation. Another resident, Nasima Akhter, gave a similar account, saying her brother and husband were also detained. Jungle Salimpur spans around 1,256 acres of hilly land under Salimpur union in Sitakunda, about five kilometres from Chattogram city. Law enforcers say the area has long served as a safe haven for criminal groups because of its difficult terrain and isolation According to district administration officials, around 3,070 acres of khas land lie under five mouzas -- Jungle Latifpur, Jungle Salimpur, Jungle Bhatiyari, Jalalabad and Uttar Pahartali -- nearly 30 percent of which is hilly terrain. Authorities say several armed groups operate in parts of the area, including gangs led by Yasin and Rokonuddin, who reportedly maintain armed followers. The groups are accused of cutting hills, occupying public land and developing illegal housing plots, which they later sold to buyers, earning crores of taka over the past two decades. In the Alinagar and Chinnomul areas, Yasin is widely known as the “king”. On October 4 last year, one person was beaten and hacked to death, and at least 14 others were injured in a clash between two groups over supremacy in Jungle Salimpur. The following day, two television journalists were attacked while reporting on the violence.

title: 9-year-old girl raped in Habiganj
body: A nine-year-old girl was allegedly raped in Habiganj’s Nabiganj on Sunday. The victim is a class-III student, said Monayem Mia, officer-in-charge of Nabiganj Police Station. The girl was first taken to the local upazila health complex yesterday afternoon and was later referred to another hospital for advanced treatment, said the OC. Quoting the victim’s family, the OC said the incident occurred on Sunday afternoon when the girl was on the way to a nearby shop. Afroz Mia, 35, of the same village, along with an unidentified man forcibly took her to a bush, and raped her. Hearing her screams, locals rushed to the scene and chased the suspects, who managed to flee. The girl was found in a critical condition and taken home, said the police officer. Her family said they did not immediately take the girl to hospital due to social stigma and fear. They demanded exemplary punishment for those responsible. OC Monayem added that legal action would be taken following a proper investigation.

title: ‘Tempted by the devil’: Gazipur imam tells police after attempted rape of 10-year-old
body: Police have taken a Gazipur mosque imam into custody after he admitted that he attempted to rape a 10-year-old girl. The accused, Khorshed Alam, 52, serves as imam of a mosque in Bairagirchala village under Sreepur municipality. Sreepur Police Station Officer-in-Charge Md Shahinur Alam confirmed the detention, saying, “The local people have detained a man on charges of attempted rape and handed him over to the police. The man is the imam of a mosque. A case is under process in this incident. The accused is currently in police custody and will be sent to court tomorrow.” The OC added that during interrogation, the imam admitted he had tried to rape the child, claiming he was “tempted by the devil.” According to police, the incident took place about 20-25 days ago when the child was allegedly assaulted in an empty room in their house. The girl later confided in her grandmother, who informed locals. Locals confronted and detained the imam today around 1:00pm before handing him over to police.

title: 9-year-old gang-raped in Habiganj
body: A nine-year-old girl was allegedly gang-raped in Nabiganj upazila of Habiganj on Sunday, police and the victim's family said today. The victim is a class three student, said Nabiganj Police Station Officer-in-Charge Md Monayem Mia. The girl was first taken to Nabiganj Upazila Health Complex this afternoon and was later referred to Habiganj Sadar Modern Hospital for advanced treatment, said the OC. Quoting the victim’s family, OC Monayem said the incident occurred on Sunday afternoon when the girl was walking to a nearby shop. Afroz Mia, 35, of the same village, and an unidentified man allegedly intercepted her, covered her face with a towel, and forcibly took her to a bamboo grove in the vicinity, where they raped her. Hearing her screams, locals rushed to the scene and chased the suspects, who managed to flee. The girl was found in a critical condition and taken home, said the OC. Her family said they did not take the girl to hospital due to social stigma and fear. They also demanded exemplary punishment for those responsible. OC Monayem also said a police team rushed to the scene after the matter came to their attention. Legal action will be taken following a proper investigation, he said.

title: Hijra person found dead with throat slit in Narsingdi
body: A Hijra person was found with their throat slit and killed in Raipura of Narsingdi, while another was critically injured in the same attack early today. The incident took place around midnight at a poultry farm in the Pirijkandi Railgate area under Mirzapur union of the upazila. Police recovered the body from the scene after being informed, Raipura Police Station Officer-in-Charge Mujibur Rahman said. The deceased was identified as Yasmin, also known as Suman, 26, from Pirijkandi village in the upazila. The injured, Chandni, also known as Babu, 26, is from the same area, and was sent to Dhaka Medical College Hospital in critical condition. Multiple injury marks were found on the victim’s body, police said. “Primarily, it is suspected that the murder may have stemmed from previous enmity,” the OC said, adding that police had launched an investigation to identify those involved and determine the motive behind the killing. He also said police were in contact with the family, although no written complaint had been filed yet.

title: Jungle Salimpur Rab camp comes under attack
body: A camp of the Rapid Action Battalion (Rab) at Jungle Salimpur in Chattogram's Sitakunda upazila has come under attack allegedly by members of a group known as Yasin Bahini, which controlled the area before a major joint operation on March 9. The attack took place around 2:00am today. Rab said its personnel returned fire in self-defence, although no information regarding casualties has yet been confirmed. The incident was disclosed in a text message sent to media outlets around 3:30am by the commanding officer of Rab-7 Chattogram, Lieutenant Colonel Hafizur Rahman. He said additional forces had been deployed to the area for further action. The text message, however, did not provide any details about the incident. Jungle Salimpur, a remote hilly area, drew renewed attention after a Rab officer was beaten to death by a group of criminals during an operation there in January. On March 9, around 3,200 members of the Bangladesh Army, Rab, Police and Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) carried out a joint drive and took control of the area for the first time. Jungle Salimpur spans around 1,256 acres of hilly land under Salimpur union in Sitakunda, about five kilometres from Chattogram city. Law enforcers say the area has long served as a safe haven for criminal groups because of its difficult terrain and isolation. Following the March operation, armed groups reportedly went into hiding. Two joint camps operated by Rab and Police were later established at SM Pilot High School and Alinagar High School in Jungle Salimpur. According to district administration officials, around 3,070 acres of khas land lie under five mouzas — Jungle Latifpur, Jungle Salimpur, Jungle Bhatiyari, Jalalabad and Uttar Pahartali — nearly 30 percent of which is hilly terrain. Authorities say several armed groups operate in parts of the area, including gangs led by Md Yasin and Rokonuddin, who allegedly maintain armed followers. The groups are accused of cutting hills, occupying public land and developing illegal housing plots, which they later sold to buyers, earning crores of taka over the past two decades. In the Alinagar and Chinnomul areas, Yasin is widely known as the “king”. On October 4 last year, one person was beaten and hacked to death and at least 14 others were injured in a clash between two groups over supremacy and land grabbing in Jungle Salimpur. The following day, two television journalists were attacked while reporting on the violence. Police had earlier arrested Yasin from Chattogram’s Kotwali area on July 19, 2022, in connection with an attack on a union parishad member. Members of his group are also accused of hill cutting, illegal possession of firearms and controlling the movement of residents in parts of the area.

title: Man shot in attack targeting BNP leader at court premises
body: One person was injured during a gun attack targeting BNP leader Liaquat Ali Member at the Cox’s Bazar court premises yesterday, police said. Police identified the injured man as Moin Uddin, a cousin of Liaquat. Following the incident, an alleged criminal was detained from the scene along with a foreign-made pistol, bullets, and magazines. The detainee, Ziaul Haque Zia -- who was also injured in a beating -- is undergoing treatment at Cox’s Bazar Sadar Hospital under police guard, said Sheikh Mohammad Ali, OC of Cox’s Bazar Sadar Model Police Station. The incident took place around 11:30am. Liaquat, general secretary of Jhilongja union BNP, had gone to the court for a hearing in a case when he came under attack, said the OC. “He was targeted in the shooting. As he moved away, another person standing nearby was shot.” Moin was first taken to Cox’s Bazar Sadar Hospital and later referred to Chattogram Medical College Hospital in critical condition. The OC said the attack was primarily believed to be linked to a dispute over local dominance. “There had also been previous attacks on Liaquat Ali’s house.” However, he declined to comment on whether others were involved in the attack.

title: The horror that befell Ramisa
body: After a five‑day investigation, police yesterday submitted the charge sheet in the case over the brutal rape and murder of eight‑year‑old Ramisa Akhter in the capital’s Pallabi. According to the charge sheet, prime suspect Sohel Rana raped and murdered the child and destroyed evidence. His wife, Swapna Khatun, 26, is accused of destroying evidence and giving false information to protect Sohel. The filing of the 47‑page document marks one of the fastest charge sheet submissions in recent times. Judge Masrur Salekin of the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal in Dhaka Metropolitan accepted the charges and set June 1 for a hearing on the charge framing, said Pankoj Peter Gomes, bench assistant of the tribunal. Earlier in the day, Pallabi Police Station Sub‑Inspector Ohiduzzaman submitted the charge sheet before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate’s Court in Dhaka. After a hearing, the case was transferred to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal. Also yesterday, the government appointed Supreme Court lawyer Musa Kalimullah as a state defence lawyer to represent the accused. Earlier on Sunday, the government appointed Azizur Rahman Dulu as special public prosecutor in the case. The charge sheet said Sohel, 30, an autorickshaw mechanic, told a Dhaka metropolitan magistrate on May 20 that he regularly took drugs in the mornings after others in the shared flat left for work. Around 9:30am on May 19, Sohel saw Ramisa next door and called her in. Once she came, he took her to his bathroom. “When she screamed, Sohel clamped a hand over her mouth and stuffed rags into it before raping her,” the confessional statement read. When the child lost consciousness, Sohel thought she had died. He then used a knife to mutilate her body in an attempt to destroy evidence, the statement said. According to the autopsy report, Ramisa died from haemorrhage and shock caused by decapitation. All of her injuries were antemortem -- inflicted before death. Sohel’s confession also narrates the chain of events that followed. He said, “Around 10:30am, while people were searching for Ramisa, her mother saw Ramisa’s shoes in front of my room and started calling out for her. As there was no response, people began banging on my door. At that, I panicked. “My wife told me to flee, and I broke the window grilles with a wrench and escaped. As the crowd kept pounding on the door, my wife held it shut and helped me flee.” She opened the door only when he successfully fled, he added. Meanwhile, Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed yesterday said the trial proceedings in the case are likely to be completed within the next five to seven days. Arrangements are being made to keep the relevant court open during the Eid holidays, he added. Referring to the recent rise in gruesome crimes, Salahuddin said, “This is a form of social degradation. We need social reform. The level, frequency and nature of rape are going beyond our limits of tolerance.” Sparked by Ramisa’s murder, protests continued for the fifth straight day in Dhaka and beyond yesterday, denouncing violence against women, children and other vulnerable groups. Demonstrators demanded swift justice for sexual violence and stronger social resistance to such crimes.

title: Nearly 6,000 minor girls raped in 10yrs
body: At least 5,942 minor girls were raped across the country between January 2016 and March 2026, human rights organisation Odhikar said in a statement yesterday. Of them, 1,018 were victims of gang-rape, 236 were murdered after the assault, and 44 died by suicide. The organisation noted that the figures likely represent only a fraction of actual cases, as many incidents remain unreported due to stigma, fear of retaliation, and harassment during judicial proceedings. Expressing concern over the recent rape and murder of an eight-year-old in Dhaka’s Pallabi, Odhikar in the statement said, “Ramisa’s death is not an isolated incident. It reflects the broader failure of state institutions, law enforcement agencies and social accountability mechanisms to ensure the safety and dignity of children.” The group highlighted serious weaknesses in the criminal justice system, pointing to the absence of child-sensitive investigation mechanisms and the ease with which alleged perpetrators secure bail and intimidate victims, perpetuating a culture of impunity. Condemning sexual violence against children, Odhikar demanded an impartial investigation and speedy trial in Ramisa’s case, alongside exemplary punishment for the killers. It also called for the establishment of child-sensitive investigation and support systems, protection for victims and witnesses, and the creation of both a public database documenting violence against women and children and a police database of convicted child sex offenders. The organisation further urged effective implementation of child protection laws and nationwide awareness campaigns against gender-based violence. Odhikar stressed that urgent reforms are needed to restore trust in justice system and ensure the safety of children across the country.

title: Rape, abuse of girls: Nine more held in 7 districts over 2 days
body: At least nine people were arrested in the last two days on charges of rape and attempted rape in seven districts. In Bandarban, a 15-year-old boy has been accused of raping a five-year-old girl in Thanchi upazila yesterday. The victim’s relatives filed a complaint with Thanchi Police Station around 10:30am yesterday. Officer-in-Charge in Thanchi Police Station, Kanan Sarkar said, “Based on the case, the accused was detained with assistance from locals. He was produced before the Bandarban District Court.” He was later sent to jail. Meanwhile, the child was sent to Bandarban District Sadar Hospital for medical examination and primary treatment. According to locals, the child was allegedly lured to the accused’s house with the promise of food and was then raped. When the victim informed her family, she was immediately taken to the local health complex for treatment. When news of the incident quickly spread among students and locals, they later surrounded the police station, demanding justice for the victim and punishment for the accused. Tension briefly escalated between locals and members of the police and Border Guard Bangladesh. In Kishoreganj, police yesterday detained a man on charges of raping a seven-year-old girl in Kuliarchar upazila. The detainee, Mahbubullah, 23, from Khalishapur village under Netrokona’s Purbadhala, is an imam of a local mosque. Citing locals, police said Mahbubullah raped the girl yesterday afternoon when she went to deliver food to him. As the news spread, locals confined Mahbubullah in the mosque. On information, police rushed to the spot and detained him, said Kazi Arif, OC of Kuliarchar Police Station. The victim’s mother filed a case last evening in this regard. In Gazipur, a man was arrested yesterday on charges of raping a nine-year-old girl on multiple occasions and taking photos. The accused, Selim Khan, 40, is a relative of the victim. Police said the incident came to light on Saturday after the victim’s elder sister found some objectionable photos on Selim’s computer. Later the same day, the victim’s father filed a case with Pubail Police Station. Selim was arrested around 4:00am yesterday from his residence, said the station’s OC Atiqur Rahman. The family said that between March 15 and May 21, the accused lured the child to his room on several occasions, raped her, recorded the acts, and saved the pictures on his computer. In Barguna, police yesterday arrested a man allegedly for raping a teenage girl. The arrestee, Alamgir Hossain, is a resident of Amtali upazila and a relative of the victim. Police said Alamgir raped the girl on May 18 when she was alone and made the same attempt again on Saturday afternoon. The victim’s grandmother yesterday filed a case, and police later arrested the accused, said Abu Shahadat Hasnain Parvez, OC of Amtali Police Station. In Savar, three people -- Saiful Islam Rana, 36; Mujibur Rahman, 48; and a 16-year-old boy -- were arrested on Saturday night on charges of raping a 16-year-old homemaker. Police said the prime accused, Saiful, a mason and neighbour of the victim, had previously made inappropriate advances towards her. On May 21, he and his accomplices broke into the victim’s room around 3:00am and raped her. They also recorded the assault on their phones and threatened the victim with publishing the video if she disclosed the incident. The victim’s mother filed a case against five people the same night, after which police arrested the three from the Kaundia area, said Noor Mohammad, inspector (investigation) of Savar Model Police Station. Another accused, Shakib, 20, and one unidentified person remain absconding. The inspector said police were trying to arrest them. The victim is receiving treatment at Dhaka Medical College Hospital’s One-Stop Crisis Centre. In Jamalpur, police on Saturday night arrested a man on charges of attempting to rape a teenager. The accused, Shahjahan Molla, 45, is a resident of Madarganj upazila’s Mirzapur area. Police said the 14-year-old girl was home alone on Thursday afternoon when the accused broke in and attempted to rape her. Hearing her screams, locals rushed there and rescued the girl, but the accused fled the scene. The victim’s mother filed a case with Madarganj Model Police Station, after which police arrested the accused, said OC Snehashish Roy. In Jashore, a medical officer of Monirampur Upazila Health Complex was arrested on Saturday night on charges of raping his sister-in-law. Dr Rafsan Jani, 45, was arrested from his residence in the Upashahar area of Jashore town, said Abu Syed, OC of Monirampur Police Station. He had been on the run since the 19-year-old victim filed the rape case in April. According to the case statement, around three years ago, Rafsan allegedly brought his sister-in-law to the district under the pretext of supporting her education and helping care for his children. During her stay, he allegedly forced her into sexual relations and secretly recorded videos of the assaults. The victim alleged that the doctor later used the footage to blackmail her repeatedly. (Our correspondents from Bandarban, Kishoreganj, Patuakhali, Jamalpur, Gazipur, Savar and Benapole contributed to the report.)

title: Mine blasts: 3 Bangladeshis killed along Myanmar border
body: Three Bangladeshis were killed in landmine explosions in an area near the Bangladesh-Myanmar border in Naikhongchhari upazila of Bandarban yesterday. The incident took place around 10:00am in Bhalukia Para area, said Naikhongchhari Police Station OC Mozammel Haque. The deceased were identified as Akyamong Tanchangya, 40; Chingkshong Chakma, 34; and Chopoching Chakma, 32 -- all residents of Bhalukia Para. According to locals, the three men were in their banana plantation when a landmine exploded, killing Akyamong on the spot. When the other two attempted to rescue him, two additional explosions occurred, killing both. Bimal Tanchangya, a local, alleged that Arakan Rohingya Salvation Army (ARSA) members frequently moved through the border area and often took shelter in local plantations. OC Mozammel last night said efforts are underway to recover the bodies and inspect the site. Contacted, Naikhongchhari UNO Enamul Hasan said it was not immediately clear who planted the mines. “Preliminary information suggests the explosions occurred in the no-man’s-land area along the Bangladesh-Myanmar border,” he said.

title: Imam arrested over alleged rape of 7-year-old girl in Kishoreganj
body: Police have arrested a man on charge of raping a seven-year-old girl in Kuliarchar upazila of Kishoreganj. The arrestee was identified as Mahbubullah, 23, of Khalishapur village in Purbadhala upazila of Netrokona. Mahbubullah is the imam of Paschim Tarakandi Jame Mosque in Ramdi union of Kuliarchar, said Kuliarchar Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Kazi Arif. According to police and local sources, Mahbubullah raped the girl this afternoon when she went to deliver food to him. As the news spread, locals locked Mahbubullah in the mosque and informed the police. Upon receiving the information, a team from Kuliarchar Police Station went to the spot and arrested him. Police said the victim has been rescued and sent to the hospital for physical examination and treatment. The OC said they are investigating the incident. “There will be no compromise under any kind of influence or pressure. Strict action will be taken according to the law through an impartial investigation,” he said.

title: 3 killed in separate incidents in Pirojpur and Pabna
body: Three people were killed in separate incidents in Pirojpur and Pabna today. In Pirojpur’s Mathbaria upazila, two men were stabbed to death in two incidents at noon. The deceased were identified as Kyum Howlader, 30, of Paschim Shener Tikikata village under Tikikata union, and Yousuf Sharif, 35, of Phuljhuri village under Dhanisafa union in the upazila. Partha Chakraborty, additional superintendent of police of Mathbaria circle, confirmed the incidents. He said between 12:30pm and 1:30pm, miscreants entered Kyum’s house and hacked him on the head with an axe while he was sleeping. At the time, his mother was cooking in the house. Later, she found him dead and informed the police. In another incident, Yousuf Sharif was hacked to death with sharp weapons allegedly by four to five neighbours over a land dispute in front of his house at around 1:30pm. Following the incident, police detained two men for questioning, the ASP said. “We are trying to identify and arrest those involved in the killings,” he added. In Pabna, a man was beaten to death allegedly over a trivial matter in Ishwardi upazila. The deceased was identified as Mahabul Hossain, 60, of Sahapur Purbo Para area under Sahapur union in the upazila, said Ishwardi Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Md Asadur Rahman. The incident happened in the area around 11:30am. Police and local sources said a goat belonging to Mahabul ate leaves from a tree owned by neighbours Bashar Munshi and his elder brother Taslim Munshi in the morning, triggering an altercation between the two sides. At one stage, they got involved in a fight. Bashar and Taslim allegedly beat Mahabul indiscriminately with wooden sticks, injuring him on the neck, head, and other parts of his body. Locals and family members rescued Mahabul with critical injuries, and took him to Ishwardi Upazila Health Complex, where doctors declared him dead. Tension spread in the area following the incident, and a team from Ishwardi Police Station rushed to the spot and brought the situation under control. The OC said police have detained Bashar in connection with the incident, while efforts are underway to arrest the other accused. Additional police have been deployed in the area to maintain law and order, he said, adding that the victim’s family is preparing to file a case over the incident. Our correspondents from Pirojpur and Pabna contributed to this report.

title: Three, including a minor, arrested over gang-rape of housewife in Savar
body: Police yesterday arrested three people, including a minor, in connection with the gang-rape of a housewife in the Kaundia area of Savar over three consecutive days. The arrestees are Saiful Islam Rana, 36; Mujibur Rahman, 48; and a 16-year-old boy. Another accused Shakib, 20, and one unidentified person remain absconding. All arrestees have been sent to court, confirmed Savar Model Police Station Inspector (Investigation) Noor Mohammad. The arrests followed a case filed yesterday under the Pornography Control Act, 2012 and Women and Children Repression Prevention Act, 2000 with Savar Model Police Station by the victim's mother, naming four people and one unknown accused. According to the case statement, prime accused Saiful Islam Rana, 36, a mason and neighbour of the victim, had previously made inappropriate advances toward her. It also added that on May 21 night, while the victim's husband was away, Rana and accomplices entered her room at around 3:00am and raped her. The acts were recorded on mobile phones. The victim was threatened with the video being circulated if she disclosed the matter. However, family members told The Daily Star last night that the abuse began earlier. On May 19, Rana and two others allegedly raped the victim while she was bathing, recording the assault. The same accused allegedly returned the following two days, using the footage as blackmail. When asked why the case mentioned only one day's incident despite the family's account of three consecutive days of assault, Inspector Noor told The Daily Star, "The case has been recorded as per the details narrated by the victim and her mother. Our senior officials have also spoken to the victim." The alleged rape incident came to light yesterday when the victim attempted suicide. Later, when Rana returned home around 8:00pm last night, victim's family members detained him. Locals subsequently beat him up before handing him over to police. The other two accused were arrested during a raid last night. Inspector Noor said raids are ongoing to apprehend the remaining accused. The victim is receiving treatment at Dhaka Medical College Hospital's One-Stop Crisis Centre, he added.

title: 72 lower court judges appointed for urgent cases during court vacation
body: The government has appointed 72 judicial officers (lower court judges) as vacation judges in different districts across the country in order to deal with urgent civil and criminal cases during the upcoming civil court vacation for a 15-day period, from June 1 to 15. The appointments have been made with permission and advice from the Supreme Court. The law ministry issued a notification to this effect today under instruction from the president, saying that the vacation judges will receive, hear and dispose of urgent civil and criminal cases during the vacation period to ensure uninterrupted judicial services. It said the judges on vacation duty will be entitled to use government vehicles and receive a 15-day vacation allowance in accordance with existing rules. The judicial officials assigned to vacation duty outside their respective stations will receive travelling allowance and daily allowance as per the rules, according the notification.

title: Man sentenced to death over rape of 11-year-old in Meherpur
body: A court in Meherpur today sentenced a man to death over raping an 11-year-old girl last year. The convict is Shakil Hossain, 25, of Chandpur Dakshinpara village under Gangni upazila. The court also fined him Tk 3 lakh, in default of which he will have to serve another year in prison. District and Sessions Judge Md Tajul Islam of Meherpur Prevention of Children Repression Tribunal delivered the verdict at noon. Advocate Mostafizur Rahman Tuhin stood for the state, while Advocate Maruf Ahmed Bijon defended the accused. The case was settled in just 29 working days. To ensure a speedy trial, testimonies from distant witnesses were taken virtually. A total of 12 witnesses testified in the case. According to the prosecution, on June 16, 2025, the child was carrying food to her father, who was working in a field, when Shakil took her to a nearby jute field and raped her. Hearing the child's cries, farmers working in nearby fields rushed to the scene, but Shakil managed to flee. Later that afternoon, locals caught Shakil, beat him up, and handed him over to the police.

title: Ramisa murder: Charges accepted against Sohel, Swapna
body: A special tribunal in Dhaka has accepted the charges against two accused in the case filed over rape and murder of eight-year-old Ramisa Akter in Dhaka’s Pallabi. Judge Masrur Salekin of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal passed the order around 5:00pm today, said Pankoj Peter Gomes, bench assistant of the tribunal. The tribunal also set June 1 for a hearing on charge framing in the case, he added. Earlier in the day, police submitted the charge sheet in the case before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate’s Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel Rana and his wife Swapna Khatun. Later, the case was transferred to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal for disposal. The accused were brought to the lockup of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge’s Court between 11:20am and 11:45am, said Sub-Inspector Ripon Mollah, in-charge of the lockup.

title: Man arrested over raping 9-year-old multiple times, taking photos in Gazipur
body: Police have arrested a man named Selim Khan, 40, on charges of raping a nine-year-old multiple times in the Pubail area of Gazipur and taking objectionable photos. The victim's father has filed a case under the Violence against Women and Children Prevention Act and the Pornography Control Act with Pubail Police Station. Pubail Police Station Officer-in-Charge Atiqur Rahman told The Daily Star that the arrested accused is the child's uncle (paternal aunt's husband). According to the family, the child was raped at least five times. The OC said that the child has been sent to the hospital. After recording the case, the accused has been sent to the court. According to the case report, Selim Khan, of Bikrampur village under Louhajang upazila in Munshiganj, had been living with his family in the plaintiff's house in Hydarabad Gazariatek area of Pubail for the past five years. The plaintiff's nine-year-old daughter, a class four student of a local madrasa, often went to Selim's room. On May 23, the plaintiff's eldest daughter, 18, went to Selim's room. While looking at the pictures on the desktop computer used by Selim Khan, she saw some objectionable and obscene pictures of her younger sister. She immediately informed other family members about the matter. Later, it was learned that the child was raped multiple times. The child's family said that between March 15 and May 21, the accused took the child to his room on several occasions by luring her with chips and other food items. The accused allegedly recorded the acts of rape and saved the pictures on his computer. Anwar Hossain, sub-inspector of Pubail Police Station, told The Daily Star, "I arrested him from Hydarabad Gazariatek in Gazipur early this morning on charges of rape. He was sent to jail by the court this afternoon." When asked whether remand has been sought for the accused, he added that remand has not been sought.

title: 15-year-old accused of raping 5-year-old in Bandarban
body: A 15-year-old boy has been accused of raping a five-year-old Tripura girl in Thanchi upazila of Bandarban. “Victim's guardian filed a complaint with the police station at around 10:30am today. Based on it, the accused was detained with assistance from locals. A case was subsequently filed, and the accused was produced before the Bandarban District Court,” Thanchi Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Kanan Sarkar said today. “The child was sent to Bandarban District Sadar Hospital for medical examination and primary treatment,” he added. According to locals, the child was allegedly lured to the accused's house with the promise of food last night, where she was raped. The girl later informed her parents about the incident, after which she was immediately taken to the local health complex for treatment. The accused is a resident of Notun Para under Thanchi Sadar union, locals said. After residents handed the accused over to police, news of the incident quickly spread among students and local people. Protesters later surrounded the police station, demanding justice for the victim and punishment for the accused. Tension briefly escalated between local residents and members of the police and Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB). With assistance from the BGB, police later sent the accused to the Bandarban District Court. Thanchi Upazila Health and Family Planning Officer Dr Mohammad Wahidduzzaman said, “After receiving information about the incident, a female doctor at the Upazila Health Complex was instructed to provide necessary medical assistance.”

title: Unidentified youth’s body recovered from Padma River in Rajshahi
body: Police recovered the body of an unidentified youth from the Padma River in Rajshahi city yesterday evening, with his hands tied and a towel wrapped around his neck. The body was found floating near the Borokuthi area along the river, police said. The deceased was in his 20s. According to police, the youth was wearing blue jeans and a green T-shirt. Part of a towel was wrapped around his neck, while the other part was used to tie both of his hands. Investigators suspect he died four to five days ago. Officer-in-Charge of Boalia Police Station Robiul Islam said police recovered the body after being informed by locals and sent it to Rajshahi Medical College Hospital morgue for autopsy. Although police are primarily treating the incident as a murder, they have not yet confirmed whether the victim was killed in the area and dumped in the river or whether the body floated there from elsewhere, he added. Inspector Bikash Mondal, in charge of the Rajshahi Metropolitan River Police Outpost, said fingerprints were collected with assistance from the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) and Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) to identify the victim through the national identity database.
