The OC added that the place where the body was recovered falls under the jurisdiction of the river police, and further legal proceedings would therefore be handled by them. No case had been filed with Boalia Police Station as of Sunday afternoon. However, due to decomposition, clear fingerprints could not be obtained, and no match was found in the database, he said. Police have sent wireless messages to police stations across the country to check for any missing person reports matching the victim’s description, but no information had been received as of Sunday afternoon. Authorities said efforts to identify the victim are ongoing.

title: Ramisa murder: Charges pressed against Sohel Rana and Swapna
body: Police have pressed charges against two accused in the rape and murder of eight-year-old Ramisa Akter in Dhaka’s Pallabi. The charge sheet was submitted this afternoon before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate's Court, Mia Mohammad Ashish Bin Hasan, deputy commissioner of DMP's prosecution division, told The Daily Star. The prime accused, Sohel Rana, and his wife Swapna Akter were brought to the lockup of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court between 11:20am and 11:45am, said Sub-Inspector Ripon Mollah, in-charge of the lockup. Yesterday, the government appointed Advocate Azizur Rahman Dulu as Special Public Prosecutor to conduct the sensational case. On Friday, the Dhaka Bar Association decided not to provide legal support to the accused, considering the gravity of the crime. On May 19, Ramisa's beheaded body was found in the house of her neighbour, Sohel, 31. A day after the killing, the victim’s father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, filed the case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing the couple and an unidentified person. The same day, accused Sohel confessed before a magistrate to raping and killing Ramisa. According to the case statement, Sohel raped the child and to conceal the crime, he beheaded her and attempted to dismember the body.

title: Man shot in attack targeting BNP leader at Cox’s Bazar court premises
body: One person was injured during a gun attack targeting BNP leader Liaquat Ali Member at the Cox’s Bazar court premises today, police said. Police identified the injured man as Moin Uddin, a cousin of Liaquat. Following the incident, an alleged criminal was detained from the scene along with a foreign-made pistol, bullets and magazines. The detainee, who was also injured in a beating, is currently undergoing treatment at Cox’s Bazar Sadar Hospital under police guard, said Sheikh Mohammad Ali, officer-in-charge of Cox’s Bazar Sadar Model Police Station. The incident took place around 11:30am at the district judge court premises, an area surrounded by key government establishments, including the office of the superintendent of police, the district judge’s residence and the district council building. The OC said Liaquat, general secretary of Jhilongja union BNP, had gone to the court for a hearing in a case when he came under attack. “He was targeted in the shooting. As he moved away, another person standing nearby was shot,” the OC said. Moin was first taken to Cox’s Bazar Sadar Hospital and later referred to Chattogram Medical College Hospital in critical condition. The OC added that the suspect, Ziaul Haque Zia, is from the Kalirchhara area of Eidgaon upazila and the attack was primarily believed to be linked to a dispute over local dominance. “There had also been previous attacks on Liaquat Ali’s house,” he added. However, he declined to comment immediately on whether others were involved in the attack. Additional Public Prosecutor Advocate Mohammad Abdur Rashid said he was inside the court of the Second Additional District and Sessions Judge during the incident. “I suddenly heard several gunshots from the eastern side. Looking through the window, I saw two bloodied men lying beside a white luxury vehicle. One of them ran into the courtroom,” he said. “Later, police detained a slim-built young man and put him into a vehicle,” he added. “If gunfire erupts in broad daylight inside the court premises, then litigants, lawyers and judges — no one is safe,” he said. Videos obtained by this correspondent show several men forcibly dragging a person into a white SUV while multiple gunshots can be heard in the background. Regarding the footage, OC Sheikh Mohammad Ali said the person being forced into the vehicle was detained suspect Zia. Further details could not be known immediately. Asked about the number of shots fired, the lawyer said he heard five to six rounds fired in quick succession.

title: Trial in Ramisa rape and murder case likely to end in 5-7 days: Home minister
body: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed today said the trial proceedings in the rape and murder case of seven-year-old Ramisa are likely to be completed within the next five to seven days. “Considering everything, we expect the charge sheet to be submitted today, and the trial is highly likely to be completed within five to seven days,” he said. Arrangements are being made to keep the relevant court open during the Eid holidays to ensure justice in the case involving the rape and murder of the child in the capital’s Pallabi area, he added. The minister made the remarks at the “BSRF Dialogue” organised by the Bangladesh Secretariat Reporters Forum at the Secretariat Media Centre today. The event was presided over by BSRF President Masudul Haque and attended by Chief Information Officer Syed Abdal Ahmed. General Secretary Obaidullah Badal moderated the discussion. Referring to the recent rise in such incidents, Salahuddin said, “This is actually a social degradation; social reform is needed. Our society has been affected by some bad cultures. The level, frequency and nature of rape are going beyond our limits of tolerance.” He mentioned the accused was arrested within seven hours of the incident. “Within one day of the accused giving a confessional statement before the court, his wife was also arrested as an accomplice. With the court’s permission, we conducted the DNA test very quickly,” he said. The minister said a special public prosecutor had been appointed solely to handle the case. Responding to a question about the return of ousted former prime minister Sheikh Hasina, the home minister said, “We have sent formal letters multiple times to bring her back. We want her to return through the proper legal process and face trial.”

title: Man held over alleged sexual assault of teenage girl in Jamalpur
body: Police yesterday arrested a man in Jamalpur’s Madarganj upazila on charges of sexually assaulting a teenage girl while she was sleeping at her residence. The accused, Shahjahan Molla, 45, was arrested from the Mirzapur area under Balijuri union last night, said Snehashish Roy, officer-in-charge of Madarganj Model Police Station. He will be produced before a court today, the OC said. According to the case statement, the incident took place on Thursday afternoon when the victim’s mother had gone nearby with goats and her father went to the Balijuri Union Parishad to collect VGF rice. At the time, the 14-year-old girl was alone at home and asleep in her room. Taking the opportunity, the accused, who was known to the victim’s family, allegedly entered the room and sexually assaulted the girl. The case statement said the accused threatened the girl with consequences if she disclosed the matter to anyone. He fled the scene after the girl screamed.

title: Ramisa murder: Accused couple produced before court as charge sheet nears filing
body: Two accused in the rape and murder of eight-year-old Ramisa Akter in the capital's Pallabi area were produced before a Dhaka court today. The prime accused, Sohel Rana, and his wife Swapna Khatun, were brought to the lockup of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court between 11:20am and 11:45am, Sub-Inspector Ripon Mollah, in-charge of the lockup, told The Daily Star. Police will submit the charge sheet before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate's Court this noon, and the case will be transferred to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal of Dhaka for its disposal, said Mia Mohammad Ashish Bin Hasan, deputy commissioner of DMP's prosecution division. "We have already taken necessary steps so that everything goes smoothly," he added. Yesterday, the government appointed Advocate Azizur Rahman Dulu as Special Public Prosecutor to conduct the sensational case. On Friday, the Dhaka Bar Association decided not to provide legal support to the accused through an emergency virtual meeting of the executive committee of the bar association, considering the gravity of this heinous offence. On Tuesday, Ramisa, a Class 2 student at Popular Model High School, was found beheaded in the house of her neighbour, Sohel, 31, after she was raped and killed. A day after the killing, the victim's father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, filed the case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing the couple and an unidentified person. On the same day, accused Sohel confessed before a magistrate to raping and killing Ramisa. According to the case statement, Sohel, a neighbour of the victim, lured Ramisa into his room and raped her. To conceal the crime, he slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body.

title: Sitakunda child murder: Police likely to press charges by May 30
body: Sitakunda police are set to press charges by May 30 against the accused in the murder case of a seven-year-old child, whose throat was slit after a rape attempt on March 1. The child, Jannatul Naima Era, was found wandering in the Sitakunda Eco Park with her throat slit. She was rescued from a hill inside the park by a group of labourers and rushed to the upazila health complex. The incident sparked nationwide outrage. Era was later transferred to Chattogram Medical College Hospital, where she succumbed to her injuries while undergoing treatment on March 3. That same day, police arrested Babu Sheikh, 45, a neighbour of the victim, after scrutinising CCTV footage in connection with the rape attempt and subsequent murder. He was later produced before a court, which sent him to jail. Speaking to The Daily Star, Mahinul Islam, officer-in-charge of Sitakunda Model Police Station, said, “We had sent the victim’s clothes, samples, and other evidence for examination. We received the DNA report from Dhaka a few days ago, which showed a positive match. We hope to submit our findings implicating Babu Sheikh by May 30.” Earlier, police said the accused had a prior dispute with the victim’s father, which led to the incident. During primary interrogation, Babu admitted that he had taken the girl to a hill inside the park from her house and attempted to rape her but failed. When she screamed and threatened to tell her parents, he slit her throat with a knife and dumped her at the foot of the hill. The victim managed to walk nearly one kilometre in that condition before being rescued.

title: Ramisa murder: Charge sheet likely today
body: Police are set to submit the charge sheet today in the rape and murder case of eight-year-old Ramisa in the capital’s Pallabi area on May 19. The Criminal Investigation Department handed over the chemical analysis and DNA reports to the investigation officer yesterday. Meanwhile, the government has said the formal trial proceedings in the case would begin after the Eid-ul-Azha holidays. Contacted by The Daily Star yesterday, Mostak Sarker, deputy commissioner of Dhaka Metropolitan Police (Mirpur Division), said, “We’ve received the post-mortem, chemical analysis, and forensic reports. We’re hoping to submit the charge sheet tomorrow [today] following the government’s directives.” Meanwhile, according to an office memo issued by the Law and Justice Division yesterday, the government has appointed Supreme Court lawyer Advocate Mohammad Azizur Rahman Dulu as a special public prosecutor to ensure a swift and effective trial. On May 19, Ramisa was found beheaded in the house of her neighbour, Sohel Rana, 31, after she was raped and killed. Sohel fled shortly after the incident, while his wife, Swapna Akhter, 26, was arrested from the scene. Sohel was arrested from Narayanganj’s Fatullah later that evening. The next day, he made a confessional statement before a magistrate, who then sent him to jail. Swapna was sent to jail by another Dhaka court as an accomplice in the crime. Speaking at a programme at the capital’s BRAC Centre yesterday, Law Minister Mohammad Asaduzzaman said the formal trial proceedings would begin after Eid, adding that filing the charge sheet without the DNA report could have raised questions about the trial later. The minister also addressed delays in High Court approvals of death sentences. “After a trial court delivers a death sentence, the case goes to the High Court for approval, where preparing the paper book often takes a long time, delaying the final verdict. The government is now working to speed up the process and make it more efficient.” At a separate event, Information and Broadcasting Minister Zahir Uddin Swapon said the government has taken all necessary measures to quickly bring the perpetrators to justice. Speaking to journalists after a meeting of the Sher-e-Bangla AK Fazlul Huq Foundation at the International Mother Language Institute in the capital’s Segunbagicha, he said public outrage and media coverage over such incidents would help the government formulate stricter laws against child abuse. Meanwhile, protests continued for the fifth consecutive day, demanding justice for Ramisa and stronger measures to ensure the safety of women and children.

title: Ex-CJ Khairul Haque shown arrested in fresh case
body: The release of former chief justice ABM Khairul Haque has been stalled after he was shown arrested yesterday in another murder case linked to the 2024 July uprising. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Sarah Farzana Haque showed Khairul arrested in a case filed with Jatrabari Police Station following an application from the investigation officer (IO), Md Ibrahim Khalil, a sub-inspector of the same police station, said Khairul’s lawyer, Motaher Hossain Saju. In his application, IO Ibrahim said he had found preliminary evidence of Khairul’s involvement in the case filed on November 16, 2024. However, Khairul is not named in the case as an accused, and the IO did not mention in the application what specific offence had allegedly been committed by the 81-year-old former chief justice. Defence lawyer Saju said his client would not be released from jail unless he secured bail in the case. Earlier, Khairul was granted bail in seven other cases, the lawyer added. During yesterday’s hearing, Dhaka Metropolitan Public Prosecutor Omar Faruq Faruqi first argued in favour of showing Khairul arrested. He said, “In connection with this case, many people have already been arrested during the investigation. In this process, the investigating officer found specific involvement of Khairul Haque. For the sake of a proper investigation, I pray that he be shown arrested in this case.” Opposing the prosecution’s plea, defence lawyer Mostafizur Rahman said, “There is nothing in the investigator’s statement that justifies showing him arrested. He is not a named accused in the case. The incident in this case took place at 11:00am. “Again, he has also been shown arrested in a case filed with Adabor Police Station, where the incident also occurred at 11:00am. One person cannot be present in two places at the same time. We pray that he not be shown arrested.” After hearing both sides, the judge ordered that Khairul be shown arrested in the case filed by Jobayer Ahmed over the killing of his brother Khobaib in Jatrabari on August 5, 2024. On May 17, a High Court bench -- following a petition filed by Khairul’s son, advocate Md Asik Ul Haque -- directed the government not to show Khairul arrested or harass him unless he is named as an accused in a specific case. Khairul was arrested at his Dhanmondi residence in Dhaka on July 24, 2025, nearly a year after the fall of the Awami League government. He was later shown arrested in multiple cases, including several filed over killings during the July uprising and allegations of manipulating the Supreme Court verdict on the caretaker government system, and has remained in jail since then.

title: Road crashes kill 16 in five districts
body: At least 16 people were killed and more than 20 injured in road crashes in Jashore, Kushtia, Dinajpur, Chattogram and Meherpur yesterday. In Jashore Sadar upazila, a covered van hit a van before ramming into a battery-run easy-bike around 11:00am, leaving three people dead on the spot. The deceased are Mohammad Ayub Ali, 43, an easy-bike driver from Sadar upazila; Brishti Saha, 24, of Ghoragachha Sahapara; and her son Souvik Saha, 5. Md Masum Khan, officer-in-charge of Jashore Kotwali Police Station, said the covered van driver had been detained. Investigation and legal proceedings were underway, he added. In Kushtia, four people were killed and at least 20-25 others injured when a passenger bus of Tanha Paribahan crashed into a sand-laden truck before plunging into a roadside ditch on the Kushtia-Rajbari regional highway in Khoksa upazila around 11:30am. Two people died on the spot, while two others succumbed to their injuries after being taken to hospital, said OC Abu Obayed of Kushtia Highway Police Station. Two of the deceased were identified as Nabil Hossain, 28, of Faridpur, and Rafia Khatun of Kushtia. The injured were taken to Khoksa Upazila Health Complex, from where five were referred to 250-bed Kushtia General Hospital. In Dinajpur, a truck hit a motorcycle coming from the opposite direction in Raniganj area of Ghoraghat upazila around 8:45am, leaving the rider and his two pillions dead on the spot. The deceased are Abdul Kaiyum Mushfique, 20; Saikat Hossain, 18; and Al Amin, 16. All were local residents, said OC Shahidul Islam of Ghoraghat Police Station. Police seized the truck, but the driver managed to flee, the OC added. In the district’s Birganj upazila, an eight-year-old girl was killed after a tractor hit her bicycle on a village road near Deuli Munshipara area in the afternoon. Morsalina was the daughter of Mominur of Sahadubi Gainpara village. Officer-in-Charge of Birganj Police Station Md Shariful Islam said she sustained critical injuries in the crash and was rushed to Thakurgaon Sadar Hospital, where doctors declared her dead. The tractor driver fled the scene immediately after the collision while a case in this regard is being filed with the police station, OC added. A three-wheeler driver was killed after a truck hit the vehicle, causing the driver to lose control before crashing into a roadside tree on the Thakurgaon-Dinajpur highway. The deceased is Prodip Chandra Ghosh, 58, of Ghoshpara village. Nirmal Chandra Mahanta, officer-in-charge of Dashmile Highway Police Station, said the collision occurred around 10:30am in the Kabirajhat area after the three-wheeler entered the highway from a regional road. An unnatural death case was filed with the police station in this connection, he added. In Chattogram, two teenagers were killed and another injured when a passenger bus of Hanif Paribahan coming from the opposite direction hit their motorcycle on the Chattogram-Cox’s Bazar highway near Ansar Camp in Patiya upazila around 1:00pm, said Mostafizur Rahman, sub-inspector at Patiya Highway Police Station. The deceased were identified as Walid Al Taslim, 17, and Shahadat Hossain Samir, 16, of Kochuai union in the upazila. The injured, Tanvirul Islam Joy, 17, was first taken to the upazila health complex and later shifted to Chittagong Medical College Hospital. SI Mostafizur said locals seized the bus, but the driver managed to flee. In Meherpur Sadar, a truck hit a motorcycle coming from the opposite direction, leaving the rider and his pillion dead. The deceased were identified as Nayan Hossain, 22, of Khandkarpara, and Jiban Ali, 21, of Bandar village in the upazila. The incident took place near PTI intersection in Meherpur town. Critically injured Nayan and Jiban were rushed to Meherpur General Hospital, where they succumbed to their injuries. OC Selim Reza of Meherpur Sadar Police Station said the bodies had been handed over to their families and a case had been filed over the incident. [Our Benapole, Kushtia, Thakurgaon and Chattogram correspondents contributed to this report.]

title: 10 held in 2 days over rape, sexual abuse of minors
body: At least 10 people were arrested on charges of rape, abetting or attempting rape, and sexual abuse in five districts over the last two days, while one accused remains on the run. In all these cases, the victims were minors. Narayanganj police arrested Hero, 22, on Friday and his accomplice Sohel, 21, yesterday for allegedly luring a six-year-old child into a cropland and raping her on Friday afternoon, said Tarek Al Mehedi, superintendent of police in the district. Quoting family members, police said the child shared the incident with her family upon returning home, after which angry locals caught Hero and beat him. Sohel, meanwhile, fled the scene. Police later rescued Hero in critical condition and took him to Dhaka Medical College Hospital. “He [Hero] is now undergoing treatment in the ICU under police custody,” said Anowar Hossain, inspector (investigation) of Fatullah Police Station. Sohel was arrested from the district’s Baktaboli area yesterday morning. Meanwhile, the victim’s medical examination has been completed, Anowar said, adding that the child’s mother filed a case in this connection yesterday. In Jashore, police on Friday night arrested Alam Gazi, 35, for allegedly attempting to rape a three-year-old child. According to police and the victim’s family, Alam lured the child into a room by offering her fried snacks and tried to rape her on Friday morning. Hearing the toddler’s screams, locals rushed in and rescued her. Alam had fled the scene by then. The child’s father filed a case, after which police arrested the accused the same day, said Maruf Hossain, officer-in-charge of Sharsha Police Station. In Magura, three youths were arrested on Friday over the alleged rape of a 14-year-old girl and the circulation of a video of the incident on social media on May 4. The arrestees are Anik, 19, Nayan Sheikh, 19, and Rana Biswas, 20. All are residents of Sreepur upazila. The victim’s mother filed a case with Sreepur Police Station on Friday, naming five accused, said Ataur Rahman, inspector (investigation) of the police station. According to the case statement, the five abducted the child from the Sreepur tempo stand, raped her and recorded the assault on mobile phones. Later, the video was circulated on social media. The remaining two accused are currently absconding, the inspector said. In Patuakhali, a mosque imam was handed over to police after being beaten by a mob over the alleged rape of a seven-year-old boy early yesterday. The accused, Md Bellal Hossain, 28, was an imam in Kalapara upazila. The victim’s father filed a case yesterday noon, said Md Shamim Hawlader, officer-in-charge of Mohipur Police Station. According to the case statement, the child went to the mosque early in the morning for Quran lessons. At one point, Bellal allegedly took the child to his bedroom on the mosque premises and raped him. After returning home, the victim shared the incident with family members, after which locals beat the imam and handed him over to police, the OC said. In the same district, three youths were sent to jail yesterday on charges of attempting to rape a 15-year-old girl on May 15. The arrestees are Md Rabbi, 30, Emon Howlader, 28, and Rubel Mridha, 32 -- all residents of Kalapara upazila. Police said they forcibly entered the victim’s house and attempted to rape her. Hearing her screams, locals rushed to the scene and rescued her, while the perpetrators fled. The victim’s mother filed a case with Kalapara Police Station on May 16. Police later arrested the trio from Dhaka yesterday. They were then produced before a court, which sent them to jail the same day, said Md Nazrul Islam, OC of Kalapara Police Station. In Savar, a teacher at a girls’ madrasa was arrested on charges of allegedly sexually abusing a 13-year-old inside a classroom. The accused, Md Kamruzzaman, 36, teaches at the madrasa in the Kamalapur area, said Imran Hossain, a sub-inspector of Savar Model Police Station. He added that the incident took place around 4:00pm on Friday, when the teacher allegedly found the class-seven student alone in a classroom and molested her. In Faridpur, a case was filed against Md Khayer Dai, 35, on charges of attempting to rape a nine-year-old yesterday. The incident took place around 2:00pm in Saltha upazila. The victim’s mother filed the case, alleging that her daughter went to Khayer’s house to collect mangoes. Khayer, a father of two, then allegedly held the child at knifepoint and took her to a nearby orchard to rape her. Hearing her screams, locals rescued the girl, but Khayer managed to flee the scene. Police are trying to find and arrest the accused, said Md Babulur Rahman, OC of Saltha Police Station. In Dhaka, Ashraful Huda Rubel, 63, was arrested in the capital’s Kalabagan yesterday for allegedly raped an eight-year-old girl in the presence of another child on Friday. The victim’s mother filed a case the same day. According to the case statement, the victim and her friend were playing in a field near Rubel’s house when he allegedly lured them into his home with chocolates and then raped one of them. After the children began crying, the accused opened the door and the girls ran away and informed their families of the incident. The victim’s brother, upon hearing of the incident, gathered with locals and confined Rubel inside his home. Kalabagan police later reached the spot and arrested him. The child was later sent to hospital for a medical examination. (Our correspondents from Narayanganj, Benapole, Jhenaidah, Patuakhali, Savar and Faridpur contributed to the report.)

title: Youth’s mutilated body found in Madaripur riverbank
body: Police recovered the mutilated body of a young man from a riverbank in Kalkini upazila of Madaripur this afternoon. The deceased was identified as Shuhin Sardar, 27, of Uttar Saheberampur Sardar Bari area in the upazila, said Zahurul Alam, officer-in-charge of Kalkini Police Station. The OC said locals informed police around 4:30pm after spotting a body in the Saheberampur Launch Terminal area. He said the victim had severe stab wounds on his abdomen inflicted by a sharp weapon. There were also injuries to his eyes, and it appeared that attempts had been made to gouge them out. After completing the inquest, police sent the body to Madaripur Sadar Hospital morgue for an autopsy, he added. “A case is being prepared in connection with the incident. Primarily, it appears to be a murder,” the OC said. Police are investigating the incident and trying to identify and arrest those involved.

title: Three Ansar members arrested over 'creating chaos' during PM’s darbar programme
body: Police have arrested three Ansar members for allegedly creating disorder during the prime minister’s Darbar programme organised as part of the 46th National Rally of the Bangladesh Ansar and Village Defence Party (Ansar-VDP). The arrestees are Raihan Uddin Sarkar, of Samantapur area under Gazipur; Ashraful Alam, from the same area; and Shakil Ahmed, of Nohorir Par area in the city, said police. All three were trainees of the Youth Leadership Course and served as TDP team leaders in their respective areas. Following the incident, Ansar and VDP Adjutant Masud Hasan filed a case with Kaliakair Police Station on Thursday. According to the case statement, a group with vested interests allegedly tried to create planned disorder with the intention of disrupting and boycotting the prime minister’s Darbar programme scheduled for May 20 as part of the 46th National Rally of the Bangladesh Ansar and Village Defence Party-2026. The complaint further alleged that mobile phone numbers of Youth Leadership Course trainees were collected, and provocative as well as threatening messages were sent using two phone numbers originating from Australia and the US. Through these messages, trainees were allegedly incited to create panic during the PM’s Darbar programme, press various demands, and raise false allegations against the Director General. On May 18 and 19, WhatsApp messages were sent to several trainees, including Shakil Ahmed. Additionally, attempts were allegedly made on May 17 to spread confusion among 177 allowance-receiving members who arrived at the Bangladesh Ansar and VDP Academy in Safipur, said the case statement. On May 18 at around 9:30 pm, several individuals entered the Youth Leadership Course barracks and threatened to boycott the assembly unless demands such as increased allowances, ration benefits, sewing allowances, 100 percent appointment of Training Instructors (TIs) from among team leaders, and the provision of boots or Oxford shoes instead of PT shoes were met by the Prime Minister. The case also alleged that false and misleading information regarding the “Sanjibon Project” was spread in an attempt to provoke and agitate the trainees. Complainant Masud Hasan said, “A case has been filed with Kaliakair Police Station over allegations of creating disorder surrounding the assembly. Police have arrested three people in connection with the case.” Shahidul Islam, officer-in-charge of Kaliakair Police Station, told The Daily Star on Saturday night, “The three arrested accused were produced before the court on Friday afternoon, where they gave confessional statements under Section 164. Later, the court ordered that they be sent to jail.”

title: Money-counting video goes viral: Local Jubo Dal leader removed from post in Netrokona
body: A local leader of Jubo Dal in Kalmakanda upazila of Netrokona has been relieved of his party post after a video showing him counting stacks of money went viral on Facebook. The individual, Md Parvez Bhuiyan, served as joint convener of Lengura union Jubo Dal in Kalmakanda upazila. A press release signed by Rakibul Hasan Ratan, senior joint convener of Kalmakanda upazila Jubo Dal, was issued today announcing the decision. According to the release, action was taken against Parvez on allegations of violating party discipline, creating social disorder, and engaging in unethical activities. The statement also said the organisation currently has no ties with Parvez Bhuiyan and will not take responsibility for any of his personal activities. The video, which spread on social media two days ago, shows Parvez counting large bundles of cash placed on a table. The footage sparked widespread discussion and criticism in the area. Contacted, Kalmakanda upazila Jubo Dal Convener Md Zahirul Islam Zahir said Parvez had actually been relieved of his post about a year ago. However, after the video circulated online, the organisation issued the statement to clarify that he no longer has any affiliation with Jubo Dal. Earlier in the day, BNP’s Netrokona district unit expelled Saifuzzaman Kajal, a member of Kalmakanda upazila BNP, after members of Rapid Action Battalion allegedly arrested him in Dhaka’s Uttara West area on April 14 with cocaine worth around Tk 1 crore. According to party sources, Saifuzzaman Kajal is the maternal uncle of Parvez Bhuiyan.

title: Release of former chief justice ABM Khairul Haque stalled after fresh arrest
body: The release of former chief justice ABM Khairul Haque has been stalled after he was shown arrested today in another murder case linked to the July uprising. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Sarah Farzana Haque showed Khairul arrested in a case filed with Jatrabari Police Station following an application from the investigation officer (IO), Md Ibrahim Khalil, a sub-inspector of the same police station, said Khairul’s lawyer, Motaher Hossain Saju. In his application, Ibrahim said there was preliminary evidence of the Khairul's involvement in a case filed on November 16, 2024. The application said, "It is absolutely necessary to show the accused arrested in this case for the sake of a fair and impartial investigation.” However, the IO did not specify in the application what offence -- murder or abetment to murder -- had allegedly been committed by the 81-year-old former chief justice. Defence lawyer Saju said his client would not be released from jail unless he secured bail. On May 17, a High Court bench directed the government not to show Khairul arrested or harass him unless he is named as an accused in a specific case. Following a petition filed by Khairul’s son, Advocate Md Asik Ul Haque, the HC also issued a rule asking the authorities to explain why the order issued by the Dhaka Chief Metropolitan Magistrate on March 30 allowing the government to show him arrested in two cases should not be declared illegal. In the petition, Asik said Khairul had been shown arrested in cases filed with Jatrabari Police Station on August 26, 2024, and Adabor Police Station on August 22, 2024, in an “illegal, arbitrary and mala fide manner”. Khairul was arrested from his Dhanmondi residence on July 24 last year, nearly a year after the fall of the Awami League government. He was later shown arrested in multiple cases, including several filed over killings during the July uprising and allegations of manipulating the Supreme Court verdict on the caretaker government system, and has remained in jail since then.

title: Rape suspect beaten by locals in Narayanganj, admitted to DMCH
body: A man accused of raping a six-year-old girl in Narayanganj’s Fatullah yesterday was beaten by locals and later admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) of Dhaka Medical College Hospital, according to police. The victim’s mother filed a case under the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act with Fatullah Model Police Station this morning, said Tarek Al Mehedi, additional superintendent of police of the district. Two people -- Hero, 22, and Sohel, 21, -- have been named in the case, he added. According to the police official, the alleged rape took place yesterday afternoon, as claimed by the victim’s family. When locals came to know the incident at night, they caught one of the suspects, Hero, and beat him. Police later rescued Hero in critical condition and took him to Dhaka Medical College Hospital. As of 11:30am today, the accused was undergoing treatment in the ICU under police custody, the official said. Sohel went into hiding after the incident, he added. Meanwhile, the process of sending the child to hospital for medical examination was underway, he said. Narayanganj Deputy Commissioner Raihan Kabir visited the victim and her family at the police station in the morning, the additional superintendent added.

title: Ctg rape suspect sent to jail after confession
body: A man accused of raping a four-year-old girl in Chattogram city’s Bakalia area confessed to the crime before a court yesterday. Mohammad Solaiman, officer-in-charge of Bakalia Police Station, told The Daily Star that the court sent suspect Monir Hossain, 35, to jail. Earlier in the day, the child’s father filed the rape case. Tension flared in the Bakalia area on Thursday night after hundreds of locals clashed with police and tried to snatch Monir from their custody, demanding that the suspect be handed over to them for “instant justice”. Witnesses said police fired tear gas shells and detonated sound grenades to disperse the crowd when they hurled brick chunks at police. At least 30 people, including 15 police personnel and two journalists, were injured. OC Solaiman said the filing of a case was underway over attacks on law enforcers, obstruction of duty, vandalism, and arson. Police have detained four people in this connection. Meanwhile, police yesterday arrested two men in the port city on charges of attempting to rape two minor girls. The incidents occurred in Hajipara under Double Mooring Police Station and Mandatila under Bayezid Bostami Police Station. The arrestees were Md Ehsan, 45, a security guard of Jalal Colony in Hajipara, and Md Hasan, 40, another security guard of Mandatila. Police said locals caught Ehsan when he allegedly tried to rape a 10-year-old child in the Hajipara area. OC Jamal Uddin Khan of Double Mooring Police Station said police later detained Ehsan. In Mandatila, security guard Hasan tried to rape a five-year-old girl, locals alleged. OC Abdul Karim of Bayezid Bostami Police Station said police rushed to the spot after receiving information and arrested the suspect. Police said both the victims were admitted to the One-Stop Crisis Centre at Chattogram Medical College Hospital. Cases were filed with the respective police stations, police added. In separate other incidents, police arrested two people on charges of sexually assaulting two minors in Savar’s Aminbazar and Habiganj Sadar upazila. Sub-Inspector Zakir Hossain, in-charge of Aminbazar Police Outpost, told this newspaper that the accused is a neighbour to the seven-year-old girl. According to the case statement, 69-year-old Razzak took the child to his room on Thursday afternoon and attempted to rape her. When the allegation spread, locals confined Razzak to his house. Police then detained him and took him to Savar Model Police Station. The child’s father filed an attempted rape case, and the police officer confirmed the accused has been shown arrested. In Habiganj Sadar upazila, a man was arrested on charges of attempting to rape a four-year-old girl yesterday. Police held suspect Bijoy Mia from the Durlavpur locality. The incident took place on Thursday evening when the child was playing near the house. The girl was admitted to Habiganj Sadar Hospital. OC Zahidul Haque of Habiganj Police Station said police visited the hospital and recorded a statement. An attempt was made to rape the child. The child’s mother filed a case with Sadar Police Station. Bijoy was produced before a court that sent him to jail yesterday. Faika Rahman, resident medical officer of the hospital, said a medical examination on the girl would be conducted today. [Our correspondents in Chattogram, Savar, and Moulvibazar contributed to this report.]

title: Ramisa murder: ‘We want a safe place for our children’
body: Protests continued for the fourth consecutive day in Dhaka and elsewhere yesterday as the outcry for justice over the brutal rape and murder of eight-year-old Ramisa grew louder. Students, local residents, and members of different social and cultural organisations formed human chains, held rallies, and blocked roads in the capital and other parts of the country, with many demanding capital punishment for the accused. Meanwhile, Ramisa’s father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, yesterday said he believed justice would be served, citing assurances from the prime minister. “The prime minister told me he had come to our Pallabi home as the father of a daughter and as an elder brother. I have 100 percent faith in the love he showed, his tears, and his assurance that I will get justice for my daughter’s murder. I believe we will get a fair and speedy trial,” he told local reporters in front of the family graveyard at his ancestral home in Shialdi village of Munshiganj’s Sirajdikhan upazila. Earlier in the day, he left Dhaka to attend Ramisa’s khulkhani. Ramisa, a Class-II student, was killed and beheaded. Her neighbour Sohel Rana was later arrested and charged with rape and murder. The accused has given a confessional statement before a magistrate. The Dhaka Bar Association announced that it would not provide any legal assistance to the accused in the Ramisa murder case. The decision was made at a virtual meeting of the association’s executive committee yesterday, said its General Secretary Mohammad Kalam Khan. Like the previous days, people from different walks of life gathered in front of Ramisa’s house in Pallabi yesterday morning and held human chains, demanding capital punishment for the accused. “We are now living in fear for our own children. No human being should commit such brutality against a child. We want a speedy trial. We want a safe place for our children,” said a woman who joined one of the human chains. After Juma prayers, several hundred people under different banners blocked the Mirpur-10 intersection. The protest, which began around 2:15pm, continued for two hours. Later, the protesters blocked the Kalshi road for several hours. Protesters said a culture of impunity has allowed heinous crimes such as rape and murder to rise. Paritran Talukder, ADC (Traffic) of Mirpur division, told The Daily Star that traffic movement from Kalshi to Mirpur-11 remained suspended for a few hours due to the protest, while vehicular movement was also disrupted at Mirpur-10. Members of Prothom Alo’s youth platform Bondhushava held a protest rally at the SAARC Fountain in Karwan Bazar, demanding the quickest possible trial and capital punishment for those responsible. The platform placed a three-point demand, including modernisation of the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act to ensure exemplary punishment and speedy disposal of cases involving violence against women and children. The platform also demanded a unified legal definition and punishment for sexual abuse against children, regardless of gender, and called for strict measures against abuse of boys in residential educational institutions, including madrasas. Religious leaders and political parties were urged to speak out strongly against such abuse. Bondhushava also called for nationwide awareness campaigns against violence against women and children through state initiatives involving media outlets, educational institutions, and religious organisations. The Gulshan Society formed a human chain at the Gulshan-2 intersection yesterday morning, demanding exemplary punishment for those responsible for Ramisa’s murder. A human chain was also held in Block-C of Khilgaon under the banner of Pallima Sangshad. Around 200 people, including members of affiliated organisations and local residents, joined the programme. Similar protest programmes were held in Dinajpur’s Nawabganj, Brahmanbaria’s Bancharampur, and Rajbari’s Goalanda. Meanwhile, the city unit of Islami Chhatra Shibir brought out a protest procession from New Market Baitun Noor Mosque.

title: Rab man stabbed to death by ‘drug trader’ in Sylhet
body: A Rab member in plainclothes was killed after being stabbed in the chest, reportedly while trying to stop a suspected drug trader in Sylhet yesterday. The suspect, Asadul Alam Bappy, was later arrested after allegedly taking a two-year-old child hostage while attempting to flee, police said. The victim, Emon Acharya, hailed from Hathazari in Chattogram and served with Rab-9, said Manzurul Alam, additional deputy commissioner (media) of Sylhet Metropolitan Police. The incident took place around noon in the Topkhana area when a team from Kotwali Police Station was chasing several suspected drug traders. Citing police, the Prothom Alo reported that Emon was taking a walk through the area when he stepped forward and caught hold of Asadul after noticing the chase. Asadul then allegedly stabbed him in the chest with a knife. Emon was rushed to Sylhet MAG Osmani Medical College Hospital, where doctors declared him dead around 1:30pm. After the stabbing, the suspect entered a nearby house and held a child hostage at knifepoint in an apparent bid to escape, police said. Police identified Asadul as a resident of the Mogoltula area in Kazirbazar of Sylhet city and described him as a listed drug trader and mugger with multiple cases filed against him in the past. Citing police, the Bangla daily reported that Asadul and his associates were also known locally as muggers and had been taking and selling drugs near Kean Bridge when police chased them. The child’s mother was talking to a neighbour when Asadul entered the house and held the knife to the toddler’s throat, according to the report. A team of eight police members later reached the scene, but Asadul ignored repeated requests to surrender, Kotwali Model Police Station officials said. He allegedly continued threatening to slit the child’s throat. At one stage, a police member quietly struck the hand holding the knife with a stick. Asadul then released the child, allowing police to quickly rescue the toddler and arrest him. Police said several cops were injured during a scuffle while detaining the suspect. Asadul was also injured. All received first aid. Police said Asadul would be produced before a court today. Emon’s body has been kept at the mortuary of Sylhet MAG Osmani Medical College Hospital. After an autopsy, the body will be handed over to his family. Manzurul said a case would be filed over the killing.

title: Unresolved murders reflect deep-rooted culture of impunity
body: Speakers at a rally yesterday said the unresolved murders of Tanvir Muhammad Taqi, Sohagi Jahan Tonu, journalist couple Sagar-Runi, and college student Mosarat Jahan Munia point to a deeply rooted culture of impunity that has emboldened criminals and eroded public trust in the rule of law. The rally titled ‘Taqi Samabesh’ was held in front of the Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban in the afternoon, organised by Santrash Nirmul Taqi Mancha demanding justice for the teenager from Narayanganj 13 years after his murder. Addressing the rally, Prof Anu Muhammad said the failure to ensure justice for Taqi, Tonu, Sagar-Runi, and Munia proves that impunity is entrenched in every tier of the state, regardless of who is in power. He alleged that the trial of the Taqi murder case was halted because the then prime minister explicitly took a stance in favour of the killers in parliament. He also expressed disappointment as the current government has not shown significant attention to expedite the trial process. Rafiur Rabbi, Taqi’s father and also convener of Santrash Nirmul Taqi Mancha, criticised the administration, stating that no progress has been made in the murder cases even three months after the BNP-led government assumed power. He also made a startling claim that a senior Rapid Action Battalion (Rab) official had told him 13 years ago that the Sagar-Runi murder mystery would never be unravelled. “We identified the culprits within 48 hours of the incident, but mark my words, the Sagar-Runi murder mystery will never be solved,” Rabbi quoted the Rab official as saying. He further alleged that the Osman family was allowed to flee the country in exchange for Tk 3.5 crore with the help of the administration and various forces. Ajmeri Osman, an accused in the Taqi murder case, was not arrested despite remaining in the country for months after the August 5 political changeover, he added. Bureaucrats from the Sheikh Hasina-led regime are still running the administration, which is why there has been no real change in the judicial process, Rabbi observed. Jamshed Anwar Tapan, convener of Ganatantrik Sangskritik Oikya, expressed concern over the rising trend of “instant justice” or mob killings by capitalising on the public hopelessness that stems from the lack of justice. Professor Samina Luthfa of Dhaka University said the society has failed to establish the rule of law and ensure a safe environment for its children. At the rally, protest art was created on an open canvas. Different cultural troupes and artistes, including Udichi Shilpi Gosthi, Samageet Sangskritik Prangan, BotTala, Prachyanat, music band Kora, Wardah Ashraf, and Armeen Musa, performed at the event, moderated by Samageet president Rebeka Nila.

title: Teacher suspended after sexual abuse allegations surface
body: A teacher at a madrasa in Pirojpur has been suspended after allegations emerged that he sexually abused male students, with the managing committee taking action following an internal investigation. “After finding proof, the madrasa managing committee has suspended Kawser Hosen, 46, a muhaddis at Togra Darul Islam Kamil Madrasa,” said Abdullahil Mahmud, acting principal of the institution, yesterday. “We will write to Kustia Islamic University authority, and they will take the next decision.” Recently, a video was leaked showing the accused teacher allegedly sexually abusing a student inside a room on the madrasa campus. Madrasa sources said the incident happened at the end of last year when the victim reportedly went to Kawser for private lessons, adding that during the incident, someone outside the room recorded the act. The matter first came to the notice of the madrasa authorities in December last year. A three-member probe committee was formed in February this year to investigate the allegations. Following the investigation, the committee submitted its report to the managing committee last month, after which Kawser was suspended in May. Md Sayful Alam, an assistant teacher at the madrasa and a member of the probe committee, said the inquiry had uncovered evidence of wrongdoing. He further said the accused had committed similar crime with more than one male child. “We have confirmed it with two children,” he said. Kawser has remained absent from the madrasa since the middle of December last year after the matter began circulating within the institution. Asked about the issue, acting principal Abdullahil Mahmud said the teacher had been kept away from duties while the investigation was ongoing. The accused Kawser could not be reached for comment as his mobile phone remained switched off.

title: 25 trees felled inside Satchari park
body: At least 25 trees, including several century-old teak trees, have been felled inside the protected Satchari National Park in Chunarughat upazila of Habiganj over the past few days, alleged locals. The illegal logging reportedly took place in the park’s Dumurtala area, where stumps, roots and piles of sawdust now stretch across nearly a kilometre of forest land. Fresh cut marks on several large teak stumps suggest the trees were removed recently, locals said. Residents alleged that the felling has continued for a long time, mostly under the cover of night. “If you walk through the forest, you will find around 25 cut trees, all felled within just two or three days,” said a local resident requesting anonymity, adding that the syndicate responsible had long enjoyed protection from influential circles. Another resident, Mifta Mia, said locals often hear chainsaws deep inside the forest at night but remain silent out of fear. Environmentalists warned that the destruction could have lasting ecological consequences for the nationally protected forest, home to endangered hoolock gibbons and numerous bird species. “To cut down a large tree is not merely to lose one tree; it destroys habitats, reduces soil moisture, disrupts biodiversity and accelerates soil erosion,” said Tofazzal Sohel, vice-president of Bangladesh Poribesh Andolon’s Habiganj unit. Satchari Range Officer Mehedi Hasan said two teak trees had been stolen and said a case had been filed with the local police station. He, however, declined to comment on allegations of insider involvement.

title: 2 men arrested over attempted rape of children in Chattogram
body: Two men were arrested in separate incidents in Chattogram city today over allegations of attempting to rape two children, police said. The incidents occurred in Hajipara and Mandatila areas. The arrestees were identified as Md Ehsan, 45, a security guard and resident of Jalal Colony in Hajipara, and Md Hasan, 40, also a security guard from Mandatila. According to police, in the Hajipara incident, two children were playing in the area around noon when Ehsan allegedly called a 10-year-old into a walled space and attempted to sexually assault the victim. Officer-in-Charge of Double Mooring Police Station Jamal Uddin Khan said locals caught the suspect and called the national emergency service 999. Police later arrived at the scene and took Ehsan into custody. Police said some residents of the colony protested when officers attempted to take Ehsan away. Officers later persuaded them and brought the suspect to the police station. In a separate incident in Mandatila, Hasan allegedly attempted to rape a five-year-old. Officer-in-Charge of Bayezid Bostami Police Station Abdul Karim said police rushed to the scene after receiving information and detained the suspect. Police said both children were admitted to the One-Stop Crisis Centre (OCC) at Chattogram Medical College Hospital. Cases were filed with the respective police stations in connection with both incidents, police added. The incidents came a day after another alleged attempted child rape incident in Chattogram’s Bakalia area sparked tension between residents and police. On Thursday, locals clashed with police and blocked roads, demanding that a suspect accused of attempting to rape a child be handed over to them. Police later rescued the accused and sent him to jail.

title: 2 journalists injured in Savar attack while reporting on drug trade
body: Two journalists were allegedly attacked by a drug dealer and his associates in Savar today. The journalists are Tayefur Rahman Tuhin, senior reporter at private television channel Desh TV, and Saddam Hossain, Savar correspondent for SA TV, said Savar Model Police Station Officer-in-Charge Arman Ali. Members of a Desh TV team were also attacked. The incident happened at around 3:30pm in Pashchim Rajashan area. The injured journalists were rescued and sent to hospital for treatment, the OC said. Speaking to reporters at Savar Upazila Health Complex, Tuhin said, “We went to the area in the morning on an office assignment to report on drug dealers and the spread of narcotics in Savar. SA TV’s local correspondent Saddam Hossain was also with us. After collecting information and statements from local residents, we were returning around noon. “At one point, we were near the alley known for Shamim’s drug business and were getting into our vehicle after recording footage from CCTV cameras installed there. A man then approached us, saying he wanted to talk. As soon as I got out of the vehicle, around 40 to 50 people led by Shamim attacked us with locally made weapons.” He further alleged, “They snatched all our belongings and later took us to Shamim’s garage, where they continued torturing us.” “When we requested to be taken to hospital, Shamim said police were coming and that we would only be allowed to leave after signing a bond. Later, police arrived and rescued us before taking us to the hospital,” he added. Saddam told The Daily Star, “At one stage, Shamim attempted to shoot me with a pistol, while another person stabbed me three times. They were angry because I had recently reported on Shamim. They attacked me with the intention of killing me.” The other injured victims were identified as Desh TV cameraperson Qayyum and driver Joynal. Dr Sonia Rahman, medical officer of the Emergency Department at Savar Upazila Health Complex, said, “We received two patients. While the condition of one of them (Tuhin) is stable, the other (Saddam) has been referred to the National Institute of Ophthalmology due to serious eye injuries.” On the night of May 10, members of Rapid Action Battalion (Rab) conducted a raid in the area in an attempt to arrest Shamim. Rab-4 Nabinagar Camp's Company Commander Md Shahinur Kabir told The Daily Star, “The raid was conducted primarily to arrest Shamim from his garage, but he escaped. Three of his associates were arrested.” “We have information regarding multiple cases against Shamim, including kidnapping and weapons-related charges,” he added.

title: 3 sent to jail over alleged attempt to sell woman to Faridpur brothel
body: A Faridpur court today sent three people, including a woman, to jail for allegedly attempting to sell a 19-year-old woman to the Rathkhola brothel in Faridpur town. The accused are Monir Sheikh, 30, Alam Fakir, 20, and Munni, 20. Md Mahmudul Hasan, officer-in-charge of Faridpur Kotwali Police Station, said the victim, a resident of Shariakandi upazila in Bogura, worked at a garment factory in Dhaka district’s Dhamrai area along with her mother. The accused lived in the same area and became acquainted with the victim. According to police, the accused lured the woman with promises of arranging marriage and a better job before taking her to Faridpur from Dhaka on May 14. They allegedly kept her in a rented house in Shibrampur area. On Thursday morning, they took her to the Rathkhola brothel in Faridpur town. After arriving there, the victim realised that the accused were trying to sell her to the brothel, the police official said. When she refused to enter, the accused allegedly tried to force her inside. At one stage, the woman screamed for help and ran to a nearby shop in front of the brothel, seeking shelter. Locals then detained the three accused and informed police. A team from Faridpur Kotwali Police Station later rescued the victim and took the accused into custody, the OC said. Police said the three accused were sent to jail by a court today after the victim filed a human trafficking case against them. The victim has been handed over to her family, he said. Two other individuals were also named in the case and remain absconding, the OC said.

title: Man arrested over attempted rape of 4-year-old in Habiganj
body: Police have arrested a man over the attempted rape of a four-year-old girl in Habiganj Sadar upazila. The arrestee was identified as Bijoy Mia, 20, of Durlavpur area in the upazila. He was arrested from Durlavpur this afternoon following the filing of a case by the victim’s mother in the morning, said Habiganj Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Zahidul Haque. According to the case statement, the incident took place yesterday evening when the child was playing near her house. Bijoy allegedly attempted to rape the child at that time. Family members grew suspicious upon seeing the child's condition. Later in the day, as her health deteriorated, she was admitted to Habiganj Sadar Hospital. Allegations have surfaced that an influential quarter attempted to mediate and suppress the matter, with the victim's family facing pressure from multiple sides. The OC said police have visited the hospital immediately upon receiving the report and recorded a statement. “An attempt was made to rape the child. The accused was produced before the court and sent to jail,” he said. Resident Medical Officer (RMO) of Habiganj Sadar Hospital Dr Faika Rahman confirmed the child remains admitted and said a medical examination was scheduled for tomorrow.

title: Madrasa suspends teacher after sexual abuse allegations surface
body: A teacher at a madrasa in Pirojpur has been suspended after allegations emerged that he sexually abused male students, with the managing committee taking action following an internal investigation. “After finding proof, the madrasa managing committee has suspended Kawser Hosen, 46, a muhaddis at Togra Darul Islam Kamil Madrasa,” said Abdullahil Mahmud, acting principal of the institution. “We will write to Kustia Islamic University authority and they will take the next decision,” he added. Recently, a video was leaked showing the accused teacher allegedly sexually abusing a student inside a room on the madrasa campus. Madrasa sources said the incident happened at the end of last year when the victim reportedly went to Kawser for private lessons, adding that during the incident, someone outside the room recorded the act. The matter first came to the notice of the madrasa authorities in December last year. A three-member probe committee was formed in February this year to investigate the allegations. Following the investigation, the committee submitted its report to the managing committee last month, after which Kawser was suspended in May. Md Sayful Alam, an assistant teacher at the madrasa and a member of the probe committee, said the inquiry had uncovered evidence of wrongdoing. He further said the accused had committed similar crime with more than one male child. “We have confirmed it with two children,” he said. Kawser has remained absent from the madrasa since the middle of December last year after the matter began circulating within the institution. Asked about the issue, acting principal Abdullahil Mahmud said the teacher had been kept away from duties while the investigation was ongoing. The accused Kawser could not be reached for comment as his mobile phone remained switched off.

title: Rab personnel killed while confronting suspected mugger in Sylhet
body: A Rapid Action Battalion (Rab) member in plainclothes was killed after being stabbed in the chest while confronting a mugger in Sylhet city today. The deceased was identified as Emon Acharya, a member of Rab-9, said Manzurul Alam, additional deputy commissioner (media) of Sylhet Metropolitan Police (SMP). Manzurul said the incident happened around noon in the Topkhana area, when a team from Kotwali Police Station was chasing several suspected muggers. Seeing this, Emon stepped forward and grabbed one of them. The man then stabbed him in the chest with a knife. Emon was rushed to Sylhet MAG Osmani Medical College Hospital, where he died around 1:30pm. The ADC said after stabbing the Rab personnel, the attacker fled and entered a nearby house, taking a child hostage. However, police subsequently arrested him.

title: Case filed over attempted rape of four-year-old in Chattogram
body: The father of a four-year-old girl filed a rape case this morning, accusing a man of attempting to rape his daughter in Chattogram’s Bakalia area yesterday. “The child’s father filed the case as the complainant. The accused, Monir, will be produced before court today,” Bakalia Police Station OC Mohammad Solaiman told The Daily Star. “Police are also filing a separate case over the attack on law enforcers, obstruction of duty, vandalism and arson. So far, we have detained four people,” he added. Local residents besieged police yesterday afternoon, demanding that the suspect be handed over to them for “instant justice” after news of the attempted rape spread. The mob asked police to leave the area, saying they would carry out the punishment themselves. At one stage, clashes broke out in phases as locals attempted to snatch the accused while police tried to prevent them. At least 30 people, including two journalists and 15 police personnel, were injured in the repeated clashes. The injured were taken to Chittagong Medical College Hospital and the police lines hospital for treatment. Around 10pm, tension escalated after police strategically moved the accused out of the area, triggering fresh clashes between locals and law enforcers. During the violence, police came under attack and a police vehicle was set on fire.

title: ‘We're living in fear for our children’: Dhaka protests Ramisa’s killing
body: Residents and activists of Pallabi and other parts of Dhaka staged protests today, demanding justice for eight-year-old Ramisa Akhter . Since morning, people from different walks of life gathered in front of Ramisa’s house in Pallabi, forming human chains and holding demonstrations under the banners of social and volunteer organisations. Besides, several hundred people blocked the Mirpur-10 intersection after Jumma prayers, demanding justice for Ramisa. “We are now living in fear for our own children. No human being should commit such brutality against a child. We want a speedy trial in the incident. We want a safe place for our children,” said a woman who joined one of the human chains in front of Ramisa’s house. They carried placards reading “We want justice for Ramisa” and “Hang the child rapist and killer”. A sombre atmosphere prevailed throughout the area as locals expressed outrage over the brutal killing, saying exemplary punishment was necessary to ensure children’s safety. Meanwhile, Ramisa’s parents and relatives left Dhaka for Munshiganj’s Sirajdikhan to attend a doa mahfil. Ramisa, a class two student, was killed and beheaded allegedly by her neighbour Sohel Rana on May 19. The accused later gave a confessional statement before a magistrate. Meanwhile, traffic movement was disrupted in the Mirpur-10 roundabout area due to the ongoing protest. Police urged patience as they diverted traffic using alternative routes to ease vehicular movement. A human chain was held in Khilgaon demanding justice for Ramisa. “When I step out to go to school, or return home, I feel scared. We girls want to move freely and safely everywhere,” said 15-year-old Nuzhat Tabassum at the human chain. The event was organised by Pallima Sangshad in Block-C of Khilgaon, Dhaka this afternoon. Pallima Sangsad President Anisur Rahman Liton said, “The state must take responsibility for the rape and murder of the child in Pallabi. The trial must be completed in the quickest possible time.” He called on social and cultural organisations in different neighbourhoods of the capital to stand against rape. The human chain began at 11:00am and ended at 12:10pm. Around 200 people, including members of affiliated organisations along with local residents, joined the programme. Meanwhile, a protest rally under the banner of “Dhorshon Birodhi Nagorik Network” was held at the Central Shaheed Minar in Dhaka this afternoon, demanding swift justice for Ramisa. At the rally, protesters called for the speedy trial of all rape cases across the country, including the recent rape and murder of Ramisa. They also demanded stricter laws and tougher judicial measures against rape in Bangladesh. The rally was addressed, among others, by Monira Sharmin, president of the platform; Rehana Akter Ruma, a neighbour of the child in Pallabi, Tarique Rahman Adel, joint convener of the Dhaka North unit of the National Citizen Party (NCP), Supreme Court lawyer Jasim Nayeb, and Jahangirnagar University student Nadia Rahman Onnesha. Besides, members of Prothom Alo’s youth platform, 'Bondhushava', in a protest rally demanded the quickest possible trial and capital punishment for those responsible for the rape and murder of Ramisa. The rally was held at the base of the Saarc Fountain in Karwan Bazar. During the programme, Zafar Sadiq, president of Bondhushava National Committee, announced a three-point demand. The demands included update of the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act to ensure exemplary punishment and speedy disposal of cases involving violence against women and children. The platform also demanded a unified legal definition and punishment for sexual abuse of children regardless of gender, and called for strict measures against abuse of boys in residential educational institutions, including madrasas. Protests were also held in Gulshan-2 and Malibagh areas of Dhaka by different socio-cultural groups protesting the rape and murder of Ramisa.

title: 23 AL leaders, activists detained in Dhaka's Dhanmondi
body: Police detained 23 leaders and activists of Awami League, whose activities remain banned, and its associate organisations from different parts of the Dhanmondi area in Dhaka this afternoon. Teams from Dhanmondi Police Station detained them from Taqwa Mosque, Sobhanbagh Mosque and the Dhanmondi 32 area while they were preparing for a procession, Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police (Dhanmondi Zone) Zishanul Haque told The Daily Star. He said those detained included leaders and activists from different districts and upazilas across the country. However, their identities and details of possible legal action were not immediately disclosed.

title: Who will save our children from our own ‘Epsteins’?
body: Our thinly woven social fabric has been torn apart yet again. A murder has shaken our belief in the social system. It snatched much more than a life. It stole our comfort of trust in one another. Photos of the Pallabi rape-murder victim have been circulating for three days -- photos stored in the parents’ phones. They will remember with anguish, as excruciating remnants of their daughter. As photos of Ramisa circulated online following news of her death, some people posted sexualised comments under them. Mind you… photos of an eight-year-old. In one photo, where she was wearing a saree, men posted sexual innuendos; one even suggested that “getting dolled up” was not appropriate. All this appeared under posts about the barbaric murder of a little girl. We raged after the Epstein files were disclosed. As it turns out, we have our own Epsteins. And this entire country appears to have become their safe haven. Over a year ago, after a six-year-old in Magura was devoured by another monster, a number of Facebook groups were found sharing photos of underage girls. Hubs of pedophiles collecting, sexualising, uttering grotesque desires. One group had over 60,000 members. Dhaka Stream reported that most posted photos are of children aged 9 to 14, in school uniforms. Depravity of this magnitude was out in the open. What were our cybercrime units and law enforcement doing? I refuse to believe our cybercrime specialists lack the capacity to act. Our intelligence can track WhatsApp threads to arrest militants; it can arrest people for supposed derogatory remarks towards government officials. Only when it comes to these blatant crimes does our law enforcement appear lost. In the first four months of 2026, 115 children have been killed -- 11 after being raped, according to Ain o Salish Kendra (ASK). Only 36 cases were filed. ASK also recorded 109 children raped, 12 sexually harassed by teachers, with only three cases filed. Behind every number is a child who didn’t have the capacity to understand what exactly happened to them and why. Behind every number is a harrowing tale. Ramisa’s father said he does not believe he will see justice. “Bangladesh will forget after 15 days,” he said. The Rape Law Reform Coalition estimates over 10 lakh pending cases, 10,000 unresolved for over half a decade. In 2025 alone, police logged 7,068 rape cases nationwide involving 1,897 child victims. Ramisa’s father has seen enough to know his daughter’s death may become just another entry. When a doctor blew the lid on the rape and pregnancy of an 11-year-old in Netrokona, she was bombarded with threats, to protect the sanctity of the madrasa. For it was a teacher of the madrasa who was accused. Strangely, it is not the dignity or sanity or life of the victim but institutions that are prioritised. Only goes to show how little regard we have for children. Our tendency, whether deliberate or not, to protect paedophiles discourages children from speaking up. Our obsession with reputation makes even our own homes unsafe. Epsteins are not born. They are cultivated -- enabled by a system of silence, ignorance, and constant cover-ups. We cannot let this slide anymore. Our country cannot be a safe haven for “Epsteins.”

title: Two arrested over fraud racket targeting govt officials
body: Police have arrested two individuals in connection with a fraud syndicate that allegedly collected large sums of money from government officials and employees by promising desirable postings and promotions using the names of different ministries, including the home ministry. The arrests were made following a complaint and subsequent investigation carried out by the Detective Branch (DB), said DMP Additional Commissioner and DB chief Md Shafiqul Islam during a briefing at the DMP media centre this afternoon. The arrestees are M Aminur Rahman Shanto, 44, and Nilufa Sultana, 56. Nilufa serves as a personal officer to an official of Discipline Branch-2 of the Ministry of Home Affairs. The group is also accused of targeting ordinary citizens and political figures, the police official added. According to police, to establish credibility, members of the racket at times introduced themselves as senior officials of the home ministry, relatives of political leaders, or senior administrative officials. Police said they took action after a written complaint was filed on Wednesday by one Kamrul Hasan, assistant private secretary to the home minister, with the DMP commissioner, alleging that an unidentified person was contacting officials via a messaging app and claiming to arrange transfers and promotions in exchange for money. Following the complaint, the DB Cyber and Special Crime (North) division launched an investigation. Acting on intelligence, police arrested Shanto from a house in West Rampura under Hatirjheel Police Station around 9:35pm on May 20, and seized a mobile phone. During interrogation, Shanto admitted to the crime, according to DB officials. His messages later led police to Nilufa Sultana, who was also arrested. Md Shafiqul Islam said police are conducting digital forensics. Preliminary findings show that there were exchanges related to transfers, postings, collection of CVs, and monetary demands for certain positions. He said investigators had recovered conversations on a messaging platform involving multiple individuals. “They discussed possible postings and how much money would be required for different positions.” He added that no senior government official’s involvement has so far been found, though investigations are ongoing. Police have filed a case with Ramna Police Station over the incident.

title: Elderly man arrested over attempted rape of 7-year-old girl in Savar
body: An elderly man has been arrested in a case filed over the attempted rape of a 7-year-old girl in Dhaka’s Savar. The accused, Abdur Razzak, 69, is of Patuakhali’s Bauphal, said police. He currently lives in the Binodbari area in Aminbazar union of Savar. Citing the case statement, Aminbazar police outpost in-charge Sub-Inspector (SI) Zakir Hossain told The Daily Star that the victim's family and the accused's family live in adjacent rooms in the same house. Yesterday afternoon, Razzak took the child to his room and attempted to rape her. Later, when the matter came to light, people confined Razzak in his house in the evening, it added. Upon receiving the news, police reached the scene, detained the accused and took him to Savar Model Police Station. Later that night the victim's father filed an attempted rape case with the police station. The police officer said the accused has been shown arrested in the case.

title: DNA sample collected from accused in Netrokona child rape case
body: The DNA sample of a madrasa teacher accused of the rape of an 11-year-old student , which led to her pregnancy in Netrokona's Madan upazila has been collected as part of the investigation, officials said. The accused, Aman Ullah Mahmudi Sagar, was taken to the CID office in Dhaka on May 16, where his DNA sample was collected the following day. Confirming the development, Netrokona Court Inspector Mohammad Riyadh Mahmud told The Daily Star that the court had ordered the DNA test on May 10 following an application by the investigating officer. The accused is currently in jail custody, while the court has fixed June 28 as the next date for the case. Investigating officer Sub-Inspector Md Akhtaruzzaman said, “As per the court’s directive, the accused was taken to the CID office in Dhaka and his DNA sample was collected. We will take further legal action once the DNA test report is received,” he said. The victim's mother filed the case on April 23 with Madan Police Station under the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act, 2000. According to the complaint, the teacher raped the minor on multiple occasions, resulting in her pregnancy. On May 7, the court placed the accused on a three-day remand. After the remand period, he was produced before the court on May 10, when the investigating officer sought a DNA test to support the probe and establish evidence. Separately, the victim was sent to a safe shelter under the Department of Social Services in Sylhet on May 12 following a court order, after her mother sought protection for her safety and future. She is currently receiving treatment and remains under protective custody.

title: Rab arrests Jashore top terror 'Bhagne Emon'
body: Rapid Action Battalion (Rab) has arrested Emon, also known as “Bhagne Emon”, one of the listed top terrorists in Jashore and a fugitive accused in 17 cases. Acting on a tip-off, a team of Rab-6 conducted a drive in the Nutun Khoyertola area of Palbari in Jashore town early today and arrested him, confirmed Rab-6 Jashore Company Commander Major Fazle Rabbi Prince. The cases filed against him include murder, extortion, terrorism, illegal arms possession, bomb attacks, and drug smuggling, according to Rab. He was later handed over to Jashore Kotwali Police Station this morning. Law enforcement sources said Emon had been absconding for a long time. Recently, intelligence reports suggested that he was staying in the Palbari area. Major Fazle Rabbi said, “Bhagne Emon is a listed top terrorist in Jashore. He is accused in two sensational murder cases. Besides, he faces cases related to arms, bomb attacks, extortion, terrorism, and drug trafficking.” He added that Emon had allegedly been operating his criminal network while in hiding.

title: Mob kills man in Jhalakathi
body: A man was killed in a mob attack in Jhalakathi’s Kathalia upazila early yesterday. The deceased was identified as Razzak Hawlader, 50, of Bashbunia village under Amua union, said Kathalia Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Md Naser Rayhan. According to locals, Razzak allegedly removed parts from a tractor in Uttar Bashbunia village around 1:30am with the intention of stealing them. He later attempted to steal a nearby electric transformer when locals noticed the incident and caught him red-handed. At one stage, agitated locals beat him, leaving him critically injured and unconscious. He was taken to Kathalia Upazila Health Complex, where the on-duty doctor declared him dead. The OC said no member of the deceased’s family had yet come to the police station to lodge a complaint. “If the relatives do not file a case, police will file a case over the killing,” he said. The OC also said Razzak was accused in at least eight criminal cases, including theft, robbery, and murder.

title: Sexual abuse of child: Clashes erupt as crowd tries to snatch suspect
body: Tension flared in Chattogram city’s Bakalia area last night after hundreds of locals clashed with police and tried to snatch from their custody a man accused of sexually assaulting a four-year-old girl, demanding "instant justice". The incident took place on Abu Zafar Road in the Nur Hossain Chairman Ghata area of South Bakalia. Witnesses said police fired tear gas shells and detonated sound grenades to disperse the crowd when they hurled brick chunks at police around 6:00pm. Later, police used pellet rounds, injuring several, including two local journalists. They were later taken to the Chittagong Medical College Hospital for treatment. Around 10:00pm, police left the scene with the suspect after reinforcements arrived, said Aminur Rashid, assistant commissioner (public relations) of Chattogram Metropolitan Police. “The suspect has been taken into custody, but I cannot disclose his location for security reasons,” he told The Daily Star. Aminur acknowledged that there was a clash between locals and police. The detainee, Monir Hossain, 35, works at a shop that rents out supplies for events, locally known as a “decorator shop”. Videos circulating on social media last night appeared to show Monir, while in police custody, admitting to sexually assaulting the child when questioned by a local journalist. However, The Daily Star could not independently verify the authenticity of the clip. Quoting the child’s family, Bakalia Police Station Officer-in-Charge Mohammad Solaiman said Monir sexually abused the four-year-old girl after taking her inside the shop near her house.
