After the child complained to her parents, the family apprehended Monir and confined him to their home. After the news spread in the area, hundreds gathered in front of the house. On information, a team from Bakalia Police Station went to the spot, detained the suspect and sent the child to a hospital for medical attention. Journalist Iftekhar Tishan, present at the scene, said as the crowd became furious and tried to snatch the accused, police fired shots, while protesters hurled bricks and stones, leading to chases and counter-chases between police and the mob around 6:00pm, which continued for some time. A photojournalist reported from the spot that a police truck was set on fire after the suspect was removed from the scene. When contacted, the CMP assistant commissioner was unable to confirm the matter, saying he had yet to receive reports of the fire.

title: Public outrage mounts over Ramisa murder
body: Public outrage over the rape and murder of eight-year-old Ramisa Akter in Pallabi continued to mount in the capital and across the country yesterday, with protesters demanding the highest punishment for those responsible and a speedy trial through a special tribunal for the third consecutive day. Students, guardians, teachers, and political activists joined demonstrations in different areas, urging law enforcement agencies to play a more proactive role in ensuring justice. Carrying placards reading “We want justice” and “Justice for Ramisa”, protesters gathered near the victim’s residence and the Pallabi Police Station. Students and locals also blocked Kalshi Road for some time, disrupting traffic in surrounding areas. Amid growing public anger, the government said a swift trial would be ensured through a proper investigation and directed the authorities concerned to take necessary steps accordingly. Eight-year-old Ramisa was found beheaded at her neighbour’s home in Pallabi on May 16. The neighbour, Sohel Rana, 31, has been accused of raping and killing the child. On Wednesday, he gave a confessional statement before a magistrate and was later sent to jail. Sohel’s wife, Swapna Akter, 26, was also sent to jail after police appealed to another court to keep her in custody as an alleged accomplice. Police suspect Swapna helped Sohel flee after the incident. The case was filed by Ramisa’s father, Abdul Hannan Molla, who named Sohel, Swapna, and an unidentified person as accused. Speaking to reporters yesterday, Law Minister Asaduzzaman said he had asked the Dhaka Metropolitan Police commissioner to complete the investigation report within a week and that the government would take all possible steps to ensure a speedy trial. “The government wants to set an example through the trial of Ramisa’s murder case, as it did in the Asiya murder case,” he said, adding that the case would be tried under the Women and Children Repression Prevention Tribunal. At a separate briefing at the Secretariat, Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed said the case would be properly investigated and the chargesheet submitted quickly so that an exemplary trial could be completed at the earliest. “A proper investigation will be conducted and the chargesheet will be submitted soon. The responsibility for judgement lies with the court.” Responding to questions about impunity, he said the claim that a culture of impunity exists in all such cases was not correct. “In some cases, justice is delayed, which makes people think they might not get it at all…. In this case, I can guarantee this much: an exemplary trial will be completed in the shortest possible time.” Speaking to The Daily Star yesterday, Mollah said, “I’m the father of a poor, destitute child…. I don’t know if my cries will reach the government.” “You are journalists. Have you been able to ensure justice for the Sagar-Runi murders?” he said, referring to the unresolved killings of journalist couple Sagar Sarowar and Meherun Runi. He also praised the efforts of law enforcers involved in the case. “I salute them -- every officer, whether from DB, CID, PBI, or the local police. I am grateful for the cooperation, sympathy, and sincerity they have shown. “But given the complexity of the law in our country, I do not know when I will see justice for my daughter or what the final outcome of the trial will be.” He also voiced concern over the influence of money in the legal process. “You know that, our government knows that, and the expensive lawyers in our country know that. They can get anyone released on bail in exchange for money. “Even a foolish, ignorant person like me understands that. Those of you who are educated surely understand it much better.” PROTESTS CONTINUED Students from different schools and colleges, parents, and local residents gathered near Ramisa’s house and Pallabi Police Station around 1:30pm. Shilpi Begum, 38, a resident of Pallabi, said, “We want the maximum punishment for the accused as quickly as possible so that no one else dares to commit such a heinous act.” Riya Moni, 22, who joined the protest with her four-year-old daughter, said, “We no longer feel safe with our children, either inside or outside the home. We have lost faith in the people around us.” BNP reserved-seat lawmaker Sanjida Islam Tulee yesterday visited Ramisa’s family and promised to help ensure quick justice. The Dhaka north units of Jamaat-e-Islami’s women wing and the National Citizen Party also staged separate protests, demanding punishment for those involved. Bangladesh Student Union also held a protest in Pallabi. Around 5:00pm, dozens of students and locals staged a sit-in on Kalshi Road, halting traffic in nearby areas. Another group demonstrated inside the Pallabi Police Station compound. Students of different institutions, including Eden College, Nalonda High School of Chhayanaut, and student platform Fulkori Asor, also held demonstrations in the capital. In separate video messages, the Bangladesh Cricket Board and several male and female cricketers expressed condolences over the incident and demanded a speedy trial. Protests were also held at different universities and in several districts.

title: Rape in madrasa: Suspect held after 10-yr-old dies by suicide
body: A Dhaka court yesterday placed a madrasa student on a five-day remand in a case filed over the alleged rape and provocation to the suicide of a 10-year-old boy in the capital’s Banasree area. The accused, Shihab Hossain, 20, a student of Alokito Quran International Hifz Madrasa in Banasree, was arrested on Wednesday from his home in Pabna’s Bera upazila in connection with the death of Abdullah, a student at the same madrasa. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Hasibuzzaman passed the order after police produced him before the court and sought a seven-day remand. During the hearing, Metropolitan Public Prosecutor Omar Faruq Faruqi and investigation officer Saiful Islam, a sub-inspector of Rampura Police Station, argued in favour of the remand. Faruqi told the court that rape incidents tarnish the dignity of society and the education system, and those responsible must be brought to justice. “In the name of service, the hujurs [teachers] make little children massage their hands and feet. Eventually, they become attracted to the children. At one stage, such incidents [rape] occur,” he said. No lawyer appeared on behalf of the accused during the hearing. According to case documents, a team from Rampura Police Station went to the madrasa on Tuesday night after receiving reports that a child had died by suicide. The body was later sent to the Dhaka Medical College Hospital morgue for an autopsy. During the inquest, officers found signs of sexual assault. This led to extensive questioning of madrasa authorities, who then revealed earlier allegations that Shihab had sexually abused four other students at the institution, according to a press release issued by Motijheel Division Police. On Wednesday, Abdullah’s mother, Tuku Ara Khatun, filed a case with Rampura Police Station against Shihab and an unnamed individual under the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act. According to police, Shihab fled the madrasa before Abdullah took his own life. A team from Rampura Police Station later tracked him down to his village home in Pabna and arrested him.

title: State enterprises bleed Tk 88,200cr every year: WB study
body: Bangladesh’s state-owned enterprises (SOEs) drained about Tk 88,200 crore from the national exchequer in a single year, emerging as one of the country’s biggest fiscal risks, according to a World Bank study. The study recommended closing down the Trading Corporation of Bangladesh (TCB), which is a budget guzzler and its effectiveness in reaching out to the poorest of the poor is debatable. The TCB was created in 1972 to provide essential food items owing to the war-ravaged economy, inadequacy of domestic production and weakness of private sector-based supply chains. “After 53 years of independence and a flourishing private sector, the need for a TCB is not obvious -- the TCB cannot be a substitute for a strong and vibrant social protection programme,” said the study, which was prepared with the support of the Policy Research Institute. Social protection to the poor should be provided through a large number of social protection programmes, including food distribution, income transfers and employment guarantee schemes. Several SOEs like the Bangladesh Petroleum Corporation (BPC), the Chittagong Port Authority (CPA), the Bangladesh Telecom Regulatory Commission (BTRC) and the Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB) earn modest profits, but most other enterprises either make very small profits or incur losses. The energy sector is the biggest source of financial losses, with the Bangladesh Power Development Board (PDB), Petrobangla and the Bangladesh Rural Electrification Board (BREB) accounting for more than 90 percent of the losses. Most of the manufacturing enterprises also make losses, even though they operate in a competitive market structure where a flourishing private sector prevails. As of fiscal 2023-24, the SOEs showed a substantial negative rate of return on assets of -5.2 percent, found the study, which was unveiled yesterday at a workshop titled “Financial Performance and Fiscal Risk of SoEs in Bangladesh”. In comparison, India obtained a ROA of 9.7 percent in 2024 while Vietnam secured an ROA of 11.9 percent in 2020. Owing to this poor financial performance, the treasury had to provide a subsidy in an amount of Tk 44,100 crore (0.9 percent of GDP) in fiscal 2023-24 just to keep the SOEs afloat. Total net fiscal transfers, including capital transfers, amounted to Tk 120,000 crore (1.7 percent of GDP). Although the treasury provides investment funds to SOEs as loans, owing to a weak financial situation, most SOEs do not service the debts, making them effectively transfers to SOEs. “The opportunity cost of this poor financial performance of SOEs is large.” To put things into perspective, Bangladesh spends 1.6 percent of GDP on healthcare and social protection and 1.8 percent of GDP on education. The deteriorating financial condition of public enterprises has become “unsustainable” at a time when Bangladesh is already facing falling revenue collection, slower economic growth and mounting pressure on public finances, the report said. Subsequently, the study called for an overhaul of the SOE sector. “The situation calls for a systematic approach to reforms.” The diagnosis of the report suggests that the SOEs as a group suffer from severe operational and efficiency constraints imposed by the underlying corporate governance environment. Price controls further add to the poor financial performance. The report also highlighted deep corporate governance weaknesses within Bangladesh’s SOE structure. It identified fragmented laws, bureaucratic control, weak oversight and lack of financial transparency as key reasons behind poor performance. The first step is to classify SOEs by market structure and functions to determine what types of reform are needed. SOEs that operate in a competitive market structure should be restructured with proper corporate governance to prepare them for eventual privatisation. These include the Bangladesh Textile Mills Corporation, the Bangladesh Steel and Engineering Corporation, the Bangladesh Sugar and Food Industries Corporation, the Bangladesh Chemical Industries Corporation, the Bangladesh Forest Industries Development Corporation and the Bangladesh Jute Mills Corporation. SOEs that function as a monopoly due to regulatory constraints should be put under competitive pressure through deregulation to allow for private participation and restructured with proper corporate governance. These include the four SOEs in the energy sector (BPC, Petrobangla, REB and PDB) and the water utilities in Dhaka, Chattogram, Rajshahi and Khulna. SOEs that provide essential services that are commercial in nature but are either natural monopolies or where government ownership is considered necessary for strategic reasons -- should be restructured through proper corporate governance. These include the Bangladesh Shipping Corporation, the Bangladesh Inland Water Transport Corporation, the Bangladesh Road Transport Corporation, CPA, the Mongla Port Authority, the Bangladesh Land Port Authority, the Bangladesh Bridge Authority, the Payra Port Authority, BTRC, CAAB and the National Housing Authority. SOEs that mostly perform non-commercial functions should be redefined to take away any limited commercial role and merged with respective line ministries that manage them. Their commercial roles should be reassigned to the private sector. This includes the five construction-related SOEs Rajdhani Unnayan Kartripakkha (RAJUK), Chattagram Development Authority, Rajshahi Development Authority, Khulna Development Authority and Cox’s Bazar Development Authority. Under this category are 19 service-related enterprises, most of which are tiny to start with: BJC, BADC, BFDC, BEZA, BSTI, BFDC (Film), BFFWT, BPRC, BIWTA, BSCIC, BEPZA, BTB, BSB, BERC, EPB, BITAC, Novo Theatre, BSRTI, BHB. SOEs that are purely regulatory in nature -- like the BTRC and the Bangladesh Energy Regulatory -- should be converted to fully autonomous regulatory bodies with full autonomy as a regulatory entity, with no government interference. “While the nation as a whole will benefit from SOE reforms, the suggested reforms are likely to face bureaucratic resistance, especially from groups who benefit from the existing inefficiencies or malpractices.”

title: S Alam Group chairman among 11 sentenced in Tk 84.5cr Islami Bank loan case
body: A Chattogram court today sentenced S Alam Group Chairman Mohammed Saiful Alam and its 10 executives to five months’ imprisonment in a case over the non-repayment of a Tk 84.49 crore loan from Islami Bank Bangladesh PLC. Judge Md Helal Uddin of Chattogram Money Loan Court-1 delivered the verdict following a petition filed by Islami Bank’s Khatunganj branch, confirmed branch official Md Ershad. The convicted individuals include Saiful Alam’s wife Farzana Parveen, his brothers Osman Gani, Md Rashedul Alam, Abdus Samad; Farzana Begum; Ahsanul Alam; OG Travels Ltd Chairman Gofranul Alam, Managing Director Hakim Ali, and directors Md Abdullah Hasan and Shahidul Alam. According to court sources, Islami Bank approved a loan of over Tk 80 crore for OG Travels Ltd, a sister concern of S Alam Group, on December 20, 2023, to purchase 134 buses. The loan was disbursed in eight phases between March 10 and July 8, 2024. However, the buses were reportedly not supplied as agreed, leaving the loan at risk. After failing to recover the loan amount, Islami Bank filed a case with Chattogram Money Loan Court-1 on August 26 last year.

title: PM Tarique Rahman set to visit Ramisa’s Pallabi home tonight
body: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman is expected to visit the home of Ramisa Akter in Dhaka’s Pallabi tonight. Sources at the Prime Minister’s Office confirmed the matter to The Daily Star this evening. Around 11:00am on Tuesday, police recovered Ramisa’s decapitated body from a neighbour's flat in Pallabi. A top student of class 2 at Popular Model High School, she lived with her family in an apartment in the Section 11 area of Pallabi. The accused, Sohel Rana, 30, her neighbour, was detained by a team of Mirpur Division Police in Narayanganj’s Fatullah around 7:00pm on Tuesday. His wife, Swapna Khatun, 27, has also been arrested.

title: Police take custody of man accused of assaulting child in Ctg’s Bakalia
body: Police on Thursday night took into custody a man accused of sexually assaulting a four-year-old girl in Chattogram city’s Bakalia area, nearly seven hours after hundreds of locals confined him at the scene. The accused, Monir Hossen, 35, was removed from the spot and taken to a police station around 10:00pm, said Aminur Rashid, assistant commissioner (PR) of Chattogram Metropolitan Police. He said several police personnel were injured in clashes with locals while trying to bring the situation under control. “The accused has been rescued from there and brought under police custody,” the police official said. Earlier in the day, hundreds of people gathered and tried to stop police from taking Monir into custody. Videos surfaced online of police firing shots to bring the situation under control. Monir works at a local decoration shop, said police. Officer-in-Charge (OC) Mohammad Solaiman, of Bakalia Police Station, said according to the child’s family, Monir Hossen sexually abused the four-year-old girl after taking her inside a decoration shop near her house. Later, the child narrated the incident to her parents. Following the incident, the child’s family held Monir and took him to their house around 3:00pm. After the news spread in the locality, hundreds gathered in front of the house to beat the accused. On information, police also rushed to the spot, the OC added. A witness said that as the public became furious and tried to snatch the accused, police opened fire to bring the situation under control at around 6:00pm. Chases and counter chases ensued between police and the mob However, no officials picked up their phones when contacted for confirmation about shots being fired.

title: Man gets life term for rape of 4‑year‑old in Satkhira
body: A Satkhira court today sentenced a man to rigorous life imprisonment over the rape of a four-year-old child in Kaliganj upazila in 2024. Judge Md Abu Bakkar Siddique of the Satkhira Women and Children Repression Prevention Tribunal announced the verdict in the presence of accused Sohorab Hossain in the court, said tribunal’s Special Public Prosecutor (PP) Advocate Sheikh Ali Ashraf. The court also fined Sohrab Tk50,000, in default of which, he has to serve additional three months' rigorous imprisonment. According to the case statement, Sohrab, a resident of Tarali village in Kaliganj upazila, is a distant granduncle of the victim. The two used to play together occasionally. On February 28, 2024, around 2:00pm, the accused lured the child into his room while playing in their courtyard. There, strangling her and threatening to kill the victim, he raped her. He then threatened her once again not to tell anyone about the incident. When questioned about the pain in her genitals in the evening, the child informed her mother, added the case details. She was then treated locally. On March 4 that year, the victim’s mother filed a rape case with Kaliganj Police Station against Sohrab Hossain following which, he was arrested. After examining the testimonies and statements of 13 witnesses and reviewing the case documents, the judge handed down the verdict today. Special PP Advocate Sheikh Ali Ashraf who stood for the state, expressed satisfaction with the verdict.

title: Rape, murder of 11-year-old in Ctg: Prime accused arrested from Narsingdi
body: Chattogram district police today arrested the prime accused in a case filed over the rape and murder of an 11-year-old madrasa student in Hathazari upazila of the district. Police arrested Md Faisal, 20, during a drive in Raipura upazila of Narsingdi on Wednesday and later handed him over to Hathazari Police Station, Kazi Tarek Aziz, additional superintendent of police (Hathazari circle) in Chattogram, told The Daily Star. According to police, the victim, Afrin Aktar, was missing for two days. On March 28, locals found a foul smell coming from a cotton warehouse in Hathazari’s Amanbazar area. There, they discovered the body and later informed the police. CCTV footage shows that a man identified as Faisal, a day labourer and neighbour of the victim, took the girl into the warehouse and left by himself after some time. Since then, police had been trying to detain Faisal. During interrogation, Faisal told police today that he picked up the girl from in front of her house on March 26, brought her to the warehouse and later raped her there, said additional SP Kazi Tarek Aziz. “As the victim tried to scream and said she would disclose the matter to her mother, Faisal and his associates murdered the girl and dumped her body inside a sack,” said the police official, quoting Faisal. The arrestee also made a confessional statement before a magistrate today, the police official added.

title: Madrasa student remanded over rape, abetment to suicide of 10-year-old in Dhaka’s Banasree
body: A Dhaka court today placed a madrasa student on a five-day remand in a case filed over the alleged rape and abetment to the suicide of a 10-year-old boy in Dhaka’s Banasree area. The accused, Shihab Hossain, 20, was arrested on Wednesday from his home in Pabna's Bera upazila in connection with the death of Abdullah, a student of Alokito Quran International Hifz Madrasa in Banasree. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Hasibuzzaman passed the order after police produced him before the court and sought a seven-day remand. During the hearing, Metropolitan Public Prosecutor Omar Faruq Faruqi and investigation officer Saiful Islam, a sub-inspector of Rampura Police Station, argued in favour of the remand. Faruqi told the court that such incidents tarnish the dignity of society and the education system, and those responsible must be brought to justice. “In the name of service, the hujurs (teachers) make little children massage their hands and feet. Eventually, they become attracted to the children. At one stage, such incidents (rape) occur,” he said. No lawyer appeared on behalf of the accused during the hearing. According to case documents, police went to the madrasa on May 19 after receiving reports that a child had died by suicide. The body was later sent to Dhaka Medical College Hospital morgue for an autopsy. During the inquest, officers found signs of sexual assault, prompting further questioning of madrasa authorities. According to a press release issued by Motijheel Division Police, madrasa authorities later disclosed allegations that Shihab had sexually abused four other students at the institution. On Wednesday, Abdullah’s mother, Tuku Ara Khatun, filed a case with Rampura Police Station against Shihab and an unnamed person under the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act. Police said Shihab fled the madrasa before Abdullah’s death. A team from Rampura Police later tracked him down to his village home in Pabna and arrested him.

title: Ramisa murder: Home minister promises ‘exemplary trial’ in shortest time
body: An exemplary trial will be completed in the shortest possible time over the rape and murder of eight-year-old Ramisa , Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed said today. He gave the assurance while responding to questions from reporters at the Secretariat this afternoon. Responding to journalists with a counter-question, the minister said, “Since we took charge, can anyone cite a single heinous crime in which police did not make every effort or failed to arrest the perpetrators within a short time? There is not one such case. I have the full list. If there has been any lapse, you may raise questions.” He said, "In Ramisa's case as well, the accused was arrested within 24 hours. The main accused's name is probably Sohel... he has been arrested along with his wife. They have given statements under Section 164 (of the Penal Code). We can assure you this much that from our end, a proper investigation will be conducted and the chargesheet will be submitted in a short time. The responsibility of judgement lies with the court." "The issue of culture of impunity that everyone always talks about is not correct in all cases. In some cases, justice is delayed, which makes people think they might not get justice. But regarding these types of crimes -- I have seen during the tenure of the interim government as well, and I want to give them credit, when several such incidents occurred during that period, they took legal action within a short time," the home minister said. "In this case, I can guarantee this much that an exemplary trial will be completed in the shortest possible time. However, I cannot talk about the punishment," he added.

title: Man dies after mob assault over alleged theft attempt in Jhalakathi
body: A man was killed in a mob assault while allegedly preparing to steal an electric transformer in Kathalia upazila of Jhalakathi early today. The deceased was identified as Razzak Hawlader, 50, of Bashbunia village under Amua union, said Kathalia Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Md Naser Rayhan. According to locals, Razzak allegedly removed parts from a tractor kept on a piece of land in Uttar Bashbunia village around 1:30am with the intention of stealing them. He later attempted to steal a nearby electric transformer when local residents noticed the incident and caught him red-handed. At one stage, agitated locals attacked him, leaving him critically injured and unconscious. He was rushed to Kathalia Upazila Health Complex, where the on-duty doctor declared him dead. The OC said no member of the deceased’s family had yet come to the police station. “If the relatives do not file a case, police will file a case over the killing,” he said. The OC said Razzak was accused in at least eight criminal cases, including theft, robbery, and murder.

title: HC rejects writ challenging legality of interim government’s activities
body: The High Court today summarily rejected a writ petition challenging the legality of activities carried out during the tenure of the interim government led by former chief adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus. The HC bench of Justice Ahmed Sohel and Justice Fatema Anwar passed the order after hearing arguments on the petition. Senior Advocate MK Rahman appeared for the writ petitioner, while Additional Attorney General Aneek R Haque opposed the petition. Writ petitioner Advocate Mohammad Mohsen Rashid told The Daily Star that he would move an appeal before the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court challenging the HC order. He submitted the petition to the High Court on May 4, seeking a directive for the government to form a commission to examine whether there were any allegations of corruption against Prof Yunus. The petition also questioned the legality of various decisions, laws enacted, reform commissions formed, and domestic and international agreements signed during the tenure of the current government, he said. Earlier, the same lawyer had filed another writ petition challenging the legality of the oath-taking and formation process of the current government. However, a High Court bench dismissed that petition. An appeal was later filed against the dismissal order, and the Supreme Court subsequently upheld the legality of the interim government.

title: BNP leader killed in Narayanganj over soil-cutting dispute
body: A local BNP leader was hacked to death in Narayanganj’s Araihazar upazila early today following a dispute over soil cutting, police said. The deceased was identified as Osman Goni, 40, of Baro Boinarchar area and general secretary of Brahmandi Union BNP. Md Alauddin, officer-in-charge (OC) of Araihazar Police Station, said the attack took place around 12:45am in a low-lying area of Pachgaon Charpara under Duptara union while Goni was supervising soil extraction work. Critically injured, he was first taken to a local private hospital and later referred to the Dhaka Medical College Hospital, where he died on the way, the OC said. Following the killing, relatives and supporters of the victim blocked the Araihazar-Gausia road this morning and vandalised several vehicles, disrupting traffic in the area. Police later brought the situation under control and cleared the road. The OC said four people, including Ramzan Ali, member secretary of Duptara union Swechchhasebak Dal, were detained for questioning in connection with the incident. Police and local sources said Goni had recently undertaken a soil-cutting project in Duptara union. Ramzan allegedly obstructed the work, leading to a dispute between the two sides on Tuesday afternoon. Family members alleged that the killing was linked to that conflict. Goni was also the grandson-in-law of Araihazar upazila BNP president Yusuf Ali Bhuiyan and uncle of former district Chhatra Dal member secretary Zubayer Hossain Jiku. Contacted by phone, Yusuf Ali Bhuiyan claimed that Goni owned an excavator and was engaged in soil extraction work in the area. “Ramzan demanded Tk 50,000 in extortion and obstructed the work after the demand was refused. We had informed police earlier,” he alleged. He also said Goni went to retrieve a stuck excavator late at night when he came under attack. “There was hardly any part of his body without injuries,” he claimed. Quoting preliminary findings, OC Alauddin said the dispute stemmed from soil being cut from one pond to fill another area. “We have brought four people in for questioning. They had an altercation with the victim the previous day over soil cutting. The investigation is ongoing to determine their involvement in the killing,” he added.

title: Rape, murder of 8-year-old in Pallabi: Law minister directs police to submit report within 7 days
body: Law Minister Md Asaduzzaman has directed the Dhaka Metropolitan Police commissioner to submit an investigation report within seven days into the rape and murder of an eight-year-old girl in the capital’s Pallabi area on Tuesday, according to ministry sources. The ministry said necessary steps would be taken to ensure the trial was completed as swiftly as possible. Ramisa Akter’s neighbour, Sohel Rana, 31, raped and then killed and beheaded her in Pallabi. The prime suspect confessed before a magistrate yesterday to raping and killing the child. Following the recording of his confessional statement by Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, a Dhaka court sent Sohel Rana, to jail. His wife, Swapna Akter, 26, was also sent to jail after police appealed to a separate court to keep her in custody as an accomplice in the killing. The case was filed by the Ramisa’s father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, who named the couple and an unidentified third person as accused. According to the case statement, Rana lured Ramisa into his home, where he raped her. He then slit her throat and attempted to dismember her body in an effort to conceal the crime.

title: Brutality laid bare
body: The accused in the gruesome murder of eight-year-old Ramisa Akter in the capital’s Pallabi on Tuesday confessed before a magistrate yesterday to raping and killing the child. After Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid recorded the confessional statement under Section 164 of the CrPC, a Dhaka court sent the accused, Sohel Rana, 31, to jail. His wife, Swapna Akter, 26, was also sent to jail after police appealed to a separate court to keep her in custody as an accomplice to the killing. The case was filed by the victim’s father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, who accused the couple and an unidentified person. Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station told The Daily Star that the prime accused had already admitted to the crime during primary interrogation. According to the case statement, Sohel, the victim’s neighbour, lured Ramisa, a second-grader at Popular Model High School, into his room and raped her. To conceal the crime, he slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body. Speaking to this correspondent, family members and neighbours said that, after hearing a child screaming, her mother, Parveen Begum, stepped out of their flat to investigate. At first, she thought it might have been another child crying. As time passed and Ramisa was due to get ready for school, Parveen began searching for her again and found one of her sandals in front of Sohel’s flat. She then began banging on the door repeatedly while other neighbours rushed to help. Panicked, Sohel hid the body under his bed, placed the severed head in a bucket in the washroom, and escaped through the window of the room he shared with his wife. When the mother and neighbours broke into the flat, they found Swapna standing in the common area. The child’s body was discovered under the bed and her head was found in a bucket in the bathroom. Sohel had gone into hiding but was arrested from Fatullah in Narayanganj around 7:00pm on Tuesday. Swapna was detained shortly after the murder. Sources at the morgue of Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital described the extreme brutality of the crime. They said that, in addition to the beheading, both arms and the left leg were nearly severed and multiple other injuries were found on the body. The body was handed over to the family yesterday. Following a namaz-e-janaza at a local mosque at 4:00pm, it was taken to Munshiganj for burial. A TRAUMATISED NEIGHBOURHOOD A heart-wrenching scene unfolded at Ramisa’s home yesterday. Parveen was seen repeatedly losing consciousness. Whenever she regained consciousness, she murmured, “Bring Ramisa back. She needs to go to school, eat her breakfast ... she can’t eat on her own.” Ramisa’s father, Abdul Hannan, also fell ill from shock. Overwhelmed with grief and frustration, he was heard saying yesterday morning, “I don’t want justice because you [the country] cannot deliver it. You have no record of ensuring justice. After 15 days, another incident will occur and that’s it.” Outside the home, traumatised residents -- many of them mothers -- staged demonstrations throughout the day, demanding exemplary punishment for those responsible. Saika Sayeed, a 34-year-old teacher, joined the protest carrying a placard calling for a safe, drug-free neighbourhood. Describing the accused as “psychopathic”, she demanded the highest punishment for the couple and expressed scepticism about the legal system, fearing Sohel might secure bail and offend again. Students and teachers from Ramisa’s school also took part in the demonstrations. When Sohel was brought to court, people, including lawyers, chanted slogans demanding the highest punishment for him, with some calling for the death penalty.

title: Woman found dead at in-laws’ house; family alleges dowry murder
body: A woman has died under suspicious circumstances in Bhedarganj upazila of Shariatpur, sparking allegations of dowry-related murder. The family of the victim, Rajlaxmi Purabi, 25, of Nagarpara in Gosairhat upazila, alleged that she was strangled to death for failing to bring dowry money. However, her in-laws have rejected the allegation and said she took her own life. Rajlaxmi’s husband, Chanchal Hawladar, 30, of Singachura area in Bhedarganj upazila, has been absconding with their two-year-old child since the incident. According to local sources and police, the incident came to light around 8:00am on Wednesday when the victim’s mother-in-law, Laxmi Hawladar, saw Rajlaxmi’s body hanging from a wooden beam. She immediately called neighbours, who rushed to the scene and took Rajlaxmi to Shariatpur Sadar Hospital, where doctors declared her dead. Speaking to The Daily Star, the victim’s relative Rinku Rani alleged that Chanchal frequently assaulted Rajlaxmi over dowry demands, but the family was financially incapable of meeting such demands. Rajlaxmi’s mother-in-law, Laxmi, denied the murder allegation. She said Rajlaxmi had asked her father for money to send her husband abroad for work. “When her father refused, she became distressed and took her own life out of anger and frustration,” Laxmi said. “Chanchal is innocent. He did not kill her,” she added. Shariatpur Sadar Hospital duty doctor Dr Hasan confirmed that Rajlaxmi was brought to the hospital in the morning. “She was declared dead after an examination. There were strangulation marks on her neck,” he said. Bhedarganj Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Abu Bakar said police were sent to the scene after receiving information. “The body was recovered from the in-laws’ house. We are investigating the matter.” “No written complaint has been filed yet, but the family has said they will file a case,” added the OC.

title: Prime accused arrested over murder of 9-year-old Ramim in Narsingdi
body: Police have arrested the prime accused in the murder of nine‑year‑old Ramim, who died after air was pumped into his rectum in Palash, Narsingdi. The accused, Sabuj Mia, 34, was arrested this morning near Arshinagar in Narsingdi Sadar Upazila. On May 6, Sabuj along with three others -- Faisal, 25; Shishir, 28; and Babu, 25 -- allegedly forced the child into a rickshaw garage at Gajaria Bazar and pumped air into his rectum and mouth using an air machine. Ramim became critically ill and later died while undergoing treatment at Dhaka Medical College Hospital. Following the incident, the victim’s father, Ripon Mia, filed a murder case with Palash Police Station, naming the four accused. All had gone into hiding after the child’s death. Shahed Al Mamun, officer‑in‑charge of Palash Police Station, confirmed that Sabuj was sent to court this afternoon with a plea for a seven‑day police remand.

title: Before we called her a victim, she was a child
body: I keep going back to her photo. Not because it tells me how she died, but because it shows me what was taken from her. A little girl is holding flowers. Her face is turned slightly away, as if someone has just called her name. Perhaps she was about to smile. Perhaps someone behind the camera asked her to look this way, and she did not. That is how children are. Half in the frame, half already elsewhere. This was not supposed to be a photo for strangers. It was meant to stay on the phone of a family member, among the photos parents keep and look at later. A child on an ordinary day. A child before anyone called her “victim”. Now we look at it after knowing too much. Ramisa was supposed to go to school around 10:30am, police said. That sentence sits heavily inside me. School time. A mother calling. A child getting ready. A sister waiting. Shoes near the door. A morning that should have ended with classwork, tiffin, and the tired return of a child who had spent the day learning. Instead, one shoe was found near a neighbouring flat. One shoe. Children leave their shoes everywhere. Parents pick them up. They scold. They laugh. They call the child careless. But here, a child’s shoe became the first sign that something was wrong. I keep thinking of her mother, Parvin Akhter, standing outside that closed door. At first, perhaps she was confused. Then worried. Then afraid in the way mothers become afraid before anyone else understands why. She knocked. Behind that door was the end of her child’s morning. We write crime reports with carefully chosen words. We say “incident”. We say “suspect”. We say “body”. We say, “forensic tests”. We say the truth will be known after investigation. All of that is necessary. But none of it can capture the sound of a mother frantically knocking. Police earlier said investigators suspected Ramisa may have been sexually assaulted before she was killed . Later, police said the prime accused, Sohel Rana, admitted during questioning that he had raped the child. This remains a police statement, and the court must establish the truth through evidence, forensic findings and trial. But even before the trial begins, something has already broken. What kind of society allows a child to disappear right next to her own home? What kind of building has doors so close to each other, and yet leaves a child so alone? And then there is the door. Police suspect the wife of the prime accused acted as an accomplice by keeping it shut until her husband fled through a window after cutting its grille. She has reportedly claimed she had taken sleeping pills and knew nothing. That, too, must be tested through investigation. But the allegation is chilling. A mother was outside, knocking for her child. Inside, according to police, another adult waited long enough for a man to escape after murdering a child. How does a human being live with that? We often think danger comes from far away. But sometimes it waits in the flat next door, behind a door we pass without fear. After a few days, this country may move on. That is what often happens. A new story will come. A new outrage will take over. The headlines will shift. The family will remain with the photo. That must not be her fate. The investigation must be exact. The evidence must be protected. The forensic report must come quickly. The trial must not drown in delay. Her family must not be left alone after the cameras leave. But even justice is too late for a child who should have reached school. I look again at the photograph. A child holding flowers. A daughter. A little sister. A schoolgirl. A child who should have reached school. A child who should have come home. And for the child who did not, justice must show no mercy. Arafat Rahaman is a journalist at The Daily Star. He can be reached at [email protected] .

title: SC upholds ex-chief justice Khairul's HC bail, no bar to his release
body: The Supreme Court today upheld the High Court orders that granted former chief justice ABM Khairul Haque six months’ ad-interim bail in two murder cases filed over incidents during the July uprising. Chamber judge of the Appellate Division of the SC, Justice Md Rezaul Haque, passed “no order” on two separate petitions filed by the state seeking a stay on the HC orders of bail. There is no legal bar for Khairul to be released from jail following the apex court chamber judge's order, his lawyer, Md Motaher Hossain Sazu, told The Daily Star. The lawyer, however, said the government has recently submitted a petition to the lower court concerned seeking permission to show Khairul arrested in a criminal case. The lower court is scheduled to hold a hearing and pass an order on the petition on May 23, Advocate Motaher added. Deputy Attorney General Syeda Shajia Sharmin represented the state while lawyer Motaher Hossain Sazu appeared for Khairul Haque during hearing on the state's petitions before the SC Chamber judge's court today. On May 12, the HC granted ad-interim bail for six months to Khairul and also issued two separate rules asking the state to explain why he should not be granted permanent bail in the cases. One case, filed with Jatrabari Police Station, accuses him in connection with the killing of Arif, while the other, filed with Adabor Police Station, concerns the killing of Rubel during the uprising, said Advocate Md Motaher. Khairul was arrested at his Dhanmondi residence in Dhaka on July 24, 2025, nearly a year after the fall of the Awami League government. He was later shown arrested in multiple cases, including several filed over killings during the July movement, and has remained in jail since then. On April 28, the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court upheld earlier HC orders granting him bail in five other cases.

title: Four sentenced to death, nine to life term in army officer Lt Tanjim murder case
body: A Cox’s Bazar court today sentenced four people to death and nine others to life imprisonment in the murder case of Army officer Lt Tanjim Sarwar. The court also acquitted five accused in the case. The verdict was delivered in the afternoon by Judge Mohammad Abul Mansur Siddiqui of the Cox’s Bazar Additional District and Sessions Judge Court-5. Those sentenced to death are Md Helal Uddin, Nurul Amin, Md Nasir Uddin and Morshed Alam. Among them, Morshed remains absconding. All are residents of Dulahazara union in Chakaria upazila. The verdict ended nearly a year and eight months of legal proceedings in the criminal case. Following the verdict, Chief Prosecutor Mohammad Jahangir said the young army officer was brutally killed while performing his duty in service of the country. “His family, the Bangladesh Army, the state and the people all expected justice to be served,” he said. He added that the court had not relied solely on allegations or one-sided testimonies. Instead, it examined witness statements, evidence, surrounding circumstances and the overall facts of the case before delivering the punishment for the four accused. Another prosecution lawyer, Ahsan Sezan, said, “Lt Tanzim was a patriotic officer. He went there to protect people’s lives and property and to ensure public security. But he was brutally killed in the situation that unfolded.” He said verdicts in both the murder and Arms Act cases were delivered today. Alongside the death sentences and life terms, 13 accused were also handed an additional 10 years in prison under sections 399 and 402 of the Penal Code. Sezan said the prosecution was “reasonably satisfied” with the judgment. He noted that the judge had highlighted issues of social justice, public safety and discipline in his observations. “The court also stressed that while ensuring punishment for the real offenders, it must equally ensure that no innocent person is convicted,” he added. He further said the verdict was delivered after considering both the prosecution’s evidence and the defence’s cross-examinations. The full judgment regarding the five acquitted accused would be reviewed and further legal steps could be taken if necessary. Meanwhile, several defence lawyers said they had been denied justice and would challenge the verdict before the High Court. Tahsin Sifat, lawyer for the fifth and sixth accused, said they were dissatisfied with the ruling, particularly the life sentences and separate punishments under the Arms Act imposed on his clients. Lt Tanjim Sarwar, 23, was killed around 1:30am on September 23, 2024 while conducting an anti-robbery operation in Purba Maizpara area of Dulahazara union. Originally from Tangail, Tanzim had been commissioned from the Bangladesh Military Academy in 2022 and was serving in the Army Service Corps. His killing triggered nationwide outrage and mourning. Two days after the incident, Senior Warrant Officer Abdullah Al Harunur Rashid filed a murder case against 17 people over the killing and alleged robbery preparations. In a separate case, Chakaria Police Station Sub-Inspector Alamgir Hossain filed charges under the Arms Act. Later, Chakaria Police Station Inspector (Investigation) Arup Kumar Chowdhury was assigned to investigate the cases. After completing the investigation, police submitted charge sheets against 18 people in the two cases. Several individuals named in the original complaint were dropped due to lack of evidence, while new accused were added based on the findings of the investigation.

title: Neighbour confesses to rape, murder of 8-year-old in Pallabi: Police
body: Eight-year-old Ramisa Akter was raped by her neighbour Sohel Rana before he murdered and beheaded her in Dhaka’s Pallabi yesterday, police said after primary interrogation. Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station told The Daily Star that Sohel (31), the main accused, admitted during interrogation that he had raped the child before murdering her. Sohel, his wife Swapna Akter (26), and an unidentified person were made accused in a case filed with Pallabi Police Station by Ramisa’s father, Abdul Hannan Mollah. Police produced Sohel and Swapna before a Dhaka court, and court sources said Sohel agreed to give a confessional statement before a magistrate. The unidentified accused is on the run. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid recorded Sohel's confessional statement after police brought him to the magistrate’s chamber, said a court staff member. Details of the statement could not be known immediately. After recording the statement, the magistrate sent Sohel to jail. Swapna was sent to jail by another Dhaka court. In the case statement, Hannan alleged that Sohel took his daughter, a second grader at Popular Model High School, to his room and raped her. He later beheaded her, intending to conceal his crime by dismembering the body. But Ramisa’s screams had caught the attention of her mother. Sohel hid Ramisa’s body under his bed as her family members and neighbours began banging on his door. Her severed head was found in a bucket in the toilet. The body was handed over to family today after an autopsy at Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital. Sohel went into hiding after the incident but was detained from Narayanganj’s Fatullah around 7:00pm yesterday.

title: Bidisha Ershad sentenced to 2 years in jail in fraud case
body: A Dhaka court today sentenced Bidisha Ershad, former wife of late Jatiya Party chairman and former president Hussain Muhammad Ershad, to two years’ imprisonment in a fraud case. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Md Jamshed Alam delivered the verdict in the absence of the accused, Hemayet Uddin Khan Heron, a lawyer for the complainant, told The Daily Star. The court also fined Bidisha Tk 10,000, with an additional one month’s imprisonment in default of payment, he said. During the trial, six prosecution witnesses testified before the court. The case was filed on February 2, 2008, with Gulshan Police Station by AKM Mosharrof Hossain Sikdar, a businessman from Dhaka’s Pallabi area. According to the case statement, Mosharrof paid Bidisha Tk 75 lakh on July 10, 2001, for a flat in Baridhara that was scheduled to be handed over by July 10, 2002. However, despite several years passing, the flat was not handed over, the complaint alleged. Later, Bidisha issued a cheque worth Tk 75 lakh, which was dishonoured on May 2, 2005, due to insufficient funds. The complainant further alleged that he went to Bidisha’s Baridhara residence on January 26, 2008, to recover the money but failed to do so and was later threatened when he made further attempts to get the money back.

title: Prime suspect arrested in Dhaka murder of Saudi returnee
body: Police have arrested the prime suspect in the murder of a Bangladeshi expatriate, whose body was dismembered in Dhaka’s Manda Mugda area a week ago. A joint team of Mugda police and Counter Terrorism officials of DMP arrested Taslima Akter, 31, from her sister’s house in Narsingdi this morning, Muhammad Harun Or Rashid, deputy commissioner of Motijheel Division Police, told The Daily Star. Deceased Mokarram Miah, 37, who worked in Saudi Arabia, was killed on May 14. His body was later dismembered and dumped in several locations across the capital. Earlier, Rab arrested two persons -- Helena Akter, 40, and her 13-year-old daughter -- on May 18. Police and Rab said the killing stemmed from Mokarram’s relationship with Taslima alias Hasna, 31, wife of another expatriate. He had sent her more than Tk 5,00,000 and demanded marriage or repayment after returning to Bangladesh on May 13 without informing his family. Mokarram demanded repayment of the money he had sent to Taslima and threatened to leak her private photos and videos after she refused to marry him. Taslima and Helena later allegedly planned to kill him. On May 14 morning, they mixed sleeping pills into his drink. When he became unconscious, they allegedly killed him. The body was then taken to a bathroom, cleaned, and later cut into eight pieces. The parts were kept in plastic bags before being dumped in multiple locations, including near the building’s garbage area. The victim’s head was later recovered about one kilometre away, based on information provided by Helena.

title: Pallabi child murder: Her shoes were outside the neighbour’s door; inside was horror
body: Ramisa Akhter had filled her home with academic trophies. On Tuesday morning, the eight-year-old schoolgirl was found brutally murdered in a flat next door. Ramisa was the top student in class two at Popular Model High School in Dhaka’s Pallabi. After securing second place in playgroup and KG, she earned roll number one in class one. Her academic trophies still sit carefully arranged at home -- reminders of a bright child who is no longer there. Around 11:00am on Tuesday, police recovered Ramisa’s decapitated body from a flat next to her family’s home in Pallabi. She lived with her family in an apartment in the Section 11 area of Pallabi. When this correspondent visited the family’s home on Tuesday evening, Ramisa’s 10-year-old sister, Raisa Akhter, was staring quietly at the trophies. “My sister was a good student. She was very attentive in her studies,” Raisa told The Daily Star, before turning her eyes back to Ramisa’s achievements. Ramisa’s mother, Parvin Begum, told reporters that her daughter was getting ready for school in the morning. “My elder daughter Raisa told me she was going to her uncle’s house in another building. I thought Ramisa had gone with her,” Parvin said. “After a while, I heard Ramisa screaming and went looking for her. When I came out of the house, I saw her shoes in front of Sohel’s flat,” she said, referring to a neighbour. Parvin said she knocked repeatedly on the door, but no one opened it. “Later, people from the neighbourhood came and broke open the door. They recovered my daughter’s body. They brutally murdered my daughter,” she said. The accused, Sohel Rana, 30, was detained by a team of Mirpur Division Police in Narayanganj’s Fatullah around 7:00pm on Tuesday, according to police. Ramisa’s uncle, AKM Nazrul Islam, told The Daily Star that locals broke open the door and found Sohel’s wife inside the flat. He said Ramisa’s headless body had been hidden under a bed, while her head was recovered from a bucket in the bathroom. “Sohel cut a window grille and fled. Even after repeated knocks, his wife did not open the door. She helped her husband escape,” Nazrul alleged. Later in the evening, this correspondent visited Ramisa’s school, where a heavy silence hung over the campus. Her class teacher, Mahbubul Hakim, said Ramisa always came to school 10 minutes early. “Today (Tuesday), she did not attend, so I was a bit worried. Later, I found out that she had been murdered. Such incidents are unacceptable,” he said. Saiful Islam, headmaster of Popular Model High School, described Ramisa as a bright student. “We are outraged by this incident. A human chain programme will be held at the school tomorrow (today),” he told The Daily Star. Pallabi Police Station Officer-in-Charge Hasan Bashir said accused Sohel Rana and his wife, Swapna Khatun, 27, have been arrested.

title: Man arrested in Aug 5, 2024 police station vandalism case dies in Ctg jail custody
body: A man arrested in a case filed over vandalism and arson at Chattogram’s Sadarghat Police Station on August 5, 2024, has died in prison custody. The deceased, Debashish Chowdhury, 45, used to work as an accountant at an ashram in the Kotwali area, said police. He lived with his family in the PK Sen area. The prison authorities said that Debashish died on Monday morning at Chittagong Medical College Hospital. After the autopsy, his body was handed over to the family on Tuesday afternoon. However, his family alleged that he was falsely implicated in the Sadarghat Police Station vandalism case because of a land dispute. They claimed that a rival party had him arrested by providing false information and that he was later tortured in prison. Debashish's mother, Pratibha Mahajan, said police arrested her son from their home on April 27. She told The Daily Star over phone, “That night we were preparing for bed after dinner when three men in plain clothes came and were calling out my son's name. At one point, they said there was a warrant in my son's name over a case of vandalism at the police station. Later, he was taken into police custody.” “I went to the police station and asked who filed the case. When I asked, police informed me it was a case over vandalism at Sadarghat Police Station on August 5, 2024,” said Pratibha. “My son is not involved with any political party. One of my two sons lives in Dhaka. Debashish used to take care of us. We have two and a half gonda (5 decimals) of land in Sadarghat. We have disputes with a few people over those. Because of that, they got my son arrested in this case,” she added. “My son is gone. What do I have left to live for? He had two young children. This land dispute has taken my son away,” Pratibha lamented. Senior Jail Superintendent of Chittagong Central Jail, Iqbal Hossain, told The Daily Star, “Debashish was an inmate of the Sangu Ward. On Monday morning, while having a conversation, he collapsed with chest pain. He was initially taken to the jail hospital and later to CMCH for advanced treatment, where he died.” Pratibha Mahajan said, “Yesterday I got a call from a number telling me that my son had a heart attack and was in a coma. When I went to the hospital, I found him dead. This afternoon, after taking the body, I came to my village home in Mirsarai.” Despite multiple attempts to contact Kazi Md Mahfuz Hasan Siddiqui, officer-in-charge of Sadarghat Police Station, for comments regarding the family's allegations, he did not respond. However, a senior officer of the Chattogram Metropolitan Police, speaking on condition of anonymity, confirmed to The Daily Star that Debashish was arrested by the police in connection with the Sadarghat Police Station vandalism case.

title: Thai crew member stabbed to death on scrap ship at Chattogram port
body: A Thai crew member was stabbed to death by a fellow crewman onboard a scrap ship anchored at the outer anchorage of Chattogram port on Tuesday. The deceased, identified as Rapheephong Klahan, 30 – a crew member of the Thai-flagged vessel MT KPP 01 – was attacked following an altercation with fellow crewman Turakorn Burussee, 48. According to Chittagong Port Authority (CPA) sources, the two men got into a fight on the deck around 12:00pm. At one stage, Burussee allegedly stabbed Klahan with a kitchen knife, leaving him critically injured. Md Emranul Hoque, head of business operations of the ship’s local agent SAM Shipping Agency, confirmed that their team rushed to the vessel after receiving information, disembarked the injured Klahan, and took him to Apollo Imperial Hospital in Chattogram. He succumbed to his injuries around 2:30pm. Later, police from Anwara and Patenga Police Stations conducted a joint drive at the ship and detained Burussee, who was placed in the custody of Anwara Police Station. Officer-in-Charge of Anwara Police Station Jubaer Chowdhury confirmed the arrest and said a case was being processed in connection with the incident.

title: ‘Pichchi Raja’ arrested at Dhaka airport, police say
body: Police say they have arrested an alleged criminal and top drug trader of Mohammadpur’s Geneva Camp, Md Raja Badsha alias “Pichchi Raja,” from Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka. He was detained around 7:30pm Tuesday after returning from Nepal with his family, said Jewel Rana, additional deputy commissioner (Mohammadpur Zone) of Dhaka Metropolitan Police. According to police, there are 29 cases against Raja -- three murder cases, seven attempted murder cases, four explosives cases, one Special Powers Act case, one anti-terrorism case, and 13 narcotics cases. Law enforcers claimed Raja had long been involved in criminal activities, including drug trading, in Mohammadpur and Geneva Camp, establishing dominance in the area through alleged criminal operations. Police said he had previously been arrested multiple times and produced before courts. After securing bail in earlier cases, he went into hiding but allegedly continued his criminal activities. ADC Jewel Rana added that law enforcers had been trying to arrest him for several days but initially received information that he was staying abroad.

title: ‘AL men instructed doctors to kill injured protesters’
body: A prosecution witness yesterday told the International Crimes Tribunal-1 that then ruling Awami League activists had threatened doctors at Dhaka hospital, instructing them to kill injured protesters of the July uprising by administering injections. “AL men told doctors at Mugda Hospital, ‘They are still alive despite being shot. Kill them by pushing injections.’ I was admitted there alongside several others with bullet wounds,” witness Md Ruhul Amin, 55, told the tribunal while testifying as the sixth prosecution witness in a crimes against humanity case over the killing of 28 people in Rampura on July 18-19 in 2024. Ruhul said following the intimidation, doctors had to release him from the hospital on July 20, 2024, a day after he was admitted with a bullet wound below his waist. He also said after he returned home in Dhaka’s Meradia, several AL activists went and threatened him and asked him to leave the area since he had been shot. “My son-in-law assured me not to leave,” he added. Two former BGB officers -- Lt Col Mohammad Redowanul Islam and Maj Rafat Bin Alam Moon -- and two former police officers -- then additional deputy commissioner of Khilgaon Md Rashedul Islam and then officer-in-charge of Rampura Police Station Md Moshior Rahman -- are accused in the case. Redowanul and Rafat are in custody, while Rashedul and Moshior are absconding. Recounting the incident, Ruhul said he went to Meradia kitchen market on July 19 to observe the student protest when BGB personnel, police, and AL men began firing at protesters. “I saw several people die and many others collapse on the road,” he said, adding that a bullet pierced through his body below the waist as he tried to flee. After he collapsed on the road, locals took him to Mugda Hospital. Ruhul sought punishment for the accused. Another prosecution witness, Saifur Rahman, also testified yesterday and said he saw several BGB members firing at protesters on Avenue Road. Later, while visiting two nearby hospitals, he saw the bodies of seven to eight victims and at least 20-25 injured people.

title: 8-year-old girl found beheaded
body: An eight-year-old girl was found beheaded in her neighbour’s home in Dhaka’s Pallabi yesterday. The victim, Ramisa Akter, was a second-grade student at Popular Model High School. Her body was found in the sublet room of Sohel Rana, 32, a rickshaw mechanic, who was detained later in the evening. The horrific murder left the victim’s family, relatives, and neighbours devastated and enraged. Mostak Sarker, deputy commissioner of Mirpur Division Police, said Sohel went into hiding but was detained from Narayanganj’s Fatullah around 7:00pm. Sohel, a sublet tenant, was living in a room of a flat with his wife Swapna, while two other families occupied the remaining rooms. The other tenants were outside when the incident occurred. Police and family members suspect that the detainee lured the child into his room, raped her, and then killed her when she screamed. The incident took place in a second-floor flat opposite the victim’s in Block B of Section 11 in Pallabi. When the child’s mother Parveen Begum, who was in her bedroom while her children were having breakfast and were about to get ready for school, saw that Ramisa was not in the flat around 10:30am, she began looking for her. The father was already out for work by then. “I suddenly heard my daughter screaming and rushed outside searching for her. Near Sohel’s flat, I found one of her sandals. I kept banging on the door again and again, but nobody opened it. They killed my daughter so brutally.” Hearing the Parveen’s screams, other residents of the building rushed to the flat and repeatedly knocked on the door, but no one responded. After breaking down the door, Parveen and the others found Swapna, 26, standing in the common area of the flat and then discovered the girl’s body hidden under the bed in Sohel and Swapna’s room. The child’s severed head was found inside a bucket in the toilet, said the victim’s uncle, AKM Nazrul Islam. He added that Sohel cut through the flat’s window grille to escape. “His wife was not opening the door when we knocked, to help him escape.” The body was sent to Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital for autopsy. Hasan Basir, officer-in-charge of Pallabi Police Station, said Swapna was also taken into custody on suspicion of being an accomplice. He added that police believe the child was raped before being murdered. “However, that can only be determined after autopsy.” Members of the Criminal Investigation Department and other agencies visited the scene and collected evidence. Md Faruk Mia, manager of a garage on the ground floor of the building, said Sohel occasionally worked for him repairing rickshaws and was addicted to yaba. Visiting the scene, this correspondent found the alley in front of the house filled with stunned and grief-stricken neighbours, many standing in silence, unable to comprehend the brutality of the killing. Some women were seen holding Parveen as she broke down. The victim’s sister, Raisa Akter, 10, said she and Ramisa had breakfast together minutes before the murder. “I went to my uncle’s house nearby when Ramisa was still eating breakfast. She was supposed to get ready for school after that,” said Raisa, shell-shocked after losing her only sister. Ride-sharing driver Masud Parvez Roni said he rented a room in the flat to Sohel for Tk 5,000 two months ago, while his brother and sister-in-law lived in another room. “My wife went to our village home two months ago, and I was outside working as a ride-sharing driver. At the time of the murder, my brother and his wife had also gone out for work.” Saiful Islam, headmaster of Popular Model High School, said Ramisa was a very meritorious student and never missed classes. She had ranked first in her class for the last two consecutive years. “We came to know about the tragic killing just minutes before her class started and visited the scene.” He added that teachers and students of the school were expected to form a human chain in front of the victim’s house this morning, demanding exemplary punishment for those responsible. At a press briefing at the Pallabi Police Station around 10:15pm, SN Md Nazrul Islam, additional commissioner for crime and operations of Dhaka Metropolitan Police, said police went to the scene immediately after receiving information about the killing, recovered the body and sent it to hospital. “We suspect that something may have happened to the child in the bathroom [of Sohel’s room]. Swabs have been collected and sent to the CID. Details will be known after investigation. “Sohel tried to dismember the body to conceal the crime but could not complete it as the child’s mother and neighbours began knocking on the door.” He added that Swapna, during primary interrogation, claimed she had taken sleeping pills and was unconscious when the incident occurred. “This claim will be verified upon investigation.” According to a press release, police also recovered the knife allegedly used in the killing, along with other evidence. Nazrul said police, during a database check, found that Sohel was earlier accused in a case under the Anti-Terrorism Act in Natore. Meanwhile, Emdadul Haque, inspector (investigation) of Pallabi Police Station, told The Daily Star that filing of a case was under process. No case had been registered till the filing of this report at around 1:40am.

title: 15 judges removed from Supreme Court Secretariat
body: The government has removed 15 lower court judges who were serving as officials of the Supreme Court Secretariat and attached them to the law ministry, effectively suspending the Secretariat’s functions. A gazette notification issued on Tuesday gave retrospective effect to the attachment of the judges from April 10, meaning their removal from the Secretariat and reassignment to the ministry took effect on that date. Among the 15 judges, 10 -- including Sheikh Ashfaqur Rahman, who was serving as senior secretary of the Secretariat -- are district and sessions judges. The remaining five are additional district and sessions judges, joint district judges, and senior assistant judges. The Secretariat was established under the Supreme Court Secretariat Ordinance, 2025, issued by the Dr Muhammad Yunus-led interim government on November 30 last year. Then Chief Justice Syed Refaat Ahmed inaugurated the Secretariat on December 10, aiming to bring the judiciary under Supreme Court control and strengthen judicial independence.

title: Murders we write
body: The final episode of the hit American crime drama television series "Murder, She Wrote" aired on May 19, 1996. I grew up watching the show, along with a myriad other fictional detectives. For a child watching it was less about homicide than hermeneutics. Sherlock Holmes arrived first, all Victorian acuity and moral chill. Poirot followed, immaculate in his vanity and precision. Feluda and Byomkesh Bakshi brought a closer cultural familiarity, detectives who spoke in tones that felt like home yet carried the austerity of logic sharpened against chaos. CID, CSI, Castle and the rest came later, each adding another layer to the architecture of forensic imagination. In "Murder, She Wrote", the protagonist Jessica Fletcher, writer turned amateur sleuth, embodied a strange promise -- that narrative intelligence might still impose order on human rupture. That belief, naive as it may seem in retrospect, was formative. It suggested that even violence could be read, parsed, and ultimately understood. The world, through such stories, appeared decipherable. The dead were narrative anchors; the living, puzzle-solvers. It is a different setting entirely when working in a newsroom. Here, the stories are not puzzles waiting for elegant resolution. They arrive both announced, invited and also unannounced, uncurated. Some are procedural, others bureaucratic, many are unbearable in their rawness. This week, in particular, has felt like ledger of deaths. The rhythm is disquietingly uniform. A dismembered body found in Dhaka's Manda. Skull and bone fragments unearthed in Mohammadpur, Dhaka. A labourer beaten to death over unpaid wages in Netrokona. A crab fisherman shot dead. A hijra individual burned to death in Cumilla. An eight-year-old child beheaded in Dhaka's Pallabi. Each line of copy is meant to be edited, shaped, made fit for publication. Yet, each carries residues that resist to be “restructured”. The act of editing and filing news is often imagined as mechanical precision, line edits, fact checks, headlines sharpened into clarity. Yet the material itself resists detachment. It seeps into consciousness through repetition -- dismemberment reported in one paragraph, a beheading in another, a body found in fragments elsewhere, a pregnant woman killed, a child murdered. There is a particular psychological dissonance in this which begins to feel disturbingly recursive, as though society is stuck replaying its own moral collapse in slightly altered variations. What begins to emerge, almost imperceptibly, is a taxonomy of violence that feels both statistical and scarring. The brutality is not always spectacular; sometimes it is banal, which is perhaps worse. It is precisely this normalisation that makes it so corrosive. One begins to notice how easily language adapts itself to horror. “Hacked to death” becomes a standard phrase, stripped of its original terror through repetition. “Body recovered” acquires bureaucratic neutrality. Even dismemberment, once a word that should arrest thought, risks becoming typographical routine. This is the quiet violence of newsroom work -- not only reporting death, but learning, against instinct, how to speak it fluently. And yet, there is another layer beneath this accumulation of incidents that demands acknowledgement rather than avoidance. These are not isolated aberrations. They are symptoms of fraying civic trust, of disputes resolved through physical assertion rather than institutional recourse, of economic precarity metastasising into desperation, of domestic hierarchies turning lethal, of substance networks entangling in cycles of suspicion and retaliation. Behind every headline lies a life not reducible to narrative convenience. Perhaps that is the most difficult editorial lesson of all -- that not every story is meant to be solved; some are only meant to be witnessed, recorded, and carried forward with a kind of reluctant clarity that neither numbs nor absolves. What does it do to a society when murder is no longer a puzzle, but a pattern it has learned to live with?

title: Man hacked to death for protesting drug abuse in Narayanganj
body: A man was hacked to death by a group of local youths on the bank of the Shitalakhya river in Narayanganj’s Bandar upazila this afternoon, a day after he protested their drug abuse. The victim, Md Jewel Hossain, 42, was of Shantinagar area in the upazila, police said. The incident took place around 12:00pm in the government housing project area of Modonganj, said Golam Mukter Ashraf Uddin, officer-in-charge of Bandar Police Station. The OC also said Jewel worked for a person who had leased a sand-extraction operation on the Shitalakkhya river in the Modonganj area. On Monday afternoon, Jewel and one of his friends had an argument with several local young men after he protested their drug abuse. “Following the incident, the youths returned to the area today and hacked him with sharp weapons,” the OC said. Critically injured, Jewel was taken to Bandar Upazila Health Complex, where doctors declared him dead, he added. The body was later sent to Narayanganj General Hospital for autopsy. The OC said police have already detained two suspects -- Akash and Ashik -- and were working to arrest the others involved. No case had been filed in connection with the incident as of 6:00pm, the police official added.

title: 'Killed for gold earrings': Chapainawabganj private tutor's body found in sack
body: Police recovered the body of a private tutor found in a sack from a house in Chapainawabganj municipality this morning. The victim, Mariam Begum, 55, was from Ujjalpara in the municipality’s Rajarampur area, said police. Chapainawabganj Superintendent of Police Gautam Kumar Biswas said police detained a homeowner and his wife over the incident from the Namo Shankarbati area, along with a goldsmith. The couple are Md Rubel, 35, and his wife Sumi Begum, 30, of the same area. According to police, the body was recovered from the detainees' house this morning. Primary inquest report showed injury marks on the victim’s head and lips, and signs that the victim's ears were torn off. The victim’s brother, Mostafizur Rahman, said Mariam used to provide private tuition to several students in the area. She taught a girl of class 5 at the house from where her body was recovered. Mostafizur said his sister left home on Monday morning to tutor students. She last spoke to her husband around 12:00pm that day and told him over the phone that she would return home shortly. However, she could not be contacted afterwards, he added. He further alleged that when the family went to the police station at night to file a general diary over her disappearance, police only noted down her name and address but did not accept the GD. Superintendent of Police Gautam Kumar Biswas said police recovered a pair of gold earrings that had allegedly been torn from the victim’s ears. He said one of the detainees, Sumi Begum, confessed that she sold the earrings to a local jewellery shop for Tk 12,000 on Monday afternoon. The goldsmith has also been detained for questioning, he added. Police primarily suspect that Sumi Begum murdered Mariam for her gold earrings, the SP said, adding that the process of filing a murder case is underway. Police sent the body to the morgue of the 250-bed district hospital for autopsy.

title: Pallabi child murder suspect arrested
body: The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) this evening arrested the prime suspect in the killing and beheading of a eight‑year‑old girl in Pallabi. The accused, Sohel, 32, was detained by a team from Mirpur Division Police in Narayanganj's Fatullah around 7:00pm. Confirming the arrest, Deputy Commissioner (Mirpur Division) of Dhaka Metropolitan Police Mostak Sarkar told The Daily Star that Sohel had gone into hiding after the murder. The victim, Ramisa Akhter, a class‑two student, lived with her family in an apartment in Pallabi’s Section 11, and was killed around 10:30am today, said Hasan Basir, officer-in-charge of Pallabi Police Station.

title: Mahi murder prime accused arrested while allegedly trying to flee to India
body: Rab has arrested Guruma Zahir, the prime accused in the murder case of Enamul Haque Shishir, alias Mahi, 27, while they were allegedly trying to flee to India through the Satkhira border. Mithun Kumar Kundu, assistant director of Rab-11 Cumilla, at a press briefing today said, Zahir was held during a raid in the Bhomra Land Port area of Satkhira on Monday night. Burichang Police Station Officer-in-Charge Lutfor Rahman said Zahir had fled to Geneva Camp in Dhaka’s Mohammadpur after the case was filed. Zahir later attempted to cross into India through the Satkhira border area. According to the first information report, Zahir, 46, and their associates allegedly tied Mahi’s hands and feet in front of their akhra (common house) in Cumilla’s Burichang Uttar Bazar on May 13. They then allegedly poured kerosene on Mahi and set them on fire. Local residents rescued Mahi and first took them to Cumilla Medical College Hospital. Mahi was later transferred to the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery in Dhaka for advanced treatment. Mahi died on May 17 while undergoing treatment in the intensive care unit. The same afternoon, the victim’s father, Kamrul Haque Sohag, filed a murder case with Burichang Police Station. The case named three accused -- Guruma Zahir, Dhopa Dola Hijra and Kamal -- along with seven to eight unidentified individuals. Police have already arrested Dola Hijra in connection with the incident. Human rights activists, local residents, and family members have alleged that police were initially reluctant to register the case. Speaking to The Daily Star, OC Lutfor Rahman said authorities had received allegations that Guruma Zahir had been operating a yaba trafficking and extortion network from a house built on government land in Burichang Uttar Bazar for around one and a half years. Mahi was also reportedly associated with the group. A team from district police is now bringing the suspect back to Cumilla for further legal proceedings, the OC added.

title: Eight-year-old girl beheaded in Dhaka's Pallabi; neighbour under suspicion
body: An eight-year-old girl was killed and beheaded allegedly by a neighbour in Dhaka’s Pallabi area this morning, police said. The victim, Ramisa Akhter -- a class two student -- lived with her family in an apartment in Pallabi's Section 11. Her father's name is Abdul Hannan Molla. The incident took place around 10:30am, said Hasan Basir, officer-in-charge of Pallabi Police Station. Quoting neighbours, Emdadul Haque, inspector (investigation) of the same police station, said preliminary allegations have been made against Sohel, 32, a tenant of a neighbouring flat, in connection with the killing.
