However, the motive behind the incident could not be confirmed immediately. The Criminal Investigation Department and other agencies visited the scene after being informed of the incident. Police officials said efforts are underway to arrest the suspect, adding that a woman has been detained for interrogation.

title: Couple, infant found dead in Madaripur
body: Police recovered the bodies of a couple and their eight-month-old child from a relative’s house in Madaripur town early yesterday. The deceased were identified as Chinmoy Das, 25; his wife, Isha Das, 19; and their infant child, police said. Police initially suspect that Chinmoy killed his wife before taking his own life and that of his child, said Madaripur Superintendent of Police Md Habibur Rahman. According to police and locals, Chinmoy was a resident of the Kalagachia area of Madaripur Sadar upazila. The family arrived at the house of Misti Baroi, the wife of Italy expatriate Jatin Baroi and a relative of Chinmoy, in the Amirabad area of the district headquarters on Sunday afternoon. Misti, a resident of the Satpara area of Muksudpur upazila in Gopalganj, had been living in a rented house in Amirabad for around three years. When Chinmoy arrived there, he introduced himself to locals as Misti’s cousin. “They [Chinmoy and his family] arrived at Misti’s residence around 5:00pm, after which Misti went out shopping,” said Madaripur Police Station Officer-in-Charge Abul Kalam Azad, quoting Misti. When she returned home around 9:30pm, she found the room where Chinmoy and his family were staying locked. She knocked on the door repeatedly but received no response. At one stage, Misti called the national emergency service 999, the OC said. On information, police rushed to the spot and recovered the bodies around 1:30am yesterday, said SP Habibur. “Police found the body of a man hanging with a child, estimated to be between six and eight months old. Beside the bed lay the body of his wife, Isha. “Misti has been detained for questioning. At this stage, we cannot confirm whether it was murder or suicide. We hope to determine the exact cause after investigation and post-mortem.” He added that Isha’s body had a catheter attached. The bodies were kept at Madaripur Sadar Hospital morgue for autopsy. Contacted last night, the hospital’s Resident Medical Officer Akhil Sarker said, “The autopsies have been completed. Rope marks were found around the necks of all three bodies.” Meanwhile, police yesterday filed an unnatural death case in this regard, the OC added.

title: Sundarbans: Crab fisherman shot dead, fellows storm forest offices
body: A crab fisherman was shot dead in the Sundarbans yesterday morning, sparking outrage that led hundreds of fishermen to vandalise two forest offices in Satkhira. The victim, Aminur Rahman, 45, of Gabura union in Shyamnagar upazila, had entered the forest with a valid pass four days earlier, according to fellow fishermen. One of the fishermen, Ramzan Ali Gazi, said, “At around 10:00am, while preparing to catch crabs at Shatamukhi canal, members of the Forest Department’s Khulna Smart Patrol Team called us over. When we delayed responding to their call, patrol team members opened fire. Aminur was hit and died instantly.” Gabura union chairman Masudul Alam said fishermen accused the patrol team of “unjust firing” and demanded action. Around 4:30pm, several hundred fishermen armed with sticks stormed the Burigoalini Station office, vandalising furniture, before moving on to the Satkhira Range office. Forester Sheikh Faruk Ahmed, 55; forest guards Mezbaul Islam, 45, Azadul Islam, 42, and Faizur Rahman, 40; and volunteer Ekhlasur Rahman, 27, were injured. Locals said the rampage lasted 30-40 minutes before police, BGB, coastguards and river police arrived to restore order. The injured staffers were admitted to the local health complex. The Forest Department said the matter is under investigation. “Joint forces are operating in the Sundarbans against bandits. We are checking whose bullets caused the death,” said Burigoalini Station Officer Fazlur Rahman. Regarding the attack on the forest office, Fazlur said they had informed police, BGB, coastguards and river police anticipating an attack. “None of them arrived before the incident. After the attack took place, members of the BGB, river police and coastguards reached the spot,” he added.

title: Man held over attempted rape after infant snatched from mother’s lap in Netrokona
body: A man was arrested today in a case filed over the attempted rape of a woman after snatching and throwing her one-month-old infant from her lap in Netrokona’s Madan upazila. The accused Abdur Rouf, 55, was detained from his house in Netrokona’s Madan this morning and later shown arrested after the victim filed a case of attempted rape with Madan Police Station in the evening, confirmed Officer-in-Charge (OC) Md Tariqul Islam. The incident happened around 8:00pm on Sunday in a secluded area near Kaijani Gudaraghat near the border of Kendua and Madan upazilas. According to the case statement, the victim’s husband had divorced her on Friday. On Sunday, she was waiting for a bus to return to her family home in Sirajganj. Around 5:30pm, she was sitting in front of Rouf’s shop in the Tambulipara area of Kendua to board a vehicle. After hearing about her plight, Rouf offered to let her stay at his house with his wife for the night. On the pretext of taking her to his home, Rouf took her to a deserted farmland. He pulled out a ramda (machete), and threatening to kill the child, he tried to rape the victim, the case statement added. At one point, he snatched the infant from her lap, and threw the baby during the rape attempt. After some struggle, the woman managed to free herself and ran to nearby Sajuria Bazar, where she alerted locals who then rushed to the scene and rescued the infant alive and unharmed from the field near a riverbank. By then, Rouf had fled the scene. Being informed, police went to the scene, rescued the victim, and sent her to the Kendua Upazila Health Complex for treatment. As the incident took place under the jurisdiction of Madan police, the victim was handed over to Madan Police Station where she filed a case this evening. The OC said police arrested Abdur Rouf in the morning and were interrogating him, adding that further legal proceedings were underway.

title: Human skull, bone fragments recovered in Dhaka's Mohammadpur
body: Police recovered a human skull and several bone fragments from the Kaderabad Housing area in Dhaka's Mohammadpur this afternoon. The remains were found between 3:00pm and 5:00pm near an electric pole in Block C of Road No. 2 in Kaderabad Housing, Mohammadpur Police Station Sub-Inspector Akhtaruzzaman Sarkar told The Daily Star. The officer said police were alerted through the national emergency helpline 999 and later recovered the remains from the spot. He said the recovered remains have been kept under police custody, while legal procedures and investigations are underway.

title: Saudi returnee killed, body dismembered in Dhaka: Woman, daughter arrested
body: Rapid Action Battalion (Rab-3) arrested a woman and her teenage daughter in connection with the killing of a Bangladeshi man who lived in Saudi Arabia and was visiting the country, and the subsequent dismemberment of his body in Dhaka’s Mugda area. Helena Akter, 40, and her 13-year-old daughter were arrested during a raid at a rented house in Mugda's Manda around 11:45pm last night, Rab-3 Deputy Director Saidur Rahman said at a press briefing this afternoon at the Rab-3 office in Dhaka. He said the victim, Mokarram Mia, 37, was killed on May 14 and his body was later cut into multiple pieces and dumped in several locations in the area. Citing preliminary interrogation, Rab said the incident stemmed from the victim’s relationship with Taslima Akter, also known as Hasna, whose husband is also a Bangladeshi living in Saudi Arabia and from the same area. The Rab official said Mokarram and Taslima developed a romantic relationship while they were both living in Saudi Arabia and later stayed in touch through social media. The victim allegedly sent her more than Tk 5 lakh during the relationship. On May 13, Mokarram returned to Bangladesh without informing his family and went to Manda to meet Taslima, where he stayed at the rented house of her friend Helena Akter. Rab said Mokarram, Taslima, Helena and Helena’s two daughters stayed in the same room at the house. Rab said Mokarram demanded repayment of the money he had sent Taslima and threatened to leak her private photos and videos after she refused to marry him. Rab said Taslima and Helena later planned to kill him. On May 14 morning, they mixed sleeping pills into his drink. When he became unconscious, Helena attempted to suffocate him with a pillow, but he resisted, leading to a struggle. Subsequently, Helena struck him with a sharp weapon, while her daughter hit him on the head with a hammer. Taslima also attacked him, after which the group ensured his death, Rab said. The body was then taken to a bathroom, cleaned, and later cut into eight pieces. The parts were kept in plastic bags before being dumped in multiple locations, including near the building’s garbage area. The victim’s head was later recovered about one kilometre away, based on information provided by Helena, the Rab official added. On May 15, they arranged a party on the rooftop of the building, and the next day, Taslima left the place with her son, according to Rab. Yesterday, locals alerted police after noticing a foul smell. Police recovered the body pieces and sent them to Dhaka Medical College for an autopsy. The victim was later identified through fingerprint and NID verification. Rab said legal proceedings are in process and efforts are underway to arrest Taslima.

title: Man killed, wife injured as assailants enter Khulna house through tunnel
body: A drug trader was murdered after a group of assailants allegedly entered his house through digging a tunnel beneath the floor in Koyra upazila of Khulna early today. The deceased was identified as Bhabotosh Mridha, 45, a local medicine trader and owner of a pharmacy at Gilabari Bazar in Maheshwaripur union. His wife was also injured in the attack took place around 2:00am in Maheshwaripur village under Maheshwaripur union. According to local Union Parishad member Mizanur Rahman Khokon, the attackers entered the mud house by digging a tunnel through the floor. Sensing movement inside the house, Bhabotosh woke up and tried to resist them. At that point, the assailants allegedly attacked him with sharp weapons, leaving him critically injured. His wife was also attacked and injured while trying to save him, the UP member said. Locals rescued the couple and rushed them to Koyra Upazila Health Complex, where the on-duty doctor declared Bhabotosh dead. His wife is currently undergoing treatment and is said to be out of danger. Khokon demanded a proper investigation into the incident and immediate arrest of those involved. Confirming the incident, Koyra Police Station Officer-in-Charge Md Shah Alam said no signs of theft were found inside the house. "We suspect the murder may have been committed for reasons other than burglary,” he said. Police sent the body to Khulna Medical College Hospital for autopsy and are trying to identify and arrest those responsible, the OC added. Meanwhile, local civil society member Nitish Sana said incidents of burglary via tunnel cutting have increased in Koyra over the past several months. He alleged that organised gangs were spraying sedative substances to render residents unconscious before carrying out thefts, causing panic among locals.

title: Couple, eight-month-old child found dead in Madaripur
body: Police recovered the bodies of a couple and their eight-month-old child from a relative’s house in Madaripur Sadar upazila early today. The deceased were identified as Chinmoy Das, his wife Isha Das, and their infant child, said Madaripur Superintendent of Police Md Habibur Rahman. Speaking to The Daily Star, the police superintendent said the bodies were recovered around 1:00am from the Amirabad area of the upazila. “Upon arrival, we saw the body of a man named Chinmoy hanging with a child, estimated to be between six and eight months old, tied with a rope around the neck. Beside the bed lay the body of his wife, Isha.” Police initially suspect that Chinmoy killed his wife before taking his own life along with the child, the SP said. According to police, the incident took place at the house of Misti Baroi, wife of Italy expatriate Jatin Baroi and a relative of Chinmoy. “We are questioning Misti and have brought her to the police station for interrogation,” Habibur said. “At this stage, we cannot confirm whether it was murder or suicide. The room where the bodies were found had been locked from the inside. We hope to determine the exact cause after investigation and post-mortem examinations,” he added. The bodies have been kept at Madaripur Sadar Hospital morgue for autopsy. The SP also said Isha had been physically ill and had a catheter attached for urinary complications. Police and local sources said Misti had been living for around three years in a rented house in Amirabad. Chinmoy arrived at the house yesterday with his wife and child, introducing himself to locals as Misti’s cousin from the Satpara area of Muksudpur upazila in Gopalganj.

title: CCC official served show-cause notice over alleged Tk 8cr deal for DC post
body: A show-cause notice was served on SM Sarwar Kamal, chief revenue officer of Chattogram City Corporation (CCC), over allegations of signing a Tk 8 crore financial agreement to secure the post of deputy commissioner (DC) of Cumilla. The Local Government Division (LGD) under the Ministry of Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives served the notice, issued on May 13 signed by Deputy Secretary Robiul Islam. The notice said the preliminary evidence gathered from various sources suggested that Sarwar Kamal had signed an agreement and deed of commitment with the Chattogram divisional commissioner, promising Tk 8 crore in exchange for the posting. The ministry directed the official, who holds the rank of deputy secretary, to submit a written explanation within three working days as to why departmental action should not be taken against him over the allegations. Although the deadline expired yesterday, it could not be confirmed officially whether he had submitted his response. Repeated attempts to contact Sarwar Kamal by phone went unanswered, and his mobile phone was later found switched off. However, speaking to the media earlier, he strongly denied the allegations, claiming his signature had been forged to create fake documents. “I have not entered into any such agreement,” he said. Sarwar Kamal was posted to the CCC on deputation in January last year. The post of deputy commissioner is equivalent in rank to his current administrative position. CCC Mayor Dr Shahadat Hossain also did not respond to phone calls seeking comment on the matter. Meanwhile, Chattogram Divisional Commissioner Md Ziauddin expressed shock over allegations linking him to the reported deal. “I am utterly surprised and shocked,” Ziauddin told The Daily Star. “A divisional commissioner plays absolutely no role in the appointment or transfer of deputy commissioners. My name has been dragged into this maliciously. This seems to be a deep-rooted conspiracy,” he added. He also questioned the ministry’s procedure in handling the matter. “In such sensitive cases, a show-cause notice is typically issued only after a preliminary investigation finds some truth to the allegations. I asked ministry officials why they issued such a letter without conducting any prior inquiry,” he said. However, the divisional commissioner clarified that the ministry had not issued any formal show-cause notice to him over the matter.

title: Tonu murder: PBI confirms fourth person's involvement following DNA test
body: The involvement of a fourth individual has been confirmed in the murder of Sohagi Jahan Tonu, a history department student of Cumilla Victoria Government College and a theatre activist. According to DNA test results conducted on samples collected from Tonu’s clothes, investigators found the blood of another person in addition to the semen of three men. With this latest finding, samples found on Tonu’s clothing now indicate the involvement of four individuals. Md Tarikul Islam, inspector of the Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) in Dhaka and the investigation officer of the case, confirmed the matter last night. Speaking to reporters, he said, “A few months ago, I sent a letter to the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) seeking details about the samples collected from Tonu’s clothes. About a month ago, I was informed that, besides the semen of three men, traces of another person’s blood were also found in the samples. This raises the number of suspects to four.” He added that although the presence of semen from three men became public in May 2017, information about the fourth individual has surfaced only now. On March 20, 2016, Tonu went to a house inside Cumilla Cantonment for private tutoring and never returned home. Later, her body was recovered from bushes near the powerhouse area inside the cantonment. Initially, it was believed that she had been raped and murdered. The following day, her father, retired Cantonment Board office assistant Yar Hossain, filed a murder case against unidentified persons with Kotwali Model Police Station in Cumilla.Two post-mortem reports submitted that year by the forensic department of Cumilla Medical College Hospital failed to determine the exact cause of death. The DNA report was considered the final hope in the investigation. In May 2017, CID informed the media that DNA tests on samples collected from Tonu’s clothes had found semen from three men. In addition, from October 2017, CID teams interrogated three individuals in Dhaka Cantonment whom Tonu’s mother had suspected. However, CID did not disclose their identities to the media at that time. On April 6 this year, PBI inspector Tarikul sought court permission to cross-check the DNA profiles of three suspects through a progress report submitted to the court. Later, on April 22, retired army personnel Hafizur Rahman was shown arrested in the case in Dhaka. When PBI sought remand, a Cumilla court granted a three-day remand for interrogation. After questioning, Hafizur Rahman was sent to Cumilla Central Jail by court order, where he currently remains. Before being produced before the court, his DNA samples were collected at the CID forensic laboratory in Dhaka. Those samples will be matched with the evidence collected from Tonu’s clothes. Tonu’s father identified Hafizur Rahman as a former senior warrant officer who had served in the Signal Unit at Cumilla Cantonment at the time of the murder.

title: Attack on shrine: 3 Jamaat men placed on remand
body: A Dhaka court yesterday placed three suspects on a two-day remand each in a case filed over the attack on the Hazrat Shah Ali shrine in the capital’s Mirpur late Thursday. Md Azam, 26, Sheikh Md Sazzadul Haque Rasel, 38, and Arman Dewan, 29, are members of Jamaat-e-Islami’s associate bodies and front organisations, according to the police’s remand plea. They were arrested from the Uttar Bishil area under Shah Ali Police Station on Saturday night. When the case investigating officer produced them before a Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate’s court, seeking a three-day remand, the court granted two days. Following the arrests, Dhaka-14 MP and Jamaat leader Mir Ahmed Bin Quasem alleged that law enforcers are unfairly targeting his election campaigners. Speaking to reporters at the International Crimes Tribunal premises yesterday afternoon, he said two of the arrestees had campaigned for the Jamaat-led alliance in the election and were not seen in the video footage of the incident. “We’re seeing a sweeping tendency to blame the opposition, which is a legacy of the fallen fascists,” the lawmaker said. On Friday, he claimed the shrine attack was an “anti-narcotics drive” by police, denying his party’s involvement. Meanwhile, speakers at a solidarity rally yesterday heavily criticised law enforcers and political parties, alleging that the attack was carried out with police indulgence and political backing. “Sadhu Guru Bhakta O Olee-Aulia Ashekan Parishad” and “Bhab-baithaki” jointly organised the demonstration on the shrine premises. Addressing the gathering, National Citizen Party leader Sarwar Tushar alleged that the administration and police essentially orchestrated the attack. “Police claimed that anti-narcotics drives are frequently conducted here. BNP carried it out once, and then Jamaat did. Have you given the BNP and Jamaat the licence to conduct anti-narcotics drives?” Tushar questioned. Alleging a unified political stance, he added, “There is an all-party consensus, including the BNP and Jamaat, against shrines.” Mohammad Romel, an organiser of the programme, echoed this sentiment. He claimed a local BNP leader first instigated the violence before Jamaat activists carried out the attack, terming the attackers “agents of foreign intelligence”. Poet and intellectual Farhad Mazhar said the so-called “Touhidi Janata”, by attacking dissenting views, is essentially accelerating the Indian BJP’s politics of “eradicating Islam”. Noting allegations of Jamaat’s involvement, Mazhar said, “We have said before that any immoral acts taking place at shrines must be stopped. But now it is being proved that you [Jamaat] are the ones committing these bad deeds, only to shift the blame onto the shrines.” Amar Bangladesh Party Chairman Mojibur Rahman Monju criticised the political apathy towards shrine security, noting that leaders only visit shrines during elections. Dismissing the pretext of anti-drug drives, Monju challenged authorities to start anti-narcotics drives from the Secretariat and parliament instead. Adding to this, Romel termed the anti-drug drives at shrines an act of “oppression against the poor”, questioning why such religious zeal is never directed at affluent areas like luxury hotels and bars. A group of unidentified people had attacked and vandalised the shrine during a weekly urs late Thursday, leaving several devotees injured. A case was filed on Saturday by a devotee named Reshmi Begum, 40, against nine named individuals and 100-150 unidentified members of Jamaat-e-Islami and its affiliated organisations over the shrine attack.

title: Woman dies trying to shield son from attack by ‘BNP men’
body: The victim, Syada Begum, 55, was the wife of Sabbir Ahmed of the Taipalong area. According to locals, slogans -- “Joy Bangla, Joytu Sheikh Hasina” -- were written on a wall of Taipalong Madrasa several days ago. Following the incident, local BNP leaders filed a complaint with Ukhiya police against several activists of the banned Chhatra League and Awami League, political activities of which are prohibited. On Saturday evening, Chhatra Dal activist Jisan Sikdar made a Facebook post regarding the graffiti. Mohammad Yunus, known to locals as a BCL activist, reacted to the post with the emoji. Witnesses said several BNP and Chhatra Dal activists later assaulted Yunus. SM Imran, a local NGO worker and a friend of Yunus, was also allegedly beaten up when he tried to save Yunus around 8:00pm. Family members alleged that Syada rushed to the spot after hearing of the attack on her son Imran. While trying to save him, she was pushed and shoved to the ground and fell ill at the scene. She was later taken to the Ukhiya Upazila Health Complex, where doctors declared her dead. Imran alleged that local ward BNP President Abdur Rahim and his son Akash, BNP leader Mizan Sikdar and his son Jisan Sikdar, Sramik Dal leader Saiful Sikdar, and 10 to 12 others attacked them without provocation. “My mother came running to save me. They grabbed her by the neck and pushed her, and she fell to the ground. She was taken to hospital immediately, where doctors declared her dead,” he said. “We are not involved in politics. I want justice for my mother,” he added. At a press conference later that night, BNP leader Mizan Sikdar and his son Jisan Sikdar claimed that they were not present at the scene during the incident. Jisan said, “We are being accused out of political vengeance. We want a fair investigation by the administration.” Talking to The Daily Star, Sarwar Jahan Chowdhury, president of Ukhiya upazila unit BNP, said they were getting conflicting statements about the incident. “Police are investigating it. If the post-mortem report and police investigation confirm the allegation of assault and it is proved that any BNP members were involved in the woman’s death, organisational action will be taken against them,” he said. ANM Sajedur Rahman, superintendent of Cox’s Bazar police, said the woman was pushed during the altercation and later died after being taken to hospital. Mujibur Rahman, officer-in-charge of Ukhiya Police Station, said no visible injury marks were found on the woman’s body in the inquest report, adding that no case was filed till the filing of this report around 8:00pm yesterday. Meanwhile, police who had detained Yunus freed him yesterday. Sabuktagin Sohel, resident medical officer of Cox’s Bazar Sadar Hospital, said the exact cause of death would be known after the autopsy report is released.

title: Hijra person dies after being torched
body: A hijra individual who was set on fire allegedly by her “guruma” (community leader) in Cumilla’s Burichang died under treatment yesterday. The victim, Enamul Haque Shishir alias Mahi, had suffered severe burn injuries and died in the ICU of the National Burn Institute in Dhaka, said police. Mahi’s father, Kamrul Haque Shohag, filed a murder case with Burichang Police Station naming three, including Dhopa Hijra Dola and Guruma Zahir, and seven-eight unidentified accused, confirmed Burichang Police Station Officer-in-Charge Lutfor Rahman. He said police have arrested Dola alias Dhopa Hijra in connection with the killing. According to the case statement, between 9:00pm and 10:00pm on Wednesday (May 13), Guruma Zahir and associates allegedly tied up Mahi in front of their akhra (community home) at Burichang Uttar Bazar. They then poured kerosene and set Mahi on fire. Locals rescued Mahi and first took them to Cumilla Medical College Hospital. Later, Mahi was transferred to National Burn Institute in Dhaka where they died under treatment. The family alleged that local police were initially unwilling to accept the case. Burichang Police Station OC told The Daily Star that Guruma Zahir had allegedly been operating a yaba trade and extortion racket from the akhra built on government land in Burichang Uttar Bazar for nearly one and a half years. Mahi was reportedly a member of that group.

title: Netrokona labourer beaten to death after son demands unpaid wages
body: A 62-year-old day labourer was allegedly beaten to death Sunday over a dispute regarding unpaid paddy harvesting wages in Kalmakanda upazila of Netrokona. The victim was identified as Babul Mia, son of late Sonahar Mia of Borodol Poschim Para village in Kharnoi union. According to family members and locals, Babul and his son, Md Sirajul Islam, harvested paddy in a field belonging to Habibur Rahman, around 20 to 25 days ago. Habibur allegedly owed them around Tk 15,000 in wages. Kalmakanda Police Station Officer-in-Charge Abul Hashem said Sirajul demanded the due payment around 8:30am today, which led to an argument between the two sides. At one stage, Habibur and his associates allegedly attacked Sirajul and started beating him. Seeing the incident from a distance, Babul rushed to save his son, but he too came under attack, the OC said. The attackers allegedly punched and beat Babul repeatedly, leaving him critically injured. Locals rescued Babul and took him to Kalmakanda Upazila Health Complex, where doctors declared him dead, the police official added. Shouvik Shrabon Dutta, a physician at the health complex, said Babul had died before being brought to the hospital. Police later recovered the body and sent it to Netrokona Modern Sadar Hospital morgue for autopsy, said the OC. “The matter is being investigated seriously. Those involved will be brought to justice and legal action will be taken against them,” Abul Hashem said. Habibur has been in hiding since the incident, while the process of filing a case is underway, police said
