title: Beheaded body found in basement of house in Dhaka’s Mugda
body: Police today recovered the beheaded body of an unidentified man -- cut into seven pieces and wrapped in polythene -- from the basement of a house in Mugda's Manda area in Dhaka. The body was recovered around 1:30pm from the basement of a house on Abdul Karim Road, said Md Jalal Uddin, inspector (investigation) of Mugda Police Station. Acting on information from locals, a police team recovered the decomposed body and sent it to the morgue of Dhaka Medical College Hospital for autopsy, he said. “The body was cut into seven pieces, and the head was missing,” the inspector said. According to the preliminary investigation, the victim was likely murdered elsewhere around six days ago. The body was then chopped into pieces, wrapped in polythene, and abandoned in the building’s basement, the inspector added. Police are reviewing CCTV footage from the surrounding area. The Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) could not identify the victim through fingerprint analysis at the scene, Inspector Jalal said.

title: CID arrests 8 over online gambling, laundering crores abroad
body: Criminal Investigation Department (CID) today said it has arrested eight members of an organised online gambling syndicate, including its alleged mastermind, on charges of running illegal betting platforms and laundering crores of taka abroad through cryptocurrency and digital hundi. According to CID officials, the syndicate transacted between Tk 1.80 crore and Tk 2 crore daily over the past six months through various international and local gambling platforms. The arrests were disclosed by Additional Inspector General of Police Mosleh Uddin Ahmed at a press briefing at CID headquarters in Malibagh today. The arrestees were identified as Md Ashraf Uddin Ahmed, 32; Sajib Chakraborty, 29; Md Ashraful Islam, 40; Md Jashim Uddin, 36; Tayyab Khan, 26; Soumik Saha, 28; Md Kamruzzaman, 36; and Abdur Rahman, 47. Mosleh said the group had long operated gambling platforms, with gamblers transferring money through mobile financial services, as well as bank accounts and crypto wallets. “The illegally earned money was later laundered abroad through cryptocurrency and digital hundi,” he explained. CID’s Cyber Monitoring Cell detected several groups during routine surveillance, leading to a case filed at Paltan Model Police Station under the Cyber Security Ordinance. On May 6, a CID team arrested four suspects in Mymensingh and Kishoreganj. Based on their information, another drive was conducted today in Narsingdi’s Palash area and Dhaka’s Dhanmondi, resulting in four more arrests. Mosleh added that CID’s Cyber Intelligence and Risk Management Unit has been conducting regular monitoring to curb online gambling. Since the beginning of May, CID has identified 116 gambling websites and forwarded them to the Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulatory Commission (BTRC) for shutdown. Additionally, 879 mobile financial service accounts and 43 bank accounts linked to illegal transactions have been sent to the Bangladesh Financial Intelligence Unit (BFIU).

title: Measles vaccine: HC writ seeks probe into Yunus, ex-advisers’ roles
body: A Supreme Court lawyer today filed a writ petition with the High Court seeking its directive to the government to investigate the role of former chief adviser of the interim government Dr Muhammad Yunus and other advisers over the measles vaccine issue. Barrister M Ashraful Islam submitted the petition as a public interest litigation, also praying for a court order barring 24 people -- including Dr Yunus and all former advisers -- from leaving the country until the inquiry is completed. The cabinet secretary, health secretary, home secretary, public administration secretary, director general of the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), and other relevant government officials have been named as respondents in the petition. Barrister Ashraful told The Daily Star that an “ill-motivated criminal act” was committed by transferring the measles vaccination system from state control to the private sector under the interim government, and that the matter requires investigation. He said the hearing on the petition is scheduled to be held at 2pm tomorrow.

title: No legal bar to Ivy’s release as SC upholds HC bail orders
body: The Supreme Court today upheld the High Court orders that on April 30 granted ad-interim bail to Selina Hayat Ivy, former mayor of Narayanganj City Corporation, in two separate murder cases filed in connection with the July uprising. Chamber Judge of the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court Justice Md Rezaul Haque passed “no order” on two separate petitions filed by the state seeking a stay on the HC orders granting bail. Following the apex court chamber judge’s orders, there is no legal bar to Ivy being released from jail, as the Appellate Division recently upheld her HC bail in 10 other cases, SM Hridoy Rahman, a lawyer for Ivy, told The Daily Star. Senior lawyer Md Motaher Hossain Sazu and lawyers SM Siddiqur Rahman and Hridoy Rahman appeared for Ivy, while Deputy Attorney General Syeda Shajia Sharmin represented the state during the hearing of the petitions today. On April 30, the HC granted ad-interim bail to Ivy and also issued two separate rules asking the government to explain why she should not be granted permanent bail in the cases. The cases were filed with Siddhirganj Police Station in Narayanganj over the killings of Selim Mondal and Abdus Salam during the July uprising in 2024. Ivy was shown arrested in the cases immediately after the High Court granted her bail in five other cases on February 26 this year. The former Narayanganj mayor was arrested on May 9 last year in connection with the murder of RMG worker Minarul and was later shown arrested in nine other criminal cases. The High Court granted bail to Ivy in all 10 cases on November 9 last year and February 26 this year following separate bail petitions filed on her behalf.

title: Abu Sayed killing: Convicted former BRUR VC sent to jail
body: Former vice-chancellor of Begum Rokeya University, Rangpur Md Hasibur Rashid, who was convicted in the Abu Sayed killing case, was sent to jail by the International Crimes Tribunal-2. The tribunal passed the order after he was produced before it today. Earlier, the tribunal sentenced Hasibur Rashid to 10 years' imprisonment on charges of command responsibility in the killing of Abu Sayed. Police arrested Hasibur Rashid from a relative’s house on Shaheed Salim Ullah Road in Mohammadpur around 8:30pm yesterday. Following the court proceedings, Prosecutor Faruk Ahmed told journalists that the convict was produced before the tribunal today and the court ordered his transfer to central jail based on the conviction warrant. “He has already been convicted and from today he will start serving his sentence,” the prosecutor said. Faruk further said the verdict in the case was pronounced on April 9, but the certified copy of the full judgment has not yet been published. “The convicted person will be able to file an appeal after receiving the certified copy of the judgment,” he added. Abu Sayed, a student of BRUR was killed in police firing during the July uprising.

title: Five-month pregnant woman killed allegedly by husband in Satkhira
body: A five-month pregnant woman was allegedly murdered by her husband in Satkhira last night. The deceased, Tashlima Khatun, 38, was from Uttar Bohera village in Satkhira Sadar upazila. The accused, Saddam Hossain, 42, of Lakshmidari village, has been absconding since the incident, said Masudur Rahman, officer-in-charge of Satkhira Police Station. The incident took place around 11:30pm in the Lakshmidari area under Bhomra union of the upazila, the OC said. According to family members and local sources, the couple had a 13-year-old daughter and a nine-year-old son. The victim’s daughter, Sadia Khatun, alleged that her father frequently quarrelled with her mother and threatened to kill her. Sadia said Saddam allegedly called Tashlima into a room around 11:00pm. A short while later, she heard groaning sounds. When she tried to enter the room, she found the door locked from the outside. The victim’s father, Nuruzzaman, alleged that Saddam regularly assaulted his daughter over dowry demands. He said he received a phone call around 11:30pm informing him that his daughter had been killed after her throat was slit. He demanded justice and the maximum punishment for the accused. Police initially suspect the murder may have stemmed from a family dispute, the OC said. The body was sent to Satkhira Sadar Hospital morgue for an autopsy.

title: Man held over rape, murder of 10-year-old girl in Munshiganj
body: Police arrested a man on Saturday afternoon over the rape and murder of a 10-year-old girl in Sirajdikhan upazila of Munshiganj, just hours after the incident. The suspect, Raja Mia, 35, is the step-maternal uncle of the victim, according to police and family members. Locals said Raja, son of the late Akbar Hawladar from Morelganj upazila in Khulna, had been living with the victim’s family for nearly six years. The victim was the daughter of a migrant worker residing in Qatar, they added. Abdul Hannan, officer-in-charge (OC) of Sirajdikhan Police Station, said family members found the child lying unconscious on a bed inside their house around 4:00pm and informed police. A police team later recovered the body and sent it to Munshiganj General Hospital morgue for autopsy. Police detained Raja Mia from the spot due to his suspicious behaviour, said the OC. OC Hannan added that initial investigation suggests the child was strangled to death after being raped. During primary interrogation, the detainee admitted to committing the crime. Meanwhile, the victim’s mother, Nazma Begum, filed a case against Raja with the police station in this regard on Saturday night.

title: Two held, two more sued over rape of minors in 4 dists
body: The body of a 10-year-old girl was recovered from her residence in Munshiganj’s Sirajdikhan upazila yesterday. The child, identified as Achia Akhter, was the daughter of Anwar Hossain, an expatriate worker. Police suspect she was murdered after being raped by one of her relatives. Family members found the child lying unconscious on a bed inside the house yesterday afternoon. On information, police rushed to the house and recovered the body, said Abdul Hannan, officer-in-charge of Sirajdikhan Police Station. “It is initially suspected that the child was strangled to death after rape. The body has been sent to the Munshiganj General Hospital morgue for an autopsy.” The victim’s mother filed a murder case last night, after which the victim’s relative and prime suspect, Raja Mia, 35, was detained, said the police officer, adding that the detainee confessed to killing the girl during primary interrogation. Meanwhile, in Jashore, a man was arrested early yesterday on charges of raping a mentally challenged minor, who later gave birth to a baby. The arrestee, Abdur Rahman, 60, is a resident of Jhikorgacha upazila in the district. The victim’s father said he first noticed unusual physical changes in his daughter around seven months ago. He later filed a complaint with Jhikorgacha Police Station, after which the accused went into hiding. On March 18, the girl gave birth through a C-section, and her father submitted another written complaint. Later, police arrested the accused from a house in Jashore town, said Shahjalal Alam, officer-in-charge of Sharsha Police Station. In Faridpur, a man was sued over the rape a third-grader on Wednesday. The accused, Jihad Khan, 30, of Faridpur Sadar upazila, is the father of two. The victim is now undergoing treatment at the One-Stop Crisis Centre of Faridpur Medical College Hospital. Her family members said the girl was returning home from school around 2:00pm on Wednesday. On the way, Jihad intercepted her, forcibly took her to a nearby cornfield, and raped her. As the girl fell sick after returning home, her family rushed her to hospital. Later that night, the girl’s mother filed a rape case with Faridpur Kotwali Police Station against Jihad, said Azmir Hossain, additional superintendent of police in Faridpur. The accused, however, went into hiding after the incident. “We are trying to arrest him,” the Addl SP said. In Patuakhali, a man was accused of raping a 17-year-old HSC examinee at her home in Patuakhali’s Kalapara upazila on Friday night. The accused, Md Rabbi, 30, is from the same village as the victim, said police. The victim’s family filed a case against him with Kalapara Police Station on Saturday. Police are trying to apprehend the accused, who has been absconding since the incident, said Md Nazrul Islam, officer-in-charge of Kalapara Police Station. (Our Correspondents from Munshiganj, Benapole, Faridpur and Patuakhali contributed to the report.)

title: Abu Sayed killing: Former VC of Begum Rokeya univ arrested
body: Former Vice-Chancellor of Begum Rokeya University Hasibur Rashid, a fugitive convict in the Abu Sayed killing case during the July uprising, was arrested in Dhaka yesterday. He was arrested from a relative’s house on Salimullah Road in the Mohammadpur area around 8:30pm, said Mohammadpur Officer-in-Charge Mesbah Uddin. The International Crimes Tribunal (ICT)-2 on April 9 convicted and sentenced two former policemen to death and 28 others to various jail terms in a crimes-against-humanity case filed over the killing of Begum Rokeya University, Rangpur (BRUR) student Abu Sayed during the July mass uprising. The two death-row convicts are former assistant sub-inspector (ASI) Amir Hossain and former constable Sujan Chandra Roy. Abu Sayed was killed on July 16, 2024, near his campus during the quota reform movement. A video showing him being shot by police while standing with his arms outstretched in defiance went viral, turning him into an icon of resistance and a symbol for the movement. His killing is widely seen as a turning point that galvanised the mass uprising, which culminated in the fall of the Awami League regime on August 5, 2024. Those sentenced to life imprisonment are Md Arifuzzaman, former assistant commissioner (Kotwali zone) of Rangpur Metropolitan Police (RMP); Rabiul Islam, former officer-in-charge of Tajhat Police Station; and sub-inspector Bibhuti Bhusan Roy, who was in charge of the university’s police outpost. They were also given an additional 10 years’ rigorous imprisonment on other counts. Former BRUR VC Rashid and former RMP commissioner Md Moniruzzaman were sentenced to 10 years’ imprisonment on charges of command responsibility.

title: Police seek public help to identify JU attempted rape suspect
body: Law enforcement agencies are working to identify a man captured in CCTV footage in connection with the attempted rape and attack on a female student at Jahangirnagar University. Authorities have sought public assistance in identifying the suspect, who was seen in surveillance footage linked to the incident. In an urgent public awareness notice posted on the verified Facebook page of Bangladesh Police this afternoon, officials requested anyone with information regarding the individual’s identity, whereabouts or any related details to assist law enforcement agencies. The statement assured that the identities of informants would be kept strictly confidential. It also said credible information leading to the suspect’s identification could be rewarded. The notice asked the public to contact 01320-089305 with any information related to the case. Female students staged an overnight sit-in in front of the JU vice-chancellor’s residence, demanding the resignation of Proctor Prof AKM Rashidul Alam as the suspect remains at large. They later moved and locked the proctor’s office.

title: Elderly man arrested over rape of mentally challenged teen in Jashore
body: A man has been arrested on charges of raping a mentally challenged teenage girl in Jhikorgacha upazila of Jashore, police said today. The accused, Abdur Rahman, 60, was arrested from a house in Jashore town early today, said Shahjalal Alam, officer-in-charge of Sharsha Police Station. According to police and the victim’s family, the teenage girl later gave birth to a baby boy following the alleged rape at Azampur village under Shimulia union of the upazila. Abdur Rahman, a father of four, is originally from the Daulatpur area of Khulna. He had long been living in Azampur with his wife and children. His extended family, including his daughter, son-in-law and grandchildren, also live in the area. The victim’s father said he first noticed unusual physical changes in his daughter around seven months ago. “At that point, there was little I could do. After discussing the matter with family members and neighbours, I filed a complaint with the police. But no action was taken then,” he alleged. On March 18, the girl was admitted to a private clinic in Navaron Bazar, where she later gave birth to a baby boy through a caesarean section. The victim’s father later submitted a written complaint to Jhikorgacha Police Station. After learning about the birth of the child on May 14, police visited the victim’s home. “Necessary legal steps have been taken in this regard,” said the OC.

title: Worker found dead in Old Dhaka warehouse
body: Police recovered the body of a 40-year-old worker from a plastic waste factory warehouse in Old Dhaka’s Kamalbagh area on Friday, suspecting the incident to be a murder. The deceased was identified as Yunus Mia, a resident of Kashipur area in Barishal. The body was recovered from the second floor of the factory in Chawkbazar around 1:30pm, said Kawsar, a sub-inspector of Chawkbazar Police Station. Yunus lived in the warehouse with several other workers, the police official said. Law enforcers rushed to the spot after receiving information from a local resident around noon. Upon arrival, they found the warehouse door open and Yunus lying dead inside, the SI added. Mahfuzar Rahaman, assistant commissioner of the Chawkbazar zone, told The Daily Star that injury marks were found on Yunus Mia’s head. Primarily, it appears to be a murder involving multiple people. The body was sent to the Sir Salimullah Medical College (Mitford) morgue for an autopsy.

title: Man hacked to death in Barishal, two arrested
body: A man was hacked to death early yesterday in Barishal city in an incident police say may be linked to drug-related disputes and prior enmity. The attack occurred around 2:45am in Palashpur. The deceased, identified as Jasim Sikder Babu, was reportedly attacked by a group of seven to eight armed men, led by an accused named Madhu Mia, in front of a building. Locals rushed Babu to Sher-e-Bangla Medical College Hospital, where doctors declared him dead. Residents said they heard screams late at night and found him lying in a pool of blood. Barishal Metropolitan Police Assistant Commissioner Pabitra Kumar Halder said the murder appears connected to narcotics-related disputes. Two suspects, Siam and Shahid, have been arrested, and police are conducting drives to apprehend the remaining accused. Following the killing, local residents staged protests demanding the arrest of all involved and exemplary punishment for the perpetrators.

title: Mirpur Shah Ali’s shrine attacked
body: A group of unidentified people attacked and vandalised the shrine of Sufi saint Hazrat Shah Ali in the capital’s Mirpur during a weekly urs late Thursday, leaving several people injured. Eyewitnesses and police insiders alleged that activists of Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami and its student wing Islami Chhatra Shibir carried out the attack. Devotees from Dhaka and different parts of the country have long attended the weekly gathering at the centuries-old Mazar Sharif of Sultanul Aulia Hazrat Shah Ali Baghdadi (RA) in Mirpur Section 1. Local lawmaker and Jamaat leader Mir Ahmed Bin Quasem denied his party’s involvement in the attack, claiming the incident was part of an “anti-narcotics drive” by police. Police, however, rejected the claim. Both the lawmaker and police alleged that drugs are regularly consumed and sold in the area, a trade Mir Ahmed claimed peaks on Thursday nights. The incident took place around 11:00pm. Witnesses said more than 1,000 people were in and around the shrine at the time, many engaged in devotional music performances. Witness Mohammad Hridoy, 30, said he was listening to Sufi music under a banyan tree on the shrine premises when the attackers stormed in. “One of them started beating me severely with a stick. He kicked my bag and asked, ‘What are you doing here?’” Hridoy told The Daily Star. He said the attackers beat devotees, searched bags, and chased people out during the hour-long mayhem. Shiuli Begum, 28, who often attends the urs seeking alms, had brought along her two-month-old child on Thursday. “I was standing with my baby in my arms while people were running around in panic. Suddenly, a boy came and struck me four times with a cane. I never thought they would hit me too,” she said. Several witnesses, including shop owners in front of the shrine, said on condition of anonymity that the attackers were activists of Jamaat and Shibir. “We have primary information that many of the attackers were from Shibir,” said a senior police officer of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police’s Mirpur Division, requesting anonymity. Several witnesses also alleged that police vehicles were stationed in front of the shrine gate during the attack, but officers remained inactive. Asked about the allegation, DMP Assistant Commissioner of Darus Salam Zone Imdad Hossain Bipul said, “A patrol car might have been there, or they might have gone to the spot after hearing about the incident.” Regarding the lack of legal action even a day later, he said, “We haven’t received any complaint yet. Action will be taken once we get one.” When asked about allegations of Jamaat-Shibir involvement, Mir Ahmed told The Daily Star, “The allegations are baseless. It was an anti-narcotics drive by the police,” he said. After being told that footage and witness accounts did not show police involvement, the lawmaker said both plainclothes and uniformed police had been present, claiming that the Mirpur deputy commissioner had already briefed the media about the anti-drug drive. However, Deputy Commissioner of DMP’s Mirpur Division Md Mostak Sarker told this newspaper that he had made no such statement. Police were not conducting any anti-narcotics drive at the time, he said. In a statement yesterday, Md Ataur Rahman Sarker, member of Jamaat’s central majlis-e-shura and publicity-media secretary of its Dhaka City North unit, claimed that law enforcers conducted an anti-narcotics drive at the shrine from 10:00pm to midnight on Thursday. Denying the party’s involvement in the incident, he said, “It has become an inherent habit of some political parties and media outlets to spread propaganda by dragging Jamaat into everything, which is highly unfortunate.” Since August 5, 2024, Sufi shrines across the country have increasingly come under mob attacks. According to a January study by Maqam: Center for Sufi Heritage, at least 97 shrines were attacked between August 5, 2024, and December 31, 2025, leaving at least three people dead and 468 injured.

title: Rape Attempt: Protests resume at JU
body: Jahangirnagar University students have resumed protests demanding the arrest of a suspect in the attempted rape and murder of a female student on the campus. The protesters, including female students, started gathering in front of the vice-chancellor’s residence around 1:30am today after the end of a 48-hour ultimatum to meet their demands, which also include swift completion of legal proceedings over the incident. While announcing the ultimatum around 2:30am on Thursday, the protesters said the university’s proctorial body must resign if the deadline was not met. Lamisha Jaman, one of the organisers of the protests, told The Daily Star that the students agreed in a discussion that the proctorial body must bear the responsibility for the failure to protect students. Earlier yesterday evening, in response to their demand for stronger measures to prevent harassment on campus, the university administration announced a 14-point set of security measures. At the outset of a press conference to announce the measures at the Senate Hall, Proctor Prof AKM Rashidul Alam strongly condemned the attack on the female student, and reiterated the administration’s commitment to ensuring the swift arrest of the accused and exemplary punishment. The female student was attacked by an outsider on the night of May 12 while returning to her residential hall. The authorities published images of the suspect, an outsider, from CCTV footage. The measures to prevent such incidents were decided at an emergency meeting chaired by Vice-Chancellor Prof Mohammad Kamrul Ahsan on Thursday. The measures include forming a quick response team to handle security emergencies, launching a dedicated hotline for urgent complaints, and making it mandatory for teachers, students, officers, and staff to carry identity cards at all times. The administration also plans to tighten control over the entry of outsiders onto the campus. Identity cards will also be compulsory for construction workers, university employees, and shopkeepers operating on campus. Authorities further decided to remove mobile vendors and create a database containing information on all relevant personnel. To strengthen security, the university will deploy additional guards at key entry points, recruit more security personnel, and seek approval from the University Grants Commission for the deployment of 100 more Ansar members, the proctor said. He added that adequate lighting and CCTV cameras would be installed in vulnerable areas across the campus. The administration has also initiated steps to repair damaged sections of the boundary wall and close unauthorised entry points. The university further announced that the tin-shed extension building of Al Beruni Hall would be declared abandoned and demolished. Officials also said a permanent committee would be formed to prevent bullying, cyberbullying, and ragging on campus. Acting Registrar Prof ABM Azizur Rahman and assistant proctors were also present at the press conference.

title: Man accused in terrorism case held in Moulvibazar
body: Police have arrested a dismissed member of the army from Barlekha upazila of Moulvibazar in connection with a case filed under the Anti-Terrorism Act in Dhaka. The arrestee, Rahed Hossain Mahed, 23, of Bishwanath upazila in Sylhet, was among two individuals named in a recent Police Headquarters alert over possible attacks on key installations. Barlekha Police Station Officer-in-Charge Moniruzzaman Khan told our Moulvibazar correspondent that Mahed had been in hiding since the issuance of the alert and was allegedly attempting to cross into India through the border area. The Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime (CTTC) unit of Dhaka Metropolitan Police arrested Rahed in the Islamnagar area under Shahbazpur Union in a late-night operation around 1:50am early yesterday, DMP said in a press release. According to the statement, Mahed was allegedly influenced by the ideology of the banned militant outfit “Dawlatul Islam Neo JMB”. Police said the case against Mahed was filed with Sher-e-Bangla Nagar Police Station on February 2. According to law enforcement sources, the operation followed an intelligence alert issued by Police Headquarters on April 23, warning of possible extremist attacks targeting key installations and security personnel, including the Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban. Police Headquarters had circulated the alert across law enforcement agencies, identifying Mahed and Rakib Hasan alias Ubaida Al Usama of Savar as suspected planners. It described them as “extremely risky for the overall security of the country”.

title: Suspected Rohingya robber shot dead by rival gang in Teknaf camp, APBn says
body: A suspected Rohingya robber was shot dead by rivals at a refugee camp in Cox’s Bazar's Teknaf, Armed Police Battalion (APBn) said. The deceased was identified as Hasan Ahmed alias Kala Hasan, 45, of Block-H at Nayapara Rohingya Camp. Mohammad Kawshar Sikder, 16 APBn commanding officer, said the members of “Saddam Group”, an armed Rohingya gang, entered the camp area last night around 8:00pm and opened fire targeting Hasan over previous enmity. Hasan sustained bullet injuries on the right side of his chest and was critically wounded. After the shooting, members of the group fled to a nearby hilly area, he added. Local Rohingyas rescued Hasan and took him to the GK Hospital adjacent to the camp. Physicians there referred him to Teknaf Upazila Health Complex for advanced treatment, but he died on the way due to excessive bleeding, said the official. A team from Nayapara APBn later reached the spot and brought the situation under control before informing Teknaf Model Police Station. Police later prepared an inquest report and sent the body for an autopsy. The APBn official said Hasan had previously been an active member of a robber group led by one Zakir. Several cases, including three arms cases, two attempted robbery cases and two abduction cases, are currently pending against him in court. He said drives are underway to collect information from the scene, identify those involved and arrest the perpetrators.

title: Indian couple held for illegal entry through Moulvibazar border
body: Members of the Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) detained an Indian couple while they were allegedly entering Bangladesh illegally through the Borlekha border in Moulvibazar early today. The detainees are Kamrul Ahmed, 32, and his wife Husna Begum Laskar, 24, of Lala village in Hailakandi district of India, said Borlekha Police Station Officer-in-Charge Md Moniruzzaman Khan. The couple were detained from the Gandhai area of Dakshin Shahbazpur union in Borlekha upazila around 6:30am. Indian identity cards and mobile phones were recovered from them at the time, according to the BGB. During initial questioning, the couple admitted to crossing the border illegally and entering Bangladesh. The OC said on Friday afternoon that the BGB handed over the detainees to police. "We are verifying their identities and processing the matter. A case is being filed by the BGB, and necessary legal action will be taken accordingly," he said. BGB-52 Beanibazar Battalion Commander Lt Col Md Ataur Rahman said after preliminary investigation it was found that they are Indian citizens. They were held while trying to enter Bangladesh. The filing of a case is underway.

title: Terrorism case accused arrested in Moulvibazar
body: Police have arrested Md Rahed Hossain Mahed, 23, a dismissed member of the Bangladesh Army and an alleged member of the banned extremist outfit “Maktabah Al Himmah Addawatul Islamiyah”, during a special operation in Baralekha upazila of Moulvibazar. The arrest was made at around 2:30pm yesterday in the remote Shaitghari area of Bobarthal, following a nearly 12-hour operation conducted by Baralekha Police Station, said Barlekha Police Station Officer-in-Charge Moniruzzaman Khan. Mahed had been in hiding since the issuance of the red alert and was attempting to flee to India via the border region, he claimed. The officer added that the suspect was later identified as an accused in a case under investigation by the Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime (CTTC) unit of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police. The case was filed with Shahbagh Police Station on February 2 under the Anti-Terrorism Act. Following a request from the CTTC unit, the suspect was handed over to CTTC officials at around 11:30pm for further legal proceedings. Moniruzzaman Khan also said the suspect had provided “important information” regarding his alleged involvement in extremist activities during initial interrogation. According to law enforcement, the operation was initiated after an intelligence alert issued by Police Headquarters on April 23, warning of potential extremist attacks targeting key state installations and security personnel, including the Jatiya Sangsad.

title: Four brothers from Ctg found dead inside car in Oman
body: Four Bangladeshi brothers from Chattogram were found dead inside a parked car in Oman on Wednesday, just days before two of them were due to return home for their weddings. The deaths have cast a pall of grief over their village in Rangunia, where wedding preparations had nearly been completed and relatives were waiting to welcome them home. The deceased were identified as Rashedul Islam, Shahedul Islam, Sirajul Islam, and Shahidul Islam of Bandarajar Para in Lalanagar union. According to family members and community representatives, the brothers had gone shopping on Tuesday evening for the upcoming weddings of the two unmarried siblings. They were scheduled to return to Bangladesh today. Two of the brothers were already married. Rashedul Islam leaves behind two children. Their elderly mother, who has long been suffering from age-related illnesses, has not yet been informed of the tragedy due to fears over her fragile health. “They had gone out to shop for the wedding of their two unmarried brothers. Everything was ready, and they were supposed to return home within days. But all their plans were shattered overnight,” neighbour Md Alauddin told The Daily Star. Another brother, Mohammad Enam, a schoolteacher living in Bangladesh, was too devastated to speak at length. “I’m not in a condition to talk to the media right now,” he said briefly. Mohammad Yasin Chowdhury, president of Chattogram Samity in Oman, said the four brothers had travelled from Barka to Muladdah for shopping. During the journey, one of them sent a WhatsApp voice message to a relative in Barka sometime after 8:00pm, saying they were feeling seriously ill and unable to get out of the vehicle. He also shared their location. However, when the relative tried to contact them about 10 minutes later, there was no response, Yasin said. Around 1:00am, two Bangladeshi expatriates spotted the four men lying unconscious inside the vehicle and alerted police. Law enforcers later arrived and recovered the bodies from the car, which was parked in front of a clinic in Muladdah around 2:00am local time. “It is believed they drove to the clinic seeking treatment after they started feeling unwell,” Yasin added. The bodies have been kept at a local hospital for autopsy under the supervision of Omani police. Rafiul Islam, labour counsellor at the Bangladesh Embassy in Oman, said Omani authorities suspect the deaths may have been caused by an air-conditioning malfunction or a buildup of toxic gas inside the vehicle. “However, the matter remains under investigation by the Omani authorities,” he said. He added that the Bangladesh mission is coordinating closely with the authorities and the victims’ family members to complete the necessary formalities and ensure the earliest possible repatriation of the bodies. Back in Lalanagar, the tragedy has left the entire neighbourhood stunned. Md Amir Hossain, a member of Lalanagar Union Parishad, said grieving neighbours have been crowding the family home since news of the deaths spread. “We are all shocked by this tragedy,” he said.

title: Murder of five: Prime suspect may have jumped off Padma Bridge
body: The main suspect in the murder of five members of a family in Gazipur’s Kapasia upazila may have jumped off the Padma Bridge in an apparent attempt to die by suicide, police said yesterday. Md Sharif Uddin, superintendent of police of Gazipur, disclosed the information at a press briefing at his office in the afternoon. The bodies of five family members, including three children, were found with their throats slit at their home in Kapasia on the morning of May 9. The victims were identified as Sharmin, 35; her three daughters -- Mim, 16, Maria, 8, and Faria, 2 -- and her brother, Rasul, 22. Sharmin’s husband, Forkan Mollah, had been in hiding since the incident. The SP said police recovered Forkan’s mobile phone on May 11 from a truck driver’s helper in Meherpur Sadar upazila during the investigation. The helper told police that he had found the phone beside the railing at the midpoint of the Padma Bridge and kept it with him. After reviewing CCTV footage from the area, investigators saw a man wearing a white shirt and black pants get out of a white private car at 6:42am on May 11. He stood beside the bridge railing for a few minutes before jumping into the river. Investigators suspect the man was Forkan, the SP said. He added that investigators believe Forkan jumped from the bridge with the intention of taking his own life after allegedly carrying out the pre-planned murders. “Relevant police stations adjacent to Padma Bridge have been alerted through wireless messages in this regard. The investigation is ongoing.” However, Sharif Uddin did not say whether the suspect’s body had been recovered. According to the family, Forkan, originally from Meri Gopinathpur village in Gopalganj Sadar upazila, worked as a private car driver and married Sharmin around 20 years ago. The family had been living in a rented house in Rautkona village for nearly a year.

title: ICT verdict in case against Inu expected any day
body: The International Crimes Tribunal-2 may deliver its verdict any day in the crimes against humanity case against former minister Hasanul Haq Inu, as arguments by both the prosecution and the defence concluded yesterday. The tribunal did not fix a date for the verdict, saying it would be announced later after the judgment is prepared. Chief Prosecututor Md Aminul Islam concluded his arguments yesterday. Speaking to journalists after the hearing, he said the prosecution had clearly proved the charges against Inu through evidence and sought appropriate punishment. “Inu, as a politician, took a position against patriotic people and was involved in various plans to suppress them. He even assisted in carrying out oppression by branding people as militants.” Inu is the sole accused in the case filed over the killing of six people in Kushtia during the July uprising. Speaking to reporters, defence counsel Sifat Mahmud said the prosecution had failed to prove the charges against Inu. “Rather, we proved that Inu had no involvement in the killing of 1,400 people, including six in Kushtia, and the injury of more than 25,000 others,” he said, adding that he believed Inu would be acquitted. The tribunal took cognisance of the charges on September 25, 2025, after the prosecution submitted formal charges based on the investigation agency’s probe report. On November 2, 2025, the tribunal framed eight charges of crimes against humanity against Inu and ordered the trial to begin. Ten prosecution witnesses, including the investigation officer, testified in the case.

title: 11-yr-old Reshmi dies a week after being caught in ‘revenge’ shooting
body: After battling for her life for a week, the 11-year-old girl who was struck by a stray bullet during a targeted shooting in Chattogram’s Raufabad area died yesterday morning. The victim, Reshmi Akthar, a class four student, died at 9:45am at the ICU of Chittagong Medical College Hospital, the hospital’s Director Brig Gen Taslim Uddin confirmed. Doctors said she succumbed to multi-organ failure. Reshmi had been on life support since the night of May 7, when masked gunmen allegedly opened fire in the area. She was out buying betel leaf for her mother when a bullet struck her in the left eye and lodged in her brain, according to family members and police. Police said the shooting was linked to what investigators described as a “revenge killing” targeting 24-year-old Hasan Raju, who was also killed in the incident. Investigators said the attack was carried out in retaliation for the earlier murder of a man named Nasir Uddin in Raozan. While Reshmi was undergoing treatment, police arrested six suspects, including the prime accused, Syedul Karim. Investigators also recovered a foreign-made pistol and clothes allegedly worn during the attack. Abdul Karim, officer-in-charge of Bayezid Bostami Police Station, said police had sought a seven-day remand for the arrested suspects. The hearing on the remand petition has not yet been held. Reshmi’s father, Riaz Ahmed, demanded justice for his daughter. “She was just a child with no connection to any conflict. I want exemplary punishment for those responsible.” Her elder brother, Faisal Ahmed, said, “The terrorists were firing at a man in our alley. They didn’t care who was walking by. Our home is now filled with a silence that hurts more than the gunfire.”

title: Shapla Chattar case: Dipu Moni, 2 journos shown arrested
body: International Crimes Tribunal-1 yesterday sent former minister Dipu Moni, former managing director of Ekattor TV Mozammel Babu, and ex-chief correspondent of the channel Farzana Rupa to jail. They were shown arrested in a crimes-against-humanity case filed in connection with the May 5, 2013 Shapla Chattar crackdown on Hefazat-e-Islam activists. In line with an earlier order following petitions filed by the prosecution, the three were produced before the tribunal. According to prosecutors, investigators found preliminary evidence of the accused’s involvement in the incident. The prosecution alleged that Dipu Moni, who was the foreign minister at the time, campaigned internationally by portraying the operation as an action against “unruly people”. Prosecutors also alleged that journalists Babu and Rupa attempted to divert the narrative surrounding the crackdown through their media coverage. ICT Chief Prosecutor Aminul earlier said investigators so far identified 58 deaths linked to the crackdown in four districts.

title: BSF shoots Bangladeshi man dead
body: A Bangladeshi man was killed early yesterday after members of India’s Border Security Force (BSF) opened fire near the Bonchowki border of Hatibandha upazila in Lalmonirhat. The deceased was identified as Khademul Islam, 25, a resident of the Bonchowki border area, said Lt Col Mehedi Imam, the commanding officer of Lalmonirhat BGB15 Battalion. The incident took place in Amjhol area, around 150 yards inside Indian territory, at about 2:00am, he said. Khademul and 10 to 12 others crossed near the barbed-wire fence inside Indian territory late Wednesday night to bring cattle from India, according to Imam. At that time, members of the Paglamari BSF camp under the 78 BSF Battalion in West Bengal’s Cooch Behar district opened fire. “Khademul suffered bullet injuries to his hand, back, and face. His companions quickly brought him back to Bangladesh. He was taken to a private hospital in Rangpur city, where he later died,” the BGB commander said. However, Khademul’s father, Amzad Hossain, said that his son was not involved in cattle smuggling. “My son used to catch fish in local water bodies. He had gone to catch fish near the border. Perhaps someone persuaded him to go near the barbed-wire fence. My son was supposed to return home in the morning,” he said. The BGB had sent a protest letter condemning the incident and invited the BSF to a flag meeting, Imam said. The flag meeting was not held until the filing of the report at 6:00pm yesterday. “BGB members have increased patrols in the border area. They are remaining alert to ensure that no tension arises along the border,” he said. The BGB has strengthened security along 558km of the border in Lalmonirhat and Kurigram districts, said Imam and Kurigram BGB 22 Battalion Commanding Officer Lieutenant Colonel Mohammad Mahbub-Ul-Haque.

title: Four arrested over rape of class 9 student in Chattogram
body: Police have arrested four people, including a teenager, on charges of raping a class nine student and molesting another girl in Chattogram’s Satkania upazila yesterday. The arrestees are Md Rakib, 20; Md Manik Islam, 20; Abdur Rahim, 19; and a 16-year-old boy, said Md Rasel, additional superintendent of police (Detective Branch and Public Relations) of Chattogram District Police. They were sent to jail after the victim’s father filed a case with Satkania Police Station early today. Rasel said two girls, aged 15 and 16, went to visit a farm in Sudarnal area under Sadaha union in Satkania yesterday noon. A group of seven youths forcibly took them to a nearby hill and later gang-raped the 16-year-old girl. The group also molested another girl. “The incident took place between 12:30pm and 3:00pm. Later, the girls informed the matter to the police. Police started a drive and arrested four accused,” he added. The rape victim was sent to the One Stop Crisis Centre of Chittagong Medical College Hospital (CMCH) for medical test. Police are looking for rest of the accused, added the official.

title: Decomposed bodies of woman, child found by pond in Faridpur
body: Police recovered the decomposed bodies of an unidentified woman and a child from the bank of a pond in Faridpur’s Sadar upazila this afternoon. Azmir Hossain, additional superintendent of police (Sadar Circle) in Faridpur, said the identities of the deceased could not be confirmed immediately. One of the victims appeared to be around 35 years old, while the other was a child aged about three. Locals said two women discovered the bodies inside a banana grove beside a pond in the Kalitala area under Char Madhabdia union around 4:30pm after noticing a foul smell. They later informed other residents. Pond owner Ekhlas Molla subsequently informed Faridpur Kotwali Police Station about the incident. Additional SP Azmir Hossain said a team from Faridpur Kotwali Police Station recovered the bodies and sent them to Faridpur Medical College morgue for autopsy. Members of the district police, the Crime Scene Unit of the Criminal Investigation Department (CID), the Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI), and the Detective Branch (DB) were working on the matter, he added.

title: Gazipur family murder suspect may have jumped from Padma Bridge: Police
body: The main suspect in the murder of five members of a family in Gazipur’s Kapasia upazila might have jumped into the river from Padma Bridge in an apparent suicide attempt, police said today. Md Sharif Uddin, superintendent of police (SP) in Gazipur, disclosed the information at a press briefing at his office this afternoon. The bodies of five family members, including three children, were found with their throats slit at their home in Kapasia on the morning of May 9. The victims were identified as Sharmin, 35; her three daughters -- Mim, 16, Maria, 8, and Faria, 2 -- and her brother, Rasul, 22. Sharmin’s husband, Forkan Mollah, had been in hiding since the incident. The SP said police recovered Forkan’s mobile phone on May 11 from a truck driver's helper in Meherpur Sadar upazila during the investigation. The truck driver's helper told police that he had found the phone beside the railing in the middle of Padma Bridge and kept it with him. After reviewing CCTV footage from the bridge, investigators saw a man wearing a white shirt and black pants exit a white private car at 6:42am on May 11. He stood beside the bridge railing for a few minutes before jumping into the Padma river. Investigators suspect the man was Forkan, the SP said. The SP said investigators believe Forkan jumped from the bridge with the intention of taking his own life after allegedly carrying out the pre-planned murders of his wife, children, and brother-in-law. “Relevant police stations adjacent to Padma Bridge have been alerted through wireless messages in this regard. The investigation is ongoing,” SP Sharif Uddin added. However, the SP did not say whether the suspect’s body had been recovered. According to the family, Forkan, originally from Meri Gopinathpur village in Gopalganj Sadar upazila, worked as a private car driver and married Sharmin around 20 years ago. The family had been living in a rented house in Rautkona village for nearly a year.

title: HC again defers verdict on Chinmoy’s bail petitions for three weeks
body: The High Court today again deferred for three weeks the delivery of its verdict on the bail petitions of former ISKCON leader Chandan Kumar Dhar, also known as Chinmoy Krishna Das Brahmachari, in four cases. The bench of Justice KM Zahid Sarwar and Justice Sheikh Abu Taher, which was scheduled to deliver the judgement today, passed the deferment order after Deputy Attorney General Syed Shajia Sharmin sought time to submit additional documents related to the cases. She told the HC bench that the attorney general’s office had prepared the documents, which would be placed before the court later by Additional Attorney General Aneek R Haque, as he is currently out of Dhaka. The HC bench then said it would deliver the verdict after the reopening of the court following its annual vacation. Both the Appellate and High Court divisions of the Supreme Court will go on vacation on May 22 and reopen on June 7, DAG Shajia told The Daily Star. On May 11, the HC deferred until today the delivery of its verdict on Chinmoy’s bail petitions in the four cases after Additional Attorney General Aneek sought time to submit additional documents related to the cases. Chinmoy’s lawyer, Apurba Kumar Bhattacharya, opposed the plea for more time. On May 10, the same HC bench rejected Chinmoy’s bail petition in a case filed with Kotwali Police Station over the killing of lawyer Saiful Islam Alif. Alif was beaten and hacked to death on November 26, 2024, during clashes near the Chattogram court building. According to the defence lawyer, Chinmoy has been accused in eight cases, including murder and sedition. He has already secured bail in three cases from the HC and the lower courts concerned. The Appellate Division of the Supreme Court has, however, stayed a High Court order granting him bail in the sedition case, the lawyer added.

title: Journalist Anis Alamgir secures permanent bail in graft case
body: A Dhaka court today granted permanent bail to senior journalist Anis Alamgir in a case filed over allegations of acquiring assets beyond known sources of income. Judge Md Sabbir Faiz of the Metropolitan Senior Special Judge’s Court in Dhaka passed the order following a petition, court bench assistant Riaz Hossain told The Daily Star. The court also accepted another petition regarding his travel abroad, allowing Anis Alamgir to stay abroad for one month. However, the judge rejected a separate petition seeking exemption from his personal appearance before the court on the scheduled date. On March 11, he was granted bail in the case until today. On January 15, ACC Assistant Director Akhtaruzzaman filed the case under Section 27(1) of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act with the commission’s Integrated Office-1 in Dhaka. On January 28, Anis was shown arrested in the case. On December 14 last year, Anis was picked up from a gym in Dhaka’s Dhanmondi area and taken to the Detective Branch office on Minto Road.

title: Bangladeshi man killed in BSF firing at Lalmonirhat border
body: A Bangladeshi man was killed early today after members of India’s Border Security Force (BSF) opened fire near the Bonchowki border of Hatibandha upazila in Lalmonirhat. The deceased was identified as Khademul Islam, 25, a resident of the Bonchowki border area, said Lieutenant Colonel Mehedi Imam, commanding officer of Lalmonirhat BGB-15 Battalion. The incident took place near sub-pillar No. 6 of the 905 main border pillar in Amjhol area, around 150 yards inside Indian territory at about 2:00am, he said. According to the BGB official, Khademul and 10 to 12 others crossed near the barbed-wire fence inside Indian territory late last night to bring cattle from India. At that time, members of the Paglamari BSF camp under the 78 BSF Battalion in West Bengal’s Cooch Behar district opened fire. “Khademul suffered bullet injuries to his hand, back and face. His companions quickly brought him back to Bangladesh. He was taken to a private hospital in Rangpur city that same night for treatment, where he later died,” the BGB commander said. His family later brought the body home. However, Khademul’s father, Amzad Hossain, claimed that his son was not involved in cattle smuggling. “My son used to catch fish in local water bodies. He had gone to catch fish near the border. Perhaps someone persuaded him to go near the barbed-wire fence. My son was supposed to return home in the morning. He returned, but as a corpse,” he said. Lieutenant Colonel Mehedi Imam said the BGB had sent a protest letter strongly condemning the incident and invited the BSF to hold a flag meeting. “BGB members have increased patrols in the border area. They are remaining alert to ensure that no tension arises along the border,” he added.

title: Election results for Aslam and Sarowar’s constituencies not before June 9, lawyer says
body: The 13th parliamentary election results of Chattogram-4 and Chattogram-2 cannot be published until June 9 as the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court today fixed the date for hearing two appeals filed against the High Court verdicts. The HC earlier had allowed Aslam Chowdhury and Sarowar Alamgir to contest the election from Chattogram-4 and Chattogram-2 constituencies. Subsequently, Aslam and Sarowar contested and won the election held on February 12. An apex court bench headed by Chief Justice Zubayer Rahman Chowdhury today also kept on record two separate petitions filed by Aslam and Sarowar seeking its directive on the Election Commission to publish their election results and to arrange their oath as elected lawmakers in the election. Although Aslam and Sarowar won the elections, results of the two constituencies have been kept withheld in compliance with the apex court orders as the appeals challenging the High Court directives that allowed them to contest the election are still pending before the top court. The appeals were filed by Jamaat-e-Islami candidates Md Anwar Siddique and Muhammad Nurul Amin against the High Court directives bringing allegations against Aslam and Sarowar of being loan defaulters. Following the appeals, the Appellate Division on February 3, directed the EC to allow them to contest the election, but ruled that the final publication of the election results will remain withheld until the disposal of the pending appeals. Later on, Aslam and Sarwar filed two separate petitions with the Appellate Division seeking modification of its February 3 directive and to order the EC to publish their election results and to arrange their oath as elected lawmakers. After a hearing yesterday (Wednesday), a five-member bench of the Appellate Division headed by Chief Justice Zubayer Rahman Chowdhury fixed today for passing orders on the modification petitions of Alam and Sarowar. Today, the top court did not pass any order on the modification petitions but kept those petitions with the records and fixed June 9 for hearing the appeals against the HC directives. Therefore, the EC cannot publish the election results of the two constituencies until June 9, Advocate Mohammad Shishir Manir, the lawyer for Anwar Siddique and Nurul amin, told The Daily Star. Senior lawyers Nihad Kabir and Mustafizur Rahman Khan appeared for Aslam, Senior Advocate Ahsanul Karim argued for Sarowar while Senior lawyer Shishir Manir represented Anwar and Nurul Amin during the hearing yesterday.

title: Man held for raping, impregnating minor daughter
body: Police yesterday arrested a man in Netrokona for allegedly raping his 16-year-old daughter, resulting in her pregnancy. The 48-year-old suspect is a resident of Purbadhala upazila. Earlier in the day, the victim, with the help of local community leaders, filed a rape case against her father at Purbadhala Police Station. Following the complaint, police arrested the accused around 5:30pm. According to the case statement and police sources, the victim’s mother divorced the man seven years ago. The girl is their only child. The victims had been working at a house in Dhaka. About six months ago, she returned to her father’s home. She was raped on multiple occasions then, the case read. She was sent to another house about two months ago for work in Mymensingh, where she found out she was pregnant. Her father brought her back and threatened her not to disclose the matter. Purbadhala Police Station Officer-in-Charge Abdullah Al Mamun told The Daily Star, “A case has been filed. The victim’s medical examination and other necessary legal procedures are underway.”

title: Six Rab men hurt as ‘drug peddlers’ attack
body: A group of 15 to 20 suspected drug peddlers attacked plainclothes members of the Rapid Action Battalion in Nabinagar village of Natore’s Lalpur upazila on Tuesday night. Police said the Rab team had gone to the area to gather intelligence on drug trafficking. Six Rab members were injured in the assault, and one of them was hospitalised. The injured officer, Shahin Hossain, 30, of Rab-5 (Natore camp), was admitted to Lalpur Upazila Health Complex. The five others received first aid. Shafikul Islam, officer-in-charge of Lalpur Police Station, told the media via WhatsApp that the incident occurred around 9:00pm. A six-member Rab-5 intelligence team was operating in plainclothes when they were intercepted near Nabinagar Government Primary School. According to police, the the attackers were led by Sohag Mahamud, 30, son of Fazlur Rahman. They demanded to know the officers’ identities. When the Rab members identified themselves and tried to leave, the group snatched their motorcycle keys, sparking an altercation that led to the assault. Police rushed to the spot, rescued the Rab members, and brought the situation under control. Suspected ringleader Sohag was arrested at the scene and sent to jail through a court yesterday. The Rab later filed a case with Lalpur Police Station. The OC said police drives are underway to arrest the others.

title: Case filed over attempted rape of JU student on campus
body: An attempted rape case was filed yesterday against an unidentified man accused of attacking a female student of Jahangirnagar University on campus the night before. Md Gafrul Hasan Chowdhury, deputy registrar of the university’s security division, filed the case with Ashulia Police Station. The incident took place after 11:00pm on Tuesday near the abandoned Fazilatunnesa Hall and the extended section of Al-Beruni Hall, according to university authorities. Citing the victim, university security officials said she was walking along a campus road when an unidentified man began following her. Upon reaching the road beside Fazilatunnesa Hall, the man allegedly wrapped a net-like object around her neck and dragged her to an area beside the extended section of Al-Beruni Hall. Students passing through the area on a motorcycle heard the victim screaming for help. Speaking to The Daily Star, Safikul Islam, a student of the Bangla department and one of those who responded, said they rushed to the scene immediately after hearing the cries. “When we reached the spot, we found a female student in a distressed state near the bushes.” The students later informed the university’s security officials, after which members of the proctorial body arrived at the scene. Deputy Registrar Gafrul said students informed him of the incident around 11:15pm. “We searched the entire area immediately, but could not find the suspect,” he said, adding that the victim was taken to the university medical centre for initial treatment, while authorities began reviewing CCTV footage to identify the accused. “Footage analysis confirmed that the suspect wrapped a net-like object around the student’s neck and dragged her into a wooded area beside the extended part of Al-Beruni Hall. Based on the footage, we have been able to make a preliminary identification of the suspect.” JU Proctor AKM Rashidul Alam said, “After analysing the CCTV footage, we have seen the suspect’s face. From what we could assess, the person involved in the incident does not appear to be a student of the university. “We are deeply distressed by the incident that took place on our campus.” PROTEST BREAKS OUT Proctor Rashidul faced widespread criticism after he said in front of his office on the night of the incident, “Ensuring security is not the responsibility of the proctor, but of the registrar.” Protesting his statement, more than 1,000 female students gathered in front of the proctor’s office last night, demanding his resignation. They alleged that he failed to ensure the safety and security of female students at the university. Lamisha Jaman, a student protester, said, “How can he say he is not responsible for students’ safety and security? Moreover, he has failed to resolve any of the [previous] harassment complaints filed with his office.” As of the filing of this report around 12:30am, the protesters were staging a sit-in at the registrar’s office, reiterating their demand for the proctor’s resignation.

title: JU students demand proctor’s resignation after attempted rape on campus
body: More than a thousand female students of Jahangirnagar University gathered in front of the university’s proctor office Wednesday night, demanding the resignation of Proctor Prof AKM Rashidul Alam following the attempted rape of a student on campus allegedly by an outsider. The protesting students brought out a torch procession around 10:10pm from the university’s women’s dormitory area and marched through several campus roads. The protesting students said that the proctor failed to ensure the safety and security of female students in the university. An attempted rape case was filed earlier with Ashulia Police Station against an unidentified individual after a female student of the university alleged that an outsider attacked her on campus late last night. The incident took place after 11:00pm near the abandoned old Fazilatunnesa Hall and the extended section of Al-Beruni Hall, according to university authorities.

title: Wife detained over alleged knife attack on sleeping husband in Lalmonirhat
body: A woman has been accused of attempting to kill her sleeping husband by slitting his throat following a domestic dispute in Babupura area of Lalmonirhat. The incident occurred earlier this morning; the accused has been detained and is in police custody, Lalmonirhat Sadar Police Station Officer-in-Charge Saad Ahmed said. According to police and family members, the husband, Hridoy Islam, 26, was asleep in his room when his wife, Jannatul Ferdous, 19, allegedly attacked him with a sharp knife. Hearing his screams, family members and neighbours rushed to the spot and rescued him in a bloodied condition. “The injured youth has deep wounds in his throat. His condition is extremely critical as the windpipe has been damaged. He has been sent to Rangpur Medical College Hospital for advanced treatment,” Lalmonirhat Sadar Hospital Resident Medical Officer Dr Karim Badsha said. Soon after the incident, angry locals held Jannatul. Police later reached the scene and took her into custody. “We were in the next room. Suddenly hearing Hridoy’s screams, we rushed there and saw him holding his blood-soaked throat, while Jannatul was standing beside him with a knife in her hand,” said victim’s father, Ershad Ali. He said Hridoy and Jannatul had frequent arguments. Police said legal action will be taken once a complaint is received; however, no written complaint has yet been filed by the victim’s family.

title: Rab team attacked during operation in Natore, one injured: Police
body: A group of 15 to 20 criminals attacked plainclothes members of the Rapid Action Battalion (Rab) in Nabinagar area of Lalpur upazila in Natore last night, said police. The incident took place at approximately 9:10pm when a six-member intelligence team from Rab-5, CPC-2 of the Natore camp, led by ASI Md Parvez Munshi, was operating in plainclothes in Nabinagar village to collect information on drug trafficking, said Lalpur Police Station Officer-in-Charge Md Shafikul Islam. Six Rab personnel were assaulted in the incident, leaving one injured. The injured Rab member was admitted to Lalpur Upazila Health Complex. According to the police statement, when the team reached the Nabinagar Government Primary School area, a group of 15 to 20 people led by Md Sohag Mahamud, 30, intercepted the officers and demanded to know their identities. When the Rab members identified themselves and attempted to leave, the group snatched their motorcycle keys, triggering an altercation that escalated into a physical attack. Police said they rushed to the scene upon receiving information, brought the situation under control, and rescued the Rab members. Following the attack, police conducted a raid in the area and arrested the suspected ringleader, Md Sohag Hossain, from the scene, though others managed to flee. He was later produced before a judicial magistrate court in Natore today. Rab has filed a case with Lalpur Police Station against the attackers. OC Shafikul Islam said drives are ongoing to arrest the remaining suspects. Sources said a drug trafficking network has long been active in the Nabinagar area, and the attackers are suspected associates of local peddlers. As of filing this report, Rab officials were not available for comment.
