title: Shapla Chattar Crackdown: ‘Try those behind killings, ensure justice for victims’
body: Terming the killings during a Hefajat-e-Islam rally at Shapla Chattar in the capital’s Motijheel on May 5, 2013 a gross violation of human rights, speakers yesterday demanded justice for those who lost their lives. Speaking at a programme titled “Shapla Massacre: A Decade of Impunity”, organised by the National Citizen Party-backed National Ulama Alliance at the Institution of Diploma Engineers in Dhaka’s Kakrail, they also demanded official recognition of the victims as “martyrs”. Writer and thinker Farhad Mazhar said resisting oppression is the essence of Islam. “Whenever I fail to stand against the oppressor, I deviate from Islam.” Referring to the May 5 incident, he said it was about citizens’ rights to speak, express anger, and protest in Bangladesh. “In bourgeois democracy, the first thing is freedom of expression and protest. But what did they show us? They showed that people can even be deprived of minimum democratic and human rights,” he said. He also criticised how the victims were portrayed after the crackdown. “I came to Dhaka to speak my words. I was shot and killed. Afterwards, they mocked me, saying I was only lying down covered in paint,” he said. “Why did I come to Dhaka? Because I am oppressed.” Hefazat-e-Islam Nayeb-e-Ameer Mufti Ahmad Ali Kasemi demanded justice for those killed during the Shapla Chattar incident, the 2021 anti-Modi protests, and the July uprising. He said Hefazat filed a case with the International Crimes Tribunal after the July uprising, but the process had not progressed quickly enough. Opposition Chief Whip in parliament and National Citizen Party Convener Nahid Islam said if those responsible for the Shapla Chattar crackdown had been brought to justice, the July 2024 killings could have been avoided. He demanded a proper investigation into the incident and justice for all extrajudicial killings and enforced disappearances carried out during the Awami League government. He criticised both the political leadership and sections of the media during the 2013 protests. Nahid also said people would take responsibility for protecting the country’s borders if the government failed to ensure national security. He said the country was once again witnessing killings along border areas and the erection of new barbed wire fences. Nahid expressed hope that people of the neighbouring country will one day remove the fences to establish genuine relations with Bangladeshi people.

title: Panic grips Bangladeshis in Lebanon
body: Panic has gripped the Bangladeshi community in Lebanon after two migrant workers were killed Monday afternoon while two others were reported missing and presumed dead later that night following Israeli air strikes in the southern city of Nabatieh. “One Bangladeshi woman was killed in Beirut in early April, and now more Bangladeshis have been killed. The latest attacks and the killings have created panic in the community. We don’t feel safe living in Lebanon right now,” Milon Khan, a Bangladeshi migrant who works at a petrol station in Beirut, told The Daily Star yesterday over the phone. The Bangladesh Embassy in Beirut confirmed that two Bangladeshis -- Shafiqul Islam and Nahidul Islam of Satkhira -- were killed Monday afternoon in an Israeli drone strike in Zebdine, Nabatieh. Later that night, more Israeli drone strikes were reported in Mayfadoun, also in Nabatieh, following which two more Bangladeshis were reported missing and presumed dead after a farmhouse was reduced to rubble. Milon identified the two Bangladeshis as Shuvo Kumar Das of Satkhira and Karim Sheikh of Narsingdi. Anowar Hossain, first secretary at the Bangladesh Embassy, said the two men had been staying at the farmhouse where they worked. “We have not been able to visit the site yet because we are still awaiting permission from the local administration, but we suspect they have been killed and that their bodies remain trapped under the rubble.” “We’ve repeatedly advised our people not to stay in southern Lebanon and relocate to safer areas in the north because of the war. In fact, many of them had already moved out of the area,” he added. Milon said some, however, may have returned under the impression of a ceasefire or at employers’ urges. Leaders of the community estimate 400–500 Bangladeshis may still be living in Nabatieh, though many are expected to move north after Monday’s strikes. Earlier, on April 8, another Bangladeshi national, Dipali Begum of Faridpur, was killed in an Israeli air strike in Beirut. According to Reuters, Lebanon’s health ministry reported 74 deaths in Israeli strikes in the three days leading up to May 11, despite a truce announced last month between Israel and Hezbollah. At least 2,869 people, including medics, women, and children, have been killed since March 2, the ministry said. The International Rescue Committee says more than one million people across Lebanon, including over 300,000 children, have been displaced, with the humanitarian situation worsening daily. Bangladeshi community leaders estimate that around 3,000 of the country’s 100,000 migrants in Lebanon have been displaced, and many have lost jobs. Anowar said the embassy has been providing food assistance to Bangladeshis in need and maintaining regular communication through Facebook and WhatsApp groups. He also said that at the embassy’s request, the Lebanese authorities had waived fines for undocumented Bangladeshis seeking to return home. “So far, around 300 people have registered to return to Bangladesh. Hopefully, they will begin flying home within the next two weeks,” he said.

title: Man sent to jail over rape of speech-impaired woman
body: A man has been sent to jail in a case filed over the rape of a young woman in Mymensingh’s Gouripur upazila. Md Yasin, 30, of Ghaterkona village, was sent to prison by a Mymensingh court yesterday afternoon following his arrest the night before, said Habibur Rahman, officer-in-charge of Gouripur Police Station. The victim, a 19-year-old woman who has a speech impediment, has undergone necessary medical attention at Mymensingh Medical College Hospital. Md Abdullah Al Mamun, additional police superintendent (admin) in Mymensingh, said, “Yasin raped the girl after breaking into her house on Sunday afternoon when her parents were away. When her parents returned later in the evening, the girl managed to inform them about the rape.” The victim’s mother filed a rape case against Yasin with Gouripur Police Station on Monday night, leading to his arrest that same night.

title: Suspect joined the search for murdered child
body: The man arrested on suspicion of murdering a four-year-old girl from a neighbouring family during attempted rape on May 6 in Sylhet joined locals searching for the child, police have said. The suspect, Zakir Hossain, 30, was seen among the locals during the search after the girl had gone missing that day, Sylhet Metropolitan Police’s (SMP) Deputy Commissioner Mohammad Saiful Islam said at a press conference yesterday. Police arrested him on Monday night after the girl’s body was found in a pond in the neighbourhood of Sonatola village of Sylhet Sadar upazila on May 8. Agitated locals later vandalised his house. The victim has been identified as Fahima Akter, daughter of Roisul Haque. Citing the statement Zakir gave during initial interrogation, SMP Deputy Commissioner Saiful said the suspect had sent Fahima to a nearby shop to buy cigarettes on the day of the incident. After the girl returned, Zakir called her to his room, closed the door, and attempted to rape her, the police officer said. Zakir admitted to strangling the child after she became unconscious at one stage of the sexual assault, Saiful said. Whether to add a rape charge will be decided once the medical report is received, the police officer said. A murder case has been filed with Jalalabad Police Station. Citing Zakir’s statement, police said he first stashed the body in a briefcase in the room and later tried to bury it inside his room. As the odour from the decomposing body spread, he dumped it in a nearby pond. Police recovered the body after being informed by the locals. Police said they recovered a piece of cloth and the briefcase used in the crime based on information given by Zakir. The items will be examined as part of investigation. “No direct evidence has yet been found of another person’s involvement,” the deputy commissioner said. “But the probe is underway. If anyone else is found to be involved, they will be brought to justice.”

title: Rohingya youth shot as rival groups clash in Ukhiya camp
body: A Rohingya youth was shot and injured in a fresh gunfight between rival armed groups at the Balukhali refugee camp in Ukhiya, Cox’s Bazar Tuesday afternoon. The gunfight took place around 3:00pm at Block-B of Camp-8. The injured, Hasmat Ullah, 22, a resident of Camp-8, sustained two bullet wounds to his right hand, Ukhiya Police Station Officer-in-Charge Mujibur Rahman said. Police rescued him from the spot and first took him to the BRAC hospital inside the camp. As his condition deteriorated, he was later shifted to the MSF hospital in Kutupalong, Ukhiya, before being taken to Cox’s Bazar Sadar Hospital. OC Mujibur said law enforcement agencies were conducting drives inside the camps to arrest the armed attackers and that patrols had been intensified. Police and Rohingya community leaders said tensions have recently escalated between a group led by Nabi Hossain -- Arakan Rohingya Army (ARA) -- and another armed group, Arakan Rohingya Organisation (ARO), over control inside the camps. On May 6, around 2:30pm, Mohammad Kamal alias Nur Kamal, 45, a community leader at a camp and younger brother of Nabi Hossain, was shot dead by ARO members at the Balukhali camp. A day earlier, on May 5 at around 6:30pm, ARO commander Kefayet Ullah Halim, 45, was killed in a shooting allegedly carried out by members of the Nabi Hossain group at Camp-7 in Balukhali. Two other Rohingyas were also injured in that attack. Police and Rohingya leaders said that in continuation of the recent violence, a group of 10 to 12 armed men engaged in another gunfight at Camp-8 on Tueaday, during which Hasmat Ullah was shot. A Rohingya community leader claimed that Hasmat Ullah was a member of the Nabi Hossain group and alleged that ARO members launched an attack on an ARA hideout.

title: ASK visits 11-year-old rape victim in Netrokona
body: A delegation from rights organisation Ain o Salish Kendra (ASK) today visited the home of the 11-year-old girl in Netrokona’s Madan upazila after she became pregnant following the alleged rape by a madrasa teacher. The ASK team visited the child’s home to assess her physical and mental condition, review the family’s security situation, and examine the circumstances surrounding the alleged incident, according to the organisation. After visiting the victim’s home and the site of the alleged rape, ASK Senior Staff Lawyer Selina Akter and investigator Tawhid Ahmed Rana met Mohammad Tarikul Islam, officer-in-charge of Madan Police Station, to discuss the progress of the investigation. ASK Senior Coordinator Abu Ahmed Faizul Kabir told The Daily Star, “This is not just an isolated crime, but a glaring example of the extreme failure of child safety and the state’s protection system.” The organisation demanded specialised medical treatment, psychological support for the child, and security for her family. “The girl is a minor. Considering her physical and mental condition, we have come to stand by her. At the same time, we are monitoring the case and the investigation process,” he added. Faizul also expressed concern over the growing number of rape cases nationwide, saying the Netrokona case was particularly disturbing because of the victim’s age. “A child went to study at an educational institution and now has another life growing inside her body. This is completely unacceptable,” he said. “It must be ensured that no influential quarters can interfere with the investigation. The victim’s family is financially vulnerable, which often leads to various pressures,” he said. On the child’s current condition, Faizul said she was suffering from anaemia and severe mental distress. “She cannot sleep at night. The child is mentally broken. We could not even speak to her normally,” he said. According to police, the victim’s mother filed a case on April 23, alleging that her daughter, a madrasa student, was raped by Amanullah Mahmudi Sagar, a teacher at the same institution, resulting in a seven-month pregnancy. Police have arrested the accused and produced him before court, which sent him to jail. On May 10, following a three-day remand, the court ordered a DNA test.

title: Highway police attacked following road accident in Ctg
body: A team of highway police was attacked by a group of people following a road accident during a routine vehicle check on the Chattogram-Khagrachari road in Chattogram’s Fatickchari upazila today. The incident took place in the Najirhat area around 6:00am, said Mobarak Hossen Bhuiyan, officer-in-charge of Najirhat Highway Police Station. The OC told The Daily Star that a highway police team signalled a pickup van loaded with fruits and vegetables, coming from Khagrachari, to stop for a routine check. Ignoring the signal, the driver sped away and later collided with a bus coming from Chattogram, leaving three people injured. Following the accident, a group of people assaulted the cops and attempted to vandalise a police van. Several police personnel sustained minor injuries. Police and local residents later brought the situation under control, the OC said. “We informed our higher authorities about the incident,” he said. However, no one was arrested in this connection, added the police officer.

title: Accused joined search after killing 4-year-old in Sylhet: Police
body: Police said a man accused of murdering a four-year-old girl in Sylhet joined local residents in searching for the child after allegedly killing her. At a press conference today, Sylhet Metropolitan Police (SMP) Deputy Commissioner (north zone) Mohammad Saiful Islam said police arrested Zakir Hossain, 30, of Sadar upazila, from Sonatola village under the same upazila on Monday night. Agitated locals vandalised the accused’s house later that night. The suspect joined the search for the victim and was also seen mingling with volunteers while police were at the scene, the deputy commissioner said. According to DC Saiful, the incident took place on the morning of May 6. During interrogation, Zakir, a relative of the victim, said he had sent the child to a nearby shop to buy cigarettes. After she returned, Zakir called her into his room and attempted to rape the child, the DC said. At one point when the child became unconscious, he strangled her to death and hid the body in a suitcase, the police officer said based on the information provided by Zakir. Citing Zakir’s statement, police said when a search began in the area, he hid the suitcase under the bed and even joined everyone in looking for the child. When the room started to smell, he tried to dump the body in a waterbody. As the body did not sink, he left it under a tree. The victim’s body was identified by locals on the morning of May 8. Police said they recovered a cloth and the suitcase used in the crime. “No direct evidence has yet been found of another person’s involvement,” the deputy commissioner said. “But the investigation is ongoing. If anyone else is found to be involved, they will be brought to justice.” Meanwhile, a murder case has been filed with Jalalabad Police Station. Whether a rape charge will be added to the case will be decided once the medical report is received, the police official said.

title: Trader found dead with hands, legs tied in Old Dhaka flat
body: A trader was found dead with his hands and legs tied in a flat in Old Dhaka’s Bangshal area today. The deceased was identified as Nisar Ali, 50, a fabric trader in Islampur area. Police recovered the body from the first floor of a five-storey building in Bagdasa Lane of Nababazar in the afternoon after being informed through the national emergency service 999. “The victim was found on a bed with his hands and legs tied with towels, while his mouth was covered with a window curtain,” said Abdul Wahab, sub-inspector (SI) of Bangshal Police Station. According to police, the building owner, Mohammad Hossain Babu, noticed lights on inside the room around 1:00pm today and called out to the tenant repeatedly. Receiving no response, he peered through the doorway after moving aside a curtain and saw the victim’s legs tied. He then informed neighbours and alerted police through 999. Quoting preliminary findings, the SI said they suspect unidentified assailants might have tied up and strangled the businessman sometime between 11:00pm on Monday and 1:00pm today before fleeing the scene. Members of the CID crime scene unit collected evidence from the flat, police said. Police said the victim had been living alone in the rented flat for the last three months after moving to Dhaka from Jashore for business.

title: 5 arrested in Dhaka's Jatrabari with firearms, explosives: Police
body: The Detective Branch (DB) of Dhaka Metropolitan Police arrested five members of an alleged inter-district robbery gang in Dhaka’s Jatrabari area yesterday while they were reportedly preparing for a robbery. Acting on a tip-off, a team from the DB’s Wari Division conducted a raid on Shahid Faruk Road in Dayaganj around 4:45pm, and detained the suspects from in front of a furniture shop, said DMP Additional Commissioner Shafiqul Islam while speaking at a press conference at the DMP Media Centre today. The arrestees are Md Liton Jabbar, 52; Ismail Hossain Mamun, 55; Md Babul Babu, 45; Ayub Bhuiyan, 30; and Md Roman, 35. Police recovered two pistols, two magazines, seven bullets, around 2.2 kg of explosives, a machete, and two motorcycles. Additional Commissioner Shafiqul said the group had allegedly been collecting firearms and bomb-making materials from the Jashore border area for a long time. “They would bring those to Dhaka and sell them to various terrorist groups,” he said, adding that there were also allegations that the gang used the weapons and explosives to carry out robberies. Two separate cases have been filed against the five detainees with Jatrabari Police Station.

title: Chattogram shooting: 6 arrested as girl hit by stray bullet fights for life
body: Police have arrested six suspects, including the prime accused, in connection with the shooting in Chattogram’s Bayezid Bostami area that killed a young man and left an 11‑year‑old girl critically injured. Confirming the development this afternoon, Deputy Commissioner (North Zone) of Chattogram Metropolitan Police (CMP), Md Amirul Islam, said the murder was linked to a dispute over local dominance. The deceased, Hasan Raju, 24, was named as the seventh accused in a murder case filed over the killing of Nasir Uddin, alias Madhu Nasir, who was shot dead in Raozan on April 26. “During primary interrogation, the arrestees confessed that Raju was killed in revenge for Nasir’s death,” DC Amirul Islam said. The prime suspect, Syedul Karim, 27, was apprehended Monday afternoon from Sugandha Beach in Cox’s Bazar. The other five arrestees were identified as Md Abdul Mannan, 37, driver of the getaway CNG auto‑rickshaw; Md Younus Mia, 24; Md Ayatullah Ali Adnan, 21; Md Abu Bakkar Siddique alias Khokon, 48; and Azgar Ali, 39. Operations were conducted across Cox’s Bazar, Double Mooring, Roufabad, and Chandgaon between Monday afternoon and early Tuesday morning. While police made progress in the investigation, another victim of the shooting, 11‑year‑old Reshmi Akthar, remains in a precarious state at Chittagong Medical College Hospital (CMCH). Reshmi, a class four student, was shot in the eye while on her way to buy betel leaf for her mother. She has since suffered multi-organ failure and remains on life support in the ICU. “The bullet is still lodged in the back of her head. As it passed through critical parts of the brain, surgery is extremely risky and could cause fatal haemorrhaging,” said Prof KM Baki Billah, head of Anaesthesiology at CMCH. CMCH Director Brig Gen Taslim Uddin said her condition is being monitored round‑the‑clock by a specialised medical board. The incident occurred on May 7, when five to six masked gunmen opened fire in front of the Bihari Colony at Roufabad. While the attackers targeted Raju, Reshmi was struck by a stray bullet. Her brother, Faisal Ahmed, told The Daily Star, “She was just walking, without sensing any danger. Three miscreants began firing at someone in our alley. A stray bullet entered through her left eye and pierced into her head.” Raju’s mother, Sakina Begum, filed a murder case with Bayezid Police Station on May 9.

title: Father, son murdered by two other sons in Dinajpur
body: A man and his son were stabbed to death allegedly by two of his sons from his second marriage following a dispute over property in Dinajpur this morning. The deceased were identified as Dulu Mia, 70, and his son Kabil, 30. Another son, Habil, was injured in the attack that occurred in Mondolpara area of Chirirbandar upazila. Officer-in-Charge of Chirirbandar Police Station Mahmudul Nabi said Dulu Mia had four sons from two marriages. A dispute had been going on over around 16 bighas of land owned by Dulu Mia. As the conflict escalated, two sons from his second marriage- Sadequl and Sakib- allegedly stabbed their father and step-brother Kabil with sharp weapons, killing them on the spot, he added. The two suspects went into hiding after the incident. The OC said police are sending the bodies to Dinajpur Medical College Hospital morgue for autopsy and efforts are underway to arrest the suspects.

title: Three Rab members assaulted, held captive for 4 hours in Brahmanbaria
body: Three members of the Rapid Action Battalion (Rab) were allegedly assaulted and held captive for nearly four hours by a group led by “Chura Shafik” in Nabinagar upazila of Brahmanbaria on Monday. The incident occurred in Khagatua Baliyara village under Ratanpur union, said Md Nur Nabi, company commander of Rab-9 CPC-1. According to Rab, four members of the force were heading to the eastern side of Durgarampur Bridge in Bancharampur on an information-gathering mission. They used the Khagatua-Majiara road as a shortcut. When they entered Khagatua village, Shafik and his associates allegedly intercepted them. Despite identifying themselves as Rab personnel, the members came under attack. The injured were identified as Habildar AKM Rashed Mosharraf of BGB, Constable Md Kajol Mia, and Constable Md Abdul Malek. Rab said Sergeant Faruk managed to escape during the attack, but the other three were detained, physically assaulted, and confined inside a house for several hours. Additional Rab-9 members later surrounded the area and, with police assistance, rescued the three confined personnel. The injured were treated at Nabinagar Upazila Health Complex. “Three Rab members were injured, including one who suffered a sharp weapon injury to the head,” said company commander Md Nur Nabi. Locals alleged that Shafik has long been involved in criminal activities, intimidation, and establishing dominance in the area. Multiple cases, including murder, theft, assault, and vandalism, are reportedly pending against him.

title: 2 Bangladeshis killed in Israeli drone strike in Lebanon
body: Two Bangladeshi workers were killed in an Israeli drone attack in southern Lebanon yesterday. The strike took place around noon local time at a residence in Zebdine, Nabatieh. Both victims were residents of Satkhira. The Embassy of Bangladesh in Beirut confirmed the deaths in a condolence message yesterday. The deceased were identified as Shafiqul Islam, son of Afsar Ali of Bhaluka Chandpur in Satkhira Sadar Upazila, and Md Nahidul Islam, son of Md Abdul Kader of Kadakati in Ashashuni Upazila. According to the embassy, the bodies are currently being kept at Nabih Berri Hospital. The embassy expressed deep sympathy to the bereaved families. Earlier, on April 8, Bangladeshi migrant worker Dipali Begum was killed in an Israeli airstrike in Beirut.

title: SC regrets upholding Azharul’s death sentence
body: The Appellate Division of the Supreme Court, in the full text of a verdict released recently, expressed regret over its earlier judgement, which had upheld the conviction and death sentence of Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami leader ATM Azharul Islam in a case filed over crimes against humanity committed during Bangladesh’s 1971 Liberation War. “This Division [Appellate Division] acknowledges, with a profound sense of judicial responsibility, that in its earlier adjudication, it failed to give due and dispassionate consideration to the evidentiary deficiencies and the broader context in which the allegations of crimes against humanity were framed against the appellant,” said the seven-member bench, headed by then chief justice Syed Refaat Ahmed, in the 74-page verdict. “The earlier judgement regrettably fell short of the high standards of scrutiny and fairness mandated in criminal proceedings of such grave nature.” On May 27, 2025, the Appellate Division scrapped its earlier judgement that had upheld the conviction and death sentence handed down by the International Crimes Tribunal against Azharul in 2014. The apex court also acquitted him of all charges and directed jail authorities to release him immediately unless he was wanted in any other case. The bench delivered the verdict following an appeal filed by the Jamaat leader, challenging the conviction and death penalty awarded by the ICT. Azharul’s lawyer Mohammad Shishir Manir said his client, who had been in jail since August 8, 2012, was released on May 28, 2025, following the SC verdict. ATM Azharul, currently nayeb-e-ameer of Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami, was elected a lawmaker from Rangpur-2 in the February 12 national election. Barrister Mohammed Belayet Hossain, another lawyer for Azharul, earlier told this correspondent that this was the first time the Appellate Division had rescinded its own judgement upholding a conviction and death sentence handed down by the ICT in a crimes against humanity case. Jamaat leaders Motiur Rahman Nizami, Abdul Quader Mollah, Muhammad Kamaruzzaman, Ali Ahsan Mohammad Mojaheed and Mir Quasem Ali, along with BNP leader Salauddin Quader Chowdhury, were executed following Supreme Court verdicts in cases related to crimes against humanity committed in 1971.

title: Man arrested over rape of speech-impaired teenage girl in Mymensingh
body: Police arrested a man today for allegedly raping a 14-year-old girl with speech-impairment in Mymensingh's Haluaghat upazila, with a local court sending him to jail. The arrestee was identified as Shakul Sangma, 56, son of Matin Marak, of Chhatugoan village in Haluaghat. During primary interrogation, he reportedly confessed to the crime, said Md Ferdous Alam, officer-in-charge of Haluaghat Police Station. According to the case statement, Shakul, a neighbour of the victim, took the girl into a nearby forest and raped her under threat. When local people began to sense what had occurred, he went into hiding. Acting on information, police raided the area and apprehended Shakul at around 8:00pm. Earlier in the day, the victim's mother lodged a formal complaint with the police station, naming Shakul as the accused. The arrestee was subsequently produced before a Mymensingh court, which ordered him remanded, the OC added. The victim was taken to Mymensingh Medical College Hospital for a medical examination.

title: Cops attacked while chasing muggers in Dhaka’s Mohammadpur; SI injured
body: A team from Dhanmondi Police Station came under an attack early today while chasing a group of muggers in Dhaka’s Mohammadpur area. One sub‑inspector was injured in the incident. One of the muggers was shot in the leg during the scuffle. Three were arrested from the scene, said Dhanmondi Police Station Officer‑in‑Charge (OC) Saiful Islam. He said the attack took place around 6:00am behind Mohammadpur Town Hall. A group of muggers on motorcycles was spotted preparing for a robbery in Dhanmondi‑27. When police chased them, the gang fled towards Mohammadpur. According to the OC, two police teams comprising ten members pursued the gang. The muggers then regrouped and attacked police with axes, machetes, and sharp weapons. As the assault continued, an officer fired at one suspect’s leg to stop the attack. Police identified the injured mugger as Sakib, who is now under treatment at Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital under police custody. Two others were arrested from the spot. The gang is accused of roaming Dhanmondi and nearby areas on motorcycles while carrying machetes and knives to commit robberies, the OC added. Sub-Inspector Saiful Alam, 35, was injured in the attack and given first aid at hospital, said Masud Rana, inspector (Investigation) of Dhanmondi Police Station.

title: RPO has no bar on Jamaat's registration as party over Liberation War role: SC
body: The Supreme Court, in the full text of its judgement on Jamaat-e-Islami’s registration, observed that the Representation of the People Order (RPO) contains no provision barring a political party’s registration based on the role of its leaders during the Liberation War. The SC made the observation in the 51-page full text of its verdict, released recently. “The 25 writ petitioners, who challenged the legality of Jamaat’s registration before the High Court, have tendered objection to the effect that due to the heinous role of its leaders during the Liberation War, it should not have been given registration to do politics in Bangladesh,” the verdict said. “Their grievance appears to be sentimental rather than legal, as the RPO does not incorporate any provision to refuse registration to any political party for the role of its leaders during the Liberation War,” it added. On June 1 last year, a four-member Appellate Division bench headed by then chief justice Syed Refaat Ahmed scrapped a 2013 High Court verdict that had declared Jamaat’s registration illegal. Following an appeal filed by Jamaat, the apex court also directed the Election Commission to resolve the party’s pending issues, including its registration. The EC later restored Jamaat’s registration and returned “Daripalla (scale)” as its election symbol, Advocate Mohammad Shishir Manir, a lawyer for the party, told The Daily Star. Jamaat lost the right to contest parliamentary elections as a party after the High Court declared its registration with EC illegal on August 1, 2013, following a writ petition. The petition was filed on January 25, 2009, by Syed Rezaul Haque Chandpuri, secretary general of the Bangladesh Tariqat Federation, along with 24 others, seeking a declaration that Jamaat’s registration was illegal. The EC later cancelled Jamaat’s registration in October 2018 ahead of the 11th national election. Jamaat subsequently filed an appeal with the SC challenging the HC verdict. The apex court began hearing the appeal on December 3, 2024. No lawyer presented arguments on behalf of the petitioners during the Appellate Division hearing on this issue.

title: July uprising case: Ex-SP Tanvir Salehin Emon released on bail
body: Former Superintendent of Police Tanvir Salehin Emon, who was arrested and sent to jail in a case filed over the murder of trader Abdul Wadud in Dhaka's New Market area during July mass uprising, has been released on bail from Kashimpur Central High Security Prison. He was released from the prison at 5:40 pm today, confirmed Senior Jail Superintendent of Kashimpur High Security Central Jail Mohammad Abdullah Al Mamun. He said Tanvir was released after verification of the court’s bail order and all related documents. The additional chief metropolitan magistrate of Dhaka granted him bail in the case on May 10. Tanvir is from Ayla village under Karimganj upazila in Kishoreganj. On February 12, detectives detained SP (basic training-2) Tanvir from Bangladesh Police Academy in Rajshahi's Sardah. Before his posting at Sardah, he had served as deputy commissioner at Dhaka Metropolitan Police headquarters. He was first sent to prison on February 12, 2025, and was later transferred to Kashimpur Central High Security Prison on September 4, 2025. He is accused in a case filed with New Market Police Station in the capital under Penal Code, 1860 along with the Explosive Substances Act, 1908. Abdul Wadud, 45, a trader at Priyangon Shopping Centre, was killed during the quota reform protests on July 19, 2024. Abdur Rahman, a relative of the deceased, filed the case on August 21 against 130 individuals, including ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina and senior Awami League leaders Obaidul Quader, Anisul Huq, Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal, Salman F Rahman, and Amir Hossain Amu. After the fall of Awami League government on August 5, 2024, Tanvir was transferred to the police academy as superintendent (basic training-2).

title: Four Kapasia murder victims had throats slit, one child strangled: Autopsy
body: Autopsies have been completed on the five victims , including a mother and her three children, who were killed in Gazipur’s Kapasia upazila last Friday. According to the preliminary autopsy report, four of the victims had their throats slit, while one child was strangled to death. At around 5:00pm today, Dr Mazharul Haque of the forensic department at Shaheed Tajuddin Ahmad Medical College Hospital told The Daily Star that Sharmin Khanam, her brother Rasul Molla, and her two daughters Mim and Maria died after their throats were slit. Another daughter, Faria, was killed by strangulation. He further said that samples, including stomach contents and other evidence, had been collected and sent to the CID lab to determine whether the victims had been given sedatives or any other substances before the murders. Further details will be known after the lab report is received, he said. The deceased are Sharmin Khanam, 35, wife of Forkan Mia; their daughters Mim, 16, Maria, 8, and Faria, 2; and Sharmin’s brother Rasul Molla, 22. Police said the horrific killings took place on Friday night at the family's home. Investigators initially suspect the murders were the result of a family dispute. Officer-in-Charge Md Shahinur Alam of Kapasia Police Station said a case has been filed in connection with the incident. The accused, Sharmin's husband Forkan Mia, of Mary Gopinathpur village in Gopalganj Sadar upazila, has been absconding since the murders.

title: Absconding rape case accused arrested in Rangpur
body: Rakibul Islam, 32, an absconding accused in a rape case, has been arrested in Rangpur, officials said. Members of Rab-13 arrested him from Darshana Mor area under Tajhat Police Station around 10:30pm yesterday, based on a tip-off, according to a press release issued today by Senior Assistant Director (Media) of Rab-13, Biplob Kumar Goswami. Rakibul, a resident of Parulia village in Hatibandha upazila of Lalmonirhat, had been on the run since a case was filed with Hatibandha Police Station on April 22. Quoting case details, Rab said the victim was later rescued and admitted to Hatibandha Upazila Health Complex before being shifted to Rangpur Medical College Hospital for treatment. Biplob Kumar Goswami said Rakibul went into hiding after the case was filed. He added that efforts are continuing to arrest the other two remaining accused.

title: HC defers verdict on Chinmoy Krishna Das’s bail petitions till May 14
body: The High Court today deferred until May 14 the verdict on the bail petitions of former ISKCON leader Chinmoy Krishna Das Brahmachari, also known as Chandan Kumar Dhar, in four cases. The bench of Justice KM Zahid Sarwar and Justice Sheikh Abu Taher postponed the ruling after Additional Attorney General Aneek R Haque sought time to submit additional documents related to the cases. Chinmoy’s lawyer, Apurba Kumar Bhattacharya, opposed the request for more time. Yesterday, the same High Court bench rejected Chinmoy’s bail petition in a case filed with Kotwali Police Station in Chattogram over the killing of lawyer Saiful Islam Alif. Alif was beaten and hacked to death on November 26, 2024, during clashes near the Chattogram court building. During the hearing, Apurba told the court that his client had been suffering from physical illness while in jail since November 25, 2024, and sought bail on that ground. Earlier, the concerned deputy attorneys general opposed the bail petitions. According to the defence lawyer, Chinmoy has been accused in eight cases, including murder and sedition. He has already secured bail in three cases from the High Court and lower courts. The Appellate Division of the Supreme Court has, however, stayed the High Court order granting him bail in the sedition case, the lawyer added.

title: HSC student arrested over gang rape of 14-year-old in Rajbari
body: Police arrested an HSC student in connection with a case filed over the gang-rape of a 14-year-old schoolgirl in Goalanda upazila of Rajbari. The arrested person has been identified as Nahidul Islam, 20, a resident of Goalanda upazila. The victim’s mother filed the case under the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act with Goalanda Ghat Police Station yesterday evening. Nahidul Islam and his friend Raihan Sheikh have been made accused in the case. According to the case statement, the victim is a class-7 student at a local school. A few months ago, she developed a relationship with Raihan. On Saturday, Raihan and Nahidul met the girl and took her out, telling her they were going for a walk. They then took the victim to the Goalanda municipal area and allegedly raped her Saturday night. The incident came to light around midnight when the suspects were spotted by locals while attempting to drop the girl off near her home. Locals then chased the duo, capturing Nahidul while Raihan managed to flee. Upon receiving the information on Sunday morning, Goalanda Ghat police took the youth into custody. Confirming the incident, Goalanda Ghat Police Station Officer-in-Charge Md Shafiqur Islam told The Daily Star that locals detained Nahidul along with his motorcycle and handed him over to police over allegations of rape. He is scheduled to be produced before a court today. The victim has been sent to a hospital for medical examination, the OC said. Police are working to arrest Raihan, the prime accused in the case, he added.

title: Journalists Shakil Ahmed, Farzana Rupa get HC bail in multiple cases linked to July uprising
body: The High Court today granted ad-interim bail to senior journalist Shakil Ahmed in five cases and his wife, senior journalist Farzana Rupa, in six cases filed over incidents linked to the July mass uprising. The court also issued separate rules asking the state to explain why the couple should not be granted permanent bail in those cases. However, the HC refused to grant them bail in another case, although it issued separate rules asking the state to explain why they should not be granted bail in that case as well. As a result, the journalist couple cannot be released from jail despite securing bail in the other cases. The orders were passed by a High Court bench comprising Justice KM Zahid Sarwar and Justice Sheikh Abu Taher following 13 petitions filed by Shakil and Rupa seeking bail. According to case documents, a Dhaka court on August 31, 2024, sent the couple to jail in a case filed with Adabor Police Station over the murder of garment worker Rubel. They were detained at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport on August 21 that year. The following day, a court placed them on a four-day remand in a murder case filed with Uttara East Police Station over the death of Fazlul Karim. On August 26, they were again remanded for five days in the Rubel murder case. Barrister Jyotirmoy Barua represented the petitioners, while Deputy Attorney General Ashiquzzaman Nazrul and Assistant Attorney General Md Al Amin appeared for the state.

title: Gazipur family murder: Five laid to rest in Gopalganj
body: The five members of a family, who were murdered in their Gazipur home, were laid to rest at their village home in Gopalganj on Sunday. Bodies of the victims identified as Sharmin, 35; her three daughters -- Mim, 16, Maria, 8, and Faria, 2 -- and Sharmin’s brother, Rasul Mollah, 22, were found with their throats slit at their house in Rautkona village under Gazipur’s Kapasia upazila on Saturday morning at around 8:00am. The five bodies were handed over to their relatives after completing autopsies at Shaheed Tajuddin Ahmad Medical College Hospital in Gazipur on Saturday night. Their bodies arrived at Uttar Charpara village of Gopalganj Sadar upazila at around 6:00am on Sunday. Their janaza was held at Paikkandi Madrasa playground at around 11:00am. Later, they were laid at Charpara Notun Graveyard in the village. Sharmin’s father, Shahadat Molla, filed a case against five people with Kapasia Police Station after the body recovery. Sharmin’s husband, Forkan Miah, who was made the prime accused in the murder case, has been absconding since the incident. Forkan, originally from Meri Gopinathpur village in Gopalganj Sadar upazila, married Sharmin, of Uttar Charpara village of the same upazila, around 20 years ago. He worked as a private car driver. They used to live in a rented house in Rautkona village for nearly a year. Sharmin’s uncle Uzzal told reporters that a domestic dispute was ongoing between the couple that resulted in the murder. “We cannot believe that Sharmin’s husband committed such a heinous crime. We want justice,” said Ratan Mollah, a cousin of Sharmin. “Sharmin’s husband, Forkan, often tortured her. But Sharmin tried to continue the relationship considering her children,” said Sharmin’s sister Fatema Begum. Sharmin’s father said, “Sharmin told me over phone on Friday night that she would come to our home on May 24. The next morning, Forkan’s brother, Jabbar Mollah, asked me over the phone to check Sharmin’s house. Then, we came to know about the incident.” One of the deceased, Mim, used to study in class nine at a madrasa in Rautkona village under Gazipur’s Kapasia upazila. Some of the students of the madrasa were seen visiting the residence where the murder took place. “We are terrified after the incident. We want immediate arrest of the killer,” said Ariful Islam, a student of the madrasa. Mosharraf Hossain, 45, a resident of nearby Pubur village, said, “It is frustrating that the killer could still not be arrested.” Surma Akter, 35, a grocery shop owner near the crime scene, said, “Even the night before the incident, the father came carrying his children and bought them food and snacks. He loved his children very much. But we still cannot understand why he committed such a crime.” Contacted, Kapasia Police Station’s Officer-in-Charge (OC) Mohammad Shahinur Alam said he hopes to arrest Forkan as soon as possible. Additional Superintendent of Police (Kapasia-Kaliganj Circle) Asaduzzaman said, “Preliminary investigation suggests that Forkan killed all five victims. However, we are investigating how five people were killed together. We are also examining whether the victims were given sleeping pills or intoxicating substances before the murders.” Gazipur Superintendent of Police (SP) Md Sharif Uddin said that two people have been detained for interrogation. Our Gazipur and Gopalganj correspondents contributed to the report.

title: SC upholds Ivy’s bail in 10 cases
body: The Appellate Division of the Supreme Court yesterday upheld the High Court bail of former Narayanganj City Corporation mayor Selina Hayat Ivy in 10 cases. The apex court dismissed five petitions filed by the state challenging the HC verdicts that on November 9 last year granted bail to Ivy in five cases and vacated its chamber judge’s orders that stayed her HC bail in other five cases. This means that Ivy’s HC bail in total 10 cases will remain effective, Deputy Attorney General Fatima Akhter and Ivy’s lawyers Md Motaher Hossain Sazu and SM Hridoy Rahman told The Daily Star. There is no legal bar to Ivy’s release from jail following the SC orders, Motaher said. A five-member bench of the Appellate Division led by Chief Justice Zubayer Rahman Chowdhury delivered the orders. The Appellate Division also asked the HC to dispose of the rules issued on February 26, directing the state to explain why Ivy should not be granted permanent bail in five cases. On May 9 last year, the former NCC mayor was arrested in connection with garment worker Minarul murder case and later she was shown arrested in nine other criminal cases. The HC granted bail to Ivy, former senior vice-president of the Narayanganj district Awami League, whose political activities are banned, in all the 10 cases on November 9 last year and February 26 this year following her bail petitions. Ivy was shown arrested in two other murder cases immediately after the HC granted her bail in five other cases on February 26 this year, said her lawyer Sazu. He said the cases were filed with Siddhirganj Police Station in Narayanganj on charges of killings Selim Mondal and Abdus Salam during the July uprising in 2024. On April 30, the HC granted ad-interim bail to Ivy and also issued two separate rules asking the state to explain as to why she should not be granted permanent bail in the cases. The state then filed two petitions with the Appellate Division seeking stay on the HC bail. The petitions are pending with the Appellate Division.

title: Mob beats three dead in Kaliakair
body: Three people were beaten to death by a mob on suspicions of cattle theft in Gazipur’s Kaliakair early yesterday. During the incident, a pickup used by the victims was also set on fire. The three are Krishan, 46, of Sylhet’s Ghasitola area; Azharul Islam, 36, of Gazipur’s Sreepur, and Md Selim, 38, of Dhaka’s Mirpur area, said police. Of them, Azharul and Selim had been accused of multiple robbery and theft cases in the past, said Shahidul Islam, officer-in-charge of Kaliakair Police Station. Quoting witnesses, police said a suspected gang of cattle thieves was passing through the Bagchala Bazar area in a pickup around 2:00am. Locals then chased the suspects, who were eventually caught and beaten by the mob. Their vehicle was set alight, said Robiul Islam, inspector (operations) of Kaliakair Police Station. On information, police went to the spot and rescued the three critically injured men before taking them to Shaheed Tajuddin Ahmad Medical College Hospital, where doctors declared them dead, he said. Asaduzzaman, an official of the hospital’s emergency department, said the three were brought dead to the hospital. A case was filed with Kaliakair Police Station, SI Yusuf, investigation officer of the case, told this correspondent.

title: Expat shot dead in South Africa: family
body: A Bangladeshi businessman was shot dead by unidentified assailants in South Africa on Saturday afternoon, according to the victim’s family. The deceased, Sumon Miah, 34, was originally from Abhirampur Pashchim Para in Tangail’s Mirzapur upazila, said Abdullah Al Mamun, officer-in-charge of Mirzapur Police Station. According to the family, Sumon went to South Africa 14 years ago and had been doing business near Newcastle city. Around 1:00pm on Saturday local time (5:00pm BST), unidentified assailants stopped his car and shot him dead. Police later recovered his body. Speaking to reporters, Sumon’s father said people known to him in South Africa immediately informed the family about the incident over the phone. Sumon’s body may reach Bangladesh on Tuesday, he said. The youngest of seven siblings, Sumon married three years ago and had a two-year-old son, his family said. Over the past decade, hundreds of Bangladeshis have been murdered in South Africa over business and personal disputes. On April 9, a Bangladeshi youth -- Sohan Hossain, 18, son of Md Dulal of Chikanmati village in Thakurgaon’s Ranishankoil upazila -- was shot dead by unidentified assailants in Zonkizizwe Township of Katlehong in Johannesburg.

title: TikToker sent to jail over harassment of Russian nationals in Natore
body: A TikToker from Rajshahi was sent to jail today following the harassment of two Russian nationals at Green Valley Park in Natore’s Lalpur upazila. Aminul Islam, 29, from Mohanpur in Rajshahi, was produced before a court and subsequently sent to jail, Lalpur Police Station Officer-in-Charge Shafikul Islam said. Another person, Russel Islam, 23, was also detained by police. However, police said he is currently under observation following a court order. Both were detained during a raid in the Rajshahi city corporation area early this morning, the OC said. According to police, the incident took place around 3:00pm on Friday when two Russian nationals working at the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant visited Green Valley Park. At the time, a group of self-proclaimed TikTokers, who were at the park for a picnic, surrounded the two foreigners to film videos. During the encounter, the Russian nationals were subjected to verbal abuse and obscene language, police said. The incident drew widespread attention after a video of the harassment went viral on social media, prompting strong public criticism. Following the incident, Green Valley Park Manager Wazedur Rahman filed a case against 10 to 15 unidentified individuals on the same day, police added.

title: Two men jailed for posing as journalists to extort school
body: A local court in Brahmanbaria has sentenced two men to five years’ rigorous imprisonment for extortion after finding that they posed as journalists and demanded money from a government primary school. The verdict was delivered today by Judge Masud Parvez of the Additional District and Sessions Judge 2nd Court. The accused, SM Ali Azam and Ashikur Rahman Rony, were present in court during the verdict. According to the case statement, on September 14, 2021, the two men visited Sharifpur Purba Government Primary School in Ashuganj, introducing themselves as journalists. They reportedly demanded access to financial documents and threatened to publish false reports against teachers when refused, allegedly demanding Tk 20,000 in extortion. Locals and teachers later held Azam, while Rony fled on a motorcycle. Acting on upazila administration instructions, police took Azam into custody. The head teacher Md Habibur Rahman filed a case the same day. Following investigation and witness testimonies, the court found both guilty. Plaintiff’s lawyer Syed Tafsir Ahmed Tanvir said the convicts had long used false journalist identities to extort money from schools and other institutions. Ashuganj Press Club President Selim Parvez said the men were not part of mainstream journalism and had instead used obscure press cards and unauthorised Facebook pages to deceive people.

title: Court orders DNA test in Netrokona child rape case
body: Amanullah Mahmudi Sagar, the accused in a widely discussed rape case in Netrokona’s Madan upazila that left a child pregnant, did not make a confessional statement during remand. Netrokona Court Inspector Mohammad Riyad Mahmud confirmed the matter to The Daily Star. After his remand period ended, he was produced before a court today, which ordered him to be sent to prison. According to Riyad Mahmud, police later submitted an application seeking a DNA test. The court approved the request and directed the authorities to take necessary steps to carry out the test.

title: Asaduzzaman Noor gets bail in 2 cases, but cannot be released yet
body: The High Court today granted permanent bail to former Awami League minister for cultural affairs Asaduzzaman Noor in two cases. The cases were filed with Mirpur and Ramna Model police stations in Dhaka on September 4 and 5, 2024, over the killings of Mamun and Liza Akhter, respectively, during the July uprising. Today, the High Court bench of Justice KM Zahid Sarwar and Justice Sheikh Abu Taher delivered the verdicts after hearing two separate petitions Noor filed last year, seeking bail on the grounds of ill health and prolonged detention. Earlier on May 4 and 5, the same bench granted Noor bail in two other cases but refused bail in another case on May 5. Noor, who has been in jail since September 13, 2024, will not be released following the High Court rulings as he is facing several other cases, his lawyer ZI Khan Panna said. Barrister Rehan Hussain also represented Noor during the hearing on the bail petitions. ZI Khan Panna said detained former Awami League chief whip ASM Feroz also secured bail from the High Court in a case yesterday, though he could not provide details of the case. Deputy Attorney General Syed Shajia Sharmin told The Daily Star that the state will file separate appeals before the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court, challenging the High Court bail orders.

title: Youth arrested for rape of 10‑year‑old in Gopalganj
body: Police have arrested a youth accused of raping a 10-year-old child in Kashiani upazila of Gopalganj. The arrestee, Morsalin Sheikh alias Raju (20), of Nizamkandi village, was arrested from Keraniganj late last night (May 9) in a special operation, Kashiani police said in a statement. The child's grandmother filed a case with Kashiani Police Station on Saturday night, confirmed Inspector (Investigation) Sheikh Taj Uddin Ahmed, its officer-in-charge. According to the case statement, the child has been living with her grandmother since her parents separated 9 years ago. On Sunday (April 3), she went to visit her aunt's house in Nizamkandi village of Kashiani upazila from her grandmother's house in Bongram of Sadar upazila. On Thursday (April 7), Mursalin, a neighbour of the aunt, took the child to a nearby forest and raped her. When the child became unconscious, Mursalin left her behind. Later, she regained consciousness at 3:00pm and returned to the aunt's house, the complaint added. When the family members found out about the matter, the victim was admitted to the 250-bed General Hospital in Gopalganj that evening. Dr Jibitesh Biswas, superintendent of the 250-bed Gopalganj General Hospital, said the child was indeed raped and was admitted to the hospital.

title: ICT-1 frames charges against Taposh, Nanak, 26 others over July uprising killings
body: The International Crimes Tribunal-1 today framed charges against former DSCC mayor Sheikh Fazle Noor Taposh, former minister Jahangir Kabir Nanak, and 26 others for crimes against humanity over the killing of nine people during the 2024 July uprising. The victims included two students who were killed in Mohammadpur. The tribunal, led by Justice Md Golam Mortuza Mozumder, framed charges against the accused, rejecting their discharge applications. While framing the charges, the tribunal said the materials on record were adequate to move forward with the trial. Other accused include former DMP commissioner Habibur Rahman, joint commissioner Biplob Kumar Sarker, former additional DIG Proloy Kumar Joarder, and the then additional DC of DMP’s Mohammadpur Zone Rawshanul Haque Shaikat.

title: Bangladeshi expat shot dead in South Africa, family says
body: A Bangladeshi businessman was shot dead by unidentified assailants in South Africa yesterday afternoon, according to the victim's family. The deceased, Sumon Miah, 34, hailed from Abhirampur Paschim Para area of Banshoil union in Mirzapur upazila of Tangail, Abdullah Al Mamun, officer-in-charge of Mirzapur Police Station, confirmed citing family members. Sumon's father told reporters that his acquaintances in South Africa informed the family of the incident over the phone immediately. Sumon's body may reach Bangladesh on Tuesday, the father said. title: Missing for 31 days, youth’s body found buried under cowshed floor in Jashore
body: Police recovered the body of a young man late last night from underneath a cowshed floor in Jashore’s Sharsha upazila. The victim, Ikramul Kabir, 25, of South Baropota village in Sharsha, had been missing since April 8, said police. Police have detained a couple -- Al Furad and his wife Munni Begum, 22, of Bosotpur Purbo Para area in connection with the killing, confirmed Sharsha Police Station Officer-in-Charge Maruf Hossain. He said a joint raid was conducted last night at the couple’s house in Bosotpur village based on the information provided by Furad after detectives detained him in connection with a missing case. Investigators initially suspect that Ikramul was strangulated to death following a dispute over an alleged extramarital affair and financial transactions, before the body was secretly buried. Ikramul had allegedly been involved in an extramarital relationship with Munni. He reportedly went missing on April 8 after going to collect money that was owed to him by the woman, said police citing family and locals. As there was no trace of him, suspicions grew and police launched an investigation after his family made a complaint. According to the complaint, Ikramul was called out from his sister’s house in the Setai area of Sharsha on the night of April 8. His mobile phone remained switched off from that time onward. Family members then contacted Sharsha and Benapole port police and Detective Branch. During the drive, police excavated the floor of a cowshed and recovered Ikramul’s body buried underground. Locals demanded exemplary punishment for those involved in the murder. Abdur Rashid, father of the deceased and the plaintiff in the case, alleged the family had received repeated ransom demands of Tk 10 lakh, but despite efforts, they could not trace him. Sharsha Police Station OC Maruf Hossain said the body has been sent to Jashore General Hospital morgue for autopsy “We hope to uncover the motive behind the murder after completing the investigation. Legal action will be taken against all those involved,” he added.

title: Mob beats 3 to death over cattle theft allegation in Gazipur
body: A mob beat three people to death over allegations of cattle theft in Kaliakair upazila of Gazipur early today. During the incident, locals also set fire to a pickup van allegedly used by the victims. The identities of the three individuals could not be known immediately, said police. Kaliakair Police Station Inspector (Operations) Md Robiul Islam said the incident took place in Bagchala Bazar area of the upazila early Sunday. According to witnesses, a suspected gang of cattle thieves was passing through the Bagchala area in a pickup van. Locals were alerted and chased them down. The suspects were caught and beaten by the mob. Later, the pickup van was set on fire. On information, police went to the scene and rescued the three critically injured men before taking them to Shaheed Tajuddin Ahmad Medical College Hospital, where doctors declared them dead. Officer-in-Charge (OC) of Kaliakair Police Station Shahidul Islam said legal action will be taken after investigation.

title: 2 killed in BSF firing along B’baria border
body: Two Bangladeshi men, including a college student, were killed after members of India’s Border Security Force (BSF) opened fire along the border in Kasba upazila of Brahmanbaria late Friday night. The incident marks the second fatal border shooting by the BSF in the last 30 days. The victims were identified as Md Morsalin, 20, of Dhajanagar village, and Nobir Hossain, 40, of Madhupur village. Morsalin was a second-year student at Gopinathpur Alhaj Shah Alam Degree College and was preparing for his upcoming HSC exams, said family members. The shooting incident took place inside Indian territory near the Dhajnagar-Pathariyadwar border, according to a BGB press release signed by BGB 60 Battalion Commander Lt Col SM Shariful Islam. A group of about 15 Bangladeshis trespassed nearly 200 yards into the Indian territory around 11:00pm on Friday for “smuggling purposes”. As they were returning to Bangladesh, a patrol team from the BSF 49 Battalion intercepted the group. A scuffle reportedly broke out before BSF personnel fired two rounds of shotgun pellets, the press release said. The injured were taken to the Bishalgarh hospital in Tripura, India, where they died while undergoing treatment, the BGB said, citing BSF authorities. Their bodies were handed over to the BGB following a battalion-level flag meeting at the Khirnal border area of Kasba in the afternoon Lt Col SM Shariful Islam, confirmed the matter, saying the BGB lodged a protest with the BSF over the incident.At Morsalin’s home in Dhajnagar, his father Hebju Miya said local youths had called his son out on Friday night. “I demand a proper investigation and justice for my son’s killing. He was a college student and was supposed to sit for his HSC exams this year.” Speaking through tears, Morsalin’s mother pleaded for the return of his body. In Madhupur village, Nobir Hossain’s son Tapan said, “My father had been away from home since Friday evening. Later we learnt that he had been killed in BSF firing.” According to rights organisation Ain o Salish Kendra, at least 34 Bangladeshis were killed by the BSF in 2025, including 24 in shootings and 10 allegedly due to physical torture. At least 38 others were also injured. This year, at least five Bangladeshis have been killed by the BSF till yesterday, including three in shootings and two allegedly due to physical torture, while four others were injured. On April 8, Ali Hossain, 49, was killed in BSF firing along the Dhabalguri border in Patgram, Lalmonirhat. A day earlier, the BSF had expressed regret over the shooting and injuring of another Bangladeshi youth, Mizan, in the same border area. On April 28, Zahed Ur Rahman, the prime minister’s information and broadcasting adviser, said border killings have fallen by 75 percent and that the government wants to bring it down to zero, which is possible through diplomatic efforts with neighbouring countries. On March 1, Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed said Bangladesh did not want any killings along the border and that India had also expressed sincerity on the issue after the outgoing Indian High Commissioner to Bangladesh Pranay Verma met him at his office. Border killings were also among the key issues discussed during Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman’s visit to New Delhi last month.

title: UPDF member shot dead
body: A member of Prosit Khisa-led United People’s Democratic Front (UPDF) was yesterday shot dead in Sajek union of Baghaichhari upazila in Rangamati. The incident occurred in the Shuknochori area of Sajek, located on the Marishya-Dighinala road. The deceased was identified as Hegera Chakma, 49. “UPDF member Hegera Chakma alias Tarun and two others spent the night at a house in Shuknochari village. When he was leaving for organisational work at around 5:45am today, terrorists of the UPDF (Democratic), who had been lying in wait, opened fire on him. He died on the spot,” said UPDF spokesperson Angya Marma in a statement. Marma blamed the UPDF Democratic Party for the murder. However, several leaders of the UPDF Democratic Party were contacted regarding the allegations, but no response was received. Police recovered the body from the scene; the body was sent to Khagrachhari Sadar Hospital for autopsy, Tofazzal Hossain, the officer-in-charge of Sajek Police Station, told The Daily Star. “No one has filed any complaint with us yet,” he said. Leaders and activists of UPDF and allied organisations staged protest and blocked the road for an hour at Ujobazar demanding a trial of the killers. They also announced a half-day blockade on the main road of Sajek Tourism on Monday protesting the murder.

title: One held over torture and abetment to teen’s suicide
body: Police on Friday arrested one person over the torture and abetment to the suicide of a teenager in Pabna’s Chatmohar upazila. Earlier that evening, police recovered the girl’s body from her residence. According to the victim’s family, the 14-year-old was assaulted and humiliated by her employer over allegations of theft earlier that day. The child used to work as a domestic helper at the home of one Hannan Mollah, who lived in the same village as the girl’s family. On Friday morning, Tk 120 went missing from Mollah’s house. The family blamed the child and tied her to a pillar and beat her in front of locals, many of whom recorded the incident. According to the child’s uncle, she could not bear the humiliation and took her own life. “We want justice,” he told journalists. The victim’s father filed a case against four people, including Hannan Mollah, with Chatmohar Police Station the same night. He accused them of torture and abetment to suicide. Speaking to The Daily Star last night, Golam Mostafa, officer-in-charge of Chatmohar Police Station, said police were trying to arrest the other accused. “In our primary investigation, we confirmed it was a suicide. We are investigating the allegations of torture,” he said, adding that the body was sent to hospital for autopsy.

title: Woman, three daughters among five murdered
body: The bodies of five members of a family, including three children, were found with their throats slit at their house in Gazipur’s Kapasia upazila yesterday morning. The deceased were identified as Sharmin, 35; her three daughters -- Mim, 16, Maria, 8, and Faria, 2 -- and her brother, Rasul, 22.
