About six months ago, Sharmin returned to her father’s home in Gopalganj but was later sent back to her husband. Uzzal also alleged that Forkan kept demanding money from the family, leading to repeated disputes. Shahin, another relative of Sharmin, said Forkan called his brother, Mishkat, on the night of the incident to tell him he had killed everyone in the house. He then asked Mishkat to let Sharmin’s family know. Mishkat could not be reached over the phone despite repeated attempts. After being informed early yesterday, Sharmin’s family asked their relatives in Gazipur to check on the house. After finding the bodies, they informed police, who recovered them around 8:00am. Lutfunnahar, wife of the house owner Monir Hossain, who is an expatriate, said her husband is currently in Singapore. She and her daughter live in a house near Sharmin’s. “After receiving the information, I went to the house and saw Sharmin wearing new clothes, tied up and hanging from the window grille, Rasul on a bed, and the three children on the floor -- all dead.” Sharmin’s nephew, Sakib Al Hasan Biswas, a student of Bhawal Ideal School and College, said Rasul had recently come to Kapasia after being lured by Forkan with promises of employment. Contacted by The Daily Star, Asaduzzaman, additional superintendent of police (Kapasia-Kaliganj Circle), said preliminary findings suggest that Forkan killed all five with a sharp weapon. “The incident may have occurred due to a family feud.” Police are investigating whether sedatives or sleeping pills were used before the murders. Additional District Magistrate Salma Khatun described the incident as deeply heartbreaking and said those responsible would be brought to justice after a thorough investigation.

title: Night guard held over attempted rape of 3-year-old in Jamalpur
body: Police have arrested a night guard for allegedly attempting to rape a three-year-old girl in Dewanganj upazila of Jamalpur. The accused, Abdul Khalek, 45, was sent to court this afternoon after being arrested from Char Kalikapur Durga Bagan Bari area last night, said Dewanganj Model Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Anwar Hossain. According to police and family sources, the girl went to play at the Durga Bagan Bari area yesterday afternoon. At the time, the accused lured her and attempted to rape her. Hearing her screams, locals rushed to the spot and rescued her. The victim’s mother later filed a case with Dewanganj Model Police Station over the incident, said the OC.

title: 9-yr-old murdered in Mymensingh
body: A madrasa student was allegedly abducted and murdered following a dispute with his father over online gambling in Mymensingh’s Muktagacha upazila this afternoon. Deceased Andaleeb Sadman Rafi, 9, of Jominpur village, was a class 2 student at a residential madrasa in Muktagacha, said Muktagacha Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Kamrul Hasan. Quoting the victim’s family, the OC said the child had been missing since yesterday morning. A general diary (GD) was lodged with Muktagacha Police Station last night in this connection. Based on suspicion raised by the child’s father, police detained Nur Muhammad Khokon, 20, a neighbour, this morning. During interrogation, Khokon admitted that he was addicted to online gambling. The child’s father, Jahirul Islam, often tried to stop him from gambling, which led to disputes between them. Out of anger, Khokon abducted and killed the child and hid the body in a sack, said the OC. Following Khokon’s statement, police conducted a raid this afternoon and recovered the body inside a sack from the septic tank at his house. Police are investigating the incident, added the OC.

title: Case filed over Gazipur family murder, two detained
body: A case has been filed over the murder of five people, including three children, their mother, and a young man, who were found with their throats slit in Rautkona village of Kapasia in Gazipur. Police have detained two people for questioning in connection with the incident, said Gazipur Superintendent of Police Md Sharif Uddin. Shahadat Molla, father of deceased Sharmin, lodged the case at Kapasia Police Station at around 7:35pm today, said Kapasia Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Md Shahinur Alam. The prime accused in the case is Sharmin’s husband, Forkan Mia. Additionally, three to four unidentified individuals have also been named as accused. The OC said accused Forkan, of Mary Gopinathpur village in Gopalganj Sadar upazila, has been absconding since the incident. The deceased were identified as Forkan’s wife Sharmin, 35, their children Mim, 16, Maria, 8, Faria, 2, and Sharmin’s brother Rasul, 22. According to local sources, Forkan worked as a private car driver. He married Sharmin around 20 years ago, and for the past year they had been living with their children in a rented house owned by expatriate Monir Hossain in Rautkona village. The killings took place at the house late last night. Police initially suspect that the murders stemmed from family disputes. Additional Superintendent of Police (Kapasia-Kaliganj Circle) Asaduzzaman said preliminary investigations suggest Forkan may have slaughtered all five victims. However, investigators are still examining how a single person could have carried out the killings alone. Police are also investigating whether the victims had been given sedatives or sleeping pills before the murders. Additional District Magistrate Salma Khatun described the incident as “extremely heartbreaking” and said those responsible would be brought to justice following a swift investigation.

title: UPDF member shot dead in Rangamati
body: A member of the United People's Democratic Front (UPDF), led by Prosit Khisa, was shot dead in Sajek union of Baghaichhari upazila in Rangamati. The incident took place this morning in the Shuknochori area of Sajek on the Marishya-Dighinala road. The deceased was identified as Hegera Chakma, 49, a UPDF member. He was the son of Rangamani Chakma of Retkaba village in Sajek. UPDF spokesperson Angya Marma condemned and protested the incident in a statement issued to the media. In the statement, he said, "UPDF member Hegera Chakma alias Tarun and two others spent the night at a house in Shuknochari village. When he was leaving for organisational work at around 5:45am today, terrorists of the UPDF (Democratic), who had been lying in wait, opened fire on him. He died on the spot." In the statement, the UPDF leader blamed the UPDF Democratic Party for the murder. However, several leaders of the UPDF Democratic Party were contacted regarding the allegations, but no response was received. Sajek Police Station Officer-in-Charge Tofazzal Hossain told The Daily Star, "We have recovered the body from the scene. The body has been sent to Khagrachhari Sadar Hospital for autopsy. No one has filed any complaint with us yet."

title: Two Bangladeshis killed by BSF in Brahmanbaria: BGB
body: Two Bangladeshi nationals were killed by members of India’s Border Security Force (BSF) along the border in Kasba upazila of Brahmanbaria late last night, according to a Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) press release issued today. According to the BGB statement, BSF personnel opened fire with pellet guns during an incident along the Dhajanagar-Pathariyadwar border area, leaving the two Bangladeshis injured. The BSF later confirmed that both men died while undergoing treatment at a hospital in India. One of them were identified as Md Mursalin, 20, of Dhajanagar village in Kasba upazila. Mursalin was an 11th-grade student of Gopinathpur Alhaz Shah Alam Degree College, said Kasba Upazila Nirbahi Officer Shamiul Islam. According to the BGB statement, the BSF confirmed that both men died while undergoing treatment at a hospital in India after suffering injuries during the incident. BGB said that, based on intelligence information, around 15 Bangladeshi smugglers entered approximately 200 yards inside Indian territory through the Dhajanagar-Pathariyadwar border area around 11:05pm yesterday with assistance from Indian smugglers. The statement said that, while returning with smuggled goods from India, the group was intercepted by a patrol team from the Pathariyadwar camp of the 49 BSF Battalion. At one stage, the Bangladeshi smugglers allegedly attacked BSF personnel, leading to a scuffle and physical altercation, the release added. During the clash, a BSF member fired two rounds of pellet at the smugglers, according to BGB. The statement said the commanding officer of the 60 BGB Battalion (Sultanpur Battalion) has contacted the BSF commandant regarding the repatriation of the bodies. A protest note is being sent to the BSF, while arrangements for a flag meeting between the two border forces are underway, the statement added. BGB also claimed that the two men had previously been directly involved in transporting smuggled goods across the border.

title: Mother, three children among 5 murdered over 'family dispute' in Gazipur
body: Five members of a family, including three children, were murdered allegedly over a family dispute at Rautkona village in Gazipur’s Kapasia upazila. The deceased were identified as Sharmin, 35, her three daughters -- Mim, 16, Maria, 8, and Faria, 2, -- and her brother Rasul, 22. Mim was a class nine student at the local Rautkona Madrasa, while Maria was in class two. Sharmin’s husband, Md Forkan Miah, remains absconding since the incident. Forkan, who is from Meri Gopinathpur village in Gopalganj Sadar upazila, was reportedly a private car driver and had been living at the rented house with his wife and children for nearly a year. Confirming the killings, Sharifuddin, superintendent of police of Gazipur, said two people were detained for interrogation. Talking to reporters, Sharmin’s uncle, Uzzal, said Forkan frequently assaulted his wife, which left her physically unwell. About six months ago, Sharmin returned to her father’s home in Gopalganj Sadar upazila but was later sent back to her husband’s house. He also alleged that Forkan often demanded money from the family, leading to ongoing disputes. Another relative, Shahin, said Forkan called his brother Mishkat on the night of the incident and claimed that he had killed everyone in the house, asking him to inform the family. Mishkat’s wife later informed Forkan’s in-laws in Gopalganj. Lutfunnahar, wife of house owner Monir Hossain, an expatriate, said her husband is currently in Singapore, while she lives nearby with her daughter. After receiving the information, she went to the scene and saw Sharmin hanging from a window wearing new clothes, Rasul lying on a bed, and the three children on the floor. Sharmin’s nephew, Sakib Al Hasan Biswas, a student of Bhawal Ideal School and College and a relative of the deceased, said they used to live together in Gazipur and that Rasul had recently come to Kapasia in search of a job after being lured by Forkan with promises of employment. Additional Superintendent of Police (Kapasia-Kaliganj Circle) Asaduzzaman told The Daily Star that preliminary findings suggest Forkan killed the five family members with a sharp weapon. The incident may have occurred due to a family conflict, he said. Police are investigating how a single person could carry out the killings and whether sedatives or sleeping pills were used before the murders. Additional District Magistrate Salma Khatun described the incident as deeply heartbreaking and said those responsible would be brought to justice after a thorough investigation.

title: ASI arrested over personal use of seized car in Gazipur
body: An official of Pubail Police Station under Gazipur Metropolitan Police (GMP) has been arrested for allegedly using a seized stolen private car for personal purposes. Assistant Sub-Inspector (ASI) Alamgir Hossain was arrested by a GMP team on Thursday after the car owner, Sharif Hossain Patwari, filed a case against him in this connection, Abu Bakar Siddique, inspector (investigation) of Pubail Police Station, told The Daily Star on Friday night. He said Alamgir was sent to jail by a court, and no remand application has been filed. Before his arrest, he was suspended from the job following the same allegation, Abu Bakar added. According to police sources, ASI Alamgir seized a stolen private car on Wednesday and brought it to the police station. Later, he allegedly started using the vehicle for his personal activities. After the matter came to light, the Police Headquarters investigated the incident and found the allegations to be true. He was then suspended. In connection with the incident, the vehicle owner filed the case against suspended ASI Alamgir with Pubail Police Station. Md Belayet Hossain, additional commissioner (Crime and Operation) of Gazipur Metropolitan Police, said ASI Alamgir was suspended and later arrested over allegations of using a seized vehicle kept under police custody for personal use.

title: Noor Ali, firm sued over laundering of Tk 115cr
body: The Criminal Investigation Department (CID) has filed a Tk 115.58 crore money laundering case against Unique Group chief Mohd Noor Ali and Borak Real Estate over allegations of building a 28-storey structure on government land in Banani and laundering earnings from hotel operations there. In a press release issued yesterday, the CID said preliminary findings found evidence that the accused illegally earned and laundered Tk 115,58,24,707 by operating a hotel business in an unauthorised building. The CID alleged irregularities and fraud in the “Banani Super Market cum Housing” project on government land under DNCC control. The case was filed with Banani Police Station on May 7 under sections 4(2) and 4(4) of the Money Laundering Prevention Act-2012. According to the CID, Borak Real Estate had an agreement to construct a 14-storey building in Banani, but allegedly violated the terms by constructing a 28-storey building without approval. Later, the Sheraton Dhaka five-star hotel was established there. The CID alleged that the project was not completed within the stipulated time and that DNCC did not receive its due share. It also alleged that the agreement was revised several times through influence. The investigation also found that the required no-objection certificates from Rajuk and the Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh were not obtained during construction, the CID said. According to the press release, the building exceeded the approved height limit, creating risks and obstacles for aircraft take-off and landing. The CID said the accused later transferred, converted and moved the illegally earned money through various means, constituting money laundering. It added that the amount of laundered money could increase after determining the actual value of the allegedly occupied assets. The CID’s Financial Crime Division is currently investigating the case and operations are ongoing to uncover further information and arrest the accused, the press release said. The Daily Star tried to contact Noor Ali for comments, but his phone was found switched off.

title: Man beaten to death on theft suspicion
body: A man was beaten to death by a mob while allegedly trying to flee after a burglary in Bogura’s Shibganj upazila early yesterday. The deceased was identified as Selim Fakir, a resident of Tinkunja village in Kahalu upazila of the district. According to locals and police, the incident took place between 3:00am and 4:00am at the house of Gopal Chandra in Chhatua Matalpara village. “Early this morning, three thieves entered Gopal Chandra’s house by digging a tunnel. Selim Fakir was caught by locals while trying to flee after the burglary. He died on the spot after being beaten by villagers,” Shibganj Police Station Officer-in-Charge Shahinuzzaman Shahin told The Daily Star. The OC said police recovered the body and sent it to a hospital for autopsy. Preparations are underway to file two cases, one over the alleged theft and another over the mob beating that led to his death, he added. Police said Selim was accused in nine cases, including theft and robbery. Purnima Saha, daughter-in-law of Gopal Chandra, said two thieves entered their house by digging a tunnel. She alleged that the intruders held her and her child hostage at knifepoint after entering the house. She said they took Tk 3.5 lakh in cash, eight bhori of gold ornaments, and the jewellery she was wearing at the time. “When they were trying to escape, we screamed for help, and my brother-in-law tried to catch one of them. Later, the villagers arrived and managed to catch one person,” Purnima said.

title: Rooppur plant gets automated control system for unit-1
body: Russia’s Rosatom nuclear energy corporation has completed the delivery and installation of the full automated process control system (APCS) for the first power unit of the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant. “This is another milestone in Bangladesh’s first nuclear power project,” Rosatom said in a press release yesterday. The system was supplied by Rosatom Automated Control Systems (RASU). The delivery included 22 subsystems covering automated process control and radiation monitoring for unit-1, which features a VVER-1200 reactor. Saikat Ahmed, media focal point officer of Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant, said the systems act as the plant’s “brain”, using operational and safety controllers to adjust valves and pumps instantly, keeping the plant within safe operating envelopes. APCS in nuclear power plants are sophisticated, safety-critical digital networks that monitor thousands of sensors -- tracking temperature, pressure, and flow rates -- to automatically manage reactor operations and ensure safety, he added. The system will monitor equipment performance, electricity generation, and technological processes during both commissioning and operational phases of the power unit. “Currently, all the automated process control equipment for the first power unit of the Rooppur NPP has been delivered and commissioned at the construction site,” said Gleb Murashov, managing director of Automated Process Control System Division at RASU. “We have implemented several improvements as part of the project. For example, the automated radiation monitoring systems have been implemented in a compact, bench-type design, a first for this type,” he added. The Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant is being constructed with Russian technology and will consist of two VVER-1200 reactors with a combined capacity of 2,400 megawatts. The Generation III+ reactor design complies with international safety standards. Fuel loading began at the unit-1 on April 28, taking the project into operational stage.

title: UP member missing for over three days
body: A union parishad member in Patuakhali Sadar upazila has been missing for over three days. Md Shahidul Islam Jomaddar, 37, is a member of Ward 3 of Lohalia Union Parishad. According to family sources, Shahidul left home around 7:30pm on Tuesday and headed towards the Patuakhali-Lohalia road. Since then, his whereabouts have remained unknown. After searching different locations without success, the family sought assistance from police. Family members said Shahidul was recently married and had been actively carrying out his public duties since being elected as a UP member by a large margin in the local government election. His maternal uncle, Md Sohrab Hossain, filed a GD with police the day after his disappearance. Patuakhali Sadar Police Station Officer-in-Charge Md Moniruzzaman said police are investigating the matter.

title: Journo arrested in 5 cases over clash, attack on students
body: Police have arrested a local journalist in Khagrachhari in five cases filed at different police stations in the district. Jiten Barua, former president of Khagrachhari Press Club, is a Somoy TV staff reporter and BSS Khagrachari correspondent. He was arrested in the town’s Shapla Chattar area on Thursday evening, said Md Kay Kislu, officer-in-charge of Khagrachhari Sadar Police Station. Of the five cases, two were filed with Khagrachari Sadar Police Station, while one each was filed with Dighinala, Matiranga, and Panchhari police stations, said the OC. Four cases are related to a clash involving BNP and Awami League activists in Khagrachhari district in 2023. The other case was filed over an attack on students on August 4, 2024. He was produced before a Khagrachari court yesterday, the police official added.

title: Body of 9-year-old girl found 5 days after she went missing in Cox’s Bazar
body: Police have recovered the partially decomposed body of a nine-year-old girl from a hilly slope in Cox’s Bazar Sadar upazila, five days after she went missing. The victim was identified as Urmi Akter, daughter of Abdur Rashid and Rasheda Akter of Kadamtali area under Khurushkul union in the upazila, police said. According to locals, Urmi went missing on the morning of May 2 after leaving home to play. After failing to find her despite extensive searches, her family filed a general diary with Cox’s Bazar Sadar Model Police Station on May 4. On Thursday afternoon, locals noticed a foul smell coming from a hilly slope in the Kadamtali area. They later discovered Urmi's body and informed police. Md Chomiuddin, officer-in-charge of Cox’s Bazar Sadar Model Police Station, said the body was recovered in a decomposed condition and sent to Cox’s Bazar Sadar Hospital morgue for an autopsy. The OC also said makeshift shelters reportedly used by drug users and dealers had been set up near the spot, and police are investigating the incident from all possible angles. Earlier, on April 22, the body of temple caretaker Nayan Das was found hanging from a tree in the same area, three days after he had gone missing on April 19. The two incidents have spread panic among local residents, who demanded the immediate identification and arrest of those involved.

title: Man beaten to death by mob after alleged burglary in Bogura

title: Young man shot dead in Chattogram city; 11-year-old girl injured
body: A young man was shot dead and an 11-year-old girl sustained bullet injuries after miscreants opened fire targeting the youth in Chattogram city's Rowfabad area on Thursday night. The deceased was identified as Hasan alias Raju, 24, a resident of Raozan upazila in Chattogram, police said. The incident took place at Shaheed Minar Goli in Rowfabad. Reshmi Akter, 11, suffered bullet injuries to her eyes and was admitted to Chattogram Medical College Hospital (CMCH), said Sub-Inspector (SI) Nur Alam Ashek, also in-charge of the CMCH police outpost. Bayezid Bostami Police Station Sub-Inspector Shahidul Islam told The Daily Star, “Raju came to Rowfabad from Raozan on May 3 to visit his sister. Around 9:15pm on Thursday, armed miscreants opened fire on Raju, leaving him dead on the spot.” Reshmi, a resident of Rowfabad area, sustained bullet injuries during the attack, said SI Shahidul. “Panic spread among locals following the incident, while the miscreants fled the scene after the attack,” he said. Later, police recovered Raju’s body from the spot, the police official added. The motive behind the killing is yet to be determined, though police are trying to link the murder to the recent spree of shootings in Raozan that has left 23 people dead over the past 22 months.

title: Man shot dead, 11-year-old girl injured in Ctg
body: A young man was shot dead, and an 11-year-old girl sustained bullet injuries after criminals opened fire in Chattogram city’s Rowfabad area last night. The deceased was identified as Hasan alias Raju, 24, a resident of Raozan upazila in Chattogram, police said. The incident took place at Shaheed Minar alley in Rowfabad. The motive behind the killing is yet to be determined, though police primarily believe the murder may be linked to the recent spree of shootings in Raozan that has left dozens dead.

title: 9-yr-old boy dies after air pumped into his rectum
body: A nine-year-old boy died after compressed air was reportedly pumped through his rectum using a tyre inflator machine at an auto-rickshaw garage in Narsingdi’s Palash upazila yesterday. The deceased, Ramim Mia, was the son of Ripon Mia of Gajaria Charkarardi village in the upazila, said Shahed Al Mamun, officer-in-charge of Palash Police Station. The incident took place around 9:00am at a battery-run auto-rickshaw garage in Gajaria Bazar, he said, quoting family members and locals. According to the family, Ramim had gone to the market to visit his grandfather, Amzad Hossain, who is a corrugated sheet trader there. The child’s father also has a sanitary goods shop in the market, the OC said. At one point, Ramim went to a nearby auto-rickshaw garage owned by one Faisal Mia. There, Sabuj Mia, 34, a rickshaw puller, allegedly pumped compressed air through the child’s rectum using a tyre inflator as a “prank”, said Ramim’s father, Ripon. He added that the child soon fell critically ill as his abdomen swelled severely. Hearing his screams, locals rescued him and rushed him to Narsingdi District Hospital. After primary treatment, doctors referred the child to Dhaka for advanced care. He later died around 5:15pm while undergoing treatment at a private hospital in the capital. Ripon demanded exemplary punishment for those who killed his son. Md Rakib Askari, duty doctor at the emergency department of Narsingdi District Hospital, said excessive air pressure likely ruptured parts of Ramim’s intestine, causing internal bleeding, severe abdominal pain, and breathing complications. Following an autopsy, the child’s body was taken to his family’s village home in Narsingdi, where he was buried yesterday afternoon. Meanwhile, the family filed a written complaint in the evening against Faisal Mia, Sabuj Mia, and four to five unnamed others, Ripon said. Confirming the matter, OC Shahed said legal action would be taken as per the complaint and that operations were already underway to arrest those involved.

title: Madrasa superintendent arrested over attempted rape of student in Noakhali
body: Police today arrested a local madrasa superintendent for allegedly attempting to rape a student in Noakhali’s Subarnachar upazila on February 5 this year. Abul Khayer, 35, was arrested from Maizdee area of the district town this afternoon based on tip-off, said Md Lutfur Rahman, officer-in-charge (OC) of Char Jabbar Police Station in Subarnachar. The accused went into hiding after the victim’s father filed a written complaint against him with Char Jabbar Police Station on April 15. Police later recorded the complaint as a regular case following an investigation. According to the case statement, the 14-year-old girl was a resident student at a local madrasa where Abul Khayer, 35, is the superintendent. On February 5, the girl’s grandmother went to the madrasa to see the girl. At that time, Abul Khayer told the grandmother that the girl had been attacked by an “evil power” and she needed an exorcism. Abul Khayer took the girl to his bedroom on the madrasa premises and tried to rape her under the pretext of exorcism, according to the case statement. When the girl started screaming, Abul Khayer released her. The victim shared the incident with her grandmother. Later, the victim’s family members informed local union parishad’s acting chairman Jamal Uddin about the matter. But Jamal kept wasting time in the name of social arbitration to settle the issue, they said Eventually, the girl's father later filed the case with Char Jabbar Police Station. After the case was filed, around 100 people attacked the victim’s house, assaulted the family members and carried out vandalism and looting, the family alleged. A video of the attack had gone viral on social media, sparking criticism among netizens.

title: Narsingdi freedom fighter murder: Accused extradited from Dubai via Interpol
body: The Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) has brought back an accused in the murder case of a freedom fighter in Narsingdi from Dubai with the assistance of Interpol. The accused, Arif Sarkar, 40, of Putia Kamargaon village in Shibpur upazila of Narsingdi, was produced before a court yesterday following his extradition. In a press release issued today, PBI said Md Harunur Rashid Khan, a former chairman of Shibpur Upazila Parishad, was shot and seriously injured at his home on February 25, 2023. He died on May 31 the same year while undergoing treatment. The victim’s son, Amanur Rashid Khan, filed a case with Shibpur Model Police Station on February 27, 2023, naming several individuals, including Arif. While local police initially investigated the matter, the probe was handed over to PBI Narsingdi on June 23, 2023, following an application by the plaintiff and instructions from Police Headquarters. PBI officials said the investigation gained momentum after another accused, Mohsin, was arrested in Dubai through Interpol. During interrogation, Mohsin provided information on the involvement and planning of Arif and other suspects. After obtaining specific evidence, PBI sought assistance from the National Central Bureau (NCB) of Police Headquarters to trace Arif’s location. Once it was confirmed that he was staying in Dubai, an arrest warrant was issued and an Interpol Red Notice was published to bring him back to the country. PBI further said a charge sheet was filed against Arif and other accused on November 24, 2025. Following his arrest by Dubai police, a special team coordinated by PBI and Police Headquarters brought him back to Bangladesh. Arif was handed over to Shibpur Police at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport as an arrest warrant was active against him. He was later produced before the court by Shibpur Police.

title: Ex-DU hall union VP Emi released from Kashimpur jail
body: Sheikh Tasnim Afroze Emi, former vice-president of Shamsunnahar Hall union at Dhaka University and a central vice-presidential candidate in the 2025 Ducsu election, was released today from Kashimpur Women’s Central Jail in Gazipur in a case filed under the Anti-Terrorism Act over playing Sheikh Mujibur Rahman’s March 7 speech. She walked out of jail at around 2:45pm, confirmed Shirin Akter, superintendent of Kashimpur Women’s Central Jail. She said that after the bail documents reached the prison authorities, all legal formalities were completed and Emi was released. The High Court on April 30 granted ad-interim bail to Emi in the anti-terrorism case. According to the case statement, a group of activists from the Awami League, Jubo League and Chhatra League gathered around 3:00pm on March 7 at the Shahidullah Hall crossing and played the historic March 7 speech on a loudspeaker. Police went to the spot after receiving information and detained Md Asif Ahmed Shoikot, former employment affairs secretary of the banned Chhatra League’s Shahidullah Hall unit, with the help of locals while he was trying to flee. Later, around 9:20pm, Abdullah Al Mamun, a leader of the organisation’s Shaheed Sergeant Zahurul Haq Hall unit, and Emi, along with 10-15 unidentified individuals, gathered in front of Gate 1 of the National Museum in Shahbagh. They also obstructed police from performing their duties and tried to snatch Shoikot from police custody, the case statement said. At that point, a group of students led by Ducsu representatives AB Zubair and Musaddiq Ali Ibne Mohammad held Mamun and Emi and handed them over to the police. The following day, the detainees were shown arrested in a case filed under the Anti-Terrorism Act with Shahbagh Police Station and were sent to jail. Police filed the case as the complainant.

title: ‘My body can no longer cope’: Key 1/11 figure Masud Uddin breaks down at ICT
body: The International Crimes Tribunal-2 today ordered the imprisonment of former Feni-3 MP Lt Gen (retd) Masud Uddin Chowdhury -- widely known for his role during the 1/11 caretaker government period -- after showing him arrested in a crimes against humanity case over incidents in Feni district during the July uprising in 2024. The accused was produced before the tribunal this afternoon. Following a prosecution plea in connection with the Feni incident, the tribunal granted permission to interrogate Masud Uddin for one day. Standing in the dock, Masud Uddin raised his hands before the tribunal and pleaded in an emotional voice: “I am a 72-year-old man. My body can no longer cope. I have been on remand since March 23. If possible, please allow the remand after a couple of days.” Prosecutor Mizanul Islam opposed the plea, saying, “Other remands and our interrogation are different. During interrogation, the accused has access to lawyers and doctors. If we fail to interrogate him at the proper time, our investigation will be hampered.” The tribunal then told Masud, “You will have protection during the interrogation. If any problem arises, inform us. We will take necessary steps.” Masud was arrested from his home in Dhaka's Baridhara DOHS on March 24. He previously served as GOC of the 9 Infantry Division during the state of emergency declared on January 11, 2007, and later became chief coordinator of the National Coordination Committee on Serious Crimes and Corruption. He was promoted to lieutenant general and posted to the National Defence College on June 2, 2008. Later, on June 8 that year, he was appointed to the Bangladesh High Commission in Canberra.

title: Shapla Chattar crackdown: ICT asks jail authorities to produce Dipu Moni, two journos on May 14
body: The International Crimes Tribunal-1 today ordered the jail authorities to produce former minister Dipu Moni, former Ekattor TV Managing Director and Editor-in-Chief Mozammel Babu, and the channel’s Principal Correspondent Farzana Rupa before the tribunal on May 14. The order came following a prosecution plea in a crimes against humanity case filed over the 2013 Shapla Chattar crackdown. After court proceedings, Chief Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam told journalists that investigators had found primary involvement of the accused, who are currently in jail custody. “The tribunal ordered that they be produced on May 14, and they may be shown arrested in the case that day,” he said. The prosecution alleged that journalists Mozammel Babu and Farzana Rupa had initially portrayed the Hefazat rally as “hate speech”. Referring to Dipu Moni, prosecutors said she was serving as foreign minister during the crackdown. “She campaigned internationally that law enforcement agencies had eliminated a group of unruly people,” they told the tribunal. Earlier, the chief prosecutor claimed that investigators have so far identified 58 deaths linked to the Shapla Chattar crackdown of May 5, 2013, across four districts.

title: Netrokona madrasa teacher on 3-day remand over rape of 11-year-old girl
body: A local court today placed madrasa teacher Amanullah Mahmudi Sagar on three days’ remand in a case of raping an 11‑year‑old girl in Netrokona's Madan upazila, resulting in her pregnancy. Police produced Sagar before the Netrokona Senior Judicial Magistrate Court at 11:45am today with a seven‑day remand plea. After hearing arguments, the court granted three days. Officer-in-charge of Madan Police Station Mohammad Tariqul Islam confirmed the order. Sagar was arrested yesterday by Rab‑14 from Gouripur in Mymensingh and handed over to Madan police. On April 23, the victim’s mother filed a rape case against him and another person. According to the complaint, on October 2 last year, Sagar lured the girl into his room after classes ended, raped her, and threatened to expel her if she spoke out. The child was allegedly raped on four or five more occasions, according to the complaint. On April 18, the girl’s mother noticed sudden physical changes and took her to a diagnostic centre, where doctors confirmed pregnancy. Police later conducted another medical examination and verified the matter. Sub-inspector of the police station Akhtaruzzaman, also the investigation officer of the case, said the case was filed after medical confirmation.

title: ‘Human trafficking’ to Russia: UK slaps sanctions on Bangladeshi travel agency
body: The United Kingdom has announced a fresh round of sanctions targeting Russia’s drone production network and groups, including a Bangladeshi travel agency, accused of exploiting vulnerable migrants to support Moscow’s war in Ukraine . The new measures, published on May 5, target 35 individuals and organisations, including those linked to human trafficking operations and companies supplying components for Russia’s military drone industry. Bangladesh’s Dream Home Travels and Tours Ltd is among the organisations facing sanctions. The British High Commission in Dhaka said the sanctions relating to Bangladesh target the travel agency for allegedly deceiving and exploiting Bangladeshis to fight in Russia’s war in Ukraine. As part of the sanctions package, the UK is intensifying efforts to disrupt Russia’s military supply chains and networks accused of trafficking foreign migrants into the war effort. The sanctions specifically target individuals involved in recruiting and transporting vulnerable migrants to fight on the frontlines in Ukraine on behalf of Russia, as well as firms supporting Russian drone factories. British officials said the move reflects the UK’s continued commitment to increasing economic pressure on the Kremlin and supporting Ukraine in pursuit of a “just and lasting peace”. According to the UK government, some sanctioned networks lured migrants seeking better opportunities before forcing or pressuring them into military service or work in Russian weapons factories. British authorities highlighted Russia’s “Alabuga Start” programme, linked to a UK-sanctioned entity, which reportedly recruits foreign workers for drone manufacturing. The UK said Russia has sharply increased drone attacks on Ukraine in recent months, causing civilian casualties and damage to critical infrastructure. British officials noted that Russia launched more than 200 drones per day into Ukraine during March 2026, the highest monthly level recorded so far, and warned that April figures could surpass that number. The sanctions aim to disrupt supply chains supporting Russia’s drone operations, including companies and businessmen providing key components and technical support from third countries. UK Sanctions Minister Stephen Doughty said, “The practice of exploiting vulnerable people to prop up Russia’s failing and illegal war in Ukraine is barbaric.” “These sanctions expose and disrupt the operations of those trafficking migrants as cannon fodder and feeding Putin’s drone factories with illicit components to target innocent civilians and vital infrastructure,” he said. Doughty added, “The UK continues to lead international efforts to disrupt Russia’s war machine, ramping up pressure on its economy and confronting its hybrid threats. We stand shoulder to shoulder with Ukraine in defence of European security and our shared values.” The sanctions also target individuals and entities based outside Russia, including in Thailand, accused of supplying drone components and other military-related goods to Russia. Among those sanctioned is Pavel Nikitin, whose company develops the VT 40 drone, a low-cost attack drone widely used by Russian forces in Ukraine. The UK also sanctioned three individuals linked to the Russian state for allegedly recruiting foreign nationals to fight in Ukraine on behalf of Russia. One of them, Polina Alexandrovna Azarnykh, is accused of helping recruit and transport people from countries, including Egypt, Iraq, Ivory Coast, Nigeria, Morocco, Syria and Yemen through Russia into Ukraine. According to the UK, many of these recruits were deployed to frontline combat positions with little training and under harsh conditions. The British government said it would continue using sanctions to counter Russia’s military activities and what it described as “hybrid threats”, while maintaining support for Ukraine. Officials said this marks the first use of the GIMTiPS regime to tackle human trafficking and the use of migration as a tool to destabilise other countries.

title: Fertiliser trader murdered over house rent dispute in Jashore
body: A 62-year-old fertiliser trader was hacked to death last night in Jashore's Abhaynagar upazila allegedly over a dispute regarding house rent. The deceased was identified as Md Anisur Rahman, owner of Joint Trading Corporation in Nawapara town. Locals said Anisur reportedly had a conflict with Shah Mahmud Hasan, another fertiliser trader, over renting rooms in a six‑storey building near Pirbari that Anisur owned. They became rival when Anisur refused to rent a room to Hasan despite having vacancy. Quoting locals, Officer‑in‑Charge Mohammad Nuruzzaman of Abhaynagar Police Station, said Hasan, along with two to three accomplices, came back and attacked Anisur around 11:00pm in front of the building, hacking him indiscriminately with sharp weapons after an altercation. Locals rescued the critically injured businessman and took him to Abhaynagar Upazila Health Complex, later shifting him to Khulna General Hospital. As his condition worsened, doctors referred him to Dhaka Medical College Hospital, but he died around 6:00am today en route to Dhaka. OC Nuruzzaman said police have intensified drives to arrest the attackers. The body was recovered this morning and sent to Jashore General Hospital morgue for autopsy.

title: Nine-year-old boy dies after air pumped through rectum in Narsingdi
body: A nine-year-old boy reportedly died after compressed air was pumped through his rectum using a tyre inflator machine at an auto-rickshaw garage in Palash upazila of Narsingdi yesterday. The deceased, Ramim Mia, was the son of Ripon Mia of Gajaria Charkarardi village in the upazila, said Shahed Al Mamun, officer-in-charge of Palash Police Station. The incident took place around 9:00am yesterday at a battery-run auto-rickshaw garage in Gajaria Bazar, police said, quoting local residents. According to the family, Ramim had gone to the market to spend time at his grandfather Amzad Hossain’s shop. Amzad is a corrugated tin trader in the market, while the child’s father also runs a sanitary goods business there, the OC said. At one stage, the child went to the garage owned by Faisal Mia. There, Sabuj Mia, 34, a rickshaw driver, allegedly pumped compressed air into the child’s body using a tyre inflator machine as part of a "prank", according to the victim’s father Ripon. The boy soon fell critically ill as his abdomen swelled severely. Hearing his screams, locals rushed him to Narsingdi District Hospital, Ripon said. After primary treatment, doctors referred the child to Dhaka for advanced care. He later died around 5:15pm while undergoing treatment at a private hospital in Dhaka, he said. Ripon alleged that Sabuj killed his son and demanded exemplary punishment for those responsible. Md Rakib Askari, duty doctor at the emergency department of Narsingdi District Hospital, said excessive air pressure likely ruptured part of the intestine, causing internal bleeding, severe abdominal pain and breathing complications. OC Shahed Al Mamun said legal action would be taken based on a written complaint from the family and that police operations were underway to arrest those involved.

title: Teacher accused of child rape sent to jail
body: The madrasa teacher accused in a case for raping and impregnating an 11-year-old girl was sent to jail in Madan Upazila yesterday. Earlier in the day, a Rapid Action Battalion-14 team detained the accused, Amanullah Mahmudi Sagor, who had been absconding, from Mymensingh’s Gouripur. He was handed over to Madan Police Station in Netrokona in the afternoon. After completing necessary legal procedures, police produced him before the Senior Judicial Magistrate Court in the evening. The court then rejected his bail petition and ordered that he be sent to jail. Confirming the matter, Mohammad Tarikul Islam, officer-in-charge of Madan Police Station, said, “We have applied for a seven-day remand of the accused. However, the remand hearing was not held today.” On April 23, the mother of the child filed a rape case against two people, including Sagor, with Madan Police Station after discovering that her daughter was seven months pregnant. The incident has since sparked outrage across the country. According to the First Information Report, on October 2 last year, after classes ended in the afternoon, Sagor told the child to sweep the mosque adjacent to the madrasa. By that time, other teachers and students had already left for their homes. After the child finished sweeping, he told her to clean his room. As soon as she entered the room, he raped her. The FIR further said that when the child cried out, he threatened to beat her and expel her from the madrasa. The child was allegedly raped on four or five more occasions in a room adjacent to the mosque’s veranda and also in classrooms, the FIR read. On April 18, when the mother suddenly noticed physical changes in the child, she took her to a local diagnostic centre for a check-up. There, a doctor found that the child was in her third term of pregnancy. Meanwhile, Sagor, founder of the madrasa, went live on Facebook on Tuesday from an undisclosed location claiming his innocence and demanding a DNA test to determine the paternity of the unborn child.

title: Rohingya man shot dead in Cox’s Bazar camp
body: A Rohingya man was shot dead at a refugee camp in Ukhiya upazila of Cox’s Bazar yesterday afternoon. The deceased was identified as Mohammad Kamal, 40, son of Musa Ahmed, from Camp-8 East in the Balukhali Panbazar area of Ukhiya. Kamal was a community leader of the same camp. Riaz Uddin Ahmed, acting commander of Armed Police Battalion (APBn)-8, said the incident took place around 2:30pm at Camp-8. Kamal was the younger brother of Nabi Hossain, leader of the Arakan Rohingya Army (ARA), also known as the Nabi Hossain group, Riaz said. Ayub Hossain, a cousin of Kamal, alleged that 12 to 13 members of the Rohingya Solidarity Organisation (RSO) opened fire on Kamal after he went to a bazaar area following Zohr prayers at a mosque. Riaz Uddin Ahmed said Kamal was rescued with bullet injuries and taken to a local hospital before being shifted to Cox’s Bazar Sadar Hospital, where he was declared dead. He was shot in the head and chest, the police official said. Nayek Saiful Islam, in-charge of the hospital police outpost, said the body was sent for autopsy. The killing occurred within 24 hours of the murder of Rohingya armed group suspected commander Kefayet Ullah Halim of Arakan Rohingya Organisation (ARO), who was killed in a gun attack at the Balukhali refugee camp in Cox’s Bazar’s Ukhiya.

title: GD filed over brutal dog killing in Badda
body: A general diary was filed with Badda Police Station this evening over the brutal killing of a free-roaming dog after video footage of the incident went viral on social media. According to the complaint, the incident took place between 8:00pm and 8:30pm on May 5 near a garment factory at Abdullahbagh Mor in the capital’s North Badda. According to the GD, the factory’s caretaker allegedly killed the dog in a “cruel and inhumane manner”, and footage of the incident, which went viral on Facebook yesterday, triggered outrage among animal welfare activists and volunteers. Volunteers from different animal welfare and rescue groups went to the spot after seeing the footage online to verify the incident. The complainants further alleged that attempts were made to remove evidence after the volunteers arrived, and that locals behaved hostilely when activists sought accountability over the alleged killing. The GD also alleged that local volunteers and activists faced intimidation during the incident. Animal welfare activists demanded punishment for those involved under existing animal welfare laws and called for ensuring the safety and protection of stray animals. Copies of the complaint were also sent to several authorities and animal welfare organisations, according to the GD. Contacted, Kazi Nasimul Azim, officer-in-charge of Badda Police Station, said, “A complaint has been filed with us in this regard, and we have initiated legal proceedings.” Speaking to The Daily Star last night, Opshora Rahman, an animal welfare activist and manager at Infotech & Advertising Industries Ltd, said they first came across the incident after the video went viral. “The factory’s caretaker hanged and killed a free-roaming dog from the area. He recorded the incident, posted the video online, and even admitted to killing the dog.... Many of us went to the area afterwards, but locals began defending the caretaker, saying he fed the dogs there and therefore had the right to kill them if they caused trouble.” Opshora alleged that when the activists protested, the factory’s director and chairman tried to take them inside the factory premises “for a discussion”. “We refused. They then took us to a nearby confectionery shop and allegedly tried to convince us to let the matter go in exchange for Tk 20,000.” “They kept saying the dog was a nuisance, that it bit people and had rabies, and that the caretaker killed it in anger. We informed them that such an act is punishable under the Animal Welfare Act 2019. We also asked them to hand over the body so it could be tested for rabies.” She further claimed that the authorities of Amana Fashion refused to hand over the dog’s body for testing, preventing activists from verifying whether the animal had rabies. Opshora said the activists then asked for evidence supporting the claims that the dog had bitten people. “As there could not be any visible proof that the dog was creating a nuisance, we asked for proof that it had bitten anyone. They could not provide any evidence.... Factory authorities later brought forward a child with a bite wound and claimed the dog had bitten him 15 days earlier and that he had since been vaccinated. “When we asked to see the vaccine card or any medical documents showing treatment for a dog bite, they failed to provide any.” She further claimed that the authorities unleashed groups of people on the activists to harass and verbally abuse them. “We have video evidence of everything.”

title: Rape of 11-year-old in Netrokona: Accused madrasa teacher sent to jail
body: A madrasa teacher accused in a case over raping and impregnating an 11-year-old in Netrokona’s Madan upazila has been sent to jail following his arrest. Rapid Action Battalion (Rab) arrested the accused, identified as Amanullah Mahmudi Sagor, and handed him over to Madan Police Station. He was produced before the Senior Judicial Magistrate Court this evening, where the court rejected his bail petition and ordered that he be sent to prison. Earlier today, a team of Rab-14 arrested him from the Gouripur area in Mymensingh. He was handed over to police in the afternoon. After completing necessary legal procedures, police produced him in court. Confirming the development, Officer-in-Charge of Madan Police Station, Mohammad Tarikul Islam, said, “We have applied for a seven-day remand of the accused. However, the remand hearing was not held today.” On April 23, the mother of the child filed a rape case against two including Sagor with Madan Police Station after discovering that her daughter was seven months pregnant. The incident has since sparked outrage across the country. According to the First Information Report, on October 2 last year, after classes ended in the afternoon, Sagor told the child to sweep the mosque adjacent to the madrasa. By that time, other teachers and students had already left for home. After the child finished sweeping, he told her to clean his room. When she entered the room, he raped her. The FIR further said that when the child cried out, he threatened to beat her and expel her from the madrasa. The child was allegedly raped on four or five more occasions in a room adjacent to the mosque’s veranda and also in classrooms, the FIR read. On April 18, when the mother suddenly noticed physical changes in the child, she took her to a local diagnostic centre for a check-up. There, the doctor discovered that the child was in her third term of pregnancy. Madan Police Station’s Sub-Inspector Akhtaruzzaman, who is also the investigation officer in the case, said, “After the child was examined, the family filed a case against the teacher. Police also officially conducted another examination at the Netrokona 250-Bed Hospital and reconfirmed the pregnancy.” Meanwhile, a video of accused Sagor claiming innocence has been widely circulated on social media since yesterday morning. In the 5 minute 40 seconds video, he said, “What has gone viral about me on social media and has been published in various newspapers and television channels -- I am in no way involved in what is being alleged against me, using my photo. I have no knowledge of this matter at all. “ ... If I am falsely accused and labelled as the offender even before the investigation, the real criminal will escape punishment. If necessary, a (DNA) test should be done to identify the actual father of this child,” he was heard saying. Speaking to The Daily Star yesterday, the victim’s mother alleged that when she went to the accused’s family seeking justice before filing a case, they instead verbally abused her and threatened to force the family out of the area if a case was filed. “His family and local elders even tried arbitration and offered a settlement of Tk 2.20 lakh. But we refused and filed the case.”

title: Looting suspects snatched away from police custody in Narayanganj
body: A group of people allegedly snatched five suspects from police custody in Narayanganj’s Fatullah this afternoon, shortly after they were detained on allegations of looting a house. The incident took place around 3:30pm in the Hashembagh area of Paschim Deobhog, said Md Hasanuzzaman, additional superintendent of police (A Circle) in Narayanganj. Speaking to reporters, Hasanuzzaman also said that after receiving a call through the national emergency helpline 999, a team from Fatullah Model Police Station rushed to the spot following a complaint of looting valuables at the house of a retired police constable. Upon arrival, the police team intervened and detained five suspects. “Later, their associates and friends gathered at the scene and forcibly snatched them away from police custody,” he said. He added that no police personnel were injured in the incident. Additional police forces have since been deployed in the area, he said. Officer-in-Charge of Fatullah Model Police Station, Mohammad Mahbub Alam, who was present at the scene, said police are working to identify and apprehend those involved in the looting. Earlier on Tuesday afternoon, three members of Rab-11 were injured in an attack by suspected drug traders in the Boalia Khal area of Masdair in Narayanganj city.

title: Woman arrested over attempted abduction of class 4 student in Netrokona
body: Police have arrested a young woman in connection with the attempted abduction of a class 4 student in Netrokona’s Mohanganj upazila. The arrestee has been identified as Israt Jahan Mim, 20, of Sonkamia village in Atpara upazila, said Mohanganj Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Md Hafizul Islam Harun. The incident took place in Adarshanagar area of Mohanganj yesterday. Today, the victim’s mother, Kalpana Akter, filed a case with Mohanganj Police Station under the Human Trafficking Prevention Act. The detained woman was later shown arrested and sent to court. The victim, from Suair village in Mohanganj, is a student at a local school. According to the case statement and family sources, the girl left home yesterday afternoon to attend private tuition with her classmates. At that time, Israt approached her and introduced herself as an “aunt,” saying that the girl’s mother had sent her. To gain the child’s trust, she mentioned familiar details such as her mother’s name, school, and teachers. The child believed her. The accused then told the girl that her mother had asked her to bring sweet potatoes from Mohanganj. At one point, she took the child on a rented motorcycle and headed toward the upazila town. Meanwhile, when the girl’s classmates returned home, her mother began searching for her. After learning from them that she had gone with an “aunt,” panic spread among the family members. Relatives began searching for her in different areas. Later, locals spotted the girl with the accused woman at the BNP office intersection in Mohanganj. They held the woman and informed the police. Police arrived at the scene and took Israt into custody. The OC said during preliminary interrogation, the accused admitted that there was a plan to abduct the child and take her to Dhaka. “She works for an organised trafficking ring, and the plan was to hand the girl over to other members of the group,” said the OC. “The accused has provided important information during interrogation and revealed the names of several accomplices. She has already been sent to court,” added the OC.

title: Missing 6-yr-old’s body recovered from Netrokona paddy field
body: Police today recovered the severely mutilated body of a 6-year-old girl from a paddy field in Kalmakanda upazila of Netrokona district, nearly 30 hours after she went missing. The victim, Jannat, was the daughter of Arshad Mia, of Jaushi village in Kailati union of the upazila, said police. According to police and locals, farm labourers discovered the body around 7:00am while cutting paddy in a field in Hugli village. They immediately informed police, who later reached the spot and recovered the body. Police said the girl went missing on Monday (May 4) around 4:00pm. Her father filed a general diary (GD) with Kalmakanda Police Station on Tuesday (May 5). The labourers who found the body said that the girl’s mouth was tied with a gamchha (traditional towel). Most of her body from the chest down -- except for her feet -- looked like it had been eaten by wild animals, they said. Kalmakanda Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Md Siddik Hossain said, “The child’s family had filed a general diary yesterday regarding her disappearance. We recovered the body and an investigation is underway. Those involved will be identified quickly and brought under the law.”

title: Man hacks wife to death in Narail
body: A 25-year-old man hacked his wife to death allegedly after a family feud in Bahirgram of Narail's Sadar early today. The victim Khadija Akter Chandni, 20, was of Alka village in Khulna’s Phultala upazila, said police. Police detained her husband, Sakib Sheikh, of Damodar Madhyapara in Phultala, over the murder. The incident took place around 12:30am when the couple were visiting Chandni's aunt's house in Bahirgram. The couple had been married for five years and had a three-and-a-half-year-old son. According to police and family sources, the couple came to Bahirgram from Khulna on Monday. Sakib, reportedly unemployed and struggling with drug addiction, frequently quarrelled with his wife over domestic issues. On the night of the murder, Sakib allegedly attacked Chandni with a boti (kitchen cleaver) when she was asleep. Relatives rushed her to Narail District Hospital, where doctors declared her dead. Officer-in-Charge of Narail Sadar Police Station Ajay Kumar Kundu said the accused initially tried to cover up the incident. “He claimed it was an accident, saying his wife fell on the cleaver. But his statements were inconsistent. After examining the scene and questioning him, he confessed to the murder,” the OC said. Additional Superintendent of Police Kamruzzaman said police recovered the weapon used in the killing and other evidence from the scene. The accused remains in custody, and legal proceedings are underway, police added.

title: Madrasa teacher accused in rape of 11‑year‑old held
body: Rab has detained fugitive madrasa teacher Amanullah Mahmudi Sagor, the prime accused in a case filed over the rape and impregnation of an 11-year-old student in Netrokona’s Madan upazila. A team of Mymensingh Rab-14 detained Sagor, 30, from the Gauripur area of Mymensingh, confirmed Madan Police Station Officer-in-Charge Mohammad Tarikul Islam. However, Rab is yet to hand over the accused to police. Sagor is expected to be transferred to police custody in the evening, said the OC. Contacted, RAB-14's Commanding Officer (CO) Naimul Hasan said, "A detailed information will be provided at a press conference around 12 noon in this regard." On April 23, the mother of the child filed a rape case against two including Sagor with Madan Police Station after discovering that her daughter was seven months pregnant. The incident has since sparked outrage across the country. According to the First Information Report, on October 2 last year, after classes ended in the afternoon, Sagor told the child to sweep the mosque adjacent to the madrasa. By that time, other teachers and students had already left for home. After the child finished sweeping, he told her to clean his room. As soon as she entered the room, he raped her. The FIR further said that when the child cried out, he threatened to beat her and expel her from the madrasa. The child was allegedly raped on four or five more occasions in a room adjacent to the mosque’s veranda and also in classrooms, the FIR read. On April 18, when the mother suddenly noticed physical changes in the child, she took her to a local diagnostic centre for a check-up. There, the doctor discovered that the child was in her third term of pregnancy.
