Following the broadcast of an investigative report titled “Extortion Worth Crores of Taka in 24 Hours” in Karwan Bazar, the extortion syndicate had allegedly been threatening Habibul in various ways, the statement read. On April 28, while collecting information for the second part of the report in Karwan Bazar area, several people allegedly confined him and his cameramen, created a mob situation, and attempted to endanger their lives. During the incident, the attackers assaulted the camera crew and subjected them to physical and mental harassment. They were reportedly detained for nearly one and a half hours and tortured both physically and mentally. The attackers also issued death threats. Later, with the assistance of a senior journalist and the police, they managed to escape safely from the scene, according to the statement.

title: DB team attacked during Tongi drug raid; 4 cops injured, 7 suspects held
body: Police came under attack while conducting an anti-narcotics drive in a drug-prone slum area in Tongi late last night, leaving four law enforcers injured and resulting in the arrest of seven individuals. The incident occurred around 11:00pm in the Keranirtek area of Amtoli under Tongi East Police Station, Gazipur Metropolitan Police (GMP) Additional Commissioner (Crime and Operations) Md Belayet Hossain said. Legal proceedings against the arrestees are underway and preparations are ongoing to file a case in connection with the incident, he added. According to police, a joint team from the Detective Branch (DB) of the north and south divisions of GMP carried out the drive based on confidential information. The team was led by Assistant Police Commissioner Md Asabur Rahman. As the team reached the residence of a listed drug trader, Runa Akter, also known as Runa Begum, they attempted to detain several suspects. At that point, the suspects drew locals to the scene, who then launched a sudden attack on the DB personnel. The attackers assaulted the police with locally made weapons, injuring several officers. The injured include Constables Ariful Islam and Rakibul Islam, and Assistant Sub-Inspectors Nure Alam and Jahanara. Police used sound grenades to bring the situation under control. A chase and counter-chase ensued, after which the attackers retreated. Police managed to nab seven individuals from the scene, while several others managed to flee. The injured police personnel were rescued and admitted to Shaheed Ahsan Ullah Master General Hospital in Tongi.

title: 4 arrested over ‘links with TTP’
body: The Detective Branch of Dhaka Metropolitan Police has arrested four people for their alleged links with Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), a militant outfit based in Pakistan. A Dhaka court yesterday placed them on a four-day remand. The arrestees are Imran Chowdhury, 29, his brother Mostakim Chowdhury, 25, Ripon Hossain Sheikh, 28, and Abu Bakar, 25. According to DB sources, its Ramna division held them and recovered firearms, bullets, explosives, and a drone during drives conducted in various parts of Dhaka. Speaking to The Daily Star yesterday, DB Chief and Additional Commissioner of Police Shafiqul Islam said the arrestees are members of an extremist outfit named “ARSA”, which follows the TTP’s ideology. Arakan Rohingya Salvation Army (ARSA) is widely known as a Rohingya militant organisation. When asked whether those arrested were linked to the Arakan Rohingya Salvation Army, the DB chief said they were connected to a new organisation also called ARSA. Meanwhile, police filed a case against the four under the Anti-Terrorism Act with Kamrangirchar Police Station. Later, the accused were produced before a Dhaka court with a seven-day remand prayer. After the hearing, Aminul Islam Junaed, magistrate of the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Court, placed the arrestees on a four-day remand. According to the case statement, the arrestees were held from Keraniganj and Kamrangirchar on Tuesday. During the drives, law enforcers recovered a foreign pistol, a locally made gun, 14 bullets, several bullet shells, multiple smartphones, a metal detector, a drone, drone-related equipment, fake military uniforms, and “jihadi” books and leaflets. The FIR stated that the arrestees were operating with the “intention of preventing the Bangladesh government or any other state from carrying out its duties.” It also noted that the four had gathered equipment to “create panic among the public”.

title: Titon killing: Control over cattle market likely motive
body: Dhaka’s underworld was jolted once again by the killing of listed top criminal Khandokar Noyeem Ahmed Titon, with investigators suspecting rivalry over local dominance and control of a cattle market as a key motive, while also examining several other angles. A murder case has been filed over the killing, though no one has been directly named as an accused. However, the case mentioned another top-listed criminal, Imamul Hasan Helal alias Pichchi Helal, and several others, including Badal alias Killer Badal alias Kaila Badal, Shahjahan, and Rony alias Dagari Rony, in connection with the rivalry. According to the complaint, Titon had recently been in dispute with them over the lease of the Bosila cattle market. Investigators and family sources said he was called to the New Market area on Tuesday for a meeting to settle the matter, and was shot dead while returning. No arrests had been made till filing of this report, but several teams from different law enforcement agencies were working to identify and arrest those involved. Titon’s elder brother, Khondaker Saeed Akhtar Ripon, filed the case against eight to nine unidentified assailants with New Market Police Station yesterday morning, Mohammad Ayub, officer-in-charge of the police station, told The Daily Star. In the complaint, Ripon said his brother was released on bail on August 13, 2024, after spending a long time in jail, and had wanted to rebuild his life through honest work. A few days ago, Titon told Ripon that he had secured a lease schedule and hoped to earn a living through business. On April 26, he said he was in dispute with Helal, Badal, Shahjahan, and Rony over the Bosila cattle market lease. The next day, he said he had been called for a meeting to resolve the matter and work together. Later on Tuesday night, family members learned that Titon had been gunned down in the New Market area. According to police, Titon entered the underworld in the early 1990s, first as a local gang member before expanding his network. He was also involved in arms trading and faced several murder cases, including the high-profile killing of businessman Babar Elahi. His name appeared second on the government’s list of 23 top criminals in 2001. Law enforcers arrested him in the Dhaka Cantonment area in 2004. A decade later, he was sentenced to death in the Babar Elahi murder case. Police officials said Titon, along with several other alleged top criminals listed by police, was released from jail after the fall of the Awami League government during the 2024 uprising. They said he did not appear in court afterward and was in “hiding”. Shafiqul Islam, additional commissioner (Detective Branch) of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police, said at a press briefing yesterday that investigators had identified some suspects in connection with the incident. “As you know, Titon himself was a listed top criminal. Initially, we believe the murder was linked to a dispute over control of the area.” About the names mentioned in the complaint, including Pichchi Helal and Badal, he said police were acting on the complaint filed by the plaintiff. “There was rivalry over dominance. As you know, Eid-ul-Azha is approaching, and there was also conflict over the cattle market. We will identify those involved and take legal action.” Contacted by The Daily Star, Titon’s brother Ripon, said Titon visited his family in Jashore twice after being released from jail and stayed in touch occasionally through messaging apps. Titon is also the brother-in-law of top criminal Sanjidul Haque Emon. Ripon added that claims of conflict between Titon and Emon were inaccurate and intended to divert the investigation. According to the family, Titon bought the schedule for the Bosila cattle market in the name of one of his friends. Meanwhile, Pichchi Helal allegedly secured the schedule in the name of Badal. They said the two sides held several rounds of talks, during which Helal reportedly proposed a negotiation. Ripon said Titon was supposed to submit the schedule for the cattle market lease yesterday. Shimul, who is acquainted with Titon, said he was not alone at the spot and was accompanied by several men. The family initially suspected Pichchi Helal due to the cattle market dispute and earlier rivalry over local dominance. However, they also mentioned another possible motive, saying the killing may have been linked to old enmity stemming from the murder case of Tipu, brother of former army chief General Aziz. Masud Alam, deputy commissioner of Ramna Division, said no CCTV cameras were found at the crime scene, but police had collected footage from nearby areas. He said the footage showed two people directly took part in the killing, while several members of the group may have been waiting nearby on four to five motorcycles to provide backup. Police were verifying issues such as previous enmity, local dominance, and lease disputes. Dhaka’s underworld has remained active since the release of several top criminals in August 2024, with multiple killings and attacks reported amid allegations of dominance battles, extortion, property grabbing, and other criminal activities. In January 2025, two computer shop owners, including Wahedul Hasan Dipu, president of Elephant Road Computer Baboshayee Kallyan Samity and elder brother of Pichchi Helal, were attacked with sharp weapons in the capital’s Elephant Road after refusing to pay extortion money. Titon’s brother-in-law, Sanjidul Haque Emon, was made one of the main accused in that case. Sources said the attack may have been linked to a power struggle between Emon and Pichchi Helal. Emon was also suspected of orchestrating the daylight shooting of another top criminal, Tariq Saif Mamun, in Old Dhaka on November 10 last year. Operating from abroad, Emon is believed to control large parts of Mohammadpur, Dhanmondi, Jigatola, Hazaribagh, and sections of New Market. Local sources said Pichchi Helal’s group controls businesses and extortion rackets in parts of Mohammadpur, Adabor, Kalyanpur, Darussalam, and Mirpur-1.

title: Limon, Bristy Killings: ‘They’re family’
body: A court yesterday ordered the prime suspect in the killings of two Bangladeshi PhD students to be held without bond on murder charges in a courtroom filled with friends of the victims demanding justice. According to Tampa Bay 28, a local news outlet, Hillsborough County Judge J Logan Murphy ordered Hisham Abugharbieh to have no contact with witnesses or relatives. He faces two counts of first‑degree murder with a weapon, alongside other charges. Prosecutors expect to present the case to a grand jury on May 7, with the possibility of capital punishment if convicted. Abugharbieh, Limon’s roommate and a former USF student, was charged last week with first-degree murder. Limon’s remains were found on Friday, while the Hillsborough County Sheriff’s Office said it found additional remains over the weekend that it has not yet identified. Limon and Bristy came to Tampa in 2024 and 2025, respectively, for higher studies at the University of South Florida. Bristy was studying chemical engineering, while Limon was studying geography, environmental science & policy. The doctoral students disappeared on April 16. With their families still in Bangladesh, their classmates and friends stepped in to represent them during the case status hearing for the suspect. “What you need to understand is that we Bangladeshi people live as a family here,” said Abir al Hasib Shourav, a friend present in the courtroom. “It is a lot to process. When we come here, 8,000 miles away from home, these people become our family or everything here, and we meet them at all events,” another friend, Rifatul Islam, said. “It is not acceptable. We are shocked that the place that should be our safe place -- our home, our own rooms, our own kitchens -- they were murdered there. I don’t know what to say; there are no words for that,” he added. State Attorney Suzy Lopez praised the Bangladeshi students’ presence. “It’s wonderful to know their friends are embracing the two people they’ve lost and want to be part of this process to get justice.” Investigators said a third roommate told them that Abugharbieh used a cart to dispose of evidence, including Limon’s belongings stained with blood. Detectives later found blood traces in his bedroom and Bristy’s ID cards in Limon’s room. Court records also revealed Abugharbieh had asked ChatGPT about disposing of a human body days before the pair vanished. Zamil’s graduate advisor at the University of South Florida, in cooperation with the Bangladesh Student Association, has launched a GoFundMe to support the victims’ families. Since the fundraiser’s launch on Tuesday, over $80K has been raised.

title: DB arrests four over alleged links to Pakistani militant outfit TTP
body: The Detective Branch (DB) of Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) has arrested four individuals linked to the Pakistani militant outfit Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP). A Dhaka court today placed all four on a four-day remand for interrogation. The arrestees were identified as Md Imran Chowdhury, 29; Md Mostakim Chowdhury, 25; Ripon Hossain Sheikh, 28; and Abu Bakar, 25. Among them, Imran and Mostakim are siblings. According to DB sources, the Ramna division of DB arrested them after conducting drives in various parts of Dhaka. During the drives, firearms, bullets, explosives, and a drone were seized. Speaking to The Daily Star this evening, DB chief and Additional Commissioner of Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Shafiqul Islam said the arrestees are members of an extremist outfit named “ARSA”, which follows the ideology of the Pakistani militant group Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP). The Arakan Rohingya Salvation Army (ARSA) is widely known as a Rohingya militant group. However, when asked whether those arrested were linked to that group, the DB chief said they had no connection with the Rohingya group. “It has no connection with the Rohingya. It is a new organisation connected with TTP,” he said. Meanwhile, police filed a case against them under the Anti-Terrorism Act with Kamrangirchar Police Station. Later, the accused were produced before a court with a seven-day remand prayer. Following the hearing, Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaed of Dhaka Chief Metropolitan Magistrate (CMM) Court placed the arrestees on a four-day remand for interrogation. According to the case statement, Imran was arrested from a house in the Koylaghat area near Tara Mosque in Kamrangirchar around 3:00am on Tuesday. Later, Mostakim was arrested from Keraniganj's Jianagar area early Tuesday, while Ripon and Abu Bakar were arrested following a raid in Kamrangirchar on Tuesday afternoon. During the drives, law enforcers recovered a foreign-made pistol, a one-shooter gun, 14 rounds of bullets, several bullet shells, multiple smartphones, a metal detector, a drone and drone-related equipment, military uniform fabrics, and various books and leaflets on jihadi ideology. The first information report (FIR) said the arrestees were operating with the "intention of preventing the Bangladesh government or any other state from carrying out its duties." It also noted that they had gathered the equipment to create panic among the public.

title: 42 lawyers barred from Supreme Court Bar polls over alleged AL ties
body: The Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) has cancelled the nomination papers of 42 lawyers out of 90 candidates for its upcoming election, citing their alleged affiliations with the Awami League, whose political activities are banned under the Anti‑Terrorism (Amendment) Act, 2025. Among those disqualified were two candidates for president, seven for secretary, two for treasurer, 10 for assistant secretaries, and 21 for executive members, said Advocate Md Humayun Kabir Manju, incumbent senior vice president of SCBA and member of its election sub‑committee. Manju, a pro-BNP lawyer and currently a deputy attorney general of the state, told The Daily Star that scrutiny revealed “direct and indirect involvement” with Awami League activities. With the cancellations, 48 candidates remain valid to contest the election scheduled for May 13-14. Disqualified lawyers strongly protested the move, arguing they submitted nominations individually, not on behalf of any party. Advocate Md Munsurul Hoque Chowdhury, a veteran lawyer and presidential candidate, called the decision “illegal and condemnable.” “This unprecedented and farcical conduct by the ad hoc committee will remain a disgraceful chapter in the 77-year history of the Supreme Court Bar Association,” said Advocate Munsurul. Incumbent SCBA Secretary Md Mahfuzur Rahman Milon confirmed the decision of not allowing pro‑Awami League lawyers to contest but declined to share the resolution, calling it an internal matter.

title: No proof Inu ordered Kushtia killings, defence tells ICT
body: The defence counsel of former minister Hasanul Haq Inu today told the International Crimes Tribunal-2 that there is no evidence to prove that six people were killed in Kushtia on Inu’s direct order. Munsurul Hoque Chowdhury, representing Inu, argued that his client was not a lawmaker during the July Uprising and had no involvement in the killings. Inu, also the president of Jatiya Samajtantrik Dal, is the lone accused in a crimes against humanity case filed over the killings. The defence said even according to prosecution witnesses, Inu was not present in Kushtia at the time of the killings. The arguments began on April 2 and are still continuing. “Only one prosecution witness claimed that the killings of six people in Kushtia took place following Inu’s order, but he could not say when or how the order was given,” the defence counsel added. The tribunal adjourned the hearing until May 4 after granting a defence plea seeking more time to continue arguments. Meanwhile, a forensic expert told the tribunal that an audio clip containing a conversation between ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina and former Dhaka South City Corporation mayor Fazle Noor Taposh matches voice samples collected from authenticated sources. According to the audio, Hasina is heard saying, “I have given instructions; now I have given direct instructions. They will use lethal weapons. Wherever they find them, they will shoot directly,” to which Taposh responded, “yes, yes.” The expert also analysed the voice of former Dhaka Metropolitan Police commissioner Habibur Rahman and told the tribunal that the voice in the disputed clip has been confirmed to be his. Former DMP commissioner Habibur and 10 other former police officers are currently on trial in a crimes against humanity case over the killing of Imam Hasan Bhuiyan Tayim, a class 12 student, in Dhaka’s Jatrabari during the July Uprising.

title: DB seizes 8 kg heroin, 1.6 lakh yaba pills in Dhaka raids
body: The Detective Branch (DB) of Dhaka Metropolitan Police arrested six people and seized 8 kg of heroin, 255 kg of cannabis, 559 bottles of phensedyl and 1.6 lakh yaba pills in separate drives across the capital. DB chief, Additional Commissioner Md Shafiqul Islam, disclosed the information at a press briefing at the DMP headquarters today. Acting on a tip-off, a team from the DB Motijheel division arrested Md Salman Hossain, 21, and Md Jahangir Alam, 35, from the PWD Staff Quarters area on Shaheed Captain Mansur Ali Sarani around 3:00pm yesterday. Police recovered 8 kg heroin and three mobile phones from their possession, he added. “Such a massive amount of heroin has not been seized in a single drive in the last two years,” Shafiqul said. In line with recent government directives, DB is tracking and arresting the root-level operators of the narcotics trade, the DB chief added. According to a DMP press release, DB 's Wari division arrested Md Ashanur, 28, with 255 kg of cannabis from Jatrabari’s Donia area around 7:00am yesterday. At around 7:00am today, the same division arrested Abul Kalam, 41, with 1.6 lakh yaba pills from the Kaptan Bazar area. Meanwhile, a DB Ramna division team arrested Md Hasan, 31 and Mayuri, 24, from Kakrail Supermarket around 6:15am yesterday. Law enforcers seized 559 bottles of phensedyl and impounded a microbus used for drug peddling. All arrestees have been sent to court, the DMP press release said.

title: Hosaf Group chairman cleared in Barapukuria coalmine corruption case
body: Hosaf Group Chairman Moazzam Hossain has been relieved from the charges of Dinajpur’s Barapukuria coalmine corruption case filed in 2008. The High Court today scrapped the proceedings of the case against him. HC bench Justice Md Zakir Hossain and Justice KM Rasheduzzaman Raja delivered the verdict after hearing a petition filed by Moazzam seeking the cancellation of the case proceedings. Earlier, on November 27, 2024, a trial court framed charges against four individuals, including Moazzam. At that time, then BNP Chairperson Khaleda Zia, the party’s standing committee member Khandaker Mosharraf Hossain, and Vice Chairman Air Vice Marshal (retd) Altaf Hossain Chowdhury were exempted from the case. Later, several others were also discharged due to their deaths. Challenging the legality of the charge framing, Moazzam filed the petition with the High Court last year. After a preliminary hearing on January 27 last year, the High Court stayed the proceedings against him and issued a rule asking why the proceedings should not be scrapped. Today, the High Court made the rule absolute and delivered its judgement. Senior lawyer ABM Altaf Hossain and lawyer Khandaker Maruf Hossain appeared for Moazzam, while lawyer Shahin Ahmed appeared for the Anti-Corruption Commission. Following the verdict, Barrister ABM Altaf Hossain told The Daily Star that Moazzam had been accused of abatement in the case. Since the principal accused had already been acquitted, the case could not proceed against an alleged accomplice. The ACC filed the case against Khaleda Zia and 15 others with Shahbagh Police Station in Dhaka in 2008. On October 5, the same year, the ACC submitted a charge sheet against 16 accused.

title: Case filed over killing of ‘top criminal’ Titon in Dhaka’s New Market area
body: The family of Khandokar Noyeem Ahmed Titon -- a listed "top criminal" according to police -- has filed a case over his killing in Dhaka’s New Market area last night. Titon’s elder brother, Khandokar Saeed Akhtar Ripon, filed the case against eight to nine unidentified assailants with New Market Police Station this morning, Mohammad Ayub, officer-in-charge of the station, told The Daily Star. Although no one was named as an accused in the case, several individuals were mentioned in the complaint. They include listed criminal Imamul Hasan Helal alias Picchi Helal, Badal alias Killer Badal alias Kaila Badal, Shahjahan, and Rony alias Dagari Rony. According to the complaint, Titon, 59, had a dispute with them over the lease of a cattle market in Dhaka's Basila. Ripon said that Titon was released on bail on August 13, 2024, after spending a long time in jail in criminal cases. He said Titon later contacted him and expressed regret for causing financial losses and damaging the family’s reputation. Titon also said he wanted to rebuild his life through honest work. A few days ago, Titon told him that he had purchased a lease schedule and hoped to earn a living through business. On April 26, Titon told his brother that he was in a dispute with Helal, Badal, Shahjahan and Rony over the lease schedule of the Basila cattle market. The following day, Titon said he had been called to a meeting to resolve the matter and work together. Later, around 11:00pm on Tuesday, family members learned that Titon had been shot in front of Shahnewaz Hall in the New Market area and taken to Dhaka Medical College Hospital with gunshot wounds. Witnesses said two men on a motorcycle carried out the attack around 8:00pm. One assailant fired multiple rounds at Titon, finally shooting him in the head before fleeing through an alley near the BGB gate. Locals chased them, but the attackers fired at the crowd to escape. Both wore hats and masks. Pedestrians and students rushed Titon to Dhaka Medical College Hospital, where doctors pronounced him dead at 8:30pm.

title: Ex-BCL man detained at TSC, handed over to Shahbagh police
body: Leaders of Jatiya Chhatra Shakti detained a suspended activist of the banned Bangladesh Chhatra League from the TSC area of Dhaka University last evening and handed him over to Shahbagh Police Station. The detained activist was identified as M Sakib, a student of the Philosophy Department from the 2021–22 academic session and a resident of Bijoy Ekattor Hall at Dhaka University. He was also suspended from the university for allegedly taking in violence on the campus on July 15, 2024. Confirming the incident, Shahbagh Police Station Duty Officer Raihan Uddin said, “If his name appears in any case, he will be arrested in that case. Otherwise, we will decide the next course of action.” Nazimuddin Saif, deputy office secretary of Jatiya Chhatra Shakti’s DU unit, who was present at the scene, said, “While we were at TSC today, we noticed a young man whom we recognised as one of those involved in the July 15 attack.” He added, “A few of us were sitting together, and some students from the Philosophy Department who were with us recognised him. After speaking with him, we learned that he had come to campus for an academic matter. We then handed him over to the proctorial team, who later shifted him to the police station.”

title: Robbery at St Eugene De Mazenod Catholic Church in Dhaka leaves priest injured
body: A robbery at St Eugene De Mazenod Catholic Church in Dhaka’s Nayanagar left a priest injured late Monday night. Father Subash Gomes is currently undergoing treatment at Continental Hospital in Dhaka, confirmed police. Vatara Police Station Officer-in-Charge Mazharul Islam said that around 2:30am two robbers broke into the church. As Father Gomes woke up and tried to intervene, they beat him and snatched his passport before fleeing with Tk 1.5-2 lakh. The OC said a team is reviewing CCTV footage to identify the perpetrators. No formal written complaint has been lodged yet, added the OC. Law enforcement agencies have since strengthened their presence in the area and launched an investigation, confirmed officials.

title: Top gangster shot dead in New Market
body: A top‑listed criminal was shot dead in front of Dhaka University’s Shaheed Shahnewaz Hall in the New Market area around 8:00pm last night. Khandokar Noyeem Ahmed Titon, 59, was released on bail in August 2024 after serving a long prison term. His name appeared second on the government’s list of 23 top criminals in 2001. Investigators believe he was killed by his rivals in the underworld. He was the brother‑in‑law of another notorious gangster, Sanjidul Islam Emon. Law enforcement sources said Emon himself is suspected of involvement. Emon was also suspected of orchestrating the daylight shooting of Tariq Saif Mamun, another top criminal, in Old Dhaka on November 10 last year. Police said Titon was long involved in extortion and tender manipulation, among other criminal activities in Rayerbazar and Mohammadpur. Though out on bail, he had been absconding without appearing before court. Masud Alam, deputy commissioner of DMP’s Ramna Division, said police are trying to track down the killers. “Footage from CCTV cameras in surrounding areas is being collected, and eyewitnesses are being interviewed.” Witnesses said two men on a motorcycle carried out the attack. One assailant fired multiple rounds at Titon, finally shooting him in the head before fleeing through an alley near the BGB gate. Locals chased them, but the attackers fired at the crowd to escape. Both wore hats and masks. Pedestrians and students rushed Titon to Dhaka Medical College Hospital, where doctors pronounced him dead at 8:30pm. Inspector Md Faruk of the DMCH police outpost said the body bore multiple bullet wounds. Police sources said Titon entered the underworld in the early 1990s, first as a local gang member before expanding his reach. He orchestrated multiple killings and built a powerful arms‑trading network. He faced several murder cases, including the high‑profile killing of businessman Babar Elahi. Law enforcers arrested him in the Dhaka cantonment area in 2004. A decade later, he was sentenced to death in the Babar Elahi case. In August 2024, he walked out on bail from Kashimpur High Security Central Jail.

title: Law minister proposes mandatory pro bono work for lawyers
body: Law Minister Md Asaduzzaman has said the government may amend laws to require lawyers to handle at least 10 percent of their cases pro bono, ensuring justice for poor and helpless citizens at no cost. “There are more than 40 lakh pending cases at the (lower) courts and 80,000 lawyers across the country. Many lawyers are moving toward shortcuts to earn money instead of focusing on commitment to the profession. These tendencies are arising due to a lack of proper training. Every lawyer must maintain ethical standards at a high level,” he told a discussion marking National Legal Aid Day 2026 at the Supreme Court Auditorium in Dhaka. The event was organised by the Supreme Court Legal Aid Committee. "Lawyers will be brought under training. An agreement has already been signed between Bangladesh Bar Council and a British law farm to this effect," he added. The minister also stressed the need for higher budget allocation for the judiciary, pointing out that while the sector generates Tk 15,000 crore annually, it receives only Tk 2,200 crore -- less than Bangladesh Television’s Tk 2,500 crore allocation. "This disparity reflects the current state of our country’s judicial sector. As the law minister, I agree with any reasonable demands you may have. I assure you that I will stand by you, breaking through all barriers if necessary. Whether it requires raising the issue in parliament or presenting it in the cabinet, I am prepared to do so," he said. Asaduzzaman recalled that legal aid was first introduced in 1994 under then prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia, and said the government continues efforts to expand the initiative. Speaking as special guest, Justice Farah Mahbub, a judge of the Appellate Division of the SC said 199,957 cases were resolved through alternative dispute resolution (ADR) since 2009, while 1,437,736 citizens received direct legal assistance. “This success shows legal aid is not merely a compassionate initiative; rather, it is an effective, result-oriented judicial mechanism,” she said. The function was chaired by Justice Kazi Zinat Hoque, Chairman of the Supreme Court Legal Aid Committee. Other speakers included Supreme Court Bar Association President Barrister AM Mahbub Uddin Khokon, Attorney General Barrister Md Ruhul Quddus Kazal, Registrar General Mohammad Habibur Rahman Siddiquee, Legal Aid Directorate DG Md Monjurul Hossain, and Supreme Court Legal Aid Officer Md Imtiazul Islam. Judges, lawyers, officials, and representatives of foreign development partners also attended.

title: New Market area shooting victim was ‘top criminal’ who secured bail after Aug 2024, police say
body: A man was shot dead in Dhaka’s New Market area tonight. The deceased was identified as Khandokar Noyeem Ahmed Titon. According to police headquarters, he is a listed top criminal in Bangladesh. After serving a long prison term, he was released on bail following the political change in August 2024. Around 10:15pm, the Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) identified him through fingerprint analysis. Sub-Inspector Shahadat Hossain of New Market Police Station confirmed the identity, saying, “he is a top listed criminal”. He added that further details about him are being collected. It has been learned that after serving a long prison term, Titon was released on bail following the July uprising. He was allegedly involved in extortion, tender manipulation, and criminal activities in the Rayerbazar and Mohammadpur areas. Although currently out on bail, he was reportedly absconding without appearing before the court. The incident occurred around 8:00pm near Shaheed Shahnewaz Hall in New Market Bottola. Pedestrians and students rushed him to Dhaka Medical College Hospital, where doctors pronounced him dead around 8:30pm. Eyewitnesses said two men on a motorcycle carried out the attack. Witness Ratan Hossain told The Daily Star that the victim was walking fast when one assailant got off the bike and fired four rounds. After he collapsed, the attacker shot him in the head and fired at bystanders before fleeing on the motorcycle through an alley near the BGB gate. Md Mezbah Rahman, a student who helped take him to hospital, said locals chased the attackers, but they escaped firing shots to intimidate the crowd. Both assailants wore caps and masks, he added. Inspector Md Faruk of the DMCH police outpost confirmed the death, saying the victim had multiple bullet wounds. Assistant Commissioner Nasim A Gulshan of New Market Zone said police visited the scene and are collecting CCTV footage.

title: HC defers bail order for journalist couple Shakil, Rupa until May 11
body: The High Court today deferred until May 11 the delivery of its order on bail petitions for journalist couple Shakil Ahmed and Farzana Rupa in seven cases, including over murder, linked to the July mass uprising. An HC bench of Justice KM Zahid Sarwar and Justice Sheikh Abu Taher passed the order following a prayer by Deputy Attorney General Ashiquzzaman Nazrul, who sought time on behalf of the state to continue investigations into the cases for one month. Earlier, on April 21, hearing on bail petitions for the couple in the seven cases concluded, and the court had fixed today for delivering its order. On August 31, 2024, a Dhaka court sent Shakil and Rupa to jail in connection with the murder of garment worker Rubel, in a case filed with Adabor Police Station in Dhaka. Earlier, on August 21 of the same year, the couple was detained at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport. The following day, a court granted a four-day remand in the Fazlul Karim murder case filed with Uttara East Police Station. Subsequently, on August 26, they were placed on a further five-day remand in the Rubel murder case. Barrister Jyotirmoy Barua represented the accused during the hearing on the bail petitions, while Deputy Attorney General Ashiquzzaman Nazrul and Assistant Attorney General Md Al Amin appeared for the state.

title: Two arrested over attack on journalists at Khulna Press Club
body: Police have arrested two individuals in connection with an attack on journalists inside the Khulna Press Club. The arrests were made late last night from the Dighir Par area in the Nirala residential zone of the city. The arrestees have been identified as Babul Gazi, 56, and Md Sabuj, 41. Both work as tailors at a shop in Akhtar Chamber. Investigation Officer Bishwajit Kumar Basu said efforts are ongoing to arrest the four named accused in the case. The two arrested were initially listed as unidentified suspects. Police collected CCTV footage from the press club shortly after the incident, in which the presence of the two individuals was clearly observed. “They failed to provide a satisfactory explanation for their presence in the footage. They claimed they were returning home via that route on the day of the incident,” he said. The suspects will be produced before a court today. The case was filed on Sunday night by Sanjoy Kumar Dutta, administrative officer of the Khulna Press Club. In the complaint, he named four individuals -- Ripon Akon, Gaus, Halim, and Mizan -- and also accused 20–25 unidentified persons. According to the case statement, the incident occurred amid campaigning for the Khulna Press Club election. At one stage, a group of miscreants entered the premises, shouted slogans, and used abusive language targeting presidential candidate Mostafa Sarwar, editor of the Khulna-based daily Proborton. When Tariqul Islam, special correspondent of Ekhon TV, approached them for questioning, he was assaulted by the attackers.

title: Mysterious parcel blast leaves van driver injured in Kushtia
body: A van driver was injured when a parcel exploded while being opened in Kushtia. The incident took place around 10:00pm yesterday in the Lahini Bottola area of Sadar upazila. Police recovered evidence from the scene. The injured, Nasir Sheikh, 50, of Lahini Karmakarpara, is undergoing treatment at Kushtia 250-bed General Hospital. Resident Medical Officer (RMO) Hosen Imam said, “One injured person has been admitted to the hospital. He suffered splinter-like injuries to his lower body, but is out of danger.” Nasir said two unknown individuals gave him Tk 30 to deliver the parcel to a local resident named Hamidul in Lahini Joardar Para, but Hamidul refused to receive it. He later returned to Lahini Bottola with the parcel, where it was opened in the presence of locals. Inside, they found a wooden box, and the explosion occurred as it was opened. “I do not know the two men who gave me the parcel. They introduced themselves as drivers,” Nasir said. Confirming the blast that left one person injured, Additional Superintendent of Police (Crime and Ops) Faisal Mahmud said, “However, it is not yet known who was behind the incident.”

title: SC upholds bail for ex-chief justice Khairul Haque in five cases
body: The Appellate Division of the Supreme Court today upheld High Court verdicts granting bail to former chief justice ABM Khairul Haque in five cases. A five-member bench led by Chief Justice Zubayer Rahman Chowdhury dismissed five separate state petitions seeking to stay the HC bail orders issued on March 8 and 11. Despite the ruling, Khairul will not be released from jail as he remains arrested in two other cases, his lawyer Advocate Md Motaher Hossain Sazu told The Daily Star. Senior lawyers Md Qumrul Huque Siddique and Motaher Hossain Sazu appeared for Khairul, while Additional Attorney General Md Abdul Jabbar Bhuiyan represented the state during the hearings. On March 11, the High Court granted him permanent bail in a corruption case filed by the Anti-Corruption Commission. The case, lodged in August last year, accuses Khairul and seven officials of Rajdhani Unnayan Kartripakkha of acquiring a 10-katha plot through false information and abuse of power. Earlier, on March 8, the High Court granted Khairul bail in four other cases. One of the cases was filed with Jatrabari Police Station over the killing of Jubo Dal activist Abdul Kaiyum Ahad during the July movement. Another was lodged with Shahbagh Police Station by Supreme Court lawyer Mujahidul Islam Shaheen, alleging forgery related to the caretaker government verdict. Two similar cases were filed in Narayanganj with Fatullah Police Station and Bandar Police Station on August 25 last year. Khairul served as chief justice from September 30, 2010, to May 17, 2011. During his tenure, the Appellate Division delivered a landmark verdict on May 10, 2011, annulling the 13th Amendment to the Constitution, which had introduced the caretaker government system in 1996. Police arrested him from his Dhanmondi residence on July 24 last year, nearly a year after the July mass uprising and the fall of the Awami League government.

title: Man arrested on charge of killing grandmother, aunt and neighbour in Faridpur
body: Law enforcers have arrested a man accused of hacking and beating three people, including his grandmother and aunt, to death in Faridpur’s Sadar upazila. The arrestee, Akash Molla, 40, allegedly carried out the murders at Gadadhardangi village around 10:00pm yesterday, after which he went into hiding. Assistant Director of Rapid Action Battalionb-10 Faridpur camp Rezaul Karim confirmed the arrest this morning. A joint team of Faridpur Kotwali Police and Rab-10 arrested him around 6:00am today from a banana grove beside his house, he said. The victims were identified as his grandmother, Amena Begum, 75, his aunt Saleha Begum, 55, and a neighbour, Kabul Chowdhury, 49. Two others -- Riyazul Islam, 38, and Arzina Begum, 38 -- were injured and admitted to Faridpur Medical College Hospital. Officer-in-Charge of Faridpur Kotwali Police Station, Md Shahidul Islam, said the accused has been brought to the police station and is being questioned. A case is being filed, and further legal procedures are underway, he said. He added that the three bodies have been kept at the morgue of Faridpur Medical College Hospital and will be handed over to the families after autopsies.

title: Faridpur man beats and hacks grandmother, aunt and neighbour to death
body: A woman and her daughter were beaten and hacked to death, along with their neighbour, by her grandson in Faridpur Sadar on Monday night, said police. The victims are Amena Begum, 75, her daughter Saleha Begum, 55, and neighbour Kabul Chowdhury, 49, a rickshaw‑puller and father of three. All the victims were from Gadadhardangi village under Aliabad union, said Faridpur Kotwali Police Station Officer‑in‑Charge Md Shahidul Islam. The accused, Akash Molla, 40, Amena’s grandson, has been on the run since the incident, he added. Quoting family, Md Razzak Sheikh, a member of Aliabad Union Parishad, said Akash hacked his grandmother and aunt to death with a spade around 10:00pm. When Kabul tried to intervene, he was also beaten and hacked to death. Another neighbour, Riazul Islam, 38, was injured in the attack. Locals rescued him and admitted him to Faridpur Medical College Hospital. Police said Akash had been working as a peon at Faridpur Tuberculosis Hospital. Relatives said Akash had been mentally unwell for a long time. A senior family member had arranged a job for him there. “At times he would not go to office due to his condition, however, at other times he behaved normally,” UP member Razzak added. OC Shahidul said police went to the spot after being informed. “The accused is absconding. Multiple teams are working to arrest him,” he said. Additional Superintendent of Police (Crime and Ops) Md Shamsul Azam visited the scene. Around 11:45pm, he said the bodies were being recovered and would be sent to the morgue of Faridpur Medical College Hospital for autopsy.

title: Limon-Bristy Killing: Murder suspect ‘searched AI on body disposal’
body: A suspect charged with killing two Bangladeshi students, Zamil Limon and Nahida Bristy, in Florida allegedly searched an artificial intelligence chatbot about disposing of a body days before the pair were last seen, according to a court filing cited by NBC News. Hisham Abugharbieh, 26, faces a first-degree murder charge over the deaths of Limon and Bristy, both 27. Limon’s body was recovered on Friday, while Bristy remains missing, although investigators believe she is dead. In a motion filed on Saturday seeking to deny bail, the American television channel reported that prosecutors alleged Abugharbieh asked ChatGPT on April 13, “What happens if a human [is] put in a black garbage bag and thrown in a dumpster.” When the chatbot responded that the scenario sounded dangerous, he allegedly followed up with, “How would they find out.” According to the filing, a roommate told investigators he saw Abugharbieh moving cardboard boxes to a compactor dumpster at their apartment complex on April 17. A subsequent search of the dumpster recovered items belonging to Limon, including his student ID and credit cards, the filing stated. DNA found on a grey T-shirt was likely Limon’s, while genetic material on a kitchen mat matched Bristy, prosecutors said. Sheriff’s investigators later found Limon’s remains in a heavy-duty trash bag. An autopsy indicated he died from “multiple sharp force injuries”. Members of the Hillsborough County Sheriff’s Office marine and dive teams [searched] the area around the Howard Frankland Bridge in Tampa, Florida, on Friday. Human remains were found Sunday (local time) during the search for Bristy, the Hillsborough County Sheriff’s Office said, but the remains have not been identified, NBC News reported. Prosecutors said in their filing that Abugharbieh claimed to have given Limon and Bristy a ride to Clearwater the day they were last seen, April 16. Investigators also alleged in the motion that Abugharbieh purchased trash bags, Lysol wipes and Febreze that night, and that blood was discovered in his apartment. He also disposed of items including Bristy’s pink cellphone cover, prosecutors alleged. Jennifer Spradley, homicide bureau chief of the Hillsborough County Public Defender’s Office, which is representing Abugharbieh, said by email that they have no comment on the case. Abugharbieh initially denied knowing their whereabouts and claimed they had never been in his car. However, investigators said he later changed his account after being confronted with location data placing both his vehicle and Limon’s phone in Clearwater. According to the motion, Abugharbieh then said he had driven the pair to Clearwater but offered no clear explanation. Data also showed he stopped along the Howard Frankland Bridge, where Limon’s body was later found. Investigators further noted that Abugharbieh had injuries, including a cut on his finger and lacerations on his legs. He reportedly claimed the finger injury occurred while cutting onions. Abugharbieh was arrested on Friday following a brief standoff. In addition to murder, he faces charges including battery, false imprisonment, failure to report a death, unlawful storage of human remains and evidence tampering. He is being held without bond at a Hillsborough County jail. A court hearing is scheduled for Tuesday. The Hillsborough County Sheriff’s Office has not disclosed a motive. Family members told NBC News that Limon and Bristy had previously been in a relationship. In a joint statement, their families requested that their bodies be handled in accordance with Islamic funeral rites and called for a memorial in their names. In a separate statement, the University of South Florida said it is mourning the loss of the two students and remains committed to student safety.

title: Muggers in disguise killed the customs official, says Rab
body: They lay in wait near a bus stop in Cumilla after midnight, posing as a CNG-run auto-rickshaw driver and passengers, watching for a lone traveller. When customs official Bullet Bairagi got off a bus late on April 24, investigators said, they had found their target. Offering him a ride, they persuaded him to board the vehicle. He had little reason to suspect the journey would end in violence. Once the auto-rickshaw headed towards a secluded area, the gang attempted to rob him. A scuffle broke out as he resisted, during which they threw him from the moving vehicle onto the footpath beside Irish Hill Hotel in Kotbari, causing severe head injuries. He died on the spot from excessive bleeding, investigators said. The Rapid Action Battalion disclosed the details yesterday after arresting five suspects in connection with the killing. At a press conference at the Rab Media Centre in Karwan Bazar, Wing Commander MZM Entekhab Chowdhury, director of Rab’s Legal and Media Wing, said all five arrestees -- Md Sohag, Ismail Hossain Jony, Imran Hossain Hridoy, Rahat Hossain Jewel and Sujon -- are active members of an organised mugging gang. They were arrested in separate drives in Cumilla. Four of the arrestees gave confessional statements before a Cumilla court yesterday, while another accused was placed on a three-day remand, said Investigation Officer Titu Kumar Nath of Cumilla Sadar South Police Station. Senior Judicial Magistrate Abida Sultana Moli recorded the statements of four accused -- Hridoy, Sohag, Sujon and Jewel -- and granted a three-day remand for Jony. Rab said Bullet was returning to Cumilla from Chattogram after a training programme. At around 8:45am on April 25, Moynamati Highway Police recovered his body beside a hotel in the Kotbari area on the Dhaka-Chattogram highway. Multiple injury marks were found on the body. Rab said it launched an investigation immediately after the body was recovered and intensified surveillance, leading to the arrests. During preliminary interrogation, the suspects said they belonged to an organised gang that mainly targeted long-distance passengers. They would lure travellers into CNG-run auto-rickshaws and later rob them at knifepoint. Rab also said the vehicle used in the killing belonged to the gang, and the driver, along with three others inside, were habitual criminals. The Rab official said Bullet, who was travelling by bus, did not get off at his scheduled stoppage at Paduar Bazar on the Dhaka-Chattogram highway. Instead, he travelled about 5.8 kilometres further to Jhagurjhuli. Investigators believe he may have fallen asleep on the bus. He fell victim to the gang when he took a CNG-run auto-rickshaw to return from Jhagurjhuli towards Paduar Bazar, also known as Jangalia Bus Stand. During the drives, Rab recovered and seized weapons and vehicles allegedly used in the crime, including a CNG-run auto-rickshaw, a machete, a hammer and other items. Rab also said the suspects have multiple cases filed against them at different police stations on various charges, including theft, robbery and drug-related offences. Bullet Bairagi served as an assistant revenue officer at the Customs, Excise and VAT Commissionerate in Cumilla’s Bibir Bazar Land Port. The day his body was recovered, his mother Nilima Bairagi filed a murder case with Cumilla Sadar South Model Police Station against unidentified individuals. Yesterday marked the first birthday of Bullet’s only son, Avyay Bairagi. The day, however, was overshadowed by grief following the killing. On Sunday morning, after legal formalities, the body was taken to his village home in Tungipara, Gopalganj, where he was buried following funeral rites. Before that, colleagues paid their last respects at his workplace. The atmosphere at the customs office was heavy with grief as coworkers bid farewell with flowers. Bullet’s mother alleged that it was a planned murder and demanded exemplary punishment for those responsible. Cumilla Customs, Excise and VAT Commissioner Abdul Mannan Sardar said Bullet had joined the 44th basic training programme in Chattogram on April 11. After completing the training, he left for Cumilla by bus from Alankar intersection at around 11:00pm on April 24. He remained in regular contact with his family during the journey. His last call came at 2:25am, when he informed them that he had reached the Tomsom Bridge intersection in Cumilla city.

title: Police make first arrests in Kushtia pir killing case
body: Police last night arrested two men over the killing of Kushtia pir Abdur Rahman, also known as Shamim al‑Jahangir, and vandalism at his darbar in Daulatpur nearly two weeks after the attack. The arrestees are Biplob, 26, and Alif Islam, 23, -- both from Pashchim Dakkhin Philipnagar, confirmed Daulatpur Police Station Officer-in-Charge Arifur Rahman. They were detained during a special operation late Sunday night in the Philipnagar area of the upazila, he said. Another person, Fazlul Ali, was taken to the police station but later released after questioning. The OC said the arrests were made based on analysis of CCTV footage from the incident site and ongoing investigation. On April 11, Shamim was beaten and hacked to death by a mob at his darbar in Philipnagar over allegations of hurting religious sentiments. The darbar was vandalised and set on fire during the attack. Following the incident, the victim’s brother Fazlur Rahman filed a case with Daulatpur Police Station on April 13, naming four individuals and accusing around 180 to 200 unidentified others.

title: Four give confessional statements in Cumilla customs officer murder case
body: Four accused were produced before the court today to record their confessional statements under Section 164 at Cognisance Court-6, while another accused was placed on a three-day remand in connection with the murder case of customs officer Bullet Bairagi in Cumilla. Senior Judicial Magistrate Abida Sultana Moli of Cognisance Court-6 received confessional statements of four accused, and issued three days’ remand for the other accused, Ismail Hossain Jony, said investigating officer Titu Kumer Nath of Cumilla Sadar South Police. Imran Hossain Hridoy, 37; Mohammad Sohag, 30; Mohammad Sujon, 32; and Rahatul Rahman Jewel, 27, recorded their statements before the magistrate. Earlier in the day, MZM Entekhab Chowdhury, director of Rapid Action Battalion’s (Rab) Legal and Media Wing, said Bullet Bairagi was killed by an organised mugging gang that lured him into a trap by posing as passengers. The information was disclosed during a press briefing held at the Rab Media Centre in Dhaka’s Karwan Bazar this noon after arresting the five accused. According to Rab, the gang targeted the victim after he got off a bus at midnight in the Jhagurjhuli area of Cumilla and later assaulted him before throwing him from a moving CNG-run auto-rickshaw, causing his death on the spot. According to the elite force, the victim went missing on April 24 while returning to Cumilla from Chattogram after a training programme. At around 8:45 am on April 25, his body was recovered from beside a hotel in the Kotbari area on the Dhaka-Chattogram highway by Mainamati Highway Police. His body had multiple injury marks. Bullet Bairagi served as an assistant revenue officer at the Customs, Excise and VAT Commissionerate in Cumilla’s Bibir Bazar Land Port. A murder case was filed with Cumilla Sadar South Model Police Station by the victim’s mother, Nilima Bairagi, against unidentified individuals.

title: Indian citizen held with $24,600 at Banglabandha border
body: Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) today detained an Indian national with a large amount of undeclared foreign currency while he was returning to India through the Banglabandha land port in Panchagarh. The detainee, Palash Majhi, 35, was held around noon at a BGB checkpoint near the zero line of the Banglabandha border, said a BGB press release. During a search, BGB members recovered US$24,600 from his possession. Palash, a resident of Kedarpara area under Khanakul police station in Hooghly district of India’s West Bengal, had entered Bangladesh through the same immigration check post on March 27, according to immigration police and BGB sources. The release said besides the US dollars, Tk 3,570, INR 5, NPR 130, a smartphone and a power bank were also seized from him. During primary interrogation, he failed to provide a satisfactory explanation or valid documents regarding the recovered dollars, BGB officials said. Officer-in-Charge of Tetulia Model Police Station, Laisur Rahman, told The Daily Star that BGB had brought the Indian national to police, but no formal complaint had yet been filed. “A case will be filed once a complaint is received,” he added.

title: Man arrested over rape of woman in Mymensingh
body: Police last night arrested a man in connection with a case filed over the gang-rape of a woman in Mymensingh’s Nandail upazila. The accused, Helal Uddin, 55, is from Kandiura village in Nandail, said police. Police produced him before a Mymensingh court this afternoon with a five-day remand prayer, following which the magistrate granted remand for two days to interrogate the accused, said Md Azharul Islam, officer-in-charge of Nandail Police Station. On Saturday, police rescued the 26-year-old victim, a mother of two, who was reportedly gang-raped in Mymensingh’s Nandail upazila. Yesterday, the victim’s father filed a case with Nandail Police Station, naming one person and four-five unnamed accused, said the OC. Quoting the case statement, OC Azharul said the victim, from Sunamganj, was travelling with her three-year-old daughter to her in-laws' house in Mymensingh’s Bhaluka upazila on April 19 afternoon. She lost her way and reached Nandail. Four people came forward offering help and she agreed. Later they took her to a secluded place, raped her, and left her there. When the woman -- in tears -- went to Shimultoli Bazar area in Nandail the following night, a woman from a nearby area took the victim and her child to her house and provided them food and shelter for five days, said the OC. On information, police rescued the woman and her child on Saturday afternoon. Later, she was sent to Mymensingh Medical College Hospital for medical test. Primarily, it is suspected that the woman was gang-raped, said the OC. Drives are on to arrest the other culprits involved in the incident, he added.

title: Protest held in Jhenaidah over journalist’s arrest in murder case
body: Journalists and family members formed a human chain in Jhenaidah today, demanding the removal of the officer-in-charge (OC) of Shailkupa Police Station over allegations that a journalist was falsely implicated and arrested in a murder case. The protest was held at the Jhenaidah Post Office intersection around 11:00 am, where demonstrators also demanded the unconditional release of the arrested journalist. According to family members, police detained Ashraful Islam, 32 -- district correspondent of online news outlet Bangla Edition -- late Saturday night and sent him to court yesterday afternoon in connection with the murder of Mohon Sheikh. The case's investigation officer, Abul Kashem Biswas, produced him before the court. Assistant Superintendent of Police of Shailkupa Circle, Akhtaruzzaman, said that Ashraful has been arrested based on findings from the investigation. He did not provide any further comments. Ashraful is now in the district jail. During the protest, journalist leaders said Mohon Sheikh, 70, was killed on April 23 following a conflict between supporters of Shailkupa upazila BNP president Abul Hossain and district Jubo Dal joint secretary Abu Zahid Chowdhury over dominance in Madhabpur village under Monohorpur union. They said the deceased was a supporter of Abu Zahid Chowdhury, while Ashraful Islam belongs to the same community. They alleged that after the murder, Ashraful had been vocal in demanding justice and questioned the role of police, particularly Officer-in-Charge Humayun Kabir Molla. Although his name was not included in the case statement, they alleged that police called him from his home late at night and later showed him arrested in the case. At the protest, Ashraful’s wife, Shanta Khatun, said, “Ashraful was home with me on Saturday night. Police from Shailkupa Police Station called him out on the pretext of having tea and then took him away. Later, I learned that he had been shown arrested in the Mohon Sheikh murder case. My husband and the deceased belonged to the same community. Politically, we are all supporters of Zahid Chowdhury.” Jhenaidah District Reporters' Unity President MA Kabir alleged that police implicated Ashraful out of personal resentment. “He became a target of police officials because he questioned their role during the murder and remained vocal in demanding justice,” he said. Journalists from various print, electronic, and multimedia outlets joined the protest and expressed solidarity. Meanwhile, Harun Or Rashid, the plaintiff in the Mohon Sheikh murder case, said he found no information linking Ashraful to his father’s murder. He submitted an affidavit to the court through a lawyer yesterday. Attempts to contact Shailkupa Police Station OC Humayun Kabir Molla for comments were unsuccessful, as he did not respond to multiple phone calls.

title: Man beaten to death in Chattogram over suspected drug link
body: A man, who was attacked allegedly by masked assailants in Satkania upazila of Chattogram last night, died while undergoing treatment at a hospital. The deceased, Mohammad Shahadat, 30, succumbed to his injuries around 5:30am. He lived near Ward No. 5 of Dhemsha union and ran a tea stall in the Rashar Matha area. Shahadat came under the attack around 11:00pm yesterday on the Chattogram–Cox’s Bazar highway near Rashar Matha area, police and locals said. According to witnesses, a group of masked men swooped on Shahadat while he was at his shop and beat him indiscriminately before fleeing the scene. Locals rescued him and took him to a nearby private hospital. As his condition worsened, he was later shifted to the National Hospital in Chattogram, where he died while undergoing treatment. Confirming the death, Officer-in-Charge of Satkania Police Station Manjurul Haque said police have identified the attackers. “We suspect the incident stemmed from a dispute over drug trade. The victim had around 10 cases filed against him, including narcotics-related charges, while the attackers are also accused in multiple cases,” the OC added.

title: US murder suspect searched ChatGPT on body disposal before Bangladeshi students’ killing: NBC News
body: A suspect charged with killing two Bangladeshi students, Zamil Limon and Nahida Bristy, in Florida allegedly searched an artificial intelligence chatbot about disposing of a body days before the pair were last seen, according to a court filing cited by NBC News. Hisham Abugharbieh, 26, faces a first-degree murder charge over the deaths of Limon and Bristy, both 27. Limon’s body was recovered on Friday, while Bristy remains missing, though investigators believe she is dead. In a motion filed on Saturday seeking to deny bail, the American television channel mentioned, prosecutors alleged that Abugharbieh asked ChatGPT on April 13, “What happens if a human [is] put in a black garbage bag and thrown in a dumpster.” When the chatbot responded that the scenario sounded dangerous, he allegedly followed up with, “How would they find out.” According to the filing, a roommate told investigators he saw Abugharbieh moving cardboard boxes to a compactor dumpster at their apartment complex on April 17. A subsequent search of the dumpster recovered items belonging to Limon, including his student ID and credit cards, the filing stated. DNA found on a grey T-shirt was likely Limon’s, while genetic material on a kitchen mat matched Bristy, prosecutors said. Sheriff’s Investigators later found Limon’s remains in a heavy-duty trash bag. An autopsy indicated he died from “multiple sharp force injuries.” Members of the Hillsborough County Sheriff’s Office marine and dive teams search the area around the Howard Frankland Bridge in Tampa, Florida, on Friday. Human remains were found Sunday (local time) during the search for Bristy, the Hillsborough County Sheriff’s Office said, but the remains have not been identified, reports NBC News. Prosecutors said in their filing that Abugharbieh claimed to have given Limon and Bristy a ride to Clearwater the day they were last seen, April 16. Investigators also alleged in the motion that Abugharbieh purchased trash bags, Lysol wipes and Febreze that night, and that blood was discovered in his apartment. He also disposed of items including Bristy’s pink cellphone cover, prosecutors alleged. Jennifer Spradley, homicide bureau chief of the Hillsborough County Public Defender’s Office, which is representing Abugharbieh, said by email that they have no comment on the case. Abugharbieh initially denied knowing their whereabouts and claimed they had never been in his car. However, investigators said he later changed his account after being confronted with location data placing both his vehicle and Limon’s phone in Clearwater. According to the motion, Abugharbieh then said he had driven the pair to Clearwater but offered no clear explanation. Data also showed he stopped along the Howard Frankland Bridge, where Limon’s body was later found. Investigators further noted that Abugharbieh had injuries, including a cut on his finger and lacerations on his legs. He reportedly claimed the finger injury occurred while cutting onions. Abugharbieh was arrested on Friday following a brief standoff. In addition to murder, he faces charges including battery, false imprisonment, failure to report a death, unlawful storage of human remains and evidence tampering. He is being held without bond at a Hillsborough County jail. A court hearing is scheduled for Tuesday. The Hillsborough County Sheriff’s Office has not disclosed a motive. Family members told NBC News that Limon and Bristy had previously been in a relationship. In a joint statement, their families requested that their bodies be handled in accordance with Islamic funeral rites and called for a memorial in their names. In a separate statement, the University of South Florida said it is mourning the loss of the two students and remains committed to student safety.

title: Customs official killed by mugger gang in Cumilla: Rab
body: Customs official Bullet Bairagi was killed by an organised mugging gang that lured him into a trap by posing as passengers, Rab said after arresting five suspects in connection with the incident. According to Rab, the gang targeted the victim after he got off a bus at midnight in the Jagarjhuli area of Cumilla and later assaulted him before throwing him from a moving CNG-run auto-rickshaw, causing his death on the spot. MZM Entekhab Chowdhury, director of Rab’s Legal and Media Wing, disclosed the information at a press briefing held at the Rab Media Centre in Karwan Bazar this noon. The arrestees are Md Sohag, Ismail Hossain Jony, Imran Hossain Hridoy, Rahat Hossain Jewel and Sujon. They were arrested in separate drives in Cumilla. Rab said the five are active members of an organised mugging gang. According to the elite force, the victim went missing on April 24 while returning to Cumilla from Chattogram after a training programme. At around 8:45am on April 25, his body was recovered from beside a hotel in the Kotbari area on the Dhaka–Chattogram highway by Moynamati Highway Police. His body had multiple injury marks. Rab said it launched an investigation immediately after the incident and intensified surveillance. Acting on a tip-off, the suspects were arrested from different areas of Cumilla yesterday. The drives led to the recovery and seizure of weapons and vehicles used in the murder -- a CNG-run auto-rickshaw, a machete, a hammer and other items allegedly used in the killing. During preliminary interrogation, the arrestees said they were members of an organised crime gang that mainly targets long-distance passengers, luring them into CNG-run auto-rickshaws before robbing them at knifepoint. The vehicle belonged to the gang, and the driver, along with three others inside, were professional criminals, Rab said. Rab further said the gang attempted to take the victim to a secluded location. When they tried to snatch his bag and mobile phone, he resisted. During a scuffle, the attackers threw him from the moving vehicle onto the footpath beside Irish Hill Hotel in Kotbari, causing severe head injuries. He died on the spot due to excessive bleeding. Rab also said the arrestees have multiple cases filed against them at different police stations, including theft, robbery and drug-related offences. Bullet Bairagi served as an assistant revenue officer at the Customs, Excise and VAT Commissionerate in Cumilla’s Bibir Bazar Land Port. A murder case has been filed with Cumilla Sadar South Model Police Station by the victim’s mother, Nilima Bairagi, against unidentified individuals.

title: Five arrested in Cumilla customs officer murder case
body: Rapid Action Battalion (Rab) has arrested five suspects in connection with the murder of customs officer Bullet Bairagi in Cumilla. During the drive, a team of Rab-11 also recovered key evidence, including the victim’s mobile phone, wallet and travel bag, and weapons allegedly used by the suspects. The information was confirmed today at a press briefing held at the Rab headquarters in Dhaka. According to Rab-11, all those arrested are residents of the Amratoli area under Cumilla Adarsha Sadar upazila. They are -- Imran Hossain Hridoy, 37, Mohammad Sohag, 30, Ismail Hossain Jony, 25, Mohammad Sujon, 32, and Rahatul Rahman Jewel, 27. They have previous records in connection with robbery cases. The arrests were made during operations conducted yesterday, Rab-11 Sector Commander Major Sadman Islam confirmed The Daily Star. Earlier, on Saturday morning, the blood-stained body of Assistant Revenue Officer Bullet Bairagi was found lying beside the Irish Hotel on the Chattogram-bound lane of the Dhaka–Chattogram highway in the Kotbari area of Cumilla. Upon receiving the information, highway police from Mainamati Crossing Highway Police Station recovered the body. He was returning home in Dhaka after completing his basic training in Chattogram. Officer-in-Charge of Cumilla Sadar Dakshin Police Station, Sirajul Mostafa, confirmed the incident to The Daily Star. In this incident, the victim’s mother, Nilima Bairagi, filed a murder case with Cumilla Sadar Dakshin Police Station against unidentified assailants. On Sunday morning, after legal formalities, his body was taken to his village home in Tungipara, Gopalganj, where he was laid to rest following funeral rituals. Before that, colleagues paid their last respects at his workplace. The atmosphere at the customs office turned heavy with grief as coworkers bid farewell with flowers. Today, April 27, marks the first birthday of his only son, Avyay Bairagi. The victim’s mother alleged that it was a planned murder and demanded the swift arrest and exemplary punishment of those responsible. Cumilla Customs, Excise and VAT Commissioner Abdul Mannan Sardar said that Bullet was serving as an assistant revenue officer. He had joined the 44th basic training programme in Chattogram on April 11. After completing the training, he left for Cumilla by bus from Alankar intersection at around 11:00pm on Friday (April 24). He remained in regular contact with his family during the journey. His last call was at 2:25am, when he informed them that he had reached the Tomsom Bridge intersection in Cumilla city. Law enforcement agencies said that investigations are ongoing regarding their involvement in the incident. The case has created a stir in the area, and law enforcement agencies are treating the matter with due importance.

title: ICT-1 allows one-day interrogation of ex-justice Manik, DU professor
body: The International Crimes Tribunal-1 today allowed its investigators to interrogate former justice AHM Shamsuddin Chowdhury Manik and Dhaka University Professor AKM Jamal Uddin for a day in a crimes against humanity case linked to the July 2024 uprising. The interrogation will take place at the ICT’s investigation agency in Dhanmondi. The tribunal passed the order after the prosecution submitted a petition seeking permission to question the two accused. Earlier this month, the court showed them arrested in the case and sent them to jail. A prosecutor told The Daily Star that, in the case filed over the July uprising, the court sent the two accused to jail after showing them arrested as alleged instigators. Meanwhile, in a separate crimes against humanity case filed over killings in Madaripur during the July uprising, the tribunal showed former lawmaker Abdus Sobhan Mia Golap arrested.

title: Two shot dead in Ctg’s Raozan in two days
body: A day after a BNP supporter was shot dead, another man was killed by unidentified gunmen in Raozan of Chattogram last night. The incident took place around 10:00pm in the Kadalpur area, Ward No 6 of the upazila. The deceased, Nasir Uddin, also known as Madhu Nasir, was a resident of Kadalpur. Earlier, on Saturday night, a BNP activist named Kawsaruzzaman, 36, was shot dead in the Jungle Raozan area under Ward No 9 of the municipality. Raozan Police Station Officer-in-Charge Sazedul Islam told The Daily Star that five to six armed assailants shot Nasir with a shotgun and fled the scene. He was taken to the upazila health complex by locals in critical condition and later referred to Chattogram Medical College Hospital by the on-duty doctors. He later succumbed to his injuries there. Police recovered three shotgun cartridges from the scene. "Nasir had six cases filed against him, including a murder case. Police are investigating the motive behind the killing," he added. The back-to-back incidents over two days have spread panic in the area, according to locals.

title: Bullet Bairagi’s last rites performed in Tungipara
body: The funeral of Customs officer Bullet Bairagi was held at his ancestral home in Tungipara last night. Preparations for the final rites began soon after his body reached his residence. The body was brought from Cumilla around 5:00pm, after which religious rituals were performed in the presence of family members. Later, after tributes from relatives and colleagues, Bullet Bairagi’s body was cremated at 10:40pm. Bullet Bairagi was the son of Shushil Bairagi of Babupur village under Dumuria union in Tungipara upazila of Gopalganj. As the body reached the Bairagi residence beside the Tungipara-Tarail road, the area went into mourning, with cries of family members, relatives, and neighbours filling the atmosphere. The deceased’s uncle Debashish Bairagi told The Daily Star that the entire house remained in mourning since morning and all funeral rites were completed according to religious traditions. He said relatives and colleagues from Dhaka and other places gathered at the village, while officials from Chattogram training centre and various Customs units also attended to pay last respects. The family demanded a fair investigation and maximum punishment for those responsible for the killing. According to family sources, Bullet left Chattogram for Cumilla on Friday night after completing training. He last spoke to his family around 2:30am. Later, his phone was contacted from unknown numbers and then switched off. On Saturday morning, the body of Bullet, 35, of Gopalganj’s Tungipara, was recovered beside the Dhaka-Chattogram highway in the Kotbari Bishwa Road area in Cumilla Sadar South upazila. He served as an assistant revenue officer at the Customs, Excise, and VAT Commissionerate in Cumilla’s Bibir Bazar Land Port.

title: ‘I just want to see her face one last time’
body: Nahida Sultana Bristy , a Bangladeshi student at the University of South Florida, was still missing yesterday as her family demanded the swift return of her body after investigators informed them early Friday that she is feared dead. Two Bangladeshi PhD students, Zamil Limon and Nahida Bristy, both aged 27, had been reported missing on April 17. Limon’s body was recovered on Friday from the Howard Frankland Bridge. Limon’s roommate, Hisham Saleh Abugharbieh, a 26-year-old US citizen and former USF student who was arrested on Friday, has been charged with two counts of first-degree premeditated murder. Despite being a non-student, Hisham lived with Limon in an apartment on Avalon Heights -- a student housing complex north of USF’s Tampa campus. Speaking to The Daily Star yesterday, Bristy’s father, Jahir Uddin Akon, recalled his last conversation with her on April 16. “Father, I am attending classes at the university. I am busy with lab work. Around 5:00pm, we will go shopping. I will go with a friend,” said Akon, an insurance company employee. “There was so much joy in her voice. She was supposed to return home in July. She used to buy things for herself and for us whenever she found time,” he said over the phone. Now, he says, that voice is gone. “No one will call me ‘father’ anymore. I used to call my daughter ‘Ma’. I will not be able to call anyone ‘Ma’ again,” he said, his voice breaking. “I have only one demand now: find my daughter’s body and bring it back. I just want to see her face one last time.” According to Akon, Bristy went missing shortly after receiving a phone call from a man identified as Hisham Saleh Abugharbieh. She went downstairs to speak with him and did not return. “I had many dreams for my daughter,” he said. “She was very good in her studies. She went to the United States to fulfil her dreams. With her, I have lost my dreams as well.” Bristy graduated in chemistry and chemical engineering from Noakhali Science and Technology University and later enrolled in postgraduate studies at Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (Buet). She secured a full scholarship to pursue a doctoral degree in chemical engineering at the University of South Florida and left Dhaka on August 12 last year. Her family, originally from Madaripur, has lived in Mirpur‑11 in Dhaka for over two decades. “We want justice. We cannot accept this death. We demand punishment for those responsible and the return of her body,” said Bristy’s cousin, Tuli Akon. State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam yesterday said Bangladesh wants the US to ensure those responsible are brought to justice. “We demand a prompt and thorough investigation into the matter so that those involved are identified and brought to justice,” she said, describing the double murder as deeply unfortunate. Shama Obaed said she personally spoke on Saturday with Bristy’s brother and Limon’s father. “We are in contact with all the relevant agencies, including the Bangladesh Mission in Washington, the US Department of State, and the FBI. We have spoken to both families and will provide all possible cooperation from our side,” she told reporters at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. USF authorities have stated that both students had health insurance through their student status that includes repatriation coverage. In a joint statement, the families of Limon and Bristy urged USF and relevant authorities to ensure Islamic funeral rites for the two victims; pursue swift justice with the highest punishment for the accused; and investigate alleged security lapses at Avalon Heights -- including roommate screening, inadequate CCTV coverage, weak security measures, and the handling of prior complaints. They also demanded the return of all personal belongings, settlement of pending financial dues, support for the bereaved families, and the establishment of a permanent memorial at the university in honour of the two victims. Meanwhile, the Bangladesh Consulate in Miami is actively working with local funeral authorities and all concerned parties to repatriate Limon’s body to Bangladesh as quickly as possible. On the other hand, the embassy is maintaining regular contact with relevant US authorities to obtain more information regarding Nahida Bristy.

title: DU student found dead at home
body: Police arrested a Dhaka University teacher after one of his students was found dead at her home in the capital’s Uttar Badda area early yesterday. Munira Mahzabin Mimo, a master’s student in theatre and performance studies who is suspected to have died by suicide, left a note that mentioned the name of the teacher and another student. Kazi Md Nasirul Amin, officer-in-charge of Badda Police Station, said, “Sudip Chakraborty, an associate professor of the department, was arrested after the student’s father, Golam Mostafa, filed a case of abetment of suicide with the station. Police had earlier picked up the teacher and a classmate of the deceased for questioning. “The student was released, as the deceased’s family had no complaint against her,” the OC said.
