The injured journalists alleged that Chhatra Dal activists attacked them even after identifying themselves as journalists. Dhaka University Journalists’ Association President Manjurul Hossain Mahi said, “We went to Shahbagh Police Station to collect news. Immediately after arriving there, we were deliberately obstructed from gathering information in a pre-planned manner. At one point, we were suddenly attacked. One after another, ten of us were brutally beaten. Shahbagh Police remained silent spectators.”PROTESTS AT JNU Jagannath University Central Students’ Union brought out a protest march on campus last night, condemning the attack on Ducsu leaders and student journalists by Chhatra Dal activists. Earlier, leaders and activists of Chhatra Dal’s JnU unit staged a procession, denouncing the circulation of “derogatory images” of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and Zaima Rahman on social media.

title: Tonu murder: PBI sends DNA sample of accused Hafizur to lab
body: The Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) collected DNA sample of retired army personnel Hafizur Rahman -- an accused in the Sohagi Jahan Tonu murder case -- and sent it to the laboratory today. Investigating officer Tarikul Islam confirmed the development to The Daily Star. On Wednesday afternoon, a special team of the Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI), led by Tarikul, produced Hafizur at Cumilla Sadar Cognisance Court-1. The investigating officer requested the presence of complainant Yaar Hossain, Tonu's father, along with other family members, as witnesses. Tarikul sought a seven-day remand, describing the allegations against Hafizur and the circumstances of his arrest. He mentioned that Hafizur was arrested from Keraniganj in Dhaka, marking the first arrest in the case after ten years. Tonu’s parents and younger brother were present in court, where her father identified the accused. The court then granted a three-day remand, allowing the PBI to interrogate the accused in custody. The order was issued at 5:12 pm, after which PBI officials escorted Hafizur from the courtroom. Following the proceedings, Tarikul held a private discussion with Tonu’s family inside the courtroom. At around 5:45 pm, the PBI team and the family left the premises. Speaking to The Daily Star, Yaar Hossain said he had identified Tarikul as being involved in the murder, adding that the accused was serving in the Cumilla Cantonment Signal Unit (5 Signal) at the time of the incident. Earlier, on April 6, the seventh investigating officer of the much-discussed case sought permission to cross-match DNA samples of three suspects: retired army personnel Sergeant Zahid, Hafizur, and soldier Jahangir Alam.

title: Sadeeq Agro owner gets permanent bail in Tk 133cr laundering case
body: The High Court today granted permanent bail to Mohammad Imran Hossain, owner of Sadeeq Agro, in a case filed over laundering Tk 133 crore. The bench of Justice KM Zahid Sarwar and Justice Sheikh Abu Taher issued the order after final hearing of a petition filed by Imran last year seeking bail. Barrister AM Mahbub Uddin Khokon represented Imran, while Deputy Attorney General Md Ashiquzzaman Nazrul and Assistant Attorney General Md Al Amin appeared for the state. DAG Nazrul told The Daily Star that the state will move an appeal before the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court challenging the bail order. Imran was arrested on March 3 last year by the CID’s Financial Crime Unit in a money laundering case filed with Mohammadpur Police Station under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act. Allegations included laundering Tk 133 crore with two others, smuggling cattle from Bhutan, Nepal, Myanmar, and Thailand, and fraudulently advertising Bangladeshi cows and goats as foreign breeds for sale at high prices in sacrificial animal markets. Sadeeq Agro came under scrutiny in 2024 after controversy over a Tk 15 lakh goat sold to Mushfiqur Rahman Ifat, son of former NBR member Matiur Rahman. Subsequent investigations were launched by the Anti‑Corruption Commission and the National Board of Revenue.

title: Bangladesh Betar employee arrested over assault of schoolboy in Ashulia
body: Police have arrested a Bangladesh Betar employee on charges of assaulting a high school student in Ashulia’s Kabirpur yesterday. The arrestee is Abdul Naeem, 35, said Ashulia Police Station Officer-in-Charge Md Rubel Hawlader. The arrest was made after a video of the assault went viral on social media. In the video, Naeem and another individual, identified as Lokman Sheikh, who is also an employee of Bangladesh Betar, were seen beating Hossain, a class 7 student of Kabirpur Renaissance Public School in Ashulia, in an open area. At one point, a voice is heard shouting, “He will die.” Following the spread of the video, police detained Naeem this morning. He was later formally shown arrested after the victim’s father filed a case with Ashulia Police Station. Naeem and Lokman, along with three unidentified individuals, were named as accused in the case. The victim’s father, Manik Mia, alleged that his son sustained injuries to his hands, legs, back, and other parts of his body. He further alleged that following the incident, Naeem and Lokman verbally abused him and his wife and also assaulted them. Later, with the assistance of locals his son was rescued and admitted to Savar Upazila Health Complex, he said. The OC said, “We immediately took action and detained Abdul Naeem, who was directly involved in the incident.” He added Lokman Sheikh is currently absconding.

title: 3 arrested over theft of construction materials From BMU Super Specialized Hospital
body: Police have arrested three alleged members of a theft ring in connection with the theft of construction materials from the Super Specialized Hospital of Bangladesh Medical University in Dhaka's Shahbagh area. The arrestees are Al Mamun Sarkar, 33; Md Mamunur Rashid, 40; and Md Masum Billah, 35. According to a press release issued by the media wing of Dhaka Metropolitan Police, a group of individuals stole scrap construction materials from the basement-2 of an under-construction section of the hospital using a mini-truck at dawn on Tuesday. A theft case was later filed with Shahbagh Police Station that evening. Police said that after analysing CCTV footage and using intelligence inputs and technological support, two of the suspects -- Mamun Sarkar and Mamunur Rashid -- were arrested from the hospital area around 7:00 pm yesterday. Later last night, at around 11:30 pm, Masum Billah was arrested from the Badda area. During the drives, police recovered four mini-truck loads of stolen construction scrap materials, estimated to be worth around Tk 10 lakh, the release said. During initial interrogation, the arrestees admitted that they are active members of an organised theft ring and confessed to stealing unused construction materials from the hospital premises, the press release added. Legal action against the accused is underway.

title: 1 killed, 11 injured as BNP-Jubo Dal clash in Jhenaidah
body: A man was killed and at least 11 others injured today in a violent clash stemming from a conflict within the local BNP and Jubo Dal in Shailkupa upazila of Jhenaidah. The incident also saw houses vandalised and looted. The clash occurred around 10:30am in Madhabpur village under Monoharpur Union of the upazila. The deceased, Mohon Sheikh, 70 was the son of the late Motleb Sheikh of the same village, said Shailkupa Police Station Officer-in-Charge Humayun Kabir Molla. He said the clash broke out over a dispute regarding local dominance and added that additional police have been deployed in the area to prevent further violence and looting. Preparations are underway to send the body for autopsy, the police official further said. According to locals and police, a long-standing rivalry over local dominance had been simmering between supporters of upazila BNP president, Abul Hossain and district Jubo Dal joint general secretary, Abu Zahid Chowdhury. Tensions escalated on last evening when supporters of Abul Hossain allegedly assaulted a supporter of Abu Zahid Chowdhury. In retaliation, both groups engaged in a violent confrontation this morning using locally made weapons. Around 11 to 12 people were injured in the clash and taken to Shailkupa Upazila Health Complex, where doctors declared Mohon Sheikh dead on arrival. One critically injured person, Abbas Sheikh, was referred to Faridpur for advanced treatment. Dr Nahid Emran Tonni, an emergency department physician at Shailkupa Upazila Health Complex, said Mohon Sheikh was brought in dead, while other injured patients are receiving treatment. One has been referred to Faridpur Medical College Hospital. Tarikul Bashar Sadad, son of Abul Hossain and Member Secretary of the Upazila Jubo Dal, claimed that supporters of the Awami League instigated Abu Zahid’s group, triggering the clash. He also alleged that the deceased and injured were BNP activists, and that members of Abu Zahid’s group vandalised and looted houses of Abul Hossain’s supporters after the incident, even taking away cattle from some households. However, Abu Zahid Chowdhury, joint general secretary of the district Jubo Dal said that the deceased Mohon Sheikh was a member of his group. He also said several others were critically injured and are undergoing treatment.

title: Woman’s body found in sack in Jashore
body: Police recovered the body of a 55-year-old woman from a roadside in Jashore early yesterday. The deceased, Sakina Begum, wife of Lal Chand Khalifa of Bejpara Main Road, was found stuffed inside a sack near her home in the Bejpara area. The body was sent to Jashore General Hospital morgue for autopsy. Her son, Shahidul Islam, said after returning home from outside around 11:00pm, he could not find her and later informed police. Around 2:30am, Shahidul spotted a sack by the roadside beside their house. On opening it, he found his mother’s body. He and his sister, Shahida Begum, identified the body. Shahida alleged that her mother was murdered in a premeditated manner and dumped in the sack. Officer-in-Charge of Jashore Kotwali Police Station Masud Khan said the cause of death would be known after investigation and the autopsy report.

title: Tonu murder: First arrest made 10yrs after killing
body: Ex-army man Hafizur Rahman, a suspect in the Tonu murder case, was produced before a Cumilla court yesterday. He is the first to be arrested after Sohagi Jahan Tonu was murdered 10 years ago. The court placed Hafizur on a three-day remand. Senior Judicial Magistrate Mominul Haque issued the order in the afternoon at Cumilla Sadar Cognisance Court-1 after the Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) produced the suspect before the court. Investigating Officer Tarikul Islam of PBI Dhaka earlier arrested Hafizur at his home. On April 6 this year, the seventh investigating officer in the much-discussed case sought permission to cross-match DNA samples of three suspects -- retired army personnel sergeant Zahid, warrant officer Hafizur Rahman, and soldier Jahangir Alam. According to court officials, the case has so far had 80 hearing dates, with seven IOs from four agencies handling the probe over the years. Nineteen-year-old Tonu, a second-year history student of Cumilla Victoria Government College, was found dead in the Cumilla Cantonment area on the night of March 20, 2016.

title: New writ challenges repeal of Supreme Court Secretariat law
body: Another writ petition was filed with the High Court today challenging the law that repealed the ordinance issued by the interim government to establish a separate secretariat for the Supreme Court. Supreme Court lawyer Md Mahmudul Hasan Mamun submitted the petition as a public interest litigation to the HC seeking its order on the government to reinstate an independent secretariat for the Supreme Court. In the petition, he prayed to the High Court to issue a rule asking the authorities concerned to explain why the Supreme Court Secretariat (Repeal) Act, 2026 that annulled the Supreme Court Secretariat Ordinance should not be declared illegal. The petition contends that an independent Supreme Court Secretariat is an institutional cornerstone and the heart of judicial independence. Petitioner Mahmudul said he will try to move the petition before the High Court soon. Earlier on April 19, seven lawyers, including Advocate Mohammad Saddam Hossein, submitted a similar writ petition as a public interest litigation to the High Court challenging the repeal of the ordinance and seeking the same directive. On April 20, the High Court postponed the hearing, saying it will stay on the cause list until the Appellate Division rules on the government’s appeal against the verdict directing the formation of a Supreme Court Secretariat. On the same day (April 20), the High Court bench of Justice Ahmed Sohel and Justice Fatema Anwar said they expect the government not to transfer the existing structures of the Supreme Court Secretariat during this time, lawyer Mohammad Shishir Manir told reporters after the proceedings. Earlier in the day, Attorney General Md Ruhul Quddus Kazal told the bench that the state will move an appeal before the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court, challenging the High Court judgement that directed the government to establish the Supreme Court Secretariat and therefore, it will not be appropriate for the High Court to proceed with the writ petition right now.

title: Missing for three days, man's body found hanging in Cox’s Bazar
body: Police today recovered the body of a man from a remote hilly area, three days after he went missing in Khurushkul union under Cox’s Bazar Sadar upazila. The victim, Nayan Das, was a sebait (custodian) of Shor Ghona Nag Panchami Temple in the Purbo Hamzar Dail area, confirmed Officer‑in‑Charge Mohammad Samiuddin of Cox’s Bazar Sadar Model Police Station. He was a resident of Fultala village in Satkania upazila's Dohazari, under Chattogram district. He said locals spotted the body on Wednesday afternoon and informed police. Family members said some people called Nayan out of his house around 9:00pm on Sunday (April 19) and he has been missing since. Locals and temple associates searched the surrounding area before finding his body hanging from a tree in the nearby hill, with a cloth tied around his neck. Police then recovered the body and sent it for autopsy. OC Samiuddin said, “The body has been sent for post‑mortem after inquest. It will be known after the autopsy report whether it was a murder or suicide.” Cox’s Bazar Superintendent of Police Sajedur Rahman said that investigators are examining all aspects, including how it happened and why in that specific location. He confirmed that the victim’s wife had filed a complaint three days earlier and police had already been investigating his missing case.

title: 3 workers abducted from Bandarban rubber plantation: Police
body: Three rubber plantation workers were abducted in Bandarban’s Naikhongchhari upazila last night. The incident took place at a rubber plantation owned by Abdul Karim Bantu in Alikhyang area of Baishari union, said Naikhongchhari Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Mozammel Haque. The abducted individuals have been identified as Enamul Haque, 24; Mohammad Hasan, 26; and Nurul Islam, 28 -- all residents of Cox’s Bazar’s Teknaf upazila, according to local sources. According to locals, the three had been working for a long time at the rubber plantation. Around 3:00am today, a gang of armed miscreants took them hostage at gunpoint from the plantation’s staff quarters, said the OC. A joint operation is underway to rescue them, the OC added.

title: Three held over theft of construction materials from BMU’s Super Specialised Hospital
body: Police detained three people today in connection with the theft of construction equipment and materials from the Super Specialised Hospital at Bangladesh Medical University (BMU). “Three have been picked up over the issue, and most of the materials have been recovered from warehouses in Dhaka's Badda,” Masud Alam, deputy commissioner (Ramna Division) of Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP), told The Daily Star. He could not immediately provide the names of the detainees. The process to file a case in this regard is underway. Prof Saifullah Munshi, director of the hospital, said an assistant engineer and a computer operator of the institution were among those detained. According to hospital sources, a group took away leftover construction equipment and materials from the hospital’s basement using pickup vans on Monday night. However, no medical equipment was stolen.

title: 3 arrested over Naogaon family murders; 2 confess, police say
body: Police have arrested three suspects in connection with the murder of a couple and their two children in Naogaon’s Niamatpur upazila. During a press briefing today at 2:00pm, Naogaon Superintendent of Police Mohammad Tarikul Islam confirmed that two of the arrestees have already confessed to the killings. The arrestees are: Sabuj Rana, 20, and Shahin Mondal, 25 -- both nephews of deceased Habibur; and Shahidul Mondal, 48, Habibur’s brother-in-law. The victims are: Habibur Rahman, 35, of Bahadurpur village; Habibur’s wife Popi Sultana, 27; their son Parvez Rahman, 9, and daughter Sadia Akhtar, 3. The victims were found with their throats slit at their home early yesterday by neighbours. Two sharp weapons have been recovered from a nearby pond and another location, said the SP. According to two of the accused -- Sabuj and Shahidul -- the incident stemmed from a long-standing grievance over a family land. Habibur’s father, Nomir Uddin, had gifted 12 to 13 bigha of land to his only son while giving his five daughters significantly smaller portions. This disparity led to resentment among the sisters, their husbands, and their children, said police. "Sabuj and Shahidul admitted that they committed the murders due to this discrimination. However, Shahin has not yet provided information regarding his involvement. We will produce him in court today and seek a remand for further interrogation," Manda Circle Assistant Superintendent of Police Abdullah Al Mahmood Shawon told The Daily Star. He added that several other relatives are suspected of involvement but have not yet been apprehended. In his confession, Sabuj mentioned that he maintained a good relationship with his grandfather, Nomir Uddin, and had even shared a meal with the victims on the night of the murder. Following the discovery of the bodies, Habibur’s father-in-law, Moazzem Hossain, filed a case with Niamatpur Police Station against unidentified individuals last night. After the incident, police initially detained five relatives for questioning yesterday, three of whom were formally arrested today. Niamatpur Police Station Officer-in-Charge Mahbubur Rahman said the suspects have been sent to court, and the bodies of the victims were handed over to the family this afternoon following post-mortem examinations.

title: First arrest in Tonu murder case after 10 years
body: A court in Cumilla has granted a three-day remand for Hafizur Rahman in connection with the Tonu murder case, marking the first arrest in the case after ten years. Senior Judicial Magistrate Mominul Haque issued the remand order this afternoon at Cumilla Sadar Cognisance Court-1 after the Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) produced the suspect before the court. Investigating Officer Tarikul Islam of PBI Dhaka had earlier arrested Hafizur Rahman from his residence and presented him before the Cumilla Sadar court. On April 6, the seventh investigating officer of the much-discussed case sought permission to cross-match DNA samples of three suspects: retired army personnel Sergeant Zahid, Warrant Officer Hafizur Rahman, and Soldier Jahangir Alam. According to court officials, the case has so far seen 80 hearing dates, with seven investigating officers from four agencies handling the probe over the years. Tonu’s parents, along with her younger brother Rubal Hossain, appeared before the Cumilla court.

title: Family of four brutally murdered
body: A couple and their two children were brutally murdered in their home, sending a shockwave through Bahadurpur village in Naogaon’s Niamatpur upazila yesterday. The victims were first bludgeoned and then their throats were slit. They were Habibur Rahman, 35; his wife Popy Sultana, 27; their nine-year-old son Parvez, and three-year-old daughter Sadia. Police and family members said the killings likely took place between 11:00pm on Monday and 5:00am yesterday. Neighbours were shaken by the sight as they discovered the bodies after Fajr prayers. They went into the house, finding the door open, which seemed unusual. Police arrived soon after. Niamatpur Police Station Officer-in-Charge Mahbubur Rahman said Habibur and his children were killed inside a room, while Popy, who appeared to have tried to flee, was chased down and slain in the yard. Investigators and relatives suspect the murders resulted from a bitter land feud with their relatives. Family sources said Habibur, the only son of 70-year-old Namir Uddin, had long-standing disputes with his five sisters after receiving the largest share of property. Police said this created deep resentment among the sisters. Popy’s mother, Sabina Begum, wept as she spoke to journalists. “They [Habibur’s sisters] have been abusing my daughter for a long time. They together killed my daughter, my son-in-law, and my grandchildren over a land-related dispute,” she alleged. Her father, Moazzem Hossain, said, “They beat my daughter a few days ago. They even tried to kill her in the past. I want justice.” Namir Uddin, who was sleeping in another room, said, “I could not understand when my son, daughter-in-law, and grandchildren were killed. I woke up hearing a commotion after the neighbours saw the bodies early in the morning.” Police have detained the five sisters for interrogation. OC Mahbubur said the nature of the killings did not suggest robbery. No case had been filed as of 8:30pm yesterday. Naogaon Superintendent of Police Mohammad Tarequl Islam said, “Initially, we suspect the murder took place due to a land-related dispute among siblings. Several units of police are investigating.” Assistant SP Abdullah Al Mahmood Shawon said the bodies were sent to the hospital morgue for autopsy and expressed hope of significant progress in the investigation within 48 hours.

title: 3 suspected robbers found dead in Teknaf
body: Police recovered the bodies of three suspected robbers from a hill in Teknaf, Cox’s Bazar, who are believed to have been killed in a clash between two rival groups. The bodies were found around 9:00am yesterday on a remote hill in the North Shilkhali area under the Baharchhara union, said Durjoy Biswas, the officer-in-charge of the Baharchhara Police Investigation Centre. The deceased were identified as Aminul Islam Robi, 19; Mujibur Rahman, 38; and Nur Bashar, 20. They were residents of the same area. Another suspect, Morshed, was critically injured in the incident and is currently undergoing treatment at a hospital under police custody, according to Durjoy. Mujibur and Morshed were known offenders with multiple robbery cases against them, while the other two were relatively new to criminal activities linked to robbery and human trafficking. Police are verifying whether they had any prior cases. The incident may be linked to abduction and human trafficking, said Saiful Islam, the officer-in-charge of Teknaf Model Police Station. “We are taking the matter seriously and investigating,” he said. Robi’s father, Ruhul Amin, identified his son at the scene after being informed. “Morshed called my son last night while he was having dinner and asked him to come out. He had been missing since then. This morning, I found his body in the hills,” Ruhul said.

title: Construction materials stolen from BMU’s Super Specialised Hospital
body: A theft took place at the Super Specialised Hospital at Bangladesh Medical University (BMU) on Monday night. A group allegedly took away leftover construction equipment and materials from the hospital’s basement using pickup vans, hospital sources said today. However, no medical equipment was stolen, hospital Director Prof Saifullah Munshi told The Daily Star. He said some construction equipment and materials had remained in the basement long after the hospital’s completion. Those items were taken last night, he said, adding that Ansar personnel deployed at the hospital tried to stop them but failed. He said a general diary has been filed with Shahbagh Police Station, and a committee has been formed to investigate the matter. Police advised them to file a case after submitting the probe report, he added. A BMU official said a Korean company had constructed the building and left some equipment there. The company had written to the hospital authorities a few months ago to collect the materials, but the matter remained unresolved due to the prevailing situation in the country. Another BMU official said there is confusion regarding whether it was a case of theft or something else. Mazharul Islam, assistant commissioner (Ramna Zone) of Dhaka Metropolitan Police, said a general diary has been filed with Shahbagh Police Station, and police are looking into the matter.

title: NICRH deputy director attacked over hospital tender dispute, says Rab
body: The attack on the deputy director of the National Institute of Cancer Research and Hospital (NICRH) was triggered by a dispute over a hospital tender between two groups, the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) said today. According to RAB, the clash involved two rival groups -- one led by Rubel and the other by the Monayem Group -- over the tender. “Acting on instructions from Rubel, who is currently in Malaysia, two to three hired attackers carried out the assault on Ahmad Hossain to intimidate the hospital authorities,” said MZM Intekhab Chowdhury, director of Rab’s legal and media wing, at a press briefing at the Rab Media Centre in Dhaka's Karwan Bazar this afternoon. The attackers were hired for only Tk 20,000, said the Rab official, quoting five suspects, who were arrested from different parts of Dhaka. Intekhab said the attackers used sharp weapons, injuring the doctor in the hand and back. The Rab official said they increased surveillance immediately after the attack. Based on intelligence and evidence, Rab-1 and its intelligence wing arrested the five suspects. The five arrestees are: Shariful Alam Karim, Aminul Islam Kalu, Salauddin Badi, Sajjad, and Arifuzzaman. Several of them are accused in multiple cases with different police stations across the country. Meanwhile, a police team also arrested two more suspects -- Yusuf Ali and Nesar Ahmed -- in connection with the same incident, Faridul Islam, officer-in-charge of Banani Police Station, told The Daily Star. Around 4:00pm on Monday, criminals stabbed Ahmad Hossain, 50, deputy director of NICRH, in Mohakhali while he was walking home after office through a lane beside the old campus of BRAC University. He was first taken to NICRH and later shifted to Dhaka Medical College Hospital, where he is undergoing treatment. Following the incident, an administrative officer of the hospital filed a case with Banani Police Station against eight to ten unnamed individuals.

title: Content creator Hasan Nasim granted bail in cyber security case
body: Content creator AM Hasan Nasim was granted bail today in a case filed on charges of spreading misleading information on social media about Jatiya Sangsad Chief Whip Nurul Islam Moni. Dhaka Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Jashita Islam passed the order following a bail petition, said Dhaka Metropolitan Police Prosecution Division Sub-Inspector Moktar Hossain. On April 18, Nazrul Islam, who claims to be a supporter of the chief whip, filed a case with Gulshan Police Station under sections 25 and 27 of the Cyber Security Ordinance, accusing some unnamed individuals. The Cyber Security Ordinance 2025, issued by the interim government, was recently ratified in parliament. Contacted by The Daily Star on April 18, complainant Nazrul Islam said he had not communicated with the chief whip before filing the case. “I acted on my own because I felt bad. The whole Patharghata area is being portrayed falsely on Facebook over a minor incident every day. It has created unrest in the locality,” he said. Asked about the legality of the case, Md Dawud Hossain, officer-in-charge of Gulshan Police Station, said, “It seemed cognisable to me, so I took the case. The court will give directions if any law was violated in filing the case.” A team of the Detective Branch of Dhaka Metropolitan Police picked up Hasan Nasim from his house in Dhaka's Agargaon area on April 17. On April 18, he was produced before the court with a seven-day remand prayer after being shown arrested in the case. Later, Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Md Hasib Ullah Pias rejected the remand prayer and sent him to jail, according to a sub-inspector working at the court. According to the police forwarding report, detectives arrested him after finding his involvement during the investigation.

title: Sirajganj court issues arrest warrant against Amir Hamza in defamation case
body: A court in Sirajganj today issued an arrest warrant against Kushtia-3 lawmaker Mufti Amir Hamza in a defamation case for allegedly describing Minister for Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Iqbal Hassan Mahmood Tuku as an “atheist” and “anti-Islamic”. Judge Suman Karmakar of the Chauhali Cognisance Court passed the order after the accused failed to appear before the court despite being summoned earlier. The case was filed on April 2 by Advocate Humayun Kabir, general secretary of the Sirajganj District Bar Association, sections 296, 500 and 504 of the Penal Code. “As the accused did not appear before the court today, the judge issued the arrest warrant,” Humayun Kabir said. According to the complaint, Amir Hamza made the remarks during a discussion at Hatash Haripur Grand Mosque on March 27, referring to a speech by the minister. “Iqbal Hassan Mahmood Tuku comes from a respected Muslim family and is actively involved with various religious institutions. He has established mosques and madrasas in his constituency and observes key religious practices,” the complainant said. “Despite this, he was described as an ‘atheist’ and ‘thoroughly anti-Islamic’, which has harmed his reputation,” he added. Meanwhile, another defamation suit seeking Tk 100 crore in damages was filed against Amir Hamza on March 30 at the Sirajganj Sadar Cognisance Court over the same incident.​

title: Four of a family murdered in Naogaon
body: A couple and their two children were found murdered in Naogaon’s Niamatpur upazila. The deceased were identified as Habibur Rahman, 32, of Bahadurpur village; his wife Popy Sultana, 25; their son Parvez, 9; and their three-year-old daughter Sadia Akter. The parents were found with their throats slit, while the children’s bodies bore head injuries, Officer-in-Charge of Niamatpur Police Station Mahbubur Rahman told The Daily Star. The incident is believed to have occurred around midnight today, the OC said, adding that the motive behind the killings has yet to be confirmed. Local neighbours said it is not known who carried out the attack under the cover of night. After Fajr prayers, seeing the door open, neighbours entered the house and found the bodies. Police were later informed and arrived at the scene.

title: NIRCH deputy director stabbed in Mohakhali
body: Criminals stabbed a deputy director of the National Institute of Cancer Research and Hospital (NICRH) in Dhaka’s Mohakhali area yesterday afternoon. The injured was identified as Ahmed Hossain, 50. The incident occurred around 3:30pm near the old campus of BRAC University. Confirming the matter, Deputy Commissioner of Gulshan Division M Tanvir Ahamed told The Daily Star that police visited the spot after the attack. Efforts are underway to identify and arrest those involved, he said. Police said Ahmed was returning home from the hospital when two to three assailants attacked him, stabbing him in his right hand and back before fleeing the scene. NICRH Director Mostafa Aziz Sumon said Ahmed initially received treatment at the cancer hospital but was later shifted to Dhaka Medical College Hospital as he sustained multiple injuries. The motive behind the attack is still unclear, with police investigating, he said. Asked whether the assault was linked to tender-related issues, he said that Ahmed is the key person for such work at the hospital and those involved in tender matters often receive threatening phone calls. Whether yesterday’s attack is connected to that will be known after the investigation, he added. Faridul Islam, the officer-in-charge of Banani Police Station, said they have collected CCTV footage from the spot and nearby areas. Police could not yet ascertain the reason behind the attack as they have not been able to talk to the injured. Health and Family Welfare Minister Sardar Md Sakhawat Husain visited NICRH following the incident and assured prompt action to arrest the culprits.

title: Suspended Ctg cop sentenced to jail in dowry torture case
body: A Chattogram court today sentenced a former traffic sergeant, who was suspended, to one year in jail in a case filed over torturing his wife for dowry. Chattogram Women and Child Repression Prevention Tribunal-1 passed the order after the court found Md Nazim Uddin guilty after examining all the evidence and witnesses, confirmed tribunal’s Public Prosecutor Mohammad Younus. He said the court also fined him Tk 5,000, in default of which, he has to serve one more year in jail. However, the court granted him bail on condition of filing an appeal. According to the court source, Nazim and Ashrefa Jahan got married in 2004. The couple has two children, and they used to live in a flat in the port city’s Jamal Khan area. The case statement said Nazim demanded Tk 10 lakh from his wife to buy the flat. As she failed to pay the amount, the cop tortured his wife in March 2020. Later, the wife lodged a complaint with the court on August 17, 2020. The court later ordered police to investigate the case and submit a report. The PP said that during the trial proceedings, Nazim divorced his wife.

title: Four arrested over extortion attempt and shooting in Dhaka's Kafrul
body: Rapid Action Battalion (Rab) has arrested four suspects in connection with a shooting incident at a garment factory in Dhaka’s Kafrul area, where extortionists allegedly demanded Tk 1 crore from the owner. A team of Rab‑4 detained Rana, 31; Sagar Sheikh, 28; Md Kalu, 28; and Shashi, 22 during a drive in Mirpur on Sunday night. At a press briefing today, Rab spokesperson Additional Superintendent of Police KN Roy Niyati said the suspects were identified through CCTV footage. According to Rab, 12-13 men stormed AKM Apparels on Saturday evening, demanded Tk 1 crore from owner Kamrul, and fired two blank shots when he refused. They vandalised a locker, threatened to kill him within three days if the money was not paid, and took away the CCTV DVR and hard disk. Kamrul later filed a case with Kafrul Police Station, prompting Rab‑4 to launch the drive. Officials said Rana was the mastermind, having surveyed the factory’s security beforehand. The suspects were also involved in extortion, drug-related offences, and attempts to establish dominance in Mirpur and Kafrul. Rab confirmed multiple cases had previously been filed against the four for robbery, theft, and extortion. Drives are ongoing to recover the firearms used in the incident.

title: Mob beats man to death over robbery allegations
body: A man was beaten to death by a mob during an attempted robbery in Pirojpur’s Nazirpur upazila early yesterday. The victim is Dulal, 26, from Hijla in Barishal, said Nazirpur Police Station Officer-in-Charge Tarikul Islam. Quoting locals, the police official said a group of around eight men entered the house of college teacher Nazmul Hasan, also known as Ujjal, in Kalardoania village early Sunday and held the family hostage to try and rob the place. At one point, Nazmul was attacked with a sharp weapon. He and his son Miskat were seriously injured and later taken to Dhaka Medical College Hospital. Neighbours rushed in after hearing screams and managed to catch one of the gang members, Dulal. He was later beaten by locals, leaving him dead on the spot, the OC said. He said they are working to identify and arrest the other suspects. A case is being prepared in connection with the incident and the body has been sent for autopsy, OC Tarikul added. Dulal was accused in at least 15 cases across different police stations, the OC said.

title: Rape Attempt: Teenager’s family, home attacked ‘for suing suspect’
body: A teenage girl’s family came under attack allegedly for suing a local madrasa superintendent for attempting to rape her in Noakhali’s Subarnachar upazila. Her house in Madhya Charbagya village was vandalised and looted, while her family members were assaulted during attack on Thursday noon. A video of the attack went viral on social media on Saturday afternoon, sparking huge criticism among netizens. The five-minute video shows a large group of people attacking a house, with many of them carrying sticks in their hands. The victim’s family members were seen crying, and the attackers were asking them to withdraw the case. According to the case statement, the 14-year-old girl was a resident student at a local madrasa where Abul Khayer, 35, acts as the superintendent. On February 5, the girl’s grandmother went to the madrasa to see the girl. At that time, Abul Khayer told the grandmother that the girl was attacked by evil power and she needed exorcism. Then Abul Khayer took the girl to his bedroom on the madrasa premises and tried to rape her under the pretext of exorcism. When the girl started screaming, Abul Khayer released her. Then the victim shared the incident with her grandmother. Later, the victim’s family members informed local union parishad’s acting chairman Jamal Uddin about the matter. But Jamal kept wasting time in the name of social arbitration to settle the issue. Finally, the victim’s father filed a case with Charjabbar Police Station on Thursday morning against Abul Khayer, said the police station’s Officer-in-Charge (OC) Md. Lutfur Rahman. Later in the day, around 100 people attacked the victim’s house, assaulted the family members and carried out vandalism and looting. Talking to journalists, the victim said the madrasa superintendent touched private parts of her body in the name of exorcism and tried to rape her. “As my father has filed case, they attacked on our house,” she told. Talking to The Daily Star, the victim’s father said, “My daughter is not the sole victim. Rather, the man (Abul Khayer) did the same things with some other girls in the past. But none disclosed it due to social stigma.” “But I have protested and filed a case. That is why they attacked our house and are pressurising me to withdraw the case,” added the father. Asked, union chairman Jamal Uddin admitted that the victim’s family members went to him, and he tried to arrange a social arbitration. He claimed the attempt failed as no party came to him on the day scheduled for the arbitration. Contacted, OC Lutfur Rahman said the girl’s mother filed another case on Saturday in connection with the attack. Later police arrested a person, Jahangir, 35, for his alleged involvement with the attack on their home. “However, attempted rape accused Abul Khayer went into hiding after the filing of the case. Police are trying to arrest him,” added the police officer.

title: Man held over rape of madrasa student in Sandwip
body: A man was arrested today over the rape of a class 7 student of a local madrasa in Sandwip upazila of Chattogram yesterday. The arrestee, Md Milad, 40, the student's neighbour, was held from Bashbaria Ferry Ghat of Sandwip while he was trying to flee the island, said Inspector (Investigation) Sujan Hawladar of Sandwip Model Police Station. The victim’s father filed a complaint with the police facility on Saturday night. The policeman said on April 18 afternoon, finding the victim alone at home, Milad raped her. Police sent the victim to Chattogram Medical College Hospital (CMCH) One Stop Crisis Centre for medical examination.

title: Indigenous community alleges land grab bid after temple attack in Dinajpur
body: At least six people were injured when a temple belonging to the local indigenous community was vandalised by a group, allegedly over a dispute involving khas (state-owned) land in Dinajpur’s Birganj upazila this afternoon. The incident took place in Sanka Christianpara village around 1:00pm, said Saiful Islam, officer-in-charge of Birganj Police Station. Quoting witnesses and locals, OC Saiful Islam told this correspondent that members of the Mormu and Soren indigenous communities had a long-standing dispute with Rejaul Islam, son of Abdul Kader from Ghoraband village, over 93 decimals of khas land. According to the indigenous families, they have been living on the land for generations. A temple and a cemetery are also located on the land. Rejaul claims ownership of the land. Around 1:00pm today, a group of 150-200 people, allegedly led by Rejaul and his uncle Azad, attacked the temple and cemetery to capture the land, the OC said quoting locals. Armed with sticks, iron rods, and sharp weapons, they vandalised the temple and the idol inside and cut down 10-12 trees in the cemetery, the OC said. The attackers also vandalised a house at the time. When members of the indigenous community resisted, the attackers assaulted them, leaving several people injured. On receiving information, police rushed to the spot, dispersed the attackers, and deployed additional forces to prevent further untoward incidents, added the police official. The OC added that police have collected the vandalised idol and other materials as evidence. Among the injured, Pius Mormu, 45, son of Mangal Jak Mormu, and Biswanath Soren, 27, son of Gonesh Soren, were admitted to Birganj Upazila Health Complex. Pius Mormu told this correspondent that they have been living on the land for generations, but the attackers are attempting to capture it illegally, which led to today’s attack. Anthony Mormu, head of the indigenous community in the village, said they have been using the land for over a century. Around 50 to 60 families live in Sanka Christianpara village, while more than 200 landless indigenous families in the surrounding area use the cemetery. He said both Hindu and Christian members of the indigenous community live in the village. Preparation is underway to file a case following the attack, he said. Speaking to this correspondent, Rezaul claimed that he purchased 41 decimals of land from a person named Mansur Ali in 1999 and another 48 decimals from the same person in 2023. He said the remaining four decimals are part of a cemetery. However, he denied carrying out any attack on the indigenous people. Dr Fariha Tasnim, a medical officer at the health complex, said Biswanath Soren sustained an arrow injury to his chest. After visiting the spot, Birganj Upazila Nirbahi Officer (UNO) Suma Khatun told The Daily Star that the administration is aware of the incident and has instructed the authorities concerned to take legal action. Additional forces have been deployed to maintain law and order. Birganj AC (Land) Diponkar Barman also confirmed that the disputed land is khas land.

title: Rab arrests main accused in murder of 6-year-old Fatema in Tangail
body: Rapid Action Battalion (Rab) today arrested the main accused in the murder of six-year-old Fatema Khatun of Tangail’s Madhupur upazila. According to a press release issued by CPC-3 of Rab-14’s Tangail camp, the accused, Md Abbas Ali, 30, was arrested from the College Para area of Tangail town. The incident occurred on April 11 when Fatema was lured to a nearby market by Abbas under the pretext of buying juice. When she failed to return home, her family filed a general diary with Madhupur Police Station. The next day, her body was discovered in a maize field near her uncle’s house. Fatema’s mother subsequently filed a murder case against Abbas and unidentified others. During preliminary interrogation, Abbas admitted to strangling Fatema to steal her gold and silver jewellery. He confessed to acting alone in the crime. Captain Tawhid, acting commander of CPC‑3, confirmed Abbas has been handed over to Madhupur Police Station for further legal action.

title: HC asks why domestic workers’ registration is not mandatory
body: The High Court today issued a rule asking the relevant government authorities to explain why the registration of domestic workers should not be made mandatory nationwide to ensure the safety of both workers and their employers. The court also asked them to explain why the government's failure to enforce the Domestic Servants' Registration Ordinance, 1961 should not be declared illegal. The ordinance makes domestic workers’ registration mandatory, provides for the issuance of registration cards, bars employment without registration, and prescribes penalties for violations. The HC bench of Justice Razik-Al-Jalil and Justice Debashish Roy Chowdhury issued the rule following a writ petition filed as a public interest litigation by Supreme Court lawyer Barrister Khadijatul Kobra Bappy. Officials concerned, including secretaries at the ministries of home, law, and labour, have been made respondents to the rule. Lawyers Khadijatul Kobra, Tanzim Al Islam and Rowshan Ara appeared for the writ petitioner during the hearing. The petitioner said that the absence of any compulsory registration, verification, or monitoring framework has created a regulatory vacuum in the domestic work sector, which endangers the life, safety, and property of employers and household members, and the dignity, security, and legal protection of domestic workers, thereby undermining public safety, social order, and lawful employment relations.

title: Mob beats man to death over robbery allegations in Pirojpur
body: A man was beaten to death by a mob during an attempted robbery in Pirojpur's Nazirpur upazila early today. Neighbours rushed in after hearing screams and managed to catch one of the gang members, Dulal. He was later beaten by locals, leaving him dead on the spot, the OC said. He said they are working to identify and arrest the other suspects. A case is being prepared in connection with the incident and the body has been sent for autopsy, OC Tarikul added. title: Police constable attacked during drug raid in Tongi
body: A police constable was seriously injured in an attack during an anti-narcotics drive in Gazipur’s Tongi Bazar area last night. The injured constable, Rahat Hossain, is currently undergoing treatment at Tongi Shaheed Ahsan Ullah Master General Hospital. Sub-Inspector Tuhin Mia of Tongi East Police Station confirmed the incident to The Daily Star this afternoon. According to eyewitnesses, police were carrying out routine anti-drug drives in different locations. During one such drive near the Islami Bank area of Tongi Bazar, Constable Rahat was suddenly attacked by suspected drug dealers. He was critically injured in the assault, and locals quickly rescued him and took him to the hospital. SI Tuhin Mia said Rahat Hossain is posted at Tongi East Police Station. A case has been filed against four to five unidentified individuals in connection with the attack, and efforts are underway to identify and arrest those involved.

title: 5 arrested over abduction of man from Tongi, victim recused: Police
body: Police have rescued a man who was abducted from Gazipur's Tongi area and arrested five alleged kidnappers in connection with the incident, said an official of Gazipur Metropolitan Police (GMP). “An operational team, using information technology, identified the locations of the victim and the suspects and conducted a raid in Mirzapur upazila of Tangail district,” GMP Inspector (Media) Khondkar Jalal Uddin Ahmed told The Daily Star this morning. The arrestees were identified as Rafiqul Islam, 36; Fazle Rabbi, 26; Rezaul Islam Hridoy, 31; Selim Reza, 37; and Sanjida Akter Rupa, 35. “A written complaint was filed with Tongi West Police Station Shakil Mia on Saturday. In the complaint, Shakil alleged that his elder brother, Zakir Hossain, 40, had been abducted by 4-5 unidentified individuals from the Abdullahpur flyover. Based on the complaint, Tongi West Police Station registered a case,” the GMP official added. The arrestees have been sent to court, police said.

title: Nine rescued after migrant trawler capsizes in Andaman Sea; six charged with trafficking
body: Nine people were rescued on April 9 in the Andaman Sea after a migrant trawler carrying Rohingya and Bangladeshi passengers capsized while attempting an illegal journey from the Cox’s Bazar-Teknaf coast to Malaysia. Six Bangladeshis have since been charged with human trafficking by the Coast Guard and are now in jail, while three Rohingya survivors have been identified as victims, Officer-in-Charge Saiful Islam of Teknaf Police Station said. The survivors were rescued by a Bangladesh-flagged vessel, MT Meghna Pride, en route from Chattogram to Indonesia, after they were found drifting at sea holding water bottles and debris. They were later handed over to the Coast Guard. According to the rescued Rohingya, at least four of the accused were directly involved in operating the trawler. One survivor said he could not confirm the roles of the remaining two. The UN and several organisations estimate that at least 250 Bangladeshi and Rohingya passengers, including children, are missing in the incident. According to agencies, the trawler reportedly sank due to heavy winds, rough seas and overcrowding, although it remains unclear when exactly the vessel capsized. However, authorities have no official list of the missing. No cases have been filed by victims’ families so far. A case was filed with Teknaf Police Station on April 11. According to the case statement, the six accused -- Md Hamid, Md Akbar, Md Tofayel, Syed Alam, Md Sohan Uddin and Mohiuddin Hriday -- are part of a trafficking network. Md Rafiqul Islam, a Kutupalong camp resident who was rescued, said, “Md Hamid and Syed Alam were the boatmen, Mohiuddin Hriday operated the engine, and Akbar acted as a broker. I cannot confirm the roles of the other two.” He alleged abuse by Akbar. “When I asked for a glass of water, he kicked me to the ground. He was the one who beat people the most.” Another survivor, Enam Ullah Imran of Camp No 1, gave a similar account. Teknaf Police Station Sub-Inspector Sanjib Kanti Nath, the investigating officer, said, “The case was filed by the Coast Guard. Their investigation found involvement of all six. We will seek a remand, then we can provide more details.” Investigators said passengers were recruited from different parts of Cox’s Bazar through brokers. Rafiqul Islam said a broker named Mah Nur from Block C of Camp No 6 lured him with a promise of work at Teknaf port. His family later paid Tk 300,000 before the broker fled after the capsize. Md Hamid, from Fadnar Dail in Cox’s Bazar town, is the prime accused. His brother Md Jubayer said, “Hamid works on fishing trawlers. He left without informing anyone to go to Malaysia. Another younger brother, Ibrahim, who was on the same journey, is still missing.” Locals alleged Hamid had prior involvement in such trips. A grocery shop owner, speaking anonymously, said, “This was his sixth trip to Malaysia. He took four others along, including his brother. Since he had gone five times before, others trusted him.” Locals also alleged Hamid’s elder brother Ilias and his wife Rozina acted as brokers. Enamul Haque, father of another accused Mohiuddin Hriday, said his son had lived in Cox’s Bazar for 15 to 17 years and worked on fishing boats but that he had no contact with him. Cox’s Bazar Deputy Commissioner Md Mannan said the administration has shared preliminary information with relevant authorities. “We have not yet received any specific list,” he said, adding that survivors have not provided clear details. Refugee Relief and Repatriation Commissioner Mizanur Rahman said uncertainty and statelessness are key drivers of such journeys. “They have no certainty of return, conflict continues in their homeland, and life in the camps is not favorable. All of this creates frustration,” he said, adding that many undertake risky sea voyages believing a better life awaits. He described it as “voluntary trafficking.” He added that the exact number of trafficked Rohingya is difficult to determine, as cases often surface only after accidents or rescue operations.

title: Drug dispute, prior enmity led to Mohammadpur murder: police
body: A financial dispute and prior enmity led to the murder of 28-year-old alleged drug dealer Asadul Haque, alias "Lambu Asadul", in Dhaka's Mohammadpur early Thursday, police said. Law enforcers have so far arrested seven people in connection with the killing. A Dhaka court on Saturday placed six of them on a four-day remand. The victim was lured out of his rented flat in Mohammadpur's Metro Housing and hacked to death near Sadeq Khan brickfield in Rayerbazar around 12:50am on Thursday. Briefing reporters at the DMP Media Centre on Saturday, Tejgaon Division Deputy Commissioner Md Ibne Mizan revealed that Asadul had been involved in the drug trade for several years. He had recently engaged in a conflict with another local drug dealer, Akhtar Hossain, 45. "Asadul had earlier fought with Akhtar, who filed a case against him. Asadul was jailed and recently secured bail. They also had a monetary dispute," the DC said. After Asadul got out of jail, Akhtar and his associates called him out at night, stabbed him, and hit him with bricks, the DC informed. Following the incident, the victim's cousin filed a murder case with the Mohammadpur Police Station. Police later arrested Akhtar, Md Munna, 24, Miraj Fakir, 22, and Nayan alias Khokon, 24, from Keraniganj. They also recovered the suspected murder weapon, a switchblade knife, and a motorcycle. Meanwhile, Rab-2 arrested three others -- Asadul Islam, 25, Md Shawon, 27, and Mominul Islam -- from the Metro Housing area. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Ariful Islam remanded Akhtar, Munna, Miraj, Nayan, Asadul Islam, and Shawon for four days after the Investigation Officer, Akkel Ali, sought a seven-day remand. Police noted that both the victim and the accused had prior criminal records. Asadul faced six cases, including four under the Narcotics Control Act. Munna had seven cases related to drugs and mugging, while Miraj and Nayan also faced previous charges. However, no prior record has been found against Akhtar. Addressing concerns about crime in Mohammadpur, DC Mizan said offenders often come from outside, commit crimes, and flee. He assured that checkpoints and regular drives would be intensified to curb such incidents. The victim, who hailed from Barishal's Gournadi, lived with his family in Mohammadpur.

title: JCD factional clash: MMC suspends classes, exams for a week
body: All classes and exams at Mymensingh Medical College have been suspended for a week after a clash between two factions of Chhatra Dal left two students injured. Students were instructed to vacate the halls by 8:00am yesterday, said Principal Prof Dr Md Nazmul Alam Khan. The decision was made at an emergency meeting of the academic council held early yesterday, he said. Additional Superintendent of Police (Admin) Md Abdullah Al Mamun said the clash broke out around 9:00pm Friday at the college dormitory. The injured -- Md Muaz and Mir Hamidur, both third‑year students -- belong to rival groups of the college unit of Jatiyotabadi Chhatra Dal (JCD). Quoting campus sources, the police official said Muaz went to Hamidur’s room where a heated exchange over refuelling a motorcycle escalated into a scuffle. Hamidur and his associates allegedly beat Muaz and forced him out. Later, as Hamidur went out for tea, he was reportedly attacked and struck on the head with a blunt object. A chase and counter‑chase followed between the two groups, triggering the clash. Police rushed to the scene and brought the situation under control. The injured were admitted to Mymensingh Medical College Hospital. Muaz was later referred to Dhaka Medical College Hospital, while Hamidur remains under treatment at MMCH. Kotwali Model Police Station OC Shebirul Islam said one person, Nafiul Islam, 25, has been detained, though no case had been filed yet. The college authorities have formed a three-member probe committee tasked with submitting a report within seven working days. JCD unit convener Tanvir Abdullah denied it was a factional clash, claiming it may have resulted from personal enmity, and said the JCD central committee is also investigating.

title: 48hrs after Pallabi teacher killing, cops clueless
body: Police are yet to identify any suspects 48 hours after a 68-year-old schoolteacher was killed with a hammer in her rented flat in the capital’s Pallabi. Police recovered the bloodstained body of Firoza Khanom Josna, a teacher at Holy Crescent Ideal School, on Friday afternoon. The inquest report, prepared after an autopsy at Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital morgue, noted severe injury marks on the left side of her head, as well as on her nose and eyes. Police also recovered a blood-stained hammer at the crime scene, which they believe had been used in the killing. Firoza had been living alone for 10 to 12 years in a rented room on the first floor of a six-storey building on Road 8, Block D, Section 12 in Mirpur, her brother Nazmul Azam told The Daily Star. She hailed from Krishnapur under Munshipara Police Station in Kurigram. Nazmul said she had married decades ago but was later divorced. She had no children and maintained little contact with her family. She occupied one room of a three-room flat, while another family lived in the remaining two rooms as sub-tenants, said one of her neighbours, Md Milon. The family had gone to their village home early Thursday and returned on Friday afternoon, he added. Abdul Mannan, a security guard at the building, said Firoza gave private tuition at various houses in addition to her teaching job. She usually left home every morning and returned around 10:00pm. When she did not leave the house even after 10:30am on Friday, the guard went to check on her. Finding the door open, he informed local resident Mohiuddin, and they entered the flat and found her lying on her bed in a pool of blood. On information, Pallabi police went to the scene. The Crime Scene Unit of the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) also collected evidence. Alamgir Jahan, officer-in-charge of Pallabi Police Station, told The Daily Star that the incident likely took place in the early hours of Friday. “The door was open. It is highly likely the killer was someone known to her, as she would not normally open the door to a stranger at that hour,” he said. The victim’s brother, Nazmul Azam, filed a murder case with Pallabi Police Station. Sub-Inspector Al-Amin, the investigating officer, said: “Despite collecting evidence from the scene and reviewing nearby CCTV footage, we have not been able to identify any suspects yet.”

title: Man sent to jail over post on chief whip
body: Content creator AM Hasan Nasim was sent to jail yesterday in a case filed on charges of spreading misleading information on social media and blackmailing Jatiya Sangsad Chief Whip Nurul Islam Moni. Earlier in the day, BNP activist Nazrul Islam -- who claims to be a supporter of the chief whip -- filed the case with Gulshan Police Station under sections 25 and 27 of the Cyber Security Ordinance, accusing some unnamed individuals. The Cyber Security Ordinance 2025, issued by the interim government, was recently ratified in parliament. The case appears to have been filed in violation of section 40(1) of the ordinance, which states, “No person, other than an aggrieved person, a person authorised in writing by such aggrieved person, or a member of a law enforcement agency, shall be entitled to file a case under this Ordinance.” Contacted by The Daily Star last night, complainant Nazrul Islam said, “I did not communicate with the honourable member of parliament before filing this case. “I acted on my own because I felt bad. The whole Patharghata area is being portrayed falsely on Facebook over a minor incident every day. It has created unrest in the locality.” Asked about the legality of the case, Md Dawud Hossain, officer-in-charge of Gulshan Police Station, said, “It seemed cognisable to me, so I took the case … . The court will give directions if any law was violated in filing the case.” A team of the Detective Branch of Dhaka Metropolitan Police picked up Hasan Nasim from his house in the city’s Agargaon area around 8:00pm on Friday. Yesterday, he was produced before the court with a seven-day remand prayer after being shown arrested in the case. Later, Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Md Hasib Ullah Pias rejected the remand prayer and sent Hasan to jail, according to a sub-inspector working at the court. The court also fixed today (April 19) for the hearing of the bail petition, the SI added. According to the police forwarding report, detectives arrested him after finding his involvement during investigation. In the case statement, the complainant said that on April 11, he saw a Facebook post on “Patharghata.com”, which said, “Three whales were brought from the sea, two sharks are on the way, Inshallah -- everyone’s invited: Chief Whip”. Chief Whip Moni had, in fact, said these lines in parliament on April 10. Meanwhile, the case statement further said that multiple screenshots of different posts were sent, with “an intent to blackmail”, to the chief whip’s WhatsApp number from an unknown number. Complainant Nazrul also claimed that the same account had repeatedly published and circulated misleading information at different times. He said he later informed Moni about the matter. Contacted, Moni said that five to seven Facebook pages had been consistently spreading propaganda since December last year. At that time, they filed general diaries with three police stations and also lodged a complaint with the returning officer. Based on that complaint, the cyber police informed him that they had tracked down the individual on Friday night. NCP STATEMENT The National Citizen Party, in a statement signed by its Joint Member Secretary (Office) Saleh Uddin Sifat and issued yesterday, has condemned the arrest of Nasim. Questioning the charges, the party noted that while section 25 of the ordinance defines “blackmailing” as threatening someone to extract illegal benefits, the First Information Report lacks any description of what benefits or actions were demanded. The NCP also highlighted the government’s contradictory stance on free speech, recalling that Prime Minister Tarique Rahman shared a caricature of himself on August 11, 2024, celebrating the restoration of political cartoons in Bangladesh. “But just two months into his government’s tenure, an activist has lost the freedom to share cartoons and has been sent to jail in a bailable case,” the statement read. Calling the case baseless, the NCP accused law enforcers of extreme unprofessionalism for “illegally arresting” a citizen, and demanded an immediate explanation from the government along with Nasim’s unconditional release.

title: Manikganj triple murder: Teen held, no case filed over mob killing of 2
body: Police have arrested a 15-year-old boy in connection with a case filed over the killing of a seven-year-old girl in Manikganj Sadar upazila. Acting on a tip-off, police arrested the teenager from Dhaka’s Nawabganj area on Friday night, said Manikganj superintendent of police Sarwar Alam yesterday. “He is currently in police custody. After interrogation, he will be produced before the juvenile court,” the SP said, adding that drives were underway to arrest another accused named Roni. Meanwhile, the mother of the child, Atika Akter, filed a murder case against five people, including the teenager, with Sadar Police Station yesterday, SP Sarwar also said. However, no case has yet been filed over the killing of the arrested teenager’s father and uncle in a mob attack on Thursday night, following allegations that the girl had been murdered. The SP said no written complaint has so far been submitted by the relatives regarding the mob killing. “If they file any complaint, it will be registered as a case,” he added. According to police and locals, Atika Akter, daughter of Dudal Mia of Bonparil village, went missing from near her home on Thursday afternoon. Around 10:00pm that night, locals found Atika’s body in a maize field near her home. The girl was found with her hands and legs tied. Police suspect that she was killed either during an attempted rape or robbery of her jewellery. Atika’s family alleged that a teenage boy was involved. Later, agitated people beat up the teenage boy’s elder brother Nazmul, 20; their father Pannu Miah, 45; and Pannu’s brother Fazlu, 28. On information, police went to the spot and rescued Nazmul alive but in a critically injured condition. Pannu and Fazlu were found dead, said Aminul Islam, inspector (investigation) of Manikganj Sadar Police Station. “We have found evidence of rape attempt on the girl. However, details will be known after getting the autopsy report,” Aminul added.

title: Neighbour held over murder of 6-year-old in Brahmanbaria
body: Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) has claimed to have uncovered the motive behind the killing of a six-and-a-half-year-old schoolgirl in Brahmanbaria, stating that she was murdered after resisting inappropriate physical contact and intent to inform her mother. A neighbour of the victim, Ishaq Mia, an auto-rickshaw driver, was detained in Mohonpur village in Brahmanbaria Sadar upazila today in connection with the case, said Sachin Chakma, SP of PBI. He said the suspect admitted to his involvement during primary interrogation. “He found the child alone near a local school on April 15 and took her out -- under the pretext of a walk -- before bringing her back to his house later that night,” he added. The suspect was alone at home at the time. When he tried to touch the child inappropriately, she resisted and said she would inform her mother. Fearing exposure, he pressed her face with a piece of cloth and suffocated her to death, added the PBI official. The girl’s body was recovered two days later, yesterday afternoon, from a bush near her house, stuffed inside a sack. The victim was the daughter of an expatriate living in Saudi Arabia and a nursery student at a local kindergarten. Her mother filed a murder case with Brahmanbaria Sadar Model Police Station against unidentified individuals, following which the PBI took over the case.

title: Manikganj triple murder: Teen arrested, no case filed over mob killing of 2
