Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Md Jewel Rana passed the order rejecting a two-day remand prayer for her submitted by the Detective Branch (DB) of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police, said a court staffer. A DB team arrested her from Dhanmondi area early today. On May 25 last year, the victim, Mohammad Ashraful, filed the case with the court, accusing deposed prime minister Sheikh Hasina and 129 others. The officer-in-charge of Lalbagh Police Station later recorded it as a First Information Report (FIR) on July 17 the same year, following a court directive. According to the case documents, Ashraful was shot in the Azimpur area of Dhaka on July 18, 2024. According to the official website of the Bangladesh Parliament, Shirin served as Speaker from April 30, 2013, until her resignation on September 2, 2024.

title: Lt Gen (retd) Masud on four-day remand in July uprising case
body: A Dhaka court today placed Lt Gen (retd) Masud Uddin Chowdhury, a key figure in the army‑backed caretaker government, on a four‑day remand in a case filed over the killing of furniture trader Mohammad Delowar Hossain during the July uprising. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Md Monirul Islam today passed the order after detectives produced Masud before the court with a seven-day remand prayer, said a sub-inspector working at the court. According to the police forwarding report, Masud was arrested in the case as a suspect. On July 6 last year, Delowar’s wife, Liza, 34, filed a case with Mirpur Model Police Station, accusing 74 people, mostly Awami League leaders and activists, in this connection. According to the case documents, Delowar was shot in the Mirpur-10 area on July 19, 2024, during the mass uprising. He died while undergoing treatment at City Care General Hospital in Dhaka’s Shyamoli area on July 21 the same year. On March 24 this year, Masud was arrested from his home in Dhaka's Baridhara DOHS by a team of detectives in a case filed with Paltan Model Police Station over human trafficking and forgery of documents. The case was filed on September 3, 2024, by a proprietor of Afia Overseas against 103 individuals, including former minister Imran Ahmed. Masud previously served as GOC of the 9 Infantry Division during the state of emergency declared on January 11, 2007, and later became the chief coordinator of the National Coordination Committee on Serious Crimes and Corruption. He was promoted to lieutenant general, posted to the National Defence College on June 2, 2008, and later appointed to the Bangladesh High Commission in Canberra on June 8, 2008.

title: July uprising: ICT-2 issues arrest warrants against Hasan Mahmud, Nowfel, 16 others
body: The International Crimes Tribunal-2 (ICT-2) today issued arrest warrants against former ministers Hasan Mahmud, Mohibul Hassan Chowdhury Nowfel, and 16 others in a crimes against humanity case linked to the July uprising in Chattogram. The tribunal passed the order after taking cognisance of formal charges filed by the prosecution against 22 accused. Of them, four are currently in jail in connection with other cases, while 18 remain absconding. The tribunal issued fresh arrest warrants for the fugitives and ordered the authorities concerned to produce the four in custody before it on April 19. The four in custody are former Chattogram-6 lawmaker Fazle Karim, Jubo League leader Azizur Rahman, Tauhidul Islam, and Md Firoz. Earlier, the prosecution submitted formal charges to the tribunal’s registrar, accusing the 22 individuals of crimes against humanity during the July uprising in Chattogram. According to the prosecution, the accused face three counts. The first relates to the killing of Wasim Akram, Faysal Ahmed Shanto, and Faruq Ahmed. The second concerns the killing of Tanvir Siddiquee, Saimon alias Mahin, and Hridoy Chandra on August 4. The third involves the injury of Jahid Hasan, Abdullah Kader, Achiya Khatun, Sanjida Sultana, and Abdullah Lubab, along with more than 100 others. Other accused include former Chattogram City Corporation mayor AJM Nasir Uddin, Awami League leader Rezaul Karim Chowdhury, Md Mohiuddin Bacchu, Helal Akbar Chowdhury Babor, former Chattogram city unit BCL general secretary Nurul Azim Rony, former ward-21 councillor Shaibal Das Sumon, Abu Salek, Esrarul Haque, HM Mithu, Nur Mostafa Tinu, Debashish Paul Debu, Zamir Uddin, Imran Ahmed Imu, Zakaria Dastagir, Mohiuddin Farhad, and Sumon Dey, among others. The case earlier drew attention after allegations surfaced that a prosecutor had sought Tk 1 crore from Fazle Karim’s family in exchange for arranging bail in the case.

title: Former speaker Shirin Sharmin Chaudhury arrested in July uprising case
body: The Detective Branch (DB) of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police arrested former speaker Shirin Sharmin Chaudhury from Dhanmondi early today in connection with a case filed over the July uprising. Shafiqul Islam, additional commissioner of DB, DMP, confirmed the development to The Daily Star this morning. “She has been taken to the DB office,” he said. Shafiqul Islam said she was arrested in a case filed with Lalbagh Police Station over incidents during the July uprising. She will be produced before a court today. Responding to a query about remand, the police official said she is currently being questioned. A decision on whether to seek remand will be taken after interrogation, he added. According to the official website of the Bangladesh Parliament, Shirin served as Speaker from April 30, 2013, until her resignation on September 2, 2024. Following the fall of the Awami League government on August 5, 2024, multiple cases have been filed against party leaders across the country. On August 27, a case was filed against Shirin in connection with the death of a jeweller, Muslim Uddin, in Rangpur during the July uprising.

title: Tonu Murder Case: Court orders DNA test of 3 ex-army men
body: In the decade-old Sohagi Jahan Tonu murder case, a Cumilla court yesterday ordered the cross-matching of DNA profile of three retired army personnel. Senior Judicial Magistrate Mominul Haque of Cumilla Sadar Cognisance Court-1 came up with the order after Inspector Tarikul Islam of the Police Bureau of Investigation filed a plea to that end. The three army personnel, all currently retired, are Sergeant Zahid, Warrant Officer Hafizur Rahman, and Soldier Jahangir Alam. Cumilla Court Inspector Mamunur Rashid said the court had earlier directed the investigation officer to appear before it on April 6 (yesterday) and provide an update on the case progress. Yesterday, Tonu’s father, Yar Hossain, appeared before the court once again to demand justice for his daughter. According to court sources, 79 hearing dates have passed so far, while six investigation officers from four different agencies have handled the case. However, no arrests have been made, and the trial has yet to begin, even though more than a decade has passed. On March 20, 2016, Tonu, a student of history at Cumilla Victoria College and also a theatre activist, went to give tuition at Sergeant Zahid’s house in Cumilla Cantonment. When she did not return home at her usual time, her father -- an employee of the Cumilla Cantonment Board -- went out in search of her. At one point, Tonu’s lifeless body was found in the powerhouse area inside the cantonment. She was taken to Cumilla CMH, where doctors said she was brought dead. An autopsy was conducted but objections were raised over the report. Her body was later exhumed for a second autopsy on March 30. The victim’s parents had said her long hair had been cut with scissors, and that there were bloodied injuries on her nose and face, as well as an injury at the back of her head. A murder case was filed with Cumilla Kotwali Police Station on March 21, a day after her body was recovered. Initially, the investigation was handled by the officer-in-charge of the Nazira Bazar police outpost. The case was later transferred to Cumilla Detective Branch of police and then to the Criminal Investigation Department. The exact cause of Tonu’s death has yet to be determined, despite two autopsies, though CID officials confirmed through initial DNA tests that she was raped before being murdered. Sperm from three unidentified individuals was found on her clothes, but investigators have not been able to match it with any suspects. The killing triggered nationwide protests, with students and citizens taking to the streets demanding justice. At the time, authorities assured action, but the case remains unresolved.

title: Bangladeshi shot by BSF along border
body: A flag meeting was held yesterday between the Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) and India’s Border Security Force (BSF) on Lalmonirhat border, following an incident in which a Bangladeshi youth was injured by rubber bullets fired by the BSF and an Indian citizen was brought into Bangladesh by angry locals. At the meeting, BGB lodged a strong protest against the BSF, and demanded that such incidents of firing at the border must not occur in the future. The hour-long battalion commander-level BGB-BSF meeting was held at Rahmatpur Gatiar Vita area, about 20 yards inside Bangladesh, near sub-pillar no. 5 of border pillar 887 at the Dhabalsuti border in Patgram upazila, in the afternoon. The BGB team was led by Commanding Officer of BGB-61 Teesta Battalion Lt Col Syed Fazle Munim while the BSF team was led by Commandant of the BSF-98 Battalion Sunil Kumar. Nayek Subedar Badsha Mia, commander of the Dhabalsuti BOP camp under BGB-61 Teesta Battalion, said a Bangladeshi man, Mizanur Rahman, 28, was injured in the shoulder by rubber bullets fired by the BSF at Gatiar Vita around 10:00am this morning. Following the incident, local people became agitated and brought Indian citizen Sahodev Barman along with cattle into Bangladesh. “The Bangladeshi youth had gone to cut grass for cattle near the border and had mistakenly crossed the zero line, entering about 10 yards into Indian territory,” added Badsha. He said additional BGB personnel were deployed as tension rose along the border from morning until noon. “At the meeting, the Indian citizen along with the cattle was handed over to the BSF. A strong protest was lodged over the shooting incident that injured the Bangladeshi youth.” Patgram Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Nazmul Haque said, “When I spoke to the family members of the youth injured by BSF firing, they informed me that he was undergoing treatment at a private hospital in Rangpur and was currently out of danger.”

title: Cop suspended over alleged cash exchange at Dhaka court
body: A police officer was suspended today over allegations of taking money from a lawyer inside the lockup at the Dhaka Chief Metropolitan Magistrate (CMM) Court. Dhaka Metropolitan Police Deputy Commissioner (Media) NM Nasiruddin said due to the initial verification of the allegation and evidence in the video, the accused police officer, Mir Mosharraf Hossain, was suspended as an immediate measure. Talking to The Daily Star tonight he said that further necessary action will be taken after an inquiry against him. According to court sources, content creator RS Fahim Chowdhury was produced before the Dhaka CMM Court to be shown arrested in an attempted murder case filed with Mohammadpur Police Station linked to the July uprising. After the hearing, while he was being taken to the lockup of the CMM Court, a lawyer was seen giving money to a police constable on duty. Meanwhile, a video of the incident was circulating on social media. The police constable was identified as Mir Mosharraf Hossain. He claimed before the media that the lawyer had tried to force money on him so that he would deliver food to the accused. However, the identity of the lawyer involved in the incident could not be immediately confirmed.

title: Govt dismisses Assistant Attorney General Abul Hassan over financial misconduct allegation
body: The government has dismissed Assistant Attorney General (AAG) Md Abul Hassan after allegations of financial misconduct were raised against him. Supreme Court lawyer Abul Hassan was appointed as an AAG on August 28, 2024. The appointment has been cancelled and he has been relieved from the position, according to a notification issued by the solicitor wing of the law ministry today. Contacted, Attorney General Barrister Md Ruhul Quddus Kazal told The Daily Star that there was an allegation against Abul Hassan of taking Tk 3.2 crore from a party, assuring them of lifting a stay order from a case, misusing his power. “I have spoken to that assistant attorney general (Abul Hassan) exclusively about the allegation. His explanation did not seem satisfactory to me,” he said, without giving details of the case and the concerned party. Advocate Abul Hassan could not be reached for his comments despite repeated attempts over phone.

title: Enforced disappearance: Complaint filed at ICT against Hasina, ex-DGFI chief Mamun
body: A complaint has been filed with the prosecution of the International Crimes Tribunal, accusing ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina and several others, including former director general of the Directorate General of Forces Intelligence (DGFI) Lt Gen (retd) Sheikh Mamun Khaled, over an alleged enforced disappearance during the Awami League’s tenure. Former Jubo Dal leader Moshiur Rahman Mamun submitted the complaint to Chief Prosecutor Aminul Islam at the tribunal this noon. According to Mamun, he was picked up on February 23, 2015, while heading to Thailand, from Dhaka airport. He alleged that plainclothes policemen detained him and kept him blindfolded and handcuffed for around six months. Mamun said he was later handed over to the Detective Branch on August 23 the same year. A few days later, he was produced before a court and placed on remand twice. He then spent nearly two years in Dhaka Central Jail before being released on bail granted by the High Court. Earlier, the International Crimes Tribunal-2 asked jail authorities to produce Sheikh Mamun Khaled before the court on April 7(tomorrow).

title: Keraniganj factory fire: Accused placed on 3-day remand
body: A Dhaka court today placed Iman Ullah Prokash, a local influential figure, on a three-day remand in a case filed over the fire at a gas lighter manufacturing factory in Keraniganj Kadamtali intersection that killed at least six people on Saturday. Dhaka Judicial Magistrate Md Tanvir Ahmed passed the order after police produced him before the court with a 10-day remand prayer, a court staffer said. Police yesterday filed a murder case with South Keraniganj Police Station, naming factory owner Akram Ullah Akaram, his son Ahnaf Akif Akram, and Iman Ullah as accused. Following the filing of the case, police arrested Iman Ullah from the Kadamtali area of Keraniganj yesterday.

title: 65-year-old man sent to jail in Gazipur for 'hurting religious sentiment'
body: A 65-year-old man was sent to jail by a Gazipur court this morning over allegations of hurting religious sentiment. The accused, Shahin Bhuiyan, was arrested from the Bormi Pathantek area under Sreepur upazila last night. A case has been filed by one Mohammad Shobir on charges of hurting religious sentiments, Inspector (Operations) of Sreepur Police Station Sanjoy Saha confirmed to The Daily Star said adding that he was produced before the court around 11:00am today. Tension spread across the Pathantek area yesterday evening after the allegations surfaced. Local residents, along with worshippers from nearby mosques, staged protest marches at different points, including Janatar Mor in Bormi Bazar, he added. Quoting locals the inspector said, during the protests, Shahin locked himself inside his house. Police, with assistance from local people, broke open the gate after nearly an hour and took him into custody. Mufti Mahdi Hasan, president of the Bormi union unit of Islami Andolon Bangladesh, alleged that Shahin had been making derogatory remarks about Islam for a long time. He claimed that recent evidence brought the matter to light, prompting public protests. Quoting the complainant, the inspector said the accused had allegedly made remarks such as calling madrasas “business institutions” and claiming that militancy is fostered there.

title: Tonu murder: IO seeks court permission for DNA cross-match
body: The investigation officer of Sohagi Jahan Tonu murder case today sought the court’s permission to conduct a cross-match of DNA profiles of three former army persons. PBI Inspector Tarikul Islam filed the appeal before Senior Judicial Magistrate Mominul Haque of Cumilla Sadar Cognisance Court-1. The three army personnel, all currently retired, are Sergeant Zahid, Warrant Officer Hafizur Rahman, and Soldier Jahangir Alam. Earlier, Cumilla Court Inspector Mamunur Rashid said the court had directed the investigation officer to appear before it on April 6 (today) and provide an update on the progress of the case. He added that further details would be disclosed after the court issues its order. Meanwhile, Tonu’s father, Yar Ahmed, appeared before the court and demanded justice for his daughter from the prime minister. According to court sources, 79 hearing dates have passed so far, while six investigation officers from four different agencies have handled the case. However, no arrests have been made, and no trial has begun even after a decade. Sohagi Jahan Tonu, a history student at Cumilla Victoria Government College and a theatre activist, was raped and murdered inside Cumilla Cantonment on March 20, 2016. The exact cause of death could not be determined despite two autopsies conducted at Cumilla Medical College Hospital. Officials from the Criminal Investigation Department confirmed through DNA tests that she had been raped before being murdered. Spermatozoa from three unidentified individuals were found on her clothes, but investigators have not been able to match them with any suspects. The killing triggered nationwide protests, with students and citizens taking to the streets demanding justice. At the time, authorities assured action, but the case remains unresolved.

title: Decomposed body of missing day labourer found in Noakhali
body: Police have recovered the decomposed and partially burned body of a 32-year-old man in Noakhali’s Chatkhil upazila last night. The body of Md Khokon was found around 10:00pm in a thicket, adjacent to “Montrir Pol” (Minister’s Bridge) area at Daulatpur village of Chatkhil Municipality, Chatkhil Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Abdul Monnaf confirmed this morning. According to the case statement, Khokon, a day labourer, went missing on Thursday night after receiving a call from an unknown number. His family filed a missing person report (GD No. 190) at Chatkhil Police Station on Saturday after failing to locate him. Following the discovery of the body, Khokon’s father filed a murder case at the police station today. Three suspects have since been arrested, the OC said. “The body appears to have been burned. However, nothing can be confirmed until the forensic report is received,” OC Abdul Monnaf said. “We are treating this as a murder. The body has been sent to the morgue of the 250-bed Noakhali General Hospital for a post-mortem examination.” The OC added that the investigation is ongoing.

title: 5 sentenced to death for killing college student in Ctg in 2007
body: A Chattogram court on Sunday sentenced five people to death and acquitted ten others for killing college student Fasiur Rahman Shaon in the port city in 2007. The five are members of a gang known as the “Gamcha Party” that operates in the city. They are Bellal Hossain, Zakir Hossain, Shahid Raja, Al Amin Gazi, and Md Sohel. Sixth Additional Chattogram Metropolitan Sessions Judge Muhammad Ali Akkas handed down the verdict after the court found them guilty beyond reasonable doubt based on witness testimonies and evidence. The court’s bench assistant, Md Rakib Uddin, told journalists that the court also fined each convict Tk 25,000. The court acquitted 10 other accused as the charges brought against them could not be proven during the trial. Among the convicted, Al Amin Gazi and Md Sohel are absconding, and arrest warrants have been issued against them. The remaining three were present in court at the time of the verdict and have been sent to jail, he added. A total of 10 witnesses testified in the case, he said. According to case documents, police recovered the body of Shaon (27) from the Badsha Mia Road area under Kotwali Police Station on July 24, 2007. He fell victim to the “Gamcha Party” while on his way to a coaching centre at the GEC intersection in the city. A case was later filed in connection with the murder. Police submitted a charge sheet after completing the investigation. The trial formally began on February 23, 2011, with the framing of charges against the accused. In 2007, a gang known as the “Gamcha Party” was active in the port city. Members of the group would pose as drivers or helpers of CNG-run auto-rickshaws, rob passengers of their belongings, and then kill them by strangling them with gamcha (locally made towels). The mystery behind the murder was later uncovered following the arrest of the gang members.

title: Ctg police arrest youth accused of fraud using names of PM, home minister
body: Police have arrested a youth from Patiya upazila in Chattogram on charges of fraud and extortion using the names of the prime minister, the home minister and other top state officials. The arrestee was identified as Riyad Bin Salim of Paikpara area under Patiya municipality. Nazmul Hasan, additional deputy inspector general of Chattogram Range, disclosed the information at a press briefing held at the office of the Superintendent of Police in Chattogram this afternoon. Riyad was arrested from his home late Saturday night, he said. Police said he had long been involved in fraudulent activities and extortion by claiming close links with high-ranking government officials. Law enforcers recovered several items from his possession, including an ID card bearing his photograph labelled "CSF Chairperson's Security Force (ID No-013)," a metal detector, a walkie-talkie handset with charger, a black-handled signal light, a monitoring cell card with his photo, a walkie-talkie-like mobile phone and a button phone set. Nazmul Hasan said Riyad used to post photos on his Facebook account suggesting “close associations” with top government officials and ministers to mislead people. Police suspect the images were generated using artificial intelligence (AI). He is also accused of creating fake ID cards of the home ministry's protocol wing. Riyad took Tk 2. 15 lakh from the wife of an accused named Kamrul Hasan, promising to secure his bail while he was in jail. A case has been filed with the local police station in this connection. Police said he is facing multiple cases, including allegations of rape and narcotics offences. He defrauded several individuals by promising jobs in positions such as tax inspector, control operator and server-in-charge at Chattogram City Corporation, said police.

title: Mobile courts fine Tk 6 lakh for gas cylinder hoarding, overpricing in Gazipur
body: Mobile courts in Gazipur have fined a total of Tk 6 lakh last night for hoarding LPG cylinders and sales at prices above government-fixed rates. During the drive conducted by Gazipur Rice Research Army Camp, authorities found evidence of multiple irregularities, including the stockpiling of about 3,000 gas cylinders, at Janani Enterprise on Niyamat Road. A mobile court led by the Gazipur district administration fined it Tk 50,000. In a separate drive in Deshipara area, Khwaja Garib-e-Nawaz Steel Bitan, was found to have hoarded around 15,000 gas cylinders. The mobile court imposed a fine of Tk 4 lakh in this case. Executive Magistrate Abu Bakkar Siddique of the Gazipur district administration said such raids were being conducted to safeguard consumer rights and ensure public safety, adding that the drives would continue. On the same day, in a separate drive in Kaliganj upazila, a trader was fined Tk 1.5 lakh for stockpiling a large number of gas cylinders without a licence and for allegedly creating an artificial shortage in the market. Assistant Commissioner (Land) and Executive Magistrate Zakia Sarwar Lima said the accused, Nipu D’Costa, failed to produce a valid licence for selling gas cylinders during questioning and could not provide a satisfactory explanation for the stockpiling. He was subsequently fined Tk 1.5 lakh under Section 6(1) of the Essential Commodities Control Act, 1956.

title: Four bystanders injured as criminals open fire on rivals in Ctg’s Bakalia
body: Four bystanders, including a 12-year-old boy, were injured by pellets after a group of criminals opened fire targeting rivals in Chattogram city’s Bakalia area last night. The injured -- Md Hasan, Jasim, Ismail Mia, and Fahim, 12, -- are currently undergoing treatment at Chattogram Medical College Hospital. All the four victims have pellet injuries, CMCH doctors confirmed. Police said five individuals were detained in connection with the incident that took place around 10:00pm in Mia Khan Nagar Flour Mill area under Bakalia Police Station, Officer-in-Charge (OC) Mohammad Solaiman of Bakalia Police Station told The Daily Star. The OC said that there had been a longstanding conflict between two groups – one led by Morshed Khan and Abdus Sobhan -- over establishing supremacy. Followers of Morshed opened fire indiscriminately with shotguns, targeting followers of Abdus Sobhan when the bystanders were injured, the OC said. According to eyewitnesses and police, none of the rival group members were injured in the attack. The attackers fled the scene after opening fire. However, bystanders, including a CNG-run auto-rickshaw driver and a flour mill worker, were injured. Morshed Khan, who identifies himself as a BNP leader, is listed among 300 criminals by city police, though he holds no position in the party, police said. OC Solaiman said, “Morshed had been on the run for a long time. After the August 5 movement, he returned to Bakalia. He claims himself to be a BNP political leader…We have detained five individuals.” A case will be filed in this connection, he added

title: 18 killed, 912 injured in political violence last month: HRSS
body: A total of 18 people were killed and more than 912 injured in 113 incidents of political violence in March, according to a monthly report by the Human Rights Support Society (HRSS). Internal conflicts within the BNP accounted for 45 incidents, leaving nine dead and 501 injured. Clashes between the BNP and Jamaat resulted in five deaths and 109 injuries, while confrontations between the BNP and the Awami League led to two deaths and 156 injuries. The report also documented violence involving the National Citizen Party and other political groups. The rights body further recorded 28 incidents of post-election violence, resulting in three deaths and 109 injuries. Law enforcement activity remained high, with around 1,500 people arrested during special joint-force drives and more than 28 political cases filed, naming 303 individuals. The report also raised concerns about freedom of expression and the treatment of vulnerable groups, noting that 59 journalists faced harassment or abuse in March. It documented abuse of 273 women and girls during the month, including 72 rape victims. Of them, 16 were victims of gang rape, while five -- including three children -- were killed after being raped. The report said 176 children were subjected to abuse in March, including 64 who died and 112 who experienced physical and mental trauma. It also noted that at least 51 children died at Rajshahi Medical College Hospital last month due to treatment-related complications, ICU shortages, and measles symptoms. The report documented at least 10 attacks on religious minority communities, leaving five people injured. Three temples, one idol, and three houses were vandalised, while one incident of land grabbing targeting minority communities was reported. According to the report, one person died due to alleged torture during a police operation in March, while at least 12 prisoners died in jails across the country. Among them were two affiliated with the Awami League and its associate bodies, and 10 general inmates. In addition, at least 13 people were killed and 38 injured in 25 mob attacks across the country. In a press release issued yesterday, the rights body said these incidents were driven by various allegations, including theft, robbery, mugging, verbal altercations, dominance disputes, and claims of religious insult. One notable incident occurred on March 4 in Munshiganj’s Lauhajang upazila, where two youths -- 32-year-old Sagar and 34-year-old Sanarul -- were tied to a tree and beaten to death overnight following accusations of stealing electric wires from a community clinic. The HRSS report, which compiled data from 16 national newspapers and the organisation’s own documentation, highlights a broader trend of instability. Earlier, the group described the rise in mob violence during the interim government period as “extremely alarming,” noting 413 such incidents over 17 months that resulted in at least 259 deaths. After assuming office, Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed has repeatedly addressed the issue. On February 18, he said mob culture would not be tolerated under any circumstances. During a meeting with the French ambassador on March 29, he said the interim government had struggled to control such violence due to its own weakness, adding that such incidents had largely ceased since the elected government took office, except for isolated cases.

title: Aminul Murder: 14 years on, family waits for justice
body: Fourteen years after the brutal killing of Aminul Islam, a labour leader from Ashulia, his family continues its quest for justice, calling for a full and impartial probe to bring all those responsible to book. Aminul, 40, was abducted on the evening of April 4, 2012, by self-proclaimed labour leader Mustafizur Rahman and an unidentified burqa-clad woman. His body was found the next morning by the roadside in Ghatail, Tangail, bearing signs of torture. The autopsy confirmed it was a murder, sparking outrage both at home and abroad. Aminul’s elder brother Rafiqul Islam filed a murder case with Ghatail Police Station. The investigation passed through four officers before Fajlul Kabir, assistant superintendent of police at the Criminal Investigation Department, submitted a charge sheet in 2013, naming only Mustafizur. Mustafizur reportedly worked as a source for intelligence agencies. In 2018, a Tangail court sentenced him to death, but he had already gone into hiding. The family and activists of the Bangladesh Centre for Workers Solidarity (BCWS), where Aminul was an organiser, rejected the verdict. They said the judgment failed to clarify Mustafizur’s role, identify accomplices, or address alleged involvement of intelligence officials. Speaking to The Daily Star yesterday, Aminul’s brother Rafiqul said the family never received justice under the Awami League government that was in power at the time. “We now want an impartial investigation to identify the real killers and masterminds, and ensure their speedy trial,” he said. Kalpona Akter, a labour rights leader, told this newspaper yesterday that Aminul had previously been detained and tortured by the National Security Intelligence in 2010, leaving him in need of hospitalisation. BCWS lodged a complaint at the time, but no explanation was ever provided. The charge sheet detailed Mustafizur’s background. He was formerly employed at Queen South Textile Mills, later worked at EPZ Medical Trust Board in Dhaka as a daily-wage MLSS staffer. Though nominally a hospital staffer, his primary role was intelligence gathering in Ashulia’s garment factories, reporting unrest and strikes to DEPZ security and intelligence officials. According to the charge sheet, on April 2-3, 2012, workers at Shanta Industries Ltd engaged in “disruptive behaviour and assaults on managers”, prompting complaints against 83 workers. Mustafizur was contacted to collect advance information on worker activities. Records show he had multiple phone conversations with intelligence officers on April 4, 2012, the day Aminul was abducted and killed. Evidence indicated that Mustafizur and the unidentified woman lured Aminul from his BCWS office under the pretext of arranging a marriage, abducted him, and disposed of his body in Ghatail, added the charge sheet. Despite a Tk 100,000 reward announced by the home ministry and several operations, both suspects remain at large. Kalpona said, “There has been no proper investigation or trial in Aminul murder. Justice has not been delivered.” Rafiqul echoed that only Mustafizur has been held accountable, while others involved remain untouched. “My brother worked tirelessly for workers’ rights, ensuring unfair dismissals and unpaid wages were addressed, and representing workers’ causes in court. Yet, his murder remains unsolved,” he said.

title: Crime boss Boro Sazzad’s deputy held in Chattogram
body: Rapid Action Battalion yesterday arrested Saddam Hossain, alias “Galakata Bacha”, the second-in-command of notorious criminal Sazzad Ali, alias Boro Sazzad. Saddam, 37, of the Muktijoddha Colony in Arefin Nagar under Bayezid Bostami area in Chattogram, was apprehended in the South Salimpur area of Sitakunda upazila early yesterday. ARM Mozaffar Hossain, assistant director (media) of Rab-7, confirmed that the raid took place around 2:45am following a tip-off regarding Saddam’s whereabouts. Saddam has long been a figure of fear in Chattogram, particularly in the Jungle Salimpur and surrounding areas, according to Rab officials. They said he was the primary enforcer for Sazzad Ali’s syndicate and oversaw various criminal activities. His criminal record, reviewed via the Crime Data Management System (CDMS), reveals at least seven cases, including murder attempts and murder filed against him with Panchlaish, Chawkbazar, Double Mooring, Bayezid Bostami, Akbar Shah, and Sitakunda police stations. “He was a key associate of Sazzad Ali and effectively ran the syndicate’s operations on the ground. His presence had created a state of panic among ordinary citizens in Salimpur,” said ARM Mozaffar Hossain. Following his arrest and initial interrogation, Saddam was handed over to the Panchlaish Police Station for further legal proceedings, he added.

title: Death following C-section sparks vandalism at Dinajpur clinic
body: A woman died during a Caesarean section at a private clinic in Dinajpur’s Birganj upazila on Friday night, triggering vandalism by her relatives and locals. The authorities later sealed the clinic, while the health department has formed a three-member probe committee to investigate the incident. Quoting the victim’s family members and locals, Officer-in-Charge of Birganj Police Station Saiful Islam said Sameja Begum, 28, wife of Abdur Razzak of Saronja village under Kaharol upazila, lost consciousness as her condition deteriorated during the C-section while giving birth to a baby girl at Birganj Clinic on Khansama Road. As Sameja did not regain consciousness, she was referred to Dinajpur Zia Heart Foundation. Family members said she died on the way to Dinajpur due to excessive bleeding. They further claimed that the clinic authorities referred her to Dinajpur despite knowing about her death in an attempt to avoid public outrage. Following the incident, agitated relatives and locals vandalised the clinic around 9:30pm, confined its staff, and staged protests by lighting fires in front of the facility. Later, police brought the situation under control, said the OC. That night, Birganj upazila Assistant Commissioner (land) and Executive Magistrate Dipankar Chandra sealed the clinic. The newborn girl is currently safe. Birganj upazila Health and Family Planning Officer Dr Afroza Sultana said it could not be confirmed whether a qualified anaesthetist was present during the operation. The OC said the clinic’s owner and manager likely went into hiding as they could not be reached over the phone till yesterday morning, while the whereabouts of the attending physician also remained unknown. Efforts are underway to contact them, he added.

title: Youth beaten to death over theft suspicion
body: A young man died after reportedly being beaten by locals on suspicion of theft in Khulna early yesterday. The deceased is Didar Sardar, 30, of Kashiani upazila of Gopalganj. He had been living in a rented house in the Arongghata area of Khulna. Police recovered his body from bushes near a railway line beside Khaja Khal Road under Arongghata Police Station. Md Shahjahan Ahmed, officer-in-charge of Arongghata Police Station, told The Daily Star that locals allegedly beat Didar over accusations of theft. He was later taken to Khulna Medical College Hospital in an injured condition, where doctors declared him dead, the OC said. The OC also said that Didar had five theft cases filed against him at different police stations.

title: Dinajpur livestock officer sent to jail in rape case
body: A Dinajpur court today sent an upazila livestock officer to jail in a case filed over the rape of a woman in Hakimpur upazila. Senior Judicial Magistrate Mustansir Rahman passed the order after the accused, Shafiul Islam, was produced before the court in the evening, said Hakimpur Police Station Officer-in-Charge Jakir Hossain. The OC said Shafiul had asked the woman, a resident of Hakimpur municipality, to visit his office yesterday for a conversation. He said the two were previously acquainted. When she went to his office around 9:30am yesterday, he locked her in the room and raped her, he added. The woman filed a case with Hakimpur Police Station yesterday afternoon, following which police arrested the accused.

title: Knife held to 3-yr-old’s throat during Sylhet auto-rickshaw robbery
body: A college lecturer was robbed in Sylhet this afternoon after assailants held a knife to his three-year-old son’s throat inside a CNG-run auto-rickshaw. The victim, Ohee Alom Reza, a Bangla literature lecturer at Balaganj Government Degree College, was travelling with his son from Ambarkhana Point to the Shahi Eidgah area for a medical appointment around 2:45 pm when the incident happened, said police. Monzurul Alam, additional deputy commissioner (media) of Sylhet Metropolitan Police, said a sub-inspector from Ambarkhana outpost had already visited the scene with the victim following the incident. “Police are working to apprehend the perpetrators and swift legal action will be taken,” he added. A case is being filed with the Airport Police Station. Reza told reporters that he and his son sat at the back of the autorickshaw, which already had two passengers. “Before the vehicle took off, two more passengers boarded, one in the back, pinning us in the middle. One of them then pulled out a knife and held it to my son’s throat,” he said. He claimed that the assailants took approximately Tk 22,000 from him but did not take his mobile phone. They later dropped the pair near Shahi Eidgah.

title: Teen sent to jail over rape of minor in Dinajpur
body: A Dinajpur court today sent a 19-year-old to jail in a case filed over the rape of a minor girl in Birganj upazila. Dinajpur Senior Judicial Magistrate Md Mostansir passed the order after the accused, Shailen Chandra Roy, of Madonshako village in Birganj, was produced before the court in the afternoon, said General Register Officer (GRO) of the court Oliar Rahman. He was taken into custody early today after the victim's father filed a case with Birganj Police Station. Quoting case statement and locals, Saiful Islam, officer-in-charge of Birganj Police Station, said around 2:45pm Friday, Shailen lured the girl to his house and raped her. Later, the victim's aunt found her crying in the courtyard with visible injuries and took her home. As her condition worsened, the family took her first to Birganj Upazila Health Complex and then to Dinajpur Medical College Hospital, where she is currently receiving treatment. Local residents and youths later detained the accused from nearby Debitala Bazar and handed him over to police in the evening.

title: Boro Sazzad’s ‘second-in-command’ arrested in Ctg
body: Rapid Action Battalion (Rab) today arrested Saddam Hossain, alias "Galakata Bacha", the second-in-command of notorious top terrorist Sazzad Ali, alias Boro Sazzad. Saddam, 37, of the Muktijoddha Colony in Arefin Nagar under Bayezid Bostami area in Chattogram, was apprehended in the South Salimpur area of Sitakunda upazila early Saturday. ARM Mozaffar Hossain, assistant director (media) of Rab-7, confirmed that the raid took place around 2:45am following a tip-off regarding Saddam’s whereabouts. Saddam has long been a figure of fear in Chattogram, particularly in the Jungle Salimpur and surrounding areas. According to Rab officials, he was the primary enforcer for Sazzad Ali’s syndicate and oversaw various criminal activities. His criminal record, reviewed via the Crime Data Management System (CDMS), reveals at least seven cases, including murder attempts and murder filed against him at Panchlaish, Chawkbazar, Double Mooring, Bayezid Bostami, Akbar Shah, and Sitakunda police stations. “He was a key associate of Sazzad Ali and effectively ran the syndicate's operations on the ground. His presence had created a state of panic among ordinary citizens in Salimpur,” said ARM Mozaffar Hossain. Following his arrest and initial interrogation, Saddam was handed over to the Panchlaish Police Station for further legal proceedings, he added.

title: Youth beaten to death over theft suspicion in Khulna
body: A young man died in Khulna early today after reportedly being beaten by locals on suspicion of theft. The deceased was identified as Didar Sardar, 30, from Arakandi in Kashiani upazila of Gopalganj. He had been living in a rented house in the Arongghata area of Khulna city. Police recovered his body around 7:00am from bushes near a railway line beside Khaja Khal Road, under Arongghata Police Station. Md Shahjahan Ahmed, officer-in-charge of Arongghata Police Station, told The Daily Star that locals allegedly beat Didar over accusations of theft. He was later taken to Khulna Medical College Hospital, where doctors declared him dead, the OC added. Didar had five theft cases filed against him at different police stations, according to the police.

title: Clash over ‘supremacy’ in Faridpur enters 2nd day; cops among 28 injured
body: A clash between residents of four villages in Faridpur's Bhanga upazila, reportedly over local supremacy, continued for a second consecutive day today, leaving at least 28 people, including a police constable, injured. The violence first broke out between 6:00pm and 7:00pm yesterday before police brought the situation under control. However, around 12 hours later, the clash resumed at about 7:15am today, said Al Amin Mia, inspector (investigation) of Bhanga Police Station. During the renewed clash, shops in Mansurabad Bazar area of Hamirdi union were attacked and vandalised. Locals said residents of Mansurabad village were on one side, while people from Khapura, Majhikanda and Singaria villages were on the other. Quoting locals, the inspector said tensions over dominance had long persisted between Mansurabad and the three neighbouring villages. Hamirdi Union Parishad Chairman Md Khokon Mia said Mansurabad is larger and more densely populated than the other three villages. “The market is controlled by the three villages, while the bus stand is under Mansurabad. Minor disputes among youths often trigger clashes, which later escalate,” he said. He added that the three villages often unite against Mansurabad over issues of local dominance. “Youths get into conflicts over eve-teasing, games, or even motorcycles. These small incidents often lead to larger clashes,” he said. The chairman said the situation had gone beyond the control of local representatives. “Even law enforcers are struggling to control the situation. If we try to intervene, we risk being attacked. That is why we are staying away,” he added. Amid the tensions, a man from Khapura was allegedly assaulted when he went to Mansurabad Bazar around 5:00pm yesterday, further escalating the situation, the inspector said. As of filing this report around noon, clashes had continued for nearly five hours. Police, who arrived in two vehicles, came under attack as rival groups hurled brickbats, leaving several officers injured. Among them, Constable Md Mashiur Rahman of Bhanga Police Station is undergoing treatment at Bhanga Upazila Health Complex, said Additional Superintendent of Police (Bhanga Circle) Md Rezwan Dipu around 12:20pm. He added that the situation was later brought under control. Tansiv Zubayer, health and family planning officer of Bhanga upazila, said at least 28 injured people had sought treatment at the upazila health complex by 1:00pm. Of them, 18 were admitted, three were referred to Faridpur Medical College Hospital, and seven were given primary treatment. Witnesses said both sides took positions at different points with locally made weapons and shields. For hours, the two groups engaged in brick-throwing and chase and counter-chase despite police presence. According to eyewitness Palash Saha of Mansurabad village, members of the army, Rapid Action Battalion (Rab), Detective Branch (DB) and additional police were deployed around 12:05pm and dispersed those involved, bringing the situation under control. No tear gas shells or blank shots were used, he said. “We rushed to the spot after receiving information and tried to bring the situation under control,” said Inspector Al Amin, adding that additional forces were deployed from Faridpur.

title: One held for ‘torturing two children’ over mobile phone theft allegations
body: Police have arrested one person in connection with the alleged torture of two children in Dhala Madhyapara area of Mymensingh’s Trishal upazila on suspicion of mobile phone theft. In a special drive, police arrested the prime accused from Gazipur early today after Md Mahabul Alam alias Bulbul Islam, the father of one of the victims, filed a complaint with Trishal Police Station yesterday against five people. The arrestee, Abdullah Al Masum, 28, a fish trader is a resident of Dhala Madhyapara area. Quoting family members, locals and the complaint statement, Md Firoz Hossain, officer-in-charge (OC) of Trishal Police Station, said the two children aged between five and eight were forcibly picked up from their home by one of the accused, Mizanur Rahman Sujon, on suspicion of mobile phone theft. They were then taken to a place nearby a pond where several others joined in beating them. Later, the children were allegedly dunked into the pond water. They were also beaten and forced to drink dirty roadside water. The incident came to the attention of police after the incident triggered widespread public outrage after being widely shared on social media. After the matter came to the notice of Trishal Police, a special operation was conducted under the instructions of higher authorities, the police official said adding that the drives are ongoing to arrest the other accused. The arrestee will be produced before a Mymensingh court later in the day, said the OC.

title: 1,600 litres of illegally stored diesel seized in Moulvibazar drive
body: A mobile court seized 1,600 litres of diesel hoarded in Kamalganj upazila of Moulvibazar last night. The drive was conducted around 11:30pm in the Chitalia area under Alinagar union, according to the upazila administration. Officials said Hiron Mia, owner of Hiron Enterprise at Chitalia Bazar, had long been stockpiling fuel illegally in violation of government regulations. Acting on a tip-off, a team led by Upazila Nirbahi Officer (UNO) Md Asaduzzaman carried out a drive. During the drive, authorities recovered 1,600 litres of diesel stored in eight big drums inside the trader’s house, the UNO said. However, Hiron Mia and his son, Jewel Mia, managed to flee after sensing the presence of the mobile court and could not be detained on the spot, he added. The seized diesel will be sold among the public at fair prices in line with government directives, the UNO said. He added that Hiron Enterprise lacked valid documents for the business, and legal action is underway. The UNO also said such drives will continue in the public interest.

title: JCD leader hacked to death in Pabna
body: A Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal (JCD) leader was hacked to death by unidentified assailants in Pabna’s Ishwardi upazila on Thursday night. The victim, Imran Hossain Sohag, 26, was a member of the upazila unit of JCD, said police. He was the member secretary of a proposed committee from a faction of the unit. According to police and locals, the attack took place near a railway line in Sara Gopalpur around 11:00pm. Sohag, from Baghoil Mannabipara village in Pakshi union, was chatting with friends at a roadside tea stall when a group of assailants arrived. Following a heated argument -- believed to be rooted in a long-standing dispute -- the attackers hacked him and fled the scene. Sohag died on the spot. Contacted, Pranab Kumar, additional superintendent of police (Ishwardi circle), said police were trying to arrest the attackers.

title: Anti-hoarding drive: 1,550 litres of fuel seized, Tk 10,000 fine imposed
body: As the government continues its drives against hoarders, large quantities of fuel have been seized in two districts. In a joint operation, law enforcement and intelligence agencies seized 800 litres of fuel in Chandanaish of Chattogram on Thursday night for being transported illegally to be sold at higher prices. Chandanaish Assistant Commissioner (Land) and Executive Magistrate Jhantu Bikash Chakma led the raid in Dewanhat area. According to upazila administration sources, 600 litres of diesel and 200 litres of octane, stored in four large drums, were being transported on a trolley from Dohazari to Bailtali Yunus Market in the upazila. Md Sayeed, son of Nur Mohammad from the market area, was intercepted while transporting the fuel, upazila administration officials said. Investigators said the fuel was intended to be sold at inflated prices in the local market, bypassing official regulations. Chandanaish Upazila Nirbahi Officer (UNO) Rajib Hossain confirmed the seizure. In Noakhali, the Subarnachar upazila administration seized 750 litres of diesel that had been illegally stored in a rooftop water tank of a residence in Char Jabbar union on Thursday night. The hoarder was fined Tk 10,000 for illegal stockpiling. The operation was conducted by Executive Magistrate and Subarnachar UNO Akib Osman. Acting on a tip-off, the mobile court raided the house of Bashir Sareng and recovered the fuel, the UNO said. Meanwhile, in Barguna and Patuakhali, a prolonged shortage of diesel and petrol has left many fishing trawlers non-operational, rendering several thousand fishermen jobless. Yusuf Fakir, a trawler owner from Mohipur in Kalapara upazila of Patuakhali, said he had prepared to head to sea with his fishing vessel, FB Ma-Babar Doa, after the Eid holidays. “I spent around Tk 50,000 on preparatory work such as collecting ice and hiring fishermen. However, the trip was cancelled due to the fuel shortage,” he said. (Our respective correspondents contributed to the report.)

title: Woman, five-year-old son found dead at home
body: A woman and her five-year-old son were found dead at their home at Tilpa Para area in Dhaka’s Khilgaon yesterday afternoon, police said. The deceased were identified as Nargis, 35, and her son Mahim. Sub-Inspector Rafiqul Islam of Khilgaon Police Station said police visited their house in the afternoon after receiving information and recovered their bodies. The police station OC Shafiqul Islam said the child was found with his throat slit, while the woman’s body was found hanging from the ceiling fan. “The woman might have stabbed the child and later died by suicide. The door was found locked from inside,” said the OC, adding that her husband was not home during the incident. Members of the Crime Scene unit of the Criminal Investigation Department, along with senior officials, visited the scene. Police said they are trying to gather further details about the incident.

title: Garer Canal gasps under encroachment, pollution
body: The centuries-old Garer Canal, an integral part of the history and geography of Habiganj’s Baniachong, is now facing a severe crisis due to encroachment and pollution. This 19-kilometre-long waterway was once vital for transportation, flood control, irrigation and fisheries in the vast haor region. On the ground, illegal structures line both banks. In several stretches, parts of the waterway have allegedly been filled in to build houses and shops. Waste from nearby markets and residential areas is being dumped directly into the canal, making the water unusable and threatening aquatic biodiversity, including native fish species. Local farmer Mifta Mia said the canal’s declining navigability has worsened water management in the area. “During the rainy season, waterlogging occurs due to poor drainage. In the dry season, there is a severe shortage of irrigation water. As a result, Boro cultivation on several thousand acres is being disrupted,” he said. Resident Shahjalal Ahmed recalled a time when large boats used to ply through the canal. Now, even small boats cannot pass. According to officials, the Bangladesh Water Development Board implemented a canal restoration and excavation project in the 2022–23 fiscal year, covering 31.6 kilometres of the main canal, including its branches, at a cost of Tk 7.12 crore. The stated objective was to ensure year-round water retention and improve irrigation for agricultural land. However, within two and a half years of the project’s completion, locals claim there is little visible evidence of proper excavation. Sajedul Islam, another resident, alleged that excavation work was not carried out in accordance with the approved map. “There is no water in many parts of the channel due to unplanned excavation,” he said. Pintu Das, a local, claimed that the actual canal lies to the west of the excavated stretch. “They dug another channel instead of the original one. Unnecessary branches were excavated while the main canal was neglected,” he alleged. Contacted, Sayedur Rahman, executive engineer at the Habiganj Water Development Board, said, “The contract value was Tk 7.12 crore, and our official records state that the excavation work has been completed.” Asked about allegations of irregularities and misuse of tree-planting funds, he said he was not posted there at the time and would need to verify the details. Another BWDB official, who did not want to be named, said, “About 70 percent of the canal has been excavated, and only 54 percent of the contractor’s bill has been paid.” Bangladesh Poribesh Andolon (BAPA) Habiganj unit General Secretary Tofazzal Sohel said the Garer Canal is not just a source of water flow, it is an important part of the environment, agriculture, and biodiversity of Baniachong. He urged the government to adopt scientific and planned re-excavation of canals, ponds and other water bodies to preserve biodiversity and ensure water retention.

title: Bangladeshi woman killed in Florida
body: A Bangladeshi woman was beaten to death with a hammer at a convenience store in Fort Myers, Florida, on Thursday, triggering a police operation that ended with the suspect’s arrest later in the day. The victim, identified as Yasmin, was a Bangladeshi expatriate living in Fort Myers. According to local police and emergency service sources, the attack took place around 7:14am (local time). Personnel from the Fort Myers Fire Department and Lee County EMS responded swiftly and rescued Yasmin with severe injuries. She was declared dead later. Preliminary investigations indicate that a man with a history of mental illness entered the store armed with a hammer and attacked her. Prior to the assault, he vandalised a vehicle parked outside the premises. CCTV footage from the scene shows the suspect wearing a yellow graphic T-shirt, black shorts, yellow or orange sneakers and carrying a backpack. He is seen striking the woman’s vehicle multiple times with a hammer. When Yasmin came out of the store to confront him, the attacker approached and struck her in the head, causing her to collapse. He then hit her several more times in the head before fleeing. Police launched a large-scale search operation following the incident. As a precautionary measure, three nearby schools were placed on lockdown. Although the suspect initially managed to flee, police were able to identify him. Authorities also said he may be linked to an unsolved homicide that occurred several months ago. Yasmin was originally from Lakshmipur district. Her death has cast a shadow of grief in the Bangladeshi community in Florida.

title: Two bodies recovered in Narsingdi, Kishoreganj
body: The bodies of two young men have been recovered in two districts, report our correspondents. In Narsingdi, the body of Monsur Ali, 25, an auto-rickshaw driver from Changao village in Madhabdi upazila, was recovered from a pond yesterday morning. Family and locals said Monsur had gone missing since he left home on Thursday night. His body was later found floating in a pond in the same village. Police recovered the body and sent it to the hospital morgue for autopsy, said Kamal Hossain, officer-in-charge of Madhabdi Police Station. The cause of death could not be confirmed immediately. “My son had no known enmity with anyone. I cannot understand why he was killed... ,” said Monsur’s father, Motalib. In Kishoreganj, police recovered the decomposed body of Abir Hossain, 20, from a maize field in Angrail Haor under Nikli upazila Thursday evening. Abir, a resident of Bhatiboratia Uttar Para, had been missing since March 9, said family. A complaint was filed with the police on March 13. Locals discovered the body and informed police. Two people were arrested in this regard, said Rafiqul Islam, OC of Nikli Police Station.

title: Man beaten for protesting stalking of daughter in Lalmonirhat, two arrested
body: Police have arrested two people for allegedly assaulting a man after he protested the stalking of his madrasa-going daughter in Lalmonirhat’s Patgram upazila. The arrestees are Samiul Islam and his son Sumon Mia, 21, of Shukurertari village under Jagatber union, said Nazmul Haque, officer-in-charge (OC) of Patgram Police Station. The arrests were made during a drive at Shukurertari village on Thursday night after the victim’s father filed a case against three alleged stalkers, including Sumon, with Patgram Police Station in this regard. Two other alleged stalkers in the case remain absconding. They are Shawon Mia, 20, and Rifat Hossain, 20, both from the same village. Efforts are ongoing to arrest them, added the OC. According to the case statement, three youths -- Sumon, Shawon and Rifat -- stopped the madrasa girl on her way home at Pachavandar village and harassed her by making obscene remarks on the road on Thursday afternoon. Upon learning of the incident, the girl’s father went to the spot and protested. Enraged by this, the stalkers brutally beat him. It was also alleged that Samiul, father of the arrested stalker Sumon, was present at the scene and took part in the assault. OC Nazmul said locals rescued the seriously injured man and admitted him to Patgram Upazila Health Complex. As his condition deteriorated, he was shifted to Rangpur Medical College Hospital at night on the same day, he added.

title: Madrasa teacher sent to jail over attempted rape of class 5 student in Noakhali
body: A Noakhali court today sent a madrasa teacher to jail in a case filed over the attempted rape of a class 5 student of the madrasa in Noakhali town. The Noakhali Chief Judicial Magistrate's Court passed the order after police produced Mohammad Maruf, 25, of Hirapur village under Badalkot union of Chatkhil upazila, before the court this afternoon, said Officer-in-Charge (OC) of Sudharam Model Police Station Md Touhidul Islam. The boy, 11, is a residential student of the madrasa, said police. Police arrested the teacher from the madrasa on Thursday night after the student's father filed a case over attempted rape with the Sudharam Model Police Station. ​According to police and the case statement, Maruf is a teacher in the Hifz department of a madrasa in Noakhali municipality. ​The incident occurred in the early hours of February 23. After the students went to sleep, the accused allegedly entered the student's room and attempted to rape him. The victim informed his family about the incident when he returned home for the Eid holidays. Later, the father of the boy filed a case against the teacher, following which he was arrested and sent to jail, said the OC.

title: 16-year-old held over involvement with Neo-JMB, police say
body: The Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime (CTTC) unit of Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) has arrested a 16-year-old boy on suspicion of involvement with the banned militant outfit Neo-JMB. According to CTTC sources, the teenager was detained during a drive conducted around 2:30pm on Thursday in Sadar upazila of Habiganj, said a press release signed by Arifa Akhter Priti, assistant commissioner of the Media and Public Relations Division of DMP. The boy had a connection with the accused, including Ahsan Zahir Khan, Daniyel Islam Hasan, and Russel alias Palash alias Abu Bacher Al Faruqi, in a case filed under Anti-Terrorism Act with Sher-e-Bangla Nagar Police Station in Dhaka recently. CTTC officials said the boy was highly active online, where he allegedly shared extremist content and attempted to recruit members. He is also accused of distributing PDF manuals on bomb-making and inciting close associates to plan attacks on Shia mosques and police checkpoints. He has been produced before a court in accordance with legal provisions, the officials said.

title: Bangladeshi woman killed in hammer attack at Florida store

The victim, identified as Yasmin, was a Bangladeshi expatriate living in Fort Myers. title: Jamalpur man killed over family feud
body: A man was killed in an alleged attack by his son’s in-laws over a family dispute in Jamalpur Sadar upazila on Wednesday night. The deceased, Abdul Hakim, 50, was a resident of Jhawla Gopalpur area. According to police, Hakim’s son, Mohammad Shamim Mia, a garment worker, had been living with his wife in Mymensingh. The couple had long been at odds due to ongoing marital discord. An arbitration was held between the two sides on Wednesday, but escalated into violence. Then, Shamim’s father-in-law and relatives allegedly assaulted Hakim, leaving him critically injured. Locals rushed him to Jamalpur General Hospital, where the on-duty physician declared him dead. Following the incident, police detained six individuals, including the father-in-law, on suspicion of involvement. Officer-in-Charge of Jamalpur Sadar Police Station, Mizanur Rahman, said the body has been sent to the hospital morgue for autopsy.

title: Son, wife held 10 months after mother’s murder
body: Police on Wednesday arrested a man and his wife nearly 10 months after the throat-slit killing of his mother in Banshkhali upazila. The suspects, Md Kashem, 28, and Nargis Akter, 25, were detained in a joint drive by police and Rab-15 in Chakaria, Cox’s Bazar. The victim, Rehena Begum, 62, was killed between the night of June 5 and early June 6 last year. Police said the couple had been in hiding since then. Investigators linked the murder to a dispute over money sent by Rehena’s elder son from abroad, which Kashem allegedly misused. The couple allegedly killed her with a sharp weapon, hid evidence and fled. Rehena was declared dead at hospital.

title: DMP continues drive to clear footpaths, roads
body: The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) continued its drive for a second consecutive day yesterday to reclaim encroached footpaths and roads, expanding operations to several new areas across the capital. Joint teams of police, particularly from traffic divisions, along with mobile courts, carried out drives in Mirpur, Mohammadpur, Kazipara, Shewrapara, Uttara, Gulshan, Kalshi, Fakirapool, Dhaka Medical College Hospital, Tejgaon and other parts of the city. During the drive, makeshift shops, roadside stalls and illegal extensions of businesses were removed from footpaths and roads. In some places, authorities seized goods and dismantled temporary structures, while in others vendors were asked to vacate voluntarily. A mobile court also conducted a drive at the entrances to the outdoor and emergency units of Dhaka Medical College Hospital, clearing illegal structures from nearby footpaths and roads, witnesses said. Shop owners present at the time were allowed to take their belongings, while unattended items were confiscated and taken away in law enforcers’ pickup vans. Law enforcers said stricter measures were enforced on the second day, following warnings issued during the first day of the drive. Field observations showed that many footpaths remained comparatively clear, as vendors began vacating occupied spaces. However, hawkers demanded compensation and rehabilitation before such drives. “We are conducting the second day of the drive from Jatrabari to Faruk Sarani, Golapbagh, Kazla, Saidabad and other areas. The drive will continue,” said Azad Rahman, deputy commissioner of the Wari Traffic Division, speaking to The Daily Star. Police also conducted a drive to evict illegal shops and structures on Ring Road in Shyamoli. Similar drives are planned for Tajmahal Road and Salimullah Road in Mohammadpur. Several private cars and motorcycles parked illegally along roadsides were fined. Some shopkeepers were also fined for placing goods on roads and footpaths. Many individuals were penalised for obstructing pedestrian movement, while others were warned. Special Metropolitan Magistrate Md Al-Faisal of the DMP led the operation. He said instructions had been issued to keep footpaths clear, but many failed to comply. “As a result, some were warned while others were fined,” he said. Responding to a question about the return of illegal structures, he said regular monitoring would be arranged in consultation with higher authorities. Around 50 police personnel, including Assistant Police Commissioner Md Aslam Sagar of the Mohammadpur Traffic Zone, took part in the drive. Earlier, on March 23, the DMP announced a coordinated citywide drive starting April 1, asking traders to remove their belongings in advance. The public notice warned that violators could face fines, imprisonment and confiscation of goods placed on footpaths and roads. Meanwhile, Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) Administrator Md Shafiqul Islam Khan reiterated that footpaths and roads must remain free from encroachment and that no business activities will be allowed there. However, he said alternative arrangements would be made for small and floating traders. He made the remarks at a meeting with hawkers and small traders at Mukul Fouz Field in Mirpur, held to discuss clearing footpaths from Mirpur-10 to Mirpur-1. “We will arrange alternative places for your businesses. You must keep in mind that no business will be allowed on footpaths or roads,” he said. He added that those who previously facilitated such businesses would no longer be able to do so. Acknowledging the traders’ concerns, he said the city corporation would take a humane approach. At the meeting, representatives of hawkers demanded designated relocation spaces, sufficient time for relocation, and suitable locations for business. They said many had been operating for years, and sudden eviction would cause hardship. They called for proper arrangements before relocation. In response, the administrator said a workable solution would be developed through discussions, and detailed talks would be held with a five-member team. He also said tokens would be issued by the city corporation to prevent extortion. “Once you receive the token, do not pay anyone asking for money -- inform us, and we will stand by you,” he said.

title: Crackdown on fuel hoarding intensifies
body: The government has continued drives against illegal fuel hoarding amid shortages that have disrupted daily life and livelihoods in several districts. Law enforcers and mobile courts seized more than 44,900 litres of diesel and petrol in separate operations in Patuakhali and Sirajganj yesterday, while fishermen in Kurigram reported acute difficulties in accessing fuel. In Chattogram, the port authority, navy and coastguards seized around 37,000 litres of stored diesel from a tanker named OT Korban Ali Sha at Sadarghat yesterday, said Chattogram Port Secretary Syed Rafayet Hamim. In Patuakhali, police seized 6,200 litres of fuel – 3,200 litres of diesel and 3,000 litres of petrol – from a trawler anchored near a ferry ghat on the Andharmanik river in Kalapara upazila around 9:30am. A mobile court later fined the owner of a local filling station Tk 20,000 for supplying the fuel to the trawler. Kalapara Upazila Executive Magistrate Yasin Sadiq, who led the court, confirmed the development. In Sirajganj, a mobile court seized around 1,729 litres of diesel and petrol from an unauthorised fuel shop at Sonamukhi Bazar in Kazipur upazila early yesterday. The shop owner was fined Tk 10,000 for illegal stockpiling, said Kazipur Upazila Nirbahi Officer Mostafizur Rahman, who led the drive. Despite the enforcement drives, fuel scarcity has left livelihoods at risk for many. In Kurigram, fishing boats were seen sitting idle along the Brahmaputra riverbanks as fishermen struggled to secure diesel. “It takes six to seven litres of diesel daily to go fishing in the river. Earlier, we could get diesel near the riverbank at a slightly higher price. Now we have to travel 10-12 kilometres to a pump and stand in queue for hours to get only two litres,” said Jhontu Chandra Das, a fisherman from Jorgachh Jelepara village in Chilmari upazila. [Our correspondents from Patuakhali, Jamalpur and Lalmonirhat contributed to this report.]

title: ‘He said he’d return to eat; he never did’
body: A grieving mother told a tribunal yesterday that her teenage son, who had been waiting for lunch, left their Gendaria home in Dhaka in 2011 after receiving a phone call just as she was about to serve the meal, and never returned alive. She said she waited with his meal until Asr prayers, but her son Sajal, then 17, did not return. She and her elder son later searched for him at hospitals, police stations and other places for over a week. “The police did not help us in any way,” she told the tribunal. Nine days later, on July 13, 2011, the family learned that two bodies were lying in a hospital in Gazipur. Her elder son Azad went there with a friend and identified Sajal’s body. “The next day, we brought the body and buried him at Jurain graveyard,” she said. Bhulu Begum, a 52-year-old domestic worker, was testifying before the International Crimes Tribunal-1 as the second prosecution witness in a crimes against humanity case against Maj Gen (retd) Ziaul Ahsan. She said her son had been involved in BNP politics and regularly attended rallies and meetings. “I later came to know that a senior officer of the Rapid Action Battalion [Rab] picked up Sajal and killed him in Gazipur because of his political activities,” she said, breaking down in tears. “I want justice for my son’s killing,” she said, as Ziaul sat in the dock. She told the court that on the afternoon of July 4, 2011, Sajal returned home from work and asked for food. Shortly after, his elder brother Azad also returned, and the two sat watching television. She told them the rice was ready but the curry was not. “At that moment, Sajal received a phone call. While speaking, he started to leave the house. His brother told him to eat first,” she said. She called out from the window, asking him to finish his meal before leaving. “He replied, ‘I’ll just go talk and come back. Get the food ready -- we’ll eat together.’” That was the last time she saw him alive. According to her testimony, at the time, the family lived in a rented house in Begumganj of Gendaria. Azad worked as a bus helper, while Sajal worked at a sand and brick shop. Ziaul Ahsan has been charged with three counts of crimes against humanity, filed on January 14, over alleged enforced disappearances and the killings of 104 people between 2010 and 2013. According to the first charge, acting on Ziaul’s plan and with his direct involvement, Sajal and three unidentified individuals were shot dead along the Bypass Road in Pubail, Gazipur, on July 11, 2011. The second charge alleges that between 2010 and 2013, at least 50 people, including former BDR member Nazrul Islam Mallik and Alkas Mallik, were shot dead at the confluence of the Baleshwar River in Barguna, and their bodies were dumped into the river on Ziaul’s instructions. The third charge states that during the same period, Ziaul was involved in the killing of another 50 people in Barguna and the Sundarbans in Bagerhat, among other places, under the guise of anti-forest bandit operations. Ziaul’s defence counsel sought his discharge, claiming he was innocent. After the testimony, his lawyer, Aminul Ghani Titto, cross-examined the witness. The tribunal set April 8 for the next hearing.

title: Man hacked to death in Pabna’s Ishwardi
body: A man was hacked to death by unidentified miscreants in Ishwardi upazila of Pabna last night. The deceased was identified as Imran Hossain Sohag, 26, from Baghoil Mannabipara village in Pakshi union. He was said to be a member of the Ishwardi upazila unit of Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal (JCD) and the proposed member secretary of a faction within the committee. However, his political identity could not be verified at the time of filing this report. According to police and local sources, the incident occurred around 11:00pm near a railway line in Sara Gopalpur. Sohag was chatting with friends at a roadside tea stall when a group of assailants arrived. Following a heated argument -- believed to be rooted in a long-standing dispute -- the attackers hacked him with sharp weapons and fled the scene. Locals reported hearing several gunshots during the attack. Sohag died on the spot. Confirming the incident, Pranab Kumar, additional superintendent of police (Ishwardi Circle), said police were dispatched to the scene immediately after receiving the information. The police officer could not provide further details at the time of filing this report. Law enforcement agencies are working to maintain order as tensions remain high in the area.

title: Indian citizen detained with diamonds worth Tk 6.61 crore in Jashore: BGB
body: An Indian national was held today in Jashore with diamonds and foreign currencies worth around Tk 6.62 crore, BGB said. Lt Col Golam Mohammad Saiful Alam Khan, commanding officer of BGB-49 Battalion, confirmed the incident. A drive was carried out on the Jashore-Jhikargacha highway near Notunhat Bazar, according to a press release issued by the commanding officer. Acting on a tip-off, a BGB patrol team intercepted and detained the suspect, identified in the press release as Sujauddin, 52, son of Abubakkar from Tamil Nadu, India, and recovered approximately 155.76 grams of diamonds from his possession. During preliminary questioning, the detainee said he had collected the diamonds from Dhaka and was attempting to smuggle them into India through the Benapole border. He planned to hand them over to an unidentified person in Kolkata. BGB officials also said the suspect had travelled multiple times over the past month between Thailand, Malaysia, Bangladesh and India. Representatives from Diamond World in Jashore examined the seized stones in the presence of police and initially confirmed them to be diamonds. The estimated value of the diamonds is Tk 6,61,39,590. In addition, BGB recovered Tk 5,530 in Bangladeshi currency, Rs 5,880 (worth Tk 7,761), US$ 550 (worth Tk 67,650), and 200 Thai baht (worth Tk 750), along with a mobile phone and a digital watch. The total estimated seizure value stands at Tk 6,62,65,161. Legal proceedings are underway in connection with the incident. The detainee has been handed over to Jashore Kotwali Model Police Station, while the seized diamonds and foreign currencies are in the process of being deposited with the Jashore Treasury.

title: 2 arrested over rape of schoolgirl
body: Police yesterday arrested two people in a case filed over the abduction and rape of a class 10 student in Jhenaidah’s Maheshpur and recording a video of the act on March 26. The arrestees are Md Hazrat Ali, 22, of Bagdiar Aair village in Maheshpur upazila, and Aser Ali alias Raju, 18, of Samanta Charatla Para of the upazila, said Maheshpur Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Mehedi Hasan. The victim’s aunt filed a case on Monday night with the police station accusing four people of rape and recording the video. Besides Hazrat Ali, the other accused are Md Shaon, 20, Nayan, 23, and Amin, 21-- from Bagdiar Aair village. Police said they are conducting drives to arrest the other accused. According to the case statement, around 8:00pm of March 26, the 15-year-old victim went to meet her friend Raju near her house. At that time, Ali and Shaon beat the victim’s friend and took her to a nearby field where Nayan and Amin were waiting. There, Ali, Shaon and Nayan raped her while Amin recorded the video on his phone. They threatened to publish the video online and kill her if she told anyone about the incident and left her there, according to the case statement. When the victim returned home the next day, she informed her paternal aunt about the matter. When the aunt confronted the accused, they threatened her too with murder, added the case details. After consulting with family and locals, the aunt filed a case with Maheshpur Police Station on Tuesday night. Talking to The Daily Star yesterday, the victim said she was scared after the incident and did not want anyone to find out. Although she revealed the matter to her aunt, she forbade her from telling anyone else. Later, the matter came to light after the suspects showed the video to several people and then they decided to go for legal action. Maheshpur Police Station OC Mehedi Hasan told The Daily Star, “The victim has been sent to a local hospital for medical check-up. One accused in the case, along with another suspect in the investigation, have been arrested. The operation to arrest the other accused is underway.” He said Hazrat Ali, who was arrested early yesterday, was sent to jail after he was produced before a court. Meanwhile, Raju, arrested in the afternoon, will be produced before a magistrate tomorrow.
