BBC Media Action Bangladesh Country Director Al Mamun said the protocol was developed to help ensure a safer working environment in the media and would serve as an accountability framework for media owners and management. “We often say the media reflects society. But when women’s participation remains limited, we must question whether the environment is supportive,” he said. He added that it would only work if institutions adopted a zero-tolerance approach. Conducting the programme, Women Journalists’ Network Bangladesh Coordinator Angur Nahar Monty said incidents of sexual harassment often remain hidden due to shame and social stigma. “We feel uncomfortable and unsafe talking about it, but silence only allows the problem to continue,” she said, adding that the protocol was developed through consultations with women and men in media and should be seen as a starting point for ensuring safer workplaces for all. Suliman Niloy, who prepared the protocol, said organisations already have legal obligations under the High Court directive and existing labour laws. “This protocol does not create new obligations. It helps institutions carry out existing responsibilities in a structured way,” he said. Shararat Islam, communications analyst at UN Women Bangladesh, said, “We have policies, but enforcement is weak. This protocol can help bridge that gap if organisations take it seriously.” Implementation by major media houses could encourage others to follow, she added. Academics, senior journalists, development partners, and media professionals also spoke at the programme.

title: Three shown arrested in Star office attack case
body: Three suspects were yesterday shown arrested in a case filed over vandalism, arson, and looting at The Daily Star’s office in Dhaka. They are: Saidur Rahman, 25; Abul Kashem, 33; and Azahar Ali, 33. All three had earlier been arrested in a separate case over vandalism and arson at the Prothom Alo office in the capital. Excluding the three, 11 others had been arrested in the case by December 26 last year, and all are currently in jail, according to court records. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid yesterday showed Saidur, Kashem and Azahar arrested in the case following an application submitted by Sub-Inspector Jahirul Islam of the Detective Branch of Dhaka Metropolitan Police, said a court staffer. The DB also sought a seven-day remand to interrogate them, and the court set March 30 for hearing on the remand prayer, he added. Jahirul said three accused were found involved in the attack on the The Daily Star office during the investigation, so he applied to the court to show them arrested in the case. Earlier, the court fixed April 26 for submission of the probe report after the DB failed to submit the report despite two previous deadlines. The Daily Star filed the case on December 22 last year with Tejgaon Police Station against 350–400 unidentified people under the Penal Code, the Anti-Terrorism Act, the Special Powers Act, and the Cyber Security Ordinance, over the attack on its head office in Dhaka’s Tejgaon area. According to the case statement, the estimated loss from the attack stands at around Tk 40 crore, subject to revision following further assessment.

title: ACC seeks to show Masud arrested in graft case
body: The Anti-Corruption Commission yesterday filed an application with a Dhaka court to show Lt Gen (retd) Masud Uddin Chowdhury, a prominent figure in the army‑backed caretaker government, arrested in a case filed over alleged embezzlement of Tk 119.32 crore through sending workers to Malaysia. Judge (in charge) Mohammad Moin Uddin Chowdhury of the Metropolitan Senior Special Judge’s Court set April 9 for hearing on the application filed by ACC Assistant Director Abul Kalam Azad, said bench assistant Riaz Hossain. On March 11, the ACC lodged a case against Masud under the Penal Code, the Money Laundering Prevention Act and the Prevention of Corruption Act. According to the ACC documents, Masud, former MP of Feni-3 and proprietor of 5M International Ltd, along with others, formed a manpower business syndicate through collusion, unlawfully monopolised the market, and extorted money by collecting amounts exceeding the government-fixed fees from workers for sending them to Malaysia. “By using his influence as a lawmaker, Masud engaged in criminal conspiracy and performed activities beyond contractual terms, receiving illegal gratification as a public servant. He allegedly embezzled a total of Tk 119.32 crore by collecting additional fees from 7,124,” said the application. On Tuesday, Masud was arrested from his residence at Dhaka’s Baridhara DOHS by a team of detectives in connection with a case filed over human trafficking and forgery of documents filed with Paltan Model Police Station. He was later placed on a five‑day remand after being produced before the court with the remand prayer. Masud previously served as general officer commanding of 9 Infantry Division in Savar during the state of emergency declared on January 11, 2007. Later, he was appointed chief coordinator of the National Coordination Committee on Serious Crimes and Corruption, promoted to lieutenant general, and posted to the National Defence College on June 2, 2008. He was transferred to the foreign ministry and appointed to the Bangladesh High Commission in Canberra on June 8, 2008.

title: 11 detained with 3,000 litres of petrol in Jamalpur
body: Eleven people were detained along with 3,000 litres of petrol while allegedly transporting it for black market sale in Jamalpur Sadar upazila early today, said police. “The incident took place around midnight in the Kalibari Bazar area under Kendua union,” said Jamalpur Sadar Police Station Officer-in-Charge Md Mizanur Rahman. “A total of 3,000 litres of petrol, contained in 15 drums, were seized from a pickup van, a locally made engine-run vehicle, a battery-run van, and an autorickshaw. Legal action is under process in this regard,” he added. The detainees are Hakim Mia, 40, of Telipara in Melandah upazila; Phul Mia, 38, of Katapur Bazar in Sariakandi, Bogura; Hafizur Rahman, 40, of Deuliyabari in Sadar upazila; Md Shah Jamal, 50, of Chanpur in Madarganj upazila; Md Maruf Hossain, 24, of Indrabari in Melandah; Md Juglu Mia, 44, of Char Jamira in Sarishabari; Md Jahurul Islam, 45, of the same area; and Md Sabuj Mia, 40, of Sengua in Sarishabari, among others. Police and locals said suspicion arose after several vehicles carrying drums of fuel were noticed late at night. The vehicles were intercepted and, upon searching them, a large quantity of petrol was found. The drivers and others present were then detained.

title: Gatekeepers’ negligence caused Cumilla train-bus crash: Rab
body: Rapid Action Battalion (Rab) today said negligence by railway gatekeepers led to the deadly collision between a bus and a train at a level crossing in Cumilla’s Paduar Bazar, which left 12 people dead and 25 others injured. According to Rab’s preliminary findings, the crossing gate was not lowered in time, leading to the accident. Both gatekeepers, Md Helal and Mehedi Hasan, assigned to the crossing were absent at the time of the accident and fled the scene afterwards, Lt Commander Md Naim Ul Haque, deputy commander of Rab-11, said at a press briefing at the Rab Media Centre in Dhaka. Members of Rab-11 arrested Md Helal, 41, from the Shankuchail area of Burichang upazila in Cumilla around 7:20pm yesterday. He is the prime accused in the case filed over the incident, the Rab official said. The crash occurred on March 22 when a bus of ‘Mamun Special’, travelling from Jashore to Lakshmipur, collided with a train while crossing the tracks beneath the Paduar Bazar Bishwaroad flyover in Cumilla Sadar South. A relative of one of the deceased later filed the case with Laksam Railway Police Station, naming both gatekeepers as accused. Rab officials said the arrestee will be handed over to the railway police station, while efforts are underway to arrest the other suspect.

title: JCD activist stabbed to death in Cox’s Bazar
body: An activist of Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal (JCD), Khorshed Alam, was killed in a knief attack in Cox’s Bazar town last night. The incident took place around 10:30pm at Kabita Chattar in the town, according to police and witnesses. Officer-in-Charge of Cox’s Bazar Sadar Model Police Station, Chhomiuddin, said law enforcers were working to identify and arrest those involved. “Witnesses and people close to the victim are being questioned. A woman who was with him is in police custody,” he said. According to police and witnesses, a group of unidentified attackers assaulted Khorshed. He suffered serious injuries after being stabbed multiple times. His friend Shah Alam and others rescued and took him to Cox’s Bazar Sadar Hospital, where the on-duty doctor declared him dead. Hospital sources said an initial examination found stab wounds on his abdomen and legs. Khorshed Alam hailed from the Isulor Ghona area under Cox’s Bazar Sadar upazila and was involved in student politics in the town. He was also known locally as a “July warrior”. Fahim-Uz-Zaman, former general secretary of Cox’s Bazar JCD, confirmed that the deceased was a JCD activist. He added that Khorshed would have received a post once a new committee was formed later. Police have taken Tarin, who was accompanying the victim during the incident, into custody for questioning. Before being taken into custody, Tarin told journalists that while they were near Kabita Chattar sea beach, a group of miscreants surrounded them and demanded valuables from Khorshed. At one stage, the attackers accused him of assaulting someone named Arif and then stabbed him several times.

title: Savar ‘serial killer’ Samrat dies at DMCH
body: Moshiur Rahman Khan Samrat -- widely known as “Psycho Samrat” -- who is accused of a series of brutal killings in Savar, has died. He was declared dead around 7:30am on Monday at Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH). Confirming the matter, Savar Model Police Station Inspector (Operations) Md Helal Uddin said the prison authorities informed them that Samrat, who had been at Dhaka Central Jail in Keraniganj, suddenly experienced severe chest pain early Monday. He was taken to DMCH, where doctors declared him dead in the morning. According to police, Samrat was allegedly involved in at least seven killings between 2025 and 2026 in Savar. Investigators found that he used an abandoned community centre in the Savar municipality area as a “death trap”. CCTV footage showing him carrying victims’ bodies on his shoulders later emerged as crucial evidence in the investigation, police said. Law enforcement agencies arrested him in January 2026. Five cases were filed against him with Savar Model Police Station. Police also said they obtained confessional statements and other evidence, including CCTV footage, in connection with the cases.

title: Three raped in three districts
body: At least three persons, including a minor, were raped in Moulvibazar, Habiganj, and Narayanganj districts since March 20. A Moulvibazar court yesterday sent a man to jail after he was arrested in a case filed over rape of a four-year-old girl in Moulvibazar’s Kamalganj. The accused, Raju Gar, 23, was arrested and produced before the court which sent him to jail, said Md Abdul Awal, officer-in-charge of Kamalganj Police Station. The incident occurred on March 20 when Raju took the child to his house in a tea garden of the upazila and raped her. After she went home, family members took her to a local hospital as her condition deteriorated. As the matter came to light, the doctors informed police. Police later arrested Raju after the victim’s father filed a case with Kamalganj Police Station on March 22. The victim is currently undergoing treatment at a local hospital. In Habiganj, a court sent a man to jail after he was produced before it in a case filed over the rape of a 24-year-old woman in a tea garden near Satchari National Park in Madhabpur on Monday. The victim was visiting Madhabpur from Brahmanbaria with two friends during Eid. While she was strolling through a secluded area, two men abducted and raped her. They also stole her gold jewellery. She filed a case with Madhabpur Police Station on Monday night. Later, police arrested Jasim Mia, 35, from Teliapara area and recovered the jewellery yesterday morning and produced him before a Habiganj court which sent him to jail in the afternoon, said Madhabpur OC Md Sohel Rana. Police are trying to arrest the other accused, he added. In Nararyanganj, police arrested two men for allegedly raping a woman after holding her husband and child hostage at knifepoint in Rupganj. The arrestees -- Afzal Khan, 30, and Abbas, 30, -- are from Tarabo municipality, said Shobzel Hossain, officer-in-charge of Rupganj Police Station, at a press briefing yesterday. The incident took place around 4:30am on Monday when the accused allegedly broke into the victim’s house, held the husband and their three-year-old child hostage at knifepoint and raped the woman. They also took away her mobile phone, police said. Police later conducted a drive and arrested the two on Monday night. The stolen phone was also recovered. The victim filed a case with Rupganj Police Station under the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act, accusing Afzal Khan and an unidentified accomplice. OC Shobzel said they are continuing the investigation.

title: Dragged from home, beaten to death
body: An admin of an anti-narcotics Facebook page was forcibly taken out of his home and then beaten to death yesterday afternoon in Brahmanbaria’s Kasba upazila. Deen Islam, 30, was the son of Shafiqul Islam, of Shimrail village under Mehari union, said police. He ran the page and a YouTube channel called, “Talash Crime Dristi”, where he regularly published video reports on drug trafficking, drug trade, and drug abuse. According to police and locals, a group of 20 to 30 people forcibly took him from his house around noon and severely beat him. They later left him in the Gangerkut area under Bhangora Police Station in Cumilla across the Buri river. Kasba Police Station Officer-in-Charge Naznin Sultana said police rescued him in the afternoon and took him to Kasba Upazila Health Complex where doctors declared him dead. Family members alleged that an influential group was behind the killing over his reports exposing drug-related activities. They accused former UP member Abdul Awal and his associates. Abdul Awal denied the allegations, claiming that he was being framed.

title: 2 dead in clashes over polls rivalry
body: Two people, including the imam of a mosque, were killed and over 100 others injured in violent clashes in Nasirnagar upazila of Brahmanbaria district yesterday. Inspector Abul Kalam Azad, in charge of Chatalpar Investigation Centre, confirmed the deaths and described the situation as “still volatile.” He added that police have yet to reach the site in full force and stop the violence, as it is in a very remote area. Brahmanbaria Superintendent of Police Shah Md Abdur Rauf said during the clash, Habibullah, the local mosque’s imam, was injured by a spear and later died at the Ashtagram Upazila Health Complex in nearby Kishoreganj district. Akhtar Mia, the other deceased, was also injured by a spear and died on the spot; his body remains at the scene. The clashes are linked to a longstanding dispute between supporters of BNP leader and newly elected MP Rahim Talukdar and those of defeated independent candidate Kamruzzaman Mamun. While Akhtar Mia was a supporter of Rahim Talukdar, Habibullah was a supporter of Kamruzzaman Mamun. According to police and locals, the violence erupted last morning in Goalnagar union, a remote area surrounded by rivers, when rival groups attacked each other with local weapons, including spears, bows and arrows. Witnesses said the clash appeared premeditated, with both sides reportedly mobilising supporters from nearby villages. The fighting quickly spread across multiple villages in the union. Doctors at Nasirnagar Upazila Health Complex said dozens of injured people were brought in for treatment. “Two people came in critical condition and were referred to Dhaka for advanced care,” said resident medical officer Shafiqul Islam. Many others received treatment locally for injuries caused by spears, sticks, and other weapons. According to SP Shah Md Abdur Rauf, the clashes trace back to the national elections on February 12. On that day, a BNP supporter, Ziaur Rahman, was detained over alleged irregularities at a polling centre, and was later sentenced to 10 days jail by a mobile court. His associates suspected that Shishu Mia, a supporter of independent candidate Kamruzzaman Mamun, was behind his arrest, triggering tension between two local groups. Mediation by local leaders and MP Rahim Talukdar temporarily eased the situation, but underlying grievances persisted. The police official said additional forces have been deployed to restore order. Earlier, on March 17, at least 25 people were injured in similar clashes over the same dispute.

title: Human trafficking case: Ex-Lt Gen Masud on 5-day remand
body: Masud Uddin Chowdhury, a retired lieutenant general widely talked-about for his role during the army-backed caretaker rule in 2007-08, was placed on a five-day remand yesterday in a case filed over human trafficking and forgery. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid granted the remand, rejecting defence lawyer Morshed Hossain Shahin’s plea for bail and cancellation of the remand. Masud, also a former Jatiya Party lawmaker from Feni-3, was sued on September 3, 2024, by a proprietor of recruitment agency Afia Overseas, under the Prevention & Suppression of Human Trafficking Act with Paltan Police Station. The case accuses 103 individuals, including former Awami League government minister Imran Ahmad. Of the accused, 40 are unnamed. After the police’s Detective Branch arrested Masud from Baridhara DOHS early yesterday, the law enforcers said the former general was accused in at least 11 cases, including five in Dhaka city and six in Feni district. Courts issued arrest warrants against him in at least three of these cases, said Shafiqul Islam, additional commissioner (DB) of Dhaka Metropolitan Police. At a press conference at the DMP media centre, Shafiqul said they initially arrested him in the human trafficking case, where he is the third accused. The suspect was hiding within the country and several attempts to arrest him had failed beforehand. In Dhaka, he faces five cases with Paltan, Banani, Kotwali, Mirpur, and Hatirjheel police stations on charges including murder, attempted murder, human trafficking, and money laundering. Replying to a query on the allegations regarding alleged illegal wealth of Masud, the DB officer said the Anti-Corruption Commission and the Criminal Investigation Department were investigating multiple complaints against him on these allegations. Masud was general officer commanding (GOC) of 9 Infantry Division at Savar when a state of emergency was declared across the country on January 11, 2007. The same year, he was made chief coordinator of the National Coordination Committee on Serious Crimes and Corruption and shortly afterwards promoted to the position of lieutenant general. On June 2, 2008, he was appointed to the National Defence College, and in less than a week, he was assigned to the Bangladesh High Commission in Canberra. The coordination committee, led by military officers, detained and interrogated prominent politicians and business figures, bringing corruption charges against them. Many of them alleged that they were tortured in custody. Masud became an MP from Feni-3 in 2018, and then again in the January 2024 election boycotted by the BNP and many other parties. Rivals from the then ruling Awami League fought their own party candidates in the election, who were widely called dummy candidates. Regarding allegations of torturing political leaders during the army-backed caretaker government, DB’s Shafiqul said the law enforcers were focusing on specific cases which are under investigation. However, he emphasised that no offender will be spared and urged victims to seek legal recourse if they have been affected. Masud was escorted to a packed courtroom of the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate’s Court amid tight security. When he was being taken back to the court lockup after the hearing, a group chanted slogans against him. Some of them were seen throwing eggs towards him. During the hearing, Dhaka Metropolitan Public Prosecutor Omar Faruq Faruqi alleged that Masud had tried to kill BNP leader Tarique Rahman, currently the prime minister, through torture. He accused Masud of introducing harassment, torture and crippling of political leaders, and the “Minus-Two Formula” -- an alleged conspiracy to drive out then BNP chairperson Khaleda Zia and Awami League President Sheikh Hasina from politics. Masud, in cahoots with one side, led a “blueprint to destroy and eliminate Khaleda and her family”, Faruqi said. The prosecutor also alleged that Masud and his accomplices collected, embezzled and laundered abroad thousands of crores of taka by promising pardon to those who would confess to their crimes. “After the 1/11 changeover, there was hardly any businessman in Bangladesh whom they did not detain and extort money from. And Masud was the mastermind behind all this,” Faruqi further said. Defence counsel Morshed told the court that the allegations against Masud were “fabricated”. He also pleaded Masud’s bail on the grounds of his age, which he claimed was 80, and different diseases.

title: Facebook page admin beaten to death in Brahmanbaria after reports on drug crimes
body: An admin of a local Facebook page in Brahmanbaria’s Kasba upazila was beaten to death this afternoon after being forcibly taken from his home, reportedly for publishing reports on drug-related crimes. The deceased, Deen Islam, 30, was the son of Shafiqul Islam, of Shimrail village under Mehari union of the upazila, said police. He operated a Facebook page and a YouTube channel called, “Talash Crime Dristi”, where he regularly published video reports on drug trafficking, drug trade, and drug abuse in the border areas of Kasba. According to police and locals, a group of 20 to 30 people forcibly took him from his house around noon and severely beat him. They later left him in the Gangerkut area under Bhangora Police Station in Cumilla district after crossing the Buri river. Kasba Police Station Officer-in-Charge Naznin Sultana said on information, Kasba police, with the help of Siddhirganj police outpost under Bhangora Police Station, rescued him in the afternoon and took him to Kasba Upazila Health Complex, where doctors declared him dead. Family members alleged that an influential group was behind the killing over his reports exposing drug-related activities. They accused former UP member Abdul Awal and his associates of involvement. However, Abdul Awal denied the allegations, claiming that he was being falsely implicated “as part of a conspiracy”. OC Naznin said the incident might have stemmed from a local dispute. The body has been sent to Brahmanbaria General Hospital morgue for autopsy.

title: ‘Masud tortured the man who is now PM,’ public prosecutor tells court
body: Dhaka Metropolitan Public Prosecutor Omar Faruq Faruqi told the Dhaka CMM Court today that the person Lt Gen (retd) Masud Uddin Chowdhury had "tortured and tried to kill" is now the prime minister. “Masud led the entire operation -- harassing political leaders, torturing and crippling them, and implementing the ‘Minus Two’ formula,” he said. Faruqi made these remarks during a five-day remand hearing in a case over human trafficking and forgery of documents filed with Paltan Model Police Station. Amid tight security, Masud was escorted to a packed courtroom of the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate’s (CMM) Court of Dhaka today. As he was being escorted back to the CMM Court lockup after the hearing, a group of people shouted slogans against him. Some of them even threw eggs at him. During the hearing, the public prosecutor said, “We saw this man (Masud) during the 1/11 (caretaker government) period... Under his leadership, thousands of crores of taka were collected. He also led a task force -- which meant abducting people, torturing them, and extorting money. He was the head of this operation.” “During 1/11, there was hardly any businessman in Bangladesh who was not detained and extorted from. Masud was the mastermind,” he further said. Defence lawyer Morshed Hossain Shahin sought bail and cancellation of the remand. “The final report was already submitted in this case once before. Now it is being reinvestigated. The allegations against him are fabricated,” the defence lawyer told the court. After hearing both sides, Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid granted a five-day remand for Masud. Masud was arrested earlier today from his home at Dhaka's Baridhara DOHS by a team of detectives. He previously served as general officer commanding (GOC) of 9 Infantry Division in Savar during the state of emergency declared on January 11, 2007. Later, he was appointed chief coordinator of the National Coordination Committee on Serious Crimes and Corruption, promoted to lieutenant general, and posted to the National Defence College on June 2, 2008. He was transferred to the foreign ministry and appointed to the Bangladesh High Commission in Canberra on June 8, 2008.

title: Man sent to jail over rape of 4-year-old girl in Moulvibazar
body: A Moulvibazar court sent a 23-year-old man to jail after he was arrested in a case filed over the rape of a four-year-old girl in Moulvibazar's Kamalganj yesterday. The accused, Raju Gar, 23, was arrested and produced before a court which sent him to jail yesterday, said Kamalganj Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Md Abdul Awal. Police said the incident took place on Friday night (March 20) in a tea garden of the upazila. The victim's father filed a case with Kamalganj Police Station on Sunday (March 22). Citing case statement, the OC said on Friday night, Raju lured the child to his house with chocolate and raped her. After she went home, the victim's family took her to Moulvibazar Sadar Hospital when her condition deteriorated. The matter came to light at the hospital and the doctors informed police. Police later arrested Raju based on a case filed by the victim's father. The victim is currently undergoing treatment at Moulvibazar Sadar Hospital.

title: 1 arrested over rape of woman visiting Habiganj tea garden
body: A 24-year-old woman from Brahmanbaria was allegedly raped by two individuals while visiting a tea garden in Habiganj district's Madhabpur yesterday. Police arrested one suspect, Jasim Mia, 35, this morning and produced him before a Habiganj court which sent him to jail in the afternoon, said Madhabpur Police Station Officer-in-Charge Md Sohel Rana. Police said the young woman was visiting Madhabpur from Brahmanbaria with two of her friends during Eid. While visiting the tea garden near Satchari National Park, she was strolling through a secluded area when two men abducted and raped her, and stole her gold jewellery. In an operation, police arrested Jasim from Teliapara area and recovered the jewellery. The OC said, upon receiving the news, police reached the spot and rescued the woman. The woman filed a case against the two men with Madhabpur Police Station that very night, he added. Police are trying to arrest the other accused, he said.

title: DB seeks five-day remand for Lt Gen (retd) Masud Uddin Chowdhury
body: Detectives want a five-day remand of Lt Gen (retd) Masud Uddin Chowdhury, a prominent figure in the army-backed caretaker government, to interrogate him in a case filed with Paltan Police Station. “So far we came to know that he was accused in at least 11 cases including five in Dhaka city and six in Feni district,” Shafiqul Islam, chief of the Detective Branch (DB) of Dhaka Metropolitan Police, said at a press briefing at DMP media centre. Of the cases, he was wanted in at least three cases in Feni which are in under trial, Shafiqul Islam said. The DB official said they initially arrested him in a case filed with Paltan Police Station under The Prevention & Suppression of Human Trafficking Act. “We will produce him before a Dhaka court and seek five-day remand for him,” he said. A team of detectives arrested him from his house at Baridhara DOHS early today. Masud was general officer commanding (GOC) of 9 Infantry Division at Savar when a state of emergency was declared across the country on January 11, 2007. He was made chief coordinator of the National Coordination Committee on Serious Crimes and Corruption and was shortly promoted to the position of lieutenant general and appointed to National Defence College on June 2, 2008. In less than a week, he was placed in the foreign ministry and was appointed to the Bangladesh High Commission in Canberra on June 8, 2008.

title: Lt Gen (retd) Masud Uddin Chowdhury arrested
body: Detectives have arrested Lt Gen (retd) Masud Uddin Chowdhury, a prominent figure during the army-backed caretaker government, from the Baridhara DOHS area early today. Shafiqul Islam, chief of the Detective Branch (DB) of Dhaka Metropolitan Police, confirmed the arrest to The Daily Star this morning. “He was accused in at least four cases and we arrested him from his house at Baridhara DOHS,” he said. Masud was general officer commanding (GOC) of 9 Infantry Division at Savar when a state of emergency was declared across the country on January 11, 2007. He was made chief coordinator of the National Coordination Committee on Serious Crimes and Corruption and was shortly promoted to the position of lieutenant general and appointed to National Defence College on June 2, 2008. In less than a week, he was placed in the foreign ministry and was appointed to the Bangladesh High Commission in Canberra on June 8, 2008.

title: Unidentified woman run over by vehicle in Dhaka’s Shahjadpur
body: An unidentified woman, approximately 50 years old, died in a road accident in the Gulshan Shahjadpur area of the capital. The incident occurred early today around 4:15am on the main road of Gulshan Shahjadpur, said police. Anindya Talukdar, Sub-Inspector (SI) of the Gulshan Police Station, said the woman was run over by an unknown vehicle on Shahjadpur main road early in the morning. However, it was not known what type of vehicle was responsible for the accident. The body has been sent to Dhaka Medical College morgue for autopsy, he said. The SI also mentioned that she was wearing a red printed saree. Despite efforts by the CID Crime Scene Unit fingerprinting, her identity could not be determined as of yet.

title: Youth stabbed to death in Rajshahi
body: A young man was stabbed to death in Rajshahi's Mohanpur upazila yesterday afternoon, reportedly following a dispute stemming from previous enmity. The victim, Md Sabbir, 21, from Berabari area in Mohanpur ran a vegetable and grocery shop. He was attacked around 4:00pm at Berabari Dighir Mor in the upazila, said Sub-inspector (SI) Modasser Hossain Khan of Mohanpur Police Station. He was taken to Rajshahi Medical College Hospital (RMCH) after the attack, where he died around 7:00pm while undergoing treatment, the police official said. His body has been kept at the hospital morgue, and an autopsy will be conducted today. SI Modasser said police have so far identified three people as being involved in the incident. They reportedly had prior enmity with the victim, which led to the stabbing. A case is being prepared in connection with the incident, he added, noting that no one has been detained yet. Efforts are underway to arrest the accused. After the autopsy, the body will be handed over to the victim's family.

title: Appellate Division sees surge in case disposal
body: In a rare development, the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court has sharply increased its rate of case disposal over the past two months, following a series of initiatives by Chief Justice Zubayer Rahman Chowdhury. According to a recent Supreme Court statement, the bench led by Justice Zubayer disposed of 4,429 cases in just 33 working days between January 5 and February 26. Of these, 2,270 cases were settled in 18 working days from January 5 to 29, while another 2,159 were resolved in 15 working days from February 1 to 26. The figures mark a significant acceleration compared to previous periods. Between July 1 and September 30 last year, only 2,257 cases were disposed of, while 4,672 new cases were filed. As of September 30, a staggering 39,417 cases remained pending before the apex court. In the preceding quarter, from April to June, 2,072 cases were settled against 4,093 filings, leaving 37,002 pending. Officials, speaking on condition of anonymity, said the chief justice has placed swift disposal of long‑pending matters at the centre of his judicial agenda since assuming office as the 26th chief justice on January 5. His approach emphasises tighter scheduling, improved bench coordination, enhanced monitoring of adjournments, and prioritisation of older cases. They described the surge as the product of a conscious administrative strategy rather than routine fluctuation, reflecting a shift toward time‑bound judicial management and efficiency. Although the latest statement did not specify how many new cases were filed during January-February or provide an updated tally of pending matters, officials said the higher judiciary is shifting from delays to a more results‑focused approach. Contacted, Supreme Court Spokesman Md Mazharul Haque told The Daily Star, "The chief justice’s proactive approach to addressing the case backlog through strategic case management and effective administrative coordination has yielded an unprecedented surge in disposals. This achievement is a clear testament to his unwavering commitment to ensuring effective and efficient justice for the citizens of the country."

title: BNP leader shot and hacked in Chattogram's Rangunia
body: A BNP leader was critically injured after assailants opened fire and hacked him at his house in Rangunia upazila of Chattogram last night. The injured, Md Osman, is the general secretary of Sarafbhata union BNP and a resident of ward 2 of the union, police said. His mother, Achia Begum, 70, also suffered bullet wounds while trying to save her son during the attack. Officer‑in‑Charge Md Helal Uddin Ahmed of South Rangunia Police Station said the attackers stormed the house around 8:00pm and fired indiscriminately. They also hacked Osman, leaving him seriously injured in the hand and abdomen. “As his mother rushed forward to protect him, she was shot in both legs,” the OC said, adding that Osman’s father was also injured during the incident. Locals rescued the family and took them to Rangunia Upazila Health Complex. Osman received primary treatment before being shifted to Evercare Hospital in Chattogram in critical condition, the OC added. Police visited the spot soon after the incident. Preliminary findings suggest the attack may have stemmed from internal conflict within the party, the OC said. Police confirmed that Osman is a follower of BNP lawmaker from Chattogram‑7 constituency Hummam Quader Chowdhury.

title: Mob kills man on suspicion of theft in Jashore
body: A man was killed in a mob beating on suspicion of theft in Chougachha upazila of Jashore today. The deceased is Alamgir Hossain, 40, of Ber Gobindapur village in Chougachha upazila. Sub-Inspector of Chougachha Police Station Abhijit Roy said some locals found him walking near the Mashila Laxmanpur BGB camp in the upazila around 4:30am today. Later, they caught and beat him on suspicion of theft, leaving him critically injured. He was first taken to Chougachha Upazila Health Complex and later referred to Jashore General Hospital, where he died under treatment around noon, said the police official. SI Abhijit Roy said that no case has been filed yet and no arrests have been made in connection with the incident.

title: Man beaten to death in Ctg’s Sitakunda, one held
body: A 30-year-old man was beaten to death after being called out of his home in Chattogram’s Sitakunda upazila last night. The deceased, Md Raju, was of Madambibirhat village under Bhatiari union. He was a father of two, police said. Police have detained a suspect, Ali Azam, in connection with the killing, said Sitakunda Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Md Mohinul Islam. The incident occurred around 9:00pm in Madambibirhat area. According to local sources, an altercation broke out between two groups over cutting of a tree shortly before iftar yesterday. Azam, a relative of Raju, took a side in the altercation. When Raju intervened and asked Azam to stop quarreling, a heated argument ensued between the two. Last night, Azam and his four sons asked Raju to come out of his house and began assaulting him, said the OC, quoting locals. Witnesses reported that Raju was struck repeatedly with bricks, leaving him dead on the spot, added the OC. The victim’s sister, Tahmina Akhtar, said she called 999, after which police recovered the body and detained Azam. The OC said the body has been sent to Chattogram Medical College morgue for an autopsy. “We have detained Azam for questioning, and the process of filing a case is currently underway,” he added.

title: Class 10 student stabbed to death in Moghbazar, 2 held
body: A Class 10 student was stabbed to death in Dhaka’s Moghbazar Madhubagh area last night. The victim is Rabby, 17, a resident of Chairman Goli in the area, said Sub-Inspector Ibrahim Khalil of Hatirjheel Police Station. The incident took place around 8:00pm at the playground of a madrasa in Madhubagh. His friends took him to Dhaka Medical College Hospital where doctors declared Rabby dead around 9:00pm. Quoting his friends, police said the incident took place likely over a love triangle. He said Rabby was walking with a girl near the madrasa field in the evening when Fahim, her boyfriend, and several others confronted him. During the altercation, Fahim stabbed Rabby in the abdomen, leaving him critically injured. Law enforcers detained Fahim and another youth shortly after the incident. The body has been kept at the hospital morgue for autopsy. An investigation is underway, the officer said.

title: Coast Guard tightens Eid river security
body: Bangladesh Coast Guard has tightened security on major river routes and launch terminals during the Eid-ul-Fitr holidays. In a press release issued on Friday afternoon, Coast Guard Media Officer Lt Commander Sabbir Alam Sujan said the force had reinforced patrols and surveillance at key river ports and ferry points as Eid travel gathers pace. Its members remain on duty to ensure passenger safety even as millions travel home for the festivities, said the release. The release further said the Coast Guard has continued round-the-clock operations in coastal and riverine areas since its inception, and that the Eid holidays are no exception. As part of the special arrangement, patrols have been strengthened at Sadarghat launch terminal in Dhaka, Chandpur launch terminal, Barishal launch terminal, Ilisha in Bhola, Nolchira in Hatiya, and launch and ferry terminals in Khulna-Mongla and different parts of Chattogram, according to the release. The Coast Guard also said additional personnel had been deployed at important river terminals, while intelligence surveillance was increased to prevent suspicious activities. The force said it remains alert to prevent theft, robbery, extortion, and acts of sabotage during the holiday rush. The statement also referred to a recent (March 17) rescue operation in Haimchar of Chandpur, where Coast Guard members rescued 104 passengers from a launch hit by a storm in bad weather and moved them to safety. It described the operation as an example of the force’s humanitarian and professional role. The Coast Guard said its security measures would continue after Eid as well to ensure the safe return of passengers to their workplaces.

title: Teen's decomposed body recovered from Karnaphuli river in Ctg
body: Police recovered the body of an 18-year-old boy from a sand-carrying dredger in Karnaphuli river near the Shah Amanat Bridge area in Chattogram today. The deceased was identified as Shahriar Fahad, son of Syed Musa Badsha of Baralia Para area of Baralia union in Chattogram’s Satkania. Fahad worked as a salesperson at a clothing store in Teribazar of the port city. Md Mizanur Rahman, officer-in-charge (OC) of Sadarghat River Police Station, said they rushed to the spot around 11:30am after receiving a call from the national emergency service, 999. The youth's identity was confirmed through a passport found in his pocket. Police suspect that the incident took place several days ago, and the body eventually drifted and got stuck in the dredger. The body was sent to the Chattogram Medical College Hospital morgue for an autopsy, he said. Speaking to The Daily Star, Fahad’s paternal uncle, Syed Nur, said that Fahad last spoke with his mother on March 14. Since then, the family had had no contact with him. “The body has decomposed significantly. We demand a proper investigation into this incident,” he said. The OC added that an investigation is currently underway, and further details will be clarified following the autopsy.

title: Rickshaw puller’s body found in Pabna
body: Police recovered the body of a rickshaw puller from a paddy field in Pabna’s Bera upazila today. The man's throat was slit. The police identified him as Md Fazlul Haque, 50, of Hatigara village in Bera upazila. Quoting family members, Md Lalmur Rahman, inspector (investigation) of Bera Police Station, said Fazlul went out with his rickshaw on Thursday afternoon but did not return. Locals spotted the body in a paddy field in Boroshila village of the same upazila this morning and informed the police. Later, law enforcers recovered the body and sent it to Pabna General Hospital morgue for autopsy. Mentioning that the motive remains unclear, the inspector said that the rickshaw was not looted and was found at the crime scene. Police are currently investigating the incident to ascertain the cause of murder, he added.

title: Tonu murder: 78 court hearing dates, no arrests in 10 years
body: Today marks 10 years since the rape and murder of Sohagi Jahan Tonu , yet her family continues to await justice, with little visible progress in the case. Although much has changed in the surrounding environment over the past decade, Tonu’s mother, Anwara Begum, remains steadfast in her demand for justice. Senior Judicial Magistrate Mominul Haque of Cumilla Sadar Court (Cognisance Court-1) has ordered the investigation officer to appear in person on the next date and submit a progress report. The Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) has been probing the case since September 2020, following a decision by Police Headquarters. PBI Inspector Tarikul Islam, the current investigation officer, told The Daily Star that he would appear in court as ordered. “As the court has ordered me to present a progress report, I will be present on the date,” he said. When asked about updates in the case, he said details would be presented before the magistrate. The next hearing is scheduled for April 6 this year, said Mohammad Mamunur Rashid, court inspector of Cumilla District and Sessions Court. According to court sources, 78 dates have already passed, while six investigation officers from four different agencies have handled the case. However, law enforcement agencies have failed to make a single arrest, and no trial has taken place even after ten years. Sohagi Jahan Tonu, a student of the history department at Cumilla Victoria Government College and a theatre activist, was raped and murdered inside Cumilla Cantonment on March 20, 2016. The cause of death could not be determined despite two autopsies conducted at Cumilla Medical College Hospital. Officials from the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) confirmed through DNA tests that Tonu had been raped before being murdered. Spermatozoa from three unidentified individuals were found on her clothes, but investigators have not been able to match them with any suspects. The incident sparked protests across the country, with students taking to the streets alongside outraged citizens. At the time, the government and relevant authorities assured justice, but those assurances ultimately proved ineffective in resolving the case. Anwara Begum told The Daily Star that she has had no contact with any PBI investigation officer in the past two years. “I don’t know who is investigating the case,” she said. With a new government in place, Anwara Begum expressed hope that justice would finally be delivered. Tonu’s father, Yaar Hossain, expressed frustration over the prolonged delay in justice. “I have suffered a brain stroke and undergone spine surgery. Day by day, I am getting weaker. Earlier, the army chief assured me that justice would be ensured. CID official Abul Kahar Akhand also assured me. But the rays of hope have faded,” he said.

title: Woman dies after falling from rickshaw during snatching attempt in Uttara
body: A woman was killed after falling from a rickshaw when a mugger attempted to snatch her bag near Uttara South Metro Rail Station in Dhaka today. The victim was identified as Mukta Akter, 21, wife of Limon Hossain of Dakshinkhan. The incident occurred around 9:30am. Her relatives took her to the emergency department of Dhaka Medical College Hospital in critical condition, where doctors declared her dead around 2:00pm, DMCH sources said. Speaking to reporters at the hospital, Limon said they live in the Faidabad area of Dakshinkhan. He works at a garment factory, and Mukta was a housewife. He said that in the morning, his wife was going to a market in Pallabi on a battery-run rickshaw for Eid shopping. He came to know when the rickshaw reached under Uttara South Metro Station, someone from a private car stretched out a hand and forcefully pulled her bag. This caused Mukta to fall on the road and sustain serious injuries. Pedestrians first took her to Uttara Modern Hospital. After being informed, Limon went there and found his wife in a critical condition. Due to delays in treatment, she was later taken to Tongi Ahsanullah Medical College Hospital, then referred to Pangu Hospital (NITOR), and eventually taken to DMCH, where doctors declared her dead. Limon said Mukta’s village home is in Sonapara village under Barguna Sadar upazila. They got married two years ago. Inspector Md Faruk, in-charge of the DMCH police camp, said the woman was brought to the hospital around noon, where doctors declared her dead. She had injuries on her head and forehead. The body has been kept at the morgue for autopsy. Turag Police Station is investigating the incident, he added.

title: Content creator murder at Shaheed Minar linked to personal dispute: Police
body: The murder of content creator Rakibul Islam at Dhaka's Central Shaheed Minar appears to have stemmed from a dispute involving a woman known to the victim, police said. The attack was planned and carried out by hired assailants brought in from Khulna. One of the prime suspects, identified as shooter Alamin, remains on the run, Ramna Division Deputy Commissioner Masud Alam told a press briefing at the DMP media centre today. Rakibul, a second-year student at Shaikh Burhanuddin Post Graduate College, arrived at the Shaheed Minar around 8:30pm on March 15. After he parked his motorbike, he was attacked by a group of five to six men armed with firearms and sharp weapons. He was taken to Dhaka Medical College Hospital in a critical condition, where he was later pronounced dead. Police have so far arrested five individuals -- Shihab, Rafin, Joy, Sagar and Salahuddin alias Saka -- from Khulna, Patuakhali and Gopalganj in connection with the killing, while at least seven others remain at large, the DC said. Two of the arrestees have given confessional statements before magistrates, two others are on remand, while Salahuddin was arrested last night and is being interrogated. DC Masud said Rakibul, though married, allegedly maintained relationships with several women. One of them is Jannat, also known as Moon, with whom he made TikTok videos. According to police, Jannat’s husband Sajid, a suspected drug dealer from Khulna, had longstanding tensions with Rakibul and had been threatening him for weeks. “From what we learned, Sajid held a grudge. It appears the group from Khulna planned the attack. They hired people and sent them to kill Rakib,” Masud said. Replying to a query, the DC said four of the arrestees directly took part in the killing. Shihab, Joy and Rafin allegedly hacked Rakibul with machetes and knives, while Sagar was present at the scene but did not participate in the hacking. He added that the coordination, supply of weapons and overall planning were handled by Salahuddin. Police recovered a pistol believed to have been used in the murder, along with three sharp weapons. The firearm will be sent for forensic testing, the DC said. Investigators said the assailants were recruited from different parts of Khulna, while another suspect managed hotel bookings and backup arrangements.“This group is dangerous. They are involved with contract killing and operate across several districts. But everyone linked to the murder has been identified,” DC Masud said, adding the group would take contracts for Tk10,000.

title: Gun attack on family in Khulna leaves 4 injured
body: Armed assailants stormed into a house in a residential area of Khulna early today and opened fire on four members of a family, leaving two of them critically injured. The victims were identified as Kazi Anisur Rahman, his wife Ranjua Begum, their son Raisul Islam and their younger son Rashidul’s wife, Fahima. Among them, Ranjua Begum and Fahima were first taken to from Khulna Medical College Hospital where they were referred to Dhaka for better treatment. The incident occurred around 6:30am in Khadijabagh Krishnanagar Tikrabad area under Labanchara Police Station. The critically injured were sent to Dhaka from Khulna Medical College Hospital for better treatment. “A group of assailants entered the family’s home and opened fire. Hearing gunshots, neighbours rushed to the scene and took the injured to Khulna Medical College Hospital,” Labanchara Police Station Officer-in-Charge Mohammad Tuhinuzzaman told The Daily Star. “The attack stemmed from a dispute over a woman-related matter. Five to six people were involved in the attack, and police have launched operations in multiple locations to arrest all of them,” he added. Since bullets could not be removed from the chest of Ranjua and the leg of Fahima, both were referred to Dhaka, the police official further said. Citing local sources, the OC said Rashidul had been imprisoned about three years ago in a drug-related case. During his time in jail, he became acquainted with a man named Imran, who was also serving a sentence in a drug case. Following their acquaintance, Rashidul reportedly began visiting Imran’s household regularly. During these visits, Rashidul developed a close relationship with Imran’s wife, Fahima. About six to seven months ago, when Imran was sent back to jail in another case, Rashidul married Fahima. Upon learning of this after his release, Imran became enraged and allegedly plotted revenge, police said.

title: Constable critically injured in Bagerhat attack as fugitive snatched from police
body: A police constable was critically injured after being hacked by an assailant while attempting to arrest a fugitive in Bagerhat's Kachua upazila this afternoon. The attacker managed to snatch the suspect from police custody during the chaos. The fugitive, Nadim Sheikh, 33, is wanted in connection with a 2024 robbery case and faces multiple allegations of extortion, land grabbing, and assault. A seven‑member police team led by Sub‑Inspector Anisur Rahman and Assistant Sub‑Inspector Imdadul Islam launched an operation at Nadim’s house to execute an arrest warrant. As officers escorted Nadim away, his younger brother Sagar Sheikh attacked with a sharp weapon, severely injuring Constable Raju Khan’s right hand, said Md Shafiqur Rahman, officer‑in‑charge of Kachua Police Station. “We successfully apprehended the suspect initially, but his brother attacked our team while we were moving him. Our operations to track down and arrest the perpetrators are ongoing,” the OC said. Constable Raju was first taken to Kachua Upazila Health Complex, but later referred to Khulna Medical College Hospital as his condition worsened. On March 20, 2022, Sub‑Inspector Rabiul Islam was critically injured in a similar attack in Bagerhat's Samankathi village. On April 1, 2025, four officers were injured in Kachua when local political activists attacked police to free a detained suspect.

title: Condition of 10-year-old Kushtia madrasa abuse victim remains critical, says doctor
body: The physical condition of the 10-year-old girl, who has been allegedly sexually abused at a madrasa in Kushtia, remains critical despite brief signs of improvement, a doctor said today. Rajshahi Medical College Hospital spokesperson Dr Sanker K Biswas said that the child was shifted from the Intensive Care Unit (ICU) to a general ward around 1:30pm today after her condition showed slight improvement. However, her health deteriorated again later in the day. She is not talking and is visibly traumatised. “As her condition worsened once more, she was taken back to the ICU around 4:00pm,” the doctor said. The girl has been undergoing treatment at the RMCH since Monday. Doctors earlier reported multiple injury marks on her body along with signs of sexual abuse. The victim’s mother said her daughter continues to suffer from severe physical and psychological distress. “She is still frightened and behaving abnormally,” she said, adding that her daughter had initially shown slight recovery before her condition declined again. Police have already arrested three individuals in connection with the incident, confirmed Rakibul Islam, investigation officer of Bheramara Police Station. The main accused, Saidul Rahman, is the head of the madrasa where the girl was a residential student. Two others were arrested for allegedly assisting in the crime. All three accused have been sent to jail following their appearance before a court on Tuesday. According to the child’s mother, she enrolled her daughter at a residential madrasa in Bheramara seven to eight months ago. Last Sunday, when she went to bring her daughter home for the Eid holiday, she found her in critical condition, with a swollen abdomen and swelling in her left leg. The child also appeared mentally distressed. Later, she was admitted to RMCH, where doctors found preliminary signs of sexual abuse. The mother also filed a case with Bheramara Police Station on Sunday night.

title: Four arrested over rape of 14-year-old girl in Mymensingh’s Bhaluka
body: Police arrested four men in Bhaluka upazila of Mymensingh for their alleged involvement in the rape of a 14-year-old girl. The arrestees -- Md Hossain, 21; Faruq Ahmed, 17; Md Arif, 17; and Md Mehdi Hasan, 20 -- all from Panchgaon village of the upazila, were produced before a Mymensingh court today, where their confessional statements were recorded under Section 164, said Additional Police Superintendent Md Abdullah Al Mamun. The victim, who lost her parents at the age of four and was raised by her stepmother, had left home two months ago following alleged mistreatment. She began working at a diagnostic centre in Mymensingh city and reportedly met a boy through Facebook six months ago. On March 14, she travelled to Bhaluka to meet him. Upon arrival at Bhaluka bus stand, a man received her and took her in a CNG-run auto-rickshaw to Panchgaon village, where she was repeatedly raped and left in critical condition. Local residents rescued her and sent her to Bhaluka Upazila Health Complex before she was referred to Mymensingh Medical College Hospital. Police Superintendent Mohammad Kamrul Hasan instructed officers to apprehend all involved in the crime.

title: 4 arrested over Shaheed Minar killing
body: Police have arrested four people in connection with the killing of a 25-year-old man in front of Dhaka’s Central Shaheed Minar. Rakibul Islam was shot and stabbed on the evening of March 15 and later died at hospital. Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Deputy Commissioner (Media) Talebur Rahman said identity and further details about the suspects would be disclosed at a press briefing later today. He added that the “mystery” surrounding the killing had been solved. According to the case statement, Rakibul, a second-year student at Shaikh Burhanuddin Post Graduate College, reached at the Shaheed Minar around 8:30pm. After parking his motorbike, he was attacked by a group of five to six men armed with firearms and sharp weapons. He was taken to Dhaka Medical College Hospital in a critical condition, where he was later pronounced dead. The following day, his father, Tarikul Islam Khokon, filed a murder case with Shahbagh Police Station against unidentified attackers.

title: Condition of Kushtia rape victim critical
body: The condition of a 10-year-girl, who was allegedly raped in a madrasa in Kushtia, is critical, said a doctor at the Rajshahi Medical College Hospital yesterday. She was initially admitted to the One-stop Crisis Centre (OCC) of RMCH on Monday morning after being rescued. “She is now in critical condition. As her physical condition is deteriorating, we have shifted her to ICU today [Tuesday] afternoon,” said the hospital’s spokesperson Dr Sanker K Biswas last night. “We have found several injury marks in her body and evidence of sexual abuse. Details will be known later after further investigation,” he added. Meanwhile, police arrested three persons in connection with the incident after the victim’s mother filed a case on Monday, said Delwar Hossain, additional superintendent of police in Kushtia. The arrestees are: Md Saidul Rahman, 50, head-teacher of Jamilatunnssa Asarsha Mohila Hafijiya Madrasa in Kuthibazar area of Kushtia’s Bheramara upazila headquarters; his wife Shamima Khatun, 42; and his colleague Risha Khatun, 20. They were produced before a court that sent them to jail yesterday, said the police officer. According to case statement, Saidul raped the girl, while the two others assisted him. In the case statement, the victim’s mother said the girl has been a residential student of the madrasa since June last year. “I went to the madrasa on Sunday morning to bring my daughter home for Eid vacation, but I found her severely ill,” she said, adding that when she asked the madrasa authorities about her daughter’s illness, they did not give proper response. The girl was first taken to a local health complex where doctors provided her primary treatment and referred her to RMCH. “Then, I took my daughter to RMCH on Monday morning,” said the mother. “My daughter has told me that she was raped by Saidul while the two other accused beat and tortured her so that she does not disclose the incident,” she also said in the case statement. Talking to The Daily Star yesterday at RMCH, the mother said, “My daughter is frightened and traumatised. In the madrasa, I found her in severe condition with a swollen abdomen and bruised left leg.” “I want justice,” she demanded. She also alleged that assocoates of the madrasa authorities tried to settle the issue with money and threats. [Our correspondents from Kushtia and Rajshahi contributed to the report.]

title: Madrasa student admitted to RMCH with signs of sexual abuse; 3 detained in Kushtia
body: A 10-year-old madrasa student was admitted to Rajshahi Medical College Hospital in critical condition yesterday morning. Doctors have found preliminary signs of sexual abuse and say the child is mentally traumatised. In connection with the incident, Bheramara police of Kushtia have detained three individuals, including the madrasa director, and sent them to jail through a court. The child's mother has filed a case with Bheramara Police Station. The child's mother, staying with her daughter at the hospital, said she had enrolled her daughter in a madrasa in Bheramara seven to eight months ago. Soon after admission, she heard that children were being abused at the institution. She said she had tried to cancel her daughter’s admission two to three months earlier. However, the madrasa director’s wife reassured her that the child would remain safe and well cared for. Last Friday evening, the child reportedly asked her mother to take her home during the Eid holidays. When the mother went to the madrasa on Sunday (March 15, 2026) to take her home, she found her daughter in critical condition, with a swollen abdomen and swelling in her left leg, apparently due to an injury. The mother then took the child to a diagnostic centre in Kushtia for an ultrasonogram, where she was informed that her daughter's condition was deteriorating. Yesterday morning, she took her daughter to Rajshahi Medical College Hospital and admitted her to the One-Stop Crisis Centre. The child was later sent to the hospital's gynaecology ward for further examinations. Sanker K Biswas, spokesperson for the hospital, told The Daily Star that the child is mentally distressed and not speaking. "Preliminary examinations have found signs of sexual abuse. Samples have already been collected for confirmation. We will be more certain once the test results are available, which have not yet been received," he said. Rakibul Islam, investigation officer of Bheramara Police Station, said a case has been filed in connection with the incident. "Three individuals, including the madrasa director, have been detained and sent to jail through the court this morning. Legal action will be taken based on the investigation," he added.

title: 21 crude bomb-like explosives found in Rajshahi
body: Members of the Rapid Action Battalion (Rab) recovered 21 crude bomb-like devices and several locally made weapons from an abandoned site in Rajshahi city early today. The drive was conducted around 12:30am in areas under Chandrima Police Station, according to a Rab-5 press release issued this morning. Acting on a tip-off, a Rab-5 team carried out the drive at a lemon orchard on the northern side of the railway field, where they found two plastic sacks abandoned at the site, the release said. Suspecting the presence of explosives, the Rab team informed its bomb disposal unit. The bomb disposal team later reached the scene and, after searching the sacks, recovered 21 crude bomb-like devices. Another white plastic sack contained several locally made weapons, including a sickle, a machete, a dagger, and a knife. Rab said locals could not provide any information about the sacks. The force primarily suspects the items were stockpiled to carry out acts of sabotage ahead of the upcoming Eid. The recovered bomb-like devices and weapons have been handed over to Chandrima Police Station for further legal action, the release added.

title: Husband sent to jail over JU student murder
body: Husband of slain Sharmin Jahan, a student of Jahangirnagar University, was sent to jail following his arrest yesterday in a case filed over the murder. Fahim Al Hasan, prime accused in the case, was arrested and produced before a court yesterday with a five-day remand prayer. The court fixed March 24 for remand hearing and ordered Fahim to be sent to jail. Sharmin’s uncle Monirul Islam filed a case with Ashulia Police Station on Sunday night, accusing Fahim and several unidentified individuals. Sharmin was rescued from her rented house in the Islamnagar area of Savar at around 4:30pm on Sunday in a bloodied and unconscious state and was taken to Enam Medical College Hospital, where doctors declared her dead. Meanwhile, JU students formed a human chain and brought out a protest march yesterday demanding justice for Sharmin, a student of the 51st batch of JU’s Public Administration Department. The human chain and protest march were organised in front of JU’s Shaheed Minar under the banner of Jahangirnagar University Research Sangsad around 2:00pm. Protesting students demanded exemplary punishment for those involved in Sharmin’s brutal murder through a fair and impartial investigation.

title: Bangladesh strengthening AI‑driven crime detection: Salahuddin
body: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed today said Bangladesh is strengthening AI-driven crime detection and enforcement as part of its zero-tolerance policy against terrorism, drugs, human trafficking, corruption and financial fraud. Speaking at a high-level session titled National Commitments/Pledges on Combating Fraud at the Global Fraud Summit 2026 in Vienna, he reiterated the government’s firm stance on national security and crime control, according to a home ministry press release. The home minister joined the session as a panelist at the Vienna International Centre this afternoon (local time). In his remarks, Salahuddin outlined Bangladesh’s specific steps to prevent money laundering and financial fraud. He identified the banking sector, non-bank financial institutions, real estate and jewellery as high-risk sectors for money laundering and pledged stronger monitoring in those areas. He said stricter oversight measures are being put in place in those sectors to ensure transparency and accountability. Referring to Bangladesh’s legal framework against financial crime, the minister said the government is committed to bringing offenders to justice through the effective enforcement of the Money Laundering Prevention Act, 2012 and the Mutual Legal Assistance Act, 2012. He also stressed the need for global legal cooperation against transnational criminal networks. Salahuddin said Bangladesh is giving special importance to enhancing the capacity of law enforcers to tackle technology-based crimes. He said the country is focussing on AI-driven crime detection and suppression to deal with emerging threats. “In the new Bangladesh, there is no place for criminals,” he said. He added that Bangladesh remains committed not only to combatting crime at home, but also to upholding its global obligations by following international conventions and protocols. Representatives from different countries attending the session praised Bangladesh’s targeted measures and its technology-based approach to tackling crime, the press release said.

title: 3 held within 24 hours over killing of youth near Shaheed Minar: Police
body: Police have detained at least three individuals in connection with the murder of 25-year-old Rakibul Islam, who was shot in front of the Central Shaheed Minar and later died at Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH) last night. Confirming the development, a high official of the Ramna Division of Dhaka Metropolitan Police told The Daily Star that police conducted drives in different parts of Dhaka following the incident and detained three individuals within 24 hours. “Primary investigation suggests that a dispute involving a woman may have led to the murder. The shooters are believed to have come from Khulna,” the official added. Last night around 8:30pm, Rakibul was shot and stabbed by unidentified assailants in front of the Central Shaheed Minar. He was rushed to DMCH in critical condition, where doctors later declared him dead. Today, the victim’s father, Tarikul Islam Khokon, filed a murder case with Shahbagh Police Station against five to six unidentified individuals. According to the case statement, Rakibul, a second-year student of Shaikh Burhanuddin Post Graduate College, arrived at the Shaheed Minar around 8:30pm last night. After he parked his motorbike, a group of five to six men attacked him with locally-made sharp weapons and firearms, leaving him critically injured.

title: Human chain demands justice for murdered JU student Sharmin
body: Students of Jahangirnagar University formed a human chain demanding justice for the murder of Sharmin Jahan, a fourth-year student of the university's Department of Public Administration. The human chain and protest march were organised in front of the university's Shaheed Minar under the banner of Jahangirnagar University Research Shongshad around 2:00pm. Students demanded exemplary punishment for those responsible through a fair and impartial investigation. They warned that if the trial is not completed quickly, they would surround the university administrative building and local police stations. Sohagi Samia, organiser of the Socialist Students' Front (JU unit), said, "Sharmin had been brutally murdered in her home. We strongly condemn and protest this murder. We demand exemplary punishment for those responsible through an impartial and fair investigation." Jucsu Vice-President Abdur Rashid Jitu said Sharmin Jahan had been deliberately killed. "Her head was crushed, and there were injury marks on her body. This human chain and protest march have been organised to ensure exemplary punishment for the culprits," he said. Sharmin Jahan was found at home in Islamnagar area around 4:30pm yesterday in a bloodied and unconscious condition and was taken to Enam Medical College Hospital, where doctors declared her dead. Sharmin's uncle, Monirul Islam, filed a case with Ashulia Police Station last night, naming Sharmin's husband Fahim Al Hasan as the main accused along with several unidentified individuals. Fahim was arrested in connection with the case and produced before the court today with a prayer for a five-day remand. The court fixed the remand hearing for March 24 and ordered that Fahim be sent to jail.

title: JU student Sharmin murder: Husband sent to jail
body: A Dhaka court today sent Fahim Al Hasan, husband of Jahangirnagar University student Sharmin Jahan, to jail in a case filed over her murder. Dhaka Senior Judicial Magistrate Ayesha Siddika passed the order, a court staffer said. The magistrate also set March 24 for hearing on a five-day remand in presence of the investigator after police produced Fahim before the court with the remand prayer, he added. The body of Sharmin, a 51st batch student of the Public Administration Department, was recovered yesterday from her home in Savar’s Islamnagar area, adjacent to the campus. Later, a murder case was filed with Ashulia Police Station in this regard. Police earlier today arrested Fahim, a student of Dhaka College, as a suspect.

title: Man shot dead in Khulna
body: A man was shot dead by unidentified assailants in Daulatpur area of Khulna city this morning, police said. The victim, Rashikul Alam Rashu, was attacked around 11:30am in front of KDA Kalpataru Market under Daulatpur Police Station. Confirming the incident, Daulatpur Police Station Officer-in-Charge Md Shofiqul Islam told The Daily Star that Rashu died after being shot by assailants. Quoting local eyewitnesses, the OC said two individuals first came to the spot and appeared to observe the surroundings. They returned shortly afterwards and opened fire on the victim. Police rushed to the scene after receiving information and recovered the body. It was later sent to Khulna Medical College Hospital for an autopsy, he added. "Law enforcers are working to identify the attackers and determine the motive behind the killing," he added. According to local sources, Rashu was previously the organising secretary of the Daulatpur thana unit of Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal and was involved in politics with Jubo Dal.

title: Uttara shopping mall vandalised over rumour of rickshaw puller’s death
body: A shopping mall in Dhaka’s Uttara was attacked and vandalised late last night over a rumour that a rickshaw-puller had been beaten to death inside the compound, police said. The attackers vandalised the ground floor of "Uttara Square" and blocked the road in front of the building. As police attempted to intervene, sporadic clashes broke out, prompting law enforcers to fire sound grenades. The situation was brought under control around 4:00am today. At least three policemen were injured in the clashes, Uttara West Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Kazi Rafiq Ahmed told The Daily Star. Police have detained 12 people for interrogation, and the process of filing a case is underway, the OC said. "We have not found any truth to the claim that a rickshaw-puller died or was injured," the OC added. According to police sources, the unrest began after an altercation and scuffle between a rickshaw-puller and a mall security guard. Following this, rickshaw or auto-rickshaw pullers along with a group of people launched the attack. Md Sakib, an employee of a clothing store on the first floor, said the mall was bustling with Eid shoppers around 11:30pm when a woman spread the rumour of the death. "The mall's central PA system announced that the front gate was broken and urged everyone to use the rear exit. Many of us managed to escape, but some were trapped as the mob moved towards the back," Sakib said, noting that ground floor shops suffered extensive damage. Following the vandalism, the shopping mall authorities decided to keep all shops closed today.

title: JU student murder: Husband shown arrested
body: The husband of a Jahangirnagar University student has been shown arrested in a case over her murder at a rented house in Ashulia. The body of Sharmin Jahan was recovered yesterday from her home in Savar’s Islamnagar area, adjacent to the campus. Sharmin’s uncle filed a murder case against Fahim Al Hasan, a student of Dhaka College, with Ashulia Police Station last night. Rubel Howlader, officer-in-charge of Ashulia Police Station, confirmed the matter to The Daily Star this morning. He said Sharmin’s bloodstained body was taken to Enam Medical College Hospital in Savar by her husband Fahim and the house owner yesterday where doctors declared her dead. Police detained Fahim as a suspect at the time, the OC said. Later that night, Sharmin’s uncle filed the murder case and Fahim was shown arrested in the case. Rubel Howlader also said Fahim will be sent to a Dhaka court today with a five-day remand prayer.

title: Two die minutes after pre-surgery injection
body: Two patients died following alleged negligence by on-duty nurses at Sher-e-Bangla Medical College Hospital in Barishal yesterday. The deceased are Helena Begum, 45, wife of the late Babul Hawlader of Sarsi village in Barishal, and Shefali Begum, 60, wife of Mannan Talukder from Dalbuganj village in Kalapara, Patuakhali. The incident occurred around 8:30am at the female ward of ENT department, on the third floor of the hospital. Relatives of the deceased said they would seek legal action over the deaths. Hospital administration sources and family members said Helena was admitted on February 23 for thyroid complications, while Shefali was admitted on March 8 for a surgery to remove a tumour in her mouth. Speaking to reporters, Helena’s relative Monir alleged that the patient was scheduled to undergo surgery at around 8:30am yesterday. However, around 7:00am, a nurse administered an injection that was meant to be used during anaesthesia. “Soon after receiving the injection, there was a sudden reaction in the patient and she died,” he said. The family of the deceased took the body home and would pursue legal action after the burial, he said. Meanwhile, Shefali’s daughter Khadija Begum said her mother was stable but fell seriously ill shortly after nurses administered several injections in the morning for surgery. “We immediately informed the nurses, but they paid no heed and took no steps to revive her. My mother died right in front of our eyes. Only after her death did the nurses respond,” she said, demanding exemplary punishment for those responsible. The allegations were brought against nurses Helen Adhikari and Molina Halder. Helen Adhikari said she did not break open the injection vial, claiming it had been opened by nurse Molina Halder. “I only administered the injections to two patients. What happened to them is very unfortunate. In my 26-year career, such an incident has never occurred. A mistake has happened,” she said. Molina Halder said the injections were administered according to the physician’s prescription before transferring the patients to the operation theatre. “When the patients’ condition deteriorated, we informed the doctor over phone and administered medicines as instructed,” she added. Nursing supervisor Khadija Begum said the deaths of two patients in the same ward were “clearly a matter of negligence”. Hospital Director Brig Gen Dr AKM Moshiul Munir said both patients were scheduled to undergo surgery yesterday. “There are certain medicines that must be administered before taking a patient to the OT, while some must be given inside the operation theatre. Anaesthetic drugs cause changes in the body that require machine support,” he said. “However, the nurses administered the drug in the ward before taking the patients to the operation theatre. As a result, the patients died shortly afterwards. This is medical negligence and a punishable offence,” he added. He said the drug, “Nor Q”, should be given during or after administering anaesthesia and must be injected slowly while the patient is on the operating table. A three-member investigation committee, headed by Assistant Prof Aminul Haque, has been formed to investigate the incident. Meanwhile, hospital authorities suspended the two nurses for negligence, added the hospital director.

title: JU student found dead in her home Husband detained
body: The body of a female student of Jahangirnagar University was recovered yesterday from her home in Savar’s Islamnagar area, adjacent to the campus. Deceased Sharmin Jahan was a student of the 51st batch of the Public Administration Department, said JU Proctor AKM Rashidul Alam. Sharmin’s husband Fahim Al Hasan told neighbours that he returned home in the afternoon and found the door locked from the outside. He said he later entered the house and found his wife lying on the floor in a bloodied state. Later, with the help of his landlord, Sharmin was taken to Enam Medical College Hospital in Savar, where doctors declared her dead, added Fahim. The body was later taken to Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College in Dhaka for an autopsy, said Rubel Howlader, officer-in-charge of Ashulia Police Station. “Initially, we suspect that she was murdered. An autopsy will be conducted, and we have already started an investigation,” added the OC. Meanwhile, police have taken Fahim into custody as the main suspect in the incident, Saidul Islam, OC of the Detective Branch (North) of Dhaka district police, told The Daily Star around 10:00pm. “We are certain that Sharmin Jahan has been killed. At this moment, her husband is our main suspect. He is being interrogated in police custody.”

title: ‘Coordinated campaign’ against unarmed civilians
body: The full verdict of International Crimes Tribunal-2 has described a coordinated collapse of police command during the July uprising, accusing law enforcers of systematic killings, destruction of evidence and obstruction of justice. The 591-page judgment, received by the prosecution yesterday, detailed how five people were killed and their bodies burned, while another victim was set on fire while still alive. The three-member tribunal led by Md Nozrul Islam Chowdhury concluded that the atrocities were part of a “coordinated and organised campaign” against unarmed civilians rather than isolated incidents.
