The victim filed a case against Suman on Sunday night with Sonagazi Model Police Station. Police immediately arrested the accused after the filing of the case, said OC Quamrul. The accused was produced before a court today, which sent him to jail, he added.

title: BTRC official attacked in Rajshahi amid allegations of extortion
body: A government official was allegedly hacked and injured over extortion demands related to the construction of his house in the Mahishbathan area of Rajshahi city yesterday evening. He is currently undergoing treatment at Rajshahi Medical College Hospital. The injured official, Israfil Haque, is an assistant director at the Dhaka office of the Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulatory Commission (BTRC). This afternoon, he came out in front of the emergency department of Rajshahi Medical College Hospital with the assistance of his relatives and briefed journalists. Israfil said he had started constructing a house about two months ago on his three-katha plot in Mahishbathan. Since the beginning of the construction work, several local individuals, including Maruf Hossain, had allegedly been demanding money from him on various pretexts, he alleged. According to him, the accused demanded large sums of money at different times. Due to security concerns, he had paid some money earlier. "I am a government official. I had taken leave to build the house. Yesterday, before iftar, a group of around 25 people attacked me with the intention to kill. I want justice," he said. Following the incident, Israfil's wife filed a case with Rajpara Police Station, naming six people, including Maruf Hossain, and accusing another 20 unidentified individuals. Attempts to contact Maruf Hossain were unsuccessful as his phone was found switched off. Officer-in-Charge of Rajpara Police Station Abdul Malek said a dispute over leaving space beside the house during construction had been ongoing for several days. "Local elders and police tried to resolve the issue. Police also went there yesterday afternoon, but the incident occurred after they left," he said, adding that the victim sustained serious injuries to the wrist of his left hand. Police have taken the case and are investigating the allegations, while efforts are underway to arrest the accused, the OC added.

title: Plaintiff failed to appear, provide evidence in case against 28 journalists: PBI
body: The Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) has submitted its findings to a Chattogram court in a case filed against 49 individuals, including Awami League leaders and 28 journalists, over allegations of attempted abduction, assault, and publishing false news during the July uprising. The report says that the plaintiff, Hasina Mamtaz, a former teacher of Mohara Sayra Khatun Quaderya Girls High School and College, did not appear before the investigation officer (IO) despite repeated notices, calls and messages over the past year, and failed to present any evidence or witnesses. Hasina had filed the case on September 4, 2024. Later, the court directed PBI to investigate and submit its findings. According to courts sources, PBI Chattogram Metro Unit Inspector Mostafizur Rahman Chowdhury submitted the report this January. The case had accused several Awami League leaders and Bangladesh Chhatra League activists of attacking the demonstrating students with lethal weapons on July 16 and 17, 2024 in Muradpur, Chattogram. The plaintiff alleged that journalists distorted facts and published fabricated reports. Among the accused are: former information minister Mohammad Ali Arafat; Hasina Mohiuddin, mother of former education minister Mohibul Hassan Chowdhury and president of the Chattogram Metro unit of Mohila Awami League (AL); AL leader Helal Akbar Chowdhury Babor; former BCL Chattogram president Nurul Azim Rony; Saibal Das Sumon; Nur Mostafa Tinu; Farid Mahmud; BCL leader Jakaria Dastagir; and journalists Suklal Das; Reaz Haidar Chowdhury; Pramal Kanti Dey Komol; Anupam Shil; Debdulal Bhoumik, secretary of Chattogram Press Club; Azhar Mahmud; Ratan Kanti Debasis; Tapan Chakrabarty; photographer Uzzal Kanti Dhar; BFUJ leader Kazi Mohsin; Ekramul Haque Bulbul; Ramen Das Gupta; Mintu Chowdhury; Uttam Sen Gupta; Kutub Uddin; Hritik Nayon; Rahul Das; Subal Barua; Runa Ansari; Rafiqul Bahar; Ayon Sharma; Aminul Islam Munna; Bishwajit Raha; Masudul Hoque; Rashed Mahmud; Hamid Ullah; Samresh Baiddya; and Shourav Bhattacharya. The case statement also alleges that journalists present at the New Market area on August 4, 2024, picked up demonstrating students and handed them over to AL leaders and activists after assaulting them. However, the investigation officer’s report emphasised that no witnesses or documentation supported these claims, and no complaint was lodged with the Bangladesh Press Council regarding false reporting. Inspector Mostafizur noted that during the protests, journalists were performing their professional duties and no evidence was found that they assaulted students or handed them over to AL activists. “We repeatedly asked the plaintiff to appear, but she did not respond. Notices were served four times, yet she neither came to the PBI office nor presented any witnesses,” he told The Daily Star. When contacted, plaintiff Hasina admitted that she had failed to appear, saying she was in Cox’s Bazar and had sent her brother to speak with police. When asked why she had neither appeared to give her testimony over the past year nor produced any witnesses, she could not provide a satisfactory explanation.

title: HC rejects bail of accused in The Daily Star office attack case
body: The High Court today rejected the bail petition of an accused in the case filed over vandalism, arson and looting at The Daily Star’s office in December 2025. The bench of Justice KM Zahid Sarwar and Justice Sheikh Abu Taher passed the order rejecting the bail petition of Julfiqar Ali Sourav, considering the gravity of the offences mentioned in the case, court sources said. "The bail petition had been rejected as it was not properly presented before the High Court bench. The bench had earlier refused to grant bail to the accused due to the seriousness of the offences," Deputy Attorney General Md Ashiquzzaman Nazrul told The Daily Star. Advocate Md Golam Kibria, who has been named as the lawyer for Julfiqar in the bail petition, told this correspondent that he did not move any petition seeking bail on behalf of any accused in the case filed over vandalising The Daily Star office. “Any junior lawyer from my chamber might have moved the petition on behalf of the accused,” he said, without mentioning the name of the junior lawyer. Following the attack, vandalism and arson at The Daily Star on the night of December 18 last year, the authorities of the English daily filed a case with Tejgaon Police Station on December 22 against 350-400 unidentified people. Section 6(1) of the Anti-Terrorism Act, Section 15(3) of the Special Powers Act, and Section 26(1) of the Cyber Security Ordinance were included in the case. According to the case statement, the attackers, carrying local weapons, sticks and flammable materials, gathered outside The Daily Star building around 12:25 am, shouting provocative slogans against the newspaper. At approximately 12:35 am, the group forcibly broke the gates to enter the premises. Inside, they physically assaulted staff, vandalised office property, looted valuables, and set fire to furniture and documents. More than 200 computers, laptops, cameras, printers and other electronic equipment were damaged or destroyed. The total estimated loss stands at about Tk 40 crore, with the figure subject to revision upon further assessment, according to the case statement.

title: Joint forces claimed control of Jungle Salimpur after drive: Ctg range DIG
body: Law enforcement agencies have claimed to establish full control in the much-discussed Jungle Salimpur area of Sitakunda in Chattogram following a joint operation. Authorities also plan to set up two security camps, one each for police and the Rapid Action Battalion (Rab), to maintain security in the vast area. Ahsan Habib Palash, deputy inspector general (DIG) of the Chattogram Range, announced the development while speaking to journalists this afternoon. However, police could not detain Md Yasin, leader of the “Yasin Bahini,” who is considered a dominant figure in the Jungle Salimpur–Ali Nagar area, as he fled during the drive, the DIG said. “Our operation is ongoing. A total of 3,200 members from Rab, police, army, BGB and APBn are participating. We have been working here since dawn,” the police official said. “Our main focus was to establish our authority in this vast area, and we have been able to do that. From today, two camps of the police and Rab will start operating here to secure the area,” he added. Law enforcement agencies launched the joint operation at dawn today with heavy equipment. The DIG said the authorities would request the divisional administration to implement previously planned development initiatives in the area. “We will request the divisional commissioner and the administration to quickly implement the plans they had taken earlier for this area. You cannot even imagine how large this area actually is,” he said. According to him, several weapons were recovered during the drive and around 15 people were detained, though the exact number could not immediately be confirmed due to poor mobile network coverage in many parts of the area. Divisional Commissioner Dr Ziauddin said the operation had restored administrative control in the locality. ““The administrative authority that needed to be set up here has now been established. The government had earlier taken development plans surrounding this area, and now we will begin implementing them,” he told journalists. When asked how security would be ensured for the camps in the hilly terrain, DIG Ahsan told The Daily Star, "If necessary, we will even deploy cannons here to ensure the security of the camps." Chattogram District Police Superintendent Nazir Ahmed said multiple teams were involved in the drive. “Ten teams are working here. Our operation is still ongoing and it will continue until the afternoon,” he told The Daily Star.

title: ASI in uniform mugged in Narayanganj, pistol snatched
body: An on-duty assistant sub-inspector (ASI) on police was mugged and his government-issued service pistol snatched in Narayanganj city early today, police said. The incident occurred around 5:45am in front of the Narayanganj City Corporation building in Nitaiganj area on Bangabandhu Road. Additional Superintendent of Police Tasmin Akter told The Daily Star that the police officer, identified as Lutfur Rahman, became separated from his team as he went to the toilet. “Three muggers intercepted him on the way and snatched the pistol he was carrying,” she added quoting Lutfur. The police official added that the ASI was in police uniform during the incident. Locals said the particular stretch of Nitaiganj is known for frequent mugging incidents despite being close to the Narayanganj City Corporation building and two government hospitals. Meanwhile, ASP Tasmin said multiple police teams are working to identify those involved and bring them under the law.

title: Joint forces launch major raid in Sitakunda’s Jungle Salimpur
body: A joint force early today launched a large-scale operation in the Jungle Salimpur area of Sitakunda upazila in Chattogram, deploying around 4,000 personnel from the army, police and Rapid Action Battalion (Rab). The operation began around 6:00am, with members of the joint forces cordoning off the entire area before conducting raids. Additional Superintendent of Police (media) of Chattogram district police, Md Rasel, confirmed the operation this morning. “Four thousand members of the joint forces are participating in the operation. Details of the operation will be disclosed later,” he said. Jungle Salimpur, a remote hilly area, came under renewed scrutiny after a Rab officer was beaten to death by a group of criminals during an operation there in January. Following the incident, the administration planned a coordinated drive to arrest armed criminals operating in the area. However, the operation was postponed as the national parliamentary election approached. Jungle Salimpur covers about 1,256 acres of hilly land under Salimpur union of Sitakunda, around five kilometres from Chattogram city. Law enforcers say the area has become a haven for criminals due to its difficult terrain and isolation. According to district administration officials, around 3,070 acres of khas land lie under five mouzas—Jungle Latifpur, Jungle Salimpur, Jungle Bhatiyari, Jalalabad and Uttar Pahartali—of which nearly 30 percent is hilly. Authorities say several armed groups have established control over parts of the area. Among them are gangs led by Md Yasin and Rokonuddin, who allegedly operate with their own armed followers. The groups have reportedly developed housing plots by cutting hills and occupying public land, later selling the plots to buyers and earning crores of taka over the past two decades. In the Alinagar and Chinnomul areas, Yasin is widely known as the “king”. On October 4, 2025, a man was beaten and hacked to death and at least 14 others were injured in a clash between two groups over supremacy and land grabbing in Jungle Salimpur. The following day, two television journalists were attacked while trying to report on the incident. Police earlier arrested Yasin from Kotwali area of Chattogram on July 19, 2022, in connection with an attack on a union parishad member. Members of his group are also accused of hill cutting, illegal possession of firearms and controlling the movement of locals in parts of the area.

title: Hadi killing: Prime accused, associate held in West Bengal
body: India’s West Bengal Police Special Task Force (STF) has arrested the prime accused and an alleged associate in the murder of Inqilab Moncho spokesperson Sharif Osman Hadi from the border area of Bongaon in the Indian state of West Bengal. The arrestees are Faisal Karim Masud, 37, a resident of Patuakhali, and Alamgir Hossain, 34, from Dhaka, according to the STF. It added that the process to repatriate the arrestees to Bangladesh has already begun. According to the STF, the arrests were made during an operation in the early yesterday (March 8) following intelligence that two Bangladeshi nationals involved in serious crimes, including murder and extortion, had fled Bangladesh and illegally entered India. “An operation was conducted, and during the intervening night of March 7–8, 2026, the two Bangladeshi nationals -- Rahul alias Faisal Karim Masud and Alamgir Hossain -- were detained from Bongaon,” the statement said. The STF said the suspects are accused of murdering Bangladeshi political activist Osman Hadi before fleeing the country. Investigators said the two allegedly entered Indian territory illegally through the Meghalaya border, travelled through several locations in India, and eventually reached Bongaon in West Bengal while attempting to return to Bangladesh. The STF said the operation was carried out based on intelligence shared by Bangladesh’s defence intelligence authorities. During preliminary interrogation, Faisal, also known as Rahul, reportedly confessed that he and Alamgir were involved in Hadi’s killing, investigators said. Indian authorities have registered a case in connection with the arrests. The suspects were produced before a court and remanded in police custody, while further investigation is underway, the statement added. The various sources said the newly appointed director general of the Directorate General of Forces Intelligence recently visited India and urged Indian authorities to arrest those involved in the Hadi murder and facilitate their return to Bangladesh. Following the request and based on specific intelligence, Indian authorities were able to detain the two suspects, the source said. Meanwhile, Inqilab Moncho last night brought out a procession at Dhaka University demanding justice for Hadi. The march was held after an iftar programme at the Teacher-Student Centre on the university campus. The procession started from TSC, through the Shahbagh intersection, and ended the rally at the Raju Sculpture. Contacted by The Daily Star, the platform’s Dhaka University convener, Fatima Tasnim Juma, said they demand the disclosure of the main perpetrator behind the killing. She added that the platform’s next programme will be announced after discussions with law enforcement agencies. Hadi, who was also an independent aspirant for the Dhaka-8 constituency, was shot in Dhaka’s Paltan area on December 12 last year. He died on December 18 while undergoing treatment in Singapore. On December 14, Inqilab Moncho Member Secretary Abdullah Al Jaber filed an attempted murder case with Paltan Model Police Station against Faisal and several unnamed individuals. The case later became a murder case after Hadi’s death. Earlier, at a press briefing on December 28, Dhaka Metropolitan Police Additional Commissioner SN Nazrul Islam said Faisal and Alamgir had crossed into India’s Meghalaya state with the help of local associates. However, India’s Meghalaya Police and the Border Security Force at the time rejected the claim. On January 6 this year, DB Inspector Faisal Ahmed, the investigation officer of the case, submitted a charge sheet against the prime accused, four of his family members, and 12 others. In the charge sheet, the IO said analysis of the accused persons’ political affiliations and Hadi’s political statements suggested the killing stemmed from political rivalry. The charge sheet also mentioned that Faisal and his associates infiltrated Hadi’s election campaign as part of a pre-planned effort to disrupt the upcoming 13th parliamentary election and create fear among voters. But on January 15, Jaber filed a petition with the court, rejecting the probe report submitted by the DB. The same day, the court directed the Criminal Investigation Department to conduct further investigation after accepting a no-confidence petition against the DB’s probe report. On February 26, a Dhaka court asked the CID to submit a probe report by March 11. Dhaka Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Jashita Islam passed the order after the CID failed to submit the report on the scheduled date, said a court sub-inspector.

title: Court orders gazette summons for Tulip, former Rajuk official in Gulshan-2 flat case
body: A special court today ordered the relevant authorities to publish a gazette asking British MP Tulip Siddiq, niece of deposed prime minister Sheikh Hasina, and Rajuk’s former assistant legal adviser Sardar Mosharraf Hossain to appear before it on March 29 in a case filed over illegally acquiring a flat in Dhaka's Gulshan‑2 by providing undue benefits to a private developer. Judge Md Sabbir Faiz of the Metropolitan Senior Special Judge’s Court in Dhaka issued the directive after receiving police reports on earlier arrest warrants against Tulip and Mosharraf, said court bench assistant Riaz Hossain. On February 18, the court issued arrest warrants against Tulip and Mosharraf after accepting the charge sheet in the case. It also set March 8 for submitting a report on the execution of the arrest warrants. On February 26, it ordered the authorities concerned to issue a red notice through Interpol for the arrest of Tulip. On April 15 last year, the anti-graft body filed the case against Tulip, Mosharraf and Rajuk’s former assistant legal adviser Shah Md Khasruzzaman for allegedly illegally acquiring the flat from Eastern Housing Limited. According to the case documents, the accused allegedly, in collusion with each other, abused their power and illegally took possession of a flat in Eastern Housing’s Gulshan-2 project without paying any money, and later got it registered. The ACC on January 13 this year filed the charge sheet against Tulip and Mosharraf.

title: 8-year-old girl found dead near neighbour’s house in Tangail
body: An eight-year-old girl was found dead in an open space near a neighbour’s house in Nagarpur upazila of Tangail this afternoon. The victim, Ayesha Akhter, was the daughter of Md Hashem Mia of Postkamari village in Mamudnagar union. According to her mother, Ayesha was last seen around 2:30 pm playing behind the house of Bahadur Miah, located near their own home. A few hours later, her paternal uncle, Fazlu Miah, discovered her body lying in an open area near Bahadur Miah’s house and informed the family. Relatives then brought the body home. The mother also noted that Ayesha had been wearing an anklet, which was missing when the body was recovered. The family suspects she may have been killed for the ornament. Md Murad Hasan, officer-in-charge of Nagarpur Police Station, said police recovered the body after being informed and sent it to the hospital morgue for autopsy. Police suspected she was strangled to death as injury marks were found on the girl’s neck. “One person has been detained for questioning. The exact motive will be confirmed after investigation,” the OC added.

title: Three sentenced to two and a half years in jail for killing 20 dogs in Dhaka
body: A Dhaka court today sentenced three men to two and a half years’ imprisonment each in a case filed over 20 dogs killed in Dhaka’s Jatrabari area. Dhaka Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Md Zakir Hossain delivered the verdict, according to court bench assistant Sayem Uddin. The convicts are Abul Khayer, Mohammad Apu, and Mohammad Manik. Only Manik was present in the courtroom during the verdict, having been brought from prison. The court sentenced each of them to two years’ simple imprisonment under Section 16(b) of the Animal Welfare Act, along with a fine of Tk 1,000, or an additional 15 days in jail in default. Under Section 16(a) of the same act, they were also sentenced to six months’ simple imprisonment and fined Tk 1,000, with another 15 days in default. The judge ordered that the sentences run concurrently. Case documents revealed that on January 23, 2021, the trio killed 20 dogs in the Lichu Bagan area of Dhalpur in Jatrabari using iron rods, pliers, and lethal injections, later packing the bodies into sacks. They were identified through video footage. Following the incident, Md Maruful Haque, field supervisor of Animal Lovers of Bangladesh, filed a case with the court on January 25, 2021. Charges were framed on May 21, 2024, and three witnesses testified during the trial.

title: Hadi murder: Prime accused Faisal Karim and associate arrested in India
body: India's West Bengal Police Special Task Force (STF) has arrested the prime accused, along with his alleged associate, in the murder of Inqilab Moncho spokesperson Sharif Osman Hadi from the border area of Bongaon in West Bengal. The arrestees were identified as Faisal Karim Masud, 37, of Patuakhali; and Alamgir Hossain, 34, of Dhaka. According to Indian media reports quoting the STF, the arrests were made on March 7 following intelligence information that two Bangladeshi nationals involved in serious crimes, including murder and extortion, had fled Bangladesh and entered India illegally. Investigators said the suspects were attempting to take shelter near the border with the intention of crossing back into Bangladesh when STF personnel conducted a raid and detained them. During preliminary interrogation, Faisal, also known as Rahul, reportedly confessed that he and Alamgir were involved in the killing of Hadi. Investigators added that the two fled Bangladesh after the murder, entering India illegally through the Meghalaya border before moving across several locations and eventually reaching Bongaon. A case has been registered in India, and the suspects were produced before a court on Saturday, where they were remanded in police custody. Officials confirmed that further investigation is underway.

title: Playing Mujib's March 7 speech: 3 former DU hall leaders sent to jail
body: A Dhaka court today sent three people, including Sheikh Tasnim Afroz Emi, former vice president of Shamsunnahar Hall Union at Dhaka University and a vice-presidential candidate in the last Ducsu election, to jail in a case filed under the Anti-Terrorism Act with Shahbagh Police Station. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Jewel Rana passed the order after police produced the accused before the court in the afternoon. The two other accused are Md Asif Ahmed Shoikot, former employment affairs secretary of the banned Chhatra League’s Shahidullah Hall unit of Dhaka University, and Abdullah Al Mamun, a leader of BCL’s Shaheed Sergeant Zahurul Haq Hall unit. According to the case statement, a group of Awami League, Jubo League and Chhatra League activists gathered around 3:00 pm yesterday at Shahidullah Hall crossing and played Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman's historic March 7 speech. Police went to the spot on information and detained Asif Ahmed Shoikot with the help of locals while he was trying to flee. Later, around 9:20 pm last night, Abdullah Al Mamun and Sheikh Tasnim Afroz Emi, along with 10-15 unidentified individuals, gathered in front of Gate 1 of the National Museum in Shahbagh. At the time, the accused chanted slogans using loudspeakers and tried to resume activities of the banned organisation, according to case details. They also obstructed police from performing their duties and attempted to snatch Shoikot from police custody, the case statement said. At that time, a group of students, led by Ducsu representatives AB Zubair and Musaddiq Ali Ibne Mohammad, held Mamun and Emi and handed them over to the police. Following the incident, police filed a case under the Anti-Terrorism Act with Shahbagh Police Station today.

title: Anis Alamgir denied bail in ACC case
body: A special court has denied bail to journalist Anis Alamgir today in a case filed over “acquiring assets beyond his known sources of income”. Judge Md Sabbir Faiz of the Metropolitan Senior Special Judge’s Court in Dhaka passed the order following a bail petition, defence lawyer Taslima Zahan Popy said. On January 28, the court showed Anis arrested in a case filed by the Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC). Earlier, the case was filed on January 15 by the ACC under Section 27(1) of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act. According to the ACC inquiry, Anis’ total wealth stands at Tk 4.25 crore, while his declared assets in the latest income tax return amount to Tk 57.99 lakh, leaving nearly Tk 3.68 crore unaccounted for. On March 5, the High Court granted bail to Anis Alamgir in another case filed under the Anti-Terrorism Act.

title: HC grants Khairul Haque bail in 4 cases
body: The High Court today granted permanent bail to former chief justice ABM Khairul Haque in four cases filed on different charges, including murder. The bench of Justice Md Khairul Alam and Justice Md Sagir Hossain delivered the verdict following four separate bail petitions filed by Khairul. However, Khairul cannot be released from jail as he remains arrested in a corruption case, his lawyer Md Motaher Hossain Sazu told The Daily Star. On March 5, 2026, the HC bench headed by Justice Md Khairul Alam fixed today for delivering the verdict after concluding the hearing on four rules issued by another bench following the bail petitions on October 26 last year, asking the state to explain why Khairul should not be granted bail in the cases. During the hearing, senior lawyers Mohammad Munsurul Hoque Chowdhury, Sara Hossain, Md Motaher Hossain Sazu, Mohammad Sayed Ahmed Raza and Mustafizur Rahman Khan appeared for Khairul and prayed to the HC to grant him bail. They argued that Khairul, who is around 80 years old, has been kept in custody for a long period and is suffering from various illnesses, including heart and diabetes-related problems. There has been no progress in the investigation into the cases, and in this situation, he may be granted bail, the lawyers told the HC. Meanwhile, deputy attorneys general Abdulah-Al-Mamun Masud, Zahirul Islam Suman, Nahid Hasan and Md Akhteruzzaman represented the state and opposed the bail petitions during the hearing. Khairul served as Chief Justice from September 30, 2010, to May 17, 2011. Under his leadership, the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court delivered a verdict on May 10, 2011, that annulled the 13th Amendment to the Constitution, which had introduced the caretaker government system in 1996. Almost a year after the July mass uprising and the fall of the Awami League government, police arrested Khairul from his Dhanmondi residence on July 24 last year. One of the cases was filed with Jatrabari Police Station on charges of killing Jubo Dal activist Abdul Kaiyum Ahad in Dhaka during the July movement. On August 27 last year, Supreme Court lawyer Mujahidul Islam Shaheen filed another case with Shahbagh Police Station, accusing him of forgery related to the caretaker government verdict. Two other cases were filed against Khairul on similar charges with Fatullah and Bandar police stations in Narayanganj on August 25 by Nurul Islam Molla and Abduk Bari Bhuiyan.

title: Mob beats suspected mugger to death in Narayanganj’s Siddhirganj
body: A man in his mid-20s was beaten to death by a crowd in Narayanganj's Siddhirganj, this morning after he was allegedly involved in an attempted mugging, police said. The incident occurred around 6:00am on the Dhaka-Narayanganj link road in the Jalkuri area, according to Abdul Barik, officer-in-charge (OC) of Siddhirganj Police Station. The victim’s identity had not been confirmed as of filing this report at 3:00 pm. According to preliminary investigation and eyewitness accounts, three men on a motorcycle attempted to rob a battery-powered auto-rickshaw. When the driver raised alarm, locals intervened. “Two of the suspects fled, leaving the motorcycle behind, but one was caught by locals. The crowd then beat him severely, resulting in his death on the spot,” the OC said. Locals also set the motorcycle on fire, which was later extinguished by the Fire Service. Police arrived at the scene about 20 minutes after being notified. The victim’s body was taken to Narayanganj General Hospital for autopsy. A knife and a machete were recovered from the site. OC Abdul Barik said they are preparing a case over the death caused by the mob attack.

title: Stepfather admits killing Narsingdi girl: police
body: Police yesterday claimed that the recent murder of a teenage girl in Madhabdi of Narsingdi was committed by her stepfather out of frustration. The accused, Md Ashraf Ali, 45, has confessed to the crime in court, Narsingdi Superintendent of Police Abdullah Al Faruq claimed at a press briefing yesterday noon. A total of nine people, including Ashraf Ali, have so far been arrested over the killing of the girl named Amena. According to a press release issued by Narsingdi police, Amena had been in a relationship with Nur Mohammad alias Nura, 28. In his confessional statement before the court, Ashraf said on the night of February 25, he took Amena with him, telling her they were going to the house of his colleague Suman. On the way, he killed her by strangling her with her scarf. Terming her involvement with Nur “socially inappropriate activities,” Ashraf said it caused him frustration as he faced repeated social humiliation because of it, which ultimately led him to commit the murder. Earlier, on February 10 at midnight, the girl was allegedly gang-raped at the house of Hazrat Ali. Police investigations found involvement of Hazrat Ali, Ebadul, Jaman, and Gaffar in the incident. On February 26, locals found Amena’s body lying in a mustard field in Darikandi, Kotowalir Char, and informed police. On the same day, the victim’s mother, Fahima Begum, filed a case with Madhabdi Police Station naming nine people as accused. Police later arrested seven of the named suspects, including Nur. Meanwhile, former Mahishashura Union Parishad member and union BNP unit vice-president Ahammad Ali Dewan has been expelled from his party position following allegations of his involvement in the incident. According to the case statement, some of the accused allegedly tried to cover up the rape incident and later threatened the victim’s family as they failed to do so.

title: 3 hurt as bombs explode at Cumilla Kali temple, nearby areas: police
body: A priest was injured as a bomb exploded at Kaligach Tala Kali Mondir during the weekly Shani puja in Baganbari Thakurpara area in Cumilla city on Saturday evening, said police. Two others -- Abdul Barek and Jihad -- were also injured when the miscreants exploded two crude bombs in front of a nearby Buddhist temple and a private office while fleeing. Priest Keshob Chakraborty, 48, and two others received primary treatment at a hospital, said Md Touhidul Anwar, officer-in-charge (OC) of Kotwali Model Police Station. Sajol Kumar Chanda, president of Mandir Committee, said the bomb exploded inside the temple around 6:30pm during the Shani puja. Witnesses who came to the temple said that Shani puja was underway at the temple in the Thakurpara area on Saturday evening. At that time, a bomb went off. A CCTV footage shows that at 6:28pm, a masked individual entered the temple carrying a bag. Several others were seen standing nearby. At one stage, the person left the bag and quickly ran away. Shortly afterwards, the bomb exploded there. The explosion created panic among the people present at the temple, and priest Keshab Chakraborty was injured. Locals said that while fleeing after the incident, the miscreants detonated two more bombs in front of a nearby Buddhist temple and a private office. As a result, Abdul Barek, son of Sujat Ali of Thakurpara Baganbari area, and Jihad, son of Nazrul Islam, were injured. They received primary treatment at a hospital. Injured priest Keshab Chakraborty said, “After the bomb explosion, a white object fell in front of me. At first, I thought something had fallen from a tree. Later, seeing smoke, others told me it was a bomb. However, I cannot say who threw it or why.” Shyamal Krishna, convener of the Metropolitan Puja Celebration Front, said, “After receiving the news, we came to the scene. It is still not clear who carried out this attack. Police have collected CCTV footage. Those who are trying to disturb the peaceful environment must be arrested quickly and brought under the law.” OC Kotwali Model Police Station, Md Touhidul Anwar, said, “We have collected CCTV footage from the scene. The matter is under investigation. It is not possible to say right now why or who carried out the crude explosions. However, operations are ongoing to arrest those involved.” He said a team from the bomb disposal unit has been called to investigate the explosion. Meanwhile, Cumilla Superintendent of Police (SP) Md Anisuzzaman visited the scene shortly after the incident. During the visit, he said that police are working to uncover the real cause behind the incident and arrest those responsible. Law enforcers cordoned off the temple premises, he added.

title: Scuffle breaks out in front of Shahbagh Police Station over playing March 7 speech
body: A scuffle broke out in front of Shahbagh Police Station on Saturday night over the playing of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman’s historic March 7 speech. Meanwhile, a Dhaka university student was beaten at that time after being accused of being an activist of the banned organisation Chhatra League. Students of Dhaka University, along with leaders and activists of Jatiya Chhatra Shakti and Dhaka University Central Students’ Union (Ducsu), were present at the scene. The tension stemmed from the detention of a former Dhaka University student and a Chhatra League leader, Aasif Ahmed, by police for playing the March 7 speech at Chankharpul intersection earlier in the evening. Following the detention, Sheikh Tasnim Afroz Emi, who contested for the vice-president post in the Ducsu election 2025, announced on Facebook that the March 7 speech would be played in front of Shahbagh Police Station. Around 9:30pm, several Dhaka University students and some leaders and activists of Bangladesh Chhatra Union gathered in front of the police station. At one stage, while the speech was being played through loudspeakers, some individuals approached from the direction of the police station and asked them to stop it, leading to a verbal altercation. Shortly afterwards, another group arrived and attempted to obstruct the programme, which escalated into a clash between the two sides. When asked, those opposing the playing of the speech identified themselves as “general people”. Later, leaders and activists of Jatiya Chhatra Shakti’s Dhaka University unit arrived at the spot and delivered speeches and chanted slogans opposing the playing of the March 7 speech. Ducsu leaders, including Literary and Cultural Affairs Secretary Musaddiq Ali Ibne Mohammad and Social Welfare Secretary AB Zubair, also reached the scene and took a position against playing the speech. After the incident, organiser Emi told the media that several people on their side were injured during the scuffle. “The unprovoked and disproportionate attack carried out on us is extremely condemnable. Their insecurity proves that we are on the right side of history,” he said. Maeen Ahmed, general secretary of a faction of the Dhaka University unit of Bangladesh Chhatra Union who was present there, said that except for Jamaat, no one in Bangladesh has objections to the Liberation War. “Apart from these children of razakars, there is no opposition to important events related to the Liberation War,” he said. Around 10:45pm, a Dhaka University student, Al Mamun of the 2020-21 academic session, was beaten by some protesters after they accused him of being affiliated with Chhatra League. Ramna Division Deputy Commissioner Masud Alam said police received information in the afternoon that a Dhaka University unit Chhatra League leader was playing Bangabandhu’s March 7 speech on a loudspeaker in the Chankharpul area. Police brought the man to the station for his own safety, fearing he could come under attack, he said. Later in the evening, a group of youths protested in front of the police station with loudspeakers, demanding his release. Around 9:30pm, some former Ducsu leaders and local people chased those demonstrating in front of the station, Masud said. During the incident, two journalists were injured while filming the scene. Police later came out of the station and rescued the two journalists. Masud said police have collected CCTV footage and are trying to identify those responsible for attacking the journalists. No new arrests or detentions have been made so far. A case is being processed over the incident, while the man detained remained in custody, he added.

title: Granduncle sent to jail over alleged rape of 9-year-old in Patuakhali
body: A 60-year-old man was sent to jail yesterday in Bauphal of Patuakhali after being arrested in Dhaka on charges of raping a nine-year-old child. The suspect, Lalu Shah, who is the brother of the child's paternal grandfather, was detained in a joint operation by Rab and police on Friday night in Lalbagh, said Bauphal Police Station Officer-in-Charge (Investigation) Atiqul Islam. OC Atiqul added that the suspect was taken to Bauphal yesterday (Saturday) morning, and then produced before court in the afternoon. The court then ordered that he be sent to jail. The arrest came after a written complaint was filed by the child’s mother at Bauphal Police Station. According to the complaint, the incident took place last Sunday. After locals rescued the child, she was admitted to Bauphal Upazila Health Complex, said OC Atiqul. He added that Lalu Shah had been absconding since the complaint.

title: Student leader beaten to death at Jhenaidah fuel station
body: A student leader died after being beaten while trying to buy fuel for his motorcycle in Jhenaidah Sadar today. The deceased was identified as Nirab Ahmed, 25, of Barobazar area of Kaliganj upazila in Jhenaidah, said police. Confirming Nirab’s political identity, Saidur Rahman, convener of the Jhenaidah District Students Against Discrimination, told The Daily Star that Nirab had been actively involved on the front lines during the July uprising. He was living in a rented mess in the Bakultala area of Adarsha Para in Jhenaidah. Additional Superintendent of Jhenaidah Police (Sadar Circle) Mahfuz Hossain said that police detained three employees of the fuel station in connection with the incident. They are Nasim Hossain, of Baraikhali village; Ramizul Islam, of Aruakandi village; and Daud Hossain, of South Kastagra village. Jhenaidah Sadar Police Station Officer-in-Charge Shamsul Arefin said Nirab went to Taj Filling Station, located in the Central Bus Terminal area on the Jhenaidah-Dhaka National Highway, to buy fuel for his motorcycle around 8:45pm. An argument broke out after the employees refused to provide the amount of fuel he had asked for. He was beaten severely and taken to Jhenaidah 250-Bed General Hospital where he died around 9:00pm. Sabyasachi Pal Suman, an emergency department physician at the Jhenaidah 250-Bed General Hospital, told The Daily Star that Nirab was brought to the hospital in a critical condition. “His back was swollen and he had injuries behind his waist and head.” “After examining him, he was declared dead at 9:05 pm,” the doctor said, adding that the death was initially suspected to have been caused by internal bleeding. A case is being filed with Jhenaidah Police Station, the OC added. Earlier on Saturday afternoon, fuel sales were halted at around 28 out of 33 filling stations in Jhenaidah, creating a severe shortage. Only two filling stations near the district town were selling fuel in limited quantities.

title: UPDF member shot dead in Khagrachhari’s Panchari
body: A member of the United People's Democratic Front (UPDF) was shot dead by unidentified miscreants in Khagrachhari’s Panchari upazila today. The deceased was identified as Apan Tripura, alias Sangram, 28, of Padmini Para village in Ultachhari union, said Angya Marma, organiser of the Khagrachari unit of UPDF, in a statement to the media today. The statement said that around 11:30am, a group of 15-20 armed men entered the Barakona area of ​​Panchari Sadar union and started ambushing them. At that time, Apan fell in front of them on his way to organisational work and was shot dead. Condemning the killing, the UPDF accused the Parbatya Chattagram Jana Samhati Samiti (PCJSS), led by Santu Larma, of carrying out the murder. However, Sajib Chakma, assistant information and publicity secretary of the PCJSS, denied the allegations. “The Jana Samhati Samiti has no involvement in such an incident. The allegation is baseless,” he said. Md Ferdous Wahid, officer-in-charge of Panchari Police Station, told The Daily Star that on information, police recovered the body and sent it to Khagrachhari General Hospital morgue for autopsy.

title: Trader stabbed to death 'over extortion' in Cox’s Bazar
body: A trader was stabbed to death after refusing to pay extortion money in Cox’s Bazar town today. The deceased was identified as Ganesh Pal, 35, a grocery shop owner at Borobazar area, said police. Cox’s Bazar Sadar Model Police Station Officer-in-Charge Md Chhomi Uddin said the incident took place in Dakshin Sahityika Palli area near the Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) camp around 3:00pm. The deceased's wife Shefali Pal and his brother Ashish Pal alleged that their neighbour, Jishan, had demanded extortion money and had earlier disputes with them over the matter. According to them, Jishan stabbed Ganesh in the afternoon after he refused to pay up. He was rushed to a hospital where the on-duty doctor declared him dead. The OC said they visited the scene after receiving information. “According to initial findings, the accused Jishan, known locally for various petty crimes, demanded money from Ganesh Pal, who denied to pay the amount. During an argument, Jishan suddenly took out a knife and stabbed Ganesh twice,” he said. He added that Ganesh was critically injured in the attack and later died from his injuries. Police also learned that another youth was present at the scene at the time of the incident, the OC said, adding that drives are underway to arrest the accused.

title: Teen girl murder in Narsingdi: Stepfather admits killing daughter
body: A stepfather today confessed before a Narsingdi court to killing his teenage daughter, Amena Khatun, whose body was found in a mustard field in Narsingdi’s Sadar upazila on February 26, police said. Md Ashraf Ali, 45, gave his statement under Section 164 before Narsingdi Senior Judicial Magistrate Md Mehdi Hasan, said Abdullah Al Faruq, superintendent of police in Narsingdi. According to his statement, on the night of February 25, Ashraf took Amena out of their home, saying they were going to visit his colleague Suman. On the way, he strangled her with a scarf. The next morning, her body was recovered from a field. He claimed he was frustrated over what he described as his daughter’s “socially inappropriate activities”, which led to the murder. The victim’s mother filed a case with Madhabdi Police Station the same day, naming nine suspects. The case statement alleged that Amena had been gang-raped by four men on February 10. Some of the accused reportedly tried to cover up the incident, threatened the family, and pressured Amena to leave the village. An arbitration meeting was scheduled for March 1 regarding the matter. On the night of February 25, Amena and her father, Ashraf Ali, were reportedly intercepted in the Boroitola area of Kotowalir Char. From there, the prime accused Nur Mohammad alias Nura and his associates allegedly took the girl away by force. Around 9:30am on February 26, locals found Amena’s body lying in a mustard field in Darikandi, Kotowalir Char, and informed police. Police later arrested eight of the nine named suspects at different times. Former Union Parishad member and Mahishasura Union BNP vice-president Ahmed Ali Dewan has been expelled from the party over alleged involvement in the case. According to the First Information Report, the accused initially tried to suppress the incident and later allegedly threatened the victim’s family, demanding she leave the village. The prime accused, Nura, was arrested from Gazipur on the night of February 27, said Additional Superintendent of Police Anwar Hossain Shamim. He added that Nura was attempting to flee to India via the Dinajpur border. The other arrested men are Ebadullah, 38, Hazrat Ali, 40, Gaffar, 37, Ahmed Ali alias Ahmed Dewan, 65, Md Imran Dewan, 32, and Md Ayub, 30, all residents of Mahishasura Union. On March 6, Ashraf was brought to Madhabdi Police Station for interrogation but his account was in conflict with other evidence in the case. During interrogation, he eventually admitted to killing his stepdaughter and later repeated the confession in court. Following his statement, the magistrate ordered Ashraf to jail.

title: Man arrested over attempted molestation of minor girl inside Kapasia health complex
body: A man was arrested in a case filed over the attempted molestation of a 15-year-old girl inside Kapasia Upazila Health Complex in Gazipur. The arrestee has been identified as Md Mamun, 30, a resident of Raonat village in Kapasia upazila. He had been reportedly undergoing treatment at the health complex. Dr Md Habibur Rahman, health and family planning officer of the health complex, told The Daily Star that Mamun attempted to molest a 15-year-old girl on Thursday night. He said Mamun tried to molest a seven-year-old child on the next day when people rushed there, hearing her screams, and informed police. Police rushed to the spot and took him to the police station, the official said. Mamun was arrested after a complaint was filed by the husband of the first victim. The mother of the 15-year-old girl said, "He took my daughter to the hospital corridor and made an indecent proposal. In the darkness of the night, he tried to force himself on her. Hearing her screams, I rushed there and rescued her. We have taken legal action regarding the incident." The same person has also been accused of attempting to molest a seven-year-old girl on Friday afternoon, the OC said, adding that no complaint has been filed in this regard. He added that legal action will be taken if any complaint is filed. Meanwhile, Member of Parliament for Gazipur-4 (Kapasia), Salah Uddin, in a post on social media today, said, "The attempt to commit such a heinous act at Kapasia Upazila Health Complex is highly condemnable. Immediate legal action will be taken against the person involved, and exemplary punishment will be ensured."

title: Prime accused held in Rangpur woman killing
body: Rab has arrested the prime accused in the murder of a woman whose throat was slit after she protested the stalking of her younger sister in Nageshwari upazila of Kurigram. The accused is Abul Kalam, 42, a resident of Char Harikesh area under Kurigram’s Sadar upazila. Acting on a tip-off, a Rab team arrested him during a raid at a house on Station Road in Badarganj upazila of Rangpur on Thursday night, according to a press release issued by Rab-13 yesterday. Biplab Kumar Goswami, senior assistant director (media) of Rab-13, confirmed that Kalam has been handed over to the concerned police station for legal action. He added that operations are ongoing to arrest the other accused in the case. The incident occurred on January 14. The victim’s father, Saifur Rahman, filed a murder case against Kalam and others with Kochakata Police Station the following day. According to the case statement, Kalam and his associates made advances on the younger sister of the deceased, Shahida Khatun, 36. Shahida came to know about the matter and called for a village arbitration against the accused in January this year. However, as Kalam and his associates failed to appear on the scheduled day, the matter remained unresolved. Around 7:30 pm on January 14, while Shahida was engaged in household work, Kalam and his associates attacked her. At one stage, they slit her throat with a sharp weapon and fled the scene, leaving her dead on the spot. The case statement notes that Shahida was targeted and killed because she protested the stalking of her sister. Kalam and the other accused went into hiding after the murder.

title: CID sues Hadi murder accused over money laundering
body: The Criminal Investigation Department (CID) has filed a case against Jubo League leader and former ward councillor Mohammad Tajul Islam Chowdhury, an accused in the Sharif Osman Hadi murder case, on charges of laundering around Tk 2.5 crore. The case was lodged with Pallabi Police Station on March 5 under the Money Laundering Prevention Act, 2012, said a press release issued by CID’s media wing. Tajul, also known as Bappi, along with six to seven unnamed accused, amassed a large amount of money through extortion and fraud in various sectors, including transport, temporary roadside markets, garment waste (jhut) trading, and cable and broadband internet businesses, in the capital’s Pallabi area. “During its inquiry, CID found discrepancies between Tajul’s declared income and the assets he accumulated,” the press release said. In total, CID found evidence of illegal acquisition, transfer and conversion of about Tk 2.51 crore. The inquiry also revealed that transactions worth over Tk 56.86 crore were made through different bank accounts linked to the accused. Currently, about Tk 6.33 lakh remains frozen in those accounts following a court order. CID further said two audit reports submitted by Tajul for 2023 and 2024 were found to be forged. The reports were shown to have been prepared by chartered accountant SM Zakaria, who died during the Covid-19 pandemic, suggesting that the accused used his name and address to produce fake audit documents. CID’s Financial Crime Unit is currently investigating the case.

title: Expatriate found dead at home
body: A man was found dead at his home in Juri upazila of Moulvibazar on Thursday night. The deceased was identified as Nazrul Islam, 33, a resident of the South Sagarnal area. He had returned from Qatar recently. According to police and family members, Nazrul worked in Qatar for the past four to five years. Around 11:30pm on Thursday, he returned home from the nearby Fultala market and went into his room. When family members later called him for sehri, he didn’t respond. They looked through a gap in the bamboo fence and found his body hanging from the grille on the wall of the house with a rope around his neck. Sub-Inspector Kabir Uddin of Juri Police Station said, “Except for the ligature mark around his neck, no other injury marks were found on the body.”

title: AL leader dies within 40 minutes of release on bail
body: An Awami League leader, who was in Panchagarh Jail, died in a hospital shortly after being released on bail. Harunur Rashid, 55, was hospitalised after falling ill on Wednesday. He died in ICU of Dinajpur Medical College Hospital on Thursday, Jailer Akherul Islam of Panchagarh Jail told The Daily Star. According to prison and hospital sources, the prison authorities received the bail order around 3:30pm on Thursday. At 3:40pm, the order was sent to the hospital via email. At 4:08pm, doctors declared Harun dead. Harun was a former member of Panchagarh Zilla Parishad and ex-organising secretary of Debiganj upazila unit AL. According to prison sources, Harun was arrested on October 16 last year in a case filed under the Negotiable Instruments (NI) Act. He was sentenced to one year of simple imprisonment. Another case had also been filed against him. Jailer Akherul said Harun received initial treatment at the prison hospital after falling ill. He was later taken to Panchagarh Sadar Hospital and then transferred to Dinajpur Medical College Hospital. A Panchagarh court on Thursday afternoon granted him bail in the NI Act case. The judge also ordered the withdrawal of another case filed under section 420 of the Penal Code. Jailer Akherul said that after receiving the bail order, the authorities quickly completed the formalities and sent it to Dinajpur Medical College Hospital so that he could be freed as soon as possible.

title: Taqi murder probe lingers after 13 years
body: Family members and leaders of various political, social, and civic organisations visited the grave of Tanwir Muhammad Taqi yesterday morning, marking the 13th anniversary of the teenager’s murder in Narayanganj. Expressing frustration over the lack of justice even after more than a decade, they demanded the investigation be completed and the charge sheet filed without further delay. Around 10:00am, mourners visited Taqi’s grave at Siraj Shah’s shrine in the Puran Bandar area and offered prayers seeking eternal peace for his soul. Prior to this, several organisations laid wreaths at the grave to pay tribute. These included Shantrash Nirmul Taqi Mancha, Narayanganj Sanskriti Jote, Khelaghar Ashor, Ganosamhati Andolon, Kranti Khelaghar Ashor, Somomona, Communist Party of Bangladesh, Bangladesh Samajtantrik Dal, Bangladesh Mahila Parishad, Udichi Shilpigosthi, and Anubhob. Those present included Taqi’s father, cultural activist Rafiur Rabbi, his younger son Rakib Muhammad Saki, member secretary of Shantrash Nirmul Taqi Mancha Halim Azad, former president of Narayanganj Sanskritik Jote Ziaul Islam Kajol, general secretary Dina Tajrin, former general secretary Dhiman Saha Jewel, district coordinator of Ganosamhati Andolon Tariqul Suzon, executive coordinator Anjan Das, city convener Niamur Rashid Biplob, district president of the Communist Party Hafizul Islam, NAP general secretary Awlad Hossain, among others. Taqi was abducted on March 6, 2013, and his body was recovered two days later from a canal connected to the Shitalakhhya River. A year later, the Rapid Action Battalion (Rab) disclosed details of the killing at a press conference, outlining where, how, and on whose orders the murder was carried out. On March 5, 2014, then Rab Additional Director General Ziaul Ahsan stated that 11 people, led by Azmeri Osman, nephew of former Awami League lawmaker Shamim Osman, were involved in Taqi’s killing. According to the investigation, Taqi’s father Rabbi had angered Shamim Osman and his associates by supporting then mayoral candidate Selina Hayat Ivy in the 2011 city corporation election and by mobilising opposition to alleged extortion and land grabbing by the lawmaker. Rabbi’s son was reportedly killed in retaliation. Following the death of Shamim Osman’s brother, lawmaker Nasim Osman, on April 30, 2014, then Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina expressed support for the Osman family in parliament. According to Taqi’s family members, the judicial process in the murder case has effectively stalled since then.

title: ‘Chilli powder rubbed on wounds, dirty water forced down their throats’
body: Relatives of the two men who were beaten to death by a mob on suspicion of theft in Munshiganj have alleged that the victims were brutally tortured before they were murdered early Wednesday. “They rubbed chilli powder on their wounds and forced them to drink dirty water,” the mother-in-law of one of the deceased said, describing the horrific ordeal. The two victims -- Sagar, 25, son of Farhad Mia, and Chhanarul, 20, son of Shahidul Islam, residents of Goalimandra village -- were attacked by locals in Louhajang upazila in the dead of the night and later declared dead after being taken to a local upazila health complex. “My son went to call his friend during sehri. Some people caught him and beat him to death. They killed my child. My precious son is gone...,” Chhanarul’s mother Rokhsana told The Daily Star in a trembling voice. She was sobbing uncontrollably, sitting in her small shack. A member of the Bede community, Chhanarul was the second of three siblings. Still struggling to contain her grief, Rokhsana said her son had never been accused of any wrongdoing. “They suspected him of theft and caught him. But there was never any complaint against him. Those who beat him to death are criminals. I demand the death penalty for them,” she said. Chhanarul earned a living by selling boiled eggs door to door. He lived with other members of the Bede community in makeshift shacks along the bank of a nearly dried-up river in the area. This correspondent also spoke with the wife of the other deceased, Sagar. Sagar left behind four children, the youngest being only three months old. “My husband drove an auto-rickshaw. During sehri he went out to start his work. While walking to the garage, people caught him on suspicion of theft and beat him to death,” said Sagar’s widow, Jannatul. “I was asleep. In the morning I woke up and learned that my husband had been killed.” Sagar’s mother-in-law Aklima said, “They [the mob] hurt them and rubbed chilli powder on their wounds. They forced them to swallow dirty water. How could one kill another by making them go through such torture? Are they even human? Only Allah knows what they were made of!” she said. Now she worries about the wellbeing of her daughter and her four grandchildren. Officer-in-Charge of Louhajang Police Station Monirul Islam said a case has been filed over the incident. “Chhanarul’s mother Rokhsana filed the case with Louhajang Police Station, naming nine people and accusing 15-20 unidentified accused,” he said. “So far six suspects have been arrested and the court sent them to jail. Operations are ongoing to arrest the remaining accused.”

title: Woman’s hair allegedly cut off over dowry demands in Jhenaidah; husband, in-laws accused of torture
body: A man has filed a case against his son-in-law and his family for allegedly cutting off his daughter's hair and confining her over dowry demands in Jhenaidah. Chandina Khatun, 22, a mother of two, accused her husband, Md Amirul Chowdhury, father-in-law Mintu Chowdhury, and mother-in-law of torturing her in a "medieval" manner. The incident occurred on Wednesday night in Bhupatipur village under Jhenaidah Sadar upazila. Family members rescued Chandina on Thursday morning and admitted her to Jhenaidah 250-bed General Hospital. Her father, Majedul Mondol, filed a case with Jhenaidah Sadar Police Station on Thursday night. According to the case statement, Chandina was physically and mentally tortured over dowry demands on Wednesday night. They allegedly cut off her hair and locked her in a room. The following day, after being informed by neighbours, her family rescued her. Chandina got married to Amirul five years ago through a family arrangement. About two and a half years ago, Amirul went to Malaysia while Chandina was pregnant with their second child. He returned about a month ago. The couple has two sons aged three and two. Speaking to The Daily Star from her hospital bed, Chandina said, "On Wednesday night, my husband suddenly accused me of sending an SMS to a man. When I denied it, he started beating me. My husband, father-in-law, and mother-in-law held me and forcibly cut off my hair. They then locked me inside an abandoned shop next to the house." Her father said, "Before my son-in-law went abroad, we gave him Tk 380,000. After returning, he demanded another Tk 180,000. When we refused, they began torturing my daughter." Attempts to contact Amirul were unsuccessful as his phone was switched off. His father, Mintu Chowdhury, said, "I was not at home during the incident. When I returned, I saw my son had cut my daughter-in-law's hair." The victim's uncle, Sajedul Islam, told The Daily Star, "If my niece had committed any wrongdoing, they could have informed us. We spoke to locals, but no one raised such allegations. My niece's husband is demanding money to go abroad again. When my brother refused, they tortured her. Now they are making false allegations." Police Inspector (Investigation) Zahirul Islam said a case was recorded on Thursday night. "We are trying to arrest the accused." The investigating officer, SI Tipu Sultan, said, "After the case was filed, we immediately launched a drive. He is currently absconding. Our operation to arrest him is ongoing."

title: CID files money laundering case against Jubo League leader accused in Hadi murder
body: The Criminal Investigation Department (CID) has filed a case against Jubo League leader and former ward councillor Mohammad Tajul Islam Chowdhury, an accused in the Sharif Osman Hadi murder case, on charges of laundering around Tk 2.5 crore. The case was lodged with Pallabi Police Station on March 5 under the Money Laundering Prevention Act, 2012, said a press release issued by CID’s media wing. According to the press release, Tajul, also known as Bappi, along with six to seven unnamed accused, amassed a large amount of money through extortion and fraud by controlling various sectors in the Pallabi area of the capital, including the transport sector, temporary roadside markets, garment waste (jhut) trading, and cable and broadband internet businesses. “During its inquiry, CID found discrepancies between Tajul’s declared income and the assets he accumulated over the years,” the press release said. In total, CID found evidence of illegal acquisition, transfer, and conversion of about Tk 2.51 crore, according to the press release. The inquiry also revealed that transactions worth over Tk 56.86 crore were made through different bank accounts linked to the accused. Currently, about Tk 6.33 lakh remains frozen in those accounts following a court order, the press release read. CID further said two audit reports submitted by Tajul for 2023 and 2024 were found to be forged. The reports were shown to have been prepared by chartered accountant SM Zakaria, who had died during the Covid-19 pandemic, suggesting that the accused used his name and address to produce fake audit documents. CID’s Financial Crime Unit is currently investigating the case.

title: Prime accused arrested in Rangpur for killing woman who protested stalking of sister
body: Members of the Rapid Action Battalion (Rab) have arrested the prime accused in the murder of a woman whose throat was slit after she protested the stalking of her younger sister in Nageshwari upazila of Kurigram. The accused is Abul Kalam, 42, a resident of Char Harikesh area under Kurigram’s Sadar upazila. Acting on a tip-off, a Rab team arrested him during a raid at a house on Station Road in Badarganj upazila of Rangpur on Thursday night, according to a press release issued by Rab-13 today. Additional Superintendent of Police Biplab Kumar Goswami, senior assistant director (media) of Rab-13, confirmed that Kalam has been handed over to the concerned police station for legal action. He added that operations are ongoing to arrest the other accused in the case. The incident occurred on January 14. The victim’s father, Saifur Rahman, filed a murder case against Kalam and others with Kochakata Police Station the following day. According to the case statement, Kalam and his associates made advances on the younger sister of the deceased, Shahida Khatun, 36. Shahida came to know about the matter and called for a village arbitration against the accused in January this year. However, as Kalam and his associates failed to appear on the scheduled day, the matter remained unresolved. Around 7:30 pm on January 14, while Shahida was engaged in household work, Kalam and his associates attacked her. At one stage, they slit her throat with a sharp weapon and fled the scene, leaving her dead on the spot. The case statement notes that Shahida was targeted and killed because she protested the stalking of her sister. Kalam and the other accused went into hiding after the murder.

title: FBI brings Bangladeshi man accused of child sexual exploitation to US from Malaysia
body: The US Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) has secured the extradition of a Bangladeshi national from Malaysia after arresting him with the assistance of Malaysian authorities. FBI Director Kash Patel confirmed that Zobaidul Amin, 28, accused of operating an international child sexual exploitation enterprise and wanted since 2022, was flown to the United States and arrived in Alaska on Thursday (March 5, 2026). He is expected to be formally charged later today, according to Malaysian newspaper Free Malaysia Today. Patel expressed gratitude to Malaysian authorities for their cooperation, saying, “Thank you to our Kuala Lumpur office, the government of Malaysia, and our great local partners all over the country who assisted with the investigation and arrest.” In a post on X, Patel shared images appearing to show three FBI officers escorting the suspect to a private jet on a runway in Malaysia.

title: 13 years after Taqi murder, family demands action on stalled case
body: Family members and leaders of various political, social, and civic organisations visited the grave of Tanwir Muhammad Taqi this morning, marking the 13th anniversary of the teenager’s murder in Narayanganj. Expressing frustration over the lack of justice even after more than a decade, they demanded the investigation be completed and the charge sheet filed without further delay. Around 10:00 am, mourners visited Taqi’s grave at Siraj Shah’s shrine in the Puran Bandar area and offered prayers seeking eternal peace for his soul. Prior to this, several organisations laid wreaths at the grave to pay tribute. These included Shantrash Nirmul Taqi Mancha, Narayanganj Sanskriti Jote, Khelaghar Ashor, Ganosamhati Andolon, Kranti Khelaghar Ashor, Somomona, Communist Party of Bangladesh, Bangladesh Samajtantrik Dal, Bangladesh Mahila Parishad, Udichi Shilpi Goshthi, and Anubhob. Those present included Taqi’s father, cultural activist Rafiur Rabbi, his younger son Rakib Muhammad Saki, member secretary of Shantrash Nirmul Taqi Mancha Halim Azad, former president of Narayanganj Sanskritik Jote Ziaul Islam Kajol, general secretary Dina Tajrin, former general secretary Dhiman Saha Jewel, district coordinator of Ganosamhati Andolon Tariqul Suzon, executive coordinator Anjan Das, city convener Niamur Rashid Biplob, district president of the Communist Party Hafizul Islam, NAP general secretary Awlad Hossain, among others. Taqi was abducted on March 6, 2013, and his body was recovered two days later from a canal connected to the Shitalakkhya River. A year later, the Rapid Action Battalion (Rab) disclosed details of the killing at a press conference, outlining where, how, and on whose orders the murder was carried out. On March 5, 2014, then Rab Additional Director General Ziaul Ahsan stated that 11 people, led by Azmeri Osman, nephew of former Awami League lawmaker Shamim Osman, were involved in Taqi’s killing. According to the investigation, Taqi’s father Rabbi had angered Shamim Osman and his associates by supporting then mayoral candidate Selina Hayat Ivy in the 2011 city corporation election and by mobilising opposition to alleged extortion and land grabbing by the lawmaker. Rabbi’s son was reportedly killed in retaliation. Following the death of Shamim Osman’s brother, lawmaker Nasim Osman, on April 30, 2014, then Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina expressed support for the Osman family in parliament. According to Taqi’s family members, the judicial process in the murder case has effectively stalled since then.

title: Pro-BNP transport workers’ leader murdered in Khulna
body: A pro-BNP transport workers’ leader was shot dead by unidentified criminals in Khulna city on Wednesday night. Deceased Masum Billah, 55, was the former president of Rupsha upazila unit of Jatiyatabadi Sramik Dal and former president of the Rupsha–Bagerhat inter-district road transport workers’ union. He hailed from Bagmara village in Rupsha upazila. Quoting witnesses, police said Masum was standing near Dakbangla intersection in the city around 9:00pm when a group of people opened fire on him. They also stabbed him. Injured Masum was taken to the Khulna Medical College Hospital, where doctors declared him dead, said police. Mohammad Tazul Islam, deputy commissioner of Khulna Metropolitan Police, said traffic police, with the help of locals, detained a suspect while he was fleeing the scene. Six to seven attackers were involved in the killing, he said. The detainee, Ahoke Ghosh, revealed the names of several individuals involved in the killing. All of them are members of a local gang, claimed Tazul.

title: Writ petition challenges Ahsan H Mansur’s removal
body: A writ petition was filed yesterday with the High Court challenging the legality of the government’s decision to remove Ahsan H Mansur from the post of Bangladesh Bank governor and appoint Md Mostaqur Rahman in his place. Supreme Court lawyer Abdullah Al Mamun submitted the petition as a public interest litigation. The petition also seeks a stay on the government order that ended Ahsan H Mansur’s tenure and installed Mostaqur Rahman as the new head of the central bank. The government’s decision violated the relevant provisions of the Bangladesh Bank Order, 1972, said Sarwar Hossain, counsel for the petitioner. According to the law, a BB governor cannot be removed from office unless they are found to be incapable or incompetent. Mansur was removed from the post without any prior notice, which he was supposed to get before his termination, as per the law. The same legal framework bars the appointment of a loan defaulter as the central bank governor. Mostaqur is a loan defaulter and has connections with a company belonging to the controversial S Alam Group, Sarwar said. The HC may hold a hearing on the writ petition before a bench as early as next week. On February 25, the government removed Mansur from the post of central bank governor and appointed Mostaqur Rahman to the position. The decision was announced through separate gazette notifications issued by the Financial Institutions Division of the finance ministry. One notification stated that Mansur’s remaining tenure as governor had been cancelled with immediate effect “in the public interest”. Another notification said Mostaqur had been appointed governor on a four-year term from the date of joining, subject to relinquishing all professional ties with other institutions and organisations. The order was also stated to take immediate effect “in the public interest”.

title: Teacher murder: Husband accuses staffer, teachers
body: A case was filed yesterday in connection with the killing of a female teacher of Islamic University in Kushtia. Victim Asma Sadia Runa’s husband Imtiaz Sultan lodged the case with Islamic University Police Station, accusing Asma’s two colleagues, Shyam Sundar Sarkar and Habibur Rahman, along with university’s officer Biswajit Kumar Biswas and employee Fazlur Rahman. Faisal Mahmud, additional superintendent of Kushtia police, told The Daily Star that Shyam Sundar and Habibur are assistant professors of the social welfare department. Biswajit was a former assistant registrar and now works at a dormitory, while Fazlur is a temporary staffer of the university. On Wednesday afternoon, Runa, 40, an assistant professor and the chairperson of the social welfare department, was stabbed to death by Fazlur at her department office. Fazlur also tried to kill himself by slitting his own throat. Fazlur, who is now undergoing treatment at the 250-bed Kushtia General Hospital, has made a confessional statement to police, said Faisal. A doctor at the hospital said Fazlur told him that he killed Runa, triggered by anger over issues such as unpaid salary, misbehaviour, and his transfer to another department. Fazlur added that he had not been paid for around nine months. In the case statement, Runa’s husband Imtiaz said, “My wife joined as the chairperson of the department in September 2024. Before her, the department was headed by Shyam Sundar. He did not hand over the income and expenditure accounts of the department during his tenure to Runa at the time of her assuming charge. “At that time, Biswajit told my wife, ‘You have become chair like the previous one. You will just sign wherever we tell you and wherever we place the papers.’’’ My wife was astonished to hear this and told them that the department’s funds must be spent with transparency. “During Shyam Sundar’s tenure as chairman, Fazlur, Biswajit, and he allegedly embezzled and misused departmental funds. Biswajit and Shyam Sundar used office assistant Fazlu at different times to refuse to cooperate with and harass my wife. At one stage, Fazlur told my wife, ‘You cannot act like a saint and leave the department’s money untouched.’” The statement further said when Fazlur was served a show-cause notice for breaching departmental discipline and non-cooperation, he apologised. However, at the instigation of Biswajit and Shyam Sundar, he again continued non-cooperation, which led to him being relieved of his duties. Fazlu was transferred to the political science department and he joined there on February 18. Biswajit also received a transfer order from the university administration. Unable to accept the transfer orders, they collectively planned the murder, the FIR said. Another accused, Habibur, was promoted from lecturer to assistant professor and began harbouring intentions to become chair of the social welfare department, the FIR added. Shyam Sundar and Biswajit could not be contacted over phone despite repeated attempts. Talking to this correspondent, Habibur said he did not know why he was accused in the case. Runa was buried at the central municipal graveyard in Kushtia town after Zohr prayers yesterday. While conducting the autopsy, doctors found 20 stab wounds to her chest, abdomen, hands, and legs, said Hossain Imam, resident medical officer of 250-bed Kushtia General Hospital.

title: Shujan’s Gazipur district vice-president murdered
body: Miscreants have strangled to death Md Kamruzzaman Molla, 65, vice-president of the Gazipur district unit of Shushashoner Jonno Nagorik (Shujan). His body, with his hands and legs tied, was recovered from the Purbo Dhirashram area of Gazipur around 12:30 am last night, Officer-in-Charge of Gazipur Sadar Police Station Aminul Islam told The Daily Star. He said efforts are underway to arrest those involved in the incident. Kamruzzaman was a resident of Gazipur metropolitan area's ward-50. According to family members and police sources, he left home around 7:00 am yesterday to go to Gazipur court regarding a case. However, the court proceedings did not take place that day as the scheduled judge was absent. Later, he left his lawyer’s chamber and did not return home. When he did not return home even late at night, family members grew worried and began searching for him. The victim’s younger brother, Kabirul Islam, said they were not aware of any personal conflict with anyone. “However, there might have been enmity related to some business matters,” he added. Shujan’s Gazipur district unit President Shafiqul Islam said Kamruzzaman was a good-natured and respectable person. “He used to run a business in Tongi and was involved in various social activities.” He strongly condemned the killing and demanded that those involved be brought to justice as soon as possible. Shafiqul said they are deeply saddened by his death. “We will stand by his family during this difficult time.” Shujan’s Gazipur district unit General Secretary Ifthekhar Shishir said a list of several individuals suspected to be involved in the murder has been provided to the police. Sub-Inspector Mizanur Rahman of Gazipur Sadar Police Station said it is initially suspected that the murder might have occurred due to previous enmity. The victim’s son, Koushik Zaman, filed a murder case with Gazipur Sadar Police Station. Investigation into the incident is underway, said the OC.

title: Ivy denied bail in another July uprising murder case
body: A Narayanganj court today rejected the bail petition of former Narayanganj City Corporation mayor Salina Hayat Ivy in a murder case filed over the death of Selim Mondol during the July uprising in 2024. Senior Judicial Magistrate Selina Khatun passed the order following a hearing on a bail petition this afternoon, said Inspector Abdus Samad, in charge of the court police outpost. On February 26 this year, police applied to show Ivy arrested in the murder case of Selim Mondol, 29, filed with Siddhirganj Police Station. The court approved the plea on March 2, Inspector Abdus Samad said. Speaking to reporters, Ivy’s lawyer Advocate Awlad Hossain said the investigation officer failed to present any reasonable grounds before the court. “Even then, the court denied bail. She has been shown arrested in this case only to harass her. Through such false cases, a message is being sent to the nation that harassment through false charges still exists, and the rule of law is absent in the country,” he said. The High Court on February 26 granted Ivy interim bail in five cases, but police applied to show her arrested in Selim Mondol murder case the same day, said the lawyer. She has been in jail for nine months. According to case documents, a multi-storey building in Siddhirganj was set on fire during clashes between protesters and police on July 20, 2024. Three workers, including Selim, who were doing interior decoration work at the Shimrail branch of Dutch-Bangla Bank Limited on the third floor of the building, were burned to death. Their bodies were recovered from the building three days later. Selim was a resident of Char Jagannathpur village in Kumarkhali upazila of Kushtia. His father, Wazed Ali, filed the murder case on June 6 last year.
