title: 4 DMP DCs transferred
body: Four officials of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP), holding the rank of deputy commissioner (DC), have been transferred. The transfer order was issued in a notification signed by acting DMP Commissioner Md Sarwar today. According to the order, M Tanvir Ahmed, deputy commissioner of the Ramna Traffic Division, has been posted as deputy commissioner of the Gulshan Division. Mostak Sarkar, deputy commissioner of the Lalbagh Division of the Detective Branch (DB), has been transferred to the Mirpur Division as deputy commissioner. Meanwhile, Ronak Alam, deputy commissioner of the Gulshan Division, has been posted as deputy commissioner of DB Lalbagh. Mohammad Moinul Haque, deputy commissioner of the Mirpur Division, has been transferred to the Ramna Traffic Division as deputy commissioner.

title: No confiscation of legally imported vapes: High Court
body: The High Court today directed the government not to confiscate or seize vapes lawfully imported by 41 businessmen in Bangladesh. The court also issued a rule asking authorities to explain why Section 6(Ga) of the Smoking and Tobacco Products Usage (Control) Act, 2005, which restricts use and consumption of Electronic Nicotine Delivery Systems (ENDS), should not be declared unconstitutional and void. The order was passed by a bench comprising Justice Ahmed Sohel and Justice Fatema Anwar, following a writ petition filed by 41 businessmen including Masud Uz Zaman, managing director of Vapor Cloud Ltd. Petitioners’ lawyer Barrister Shanjid Siddique argued that the provision is discriminatory, as it bans vapes, recognised globally as a harm‑reduction alternative, while allowing the manufacture and sale of traditional cigarettes, a major cause of cancer. He said this violates the equality clause under Article 27 of the Constitution. Senior Advocate Ahsanul Karim and Barrister Shanjid Siddique represented the petitioners, while Deputy Attorney General Khan Ziaur Rahman appeared for the state.

title: Idol vandalised at Patuakhali temple; case filed
body: An idol has been vandalised at a Hindu temple in Patuakhali’s Bauphal upazila, police said. The incident happened at Sri Sri Shitola-Kalimata Temple at Bhubon Sahar Kachari area under Bauphal Sadar union last night around d 9:30 pm. Bauphal Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Md Siddikur Rahman said upon receiving information, they have visited the scene. Visiting the temple today, an idol was found vandalised at a room of the temple. President of the temple’s committee, Anil Chandra Ganapati, said he reported the matter to police last night. Locals believe that some non-local miscreants might have vandalised the idol in an attempt to create an unstable situation in the area. “The temple committee’s president has filed a case against unnamed individuals in connection with the incident. An investigation is being conducted, and necessary legal action is being taken,” added the OC.

title: Jamaat activist killed in clash with BNP men in Chuadanga’s Jibannagar
body: A local Jamaat-e-Islami activist was killed, reportedly in a clash with BNP leaders and activists, at Hasadah Bazar in Jibannagar upazila of Chuadanga yesterday evening. "The deceased has been identified as Hafizur Rahman, an activist of local Jamaat-e-Islami and younger brother of Mofizur Rahman, ameer of Banka union unit of Jamaat-e-Islami," said Jibannagar Police Station Officer-in-Charge Solaiman Sheikh. "The confrontation unfolded in phases outside the gate of a Kamil madrasa from 7:30pm to 9:00pm last night. At least six people from both sides sustained injuries during the incident," he added. “One of the people critically injured in the clashes later died while being taken to Dhaka. Following a post-mortem at Chuadanga 250-bed General Hospital, the body was handed over to the family," Chuadanga Superintendent of Police Mohammad Monirul Islam told The Daily Star. Jibannagar Upazila Nirbahi Officer Md Ashraful Alam Rasel said tension remained high in the area. "Police, army, and other law enforcement personnel visited the scene at night. An application has been submitted to the deputy commissioner requesting additional forces," he added. According to police and locals, the clash erupted from an earlier attack on Mehdi Hasan, convener of Hasadah union Swechchhasebak Dal, in Sutia village on February 13. Police rescued Hasan and admitted him to the upazila health complex. Yesterday evening, Jamaat leaders Mofizur Rahman and Hafizur Rahman were travelling with a few activists to the party office at Hasadah Bazar on motorcycles when they were obstructed in front of the Kamil madrasa by Mehdi Hasan, who allegedly assaulted them. In the ensuing retaliation, at least six people were injured, they added. Jibannagar upazila BNP President Anwar Hossain Khan held Jamaat responsible for the incident, claiming that the party had been repeatedly attacking BNP leaders and activists since the election. He alleged that Jamaat men had brutally assaulted the Swechchhasebak Dal leader before handing him over to police in an injured condition, which led to yesterday evening's clash. Upazila Jamaat Ameer Maulana Sazedur Rahman countered that Jamaat leaders and activists were innocent and had been attacked with locally made weapons. Chuadanga-2 constituency lawmaker and Ameer of district Jamaat-e-Islami, Md Ruhul Amin, told The Daily Star that it was not a clash but an attack. He said a young man from Sutia village had gone to Hasadah Bazar yesterday to buy iftar items. There, BNP activists assaulted him. Later, our men went to the spot and asked the person who had beaten him to come forward for a mutual settlement. They were standing beside the market at the time. Then 20 to 25 men arrived on motorcycles and launched a sudden attack. He said one activist was killed and three others were in critical condition. They have been admitted to Chuadanga Sadar Hospital. A total of five of our men were injured in the attack. We demand a fair investigation and justice over the incident.

title: Roommate killed Obaidullah over argument, dismembered body across Dhaka: Police
body: A quarrel over a loud phone conversation allegedly led to the murder of Md Obaidullah by his roommate. His dismembered body parts were later recovered from at least four locations across Dhaka, police said. The information was disclosed at a press conference at the DMP Media Centre on Minto Road by Harun-or-Rashid, deputy commissioner of the Motijheel Division of Dhaka Metropolitan Police. “The two had been sharing a flat on Jasimuddin Road in Kamalapur for the past three months. On the night of February 27, an altercation took place, which ultimately led to the murder,” he said. Obaidullah, a marketing official at Gonoshasthaya Homeo, was allegedly killed by Shahin Alam, who works at Hirajheel Hotel in Motijheel. Shahin has been detained in connection with the murder. According to police, the argument began after Shahin returned home late from work. Obaidullah had sent him out to buy cigarettes and later food. Displeased, Shahin became angered after Obaidullah allegedly ate the food alone. Later at night, Obaidullah was speaking loudly on the phone. Shahin, who was tired, asked him to lower his voice. An argument followed, during which Obaidullah allegedly verbally abused Shahin and his parents, Harun said. Quoting the suspect, the DC said that when Obaidullah went to the bathroom to wash clothes, Shahin attacked him from behind with a machete, killing him on the spot. “To avoid detection, he dismembered the body and disposed of the parts at different locations. Black polythene bags collected from Shahin’s workplace were reportedly used to carry the body parts, and some were transported in a CNG auto-rickshaw under the pretext of ‘toxic chemicals’, ” the police official said. Police recovered a hand in front of Ananda Community Centre in Naya Paltan, two legs near Baitul Mukarram Mosque, a hand from Kamalapur railway station, and the head from a garbage container near Kamalapur, later taken to Jatrabari. Another part was found near Aminbazar bridge, and efforts continue to locate remaining parts. Shahin was identified through CCTV footage showing a young man riding a bicycle near one of the dumping sites. Police recovered the bicycle and the machete allegedly used in the crime from his residence, the DC said. During initial interrogation, Shahin reportedly confessed to the killing. Investigators are also examining his claim that the victim had previously made “immoral proposals” to him.

title: Seven on 8-day remand in Narsingdi teenage girl rape and murder case
body: A court in Narsingdi today granted an eight-day remand for seven accused in connection with the gang rape and murder of a 15-year-old girl. The Narsingdi District Judge Court issued the order without any lawyers representing the accused during the hearing. Sub-Inspector Md Omar Kaiyum of Madhabdi Police Station, the investigation officer of the case, said the police had sought a 10-day remand but the court grants eight days. “Seven accused, including the prime suspect Nur Mohammad alias Nura (28), have been placed under remand,” he added. The victim was reportedly abducted on Wednesday night from Mahishasura area by a group of four to five people, led by Nur Mohammad, in front of her father. Her body was found the following morning in a mustard field in Dorikandi area, with an orna wrapped around her neck. A case was filed by the victim’s mother on Thursday night, naming nine individuals. Police have arrested seven of them in a three-day operation. Former Union Parishad member and Mahishasura Union BNP vice-president Ahmed Ali Dewan has been expelled from the party over alleged involvement in the case. According to the First Information Report, the accused initially tried to suppress the incident and later allegedly threatened the victim’s family, demanding she leave the village. The prime accused, Nura, was arrested from Gazipur on Friday night, said Additional Superintendent of Police Anwar Hossain Shamim. He added that Nura was attempting to flee to India via the Dinajpur border. The other arrested men are Ebadullah, 38, Hazrat Ali, 40, Gaffar, 37, Ahmed Ali alias Ahmed Dewan, 65, Md Imran Dewan, 32, and Md Ayub, 30, all residents of Mahishasura Union.

title: Key suspect arrested over Pabna double murder; case handed to DB
body: Police last night arrested a key suspect in connection with the murder of a woman and her granddaughter at a village in Pabna's Ishwardi upazila. The arrestee was identified as Md Shariful Islam, a local resident, said Md Rashidul Hasan, officer-in-charge of Pabna Detective Branch (DB) of police. “We have identified several clues regarding this killing and are working to arrest those responsible,” the DB official said, adding that details would be disclosed at a press conference. The incident occurred Friday night in Bhabanipur Uttarpara village. Yesterday morning, neighbours found the blood-stained body of Sufia Begum in her courtyard. When her granddaughter Jamila went missing, locals launched a search and later found her body in a mustard field near the house. Speaking to journalists, Jamila’s mother Shirina alleged that a local youth had been stalking her daughter. “Her father had gone to Dhaka, and the criminals took that opportunity to carry out the attack,” she said, demanding punishment for those responsible. Md Mominuzzaman, officer-in-charge of Ishwardi Police Station, said the attackers entered the house late at night, killed the elderly woman, and then took the granddaughter away. Morjina Khatun, daughter of the deceased Sufia Begum, filed the case on Friday night, the OC added. Additional Superintendent of Police Pronob Kumar said the case has been formally transferred to the DB and that multiple agencies are working to arrest those responsible. Dr Sharmin Sobnom, a forensic physician at Pabna Medical College and Hospital, said samples have been collected for chemical analysis. She declined to comment on the possibility of sexual assault until the final report is prepared.

title: Journalist assaulted for 'inquiring about alleged gambling den' in Shariatpur
body: A journalist was assaulted in Gosairhat upazila of Shariatpur reportedly for collecting information about a gambling and drug operation. He was hospitalised after the attack, and a criminal case has been filed over the incident. Nayan Das, Shariatpur correspondent of the online news portal Dhaka Post, claimed he was attacked on Thursday afternoon in Nagerpara Bazar area while travelling to Shariatpur town on professional duties. “Nayan Das lodged a complaint naming Saidul Akon, Monir Jamaddar, Nazrul Kazi and Likhon Kazi, along with several unidentified individuals on Friday. The complaint was formally recorded as a case on Saturday,” Gosairhat Police Station Officer-in-Charge Azizul told The Daily last night. Quoting the case statement, the OC said that following allegations from locals about ongoing drug and gambling activities in Molongchara, Nayan Das and several other journalists visited the area on February 23 and captured photographs and video footage. Sensing the presence of journalists, those involved fled the scene. Subsequently, on Thursday, several members of the alleged group intercepted Nayan Das at Nagerpara Bazar and assaulted him. Locals later rescued and took him to Gosairhat upazila Health Complex, police said, adding that efforts are underway to arrest the accused. Speaking to The Daily Star, Nayan Das said acting on the information from locals, he went to the location with local journalists Shahed Ahmed Babu and Hasan Sikdar, where they recorded video footage and took photographs of the alleged activities. Upon seeing them, the gamblers and drug peddlers fled, he said. While passing through Nagerpara Bazar on Thursday, he was attacked by Saidul Akon, Monir Jamaddar, Nazrul Kazi and Likhon Kazi, along with several unidentified associates allegedly involved in gambling and drug activities, he said. They struck him with sticks on different parts of his body, punched him in the head and snatched his camera and mobile phone. Locals later rescued him and took him to hospital, he added. The statements of the accused could not be obtained as they could not be contacted. Dr Hafizur Rahman Mia, health and family planning officer of Gosairhat upazila, said a patient named Nayan Das was admitted with visible injuries to his shoulder, head and several other parts of his body, and has been hospitalised for treatment. “Attacks on journalists are increasing at an alarming rate across the country. Even two days after the incident, no arrests have been made, which raises concerns,” Mohammad Rajib Hossain, general secretary of the Shariatpur Online Journalists Association, told The Daily Star. Failure to swiftly bring the perpetrators to justice would encourage the recurrence of such incidents, he added.

title: BNP man beaten to death ‘by rivals’
body: A BNP activist was beaten to death allegedly by supporters of a rival faction in Charghat upazila of Rajshahi on Friday night. The deceased was Ershad Ali, 65, a Yusufpur union BNP member and follower of Rajshahi-6 lawmaker Abu Sayeed Chand, said locals. He was attacked around 9:30pm in Sipaipara village. Charghat Police Station Sub-inspector Sirajul Islam said the accused are followers of Anwar Hossain Uzzal, a former district BNP vice-president who had sought the party nomination for the same constituency. Tension flared after Juma prayers over a disagreement on who would be chief guest at a gathering -- Uzzal or MP Chand. Later, while returning home after Taraweeh, Ershad was attacked by several men who beat him with sticks, killing him. Uzzal could not be contacted for comments. The body was sent to Rajshahi Medical College morgue. Police are trying to arrest the accused, who fled after the incident.

title: Man killed over mosque fund dispute
body: A man was killed in a clash between two groups over mosque funds in Chhatak upazila of Sunamganj yesterday. The deceased is Fazal Miah, 50, of Puran Noapara village. Mizanur Rahman, officer-in-charge of Chhatak Police Station, confirmed the incident and said Fazal’s body was sent to Sunamganj District Hospital for autopsy. He said there had been a longstanding dispute between Mashuk Miah and Fazal over the mosque management committee. Around noon, the two became involved in an altercation over the mosque funds, which led to a clash between their supporters using local weapons. At one stage, Fazal was critically injured and died on the way to hospital, the OC said.

title: Woman, teen granddaughter killed in Pabna
body: An elderly woman and her teenage granddaughter were allegedly killed by unidentified assailants in Bhabanipur village of Ishwardi upazila, Pabna, in the early hours of yesterday. Police recovered the bodies of Sufia Begum Sufi, 70, and Jamila Khatun, 16, and sent them to the morgue of Pabna General Hospital for autopsy, said Md Mominuzzaman, officer-in-charge of Ishwardi Police Station. Sufia was found dead inside their home, while Jamila’s body was discovered in a field about 500 metres away, he said. At the time of the incident, no other family members were present. Jamila lived with her father, Joynal Khan, and grandmother, while her mother, Shirina Begum, resides separately. Neighbours told The Daily Star they went to the house after hearing a noise and found Sufia’s body. Jamila was later found in the nearby field. Speaking to journalists, Shirina alleged that a local youth had been stalking her daughter. “Her father had gone to Dhaka, and the criminals took that opportunity to carry out the attack,” she said, demanding exemplary punishment for those responsible. The OC said the attackers entered the house late at night, killed the elderly woman, and then took the granddaughter away. Her body was later found in the field. In reply to a query, he said that police were awaiting the autopsy report to determine whether Jamila had been sexually assaulted. “We are investigating the incident and trying to arrest those involved,” he said, adding that the process to file a case over the incident was underway. Pabna’s Superintendent of Police, Md Anwar Jahid, along with other senior officers, visited the scene. “Police are working to identify the criminals. The investigation is being conducted from multiple angles,” Anwar told journalists.

title: Body parts of man recovered from different Dhaka areas
body: Police have identified the man whose severed body parts were found scattered across different areas of the capital. The victim was Md Obaidullah, 29, a marketing officer at Gonoshasthya Homeo, a homeopathy clinic at Purana Paltan. He was originally from Narsingdi. Police recovered two severed hands from between gates 1 and 4 of the National Stadium in Gulistan and a leg from in front of the Scout Bhaban in Kakrail early Friday. The other severed leg was found in the Kamalapur Railway Station area yesterday noon. Mohammad Harun-or-Rashid, deputy commissioner (Motijheel division) of Dhaka Metropolitan Police, said the victim was identified through fingerprint analysis. Until 8:00pm yesterday, police were searching for the remaining body parts. “We have spoken to his family about filing a case,” Harun said. “We are analysing CCTV footage to identify the killers and the motive.” He said, alongside DMP, the Detective Branch and other agencies are also investigating the case. Robin, a colleague of the victim, said, “Our office was closed for the last three days. We have no idea what happened. We only learned about it when DB officials visited our office in the morning.” The recovered body parts have been sent to the Dhaka Medical College morgue.

title: Attacks on Star, Prothom Alo: Home minister orders probe report within two months
body: The unprecedented attacks on Prothom Alo and The Daily Star have tarnished Bangladesh’s reputation globally, Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed said yesterday. Speaking to reporters after visiting “Alo” (Light), an exhibition portraying Prothom Alo’s endeavour to rise from the ruins, at the newspaper’s charred building yesterday afternoon, he also said he has directed police to submit charge sheets over the attacks on the newspaper offices within two months following a fair investigation. Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman, Information Minister Zahir Uddin Swapan, prime minister’s advisers Zahed Ur Rahman and Mahdi Amin, and National Citizen Party leader Sarjis Alam also visited the exhibition, in the presence of Transcom Group Chief Executive Officer Simeen Rahman and Prothom Alo Editor Matiur Rahman. Afterwards, Salahuddin Ahmed and Khalilur Rahman visited the torched office of The Daily Star on the capital’s Kazi Nazrul Islam Avenue. The premises were vandalised and set on fire, trapping 28 journalists and staffers inside at the time. On the night of December 18, 2025, coordinated mobs attacked and set fire to the offices of two of Bangladesh’s leading newspapers and the cultural institution Chhayanaut in Dhaka. The following evening, the central office of Udichi Shilpigosthi, another cultural organisation, was also attacked and burned. Outside the Prothom Alo office in the capital’s Karwan Bazar, Salahuddin further told reporters, “With the attacks, a message went to the world that fanatic forces were in a strong position in Bangladesh and could attack any media outlet at will. Our image was tarnished, and we were ashamed. “By ensuring exemplary punishment, we want to send an opposite message to the world -- that extremist and fanatic forces cannot hold back the progress of Bangladesh.” He added, “We [the BNP] strongly condemned the attacks when they occurred. But now, as I am in charge of the home ministry, the Prothom Alo family and the community of journalists, writers, intellectuals and litterateurs all have one demand -- a proper investigation.” The home minister said the Detective Branch of police is currently probing the incidents and has been instructed to conduct the investigation fairly before submitting the charge sheets within two months. “Our duty is to ensure a fair investigation, while the judiciary will carry out the trials in the cases linked to the attacks.” Salahuddin, who is also a standing committee member of the ruling BNP, sought public cooperation to ensure justice and prevent the recurrence of such heinous acts. About the exhibition, he said it felt like a “living museum”. “They [Prothom Alo] have tried to show how one can rise from the ruins. What we have seen and learned is that communal extremist forces may try to pull back the rope of progress, but history shows they have never succeeded.” Referring to the BNP’s election manifesto, he said, “In our manifesto, we said we want an independent media and will ensure full freedom of the media. We also believe in the full independence of the judiciary and will establish that as well.” Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman termed the attacks on Prothom Alo and The Daily Star antithetical to a civilised society. “I had to face questions from the diplomatic community at home and abroad due to this attack. Our heads have bowed down in shame internationally.” He said no government can shirk responsibility for such attacks and that this government will ensure a proper trial and exemplary punishment. “The attacks on Prothom Alo and The Daily Star were something we had never seen before. It was an attack on the independent media. Intimidation, arson, destruction of lives and property, and vandalism cannot be part of a civilised society.” Referring to the BNP’s mandate, the foreign minister said, “This mandate is the strongest in Bangladesh’s history. From the government’s side, we will keep our word.” Expressing sympathy for the Prothom Alo and The Daily Star families, he said he hoped they would rebuild their institutions from the rubble and ashes and resume their work as truly independent media in Bangladesh. Information and Broadcasting Minister Zahir Uddin Swapan reaffirmed the government’s commitment to ensuring media freedom, describing any attack on the press as an attack on civilisation itself. “We are pledge-bound to protect press freedom. A close look at the trail of destruction suggests that an anti-civilisation mindset was at work.” Adviser Zahed Ur Rahman said a certain quarter had “manufactured consent” over a long period to carry out the attack. “We have ousted Sheikh Hasina’s autocracy and fascism. We will not allow fascism to be re-established here. We did not fight to have newspapers shut down; we fought to build a democratic Bangladesh.” Later, the US Ambassador to Bangladesh Brent T Christensen also visited the exhibition at the Prothom Alo office, as did politicians, writers, journalists, artists and representatives of civil society. During his visit to The Daily Star, the home minister, accompanied by the newspaper’s Editor and Publisher Mahfuz Anam, examined the heavily damaged ground, first and second floors before visiting the newsroom. DMP Acting Commissioner Md Sarwar, Deputy Commissioner (Tejgaon Division) Ibne Mizan, DB Chief Shafiqul Islam, along with other police officials, also visited both newspaper offices. Following the twin attacks on the two dailies on December 18, two cases were filed -- one by Prothom Alo and one by The Daily Star -- on December 22. So far, 37 people have been arrested. The court set March 8 for the probe report in The Daily Star case and March 5 in the Prothom Alo case.

title: 7 held over rape, abduction and murder of teen
body: Seven people have so far been arrested in connection with the abduction, rape and killing of a teenage girl in Narsingdi’s Madhabdi upazila of Narsingdi. The prime accused, Nur Mohammad, 28, locally known as Nura, was arrested from Gazipur, and Hazrat Ali, 40, from Mymensingh on Friday night. The rest were arrested on throughout Thursday and Friday, said police. All the arrestees were sent to jail through the courts. Police sought a 10-day remand for each of the accused, said Narsingdi Superintendent of Police Md Abdullah-Al-Faruk. “The hearing on the remand petitions will be held tomorrow [today],” he told reporters at press conferencea press conference at his office yesterday. Four of the arrestees were directly involved in the rape, he said, adding that the other three allegedly tried to hush up the incident through a local arbitration , he said. Additional SP Anwar Hossain Shamim said Nur was planning to flee from Bangladeshthe country illegally to avoid arrest. On Thursday morning, police recovered the body of the 15-year-old, Amena Akter, from a cropland in the upazila. There was a scarf wrapped around the neck. The victim’s mother, Fahima Begum, filed a case with Madhabdi Police Station on Thursday night. Earlier, the girl’s father, Ashraf Ali, alleged that Nurul and four to five associates abducted her on her way home and raped her. “After that, Nur kept stalking my daughter. Feeling insecure, we decided to send her to a safer place,” he said, adding that on Wednesday night, he was taking his daughter to a relative’s house when Nurul and his associates intercepted them around 10:00pm in Boroitala area and abducted her. Meanwhile, Ahmed Ali Dewan, who was earlier arrested in the case, was expelled from his position as vice president of Mahishashur union BNP on Friday. Amena’s family claimed they went to Ahmad Ali Dewan, who was a former member of the union parishad, to seek justice when the rape incident took place. “Then, he arranged a Salish [social arbitration] to settle the issue. But he did not take any action against the rapists. Instead, he advocated for the rapists and shifted the blame on my daughter. He asked us to leave the area by March 1,” Fahima told journalists yesterday. She further alleged, “Ahmad Ali made the decision after taking a Tk 8,000 bribe from the rapists. We were also threatened in many ways to suppress the incident.” Ashraf said, “We rejected the decision and attempted to file a complaint with police. But we were threatened with death.” Ahmed Ali denied mediating any arbitration and said he was not home when the family came to see him that night. About the allegation, SP Faruk said it was being investigated.

title: JU suspends academic certificates of ex-student over rape allegations
body: Jahangirnagar University (JU) has suspended the academic certificates of a former student following allegations that the person lured a female student to a house near the campus, confined her and raped her. The development was confirmed in a press release signed by JU’s acting director of public relations Mohammad Mohiuddin on Saturday night. A six-member probe committee has also been formed to investigate the incident. The accused, SM Tarikul Islam, was a student of the 44th batch of the Institute of Information Technology (IIT). According to the release, on February 24 around 6:00pm, a student of the Public Administration department was allegedly threatened and forcibly taken to a residence in Islamnagar area, adjacent to the campus. There, her hands, legs and mouth were tied, and she was subjected to physical and mental torture, including rape. To investigate the allegations and submit a report with recommendations, the university formed a six-member committee headed by Prof Mohammad Mafruhi Sattar, dean of the Faculty of Biological Sciences, the release added. The victim filed a case against the accused, who she was in a relationship with, with Ashulia Police Station on Wednesday.

title: Masked gunmen open fire on ex-MP Mujibur’s house in Ctg
body: Masked criminals opened fire, targeting the residence of Mujibur Rahman, owner of Chattogram-based Smart Group, in the port city today, demanding crores of taka in extortion. According to police, the incident took place around 6:30am in the Chandannpura area under Chawkbazar Police Station. Mujibur was an Awami League lawmaker from the Chattogram-16 constituency before the fall of Hasina government on August 5, 2024. This is the second gunfire attack on his house, triggering huge panic among locals in the area. No casualties were reported, though he and other family members were inside at the time. Following the attack, senior officials of the city police visited the scene. Earlier, on January 2, his house was attacked in a similar style for extortion. Confirming the matter, Deputy Commissioner (South) of Chattogram Metropolitan Police (CMP) Hossain Kabir Bhuiya, told journalists, “The shots were fired from the back of the house to intimidate him over extortion. This time, attackers arrived in a private car and on motorcycles, fired from the rear end of the house, and fled shortly.” “We suspect all the attackers are followers of terrorist Boro Sazzad. A similar attack was carried out on his house earlier on January 2. We are trying to identify them,” he said. CCTV footage shows three masked men approaching from behind the house. One was carrying a pistol, another an SMG, and the third had a shotgun. The three began firing indiscriminately at the house. Approximately 15 rounds were fired from the three weapons. Another armed individual was seen standing nearby before they fled. Mujibur Rahman told The Daily Star, “Five brothers and our families live here. After completing Fajr prayers, we were all asleep when the attack happened behind the building. Armed police were stationed in front of the house at the time. We also had four personal gunmen. The attack took place despite their presence. I later called 999 for additional support.” He also said the criminals had called him earlier. After he blocked their numbers, they phoned his elder brother, Mostafizur Rahman, chairman of Smart Group, several times for extortion. From one foreign number, a caller identified himself as Sazzad, and from another as Emon. As Mostafizur did not respond to the calls, a message was later sent to his mobile phone that read, “Wait and see,” Mujibur added. “We are living in fear. Following the first incident, we stopped going outside alone without a reason. Around 35,000 people work in our companies. If we are not allowed to operate our business, we will shut down. If the government cannot ensure our security, we will have no option but to leave the country to save our lives,” he said. Police officials said that for more than two decades, Sazzad Ali has been controlling an extensive criminal network in the city and district from abroad. He is on Interpol’s "most wanted" list under the name Sazzad Hossain Khan. Police say that Sazzad’s followers open fire if extortion demands are not met. More than 500,000 people across five police station areas -- Chandgaon, Bayezid Bostami, Panchlaish, Hathazari, and Raozan -- live in fear due to his gang. Since August 5 last year, his followers have been named in 10 murder cases in the district, including double-murder incidents. At times, they allegedly kill rivals to maintain dominance, and at other times act as hired killers. Sazzad Ali Khan, son of contractor Abdul Gani from the Chalitatoly area, first became known in the criminal underworld in 1999 after the murder of Councillor Liaqat Ali Khan. Although he was acquitted due to a lack of witness, a new chapter in the city’s crime world began with him at that time. On July 12, 2000, eight people -- including six leaders and activists of Chhatra League -- were killed in a burst-fire attack in Bahaddarhat. Police and various agencies claim Sazzad led the incident, which became known as the “Eight Murder” case. In October of the same year, he was arrested with an AK-47 rifle. After securing bail, he left the country in 2004 and has since controlled his group from abroad. However, he was acquitted in the “Eight Murder” case later. Initially, the group was formed with Nur Nabi Maxon, Sarwar Hossain, Akbar Hossain, and Chhoto Sazzad. Maxon later died in India, and Sarwar left the group. On November 5 2025, Sarwar was shot dead during an election campaign of a BNP candidate in Bayezid Bostami. Boro Sazzad was blamed for the killing. Since 2015, the helm of the gang in Chattogram was taken over by Chhoto Sazzad, also known as Sazzad Hossain, who is now behind the bar. Police say that last year, Akbar Hossain, also known as Dakaiya Akbar, was shot dead at Patenga Sea Beach due to internal conflict and for criticising both Boro and Chhoto Sazzad. According to police, at least 50 shooters and associates are active in Boro Sazzad’s group.

title: Home minister promises action over attacks on Prothom Alo, Daily Star
body: The unprecedented attacks on Prothom Alo and The Daily Star tarnished Bangladesh's reputation globally, Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed said today. After visiting “Alo” (Light), an exhibition at Prothom Alo’s office highlighting the newspaper’s recovery from the December 18 attack, Salahuddin said he has directed the Detective Branch (DB) to complete its investigation and submit a charge sheet. “The responsibility of ensuring a fair investigation lies with us. The Detective Branch has been instructed to finish the probe within the next two months, after which the judicial process will begin,” he told reporters at around 4:30pm. Condemning the incident, he added: “We are ashamed. It sent a message to the world that newspapers in Bangladesh can be attacked at will, and that anti-progressive, communal, and extremist forces are thriving here.” He said the government would send a counter-message to the international community by ensuring an “exemplary trial” for the attackers, reiterating its commitment to safeguarding full press freedom in line with its election manifesto. Foreign Minister Dr Khalilur Rahman, who accompanied the home minister, described the attacks on Prothom Alo and The Daily Star as “antithetical to a civilised society”. “I had to face questions from the local diplomatic community and abroad due to this attack. Our heads have bowed down in shame internationally,” he said. “Today, we can pledge that such incidents will not happen again,” he added, expressing hope that the newspapers would recover strongly from the damage. Prime Minister’s Adviser Jahed Ur Rahman said a “certain quarter” had “manufactured consent” over a long period to carry out the attack. “We have ousted Sheikh Hasina’s autocracy and fascism. We will not allow fascism to be re-established here. We did not fight to shut down newspapers. Rather, we fought to build a democratic Bangladesh,” he said. Senior officials from the Dhaka Metropolitan Police and the Detective Branch, along with Transcom Group Chief Executive Simeen Rahman, were present during the visit.

title: Elderly woman, teenage granddaughter found murdered in Pabna
body: An elderly woman and her teenage granddaughter were found murdered at Bhabanipur village in Ishwardi upazila in Pabna early today. The deceased -- Sufia Begum Sufi, 70, and her granddaughter Jamila Khatun, 16, -- both lived in the same house, said Md Mominuzzaman, officer-in-charge of Ishwardi Police Station. Police recovered the bodies and sent them to the Pabna General Hospital morgue for autopsy. The OC said, “Assailants entered the house late at night and killed the elderly woman. They then abducted the granddaughter. Her body was later found in a nearby field, about 500 metres away, ” the OC said. He said police were investigating whether the girl had been sexually assaulted before being killed, adding that this could only be confirmed after the autopsy report. Police are investigating the incident and trying to arrest those involved, the OC added.

title: Narsingdi rape, murder: Seven including prime suspect sent to jail
body: Seven people, including the prime accused, have been sent to jail over the abduction, gang rape and subsequent murder of a 15-year-old girl in Narsingdi’s Madhabdi. Police sought a 10-day remand for each of the accused. The hearing on the remand petitions will be held tomorrow, Abdullah Al-Faruk, superintendent of police (SP) of Narsingdi, told a press conference at his office this afternoon. Of the nine accused named in the case, seven people -- former Mahishashur Union member Ahmad Ali Dewan, 65; his son Imran Dewan, 25; Mohammad Ayub, 40, a cousin of prime accused Nura; Ebaidullah, 38; Abdul Gaffar, 40, of Hossain Bazar; and Hazrat Ali -- have been arrested so far. Anwar Hossain Shamim, additional superintendent of police (Narsingdi Sadar Circle), told The Daily Star this morning that Nura had planned to flee through the northern border district of Dinajpur. “Upon sensing the presence of law enforcers, Nura tried to escape,” he said. Md Kamal Hossain, officer-in-charge of Madhabdi Police Station, said four of those arrested were directly involved in the rape, while the remaining three allegedly tried to hush up the incident through a local arbitration. Meanwhile, Ahmad Ali Dewan, vice-president of Mahishashur Union unit of BNP and a former Ward No. 9 member, was expelled from the party last night through a press release following allegations of involvement in the crime. The victim’s mother, Fahima Begum, filed a case with Madhabdi Police Station on Thursday night, naming nine accused, said Rezaul Karim Mallik, deputy inspector general (DIG) of the Dhaka Range. He spoke to journalists at the police station after visiting the crime scene. According to the case statement, several of the accused attempted to suppress the rape allegation after the incident. The family alleged that the accused threatened them and instructed the girl to leave the village. The SP said the girl had been gang-raped around 15 days before the killing. On February 25 at about 9:30pm, the accused allegedly intercepted Amena Akter and her father, Ashraf, at Boroitala in Kotowalirchar and forcibly took her away. Police recovered the body of Amena, 15, from a cropland in Madhabdi on Thursday morning. An autopsy was conducted at Narsingdi Sadar Hospital, said Resident Medical Officer Dr Farida Gulshanara Kabir. “The victim was strangled to death with an orna wrapped around her neck. There are also signs indicating that she was raped before the murder,” she told The Daily Star. The body was handed over to the family and buried later in the afternoon. The family has been placed under police protection over security concerns, the OC added. Her parents alleged that she was abducted in front of her father on Wednesday night and later killed by a group of stalkers who had gang-raped her around two weeks earlier.

title: Cancel bails of Ivy, Bodi, other AL leaders
body: Jamaat-e-Islami has expressed deep concern over the granting of bail to Awami League leaders arrested in connection with the July killings and the reopening of party offices despite a ban on its activities. In a statement yesterday, the party’s Secretary General Mia Golam Porwar alleged that leaders and activists of AL and the “fascist Hasina government” carried out indiscriminate killings of students and civilians during the July uprising. He claimed that those directly involved in the killings are being granted bail one after another, while AL offices are reopening in different parts of the country despite the ban. Porwar said there are fears that anti-state activities could be reorganised from those offices, calling the developments an ominous sign for democracy. He said former Narayanganj City Corporation mayor Selina Hayat Ivy, whom he accused of being active in suppressing the July uprising, has been granted six months’ interim bail. On the same day, former AL lawmaker Abdur Rahman Bodi was also granted bail. He further alleged that AL leaders and activists are being released on bail in large numbers across different districts. He demanded immediate justice over the killings, warning that those released on bail could again become involved in violence, for which the government would bear responsibility. Porwar also claimed that some individuals released on bail have been accused of looting and organised extortion in different areas and demanded their arrest and trial. Porwar demanded that the bail of Bodi, Ivy, and other AL leaders be cancelled and that they be brought to trial quickly. He also urged an investigation into the reopening of AL offices and necessary measures to stop such activities, warning that otherwise a mass resistance involving students and the public would be built.

title: Man beaten to death, brother hurt ‘by neighbours’
body: A man was beaten to death and his brother injured allegedly by their neighbours following a dispute over setting up a clothesline in Faridpur yesterday morning. The deceased was identified as Jewel Ahmed, 40. His younger brother, Sohel Ahmed, 24, was admitted to Faridpur Medical College Hospital. Locals said one Md Sarfaraz, 55, who earns a living by making and selling paper bags, lived in Goalchamot Mollah Bari Road area under Sadar upazila with his wife Moni Begum and sons Shahriyar, 22, and Rifat. Moni Begum attempted to fix a bamboo pole and string a clothesline along Jewel’s boundary, leading to an altercation. Witness Sajib Sheikh said Sarfaraz, his sons, and two of his employees broke into Jewel’s house and beat him and Sohel. Jewel was declared dead at the hospital. Faridpur Kotwali Police Station Officer-in-Charge Md Shahidul Islam said Sarfaraz and Moni Begum were detained.

title: 3 DB men attacked in Manikganj; 9 held
body: Three members of Manikganj district Detective Branch (DB) of police, including a sub-inspector, were injured in an attack while conducting an anti-drug operation in the district’s Singair upazila on Thursday. Police arrested nine people in connection with the incident as of last evening. Singair Police Station OC Mazharul Islam said a DB team, led by SI Md Anwar Hossain, went on an operation in Char Ulail village under Dhalla union on Thursday afternoon. During the drive, one Md Lablu alias Labu Mia, 45, was arrested with 20 pieces of yaba pills. Three of the team were injured as they were attacked by Lablu’s relatives and some locals on their way back, accompanying Lablu. The injured are SI Anwar Hossain, constables Mirza Rezaul Karim and Hasan Ali. The two constables are currently undergoing treatment at hospital, while the sub-inspector received first aid. At that time, the attackers snatched Lablu, added the OC. SI Anwar filed two cases with Singair Police Station today -- one under the Narcotics Control Act, naming Lablu as an accused, and another against 19 named individuals along with 15 to 20 unidentified individuals. Those who have been arrested are Purnima Begum, 20; Shabana, 26; Jahanara, 23; Azimuddin, 65; Aminur, 27; Antar, 20; Mou Akhtar, 19; Asma Begum, 45; and Abdur Rouf alias Jewel, 26. Preliminary evidence suggests that the arrested individuals were involved in the attack. Efforts are underway to arrest the remaining accused, the OC said. The investigation officer of the case, Md Rezaul Karim, said all of the arrested have directly participated in the attack. However, relatives of the arrested individuals said the real attackers have fled, and those who have been arrested are innocent. Further legal action will be taken based on the investigation, added the OC.

title: 5 held over Narsingdi girl rape, murder
body: Five people have been arrested in connection with the abduction and killing of a teenage girl in Madhabdi upazila of Narsingdi, in what police say was an attempt to suppress a rape incident. The victim’s mother, Fahima Begum, filed a case with Madhabdi Police Station on Thursday night, naming nine accused, said Rezaul Karim Mallik, deputy inspector general (DIG) of the Dhaka Range. He spoke to journalists at the police station yesterday noon after visiting the crime scene. The arrestees are former member of Mahishashur union Ahmad Ali Dewan, 65; his son Imran Dewan, 25; Mohammad Ayub, 40, a cousin of prime accused Nurul; Ebaidullah, 38; and Abdul Gaffar, 40, of Hossain Bazar area. According to the DIG, two of them are directly accused in the rape, while the other three allegedly acted as local arbitrators in an effort to hush up the incident through a so-called social arbitration. The prime accused, Nurul, remains at large, and drives are underway to arrest the remaining suspects. Local MP Khayrul Kabir Khokon, who accompanied the DIG during the visit, told reporters that political identity would not shield anyone. “Criminals must face the law. There will be zero tolerance,” he said, urging lawyers not to assist those accused in what he termed a “heinous and inhuman” crime. An autopsy was conducted at Narsingdi Sadar Hospital yesterday, said Resident Medical Officer Dr Farida Gulshanara Kabir. “The victim was strangled to death with an orna (scarf) wrapped around her neck. There are also signs indicating that she was raped before the murder,” she told The Daily Star. The five arrestees were sent to jail by a court yesterday, said Md Kamal Hossain, officer-in-charge of Madhabdi Police Station. Police have sought a 10-day remand for each of them; the hearing is scheduled for Sunday. The body was handed over to the family and buried later in the afternoon. The family has been placed under police protection over security concerns, the OC added. Police recovered the body of the 15-year-old, Amena Akter, from a cropland in Madhabdi on Thursday morning. Her parents alleged that she was abducted in front of her father on Wednesday night and later killed by a group of stalkers who had gang-raped her around two weeks earlier. Rights groups and student organisations have condemned the killing and demanded exemplary punishment. Manusher Jonno Foundation (MJF) expressed deep anger and concern in a statement yesterday, calling for justice and accountability. The incident once again shows that women and children remain gravely unsafe, it said. Citing data from Ain o Salish Kendra, MJF noted that 35 children were subjected to various forms of violence and abuse and 25 were killed last month, nearly one child falling victim each day. It urged the newly elected government to fulfil its pledge to ensure justice and protect women and children, and to guarantee immediate security for the victim’s family. In a separate statement, Human Rights Support Society (HRSS) termed the incident a “grave breach” of human rights. Referring to its own data, the organisation said 2,047 women and girls faced violence in 2023, including 828 rape victims, of whom 474 were children. It demanded a prompt, transparent investigation and trial under the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act. Meanwhile, Dhaka University Central Students’ Union and Jagannath University Central Students’ Union staged separate protests on their campuses yesterday, calling for exemplary punishment for those responsible.

title: Prime accused arrested over murder of teenage girl in Narsingdi
body: Two people, including the prime accused in the rape and murder of a teenage girl in Narsingdi's Madhabdi, has been arrested. The main accused, Nurul, alias Nura, was arrested from Mawna in Gazipur, and another accused, Hazrat Ali, was apprehended from Gouripur in Mymensingh, said police. Narsingdi Superintendent of Police Md Abdullah Al Faruq said they were arrested around 9:00pm on Friday. Meanwhile, Ahmed Ali Dewan, who was earlier arrested in the case, has been expelled from his position as vice president of the union unit of BNP. In an official letter, signed by Sadar Upazila BNP President Abu Saleh Chowdhury and General Secretary Md. Iqbal Hossain, the party suspended him around 10:00pm on Friday. Md Iqbal confirmed the information to The Daily Star. Earlier on Friday afternoon, Deputy Inspector General (DIG) of Dhaka Range Rezaul Karim Mallick informed the media that five accused had been arrested in connection with the case. With these latest arrests, police have now detained seven out of the nine accused in the teenage girl’s murder case. According to the case statement, the victim was abducted, raped and murdered on February 25. The next day, her body was recovered from a cropland. The victim’s father, Ashraf Hossain, told The Daily Star that 15 days before the incident, a group of six youths led by Nurul had abducted and raped the girl. When the family tried to file a case, they were given death threats.

title: JU student files rape case against former student
body: A female student of Jahangirnagar University (JU) has filed a rape case against a former student of the university. The accused, SM Tarikul Islam, was a student of the 44th batch of the Institute of Information Technology at the university. The woman filed the case with Ashulia Police Station on Wednesday, alleging that she was called to Tarikul’s residence near the campus and raped, confirmed its Officer-in-Charge Rubel Howlader. Sub-Inspector Miraj Akon, the investigating officer of the case, citing the case statement, said the victim was in a relationship with the accused. On February 24, after iftar, the accused allegedly raped and assaulted her in his house in the Islamnagar area. Police later rescued the student after she called 999, he said. She was taken to Savar Upazila Health Complex for medical examination. Law enforcers, including police and Rab, are conducting drives to arrest the accused, the SI added. University Proctor AKM Rashidul Alam said they received a written complaint from the victim yesterday. The complaint has been filed and forwarded to the vice-chancellor’s office. The university administration will provide the highest possible support to the student, he added.

title: Student beaten ‘by JCD men’ at Dinajpur Medical College
body: A medical student was beaten allegedly by supporters of the Chhatra Dal convener of Dinajpur Medical College unit on Thursday night reportedly over establishing supremacy. The incident took place around 11:00pm in front of the medicine club of the college, said police and students. Witnesses said there has been a longstanding conflict over the presidency of the medicine club, a voluntary organisation of Dinajpur Medical College. Finding Nahid Hasan, a fifth-year student and president of the medicine club, alone, some supporters of Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal (JCD) Convener Dr Nuruzzaman attacked him and beat him for “not supporting him”, they said. Nahid and several other students, including one Sajib, alleged that Dr Habibullah Rasel, assistant superintendent of the boys’ hostel, was also involved in the assault. Soon after the incident, a video clip of the assault went viral on social media. Rokaiya Tamanna, also a student of the college, alleged that her phone was snatched and damaged while she was recording a video of the incident. Talking to The Daily Star over the phone, Nahid and Sajib alleged that ahead of the national election, Nuruzzaman had threatened to assault them “for not being loyal to him”. Nahid and Sajib are also involved in BNP politics but not aligned with JCD. “To establish his supremacy, a group of students loyal to Nuruzzaman attacked Nahid around 11:00pm, leaving him seriously injured. Assistant superintendent Dr Rasel was also involved in the attack,” said Sajib. Contacted, Principal Sheikh Sadek Ali admitted the involvement of the hostel superintendent and said the incident was “very embarrassing”. “Necessary steps will be taken after a meeting of the disciplinary committee,” he added. Dr Habibullah Rasel could not be reached for comments despite repeated phone calls. JCD Convener Dr Nuruzzaman denied any involvement in the attack. He claimed that Nahid and his associates had earlier assaulted members of another group, and that Nahid was beaten later at the emergency department in retaliation. Officer-in-Charge Nur Nabi of Dinajpur Kotwali Police Station said a clash between two JCD factions took place around 11:30pm, but no complaints had yet been filed by either party.

title: Two Indian nationals detained at Kurigram border
body: Police detained two Indian nationals while they were moving suspiciously near the Balarhat border area in Phulbari upazila of Kurigram on Friday evening. The detainees are Akhirul Khandakar (22), son of Sayeed Khandakar of Natkobari in Cooch Behar of India, and Faruk Mia (23), son of Jamir Ali of Kishamat Karla in the same district. Mahmud Hasan Nayeem, officer-in-charge (OC) of Phulbari Police Station, confirmed the incident. He said locals noticed the two men roaming around suspiciously in Purbo Phulmati Balarhat border area under Naodanga union and informed police. Later, a team from Phulbari Police Station rushed to the spot, detained them, and brought them to the station. During preliminary questioning, the detainees identified themselves as Indian nationals. Their identities were later verified, confirming that they are residents of the Cooch Behar district in India. The matter has been reported to the Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB). After necessary verification, the detainees will be handed over to BGB, OC Mahmud added. Lt Col Mehedee Imam, commanding officer of Lalmonirhat 15 BGB Battalion, said the Indian Border Security Force (BSF) has already been informed. Preparations are underway to hand them over to BSF by Friday night after completing formalities through a flag meeting.

title: 4 arrested over Narsingdi teen’s abduction and killing
body: Police have arrested four people after a case had been filed in Narsingdi’s Madhabdi over the abduction and killing of a teenage girl , allegedly to suppress a gang rape incident. “A case was filed with Madhabdi Police Station last night by the victim’s mother, Fahima Begum, accusing eight individuals of abducting her daughter and killing her in a cropland to cover up a gang rape incident,” said Madhabdi Police Station Officer-in-Charge Md Kamal Hossain. Nurul Islam has been named prime accused. “Four have so far been arrested. Efforts were underway to arrest the remaining accused involved in the incident,” he added. The four arrestees are former ward member of Mahishashur union Ahmad Ali Dewan, 65; his son Imran Dewan, 25; prime accused Nurul’s cousin Mohammad Ayub, 36; and Ebaidullah, 38. The victim, a garment factory worker, lived with her parents in a rented house in the Darikandi area and was a resident of Bilpar. The victim’s father, Ashraf Hossain, alleged that around 15 days ago a group of six youths led by Nurul abducted and raped the girl. He told The Daily Star that the family attempted to file a case but were threatened with death if they proceeded. “They even intercepted us on our way to the police station. Being intimidated, we returned home,” he said. Ashraf said they later informed Ahmed Ali, a member of ward 9 of Mahishashur union, who settled the matter through a social arbitration. Ahmad Ali, then acting as arbitrator, allegedly struck a deal with the perpetrators, pocketing a large sum of money, the victim's father alleged. The family was reportedly pressured to leave the village. “But Nurul kept stalking my daughter. Feeling insecure, we decided to send her to a safer place,” Ashraf said. On February 25, while Ashraf was taking his daughter a relative’s house, Nurul and his associates abducted her from Boroitola area, the case statement says. Failing to find her despite searching, he said he informed Ahmed Ali. “We found my daughter’s body on Thursday morning in a mustard field,” he said. “They killed my daughter after raping her again. I want justice.” Ahmed Ali denied mediating any arbitration and said he was not home when the family came to see him that night. Farida Gulshana Kabir, resident medical officer of Narsingdi Sadar Hospital, said the body has been received and an autopsy will be conducted on Friday (today). Narsingdi Additional Superintendent of Police (ASP) Sujon Chandra Sarker said the body was recovered with a scarf wrapped around her neck. “Details will be known after the autopsy,” he added.

title: Ex-UP member found injured on riverbank dies
body: A former union parishad member died after being rescued in critical condition from a riverbank in Brahmanbaria. The deceased -- Amir Hossain, 40 -- a former member of Ward No-3 under Banshgari Union Parishad in Raipura upazila of Narsingdi. Police said he was found lying on the bank of the Meghna River around 9:00am in the MP Tila area under Salimganj union in Nabinagar upazila, a border area between Brahmanbaria and Narsingdi. “He was in critical condition, with several injury marks on his head and body,” said Sunil Chandra Sutradhar, in-charge of Salimganj River Police Outpost under Nabinagar Police Station. He was taken to Nabinagar Upazila Health Complex, where doctors declared him dead. The body was later sent to the 250-bed Brahmanbaria General Hospital for autopsy. Dr Habibur Rahman, Nabinagar Upazila Health and Family Planning Officer, said the victim was brought dead and had multiple injuries. “Primarily, it appears he was murdered. Police are investigating,” said the police officer Sunil Chandra. Amir was accused in five cases filed with Raipura Police Station, he added. According to locals and police, Amir was elected a UP member in 2021 and was involved in local Jubo League politics. He went to Malaysia after the political changeover on August 5, 2024, and returned about four months ago. Police said he was attacked by miscreants on Wednesday night while travelling by boat to his father-in-law’s house.

title: Man behind DU assault a murder case accused
body: Dhaka University authorities have formed a three-member committee to investigate allegations that two students harassed and assaulted two women early Wednesday near the Raju sculpture at TSC. The accused are Shahriar Islam Tushar, a 2023–24 student of the Department of Theatre and Performance Studies and a resident of Bijoy Ekattor Hall, and Rakib Ahmed Sohan, a 2023–24 student of the Department of World Religions and Culture and a resident of Zia Hall. Rakib is also an accused in a 2024 murder case filed with Kaliakoir Police Station in Gazipur, said police. DU Proctor Saifuddin Ahmed told The Daily Star that the committee was formed after two men accompanying the women submitted written complaints to his office yesterday. A video circulating on social media shows one of the accused holding a bamboo stick and appearing to lunge at a woman. The women are heard accusing the men of assault. One says they were not safe at Dhaka University, as university students hit them. She also alleged that the men called them prostitutes because of their clothing. Another woman says, “We came to TSC after having sehri at Nazirabazar. They hit my rider. They are calling us prostitutes. How can they raise their hands on women?” Shahriar denied assaulting any woman. He said he had a scuffle with a man accompanying them but did not hit the women. He claimed the group appeared to be “indecent and intoxicated” and behaved rudely when asked about their identities, leading to an argument and physical altercation with the man. He alleged that when one of the women charged at him, and he tried to push her away, she accused him of slapping her. Rakib could not be reached for comment. In a separate media statement, he admitted holding a bamboo stick but denied assaulting anyone. The proctor said CCTV footage has been reviewed, and four DU students were identified at the scene. He said the footage does not clearly show the women being beaten with sticks, though the men appeared to threaten them and struck the accompanying man on the head with a helmet. “Whether the women were hit requires further review,” he added. The proctor noted that the women did not file complaints; the written complaints came from the two men with them, one identifying himself as a ride-share driver and the other as a friend. According to the complaint, the group was standing at TSC for tea after sehri when two to three men questioned, verbally abused and later attacked them with a helmet, also striking the women. The DU probe committee is expected to submit its findings after reviewing CCTV footage and the written complaints. Meanwhile confirming the murder case against Rakib, OC Khandkar Nasir Uddin of Kaliakoir Police Station in Gazipur said a charge sheet has been submitted. Rakib, son of Abdur Rahim of Safipur Bazar, and his twin brother Shakib are accused in the case and have reportedly been absconding. According to the case statement, on September 9, 2024, a young man named Sabbir Hossain was allegedly hacked and thrown from the roof of a 10-storey building in Safipur Paschimpara, Kaliakoir. The complaint alleges Rakib and Shakib were involved. The complainant, Sabbir’s elder brother Md Mohiuddin Abir, later filed a murder case against three accused. He has alleged in media statements that despite the submission of the charge sheet several months ago, no arrest warrant has yet been issued and the accused have not been arrested. Police said the case was investigated by Gazipur detective branch, which will take further steps, including arrests once warrants are issued. Gazipur DB OC Hasmat Ullah said due to “various circumstances”, no operation had been conducted earlier, but steps will now be taken to arrest the accused.

title: Gulshan flat case: Issue Interpol red notice for Tulip
body: A Dhaka court yesterday ordered the relevant authorities to have a red notice issued through Interpol for the arrest of British MP Tulip Siddiq, niece of deposed prime minister Sheikh Hasina, in a case over alleged corruption in acquiring a flat. Judge Md Sabbir Faiz of the Metropolitan Senior Special Judge’s Court in Dhaka passed the order following an application filed by Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) Assistant Director AKM Motuza Ali Sagar, said court bench assistant Riaz Hossain. On February 18, the court issued arrest warrants against Tulip, the MP for Hampstead and Highgate in London, and Rajdhani Unnayan Kartripakkha’s (Rajuk’s) former assistant legal adviser Sardar Mosharraf Hossain after accepting the charge sheet in the case. The court also set March 8 for submitting a report on the execution of the arrest warrants. On April 15 last year, the anti-graft body filed the case against Tulip, Mosharraf and Rajuk’s former assistant legal adviser Shah Md Khasruzzaman. Tulip allegedly provided undue benefits to private developer Eastern Housing Limited to illegally acquire the flat in Gulshan-2. According to the case documents, the accused allegedly, in collusion with each other, abused their power and illegally took possession of the flat without paying any money, and later got it registered. The ACC on January 13 this year pressed charges against Tulip and Mosharraf. Between November 27 last year and February 2 this year, Sheikh Hasina was jailed for 36 years in six cases involving the Purbachal plot scam in Dhaka. Her elder niece, Tulip, was also sentenced to six years’ imprisonment in three of the six cases.

title: Teenager ‘abducted’, murdered in Narsingdi
body: Police yesterday recovered the body of a teenage girl from a crop field in Narsingdi’s Madhabdi upazila. The deceased, Amena Akter, 15, was a garment worker and a resident of Bilpar area. She lived with her parents in a rented house in Darikandi. Narsingdi Additional Superintendent of Police (ASP) Sujon Chandra Sarker said the body was recovered with a scarf wrapped around her neck. The victim’s parents alleged that she was killed by a group of stalkers who had gang-raped her around two weeks ago. Speaking to journalists, the victim’s mother Fahina Begum said Amena had a relationship with Nurul Islam, 25, of the same area. “When we came to know about it, we requested Nurul to marry my daughter. But he refused,” she said. The girl’s father, Ashraf Hossain, alleged that around 15 days ago, Nurul and four to five of his associates abducted his daughter when she was on her way home from work and raped her. He told The Daily Star that the family attempted to file a case but was threatened by Nurul. “They intercepted us on our way to the police station. Being intimidated, we returned home,” he said. Ashraf claimed they later informed Ahmed Ullah, a member of Ward-9 of Mahishashura Union, who settled the matter through a an arbitration. “But Nurul kept stalking my daughter. Feeling insecure, we decided to send her to a safe place,” he said. According to the father, on Wednesday night, he was taking his daughter to a relative’s house when Nurul and his associates allegedly intercepted them around 10:00pm in the Boroitala area and abducted her. Failing to find her despite searching, he said he informed Ahmed Ullah. “We found my daughter’s body on Thursday morning in a mustard field,” he said. “They killed my daughter after raping her again. I want justice.” Ahmed Ullah denied that he had conducted any arbitration and said he was not at home when the family came to see him that night. Farida Gulshana Kabir, resident medical officer of Narsingdi Sadar Hospital, said the body has been received and an autopsy will be conducted today (Friday). ASP Sarker said police are investigating the incident. “Details will be known after the autopsy.” Regarding the earlier rape allegation, Md Kamal Hosaain, officer-in-charge of Madhabdi Police Station, said police were unaware of any such incident, as no complaint had been filed. Nurul went into hiding after the incident, the OC said, adding that police detained one person, Ebadullah, 38, yesterday for his alleged involvement. “The victim’s family is preparing to file a case tonight,” he said yesterday.

title: Youth stabbed to death in Ctg
body: A young man was stabbed to death by a group of miscreants in the BITAC Stadium area under Pahartali Police Station in Chattogram city on Thursday night. The deceased was identified as Akash Das, 30, son of Babul Das of South Kattali in Sagarika area of the port city. Victim's brother Sagor told The Daily Star that a group of assailants stabbed Akash near the BITAC Stadium around 8:30pm and fled the scene. Sub-Inspector (SI) Mashudur Rahman of Pahartali police station told The Daily Star that the victim was rushed to Chattogram Medical College Hospital by his brother, where the on-duty doctor declared him dead after examination. "Reason behind the killing could not be ascertained immediately," he added. Police were trying to arrest the killers. The body has been kept at the hospital morgue for autopsy. Legal proceedings are underway, added the police official.

title: Teenager found dead in Narsingdi field; family alleges rape and murder

He told The Daily Star that the family attempted to file a case but were threatened with death if they proceeded. “They even intercepted us on our way to the police station. Being intimidated, we returned home,” he said. Ashraf claimed they later informed Ahmed Ali Dewan, a member of ward 9 of Mahishashura union, who settled the matter through a social arbitration. “But Nurul kept stalking my daughter. Feeling insecure, we decided to send her to a safer place,” he said. According to the father, on Wednesday night, he was taking his daughter to a relative’s house when Nurul and his associates intercepted them around 10:00pm in Boroitala area and abducted her. Failing to find her despite searching, he said he informed Ahmed Ali Dewan. “We found my daughter’s body on Thursday morning in a mustard field,” he said. “They killed my daughter after raping her again. I want justice.” Ahmed Ali Dewan denied mediating any arbitration and said he was not home when the family came to see him that night. Farida Gulshana Kabir, resident medical officer of Narsingdi Sadar Hospital, said the body has been received and an autopsy will be conducted tomorrow (Friday). ASP Sarker said police are investigating the incident. “Details will be known after the autopsy.” Regarding the earlier rape allegation, Md Kamal Hosaain, officer-in-charge of Madhabdi Police Station, said police were unaware of any such incident, as no complaint had been filed. Nurul went into hiding after the incident, the OC said, adding that police detained one person, Ebadullah, 38, today for alleged involvement. “The victim’s family is preparing to file a case tonight (Thursday),” he said. Note: This report has been updated with correct info at 12:05pm on February 27

title: Netrokona court awards life term to man for strangling wife to death
body: A court in Netrokona has sentenced a man to life imprisonment for strangling his wife to death, additionally imposing a fine of Tk 10,000. Judge Mosammat Mariyam-Mun-Munjuri of the Netrokona District and Sessions Judge Court delivered the verdict this afternoon. Public Prosecutor Abul Hashem confirmed that the accused was present in court at the time of the verdict. The convict, Md Abu Bakkar, 62, is from Molamkhar Char area under Karimganj upazila in Kishoreganj. The victim was Rezia Khatun, 38, was a resident of Basuntia village in Mohanganj upazila. According to court sources, it was the second marriage for both Abu Bakkar and Rezia Khatun. After marriage, Abu Bakkar began living at his wife's residence, and their marital life was frequently marked by disputes. On the night of April 29, 2014, following a family conflict, Abu Bakkar strangled Rezia Khatun with his shirt. He subsequently concealed the body in a haystack beside the house and informed his son from his first marriage over the phone. Police recovered the body the following day. The victim's sister, Beauty Akter, filed a murder case with Mohanganj Police Station the next day. After completing the investigation, police submitted the charge sheet to the court on February 28, 2018. The court delivered the verdict after recording testimonies from 11 witnesses.

title: 70-year-old shot dead while confronting armed cow lifters in Ctg
body: A 70-year-old man was shot dead as he attempted to stop a cattle theft in Chattogram’s Chandanaish upazila early today. “The victim, identified as Chandan Dey, confronted the robbers at his cowshed in Badurpara area of the municipality around 4:45am, Chandanaish Police Station Officer-in-Charge Eliash Khan told The Daily Star. The assailants took one cow from his cowshed before fleeing in a pickup van, the OC said. Chandan was shot in the face when he tried to intercept the cow lifters' vehicle when they were taking away his cow, he said. He suffered critical injuries and died on the way to the hospital, the OC added. Police added the gang looted a total of three cattle, including one of Chandan's one from the locality. Authorities recovered Chandan's body and sent it to Chattogram Medical College Hospital morgue for an autopsy. Police said they are working to identify and apprehend the attackers.

title: Court orders Interpol red notice for Tulip Siddiq in Gulshan flat case
body: A special court today ordered the relevant authorities to issue a red notice through Interpol for the arrest of British MP Tulip Siddiq, niece of deposed prime minister Sheikh Hasina, in a case filed over acquiring a flat in Gulshan-2 illegally by providing undue benefits to a private developer. Judge Md Sabbir Faiz of the Metropolitan Senior Special Judge’s Court in Dhaka passed the order following an application filed by Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) Assistant Director AKM Motuza Ali Sagar, said court bench assistant Riaz Hossain. On February 18, the court issued arrest warrants against Tulip, the MP for Hampstead and Highgate in London, and Rajuk’s former assistant legal adviser Sardar Mosharraf Hossain after accepting the charge sheet in the case. The court also set March 8 for submitting a report on the execution of the arrest warrants. On April 15 last year, the anti-graft body filed the case against Tulip, Mosharraf and Rajuk’s former assistant legal adviser Shah Md Khasruzzaman for allegedly illegally acquiring the flat from Eastern Housing Limited. According to the case documents, the accused allegedly, in collusion with each other, abused their power and illegally took possession of a flat in Eastern Housing’s Gulshan-2 project without paying any money, and later got it registered. The ACC on January 13 this year filed the charge sheet against Tulip and Mosharraf. Between November 27 last year and February 2 this year, Sheikh Hasina was jailed for 36 years in six cases involving the Purbachal plot scam in Dhaka. Her elder niece, Tulip, was also sentenced to six years’ imprisonment in three of the six cases.

title: Youth arrested over murder of 14-year-old girl in Rayerbazar
body: Police have arrested an 18-year-old youth in connection with the murder of a 14-year-old schoolgirl in Dhaka's Rayerbazar area. Siam was picked up from his residence in Kathalbagan area, Dhaka Metropolitan Police (Dhanmondi Zone) Assistant Commissioner Shah Mostafa Tarikuzzaman told The Daily Star this morning. "In primary interrogation, Siam confessed to the crime. He also said the victim and him were previously acquainted,” Mostafa told The Daily Star this morning. Family members said she was attacked in front of their home at approximately 9:00pm last night. Speaking to journalists, the victim’s father, Belal Hossain, said his daughter was a class eight student at Rayerbazar High School. She had gone outside with her younger brother last night. “After a while, we heard commotion. When we went downstairs, we saw that someone had hacked my daughter and left her there. She was critically injured. We first took her to Sikder Medical, and later transferred her to Dhaka Medical College Hospital,” he added. Doctors at Dhaka Medical College Hospital declared the schoolgirl dead around 10:15pm. The victim’s mother, Nadia Begum, alleged that Siam had been harassing her daughter over mobile phone for the past three to four years. “I once scolded him over the phone. He killed my daughter. I want justice,” she said.

title: Lawyers’ protest brings court activities in Barishal to a standstill for three days
body: Judicial activities at all courts in Barishal have reportedly remained suspended for three consecutive days protesting the arrest of district bar association and the filing of a case against 12 lawyers, leaving several of litigants in distress. Sabuj Hawlader was seen moving from one courtroom to another from morning until noon today, holding his case documents. Speaking to reporters on the court premises, he said a case under the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act had been filed three months and 10 days ago against three individuals, including Akbar Ali Hawlader, who is currently on bail. “When we moved the High Court seeking bail, it directed us to apply before the lower court. But for the last three days, the court's activities have remained suspended. I have been unable to file the bail petition,” Sabuj said. He added that the deadline for submitting the bail application expires on Sunday. “With Friday and Saturday being holidays, Thursday was effectively the last working day. But as the courts are not functioning, I am deeply worried,” he said. Over the past three days, thousands of litigants have been unable to access judicial services as all courts, including the District and Sessions Judge’s Court, have remained non-functional. Many arrived at the premises as early as 9:00am, only to return without any progress in their cases, reports our correspondent on the spot. Lawyers alleged that a case was filed yesterday under the Speedy Trial Act against President of the Barishal District Bar Association, Sadiqur Rahman Linkon, and 11 other lawyers on charges including vandalising a courtroom and threatening a judge. The case was lodged by Rajib Majumder, bench assistant of the court of the Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate. Linkon was arrested and sent to jail later that afternoon. In the morning, protesting lawyers demanded his immediate release on bail and warned that court activities would be shut indefinitely if he was not granted bail within the day. “Judicial activities across Barishal have remained suspended for 72 hours. Litigants are suffering, but when lawyers themselves are facing injustice, there is little we can do,” one protesting lawyer said, wishing anonymity. He said the movement would continue until the “false case” is withdrawn and the bar association president is released. On Tuesday around 2:30pm, a group of agitating lawyers led by Linkon allegedly vandalised the courtroom of the Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate. CCTV footage of the incident later circulated on social media.

title: Two women allegedly harassed at DU campus; university forms probe body
body: The authorities of University of Dhaka have formed a three-member committee to investigate allegations that two of its students had harassed and physically assaulted two women in the early hours of Wednesday near the Raju Sculpture at TSC on the university campus. Dhaka University Proctor Saifuddin Ahmed told The Daily Star that the committee was formed as two men accompanying the women submitted written complaints to his office yesterday. A video circulating on social media shows one of the accused holding a bamboo stick and attempting to kick one of the women. The women are heard accusing the men of physically assaulting them. One woman is heard saying, “We are not safe in front of University of Dhaka. We are not safe after August 5. University boys beat us. They say our clothes mean we are prostitutes.” Another woman says, “We came to TSC after having sehri at Nazirabazar. They slapped my rider. They are calling us prostitutes. How can they raise their hands on women?” At one point, someone from off-camera is heard saying, “There is no evidence,” to which the woman responds, “There is CCTV footage.” Another woman, expressing anger, says, “Why did he slap me? Why would a Dhaka University student hit me? Can’t I come here?
