Contacted, Foyzur yesterday told The Daily Star that the committee had recorded statements of another seven students, one guardian, and seven to eight teachers of the school so far, and all of them substantiated the allegations against the headmaster. He also said that the accused headmaster appeared before the committee on February 17. “He, however, refuted all the allegations, terming them a conspiracy against him,” Foyzur said, adding that the committee will submit its report next week. Earlier, on February 10, the accused headmaster told The Daily Star over the phone that he was busy and would call back later. However, he has not responded to repeated phone calls since then. Shah Mohammad Rezaul Karim, assistant headmaster of the school, on February 16 said the headmaster has been absent since February 10 and has not delegated any responsibilities during his absence. He said he heard some students had filed complaints with the DC but was unaware of the details. The issue came up on February 10 when four to five alleged victims and their guardians approached a local human rights organisation with the allegations of sexual assault by the headmaster. Human rights activist Dow Nai Pru Neli said they took the victims to the deputy commissioner’s office, where a written complaint was submitted. The Daily Star talked to a number of complainants and their family members, who alleged that the headmaster exploited poor and vulnerable students by misusing his power. An eighth-grade student, requesting anonymity, alleged that he was called to the headmaster’s room where he was sexually assaulted. Out of fear and shame, he initially kept silent but later informed his grandmother and a local human rights activist before filing a written complaint with the district administration. A ninth-grade student made similar allegations, adding that at least 15–20 other students may have suffered similar abuse. One guardian alleged that after his son failed eighth grade and was readmitted, the headmaster offered to “guide” him privately and asked him to attend evening sessions. Months later, the boy refused to visit the headmaster and displayed signs of fear before eventually disclosing the alleged abuse. A temporary computer operator alleged that he was called to the headmaster’s room after office hours and was subjected to forced inappropriate conduct. He claimed he was threatened with dismissal if he resisted. Muhammad Faridul Alam Hossaini, deputy director of secondary and higher education for the Chattogram region, said his office had not yet received any formal complaint. He also said the headmaster had not applied for leave.

title: Former student leader hacked in Dhaka’s Mohammadpur
body: A man was hacked and critically injured by miscreants in Dhaka’s Mohammadpur area on Sunday night. The incident took place in the Muyure Villa area of Mohammadpur, said Juel Rana, additional deputy commissioner of Dhaka Metropolitan Police. The victim was identified as Ibrahim, 27, a former coordinator of the Students Against Discrimination platform. The police officer said Ibrahim was first taken to Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College and Hospital and later shifted to the National Institute of Traumatology and Orthopaedic Rehabilitation (NITOR) for better treatment. Preliminary investigation suggests the attack may have been carried out over the possession of an office that once belonged to the Awami League, whose activities are now banned, said Juel Rana. “A group of extortionists had reportedly been trying to take control of the office for the past few days, leading to a dispute with Ibrahim,” he said. “However, since he was a coordinator of the anti-discrimination movement, we are also investigating whether the attack was politically motivated,” he added.

title: Ward-level BNP leader shot by alleged extortionists in Dhaka’s Kalabagan
body: A ward-level BNP leader sustained a bullet injury on Sunday night after being attacked by alleged extortionists in Dhaka's Kalabagan area. The incident occurred around 9:30pm in front of a shoe market opposite Bashundhara Shopping Complex in Panthapath. The injured, Shafiqur Rahman, 55, former joint general secretary of ward 16 unit of BNP, is a shoe supplier for pavement shops in the area, said Monir Hossain, a shop owner who rushed him to hospital. Quoting Shafiqur, Monir alleged that local extortionists had been demanding money from him for several days. “They caught him tonight, demanded payment again, and asked why he wasn’t answering their calls. At one stage, they shot him and fled,” Monir said. Shafiqur was first taken to a nearby hospital and later shifted to Dhaka Medical College Hospital. He sustained a bullet wound in the palm of his left hand. Inspector Md Faruk of the DMCH police camp said Shafiqur was receiving treatment at the emergency department and was now out of danger. Kalabagan police are investigating the incident, he added.

title: 8-year-old killed after being hit by vehicle in MP’s convoy in Cox’s Bazar
body: An eight-year-old boy was killed this afternoon after being hit by a vehicle in the convoy of Cox’s Bazar-2 (Maheshkhali–Kutubdia) MP Alamgir Mohammad Mahfuzullah Farid in Badarkhali of Chakaria upazila. The deceased, Md Khaled Bin Walid, was the son of Amanul Islam and Sumaiya, of Kabirer Ghat in Techchipara, police said. He was a class two student at a local madrasa. The accident occurred around 4:30pm near Badarkhali Fazil Madrasa. Khaled was taken to Badarkhali General Hospital, where doctors declared him dead. Witnesses said he was hit by the third vehicle in the MP’s convoy while crossing the road to a shop. Officer-in-Charge of Chakaria Police Station Mohammad Monir Hossain said the accident did not involve the MP’s personal vehicle, but rather another vehicle in his convoy. He said the child was crossing the road to go to a nearby shop when the accident occurred. An agitated crowd later intercepted the vehicle in Ferryghat, brought it back to the scene, and vandalised it. The MP’s car had already left the area. No case had been filed as of 9:00pm, but police have taken the vehicle into custody, he said. Contacted, MP Farid confirmed the incident, describing it as “very tragic.” He said the vehicle was rented for election campaigning and had no passengers at the time. The driver fled immediately after the accident, he added.

title: Missing school student's body found in septic tank in Gaibandha
body: Police recovered the body of a 16-year-old student from a septic tank in Gaibandha’s Gobindaganj upazila this afternoon. The deceased, Nurma Khatun, was a class 10 student at Taltala Dimukhi High School. She was the daughter of Nazrul Islam of Samaspara Choudhuripara village under Talukkanupur union. Speaking to reporters, the victim’s father said his daughter went missing from their home around noon. After searching various locations without success, her body was later discovered inside an open septic tank at their neighbour Hazrat Ali’s house in the afternoon. Confirming the incident, Mozammel Haque, officer-in-charge (OC) of Gobindaganj Police Station, said, “Upon receiving information from locals, police recovered the body from the spot.” "The body is being prepared to be sent to the Gaibandha Sadar Hospital morgue for an autopsy." “A case regarding the incident is currently underway, the OC added.

title: AL leader arrested over last Nov's Tangail bus arson
body: Police arrested a leader of Sakhipur upazila Awami League today in connection with setting fire to a moving bus on the Dhaka-Tangail highway in Baoi Khola in Tangail's Basail upazila last November. The arrestee, Jahid Iqbal Jahangir, is the joint general secretary of Sakhipur Municipality unit of Awami League, said police. Police and witnesses said Jahangir had placed a wreath at the Central Shaheed Minar in Sakhipur on behalf of the Sakhipur upazila AL and Muktijoddha Sontan Sangsad on February 21. Officer-in-Charge of Sakhipur Police Station Helal Uddin told The Daily Star that Jahangir was picked up from Uttara intersection in Sakhipur municipality and later handed over to Basail Police Station. Basail OC Alamgir Kabir said miscreants torched a passenger bus in Baoi Khola area of Basail upazila around 1:00am on November 12, 2025. A female passenger injured in the incident died six days later while undergoing treatment. The following day, Gorai Highway Police SI Ismail Hossain filed a case with Basail station against several unidentified suspects. Jahangir has now been arrested as a suspect in that case and sent to court, OC Kabir confirmed.

title: Teenage auto-rickshaw driver found dead in paddy field in Noakhali
body: The body of a teenage auto-rickshaw driver was recovered this afternoon in a paddy field near Munshi Bari Bridge of Kutubpur union in Noakhali's Begumganj. The deceased was identified as Md Abdul Ahad, 17, said police. Inspector (Investigation) of Begumganj Model Police Station Md Habibur Rahman said Ahad’s body was discovered with his mouth taped shut. Robbers killed him and fled with his vehicle, police suspect. Family members said Ahad had been living with his maternal grandparents in Kutubpur since his parents’ separation. For the past two years, he made a living by driving a battery‑run auto‑rickshaw. On Saturday night around 9:00pm, he left with the vehicle but did not return. Both Ahad and the auto‑rickshaw went missing. On Sunday afternoon, a local farmer found the body while tending to his crops. Police recovered the body and sent it to Noakhali General Hospital morgue for autopsy. Inspector Habibur said initial findings suggest that miscreants suffocated Ahad and fled with the vehicle. Police are working to identify and apprehend those involved. ASP Imran said, “We have obtained a few names of potential suspects. We have begun our investigation.”

title: Local BNP leader detained in Habiganj for ‘verbally abusing’ OC over phone
body: The Detective Branch today detained Ferdous Chowdhury Tushar, president of Bahubal upazila unit BNP in Habiganj, on charge of verbally abusing the local police station’s officer-in-charge over the phone, said police. “A team of detectives picked up Ferdous Chowdhury Tushar from his residence in Shayestanagar area of Habiganj town around 12:00pm for verbally abusing Bahubal Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Mohammad Saiful Islam,” said Shamim Iqbal, officer-in-charge of the district DB police. Additional Superintendent of Police (Crime and Operations) Raki Rani Das said the next legal procedures against the BNP leader are underway, and further details will be provided later. Recently, an audio clip went viral on social media in which the Tushar allegedly made offensive remarks at OC Saiful Islam during a phone conversation. In the circulated audio, it is heard that the OC was speaking to someone else when Tushar allegedly interrupted and began using abusive language toward the OC from the other end of the line. Mokhlesur Rahman, a member of the district BNP, was on the other side in the conversation with the OC. “I was speaking over the phone with the OC when Tushar started speaking from the side and used some offensive words. I called the OC again and urged him not to mind his behaviour,” Mokhlesur said. The audio sparked widespread discussion and criticism in political circles as well as among the general public. Law enforcement agencies subsequently took the matter into consideration, leading to his detention, police said. Before his detainment, Tushar, however, spoke to local journalists and denied the allegation, claiming the audio had been manipulated. “I have not called the OC in the last two months. I was speaking to my manager. Someone edited the audio and spread it on Facebook,” he said.

title: Four injured in pellet gun attack over 'unauthorised' sand extraction in Brahmanbaria
body: Four villagers were injured after sand extractors allegedly fired pellet guns when locals tried to prevent them from digging sand beyond the approved area of the Meghna River in Nabinagar upazila of Brahmanbaria this morning. “The incident occurred near Charlapang village. Police, acting on information, rushed to the spot, and legal proceedings are underway,” said Nabinagar Police Station Officer-in-Charge Rafiqul Islam. The injured were identified as Alim Mia, Nuru Mia, Safor Mia, and Nurul Haque, all residents of Charlapang village under Paschim Union, the OC added, noting that “the situation is now under control.” According to police and local sources, Samiul Traders had a lease to extract sand from a designated section of the Meghna River. However, villagers alleged that the company was operating beyond the approved boundary, extracting sand from areas near Charlapang village. Locals said the unauthorised extraction posed a serious erosion threat to nearby croplands and homesteads, raising fears of land loss and displacement. When sand extraction resumed in the disputed zone this morning, villagers gathered to stop them, leading to an altercation. Witnesses claimed that the sand traders had brought in hired men from the Mirzachar area of Raipura upazila in Narsingdi, transporting them across the river by speedboats and boats. The group, reportedly armed with pellet guns, opened fire on villagers during the confrontation, injuring four. The injured were initially taken to a local health complex and later referred to Dhaka for advanced treatment, according to witnesses.

title: Locals besiege Adabar Police Station protesting extortion, factory attack; five arrested
body: At least five people were arrested after locals besieged Adabar Police Station last night, protesting alleged extortion and an attack by a teenage gang at a factory in the area that left several injured. The arrestees include Rasel, the prime suspect, said Abdul Malek, inspector (investigation) of Adabar Police Station. Witnesses said a group of people — mostly owners and employees of garment and embroidery factories — surrounded the police station, demanding an end to extortion and the arrest of those who attacked a factory named Abir Embroidery. Speaking to reporters early today, Abdullah Al Mamun, assistant commissioner of Mohammadpur Zone, said 10 to 12 armed youths stormed the factory with machetes, allegedly attempting to snatch mobile phones and cash. Several workers were injured and taken to hospital, he said. Tensions mounted as news of the attack spread to nearby factories. Residents and businesspeople blocked a nearby road and laid siege to the police station, alleging that authorities had failed to curb growing incidents of extortion and mugging in the area. Speaking in front of the police station, a factory owner claimed the teenage gang had created a reign of terror in Adabar by regularly demanding extortion money. Those who refused were allegedly attacked with machetes. “Whenever employees return home after collecting their salaries, the gang snatches their mobile phones and cash,” said the owner of another embroidery factory. “We want a crime-free Adabar,” he added. “We came to the police station so that police take action to stop the crime,” said another protester. Mostafiz Raihan Jahir, owner of the embroidery factory, filed a case over the incident.

title: Man kills expatriate brother over Tk 5 dispute in Lakshmipur, police say
body: A dispute over Tk 5 in an electricity bill turned deadly in Ramganj upazila of Lakshmipur, where an expatriate was allegedly killed by his elder brother, police said. "The victim, Alamgir Hossain, was allegedly beaten to death by his elder brother, Khorshed Alam, and several others at North Badarpur village around 8:30pm yesterday," said Ramganj Police Station Officer-in-Charge Md Firoz Uddin Chowdhury. The altercation began over the electricity bill shortfall and later escalated into a fatal assault, the OC said The suspect and his associates involved in the incident are now absconding, police said. Alamgir, who had been working in Dubai for years, recently returned home on leave. He and his brother, sons of the late Achan Ullah, lived in separate parts of the same family house and used a shared electricity meter. Police and locals said the dispute arose over a Tk 5 shortfall in the January bill. Alamgir had paid his share but was short of Tk 5 due to a lack of small change, which led to an argument. According to Alamgir’s wife, Sabina Yasmin, the brothers first argued before iftar, and the quarrel turned into a scuffle. Later, around 7:30pm, Alamgir went to a nearby tea stall where Khorshed confronted him again. Witnesses said Khorshed and his associates then assaulted Alamgir with punches, kicks and sticks, leaving him critically injured before fleeing. He was taken to Ramganj Upazila Health Complex, where doctors declared him dead around 8:30pm. Police recovered the body and sent it to Lakshmipur Sadar Hospital for autopsy this morning. A murder case is being prepared, police said.

title: 270 cartons of cigarettes, 15 smartphones seized from Dubai-returnee at Ctg airport
body: Officials from airport intelligence and customs agencies seized 270 cartons of cigarettes and 15 smartphones from a passenger arriving from Dubai at Chattogram Shah Amanat International Airport yesterday morning, according to a press release. The operation was jointly conducted by the airport unit of National Security Intelligence (NSI), Customs Intelligence and Investigation Directorate and the airport customs branch. At around 9:45am, officials searched the baggage of a passenger arriving on Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight BG148 from Dubai and recovered “a total of 270 cartons of cigarettes (Mond) and 15 mobile phones (five iPhones and 10 Google Pixel phones)”, the release said. The passenger was identified as Mohammad Hossain Zahed Habib (passport no. A15799208), a resident of West Farhadabad in Fatikchhari, Chattogram. According to the statement, revenue amounting to Tk 9,90,000 was realised from the seized goods, including Tk 5,40,000 from cigarettes and Tk 4,50,000 from mobile phones. The confiscated items were seized at Departmental Memoranda (DM) value and will remain in the custody of Chattogram Customs House. The passenger was later released after being verbally warned by NSI and customs officials. The authorities said their efforts would continue to prevent revenue evasion and the entry of prohibited imports. “To prevent revenue evasion and stop the entry of any banned imported goods, the efforts of airport NSI, airport customs, customs intelligence and, above all, the airport authorities will continue,” the release added.

title: Sramik Dal leader shot in Raozan
body: An upazila-level Sramik Dal leader was shot and injured by armed miscreants in Raozan upazila of Chattogram on Friday night. The incident took place around 7:30pm at Chowdhury Market in Ward no-9 of Raozan municipality. The injured, Mehedi Hasan, 32, was admitted to a private hospital after the incident. Local sources said Mehedi is the organising secretary of Upazila Sramik Dal, although the information could not be independently verified. According to local sources, Mehedi was returning from Shah Awlia Mosque after offering prayers when a group of armed criminals opened fire and fled the scene. He sustained bullet injuries to his chest and leg. Assistant Superintendent of Police (ASP) of Rangunia Circle, Balayat Hossain, told The Daily Star, “After hearing about the incident, police went to the spot but found nothing. We are collecting information and trying to identify the attackers. Action will be taken after receiving a complaint.”

title: Cop stabbed at Jatrabari checkpoint
body: A police constable was stabbed by miscreants during a search at a checkpoint in Dhaka’s Jatrabari area yesterday. Police also recovered an abandoned bag with five crude bombs and another explosive device from the scene. The injured, Md Shah Alam, 33, a constable of Jatrabari Police Station, is currently undergoing treatment at Dhaka Medical College Hospital. SI Md Sahidur Rahman of the police station said a team of four to five policemen was on mobile duty near the Kutubkhali Pocket Gate area. Around noon, they intercepted four youths carrying two bags due to suspicious movements. As Shah Alam attempted to search the bags, one of the youths suddenly pulled out a knife from his waist and stabbed him on his forehead. When the police team chased the attackers, the miscreants exploded a crude bomb and managed to flee the scene, the SI added. The abandoned bag containing the explosives was later handed over to the Bomb Disposal Unit.

title: Rumeen accuses BNP men of assault at Shaheed Minar
body: Rumeen Farhana, MP from Brahmanbaria-2, yesterday said she was obstructed and attacked while attempting to place a wreath at the Sarail Shaheed Minar during the first hour of International Mother Language Day. Her supporters blocked the Dhaka-Sylhet highway following the incident. Speaking to local journalists, she said, “As an elected member of parliament, I was supposed to place the first wreath at 12:01am. But some BNP men launched an attack. I was pushed aside, and a situation was created where I could have been knocked to the ground.” “After 17 years, BNP has returned to power. If the party does not immediately control its activists at the local level, the consequences will be dire,” she said. Describing the incident as “premeditated,” she claimed that the local BNP president and secretary were not present and a locally known “goon” led a group of unruly youths in carrying out the attack. Rumeen also linked the incident to political rivalry, saying her victory as an independent candidate had fuelled resentment among her opponents. Terming the law-and-order situation “vulnerable”, she said police had tried to intervene but “five or ten officers cannot control such a violent situation when ruling party activists unleash mayhem.” “I want justice. I have already filed a case,” she said.

title: Six detained outside PM Tarique Rahman’s Gulshan residence
body: Police this evening detained six people, including five women, from in front of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s residence on Gulshan Avenue in Dhaka. Their identities were not immediately known. Rakibur Rahman, inspector (investigation) of Gulshan Police Station, said the group had staged a sit-in outside the residence, claiming they wanted to meet the prime minister. “They were sitting in front of the house, saying they wanted to meet him,” the officer told The Daily Star. Asked about the purpose of the sit-in, the detainees gave inconsistent answers, prompting police to take them to the station for questioning, he added. Police said further details would be available after initial interrogation.

title: Constable stabbed at Jatrabari checkpoint, crude bombs recovered
body: A police constable was stabbed by miscreants during a search at a checkpoint in Dhaka’s Jatrabari area this noon. Police also recovered an abandoned bag with five crude bombs and another explosive device from the scene. The injured, Md Shah Alam, 33, a constable attached to the transport section of Jatrabari Police Station, is currently undergoing treatment at Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH). Sub-Inspector (SI) Md Sahidur Rahman of the police station told The Daily Star that a team of four to five policemen was on mobile duty near the Kutubkhali Pocket Gate area. Around noon, they intercepted four youths carrying two bags due to suspicious movements. As Constable Shah Alam attempted to search the bags, one of the youths suddenly pulled out a knife from his waist and stabbed him on his forehead. When the police team chased the attackers, the miscreants exploded a crude bomb and managed to flee the scene, the SI added. The abandoned bag containing the explosives was later handed over to the Bomb Disposal Unit. Shah Alam was initially taken to the Central Police Hospital in Rajarbagh before being shifted to DMCH. Doctors at the DMCH emergency department said the constable is currently receiving treatment and undergoing medical tests, including a CT scan of his head.

title: 2 killed by mob on mugging suspicion
body: Two suspected muggers were allegedly beaten to death by a mob of villagers in Sadullapur upazila of Gaibandha early yesterday. The incident took place in the Mujahidpur area of Khoddokomarpur village, police said. The deceased were identified as Lebu Mia, alias Bhondol, 24, of Satarpara village, and Moinul Islam, 50, of Mostafapur village in Palashbari upazila, said Sarowar Alam Khan, officer-in-charge (OC) of Palashbari Police Station. According to police and witnesses, three muggers on a motorcycle intercepted a woman and her relative on Sadullapur-Thutiapakur road when they reached the Madarhat Kheya Ghat area upon arrival from Dhaka on a night coach around 4:30am. Brandishing sharp weapons, the suspects robbed them of cash and gold ornaments, the witnesses said. “When the victims screamed for help, locals began chasing the muggers. While attempting to flee, the suspects lost control of their motorcycle and crashed in the Mujahidpur area,” said Bidroh Kumar Kundu, additional superintendent of police (Gaibandha Circle). “Two of them were caught and beaten to death on the spot by the locals, while the third suspect managed to escape,” he added. Family members said Lebu Mia, the only son of widow Phulmati Begum, had been working in Dhaka as a rickshaw puller for three years. He lived there with his wife and one-year-old son and had returned to the village just two days ago to visit his mother. The other deceased, Moinul Islam, had married Lebu’s cousin as his second wife and was living with his father-in-law in Satarpara. Abdul Alim, OC of Sadullapur Police Station, said police recovered the bodies and sent them to Gaibandha General Hospital morgue for autopsy. The motorcycle used by the suspects was seized. Lebu Mia’s mother, Phulmati, filed a murder case in connection with the incident, the OC added.

title: Job seeker jailed for using electronic devices during recruitment test in Kishoreganj
body: A mobile court today sentenced a job seeker to 28 days in jail for adopting unfair means by using electronic devices during a recruitment test for the deputy commissioner’s office in Kishoreganj. The incident took place this morning at Kishoreganj Government Boys’ High School. The convict, Subrata Das, 29, son of late Sudhangshu Das of Barahati village in Mithamoin upazila, was caught using electronic devices in violation of government orders. Mohammad Nahid Hasan Khan, additional deputy commissioner (Revenue) of Kishoreganj and president of the recruitment committee, confirmed the development. He said Subrata was arrested immediately after the matter came to light. Later, Subrata was produced before a mobile court led by Md Riyad Hossain, assistant commissioner and executive magistrate of Kishoreganj. The court sentenced him to 28 days in prison and fined him Tk 100. In default of payment, he will serve an additional two days in jail.

title: DMP chief urges traders to cooperate during market monitoring drives
body: Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Commissioner Sheikh Md Sazzat Ali today urged traders to fully cooperate with magistrates of the Directorate of National Consumers' Right Protection (DNCRP) during market monitoring drives. Speaking at a meeting with the Moulvibazar Traders' Association in Dhaka’s Chawkbazar around 3:00pm, the commissioner termed a recent altercation between a trader and a DNCRP magistrate an "undesirable incident". He urged the traders to help ensure transparency and fair prices in the market. He also instructed them to keep commodity prices stable and refrain from food adulteration during the holy month of Ramadan. The meeting follows an incident on Wednesday when DNCRP Magistrate Abdul Jabbar Mondol led a drive in the Moulvibazar area in Dhaka to monitor prices ahead of Ramadan. During the drive, Mohammad Ali Bhutto, president of the Moulvibazar Traders' Association, engaged in an altercation with the magistrate over price hikes. DNCRP Director General Faruq Ahmed summoned the association's leaders to his office following the incident, according to Haji Abul Hashem, vice-president of the traders' platform. On Thursday morning, Bhutto met the DG at his office and expressed regret over Wednesday's altercation, Hashem told The Daily Star.

title: SCBA election on March 11-12
body: After two years, the annual election for 2026-2027 session of the Supreme Court Bar Association’s (SCBA) executive committee is going to be held on March 11 and 12. SCBA’s acting secretary Md Mahfuzur Rahman Milon issued a notification to this effect on February 18. As per the election schedule, nomination papers will be submitted between 9:00am and 3:00pm from February 19 to March 1. The scrutiny of nomination papers will take place on March 1, while the deadline for withdrawal of candidature has been set for March 4. Around 11,000 lawyers have been registered as voters in the election, SCBA's Administrative Officer Md Robiul Hasan told The Star. The last SCBA election was held in March 2024 in a very controversial manner where pro-BNP lawyers won four key posts, including that of president, while then Awami League-backed candidates took ten other positions, including that of secretary. Following the July 2024 mass uprising that led to significant political changes across the country, pro-AL lawyer leaders stopped attending the SCBA proceedings. Subsequently, on August 18, 2024, a section of SC lawyers formed an interim executive committee of the SCBA, making pro-BNP lawyers AM Mahbub Uddin Khokon and Md Ruhul Quddus Kazal its president and secretary respectively for 2024-25 session. Barrister Ruhul Quddus Kazal, however, refused to discharge responsibility of the secretary of the interim committee. Later on, Assistant Secretary Barrister Md Mahfuzur Rahman Milon, was given the responsibility of secretary.
